90 characters in length. In the IP Address (or PC name) edit box, either specify the exact IP address of the WanClient computer or specify the computer name of this computer instead. Note: If the computer name is specified then the WAN requires a LMHOSTS file or a WINS server to resolve the computer name into its corresponding IP address. The Port field, displays the port address that is being used by WanLink and cannot be changed. The Connect timeout edit box, is not used currently by Wanlink. In the Transaction timeout edit box, specify the time in seconds before a requested transaction made to the server fails. The default value of 5 is required for fast networks and a value from 15 – 20 can be used for slower networks. In the Retries edit box, specify the number of reties to be automatically attempted when attempting to establish a connection to this WanServer computer. In the Ping timeout edit box, specify the period in seconds to wait after the communications fail before the client will retry to establish communications. text: Adding added values Top Adding added values The Summation spider adds the numerical values to be added together to create a total. The final total is calculated by subtracting the added total from the subtracted total. To add one or more values that are to be added to the total If necessary, add and/or select the required Summation spider and/or open its configuration view. For details, see Adding Summation spiders . In the New Input section, double-click the Add value entry. This will add an input called Add value# to the Inputs and section, where # is a unique number starting from 1. Note1: The value of this input can either be supplied by another spider or Data spider (e.g. property or data element) via a silk or it can be typed in manually. Note2: Only numerical values can be typed in, if a string value is typed in, the cell will not accept this input until either the text is removed or a numerical value is entered instead. Tip1: When creating a silk, it is also possible to simply drag onto the Add value entry directly, in the New Input section, to add an input to the Inputs section and connect it to the silk in one easy step. For details, see Creating silks . Tip2: When typing

drag onto the Add value entry directly, in the New Input section, to add an input to the Inputs section and connect it to the silk in one easy step. For details, see Creating silks . Tip2: When typing in a value manually, double-click the value column to the right of the Add value# input name in the Inputs section and type in the required value. Repeat this until all the required values have been added. Note1: The Added Values Total output in Outputs section, adds together all of the values of these Add value# inputs. Note2: This calculation is only performed if all the inputs are numerical values. Note3: If a string value is supplied then the spider will try to convert the string value to a number before using it. If it cannot be converted, the input is meaningless and will not be used. -->

text: Adding and Configuring Series Top Adding and Configuring Series Each charting control displays one or more series that provide the charted values and which are usually chart specific. Adding parameters Top Adding parameters Use parameters when you or your users need to change the value of something frequently, such as a constraint. In other words, in every situation where a hard-coded value is too inflexible. For a practical example of using Select queries one of which uses parameters, which are supplied by controls on a graphic form, see How to chart and/or report data from a database . Parameters are essentially place-holders for values that can be dynamically specified, for instance when different users require different values. To add a parameter: Right-click and select the required value placeholder as follows: Add String Parameter: A placeholders for textual values. Add Generic Parameter: A placeholder for values of other data types, such as numeric or date time values. Add SQL DateTime Parameter or Add Access DateTime Parameter A database-specific placeholders for date time values. The default parameter name is the field name of the selected table. Example: Tip: Rename this default parameter to make it easier to recognise, when assigning a value to it, by manually editing the parameter name, taking care not to remove the encompassing '<!!' and '!!>' and a

ip: Rename this default parameter to make it easier to recognise, when assigning a value to it, by manually editing the parameter name, taking care not to remove the encompassing '<!!' and '!!>' and any additional data-type formatting characters. You can also double click the name in the Parameters list. If necessary, specify the following data type-specific formatting for this added parameter: Data Type Additional Formatting Example Numeric None <!!parameterName!!> String Enclose the inserted parameter in single quotation marks (“’”) Note: This additional formatting can be added automatically by selecting Add String Parameter . ‘<!!parameterName!!>’ DateTime Enclose the inserted parameter in hashes (“#”) #<!!parameterName!!># -->

Note2: Only numerical values can be typed in, if a string value is typed in, the cell will not accept this input until either the text is removed or a numerical value is entered instead. Tip1: When creating a silk, it is also possible to simply drag onto the Subtract value entry directly, in the New Input section, to add an input to the Inputs section and connect it to the silk in one easy step. , it is also possible to simply drag onto the Subtract value entry directly, in the New Input section, to add an input to the Inputs section and connect it to the silk in one easy step. For details, see Creating silks . Tip2: When typing in a value manually, double-click the value column to the right of the Subtract value# input name in the Inputs section and type in the required value. text: Adding the slots we're interested in Top Adding the slots we're interested in For details, see Steps required to Monitor Real-time Data . Initially the Properties collection object contains no Property objects, but it provides a method named Add that is used to add Property objects to the Properties collection. Each Property object in the Properties collection defines a slot to be monitored. The Add method accepts one parameter, the required slot name. The following VBA code shows how to add the value and rawValue slots to the Properties collection: Set prop = props.Add("value") Set prop = props.Add("rawValue") Once the Properties collection is set up, it must be associated with a tag as part of a Request object. In order to facilitate this, each Request object provides a method named Add that handles the creation of the Request object. The Add method accepts a tag and properties collection (i.e. agent name and list of slot names) as parameters. The following VBA code creates requests for Analog tags AN01 and AN02, value and rawValue slots: Set req = reqs.Add("AN01", props) Set req = reqs.Add("AN02", props) -->

text: Adding your own Queries Top Adding your own Queries PLEASE NOTE: This help topic assumes that you are familiar with working with databases and creating SQL queries. Instead of only using the default queries to analyse your logged incidents, you can add your own queries to the Adr_AM_UserQueries table of the AlarmManagement database. Then these queries will also appear in the View Data and View Graph dialogs of this AlarmManagement agent. WARNING! It is recommended that you do NOT edit any table in this database, apart from Adr_AM_UserKPIs and Adr_AM_UserQueries ; otherwise you WILL lose data. Note: If you want to remove the queries you have created, simply delete the Adr_AM_UserQueries table and they will be re-created when the Agent Server starts up. First you need to create the SELECT SQL statement for your query. In this example, we will add a custom downtime reporting query that: Displays the actual reason and sub reasons (not just their IDs) Displays the downtime in the hh:mm:ss time format Displays the category name instead of the category ID Displays the incident name instead of simply the incident ID Displays the unacknowledged time in the hh:mm:ss time format Example entri

ime format Displays the category name instead of the category ID Displays the incident name instead of simply the incident ID Displays the unacknowledged time in the hh:mm:ss time format Example entries returned by this custom query: Note: the Category name (instead of CategoryId) column, the display format of the UnacknowledgedTime and Downtime columns and the textual descriptions provided in the Reason and Subreason columns. The SQL syntax for this query is, as follows: SELECT TOP %t Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents.Idx,DT,Process,Adr_AM_Categories.Category AS Category,Incident,Data,Description,Filter,Priority,Shift,Operator,Acknowledged_dt,Acknowledged_by,Cleared_dt,convert(varchar,convert(datetime,1.0*UnacknowledgedTime / (60*24*24)),8) as UnacknowledgedTime,convert(varchar,convert(datetime,1.0*ActiveTime / (60*24*24)),8) as ActiveTime,Adr_AM_Reasons.Reason as Reason,Adr_AM_SubReasons.SubReason as Subreason,Notes FROM Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents INNER JOIN Adr_AM_Categories ON Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents.CategoryId = Adr_AM_Categories.CategoryId INNER JOIN Adr_AM_Reasons ON Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents.ReasonId = Adr_AM_Reasons.Idx INNER JOIN Adr_AM_SubReasons ON Adr_AM_HistoricalInciden

oricalIncidents.CategoryId = Adr_AM_Categories.CategoryId INNER JOIN Adr_AM_Reasons ON Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents.ReasonId = Adr_AM_Reasons.Idx INNER JOIN Adr_AM_SubReasons ON Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents.ReasonId = Adr_AM_SubReasons.ReasonIdx AND Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents.SubReasonId = Adr_AM_SubReasons.Idx WHERE dt > '%b' AND dt < '%e' ORDER BY dt DESC To add your own query: Open SQL Server Management Studio and connect to the SQL Server that contains the database that the required AlarmManagement agent is connected to. Display the db.Adr_AM_UserQueries table. Right click this table and select Edit top 200 rows . This displays an editable grid of the queries. Select the bottom new (NULL) record and type in the name of this custom query into the Name field e.g. “Custom downtime”. This is name that is displayed in the Query list box when selecting the query. If necessary, provide the necessary Description to help your operators and other users to know what this query will return e.g. “Provides the actual reasons and the downtime in hh:mm:ss time format...”. Either type in the required SELECT SQL statement into the Query field or, in this case, paste it. Note: When pasting in a query

rovides the actual reasons and the downtime in hh:mm:ss time format...”. Either type in the required SELECT SQL statement into the Query field or, in this case, paste it. Note: When pasting in a query, ensure that this SELECT SQL statement copies as a SINGLE line without any carriage returns! Select the next NULL record to commit (save) this query (newly edited record). Restart the Classic User Interface and open the View Data dialog of this AlarmManagement agent to use this new query. You will now find a new query called “Custom downtime” in the Query list. Other things you can do: If necessary your query can support: One or more of the following constraints: these constrains are provided by the View data dialog so that your users can choose which incidents they need to analyse. Top (%t): This allows your users to specify the number of topmost (most recent) incidents that are to be returned by the query. For instance, this %t constraint is used by the "Most frequent alarms (count by type)" query, as follows: SELECT TOP(%t) Incident, Count(Idx) AS [Count] FROM Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents WHERE dt > ''%b'' AND dt < ''%e'' GROUP BY Incident ORDER BY Count DESC From (%b) and/or To (%e)

ype)" query, as follows: SELECT TOP(%t) Incident, Count(Idx) AS [Count] FROM Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents WHERE dt > ''%b'' AND dt < ''%e'' GROUP BY Incident ORDER BY Count DESC From (%b) and/or To (%e): These constraints allow your users to specify the time period during which the required incidents occur. For instance: WHERE dt > #%b# AND dt < #%e# If necessary, you can provide ONLY one of these constraints, without the other. For instance: WHERE dt > #%b# Now (%now). This allows users to specify the current date and time. For instance you can obtain the last 8 hours in SQL by using the following expression: WHERE dt > DATEADD(Hour, -8, '%now') AND dt < GetDate() Shift times: This constraint is enabled when you specify the From (%b) and/or To (%e) constraints (see above), which allows your users to specify the shift during which the required incidents occur. Operator ( %o). This allows your users to display all the incidents that are logged against a specific operator. For instance: WHERE Operator='%o' Category ( %c). This allows your users to display all the incidents that are logged for a specific category. For instance: WHERE CategoryId='%c' One or more of the following KPI targ

ERE Operator='%o' Category ( %c). This allows your users to display all the incidents that are logged for a specific category. For instance: WHERE CategoryId='%c' One or more of the following KPI target values: these are the ideal values that you want to achieve. Average alarm rate (%AAR). This per hourly count is 6 by default. For instance, this %AAR KPI target value is used by the "Most frequent alarms (count by type)" query, as follows: SELECT TOP(%t) Incident, Count(Idx) AS [Count] FROM Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents WHERE dt > ''%b'' AND dt < ''%e'' GROUP BY Incident ORDER BY Count DESC Burst rate (%BR). This per hourly count is 60 by default. Percent upset count (%PUC). This number is 30 by default. Percent upset (%PU). This percentage is 2 by default. Intermittent alarm period (%IAP). This time period in seconds is 10 by default. Bulk acknowledgement period (%BAP). This time period in seconds is 1 by default. Average alarm duration (%ALD). This time period in seconds is 60 by default. Average acknowledgement duration (%AKD). This time period in seconds is 10 by default. If necessary, you can customise these default KPI target values and/or add your own and reference them in your

t. Average acknowledgement duration (%AKD). This time period in seconds is 10 by default. If necessary, you can customise these default KPI target values and/or add your own and reference them in your queries by using the % prefix. For details, see Customizing KPI target values . Add your own KPI target values : once added, your custom queries can ALSO use these KPI target values! Instead of only using the default queries to analyse your logged incidents, you can add your own queries to the Adr_AM_UserQueries table of the AlarmManagement database. It is recommended that you do NOT edit any table in this database, apart from Adr_AM_UserKPIs and Adr_AM_UserQueries ; otherwise you WILL lose data. Note: If you want to remove the queries you have created, simply delete the Adr_AM_UserQueries table and they will be re-created when the Agent Server starts up. First you need to create the SELECT SQL statement for your query. ime format Displays the category name instead of the category ID Displays the incident name instead of simply the incident ID Displays the unacknowledged time in the hh:mm:ss time format Example entries returned by this custom query: Note: the Category name (instead of CategoryId) column, the display format of the UnacknowledgedTime and Downtime columns and the textual descriptions provided in the Reason and Subreason columns. Adroit Data Files Top Adroit Data Files WARNING: All Custom agents and their files (*.DLL, *.VBS, *.CSV) need to be manually backed up . Adroit datasources Top Adroit datasources Adroit is a SCADA product that is used to supervise and control processes. The Agent Server is the storage facility for all the real time and historical data. Click for more details: This data is stored and managed by intelligent objects, known as agents, of which there are different types. Each agent contains externally accessible data attributes, or slots, which in addition to being displayed can, if necessary, be used to interact with and configure their agent too. Tip: See Moving from the Classic Adroit UI for Classic UI feature equivalents in SmartUI . An Adroit datasource exposes the configured agents and their slots of either a standalone Adroit Agent Server on a specific computer or to an Adroit Cluster (a set of two replicated Agent Servers). Note: When displaying Adroit tags you can display bad-tag status indicators on relevant controls and/or vectors. For details, see Bad tag status indicators . This datasource is added within the Datasources category of the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager . For details, see Adding Adroit datasources . Click for advanced Adroit datasource usage information: When connecting to an

tasources category of the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager . For details, see Adding Adroit datasources . Click for advanced Adroit datasource usage information: When connecting to an Adroit Cluster, the Adroit datasource seamlessly switches between the two Agent Servers in the cluster, when one becomes unavailable. However, the automatic tracking of the active master Agent Server within the cluster is NOT supported. The Adroit datasource connects to the primary Agent Server (first specified Agent Server) and connects to the secondary ( Partner Server ) when the primary fails. Therefore the Adroit datasource does not connect to the master Agent Server, if the Agent Server it is currently connected to becomes the standby. The Adroit datasource can be updated, locked or removed, if necessary. For details, see Updating datasources , Locking datasources or Removing datasources . When loading a Agent Database (.wgp) file from a previous version of Adroit, Adroit 10 uses the saved status bit information to configure the IO flags setting of all the Device agents and when the Agent Database (.wgp) file is saved then these status bits are switched OFF in the Agent Database (.wgp) file. o not expect you to experience any problems, it is recommended to completely back up all the existing Adroit projects, before installing Adroit 10 to ensure that all the Adroit data, system, registry and event files are backed up. 4. Scan Point Licensing ---------------------------- Normally a scan point license is consumed whenever a tag is scanned to a front-end device. However, there are a number of other areas that consume scan point licenses as follows: Note: This is in accordance with the generally adopted Adroit policy, where information is provided freely, but where you are obliged to pay for the service of manipulating information. 1. Each DbAccess and Script agent consumes a single scan point license to run. This license is checked before doing a DbAccess transaction for the first time (on a per agent basis) or running the Script for the first time (on a per agent basis) and is only returned when the agent is deleted. 2. Any derived Custom agent, containing a Script engine, will consume a scan

gent basis) or running the Script for the first time (on a per agent basis) and is only returned when the agent is deleted. 2. Any derived Custom agent, containing a Script engine, will consume a scan point license. 3. Any pokes performed (i.e. an operation that changes the value of an agent.slot), using either the Adroit OLE Automation Interface (MISSRVR) or the Adroit ActiveX component (AdroitX.OCX) will consume a scan point license for each unique tag (agent.slot) that is "poked". Also, as the AlarmTag, LogTag and ScanTag functions all use pokes internally, calls to these functions will also consume scan point licenses. Also the FetchChanges & FetchValues functions of the Adroit ActiveX component also consume scan point licenses for the same reason. 4. Any tag (agent.slot) writes from the Adroit OPC Server will consume one scan point license per unique tag. 5. Once a Command agent has been allowed to perform commands, scan point licenses are consumed by every unique phone number specified by this agent and / or used to send SMS messages to it. 6. The SNMPManager agent consumes a scan point for each unique value of an SNMP object that is polled (monitored), written (controlled) o

cified by this agent and / or used to send SMS messages to it. 6. The SNMPManager agent consumes a scan point for each unique value of an SNMP object that is polled (monitored), written (controlled) or trapped (received as an SNMP event). 7. Any agent created for a UDT agent type created by the UDT Agent Type Designer consumes (number of slots-1) scan points. The other scan point will be consumed if and when its rawValue slot is scanned. ONLY in HMI Mode: Each Marshal agent used, consumes 16 scan license points. 7.) Adroit Logging Factor Top Adroit Logging Factor When Adroit logging was originally developed in 1992 a design criteria was accepted which has come to prove problematic for some installations in the real world. Up until 1992 the generally accepted default practice was for users to datalog all points at 1 second. However, due to CPU, HDD speeds and serial protocol speeds, the fastest data could only logged at 4-5 seconds. Therefore the log file created by Adroit was deliberately engineered to always be 20% of the expected size, since Adroit only stores data when it in physically changes. This logging design started to become a problem when hardware and protocol speeds improved OR where high logging time deadband values (or sample rates) were used especially for Analog agents where one could be assured that its value WAS going to be different at each sample period. In these cases, only 20% of the specified historical data is actually recorded. The legacy default for Adroit ’s proprietary logging of using a 20% datalog compression factor has been REMOVED for all new installations, since it unnecessarily misleads users when configuring logging periods. However, if a legacy WGP file is o

logging of using a 20% datalog compression factor has been REMOVED for all new installations, since it unnecessarily misleads users when configuring logging periods. However, if a legacy WGP file is opened by a new installation of Adroit , that the logging periods configured for some or all of the Datalog agents will exceed the allowable size limit of 5000000 samples (or 95 MB) per Datalog agent. This will occur since the legacy method of accommodating this 20% datalog compression factor allowed the required log period to be up to 5 times greater. In these cases these "non-compliant" Datalog agents will display "error load completion" events. Note: Ensure that you have enabled the logging of Adroit system events in order to identify these non-compliant Datalog agents. For details, see Enabling the logging of Adroit system events. To remedy these "non-compliant" Datalog agents either set the LogCompressionFactor value in the Adroit registry back to its legacy default of 5 and restart the Agent Server OR reconfigure the logging periods of the affected Datalog agents, which should typically require the currently specified logging period to be divided by 5. -->

Adroit Scripting Service Policy Top Adroit Scripting Service Policy This additional functionality provided by the Script agent in supporting a fully integrated programming environment (Microsoft’s VBScript or JScript), allows users to automate complex or repetitive tasks, define their own subroutines and functions as well as pass data to other applications. Because of users taking advantage of this technology we have found that we are spending an enormous amount time de-bugging scripts. Adroit Technologies is proud of its reputation for superior service and support and wish to maintain this reputation in the marketplace. In order to do this we are implementing a scripting service policy. This policy is designed to give users access to relevant skills as well as confidence about taking advantage of this technology in realizing sound Adroit solutions. What Adroit Normal Support Covers Adroit Standard Technical Support covers the Visual Basic and Java scripting Agent in the following ways: We explain how to create, edit, troubleshoot and debug Visual Basic and Java scripts. We identify and account for bugs in the Visual Basic and Java scripting Agent. We provide some sample scripting

: We explain how to create, edit, troubleshoot and debug Visual Basic and Java scripts. We identify and account for bugs in the Visual Basic and Java scripting Agent. We provide some sample scripting code that you can adapt for your own use. What Adroit Scripting Service Covers Script design. Script writing. Script debugging. Scripts written by third parties. Modified versions of scripts supplied with Adroit . Application programming interface (API) or other system-level calls Should users require assistance for any of the above items, the following procedure will apply: Users must provide the Adroit Support Desk with the following: Order number. Traveling time is charged according to these hourly rates. The Adroit Support Desk will provide time sheets. We have designed and costed the above service with a view to enabling our users to take full advantage of this scripting technology and believe that it is a step towards continued service excellence. -->

Overview The system allows telemetry functionality for efficient communication to highly distributed systems. We have attempted to support the most important aspects required for a distributed system, namely: • The need for time-stamped data so that events, rather than just register values, can be stored. • An event is a register value (16-bit or 32-bit) and a timestamp with second resolution. Time of arrival (100ms separation) is attempted to be maintained if change events are registered faster than a second. • The need to store in a buffer the events for later retrieval to a SCADA. This is especially needed at a time when communication becomes available and/or

e events are registered faster than a second. • The need to store in a buffer the events for later retrieval to a SCADA. This is especially needed at a time when communication becomes available and/or when the need arises to drill down and retrieve most specific data that would not normally require operator attention. For example, a temperature reading trend would only be of interest if say a high temp alarm were to be received. • Efficient means of communication especially if data costs are an issue. 1.1. Supported Hardware Adroit supports communication with the following PLCs: Mitsubishi FX3U with FX3U-ENET using the following “FXM2M613a” Library function block. Mitsubishi FX5 PLC using the FX5U_M2M GX Works3 “FX5U_M2M634” program. [As of 17/Feb/2022 found in FX5U_M2M_Rev634.gx3] Mitsubishi QnUDE PLC using the following “QUDEM2M621” Library function block. Mitsubishi L-Series PLC using the following “QUDEM2M621” Library function block. ________________________________________________

AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer controls Top AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer controls The AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer control allow users to view and/or locate and/or filter and/or print and/or export their historical Adroit alarms, that are stored in the AlarmManagement agent SQL Server database. From Adroit 8.4 onward, an unlicensed AlarmManagement agent provides the Historical alarm mode option, which only saves your historical acknowledged alarms, so that you can see the full life-cycle of each alarm in each row of the Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents table. For more details, see Historical Alarm mode . How to use the AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer control: this describes the recommended procedure for using this control to view and filter historical alarms. Ensure that you have an AlarmManagement agent that is logging alarms to a SQL Server database. If necessary, create the project and the graphic form that you want this control to be on. Add this AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer control to the required graphic form. For details, see Adding AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer controls . In the DataSource tab of the Initial Configuration dialog, the Server should already specify your current SmartUI Server,

d graphic form. For details, see Adding AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer controls . In the DataSource tab of the Initial Configuration dialog, the Server should already specify your current SmartUI Server, if necessary select the required one; if you already have an OLEDB Datasource for your AlarmManagement agent SQL Server database, select the name of this datasource from the list box or click the New button to create this OLEDB datasource. For details, see Creating a new OLEDB datasource . In the Historical Data Update Settings section, select how you want this control to refresh itself with more recent alarms. For details, see Configuring how to update AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer controls , which ALSO describes the TWO methods of linking the Alarm Management database table to this control. Advanced Control Recipe Properties Top Advanced Control Recipe Properties Edit the advanced properties of the selected control recipe. File Import Details of Control . Rollback On Verification Failure: If this feature is active and a verification failure occurs, one of the following rollback actions will occur: Rollback to pre-recipe values. All values that were set during the execution will be reset to the values they had before the recipe was executed. Rollback to a specified step. Execution will continue from the specified step. Run another recipe. Execute another control recipe. Note: If this feature is not active, recipe execution will be terminated on verification failure. Verification Time: This is the time in milliseconds that the control recipe execution will be delayed, before verification checking begins. The default setting is two seconds. Note: Names used in the recipe agent e.g. to define recipes and batches, CANNOT contain the ‘%’ character. -->

To display this dialog: If necessary, launch the Classic User Interface, as follows: click the Start menu, Programs, Adroit 10 and select the Classic User Interface item). Click on the Configurator toolbar button to display the Agent Configuration dialog box. Ensure that the System checkbox is checked to display the Datalog agent type in this list. Click the down arrow in the Type drop down list Click the Datalog agent type. Click any of the agents in the Agents list. Click the Edit button. Click the Advanced… button in the Edit Datalog Agent dialog. Note: This dialog can only be displayed, once you have logged an agent and have thereby created a Datalog agent. These settings are divided into the following three main sections: Note: The settings in the General and SQL logging sections require the Agent Server to be RESTARTED before applying the configured setting/s. Tip: Click the section headings to show or hide their settings. General: Datalog system buffer size (Kb) This setting specif

the Agent Server to be RESTARTED before applying the configured setting/s. Tip: Click the section headings to show or hide their settings. General: Datalog system buffer size (Kb) This setting specifies the size of the global "datalog change queue", which is 500 Kb, by default. Click for more details: All changes arriving at the data logging subsystem are added to a "datalog change queue". This ensures that these historical updates do not affect the throughput of any real-time updates. These changes are stored in this queue until Adroit reads them off. Therefore, the size of the queue must be able to handle the maximum spike of changed values that a plant can expect. This maximum number of changes is generally proportional to the number of tags logged. The default size of 500Kb, allows for approximately a spike of 11000 changes. It is possible that the sustained (not the instantaneous) rate of plant changes will exceed the rate at which the data logging subsystem is able to operate. In this case, the Agent Server is simply not capable of handling the data logging requirement and the computer will require upgrading or the data logging task musts be split over separate Agent Servers

n this case, the Agent Server is simply not capable of handling the data logging requirement and the computer will require upgrading or the data logging task musts be split over separate Agent Servers OR less tags need to be logged. For this reason we recommend that you use the PerfMon agent to monitor "SubManQueueLen" performance counter of the Agent Server to ensure that it always tends towards 100%, as this counter indicates the free datalog buffer queue. If this value is steadily decreasing, then the rate of datalogging is exceeding the rate at which the values can be committed to disk and the Flush lazily global logging setting should be turned ON. Note: The default value is big enough to handle short term spikes in putslot rates and should not need to be changed. Tip: When specifying the required buffer queue size, use the provided buttons to increase/decrease this value in 64 KB increments/decrements. Disable legacy file compression of 5:1 (LogCompressionFactor =1) This setting removes the legacy default 20% datalog compression setting when using the proprietary logging of Adroit and is ON (checked) by default for new installations. This setting is removed as it unnecessaril

removes the legacy default 20% datalog compression setting when using the proprietary logging of Adroit and is ON (checked) by default for new installations. This setting is removed as it unnecessarily misleads users when configuring logging periods and has been outmoded by the newer hardware. Click for more details . Flush lazily (LazyFlushing = 1) This setting determines how Adroit writes logged values to disk, which is ON (checked) by default, so that Adroit logs its values to the file cache of the Windows operating system. If you uncheck this option (turn it OFF) then logged data is immediately written to disk. Click for more details: If checked (the default option), this results in a DELAY before this cache saves the data, due to the amount of file I/O activity on the computer. Therefore, if the computer is not on a UPS and there is a power failure, ALL datalog values that have not been committed to disk by Windows will be LOST. If unchecked, all logged values are IMMEDIATELY written to disk but this increases the CPU load and slows the Agent Server down. Therefore we recommend that you use the PerfMon agent to monitor the CPU load for very high values and also monitor the "Su

ten to disk but this increases the CPU load and slows the Agent Server down. Therefore we recommend that you use the PerfMon agent to monitor the CPU load for very high values and also monitor the "SubManQueueLen" performance counter of the Agent Server, which indicates the free datalog buffer queue and should remain around 100%. If this value is steadily decreasing, then the rate of datalogging is exceeding the rate at which the values can be committed to disk and flush lazily should be turned ON. In this case a UPS is highly recommended to allow operators to effect a controlled shutdown of the Agent Server computer, thereby preserving all datalogged values. ast entries in the log as the Post_Startup_Value and Last_Known_Value. All intermediate values will be marked as normal or bad. :), which is OFF (unchecked) by default, so that this ‘Post_Startup_Value’ is logged by the Agent Server. However, if you have logged a large number of values (this amount is site-dependant) to SQL, then the logging of these Post_Startup_Values can significantly increase the time the Agent Server takes to startup. Note: ONLY suppress the logging at startup IF there IS a real issue with startup times when logging to SQL. In this case, you can check this setting (turn it ON), which stops the Agent Server from retrieving any logged values to reduce the time taken by the Agent Server to startup. Support compression algorithm on demand logging (SupportCompressionOnDemand = 1) This setting enables the use of Datalog compression algorithms when using the Demand Mode of datalogging, by default, this setting is OFF (unchecked) so you are unable to use compression algorithms when Demand logging. Click for more details about Demand logging: The D

sing the Demand Mode of datalogging, by default, this setting is OFF (unchecked) so you are unable to use compression algorithms when Demand logging. Click for more details about Demand logging: The Demand mode of data-logging, unlike the default Continuous mode, only logs a data value when the LogNow or Trigger slots of the Datalog agent are activated. This allows you to decrease the size of your log files by using a script (or some other external intelligence) to drive the logging of a datalog. For instance, by only triggering the log when the value is between certain limits or at particular times of the batch, instead of logging every change in value. For further details, see Demand Logging . To further reduce the size of your datalogs, you can check this setting (turn it ON), so that you can specify a Time deadband and employ one of the datalog Compression Methods. For details, see Data Logging Compression Methods . Settings that affect the operation of the data logging system that are typically applied irrespective of the selected Datasource (the Adroit proprietary log files or SQL logging) SQL logging: Check for existence of database tables on startup (CreateTablesOnStartup =

are typically applied irrespective of the selected Datasource (the Adroit proprietary log files or SQL logging) SQL logging: Check for existence of database tables on startup (CreateTablesOnStartup =1) This setting causes the Agent Server to attempt to create the necessary tables in SQL at startup, for each value that is being logged to a SQL database, which is ON (checked) by default. This can increase the time the Agent Server takes to startup, especially if you have a large number of values that are being logged to SQL. If this option is UNCHECKED (turned OFF): Adroit creates the necessary tables when creating NEW datalogs (from the Configurator). Adroit does NOT check for the existence of these tables when the Agent Server starts up. This means that datalogs will NOT write if their tables do not exist. Therefore, if you have a large number of values that are being logged to SQL and you have ensured that the datalogs for these EXISTING values have their necessary tables, then UNCHECK this option (turn it OFF) to reduce the time taken by the Agent Server to startup. Disable database table name prefixes (DisableADOTableNamePrefix = 1) This setting causes the Agent Server to creat

CK this option (turn it OFF) to reduce the time taken by the Agent Server to startup. Disable database table name prefixes (DisableADOTableNamePrefix = 1) This setting causes the Agent Server to create tables for each value that is being logged to a SQL database, by using the following table name format AdroitRawLog_[tablename], which is OFF (unchecked) by default. If you prefer Adroit to ONLY specify the table name and hence create shorter table names, then check this setting (turn it ON). This removes this "AdroitRawLog_" table name prefix, so that Adroit only uses the specified table name. Add normal timestamp fields to database tables (LogADODataTimes = 1) This setting causes the Agent Server NOT to log readable timestamps for values that are logged to SQL databases, which is OFF (unchecked) by default. So that ONLY the Adroit timestamp of the change in value is provided, this is not ‘readable’ in SQL as this does not conform to the DateTime value type. If you want Adroit to provide an additional column containing readable timestamps to the database table, then you can check this setting (turn it ON). However, then you must DELETE all your existing database tables and allow Adr

e an additional column containing readable timestamps to the database table, then you can check this setting (turn it ON). However, then you must DELETE all your existing database tables and allow Adroit to re-create them with an added timestamp column. Tip: We recommend that you check this setting (turn it ON) before logging values to the SQL database. Use only proprietary logged data for trends (ProprietarySetPreference =1) This setting prevents Adroit from using data from SQL for trending, regardless of the circumstances, this is OFF (unchecked) by default. Typically you would turn this setting ON if you use at least 2 log sets to log ALL your values, one that logs to Adroit ’s proprietary log files and another that logs to SQL. In this case, by enabling this setting Adroit will ONLY trend data from the log set that logs values to Adroit ’s proprietary log files and NEVER trend data from a log set that logs values to SQL. This ensures that your trends quickly retrieve and display their historical data. Settings that ONLY apply when using OLEDB Data Logging or the SQL Datasource. IMPORTANT: Although reference is only made to SQL in these settings, they apply to any OLEDB compatib

eir historical data. Settings that ONLY apply when using OLEDB Data Logging or the SQL Datasource. IMPORTANT: Although reference is only made to SQL in these settings, they apply to any OLEDB compatible database. UI settings (no restart required): Create datalog agents automatically (AutoCreate = 1) This setting causes the Agent Server to immediately create a Datalog agent when you log an agent from the Configurator, which is ON (checked) by default. Since each agent has a default logging slot that is automatically selected, you can uncheck this option (turn it OFF) if you usually need to log another slot. In this case, a confirmation dialog is launched, asking the user whether a new Datalog agent should be created, before a slot of an agent can be logged. Settings that ONLY apply to the Configurator dialog within the Classic User Interface. -->

Add normal timestamp fields to database tables (LogADODataTimes = 1) This setting causes the Agent Server NOT to log readable timestamps for values that are logged to SQL databases, which is OFF (unchecked) by default. So that ONLY the Adroit timestamp of the change in value is provided, this is not ‘readable’ in SQL as this does not conform to the DateTime value type. If you want Adroit to provide an additional column containing readable timestamps to the database table, then you can check this setting (turn it ON). However, then you must DELETE all your existing database tables and allow Adr

e an additional column containing readable timestamps to the database table, then you can check this setting (turn it ON). However, then you must DELETE all your existing database tables and allow Adroit to re-create them with an added timestamp column. Tip: We recommend that you check this setting (turn it ON) before logging values to the SQL database. Use only proprietary logged data for trends (ProprietarySetPreference =1) This setting prevents Adroit from using data from SQL for trending, regardless of the circumstances, this is OFF (unchecked) by default. Typically you would turn this setting ON if you use at least 2 log sets to log ALL your values, one that logs to Adroit ’s proprietary log files and another that logs to SQL. In this case, by enabling this setting Adroit will ONLY trend data from the log set that logs values to Adroit ’s proprietary log files and NEVER trend data from a log set that logs values to SQL. This ensures that your trends quickly retrieve and display their historical data. Settings that ONLY apply when using OLEDB Data Logging or the SQL Datasource. eir historical data. Settings that ONLY apply when using OLEDB Data Logging or the SQL Datasource. IMPORTANT: Although reference is only made to SQL in these settings, they apply to any OLEDB compatible database. Agent Functionality Top Agent Functionality The "functionality" of an agent can be defined as the sum total of all the inherent knowledge built into an agent type or the operation or method of the agent. For details, see About Agents . The functionality of an agent is structured, much like the data or slots of an agent as having both generic and type-specific functionality. For details, see Data Structure of an Agent . Generic functionality is something that all types of agents possess, whereas type-specific functionality is confined only to agents of the specific type. Some of the generic functionality possessed by all agent types are, for example, the ability to add, remove, copy, save, and load instances. Agent List CSV File Format Top Agent List CSV File Format This file is created when an Alarm agent is exported to store the agents which are alarmed by this agent. The filename adheres to the following naming convention: xxxxx- AGNTLST.CSV, where xxxxx represents the name of this Alarm agent. This file consists of the following columns, from left to right: Tagname: the name of the agent that is being alarmed. Note: This does not specify which slot (value) of this agent is being alarmed. Typeindex: this specifies the zero-based index number of the required alarm type. This can be calculated when the required TYPLST.CSV file is opened in MS Excel, by subtracting two from the specified row number of the required alarm type. For example if the required alarm type is in row 51, then its index value will be 49. For details of the format of this CSV file, see Type List CSV File Format . Route number: A valid route number from the route list file. Acknowledge: 1 is a normal acknowledgeable alarm, while 0 is an alarm that cannot be acknowledged. Reserved: 1 Reserved: 0 Reserved: 0 Inhibit time: The future date/time when this incident (alarmed tag) will be re-enabled, as specified using the

rm, while 0 is an alarm that cannot be acknowledged. Reserved: 1 Reserved: 0 Reserved: 0 Inhibit time: The future date/time when this incident (alarmed tag) will be re-enabled, as specified using the Inhibited until checkbox of the Alarming dialog. It is saved to the CSV as the two parts of a FILETIME variable e.g. if this is not set then the following value is saved: ",0 0" Note: Inhibit times are DISCARDED when IMPORTING alarm configurations. Delay time: The number of seconds that the alarm system should wait, once this incident (alarmed tag)becomes active, before this incident is recognised as being ‘officially’ active. Conditional expression: An expression that must be true before this incident becomes active. -->

Agent or Slot Integrity Monitoring (Bad Handling) Top Agent or Slot Integrity Monitoring (Bad Handling) The first bit in the status word, statusBad or statusBit00 , is the only bit an application needs to monitor to determine the integrity of an agent or slot. For further details of this status word, see Agent status words or Slot status words . This bit itself is a combination of statusConnectionBad (a.k.a. statusRemoved), statusScanBad and statusAgentBad . For details, see Connection Bad , Scan Bad or Agent Bad . Note: This statusBad bit CANNOT be set directly but will only be set depending upon the values of the other three bits for the specified agent (agent status word) or slot (slot status word). If the statusScanned bit of an slot is set, on start up the Agent Server switches also turns on the statusScanBad bit of this slot as well, until the first successful scan transaction for the slot, at which time the Scan Agent will reset the statusScanBad bit of this slot. -->

text: Agent Persistence Files Top Agent Persistence Files Agent persistence files are files that store the data calculated by a Counter or Statistical agent. Their purpose is to ensure that none of this data is lost. Previously this data could only be saved by frequently saving the entire Agent database via a Script or Expression agent. However, this practice is dangerous as .WGP files can corrupt if a power failure occurs during the save. Note: This is a GLOBAL setting for each agent type, which is set in the respective agent configuration dialog. Once enabled, a persistence or (.WORK) file is created for each agent, which is saved when the data of this agent is updated. WARNING! If there are large numbers of Statistical and/or Counter agents, saving their persistence files can increase the CPU load of the Agent Server computer. These persistence files are stored in the Work subfolder of the designated project folder, which is typically C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Configurations\Default \Work. These agent persistence settings are currently saved to the following location in the registry: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Persistence See Also: Project f

These agent persistence settings are currently saved to the following location in the registry: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Persistence See Also: Project folder . Agent Persistence Files Top Agent Persistence Files Agent persistence files are files that store the data calculated by a Counter or Statistical agent. Their purpose is to ensure that none of this data is lost. Previously this data could only be saved by frequently saving the entire Agent database via a Script or Expression agent. However, this practice is dangerous as .WGP files can corrupt if a power failure occurs during the save. Agent Referencing Convention Top Agent Referencing Convention The following convention can be used when referring to agents: [\\AgentServerName\]AgentName This allows agents to be specified or referred to, as follows: Explicitly , by including the Agent Server name. For instance \\AS1\ANA001 This ensures that there is no ambiguity in specifying the required agent. In general, this format may be used in any Classic UI dialog except when adding or copying agents. Implicitly agent names, by omitting the Agent Server name. For instance ANA001 In this case Adroit will first search the Agent Server it is currently connected to for that agent, implicitly assuming it is on that server. If it does not find the agent, it will look in all the other Agent Servers in the same project for agents of the same name. If only one agent is found on a remote Agent Server, it will use that one. If more than one agent of that name is found on the remote Agent Servers, then the action taken depends on the mode of the local Agent Server (as specified in the Adroit Setup utility), as follows: If this is a Stand-alone / Distributed server then any duplicate agent names found on two or more remote Agent Serve

e of the local Agent Server (as specified in the Adroit Setup utility), as follows: If this is a Stand-alone / Distributed server then any duplicate agent names found on two or more remote Agent Servers will be ignored by the user interface. If this is a Cluster aware server or Cluster server then the duplicate tag name found on the first (alphabetically) remote Agent Server will be used. When that becomes unavailable, the tags on the next Agent Server will be used by the user interface, and so on. Note: If a duplicate agent name is found on the local Agent Server (if running) and any remote Agent Servers, the local agent will always be used. -->

Agent Server Communication within Networks Top Agent Server Communication within Networks Agent Servers with the same project name are typically connected by means of Agent Server broadcasts, so that any one Agent Server can directly gain access to any of the other Agent Servers in the project. For further details on projects, see About Adroit Projects . Note: Agent Servers generate an event every minute if remotely connected Agent Servers have a time difference of more than two seconds, to indicate that there is a time synchronization issue. Agent Server broadcasts are highly effective for relatively small Agent Server networks, which are connected on the same domain. However, this approach is inflexible and explicit Agent Server connections are required instead for the following two networking configurations: Inter-domain Agent Server networks, since the Agent Server broadcasts do not operate across domains or over a WAN Large scalable Agent Server networks , since it may be undesirable to maintain a large, potentially resource intensive, grid of fully connected Agent Servers. Note: This is a problem for slower (10MB, WLAN) networks where bandwidth was at a premium especially if

ble to maintain a large, potentially resource intensive, grid of fully connected Agent Servers. Note: This is a problem for slower (10MB, WLAN) networks where bandwidth was at a premium especially if the network is not dedicated to SCADA operations. However, 100MB networks handle this easily. For further details of mechanisms provided by Adroit to connect Agent Servers together and their limitations and how to configure each of these mechanisms, see Agent Server Connection Methods . -->

Agent Server Connection Methods Top Agent Server Connection Methods Adroit provides three methods for allowing multiple distributed Agent Servers to seamlessly share their agents and the data that they contain. In other words, the ability to refer to agents within another Agent Server. Note: Proxy agents are automatically created when an Agent Server accesses an agent that exists in a remote Agent Server. Using the Project Name: This is the default method for connecting distributed Agent Servers, in which case you specify the SAME project name for ALL the Agent Servers that need to connect to each other, which adds them to this project. Network broadcasts are then made between ALL these Agent Servers to provide each other with two-way access to their agents. Click here for the limitations of this method and/or how to configure this method: Disadvantages: In practice each Agent Server within a project typically only connects to agents in SOME of the other specified Agent Servers, which results in unnecessary network traffic between the Agent Servers that are not actually communicating with one another. This connection mechanism uses Agent Server broadcasts, which do not work across

results in unnecessary network traffic between the Agent Servers that are not actually communicating with one another. This connection mechanism uses Agent Server broadcasts, which do not work across domains or routers/switches (a WAN). You need to use the explicit connection mechanism to connect Agent Servers that are in DIFFERENT domains or on OPPOSITE sides of a router or switch or any other network component that blocks network broadcasts. Click Agent Server Configuration again in the right hand pane. Specify the SAME Project Name . Note1: Project names must not contain any embedded spaces. Note2: When more than one project name is being used on the same network, ensure that the first 3 characters of each Project Name are UNIQUE. nt Server Name are UNIQUE. If necessary, ensure that the remote Agent Server broadcasts are enabled, by clicking the Options… button to the right of the Project Name field and ensuring that the Enable remote servers to automatically detect this server checkbox is checked in the Project Options dialog (this is the default setting). Creating Explicit Agent Server Connections: This is the ONLY way to connect Agent Servers that are in DIFFERENT domains or on OPPOSITE sides of a router or switch or any other network component that blocks network broadcasts. In this case you specify exactly which Agent Servers you want your Agent Server to connect, however, these connections are not two-way. Agent Server Connection Methods Top Agent Server Connection Methods Adroit provides three methods for allowing multiple distributed Agent Servers to seamlessly share their agents and the data that they contain. In other words, the ability to refer to agents within another Agent Server. Note: Proxy agents are automatically created when an Agent Server accesses an agent that exists in a remote Agent Server. Using the Project Name: This is the default method for connecting distributed Agent Servers, in which case you specify the SAME project name for ALL the Agent Servers that need to connect to each other, which adds them to this project. Network broadcasts are then made between ALL these Agent Servers to provide each other with two-way access to their agents. Agent Server Grid Top Agent Server Grid The Agent Server grid, consists of the following fields, each of which displays relevant runtime information about the current Agent Server session, as follows: Note: The grid provides the following standard configuration options . The first untitled field numbers the information items in the grid. Item: This field specifies the configuration item, which is being displayed. Value: This field specifies the current configuration of the specified item, which cannot be edited. The following list describes what the listed Items of the selected Agent Server object refer to: Server mode: This indicates the current mode of this Agent Server i.e. Master or Standby , if it is part of a cluster or Normal if it is a standalone Agent Server. Previously stopped at: This indicates the time at which the previous Agent Server session was stopped. Started at: This indicates the time at which the current Agent Server session was started. Running time (hours): This indicates the current duration of the current Agent Server session in hours. Licenced scanpoints: This indicates the number of points that are currently scanned out of the total licensed number of sca

indicates the current duration of the current Agent Server session in hours. Licenced scanpoints: This indicates the number of points that are currently scanned out of the total licensed number of scanned points that are allowed by current Agent Server session. Licenced Clients: This indicates the number of Client licenses that are currently being made to this Agent Server out of the total licensed number of Client licenses that are allowed to the current Agent Server session. Licenced Web Clients: This indicates the number of Web Client licenses that are currently being made to this Agent Server out of the total licensed number of Web Client licenses that are allowed to the current Agent Server session. Licenced for Adroit drivers: This indicates whether the current Agent Server session is licensed to use Adroit drivers, a 1 indicates that this license is in effect. Licenced for HMI mode only: This indicates whether the current Agent Server session is licensed to only operate in HMI mode , a 1 indicates that this license is in effect. Licence expiry: This indicates the expiry date of the HASP being used by the current Agent Server session Total putslots: This indicates the total n

ode , a 1 indicates that this license is in effect. Licence expiry: This indicates the expiry date of the HASP being used by the current Agent Server session Total putslots: This indicates the total number of putslots made within the current Agent Server session. Total subscriptions: This indicates the total number of subscriptions made within the current Agent Server session. Agent Server clients can subscribe to particular values within the agents, and they are only notified when these values change. Total active agents: This indicates the total number of configured agents in the current Agent Server session. Total system agents: This indicates the number of agents that have been created by Adroit in the current Agent Server session. Total user agents: This indicates the number of agents that have been created by the user in the current Agent Server session. A list of the currently filtered agent types , in alphabetic order, indicating the number of configured agents for each agent type. -->

Agent Server Master Write Scanning Strategy Top Agent Server Master Write Scanning Strategy This scanning configuration should be used when the Agent Server is required to be the master during normal runtime operations. This should be used when Agent Server is required to be the master during normal runtime operations. This is a preferred strategy to Forceoutputs=0, but can cause permanent writes to the process value, if the front-end devices (PLCs) do not accept the Agent Server value. Front-end devices (PLCs) should not overwrite Agent Server values. For details of all the scanning strategies offered, see Scanning Strategies or for further details on the effect of combining the available global and tag-specific scanning settings, see The Effect of Combining Scanning Settings . Required global scanning settings: ForceOutputs = 1 SyncProcessToServerOnFirstScan can be set to 1, if required, in which case, see below as to its effect. Required tag-specific scanning settings: Output Enable = 1 Scan Inhibit = 1 Operation of strategy: When the Agent Server is started, the Agent Server receives the values of these scanned tags from the front-end devices (PLCs). Note: If SyncProcessToServe

Agent Server Window Top Agent Server Window This window contains a list of events, along with the date and time at which they were logged to this window, detailing the loading of the Agent Server e.g. the component Adroit agents, it also contains the following troubleshooting tools and aids. The Agent Server window title bar , displays both the current status of the Agent Server and the current Adroit configuration. The status bar displays the percentage of physical memory being used by the system. When this is greater than 100 % then all physical memory is occupied, requiring the use of the virtual memory (the paging file), which will slow down the performance of the system and of the Agent Server. Ideally, this figure should not exceed 75%. The File menu, contains the following commands: The Save Messages command, allows a text file and path to be selected, into which the current logged events in this Agent Server window can be saved, by default, a "message.txt" file will be saved to the "My Documents" folder. The Exit command closes the Agent Server window. The View menu, contains the following commands: The Explorer command, which launches the Adroit Project Explorer once the A

the "My Documents" folder. The Exit command closes the Agent Server window. The View menu, contains the following commands: The Explorer command, which launches the Adroit Project Explorer once the Agent Server has loaded. For details, see The Project Explorer . The Status Bar command, displays or hides the status bar at the bottom of this window. A tick symbol indicates the status bar is visible. The Options menu, contains the following commands: The Spacer command inserts a line into the Agent Server window with the current date and time, containing the following text "====SPACER====" The Jotting command provides you with a dialog box, so that related details or comments can be entered into this Agent Server window, along with the date and time at which the entry is made. The Pause command suspends the loading process, a tick symbol alongside this command, indicates that the loading process is currently being suspended. To resume loading click this command again, removing this tick. The Debug sub-menu which contains the following commands: Debug Flags… containing all the debug flags that were originally located in the Adroit setup program. These are off by default and are only intended to be used by the Adroit support engineers, for diagnosing system problems. (see Adroit Support Debug Flags for a description of these flags) Note: When these debug flags are enabled, the performance of the Agent Server will decrease. Log thread creation events , this logs an event to the Agent Server window, whenever a thread is created. A tick symbol alongside this command indicates that it has been selected. Log thread destruction events , this logs an event to the Agent Server window, whenever a thread is destroyed. A tick symbol alongside this command indicates that it has been selected. Log system events , this enables all internal events in the Agent Server to be logged to the event log. A tick symbol alongside this command indicates that it has been selected. Note: the Debug Flags… and Log system events items are not saved when they are set from the Agent Server window. To save these items, they must be configured from the Adroit Setup program . g Flags… and Log system events items are not saved when they are set from the Agent Server window. To save these items, they must be configured from the Adroit Setup program . The Minimise to tray command, affects where and how the Agent Server window appears when it is minimised. Normally, when minimised this window appears in the task bar along with any other currently open program. When this command is selected, however, the Agent Server window appears as the following icon , which is placed into the tray in the bottom right of the screen. A tick symbol alongside this command indicates that the Agent Server window will become a tray icon when it is minimised. The Agent Server window Tray Icon . Note: If this Minimise to tray command is selected, then on the next startup the Agent Server window will immediately startup as a tray icon; similarly if this is disabled then on the next startup the Agent Server will startup as an Agent Server window. The Help menu, contains the About… command, which displays the Adroit version information dialog. -->

Agent Status Top Agent Status The overall status of an agent can be determined from its status slot, which is a header or generic slot and so is common to all agent types, and shows the status as determined by the status of the individual slot, for instance if one of the agent slots is scan bad, then the agent status slot will show scan bad. In contrast, the statusRaw header slot the agent shows the status of the agent, without any regard for the status of the individual slots. For instance, if one of the agent slots is scan bad, the agent status slot will not necessarily show scan bad unless the agent itself has been marked as scan bad. For details on the structure of data in an agent, see Data Structure of an Agent . This status slot is a 32 bit word containing configuration and run-time status information about the agent. Each bit of this 32 bit word is also exposed as a slot, allowing up to 32 status flags to be accessed at any time. Note1 : In addition to this overall agent status word, there is also a status word for each slot of an agent, which can provide better monitoring and control of the agent. For details, see Slot Status Words . Note2: The first bit in the status word

word, there is also a status word for each slot of an agent, which can provide better monitoring and control of the agent. For details, see Slot Status Words . Note2: The first bit in the status word, statusBad , is the only bit an application needs to monitor to determine the integrity of an agent or slot. For details, see Agent or Slot Integrity Monitoring (Bad Handling) . Note3: These bits can be viewed and/or set via the Agent Header configuration dialog. For details, see Editing the Header of an Agent . This status slot is divided into two portions: The first 16 bits (0 to 15) are known as the Common Status bits as they are common across all agent types, each having a fixed purpose. Their equivalent slots each have unique slotname, which follows the naming convention of statusXxxxxxXxxxxx. e.g. statusScanBad. These status bits are further classified into control, condition and configuration bits. For details, see Common Status bits . The second 16 bits (16 to 31) are known as the Specific Status bits and they are agent type-specific. Their equivalent slots are called statusBit16 up to statusBit31. For details of these slots, see the Agent Types and their Slots Reference . For

Specific Status bits and they are agent type-specific. Their equivalent slots are called statusBit16 up to statusBit31. For details of these slots, see the Agent Types and their Slots Reference . For instance an Analog agent uses the first type-specific bit to indicate a Low Alarm condition, whereas an Expression agent uses this bit to indicate a result value Equal to Zero. Write access is restricted to the control bits (agentStatusBit xx ), where xx is: 01,02,03,05,08,09, or 11. -->

Agent Subscriptions Top Agent Subscriptions The concept of a subscription is based on the principle of “listening” for updates from a specific Agent tag (or slot). The process of subscribing is setting up the “listener”, by registering with the underlying mechanism of the relevant agent tag. Other traditional mechanisms usually rely on explicitly reading a data point to update a value, where as subscriptions allow the change to be sent asynchronously to any “listeners”. The result is that the subscription mechanism is more responsive and less redundant so that only actual changes are sent and only when the change occurs. Subscriptions are the basis of most communication within the Agent Server, and between the Server and the connected clients, (Operators for example) . -->

Agent Subscriptions Top Agent Subscriptions The concept of a subscription is based on the principle of “listening” for updates from a specific Agent tag (or slot). The process of subscribing is setting up the “listener”, by registering with the underlying mechanism of the relevant agent tag. Other traditional mechanisms usually rely on explicitly reading a data point to update a value, where as subscriptions allow the change to be sent asynchronously to any “listeners”. The result is that the subscription mechanism is more responsive and less redundant so that only actual changes are sent and only when the change occurs. Subscriptions are the basis of most communication within the Agent Server, and between the Server and the connected clients, (Operators for example) . -->

Agent Type Structural Reference Top Agent Type Structural Reference The aim of this reference is to describe the structural details of each agent type provided by Adroit , by describing the slots (values) that each agent type exposes and how each agent type is saved in the Adroit database (.WGP) file. Since, an Adroit configuration is made of many different agents, each of which is a unique instance of one of the supported agent types. Each agent, in turn, contains externally accessible data attributes, or slots, whose type corresponds to one of the supported slot types. Agents, Slots, Tags and their relation to Values Top Agents, Slots, Tags and their relation to Values Agents are the fundamental building blocks of Adroit . They are called agents because, in addition to containing data, like simple database records, they also usually contain the ability to operate or act on their own data. For further details, see About Agents . Note: In Adroit , the data or values contained within agents are called slots. For further details, see About Agent Data . Therefore the following method is used when referring to values within Adroit : agentName.slotName, which specifies both the name of the value and its associated agent. Note: In Adroit , this fully qualified named value (or agentName.slotName reference) is known as a tag. For example, a tag containing the value of the rawValue slot of an Analog agent called ANA1, would be written as: ANA1.rawValue -->

Alarms can be transmitted via cellular phone Short Message Service (SMS) or paging service direct to a designated person. Alarm Shelving Top Working with Alarm Shelving (Alarm Inhibiting) This is process of temporarily removing (deactivating) one or more alarms from the entire alarm system (not just the local client), typically for a specific time period. Then when the time is up, if the alarm was active at the time that it was shelved, it will again be added to the alarm system. However, in Adroit -speak a shelved alarm is typically referred to as an inhibited alarm. Currently alarm inhibiting (shelving) can be managed via the following routes: The Manage Configured Alarms graphic form (part of the default System Information project) : this allows you to inhibit (shelve) or uninhibit every configured alarm in an Agent Server, regardless of its alarm list or whether it is active or not. For instance, if you have planned maintenance for a specific plant section, then you can use this graphic form to select all the alarms in this section and inhibit them until the maintenance is over. For details, see Alarm Shelving via the Manage Configured Alarms graphic form . The AlarmViewer control: this allows you to inhibit (shelve) or uninhibit any active alarm in an alarm list (of a specific Alarm or AlarmList

Shelving via the Manage Configured Alarms graphic form . The AlarmViewer control: this allows you to inhibit (shelve) or uninhibit any active alarm in an alarm list (of a specific Alarm or AlarmList agent). For details, see Alarm Shelving via the AlarmViewer control . You can also manually configure alarm inhibiting (shelving) via the Alarm agent. For details, see Temporarily Suspending Alarming (Alarm Shelving or Alarm Inhibiting) . -->

text: Alarm Types Top Alarm Types An alarm is triggered when one or more of the status mask bits in an alarm type of an Alarm agent matches any status bits in the agent being monitored. For an agent to be monitored, you have to apply one or more alarm types to the agent (see Alarming an Agent ). The creation of alarm types is discussed here. Alarm Types are defined on a per Agent Type basis, which are pre-configured in the postload Adroit database file . This means that one set of Alarm types will be created for Analog agents and another set for Digital agents. Agent Types may take the form of a descriptive abbreviation, e.g. "Overheating" for Analog agent types, or "Tripped" for Digital agent types. Each Alarm Type must be edited to define the alarm triggers that take the form of a descriptive abbreviation, e.g. "Overheating" for Analog agent types, or "Tripped" for Digital agent types. Each Alarm type must be edited to define the alarm triggers that take the form of a status word mask wherein specific bits are set. To add or edit an alarm type . -->

Alarming in Adroit Top Alarming in Adroit Alarm agents can monitor other agents for preset conditions or states. So that when a monitored condition occurs in an agent its Alarm agent uses predefined reporting methods to alert the necessary people and/or applications. That is why alarming primarily involves the configuration of the following two things: The preset conditions or states of each agent that you need to alarm, known as alarm types, which each constitute a separate alarm or event. The alarm routes that specify which alarm destinations (reporting mechanisms) you need to use to communicate the generated alarms and events to the necessary personnel and/or applications. Therefore, you need to select the following for each agent that you want to alarm: Which predefined alarm type/s you want the selected Alarm agent to monitor. Which alarm route each alarm type should be reported by this Alarm agent. When a monitored agents enter into conditions defined by a specified alarm type, these are known in Adroit as an incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be

hese are known in Adroit as an incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). . However, an incident is ONLY an alarm, if it needs to be responded to ; otherwise it is an event. Is it recommended that you create an alarming strategy a set of guidelines or a plan to optimise the configuration of the alarming of agents. Once created it can easily be transferred and adapted for other projects, as required. BEFORE you start alarming agents to determine how best this can be achieved. For instance, you cannot alarm one agent using two different Alarm agents. For more details about how alarm types are configured and managed, see About Alarm Types . For details about how alarm routes are configured and managed, see About Alarm Routes . For details of the other alarming settings, see Additional Alarming Configuration . For some reasons for and recommendations when creating an alarming strategy, see About Alarming Strategies . For more details about the requirements for an effective alarm, see Effective Alar

ration . For some reasons for and recommendations when creating an alarming strategy, see About Alarming Strategies . For more details about the requirements for an effective alarm, see Effective Alarm Characteristics . Alarms are typically viewed using Alarm List Viewer windows. For more details see Displaying Alarms or About Alarm List Viewer Windows. -->

Alarming IOT agents Top Alarming IOT agents As previously mentioned on how to create a 2KVAPump IOT agent, oher IOT agents of many different types may be created for devices and machines. For each IOT agent type created that contains status slots (as defined in the <HeaderSlots> section of the IOT Definition XML discussed) , you should create a new Alarm agent.
