Alarming Overview Top Alarming Overview The alarm system is a critical component for any process, which alerts your operators when components of the process are operating outside of their normal functioning. Adroit provides a flexible alarming capability in that any slot a value (attribute) or field within an agent that can be retrieved and/or set. of any agent an instance of an agent type, that stores data and typically provides the ability to operate or act on this data. can be alarmed. In this way any situations, ranging from plant upsets or process variable excursions to failures within the Adroit system itself can be monitored. Alarming is managed by an Alarm agent, which communicates the incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). when they occur, to the relevant personnel and/or applications. You can announce an alarm by using one or more of the following methods: by a siren or through the activation of audiovisual multimedia by a list of unacknowledged and acknowledged alarms by SMS or m

You can announce an alarm by using one or more of the following methods: by a siren or through the activation of audiovisual multimedia by a list of unacknowledged and acknowledged alarms by SMS or mobile pager messages or electronic sign display by logging the alarm to an OLE DB compliant database by logging the alarm to the Windows application event log by printing the alarm to hardcopy by launching a process-specific page of hypertext help by graphical display on a mimic by textual display on a mimic In the past alarms were hardwired into the panels, which limited their number; now alarms are software-driven, which can lead to an unlimited number of alarms. While one’s intention is often to keep the operators better informed by increasing the number of alarms, the result is that operators become overloaded and confused and may even start ignoring alarms! Therefore LESS alarms are MORE effective. Alarm Management is therefore an important aspect of process control as it counteracts inefficient alarming. This allows you to create an alarming system that alerts the operator to the most relevant alarm for the current incident. For more details about creating alarms in Adroit , see

inefficient alarming. This allows you to create an alarming system that alerts the operator to the most relevant alarm for the current incident. For more details about creating alarms in Adroit , see Alarming in Adroit . For more details about displaying alarms in Adroit , see Displaying Alarms in Adroit . For more details about industry guidelines concerning Alarm Management and how this is addressed by Adroit , see About Alarm Management . -->

Alarming strategy Top About Alarming Strategies BEFORE any agent is alarmed it is RECOMMENDED to create and use an Alarming strategy. An alarming strategy is simply a set of guidelines or a plan to optimise the configuration of the alarming of agents. Also once created it can easily be transferred and adapted for other projects, if required. Although this may seem unnecessary to take the time to create such a strategy, as with all planning a little time spent in the beginning is richly rewarded by the end of a project. An alarming strategy is necessary for the following reasons: It simplifies the initial engineering of the alarming. It ensures that the required alarms will be sent to the desired destinations and can be correctly filtered. It eliminates confusion, with regard to the often complex routing of alarms. It prevents the re-engineering of the alarming, if a mistake is detected after the initial alarming configuration has been performed. Although this is not a definitive description of creating an alarming strategy, the following issues need to be considered when this is being formulated: Display of Alarms: Determine which alarm destinations will be used i.e. how the alarms

ption of creating an alarming strategy, the following issues need to be considered when this is being formulated: Display of Alarms: Determine which alarm destinations will be used i.e. how the alarms will alert the relevant plant personnel and the standards that are to be used for each destination. For instance: capitalization rules; the number and width of columns to display etc. In this way it is possible to ensure a consistent look and feel for the displayed alarms, which will assist the plant personnel in responding to alarms quickly. Filtering of Alarms: An alarm priority can be specified for each agent, so that alarm agents can filter out all the alarms generated by low priority agents, if necessary. However, since this alarm priority is tag-specific rather than alarm-specific, it cannot be used as an efficient alarm filtering mechanism, for instance if we only want to display a sub-set of the alarms configured for an agent. The only mechanism in Adroit that can achieve this is to use an Alarm list as a destination and use the alarm viewer filtering mechanism. Routing of Alarms : Construct a routing schematic, which details the alarm destinations that are to be used by each

to use an Alarm list as a destination and use the alarm viewer filtering mechanism. Routing of Alarms : Construct a routing schematic, which details the alarm destinations that are to be used by each route, in each Alarm agent: Note: By default Operator Action Behaviours are routed along route 1, specify the LMOperatorAction registry value if you need to specify another alarm route. Decide on the number of agents to alarm per Alarm agent - there is no limitation for this. Decide on required number of alarm routes to use. Note: Do not use route 0 or 1 as these are predefined Adroit system routes. Decide which routes need to be logged persistently i.e. to the Eventlog and which should be sent to DbAccess for access from 3rd party MES applications etc. Note: Ensure that the alarms generated from a single agent are routed using the SAME alarm agent. For instance, the Hi and HiHi alarms of an Analog agent must both be routed using the SAME Alarm agent. Decide which alarms must be sent as SMS Short Message Service is a service (protocol) for sending short text messages to and from mobile phones. , by allocating a route for SMS's. Although you probably will need to have more than one rout

S Short Message Service is a service (protocol) for sending short text messages to and from mobile phones. , by allocating a route for SMS's. Although you probably will need to have more than one route that uses a Notify agent or Command agent as a destination. Decide which alarm types will go on which route – IMPORTANT if using more than one Alarm agent in this strategy – you can't alarm a tag on 2 different Alarm agents. For instance, considering the following two alarms of an Analog agent called Tank_level: The Hi alarm could be sent along route 2 for an operator to act on (via an alarm window). The HiHi alarm actually sends an SMS to someone. Therefore, if your strategy involves using different Alarm agents to split other various sections of our plant up, these routes will be different but end in the same destinations e.g. same alarm list. For further details about using alarm lists, see Displaying Alarms . -->

Alarming Templates Top Alarming Templates You can add Alarming templates to configure the alarm the process of monitoring an agent for the occurrence of a specific abnormal condition or state (alarm type). settings for one or more alarm types, which are usually manually specified when alarming agents. Alarm types, in Adroit , define the conditions or states of your process values (agents) that are set when they no longer operate within their normal operating range. Note: The Connector used by the Adroit DB Generator utility to connect to the required source (3 rd party application) determines whether templates can be used or not. Usage Example: You can create an alarming template for a particular agent type, like Analog agents and pre-configure the required alarming settings for each of their default and/or custom alarm types, to save your users engineering time. Default templates: Since these templates are alarm type-specific, NO default template can be created. Each alarming template allows you to specify ONE alarm agent that is used to monitor the alarm types that you specify. The required Route , which specifies the required mechanisms (agents) used to report this incident to the necessary personnel and/or applications. AlarmManagement Database Tables Top AlarmManagement Database Tables The AlarmManagement agent creates and maintains the following tables in its associated OLE DB database: IMPORTANT: To clear the Alarm Management database - simply to delete all the tables and then restart the Agent Server, which recreates and populates the tables correctly. DO NOT use a script to empty this database, since many of the tables use an auto-incrementing index field, which is NOT reset in this case causing all manner of problems. WARNING! If you delete any of these tables, they will be recreated with their default configuration when the Agent Server is restarted, BUT you will LOSE any previous configuration or data that the tables may have contained. Adr_AM_AssociatedValues: This table stores the values of the tags that are associated with each incident. Each tag associated with an incident is stored as a separate record in this table. This table has the following fields (columns): Idx: The Key field, which is a unique, automatically incrementing number. IncidentIdx: The unique incident index value of the associated incident record, which is an Idx value in either the Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents or Adr_A

is a unique, automatically incrementing number. IncidentIdx: The unique incident index value of the associated incident record, which is an Idx value in either the Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents or Adr_AM_CurrentIncidents table. Tag: The name of the tag associated with the incident specified by IncidentIdx . TagValue: The value of the associated Tag . Adr_AM_Categories: This table defines the hierarchical structure used to categorise the incidents. Each category is stored as a separate record in this table. This table has the following fields (columns): CategoryId: The Key field, which is a unique, automatically incrementing number. ParentId: The unique category ID of this category’s immediate parent i.e. the category that is above this category in the hierarchy. Category: The name of the category specified by CategoryId . OperatorTag: An optional field for a tag that contains the name of the Operator that will be logged for all the incidents in this category and, if necessary, its sub-categories too. Adr_AM_CurrentIncidents: This table is the initial destination for every incident generated by the alarm agents and logged by the AlarmManagement agent/s. Incidents are ONLY moved to the

tegories too. Adr_AM_CurrentIncidents: This table is the initial destination for every incident generated by the alarm agents and logged by the AlarmManagement agent/s. Incidents are ONLY moved to the Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents table if they are valid and they have been cleared and/or acknowledged and when any mandatory reasons and/or notes have been specified. Note: All entries in this table are DELETED when an Agent Server starts. This table has the following fields (columns): Idx: The Key field, which is a unique, automatically incrementing number for each incident that is logged to it. dt: The date and time of the occurrence of this incident. Process: The name of the AlarmManagement agent that logged this incident. This is required to uniquely identify incidents across the enterprise (if multiple agents log to the SAME database. Note: These names have a maximum of 30 characters. CategoryId: The unique identification of the category in which this incident is located. IncidentID: This is an important field as it uniquely identifies each incident in this database. This is simply the index ( Idx field) that is used for an incident the FIRST time that the incident is logged to the d

s is an important field as it uniquely identifies each incident in this database. This is simply the index ( Idx field) that is used for an incident the FIRST time that the incident is logged to the database. Incident: The name of the incident, which is the agent name and alarm type combination e.g. KILNTEMP.HI Data: The Reported data values for this incident as received from Adroit . Description: The description of the agent causing the incident. Filter: The Agent filter group as received from Adroit for the agent referenced by the incident. Priority: The Agent priority as received from Adroit for the agent referenced by the incident. Shift: The Shift number in which incident occurred, in other words the dt is greater than the starting time of this shift and less than the starting time of the next shift. Operator: This is the value of the tag configured for the Operator tag setting of the category in which this incident is located (or of the CLOSEST higher-level categories, if any). Acknowledged_dt: The date and time that the incident was acknowledged. Note: This time is equal to the dt field, if the incident does not require acknowledgement. Acknowledged_by: The name of operator

cknowledged_dt: The date and time that the incident was acknowledged. Note: This time is equal to the dt field, if the incident does not require acknowledgement. Acknowledged_by: The name of operator who acknowledged the alarm. In other words the name of the currently logged on user of the Adroit client (or Windows). Cleared_dt: The date and time that this incident was cleared. Delay: The Delay field from the Incident table. In other words the number of seconds the incident needs to be active ( Cleared_dt field – dt field) in order to be considered valid. If the alarm is cleared before this Delay then the incident is removed from the Adr_AM_CurrentIncidents table. ReasonId: The Idx field from the Reasons table that is associated with the currently specified reason. If this is 0 then it is assumed that no reason has been specified. SubReasonId: The Idx field from the SubReasons table that is associated with the currently specified sub-reason. If this is 0 then it is assumed that no sub-reason has been specified. Notes: The text specifying any notes that have been specified for this incident. Record_dt: The date and time that this incident was received by the SQL database, which can

reason has been specified. Notes: The text specifying any notes that have been specified for this incident. Record_dt: The date and time that this incident was received by the SQL database, which can be used to improve the quality of the AM reports. Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents: This table stores every completed incident in other words the incidents from the Adr_AM_CurrentIncidents table that have been cleared and/or acknowledged and whose mandatory reasons and/or notes have been specified. This table has the following fields (columns): Idx: The Key field, which is the unique Idx field that this incident had in the Adr_AM_CurrentIncidents table, before it was moved to this table. dt: The date and time of the occurrence of this incident. e Type parameter is not used (is empty). Note: This must be -1, if the Type parameter is being used (is specified). Provides the means to acknowledge individual alarms either locally or globally. Note: This functionality can also be intentionally disabled (for security reasons). Provides the means to inhibit ( shelve alarm shelving is the process of removing an alarm from the entire alarm system for a specific time period. This also known as inhibiting an alarm. ) and uninhibit individual alarms. Note: This functionality can also be intentionally disabled (for security reasons). Allowing Commands to be Performed Top Allowing Commands to be Performed Although all Command agents are able to send and receive textual messages, it is necessary to manually specify whether a Command agent should analyse the SMS messages that it receives for commands, for the following reasons: Security: once enabled, these commands can be used to obtain and/or control any process value or slot exposed by the Agent Server. Licensing: once enabled, scan point licenses are consumed by every unique phone number that is able to send an SMS command to this Command agent i.e. by both the configured recipient phone number and any additional cell phone numbers that are specified or used to send SMS messages to it. For details, see Specifying the Recipient Phone Number and Specifying Additional Callers . Note: By default a Command agent is not able to receive textual commands. Furthermore, it is also necessary to specify which commands this Command agent is able to perform. For details, see Specifying Permitted Commands or for details of the available commands that can be performed, see Available Commands . Note: The Command agent is ONLY able to perform the commands that have been specifi

ecifying Permitted Commands or for details of the available commands that can be performed, see Available Commands . Note: The Command agent is ONLY able to perform the commands that have been specifically selected, since certain commands pose a greater security and operational risk than others. To enable a Command agent to perform textual command messages that it receives: Edit the required Command agent. For details, see Editing Agents . This will display the Edit Command agent dialog. If necessary, select the General tab, the default selection. Under the Commands group, check the Enable commands checkbox, the default is unchecked. WARNING! Once this checkbox is enabled, scan point licenses will be consumed by every unique phone number specified by this agent and used to send SMS messages to it. By default, NONE of the available commands are selected, since certain commands pose a greater security and operational risk than others. Note: Once this checkbox is checked, the AllCommands specific status bit for this agent will also be checked, to indicate that this Command agent is able to receive commands. For details, see Specific Status Bits . -->

Alternate Secondary Port Enabled Top Alternate Secondary Port Enabled Using the same PC port / resource, but different PLC ports / resources. Adroit drivers can make use of a different PLC addressing to cater for the possible failure of some communications hardware component. For this to be effective, the PLCs used need to have separate addresses and both PLCs need to be able to be independently accessed by the Adroit drivers. Note: This only applicable to network-able (RS485, RS232, Ethernet, L2, Allen-Bradley Data Highway, Modbus + etc...) communications. A device goes into recovery whenever a Read or Write transaction fails. This failure is a 3 step process: Adroit requests an update from the front-end device. Timeout Phase: the request is sent to the front-end device, and times out or gives an invalid response. Retry Phase: Step 2 is repeated for the number of retries configured. If the retries are exhausted and there is still no valid response, the Adroit driver will use the secondary PLC address, if it is configured when this step is reached. This involves the driver connecting to the alternate (address Y) port and only occurs once in any transaction. The driver then runs thr

dary PLC address, if it is configured when this step is reached. This involves the driver connecting to the alternate (address Y) port and only occurs once in any transaction. The driver then runs through Steps 2 and 3 using the secondary port. If, at some later time, the secondary port should fail, communications will switch back to the primary port, and will continue through the primary hardware if this has been repaired. After which scanning resumes immediately. -->

text: Applying profiles to allowed users or groups Top Applying profiles to allowed users or groups User profiles are collections of user settings and configurations that need to be associated with one or more of the allowed groups and/or users and stored on the SmartUI Server computer. Click for more details: Since a user must log into a SmartUI Server, in order to use a SmartUI Client (Designer or Operator), the profile that stored on this SmartUI Server and associated with this user is then automatically applied to this user’s log-on session. Profiles apply the same user settings and configuration, irrespective of the computer that is being used and so can be known as roaming profiles. While the same profile can be applied to one or more allowed users or groups, each allowed user or group can only belong to a single profile. Click for more details: Therefore, if profileA is applied to userA and then profileB is also applied to userA, then userA loses his/her association with profileA and only becomes associated with profileB. text: Applying Security Policies Top Applying Security Policies The Adroit Security Manager allows you to implement the specified security settings on the local and/or a remote computer. It is also possible to save these security settings to create a global Adroit security policy (security configuration), which can be applied to another Adroit computer, by simply opening this policy in its Adroit Security Manager. For instance: you may have one security configuration for your remote Classic User Interface or operator–only computers and one for your Agent Server computers. To implement all the enabled security policies on the local computer: this applies ALL the security policies (options) that you have enabled to the local computer. Note: It is recommended that you log off the computer to ensure that these changes are made. Click on the Apply policy menu item. This applies all the security policies to the local computer that have their Apply Policy checkbox checked. IMPORTANT: These security policies affect ALL the users and groups on this computer and not just the Adroit users and groups. Select the required computer using the Browse for Computer dialog. This applies all the security policies that have their Apply Policy checkbox checked to this remote computer. Note: It is recommended that the specified computer is logged off to ensure that these security changes are made. Note: You need Adminstrative rights on the selected computer in order to perform this configuration. To save the security configuration: this saves the configured Adroit groups and users and their group memberships and all the security policies that have been enabled and/or the Classic UI document and/or menu security settings. Arranging tool windows Top Arranging tool windows The primary reason for arranging tool windows is to increase the viewing and editing space provided by the Design workspace . Audit Policy Top Audit Policy Windows can track selected activities of users, by auditing security events and then placing entries in a computer’s security log. Windows can record a range of security event types, from a system-wide event such as a user logging on, to an attempt by a user to read a specific file. Both successful and unsuccessful attempts to perform an action can be recorded. Use the Audit policy to determine the types of security events Windows NT-based Operating Systems will log. When administering domains, the Audit policy affects the security logs of the domain controller and of all servers in the domain, because they share the same Audit policy. When administering a Windows computer that is not a domain controller, this policy affects only the security log of that computer. Entries in a security log can be reviewed using Event Viewer. -->

Authorizing changes made to values Authorizing changes made to values This is only needed when you have configured one or more data elements to require authorization via the data element security dialog in the Smart UI Designer. When a value (data element) requiring authorization is changed then this change in value (write) must be authorized (before it is effected) as follows: If the currently logged on user does NOT have write access to at least one of the data elements that are being written to, then the User Rights Elevation dialog is displayed by the Smart UI Operator or Designer, to provide the Username and Password of a user with write access to the specified data element, along with Comments , if required. Then the Authorize Data Element Writes dialog is displayed so that this or any other unauthorized changes (writes) made to the values (data elements) can immediately be authorized, as described by the next point. If the currently logged on user has write access to at least one of the data elements that are being written, then the Authorize Data Element Writes dialog is displayed by the Smart UI Operator or Designer,so that this or any other unauthorized changes (writes) m

e of the data elements that are being written, then the Authorize Data Element Writes dialog is displayed by the Smart UI Operator or Designer,so that this or any other unauthorized changes (writes) made to the values (data elements) can immediately be authorized. Note: This dialog does NOT display any data elements whose write authorizations have been deferred. Specify the Username and Password of the authorizing user, if required Comments , which typically provides the justification for granting the requested change/s. Tip: When specifying the name of the tag, use the browse button to the left of this cell to browse for the required tag (agent.slot). For details, see Selecting the Agent and Slot Names . text: Automatic master mode assignment Top Automatic master mode assignment In automatic mode, the systeminfo.serverMode is automatically controlled by the state of the partner server and the state of the local systeminfo.serverstate slot. Rules and implications Starting conditions for a new cluster server. Each server can be optionally configured to make itself master after a configurable period of time elapsed after this server has started (loaded). When this time period has elapsed after startup, if the server has not yet detected another cluster server in that project, then it will set itself to master. If, however, it does detect other cluster servers and no master server exists in that list of servers, then it will elect itself as master if it is the lowest alphabetically named server (i.e. closest to ‘a’) in its list of healthy standby cluster servers. Consequences on the cluster of adding a new cluster server. No automatic changes are incurred on any cluster server when adding a new server to the cluster. All cluster servers loadup as standby servers. Therefore, if a master already exists in the cluster, adding a new server will not cause an automatic master mode switch between t

server to the cluster. All cluster servers loadup as standby servers. Therefore, if a master already exists in the cluster, adding a new server will not cause an automatic master mode switch between the servers. If it is required that a newly started server take over as master, and then the options in (4) below can be used. Consequences on the cluster of removing a cluster server. The process of removing a server incorporates both normal program termination and abnormal program termination (software or hardware failures). No automatic changes are incurred on any cluster server when removing a standby server from the cluster. However, when the master server is removed, the remaining healthy standby server will become master. Consequences on the cluster when changing a server’s serverMode and/or serverState slots: The serverMode slot of a healthy standby server is set to master. The server hosting this operation will first set the remote cluster server serverMode slot to standby and only then set itself to master. The serverMode slot of a healthy master server is set to standby. The server hosting this operation will not take any further action. The healthy remote standby server will

then set itself to master. The serverMode slot of a healthy master server is set to standby. The server hosting this operation will not take any further action. The healthy remote standby server will detect the change and switch to master mode. The serverState slot is set from healthy to unhealthy for a standby server. The remote cluster server will not take any action. The serverState slot is set from healthy to unhealthy for a master server. The master server will simultaneously set itself as standby, so that an unhealthy master is never obtained in the cluster. The remote server will detect the change (from healthy master to unhealthy standby) and become the master server. The serverState slot is set from unhealthy to healthy for a standby server. The remote cluster server will not take any action. An automatic election for master mode at a healthy standby server will occur when: a healthy master server is removed when the current healthy master server becomes unhealthy the user sets the serverMode slot of a healthy standby server to master or the user sets the serverMode slot of a master server to standby. This results in a new master and the Adroit system will ensure that the

ts the serverMode slot of a healthy standby server to master or the user sets the serverMode slot of a master server to standby. This results in a new master and the Adroit system will ensure that the existing master is relegated to standby, thereby ensuring that two master servers cannot exist in the cluster. Suggested method of operation Start both Agent Servers in the cluster at the same time, and then the server with the lowest alphabetical name (i.e. closest to ‘a’) will become the master server. In an unplanned master server computer or software termination, the standby server will take over and the automatic UI’s will switch to the new master server. If, however, a master server takeover is planned, simply set the desired standby server as master and the current master will be delegated to standby. Thereafter, the automatic UI’s will switch to the new master server. Adding a new cluster server to the cluster will have no effect on the system. A planned takeover can be implemented either before a planned computer shutdown occurs or when the repaired computer is brought back into the cluster and is instructed, using the manual override, to take over as master. -->

Automatic Sending of Values Top Automatic Sending of Values The Command agent is able to send an automatic SMS message that contains the value of a tag (agent.slot) to remotely monitor the status of important process values. For details of the other methods of sending SMS messages, see Sending SMS Messages . The following mechanisms can be used to send these automatic messages: On change: In this case an SMS message is sent whenever the value of the specified tag changes. For details, see Automated Sending On Change of Value . On significant change: In this case an SMS message is ONLY sent when the change in the value of the specified tag exceeds a specified deadband. For details, see Automating Sending On Significant Change of Value . By triggering: In this case, an SMS message is ONLY sent when it is triggered by another tag i.e. when the value of this tag changes. For details, see Automating Sending By Triggering . Tip: This last mechanism can be used to send or report values at pre-configured intervals, simply by configuring an Expression or Script agent to provide an appropriate trigger. The received automatic SMS message, adheres to the following format: <SUB UPDATE> tagName

-configured intervals, simply by configuring an Expression or Script agent to provide an appropriate trigger. The received automatic SMS message, adheres to the following format: <SUB UPDATE> tagName = value In this case, tagName is the name of the tag whose value is to be displayed. Note: If the default formatting of real numbers has been configured for this Command agent, this format will be used to display real or floating-point values. For details, see Default Real Number Formatting . -->

Automatic WGP File Backups Top Automatic WGP File Backups Adroit WGP files can be automatically backed up when they are saved to ensure that at most only the changes made since the last save will be lost. Both the number of days for which these files are to be saved for and the maximum number of backup files can be specified to avoid backup duplication and conserve disk space. WARNING! This feature is merely intended to AUGMENT the existing backup system and NOT to REPLACE it i.e. it is still imperative that an efficient backup system is in place! For details, see Creating Backup Procedures . Note1: These backup files will be created in the folder in which the WGP file resides, EACH time it is saved, regardless as to whether its contents have been changed or not. Note2: Restoring these saved WGP files is still a manual process, which requires: stopping the Agent Server, renaming the WGP file that is currently being used; locating and renaming the required backup file to this name and restarting the Agent Server. The names of these automatically created backup copies, adhere to the following format: name.yyyymmdd_hhmmss_v_n.wgp Where: name: is the normal name of the WGP file yymmdd:

estarting the Agent Server. The names of these automatically created backup copies, adhere to the following format: name.yyyymmdd_hhmmss_v_n.wgp Where: name: is the normal name of the WGP file yymmdd: is the date of the save e.g. 20041101 hhmmss: is the time of the save e.g. 163715 v: is an incremental version number Note: This version number will increment when this WGP file is saved, even if nothing has been changed in the WGP file. n is the number of agents stored in the WGP file Note: This is still stored in the first line of the WGP file, as before. Note: In addition to automatic backup, Adroit WGP files also contain version information. For details, see Versioning WGP Files . -->

text: Automating Sending By Triggering Top Automating Sending By Triggering The Command agent is able to send an automatic SMS message that contains the value of a tag (agent.slot) to remotely monitor the status of important process values. One of the methods by which these messages can be automated, is by ONLY sending a message when it is triggered by another tag i.e. when the value of this tag changes. For details of the other methods, see Automatic Sending of Values . Tip: This method of sending automated SMS messages can be used to report values at pre-configured intervals, simply by configuring an Expression or Script agent to provide an appropriate trigger. To send an SMS message when the value of its triggering tag changes: If necessary, add a Command agent. For details, see Adding Agents . Edit the required Command agent. For details, see Editing Agents . This will display the Edit Command agent dialog. Select the Subscriptions tab. If necessary, click the Add subscription button to add a new entry. If necessary, select the Tag/Pseudonym cell, in the required row and specify the name of the required tag or its pseudonym, whose value is to be automatically sent to the designated r

add a new entry. If necessary, select the Tag/Pseudonym cell, in the required row and specify the name of the required tag or its pseudonym, whose value is to be automatically sent to the designated recipient of this Command agent. Tip: When specifying the name of the tag, use the browse button to the left of this cell to browse for the required tag (agent.slot). For details, see Selecting the Agent and Slot Names . Note: When using a pseudonym, ensure that it has been created, that it is spelt correctly and that the use of pseudonyms have been enabled for this Command agent. For details, see Creating Pseudonyms or Enabling Pseudonyms and Macros . Select the Trigger / Deadband cell and specify the name of the required tag, which is to act as the trigger. For instance, if systeminfo.hour is specified, the value of this tag, specified in step #, will be sent every hour. The designated recipient of this Command agent, will then receive automatic SMS message whenever the value of the specified trigger tag changes, which adhere to the following format: <SUB UPDATE> tagName = value In this case, tagName is the name of the tag specified in step 5. Note: If the default formatting of real n

fied trigger tag changes, which adhere to the following format: <SUB UPDATE> tagName = value In this case, tagName is the name of the tag specified in step 5. Note: If the default formatting of real numbers has been configured for this Command agent, this format will be used to display real or floating-point values. For details, see Default Real Number Formatting . -->

Automating Sending On Significant Change of Value Top Automating Sending On Significant Change of Value The Command agent is able to send an automatic SMS message that contains the value of a tag (agent.slot) to remotely monitor the status of important process values. text: Available Agents Top Available Agents The most fundamental building blocks of Adroit are intelligent objects called agents, which in addition to being able to manipulate their own data can read and write to other agents and so influence them. For further details, see About Agents or How agents can be used . An Adroit configuration is therefore made of many different agents, each of which is a unique instance of one of the supported agent types. For details about how to reference agents, see Agent Referencing Convention . Each agent type provides externally accessible data attributes, or slots. For a description of the slots provided by each agent type, see Agent Type Slot Reference . The following is an alphabetic list of all the available agent types: The Accumulator agent : to analyse an accumulating process value to calculate its difference in value (or delta) between successive events or over a specific time period. The AgentGroup Agent : combines agents that have something in common into groups. The Alarm Agent : manages how incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each inciden

on into groups. The Alarm Agent : manages how incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). are communicated to the necessary personnel and/or applications. The AlarmList Agent : lists current or unacknowledged incidents to display in an Alarm List Viewer window. The AlarmManagement Agent : configures and records your active incidents so you can improve your alarming configuration. The Alias Agent : creates a reference to an existing agent to adopt its Behaviour and state information. The Analog Agent : stores a real (floating point) value and provides engineering functionality such as scaling. The ARec Agent : configures up to 256 states using truth table type logic on up to 32 bits. The Audit agent : supplements the Agent Server auditing by monitoring one or more tags for ANY change in value. The Beeper Agent : provides simple audio output using the built-in PC loudspeaker. luated to determine whether it returns any rows. If the subquery returns at least one row, the result of EXISTS is TRUE. LIKE A character string comparison for SIMILAR pattern matching. LIKE "string" searches for values matching specified "string". If Field = string, then row is displayed. NOT LIKE A character string comparison for EXCLUSIVE pattern matching. NOT LIKE "string" searches for values not matching specified "string". If Field <> string, then row is displayed. The "string" specified for the LIKE and UNLIKE comparison operators support the following wildcards: ‘%’ can be used as a placeholder for ANY number of characters. For instance “AB%” returns fields whose values are: “AB”, “ABC”, “ABCD” etc. Tip: "%AB%" returns all fields containing "AB" anywhere in their values. ‘_’ can be used as a placeholder for a SINGLE character’. the trigonometric cosine of the given angle (in radians) exp(value) the constant 'e' raised to the power of the given value. Available operators Top Available operators The expression string is a sequence of operators and their operands the term(s) or sub-expression(s) that an operator acts upon. , which are evaluated and resolved to produce the Result output. The operators follow a strict precedence, which define the order in which their operands are evaluated. In addition to this, operators also act on either the operand on their left or the operand on their right, which is known as their "associativity". Click for more details: The following table shows the precedence and associativity of operators (from highest to lowest precedence): The first column of the table also specifies how the operator is to be used, and designates the operands, as follows: Primary: primitive members of expressions like constants, variables or functions. Terms: separable parts of expressions, and can be signed terms or the product, quotient or modulus of two signed terms. Note1: Operators in the same segment of the table have equal precedence and are evaluated from left to right in an expression. Note2: This order of precedence can be overridden through the use of brackets '('..')', to force some parts of an expression to be

ual precedence and are evaluated from left to right in an expression. Note2: This order of precedence can be overridden through the use of brackets '('..')', to force some parts of an expression to be evaluated before others. Operations within brackets are always performed before those outside. Although within the brackets operator precedence is maintained. Operator & Usage Name or Meaning Associativity – primary minus sign right to left + primary plus sign right to left primary / primary division left to right primary * primary multiplication left to right term + term addition left to right term – term subtraction left to right The following table provides the available Boolean operators: Note: The Associativity of Boolean operators is always from left to right with the exception of the Boolean inversion ! operator which is from right to left. Since Boolean True is evaluated as 1 and Boolean False is evaluated as 0, the following equation: ((!i1&&i2)+(i2*20)), where i1 = 0 and i2 = 1, evaluates to: ((1)+(20)) = 21. IMPORTANT: When adding multiple “&&” , “||” and other expressions, for instance: (i1<i2)&&(i1>10), each expression MUST be enclosed in parentheses “()”. If these parent

evaluates to: ((1)+(20)) = 21. IMPORTANT: When adding multiple “&&” , “||” and other expressions, for instance: (i1<i2)&&(i1>10), each expression MUST be enclosed in parentheses “()”. If these parentheses are left out, these expressions do not evaluate correctly. Boolean Operator & Usage Name or Meaning Examples term == term Boolean equality “2==3” returns false (0) “3==3” returns true (1) term != term Boolean inequality “2!=3” returns true (1) “3!=3” returns false (0) term < term Less than “2<3” returns true (1) “3<3” returns false (0) term > term Greater than “2>3” returns false (0) “3>3” returns false (0) term <= term Less than or Equal “2<=3” returns true (1) “3<=3” returns true (1) term >= term Greater than or Equal “2>=3” returns false (0) “3>=3” returns true (1) ! term Not – Boolean inverse “!1” returns false (0) “!0” returns true (1) “!n” returns 0, where n is not equal to 0 term && term Boolean AND l“1&&1” returns true (1) “1&&0” returns false (0) x&&y returns true (1) where x and y are non-zero term || term Boolean OR “1||1” returns true (1) “1||0” returns true (1) “0||0” returns false (0) x||y returns true (1) where either x and/or y are non-zero -->

Available spiders Top Available spiders Spiders and their links (silks) are essentially a visual programming language, which allows data to be transferred and/or manipulated, typically by means of drag and drop. Click for more information: For an overview, see Introduction to spiders and silks . Spiders are usually only manually added to the spider workspace, to perform additional manipulation or formatting of data. For details on how to add a spider to the spider workspace, see Adding spiders . Tip: In addition to manually configuring spiders and silks, it is also possible to perform bulk configuration, by exporting and importing this configuration. For details, see Importing spiders and silks . Spiders are organised into the following categories to make it easier to selected the required spider: Advanced: Spiders that perform advanced functionality or configuration, such as, providing scripting functionality, adding performance counters, executing special functions, formatting string values or changing the visible level of a graphic form or dynamically changing the names of data elements and if necessary configuring their values. This briefly describes the operation performed by

Backing Up Adroit Database (.WGP) Files Top Backing Up Adroit Database (.WGP) Files The Adroit database or .WGP file stores almost all of the data and configuration of the Agent Server, including the added agents, their values and their alarming, logging and scanning configuration. For this reason, it is essential that this file, along with the other Adroit project files, be frequently backed up to ensure that the integrity of this data is preserved. Since if this file is either deleted or becomes corrupted without having a recent backup, many man hours of effort will be lost. Adroit WGP files, from Adroit 6 onwards, provide two additional features to assist with their regular back up, as follows: WARNING! These features are merely intended to AUGMENT the existing backup system and NOT to REPLACE it i.e. it is still imperative that an efficient backup system is in place! Automatic backup of WGP file on each save: To further ensure that changes made to the WGP file are safeguarded between the regular backups, WGP files can now be automatically backed up each time they are saved. For details, see Configuring Automatic WGP File Backups . Note1: If this is implemented, then at most onl

en the regular backups, WGP files can now be automatically backed up each time they are saved. For details, see Configuring Automatic WGP File Backups . Note1: If this is implemented, then at most only the changes made since the last save will be lost. Note2: Restoring these saved WGP files is still a manual process, which requires: stopping the Agent Server, renaming the WGP file that is currently being used; locating and renaming the required backup file to this name and restarting the Agent Server. Version information saved in the WGP file: In addition to providing an audit trail of changes for debugging and troubleshooting purposes, this versioning information can also be used to assist in locating the required backup file when recovering lost changes. For details, see Versioning WGP Files . For details on creating a backup procedure to guarantee disaster avoidance and to easily transfer a project to another system, see Creating Backup Procedures . -->

Backing up and restoring MAPS projects Top Backing up and restoring MAPS projects You can backup your MAPS projects for safe keeping and/or to move them to another Server and restore them later. To backup a project: Right click the required MAPS project in the MAPS window and select the Backup option. This creates a copy of your MAPS project and a compressed .ZIP file, whose file name is the date and project name, e.g. 6-14-2011_ACME.zip. Both this ZIP file and the copy of your MAPS project folder, is saved to the MAPS project path that you specified when creating the project. Typically this is C:\MAPS \ProjectBackups\YourProjectName. To restore a previously backed up project: Right click on the MAPS root node of the MAPS window and select the Restore option. Select the .ZIP file of the required MAPS project that you want to restore. This will restore this project, if it does not already exist. -->

text: Backing up Server data Top Backing up Server data By default, the SmartUI Server backups ALL of the data that it saves, which includes the profiles, projects and the other data that it stores to guard against its possible corruption, accidental deletion etc. Tip: The Adroit Config Editor provides a System Backup and Restore feature that can backup and restore your SmartUI and/or Adroit user-configuration. For details, see System Backup and Restore . For details on configuring this backup setting and also how long the backed up data should be stored before it is deleted, see Server saving and backup settings . These backups are stored in a subfolder called BACKUP, which is created in the folder in which the various data items have been configured to be saved. For details on specifying these storage locations, see Server directory settings . Each backup consists of two files, namely the FileName file, which depends on the type of data that is being backed up and the FileNameINDEX file, both of which have the current date and time appended to their names. oth of which have the current date and time appended to their names. Overview This driver makes use of the BACnet Stack library supplied by sourceforge.com. The driver supports these functions at the moment: ReadProperty ReadPropertyMultiple WriteProperty Not all devices support ReadPropertyMultiple. For reading we will always try to do a ReadPropertyMultiple and if it fails the driver will revert to a ReadProperty call instead. ReadProperty is much slower and has a limitation of only supporting 255 Items that can be scanned i

to do a ReadPropertyMultiple and if it fails the driver will revert to a ReadProperty call instead. ReadProperty is much slower and has a limitation of only supporting 255 Items that can be scanned individually. The driver also supports Ethernet connection through a WhoIs function call. NOTE: Please ensure broadcasting is enabled on all routers and internal network between driver and BACnet devices to ensure successful communications. Also only UDP is used so ensure UDP is enabled through any firewalls. UDP port 47808 is used. _____________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ ATQMS-DRVR-DOC-D_BACNET.docx P a g e | 5 2. BACnet Device Details Enable shadow scanning from master to standby – If enabled will stop any communication to the BACnet device when the Agent server is in standby mode. This is only required and comes into working when the actual IP Address of the unit is unknown or will change dynamically. IP Address – The static IP Address of the BACnet device. If this is specified the Station ID is ignored as connection happens purely based on IP and UDP Port then. APDU – The maximum size in bytes that can be transferred over Ethernet. 1495 bytes is the maximum allowed on a single network packet and then some devices may implement segmentation of packets. Basic Principles of DbAccess Agents Top Basic Principles of DbAccess Agents Each DbAccess Agent represents a transaction on a row, in a table, in a database. Before any transactions can take place, a connection to a database has to be established and a table in this database has to be identified, that requires or contains the information necessary for a transaction. IMPORTANT: If you are connecting to a database across the network and your Agent Server is running as a service, then ensure that the user profile that the Agent Server service uses to log onto the computer HAS the necessary rights to browse the network and connect to the remote database. This should NOT be the default Local System account. See Configuring Agent Server Service User Profile. The table will consist of a number of fields or columns; and each field may be linked to a tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). . Note1: Table names and field names should not contain spaces as each database vendor supports spaces differently. Note2: The DBAccess agent encloses SQL statements field names in square brackets if the field names contain spaces. The following transactions are supported: insert

vendor supports spaces differently. Note2: The DBAccess agent encloses SQL statements field names in square brackets if the field names contain spaces. The following transactions are supported: insert, update, delete and retrieve: An insert or an update transaction is used to transfer information from Adroit into the table, as follows: An insert transaction simply takes the values of tags and inserts a new entry into the end of the table, this is useful for accumulating a history of information on tags. An update transaction is responsible for keeping a record or a row in a table updated with the values of tags. A delete transaction can be used to remove a number of rows in a table. A retrieve transaction is used to transfer information from the table to Adroit . This is useful for applying a recipe management system or for updating Adroit with the results obtained from a 3 rd party application. These database transactions can be executed in the following ways: On demand by poking a one into the agent's runNow slot, or, by clicking the "Trigger now" button, when editing the agent. By scheduling , based on a simple schedule; e.g. to transact every three seconds, or, to transact ever

e into the agent's runNow slot, or, by clicking the "Trigger now" button, when editing the agent. By scheduling , based on a simple schedule; e.g. to transact every three seconds, or, to transact every twenty-four hours synchronised at six 'o clock in the morning. By triggering , based on a list of tags e.g. when the digital tag PUMP.value switches on, or, when the analog tag DAM_LEVEL.value changes. By using a combination of triggering and scheduling . For instance, using scheduling on condition that triggering has occurred, will apply a time dead band to the triggering of the transactions, e.g. to transact every five seconds but only if the tag DAM_LEVEL.value has changed. This prevents a flood of triggers initiating multiple transactions. -->

The following transactions are supported: insert, update, delete and retrieve: An insert or an update transaction is used to transfer information from Adroit into the table, as follows: An insert transaction simply takes the values of tags and inserts a new entry into the end of the table, this is useful for accumulating a history of information on tags. An update transaction is responsible for keeping a record or a row in a table updated with the values of tags. A delete transaction can be used to remove a number of rows in a table. A retrieve transaction is used to transfer information from the table to Adroit . This is useful for applying a recipe management system or for updating Adroit with the results obtained from a 3 rd party application. These database transactions can be executed in the following ways: On demand by poking a one into the agent's runNow slot, or, by clicking the "Trigger now" button, when editing the agent. By scheduling , based on a simple schedule; e.g. to transact every three seconds, or, to transact ever

e into the agent's runNow slot, or, by clicking the "Trigger now" button, when editing the agent. By scheduling , based on a simple schedule; e.g. to transact every three seconds, or, to transact every twenty-four hours synchronised at six 'o clock in the morning. By triggering , based on a list of tags e.g. when the digital tag PUMP.value switches on, or, when the analog tag DAM_LEVEL.value changes. By using a combination of triggering and scheduling . For instance, using scheduling on condition that triggering has occurred, will apply a time dead band to the triggering of the transactions, e.g. to transact every five seconds but only if the tag DAM_LEVEL.value has changed. This prevents a flood of triggers initiating multiple transactions. -->

Basic principles of server mode assignment strategies in Adroit Top Basic principles of server mode assignment strategies in Adroit The state of a cluster server is recorded in the systeminfo.serverMode (0, 1, 2 = master, standby, normal respectively) and systeminfo.serverState (0, 1 = unhealthy, healthy respectively) slots for every cluster server. A new cluster server always starts up as a standby server. The serverstate slot always starts up as healthy and remains as such unless the user changes it to unhealthy (0) via a script, expression agent or a similar means. It is the user's method of informing the Agent Server that something in the server is not healthy and it needs to relinquish it's master state. Manual master mode assignment . Automatic master mode assignment . -->

Beeper Agent - Slot Details Top Beeper Agent - Slot Details The Beeper Agent provides simple audio output using PC speaker. The pitch depends on the start slot value, which may be any integer from zero upwards. A start value of zero means silence. The higher the priority of this agent is set, the more urgent the beeping. Start slot is reset to 0 on Shutdown, unless dataPersist is set to 1 This agent is located in the following file: T_BEEPER.DLL Slots: Slot Name Type Function dataPersist BOOLEAN Save the Start value when saving this agent to the agent database file (.WGP). reset BOOLEAN Resets the beeper. start INTEGER Starts the beeper, this is ALSO the count value of the beeper, a value of 0 will turn the beeper off and non zero values determine the frequency (pitch) of the beeper. Specific status bits: None Methods of creation: Manual Agents created by default: aBeeper For a description of which of these slots are saved to the Adroit database file (.WGP), see: Beeper Agent - Database File Format . -->

Bind Value Behaviours Top Bind Value Behaviours This Behaviour can drive a data element (value) to and/or from the value of a property of a control or vector. Usage examples: Displaying a value on a label or button with applied string formatting. Driving a gauge control from the value of an Adroit agent. Driving a slider control from the value of an Adroit agent and writing this value back to Adroit when the slider is manually adjusted. The Bind Value Behaviour provides the following options: To Control Property: this is the default option, where a value (data element) is linked to a property of a control/vector. If this is a String property, then you also have the option of applying string formatting to this value before it displayed. This allows a data element (value) to drive the value of a property of a control/vector. From Control Property: this connects a property of a specific control or vector to a value (data element) and specifies which event of this control or vector is used to update this data element with the current value of this property. This allows the value of a property of a control or vector to drive the value of a data element. Both (To/From Control Property):

to update this data element with the current value of this property. This allows the value of a property of a control or vector to drive the value of a data element. Both (To/From Control Property): this both sets a property of a control or vector to a data element and when a specific user event occurs to this control or vector, then the current value of this property is written back to this data element. This facilitates a two-way feedback connection between the specified property of the control/vector and the data element. Bind Value Behaviours Top Bind Value Behaviours This Behaviour can drive a data element (value) to and/or from the value of a property of a control or vector. Usage examples: Displaying a value on a label or button with applied string formatting. Driving a gauge control from the value of an Adroit agent. Driving a slider control from the value of an Adroit agent and writing this value back to Adroit when the slider is manually adjusted. The Bind Value Behaviour provides the following options: To Control Property: this is the default option, where a value (data element) is linked to a property of a control/vector. If this is a String property, then you also have the option of applying string formatting to this value before it displayed. This allows a data element (value) to drive the value of a property of a control/vector. From Control Property: this connects a property of a specific control or vector to a value (data element) and specifies which event of this control or vector is used to update this data element with the current value of this property. This allows the value of a property of a control or vector to drive the value of a data element. Both (To/From Control Property):

Both (To/From Control Property): this both sets a property of a control or vector to a data element and when a specific user event occurs to this control or vector, then the current value of this property is written back to this data element. This facilitates a two-way feedback connection between the specified property of the control/vector and the data element. Blinking spiders Top Blinking spiders The Blinking spider can start and stop a color blinking i.e. alternating between two pre-defined colors at a specified interval in milliseconds. When this blinking is stopped, another pre-defined color can be displayed. This spider can be used to configure color properties of graphic forms and their form components. To add this spider to the spider workspace . To define the required blinking . To specify the static color . To stop or start the blinking . Configuration Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider. Note: Menu items that are enabled will have a tick mark to the left of them. Detail View: This can be used to display the configuration view of this spider, so its name, description, inputs and outputs can be configured. For details, see Working with spider configuration views . Tip: Double-click the title bar of the spider to display or hide the configuration view of the spider. Delete Spider: This can be used to remove this spider from the spider workspace. For details, see Removing spiders . Trigger Spider From Event: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its scrip

ider: This can be used to remove this spider from the spider workspace. For details, see Removing spiders . Trigger Spider From Event: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by means of an event. For details, see Triggering a spider from an event . This is disabled by default. Enable Silk Triggering: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by any silks that are attached to the inputs of this spider. For details, see Triggering spiders . This is enabled by default. Propagate Outputs At Startup: This enables the spider to supply the silks connected to its outputs with values as soon as its spider workspace enters into running mode. For details, see Working with spider workspaces or Sending spider outputs at startup . This is disabled by default. Trigger Now!: This will cause this spider to immediately be triggered. Browsing for data translation keys Top Browsing for data translation keys Data element translation uses the Key column to translate textual data displayed by graphic forms for the current project. Note: Each Key represents the full string value of a data element, this does not do partial string matches. In other words, only textual data elements (from any datasource) whose values EXACTLY match any of the Key column strings will be translated when the graphic form is displayed. For example, you can specify the textual states of digital values, such as On or Off so that all of them that these states will be appropriately translated when they are displayed on a graphic form. To browse for data translation string phrases or keys Open the required project in the Enterprise Manager . For details, see Opening Projects . Double-click its Translation object or its icon . This displays the Translation configuration dialog , which can be maximised and/or manually resized as required . If necessary, add the required language first. For details, see Adding languages to projects . If necessary, select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clickin

y, add the required language first. For details, see Adding languages to projects . If necessary, select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the Data tab. Click the browse button to the right of the required Key column entry to display the Data Element Browser dialog. For details on using this dialog to select data elements. see Working with the Data Element Browser . Click the Finish button when you have selected the required textual data element value. This only imports textual (String) values and displays a summary of this string value importing process, displaying the number of imported and duplicate strings. If necessary configure other Key values and then click the Finish button when are done. For instance: Adroit.Analog.*.agentDescription Note1: If a slot is a number or a date/time value then this

d notation: AdroitDatasourceName.TagName.*.slot to return all agents that contain this slot. For instance: Adroit.Analog.*.agentDescription Note1: If a slot is a number or a date/time value then this is not added, since this value cannot be translated. Note2: A warning is displayed if this operation involves more than 10 000 slots. Browsing for OPC Item Addresses Top Browsing for OPC Item Addresses Typically, when using the OPC client an application that uses the data provided by an OPC server. driver, the browse button next to the Address field in the scanning dialog is enabled and when clicked, the OPC Browser is automatically launched. This utility allows you to browse for and select the required address of an OPC item in an OPC server. Example: This application does not inherently support a connection to a remote OPC server. Click for more details: This ONLY occurs if the remote OPC server has been configured as a valid Adroit device, in which case you can launch this program as follows: OPCBROWSER.EXE /d:devicename. This allows you to keep the browser open after browsing in a scan-tag, avoiding the time needed for the browser to open each time. Note: The speed of browsing is a function of the OPC tag database size and the OPC server itself, not the browser. How to use this OPC Browser to obtain an OPC Item Address: Before the OPC Item Browser for all OPC Servers is displayed, it connects to all the local OPC Servers, and any remote OPC Servers specified in the device’s configuration, that are running Not

ddress: Before the OPC Item Browser for all OPC Servers is displayed, it connects to all the local OPC Servers, and any remote OPC Servers specified in the device’s configuration, that are running Note: If no OPC Servers are running then the OPC Item Browser will not open Once the OPC Item Browser for all OPC Servers is displayed, the required OPC Server can be opened in the left pane and the configured tree structure can be browsed. Tip: Use the Esc key to abort the current browse operation. The right windowpane displays all the configured items that exist for the currently selected branch of the tree in the left windowpane. Tip: When browsing OPC Servers with large lists, use the Filter list box to limit the displayed items and easily locate the required item. When an OPC item a string, uniquely describing an individual data element residing in an OPC server. It may be up to 80 characters long, and structured hierarchically typically using a period "." to separate each level. is selected (highlighted), the status bar is filled with the data pertaining to it. cted (highlighted), the status bar is filled with the data pertaining to it. Note: The Detail mode in the browser has been enhanced for use with certain OPC Servers. Tip: Check the Persistent checkbox to save and restore the last selected OPC item between browser sessions. So that it is no longer necessary to re-browse for it, when the OPC Browser is displayed again. To select an item in the right windowpane, double click on the required item. This places the selected item into the third windowpane and copies this fully qualified path of this item to the clipboard. Building the SCADA views Top Building the SCADA views After creating a MAPS project, you need to construct the views of your process by organizing the equipment graphics and adding the necessary static elements. Tip1: You can resize the graphical representations of the MAPS templates (equipment items), by selecting the required image and dragging its size handles. By default, the resizing of the equipment name text is disabled, but this can be enabled by setting the TextScaling property of the TextBox control to TRUE. Tip2: Add a FileBrowser control to allow SmartUI users to display to view, edit, upload and/or delete documents pertaining to ALL the ISA S88 / S95 hierarchical levels of your MAPS project or to simply view the documents within a specific folder on the SmartUI Server computer. For details, see FileBrowser controls . Creating or recreating the default SCADA views: Immediately after creating a project, you need to create (build) ALL the applicable SCADA views for the project. If you corrupt or make a mistake when configuring these default graphic form/s, then you can perform recreate the applicable graphic forms to reset them to their default configuration. Either right

t. If you corrupt or make a mistake when configuring these default graphic form/s, then you can perform recreate the applicable graphic forms to reset them to their default configuration. Either right click the MAPS project and select Build Project and in the dialog ONLY check the Rebuild all graphics checkbox and click Finish to re/create ALL the default SCADA views in this project. This is typically used after creating a project. Or right click the applicable plant Area and select Rebuild all graphics to re/create ALL the default SCADA views in this plant Area. This is typically used if you need to recreate more than one graphic form in this plant Area. Or right click the applicable project , plant Area or unit and select Rebuild graphic to ONLY re/create this default SCADA view. This is typically used if you have corrupted or made a mistake with a single graphic form and need to reset it to its default configuration. Configuring your SCADA views: The MAPS project and each of its components provide a right click menu item to open its default graphic form. Typically, you will only edit your unit graphic forms, as follows: Right click each unit and select Open unit graphic form and

ponents provide a right click menu item to open its default graphic form. Typically, you will only edit your unit graphic forms, as follows: Right click each unit and select Open unit graphic form and re-arrange generated graphics and add the statics from the Static Graphics folder, as needed to complete your project. Note: You can preview the shapes in the Static Graphics folder by right clicking them and selecting the Preview option. Tip: Open the Templates window from the View menu to build your own custom set (library) of generally used Static Graphics . Note: When copying graphic forms, use the right click Copy with Spiders option or the CTRL+SHIFT+C shortcut, otherwise the associated functionality will NOT be provided for the equipment that you copy. Click the Save button to save your configuration of each graphic form. After configuring your SCADA views: Right click the MAPS project again and select Build Project and in the dialog ONLY check the Build Operator View

n to save your configuration of each graphic form. text: Bulk Scanning or Scanning Import Top Bulk Scanning or Scanning Import Instead of using the Tag scanning configuration dialog to configure the scanning of a large number of tags (agent.slot) for the same device, it is also possible to scan a single tag, export the scanning configuration to a spreadsheet application, perform the required bulk configuration and import this configuration. Note1: This method is ONLY recommended when adding more than 100 scan points to the same device: Note2 : Check that your communications are working before and after the importing of the scan points. Backup your Adroit database file (.WGP). For details, see Backing Up Adroit Database Files . Scan at least one tag (agent.slot) to the required device . Export the Device agent type , i.e. click the No button for all the other preceding agent type message boxes. In the Choose file to contain conversion dialog, select the location to save the Device agent files, it is recommended to leave this as the default location of the Adroit system folder, typically C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit and save the ‘Device.CSV’ file, then save the scan files for each of the device agents, of the name format Dev

cation of the Adroit system folder, typically C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit and save the ‘Device.CSV’ file, then save the scan files for each of the device agents, of the name format DeviceName-SCAN.CSV, where DeviceName is the name of the Device agent. When the next agent type message box is displayed, click Cancel , to stop the exporting process. In either a CSV or text editor, open the DeviceName-SCAN.CSV, where DeviceName is the name of the Device agent that the tags have been scanned to. This file will contain four columns or comma-separated values, from left to right as follows: Address, agent.slot, Scanning Interval (period), Deadband Note: These fields are identical to those displayed in the Currently scanned tags list, when adding a scanning a tag. For details, see Scanning Example . Add the agents and their slots that are to be scanned, their required scan addresses and if necessary the required periods and deadbands. Save and close this CSV file. Edit the required Device agent . Stop this device agent . Note: If the DeviceName-SCAN.CSV contains only new scan points, skip the following step. Remove all the scan points from this device. Click Import… button a

red Device agent . Stop this device agent . Note: If the DeviceName-SCAN.CSV contains only new scan points, skip the following step. Remove all the scan points from this device. Click Import… button and browse in the required Devicename-SCAN.CSV file, where DeviceName is the name of the selected Device agent. Note: If messages are displayed during the importing of this scanning configuration, see Common Reasons for Scanning Import Failure for the possible reasons. Start this device agent . Verify that the communications are still fine and all I/O tags work as expected. Save your Adroit database file (.WGP) again and finally perform a full test by restarting the Agent Server to verify proper loading etc. -->

Calculating statistics from Analog values Top Calculating statistics from Analog values The Analog agent can be enabled to calculate the following statistics from its value slot: sum (total), average, standard deviation, minimum, maximum and direction of change (trend). These statistics are only calculated, when the Integer statsPeriod slot is set to the number of minutes that you want the value slot to be recorded for statistical evaluation. This is a "rolling" period, which specifies the maximum sampling time from "now" (the current time) into the past for the specified period. In this case the value slot is recorded every second over this timespan and the statistics are calculated from these recorded values. IMPORTANT: Since the calculation of these statistics can affect performance if used excessively, please ensure that you ONLY calculate statistics for the Analog values you need them for. Setting the statsPeriod slot to 0 (the default value) disables the calculation of these statistics for an Analog agent. Tip: You can use the Statistical period (mins), 0 to disable field of the configuration dialog to configure this statsPeriod slot for an Analog agent. These statistics are

istics for an Analog agent. Tip: You can use the Statistical period (mins), 0 to disable field of the configuration dialog to configure this statsPeriod slot for an Analog agent. These statistics are saved into the following slots of the Analog agent, so that they can be separately reported, as needed: Note: If necessary, you can reset these statistical calculations by setting the Boolean statsReset slot to 1 (True) which clears the recorded values. statsAverage : The average of all the recorded values. statsMax : The highest recorded value. statsMin : The lowest recorded value. statsStdDev : The standard deviation of all the recorded values. statsSum : The total of all the recorded values. statsDirection : This compares the newest recorded value (the current value slot) to the oldest recorded value and displays the results of this comparison, so that you can determine the general direction in which it is changing (its trend) as follows: 0 typically means that the value has not changed. 1 if the current value is higher, so that the trend of the value is moving up -1 if the current value is lower, so that the trend of the value is moving down. However, you can also specify an option

. 1 if the current value is higher, so that the trend of the value is moving up -1 if the current value is lower, so that the trend of the value is moving down. However, you can also specify an optional minimum deviation or deadband to ensure that this trending direction only indicates significant changes in value. In this case set the statsDirDev slot, to the required decimal percentage value (a value from 0 to 1) so that deviations in value less than or equal to this specified percentage result in the statsDirection slot being set to 0 meaning “no change”. For instance, if you set the statsDirDev slot to 0.10, then only when the newest recorded value differs from the oldest recorded value by more than 10 % will the statsDirection slot display whether the current value is higher (1) or lower (-1). -->

Calculations in Expressions Top Calculations in Expressions Examples of expressions . An expression can be thought of as a collection of terms associated by mathematical operators, which are evaluated in a strict order of precedence. Mathematical Operators . Mathematical Functions . This order can be overridden by using brackets. Each term of the expression is composed of primary elements, which can either be signed (or complemented) numbers or variables (v1 to v20, and v99 which is equivalent to "value"), or sub-expressions. This recursive definition of an expression means that expressions can be nested to any level of complexity. Note: v1, V1, v01 and V01 are all valid representations of the input slots. Each Expression agent contains an expression field in which you enter an ANSI-C expression string. The expression can include spaces, round brackets and new line characters for clarity, as well as C and C++ style comments after the expression to document its purpose (i.e. // comment or /* comment */). Note: It is not advisable to use the slots of scan agents in expressions, since the names of these agents are not fixed, but are changed by Adroit according to the scanning configur

or /* comment */). Note: It is not advisable to use the slots of scan agents in expressions, since the names of these agents are not fixed, but are changed by Adroit according to the scanning configuration. -->
