Catch-up Top Catch-up When a new server is added to the cluster, it must become a mirror image of the active member of the cluster. The new server must restore its historical data (historical catch-up) that it lost during the down time. This historical synchronization or Datalog catch-up is facilitated by a new agent called the SystemDatalog agent . Note: For performance reasons, the SystemDatalog agent ONLY provides the Time datalog catchup method, of catching up the data between two specified date/times. Note: Datalog catch-up is not supported when OLE DB logging is being used as this would only further delay a task which is already time consuming and CPU intensive. As OLE DB logging is logging to a database, this database could be equipped with the querying/replication tools required to fill any holes that exist. Historical data catch up of the newly added standby server -->

Changing data element referencing Top Changing data element referencing By default the namespace one or more names separated by periods (or dots), where each name represents an individual item and the entire namespace indicates the relationship or lineage of the leftmost term i.e. grandparent.parent.child. of a data element (and its Data Element spider) specifies the SmartUI Server that it is located on, which definitively describes a data element but is also very inflexible. For this reason, it is possible to specify how the SmartUI Server component of this naming convention is specified for each Server that provides data into or out of a spider workspace. Click for more information: The default data element (and Data Element spider) unambiguous naming convention: [MACHINENAME] ServerName.DatasourceName.[datasource-specific structure].itemName Although, this convention definitively describes a data element it is also very inflexible. For instance if the same SmartUI Server is located on a different computer then this namespace will no longer be valid and its associated Data Element spider will not connect to this data, unless it is removed and the data is reconnected manually. Each charting control displays one or more series, as follows: BarChart : Each charted series is either a series of horizontal bars representing values or a series of points that are usually connected to form lines. ColumnChart : Each charted series is either a series of vertical columns representing values or a series of points that are usually connected to form lines. LineChart : Each charted series is a series of points that are usually connected to form lines. PieChart : Each charted series is a series of slices or segments to form a complete pie or circle. XYPlotChart : Each charted series is a series of points that are plotted from two sets of values, one providing the X or horizontal coordinate and the other providing the Y or vertical coordinate of each point. on shadowing: Check this checkbox to copy (shadow) all the transactions initiated by a client on a server to the other server in the cluster to provide total data replication. Code to enable ImageList component usage Top Code to implement the ImageList component The Imagelist component is a graphic form component that can be added to a graphic form from the Windows Forms category of the Toolbox window. This component maintains a developer-provided list of images typically for use with controls that need to display more than one image. For instance, this can be used to provide images for the different states of a button. Before the Imagelist component can be used, however, it needs to be associated with the control(s) on this graphic form that will use it. This association can be performed programmatically, by adding code to the Form_Load event of a graphic form. Command-line Options for Driver Monitor Top Command-line Options for the Driver Monitor The following options can typically be either entered into the Command line options edit box in the Options menu of the Driver Monitor Launcher and allows you to further customise this application for your specific requirements: /A This option toggles the output display of the Datascope screen between the default hexadecimal (binary) format and ASCII format Tip: We recommend that you ALWAYS display the Datascope in ASCII format, even for known Binary(hex) type protocols, because the newer drivers provide extra information usually in a readable (English) format and also convert the hexadecimal display to ASCII to remain compatible. For further details, see Datascope screen . /L This option will log the communication messages and errors as they occur between Adroit and the specified front-end device. The logged information is typically stored in a .TXT file with the same name as the device name. The following additional options can be used in conjunction with this /L option: /F <filename> This sub-option allows you to specify the name of the file that is used to log the Datascope screen e.g. /Ferr

ollowing additional options can be used in conjunction with this /L option: /F <filename> This sub-option allows you to specify the name of the file that is used to log the Datascope screen e.g. /Ferrors.txt specifies a file called 'errors.txt' /T This sub-option adds timestamps to the logged data, so that time at which the data is logged to file will also be recorded. /H This option logs the device-specific communication messages and errors to an HTML page to preserve the color of the datascope to make the troubleshooting process easier. The output file created by this option has the same name as the device name and a .HTM extension. Note: The log files created by the /L and /H options are located in the folder in which this utility is launched. This is usually the Adroit system folder (typically C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit ) otherwise open the properties of the shortcut used to launch this application to determine this folder. WARNING! Both the /L and /H options will append to an existing log file, which has no size limitation and so can consume all the free disk space, unless these log files are properly managed. /N This will suppress the warning that usually app

append to an existing log file, which has no size limitation and so can consume all the free disk space, unless these log files are properly managed. /N This will suppress the warning that usually appears when more than one Datascope window is opened on a computer. /G This only applies to GST drivers and is used to open up a specialised diagnostics screen. /SCREENn This will automatically open the specified screen. Where: /SCREEN1 = Datascope. /SCREEN2 = Diagnostic Counters. /SCREEN3 = Error Log. /SCREEN4 = GST FEP scope – this is only available when the /G option is used for GST drivers. A usage example of these options /A /SCREEN1 /L /T /Ferrors.txt This will automatically log the Datascope output in ACSII with times, to the file called errors.txt, without requiring any user interaction! -->

Common Device Configuration Top Common Device Configuration Although the dialog displayed when adding or configuring a device is protocol driver specific, this dialog will generally contain the following groups of configuration parameters: Note: This protocol driver configuration for each device is saved in the system registry; therefore it is necessary to reconfigure the devices if they are to be run on another computer. For further details, see About Protocol Drivers . The rates at which the scanning or communication occurs can be defined for the individual I/O ports. Primary and secondary parameters Each device contains primary and secondary parameters that define the available connection channels (or routes) and parameters. The secondary information is optional and is used in the event of a failure on the primary connection, or vice versa. How this secondary port works is simple, if the driver is using the primary configuration parameters and the communication fails, the driver will switch over to (and re-initialise) the secondary port and continue communicating via it if possible. Once the primary port becomes available again, the driver may be forced into reverting to it by b

l switch over to (and re-initialise) the secondary port and continue communicating via it if possible. Once the primary port becomes available again, the driver may be forced into reverting to it by breaking the secondary port link, long enough to force the driver to do the switch back. This cycle may be repeated as often as fault conditions occur. Communication Failure Handling . PLC Details This group of details relates to how to address the FED (front-end device), and will contain details such as routing information or ID’s on a multi-drop that is specific to the FED’s protocol. Necessary details such as the model in the range may appear here. Selecting the incorrect model will most often cause problems. Local Details Port configuration parameters are often required by a driver to allow it to decide which port to use on the Adroit computer. Any additional parameters in this group will show default settings that may need to be changed. Only parameters that are configurable on the FED will be shown here. In other words, if the FED does not support different baud-rates, this setting will not be optional in our driver. Related topics: Add Device -->

Common Reasons for Scanning Import Failure Top Common Reasons for Scanning Import Failure When importing scanned tags (agent.slot) from the CSV Comma Separated Value file containing data, which consists of a number of fields in one or more rows, in which the different fields (values) are typically separated by commas. file, the following messages may be displayed: "Invalid device address" or "slot already scanned". For details on importing scanned tags, see Bulk Scanning . These messages appear in either of 4 known cases: The scan-tag you wanted to scan does not exist (the slot may be missing or the tag may not exist). Ensure that the tag already exists. The scan-address is not recognised/interpretable by the driver. Try a different address or read the driver documentation that was installed with the driver. The slot you tried to scan is already scanned. Edit the tag, click on header, and then click Advanced, select the desired slot from the list; to see if the "scanned" header bit is on for any specific slot. The operation timed out! The operation may still succeed however, close and re-open the Configurator to check. This occurs only after about 10 seconds of waiting with an hour

text: on for any specific slot. The operation timed out! The operation may still succeed however, close and re-open the Configurator to check. This occurs only after about 10 seconds of waiting with an hourglass mouse cursor. Stopping the device or reducing scan backlog helps reduce this occurrence. text: Common Status bits Top Common Status bits The overall status of an agent can be determined from its status slot, which is a 32 bit word containing configuration and run-time status information about the agent, each bit of which is also exposed as a slot. For details, see Agent Status . The first 16 bits (0 to 15) are known as the Common Status bits as they are common across all agent types, each bit has a fixed purpose. Their equivalent slots each have unique slotname, which follows the naming convention of statusXxxxxxXxxxxx. e.g. statusScanBad. These Common Status bits are further classified into control, condition and configuration groups, as follows: Note1: These are NOT contiguous groupings of bits, for instance the first bit statusBit00 is a condition bit NOT a control bit! Note2: The first bit in the status word, statusBad , is the only bit an application needs to monitor to determine the integrity of an agent or slot. For details, see Agent or Slot Integrity Monitoring (Bad Handling) . The first group is called Control bits, which can be modified by the user. Each bit can therefore be set or reset by the user, to control an agent’s operator, logging, alarming, and scanning

dling) . The first group is called Control bits, which can be modified by the user. Each bit can therefore be set or reset by the user, to control an agent’s operator, logging, alarming, and scanning functionality. The second group is called Condition bits, which are not directly modifiable by the user, and may only be viewed. They report on an agent’s integrity and alarm state, etc. Note: All agent Specific Status bits are also Condition bits, since they are not directly modifiable by the user. The third group is called the Configuration bits, which are also not directly modifiable by the user, since they only provide configuration information about an agent, namely whether or not it has been scanned and/or alarmed. -->

Condition Bits (not directly modifiable by the user) Top Condition Bits (not directly modifiable by the user) Condition Bits fan-in, which means that an agent condition bit is automatically set to 1 whenever one of the corresponding slot condition bits is set to 1. The converse, however, is not true, i.e. an agent condition bit being set to 1 does not cause the corresponding slot condition bits to be automatically set to 1. Note: The condition bit fan-in uses positive logic: only one slot bit needs to be set for the corresponding agent bit to be set, and resetting a slot bit does not necessarily cause the corresponding agent bit to be reset (because the corresponding bit for another slot may be set). Because the agent bit might have been set by the user or system - and we don’t want to lose this information - all agent condition bit values are derived by combining slot condition bits with the agent condition bits. For this purpose, the agent status retains a raw and a derived status word. If an agent bit is therefore set before one of its slot bit are set, it would still remain set when all slot bits are reset. Bad . Connection Bad . Alarm(s) Unacknowledged . Subscriptions active .

CMD StartReg Data 00 01 00 02 00 03 00 65 00 00 01 06 Write Request device Bytes Command StartReg Range Data 01 05 66 00 00 01 00 7F Write Response device bytes Command StartReg 07 00 xx Xx xx device = (OID) of the targeted device on the Conet network. Bytes = number of bytes in the telegram, excluding the first three. Command code: 64h = 100 etc. StartReg = offset into the DIT table from which data is to be read or to which data must be written. Configuration Problems Top Configuration Problems The most commonly experienced fault in the first-time use of any communications link is incorrect configuration. In many cases, a single resource is used to communicate to multiple devices. Serial communications When configuring serial communications of any type, be sure to specify the correct data and stop-bit settings if available for selection. If these settings are unknown, then the documentation for the remote device should be examined to find out the following information: whether the settings are fixed and unchangeable whether they exist as dipswitch settings whether the devices are software configurable In the case of dipswitches or software configuration, it may be necessary to re-start the device for the settings to take effect. Because some of our older serial protocol drivers do not interpret error codes and translate them to English, I include a brief listing of serial communications error codes. These codes are separate from the Win32 codes. They can also be OR'ed together, and for that reason we supply the hex values here. 0x0001 = Receive Queue overflow 0x0002 = Receive Overrun Error 0x0004 = Receive Parity Error 0x0

om the Win32 codes. They can also be OR'ed together, and for that reason we supply the hex values here. 0x0001 = Receive Queue overflow 0x0002 = Receive Overrun Error 0x0004 = Receive Parity Error 0x0008 = Receive Framing error 0x0010 = Break Detected 0x0100 = TX Queue is full 0x0200 = LPTx Timeout 0x0400 = LPTx I/O Error 0x0800 = LPTx Device not selected 0x1000 = LPTx Out-Of-Paper 0x8000 = Requested mode unsupported (e.g. An error value of 12 is equal to 8 + 4 which means "Receive parity" and "Receive framing" error.) Networks If the communications are via a protocol such as TCP/IP, NetBIOS or other LAN protocol, the resource may be connected to the existing office LAN. To eliminate the possibility of interference, a "private" network should be created to reduce the chances of poor network termination or excessive traffic causing problems. Networking programs and Adroit protocol drivers rely on certain network drivers being operational before they can run. If this is the case, you will have to install any networking protocols required in the documentation. If the front-end computer is using one protocol, the Adroit scanning station must be running similar or compatible network lay

If the front-end computer is using one protocol, the Adroit scanning station must be running similar or compatible network layers before communication can be established. To see which network software you have loaded in Windows, you must open the Network Connections in the Control Panel , select the existing network connection, right-click and select Properties , select the software component and network card in question in this dialog, and click on the Configure button. Also check that there are no disabled networking software components. -->

Forecolor : specify the color of the tool tip text Font : specify the font of the tool tip text. Initial Delay : specify the delay, in milliseconds, after which the tool tip is triggered to be displayed to prevent the unintended display of this tool tip text. Auto Pop Delay : specify how long, in milliseconds, this tool tip should be displayed before it closes. Anchor : select the required position on the form component to display the tool tip from the available options. If you choose Custom then use the Location input to specify the offsets relative to the Top, Left corner, in pixels. If you want to add one or more values or other variables to the tool tip text: Dou

If you choose Custom then use the Location input to specify the offsets relative to the Top, Left corner, in pixels. If you want to add one or more values or other variables to the tool tip text: Double click the + New Input to add their placeholder inputs, typically 0, 1, 2 etc. Then link the required values to these inputs to dynamically provide the values of these inputs. Type in the required Text input and manually add any value placeholder that you want to display in this text, these placeholders take the form of the respective input number enclosed in braces '{}', for instance '{0}'for input 0. The first untitled field is the index of the periods of time in the grid. Start datetime: This column can specify the date and/or time at which this period of time is scheduled to commence. The default value is the current date and time. If this is left blank, then this cell is disabled and all date/times are valid. End datetime: This column can specify the date and/or time at which this period of time is scheduled to end. The default value is the current date and time. If this is left blank, then this cell is disabled and all date/times are valid. Click the cell of the required column and configure it, as follows: Note: To ONLY specify a time and NOT a date, then enter the following date: 1 /1 / 1970 Either click the downward arrow of the list box and use the supplied calendar to select the required date; the current date is selected by default. Or click in the list box, over the required date and time digits to select them, then either type in the required unit or use the spin control arrows to increase or decrease the value accordingly. Note1: Only numbers can be typed in and if the number that is entered is too great for the specified unit it will be disregarded Note2: The date and time is displayed as per the Regional Settings of the computer. Weekdays: This column can specify the days of the week, which need to be included during this scheduled period of time. By default all the days of the week are included. Click the cell of this column and configure it, as follows: Click the downward arrow on the right of this cell. Note: If no Weekdays are selected then this entire scheduled period entry is disabled. Configuring Accumulator Agents Top Configuring Accumulator Agents You are typically required to configure an Accumulator agent to analyse an accumulating process value and to calculate its difference in value (or change) between successive events or over a specific time (interval) . To do this, click on and read each of the following options: 1. Open the Accumulator agent dialog First, open the Edit Accumulator Agent dialog as follows: Select the name of this agent. For details, see To Select an Agent . If an agent does not exist, you may add an Accumulator agent. For details, see To Add a New Agent . Right-click and select the Edit option to display the Edit Accumulator Agent dialog. 2. Define the accumulating value In the Edit Accumulator Agent dialog, you can specify the accumulating process value that you want to monitor and assess, in one of the following two ways: Find the inputTag property, click the browse button then select the slot which represents the ever-increasing process value. In this case, the selected value of this tag will be assigned to the inputValue slot. If the inputTag slot is NOT specified, then you need to drive the inputValue slot, typically by scanning t

value. In this case, the selected value of this tag will be assigned to the inputValue slot. If the inputTag slot is NOT specified, then you need to drive the inputValue slot, typically by scanning this to the required accumulating process variable stored on the front-end device or using a script or expression. 3. Specify how you want each period to be defined Typically, you define a constant interval of time over which the differential increases in value is calculated. The agent provides you with the ability to select the method you’d prefer to use. You do this on the intervalMode slot property, as follows: Note: The triggerNow slot (and button) performs a manual end of period, which is effective in any mode selected by this intervalMode slot. IntervalMode options 0 - 2 These first three interval options use the intervalTag , which is a tag you can browse to set when the end of an interval has occurred: 0 = Interval tag value goes to zero The end of the interval occurs when the value of the intervalTag changes from any non-zero value to a value of zero [0]. 1 = Interval value goes (from zero) to non-zero The end of the interval occurs when the value of the intervalTag changes fro

of the intervalTag changes from any non-zero value to a value of zero [0]. 1 = Interval value goes (from zero) to non-zero The end of the interval occurs when the value of the intervalTag changes from a value of zero [0] to any non-zero value. 2 = Any interval tag value change The end of the interval occurs when the value of the intervalTag changes in value to any other value (a different value from its current value). IntervalMode options 3 - 4 The next two options let you to define the required interval by making use of the system time (the time of the Agent Server computer) and the interval slot, which specifies the duration of each period in minutes: 3 = Synchronised (to clock - default) The agent forces the periods to be synchronised with the system time (i.e. the time of the Agent Server computer) . Therefore, the initial period of the current hour always begins at the start of the current hour (0 seconds or 0 minutes) which is how the current period is calculated when this agent is enabled. As an example, if you have an interval of 10 minutes, the first period of this hour starts on the current hour to 10 minutes past the hour; the second period of this hour starts at 10 mi

t is enabled. As an example, if you have an interval of 10 minutes, the first period of this hour starts on the current hour to 10 minutes past the hour; the second period of this hour starts at 10 minutes past the hour and end at 20 minutes past the hour, and so on. A further example, if the agent is set to use the intervalMode of 3 with an interval of 10 minutes and the agent is enabled at 10:02, then the first period will end at 10:10 for this mode (a partial interval of only 8 minutes to enforce the ending time of this period, which began at 10:00 even though the agent was only enabled at 10:02) . However, if this same agent is enabled at 10:45, then the first period will end at 10:50 for this mode (a partial interval of only 5 minutes to enforce the ending time of the current period, which began at 10:40). Important: If you are using this method, then you need to ensure that the specified interval is divisible into 60 or is a multiple of 60 otherwise period timing errors will occur. 4 = Not synchronised (to clock) The agent sets the starting time of the periods to the exact time that this agent is enabled and calculates all the successive periods by adding the specified interv

r. 4 = Not synchronised (to clock) The agent sets the starting time of the periods to the exact time that this agent is enabled and calculates all the successive periods by adding the specified interval number of minutes to this starting time. For example, if the agent is set to use the intervalMode of 4 with an interval of 10 minutes and this agent is enabled at 10:02, then the first period will end at 10:12 for this mode (a full interval from the starting time) and the next period will end at 10:22, and so on. IntervalMode option 5 If you choose the final option then you typically need to devise a method of driving the triggerNow slot via a script or expression or this agent can calculate the differential value whenever you choose to. 5 = Manual trigger The rate of change and its alarm limits only applies when using periods that have regular intervals. 4. Configure the required alarm limits and if necessary their deadband If necessary, you can configure the alarm limits and the deadband when required, for this differential value, and the rate of change of this differential value over the specified period. Tip: The deadband slot is used to desensitise these alarm limits and preven

and when required, for this differential value, and the rate of change of this differential value over the specified period. Tip: The deadband slot is used to desensitise these alarm limits and prevent unnecessary alarms if the value is oscillating. In other words, this specifies the ‘band’ (size of) the ‘dead’ area outside these alarm limits, which the value must reduce by before the alarm is cleared. Important: The deadband slot ONLY applies to the alarm limits for the differential value and NOT to the rate of change alarm limits. When the value reaches or exceeds this alarm limit, the VHighHigh status bit is set to [1] (enabled) , which can be alarmed using the VHighHigh default alarm type. The valueHi alarm limit specifies the first alarm limit for a high value , which if reached, should require corrective action as soon as possible. When the value reaches or exceeds this alarm li

type. The valueHi alarm limit specifies the first alarm limit for a high value , which if reached, should require corrective action as soon as possible. When the value reaches or exceeds this alarm limit, the VHigh status bit is set to [1] (enabled) , which can be alarmed using the VHigh default alarm type. The valueLo alarm limit specifies the first alarm limit for a low value , which if reached, should require corrective action as soon as possible. When the value is lower or equal to this alarm limit is reached, the VLow status bit is set to [1] (enabled) , which can be alarmed using the VLow default alarm type. The valueLoLo alarm limit specifies the second alarm limit for a low value , which if reached, should typically require urgent and immediate corrective action. When the value is lower or equal to this alarm limit is reached, the VLowLow status bit is set to [1] (enabled) , which can be alarmed using the VLowLow default alarm type Note: Whenever the Low-low alarm is on, the Low alarm must, by definition also be on. Similarly, whenever the High-high limit is reached, the High limit will already have been passed. Rate of change The following alarm limits can be defined for t

w alarm must, by definition also be on. Similarly, whenever the High-high limit is reached, the High limit will already have been passed. Rate of change The following alarm limits can be defined for the rate of change of this differential value over the specified period in the Rate alarm levels section of the properties dialog: Note: The deadband slot does NOT apply to these rate alarm limits. The rateHiHi alarm limit specifies the second alarm limit for a high rate , which if reached, should typically require urgent and immediate corrective action. When the rate reaches or exceeds this alarm limit, the RHighHigh status bit is set to [1] (enabled) , which can be alarmed using the RHighHigh default alarm type. The rateHi alarm limit specifies the first alarm limit for a high rate , which if reached, should require corrective action as soon as possible. When the rate reaches or exceeds this alarm limit, the RHigh status bit is set to [1] (enabled) , which can be alarmed using the RHigh default alarm type. The rateLo alarm limit specifies the first alarm limit for a low rate , which if reached, should require corrective action as soon as possible. When the rate is lower or equal to th

efault alarm type. The rateLo alarm limit specifies the first alarm limit for a low rate , which if reached, should require corrective action as soon as possible. When the rate is lower or equal to this alarm limit is reached, the RLow status bit is set to [1] (enabled) , which can be alarmed using the RLow default alarm type. The rateLoLo alarm limit specifies the second alarm limit for a low rate , which if reached, should typically require urgent and immediate corrective action. When the rate is lower or equal to this alarm limit is reached, the RLowLow status bit is set to [1] (enabled) , which can be alarmed using the RLowLow default alarm type. 5. Configure the SQL Server database to store the values of each period To maintain a history of the differential values for each period you must specify the SQL Server database and table that is used to store these records: Specify the connection string to this SQL Server database in the connection field by using the Data Link Properties dialog. For more details, see Creating a SQL Server database connection string . Note: If you specify global , the Global OLE DB connection string of the Agent Server is used, which is specified in th

dialog. For more details, see Creating a SQL Server database connection string . Note: If you specify global , the Global OLE DB connection string of the Agent Server is used, which is specified in the Adroit Config Editor . Typically, you can launch this tool from the Desktop shortcut. Select the Agent Server Configuration Welcome menu item. Select the Advanced Agent Server Configuration option. At the bottom of the dialog, the Global OLE DB connection field is available for you to specify this connection string. Specify the required table name in this database to store these records in the tableName field. By default, this table name is set to the name of this Accumulator agent. When you are using a clustered Agent Server, then the standby clustered partner will, by default, not log these records to this database, thus preventing duplicate records. However, you can change this, if required, by configuring the disableOnStandby slot setting. Each record specifies a unique index (idx) ; the date and time at which the period ended (dt) ; the differential value (value) and the inputValue - the value of the accumulating process variable (accumulator) at this time. If a valid connection

the date and time at which the period ended (dt) ; the differential value (value) and the inputValue - the value of the accumulating process variable (accumulator) at this time. If a valid connection and table is specified, the History table will be created as follows: Column name Type Description idx Int Auto incrementing index dt datetime Period end date and time value float Calculated value for period accumulator float The accumulator reading (inputValue) at the end of the period If you want automatic management of this data, then specify how many days worth of data you want this table to store in the housekeepDays field, to ensure that you keep the most relevant (most recent) records only. Note: The default value of 0 disables this functionality. 6. Enable the agent To start analysing the accumulating process: You should enable this agent to start analysing the accumulating process value and calculate its differential value for each period and its rate of change and, if required, also log the values of each period to the specified history table in the SQL Server database. To enable this agent, set the enable slot of this agent (in the General section of this properties dialog)

also log the values of each period to the specified history table in the SQL Server database. To enable this agent, set the enable slot of this agent (in the General section of this properties dialog) to True. 7. Values calculated by the agent for each period At the end of every period: The differential value of the previous period is saved to lastValue . The differential value of the current completed period is calculated as: inputValue - startValue. The rate of change of the previous differential value and period is calculated as: lastValue * 60 (minutes per hour) / (last period length in minutes) = value per hour. A new record is added to the tableName (in the database by connection , if specified) containing the period start and end times, values and differential value and rate for the period. A new period will commence immediately and the startValue will be assigned to the inputValue . Tip: You can view the amount of time that has passed (elapsed) from the start of the current period, in minutes, by viewing the elapsedTime slot. -->

Configuring AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer columns Configuring AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer columns The AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer control allows you to choose which columns are displayed, their order and their specific properties via the Columns tab of the Initial Configuration and the Columns Configuration and General Configuration Settings dialogs, as follows: To display or hide a column: check or uncheck the checkbox in the Columns list on the left. To change the order of the displayed columns: select the required column in the Columns list on the left and then click the or arrow to move it up or down as required. To edit the properties of a column: select the required column in the Columns list on the left and then modify the required property in the Column Properties section on the right. The Best Fit Columns checkbox is checked by default to force all the displayed columns in the grid to automatically resize their widths so that their contents fit in the control without requiring any horizontal scrolling. Available column properties: Property Configuration DisplayName changes the name of the column heading in the grid. BestFit determines whether the column auto-sizes (if True)

ny horizontal scrolling. Available column properties: Property Configuration DisplayName changes the name of the column heading in the grid. Configuring Agent Server auditing Top Configuring Agent Server Auditing The configuration settings that enable the auditing of the Agent Server and that specify the required OLE DB The open standard for accessing data from a variety of sources. An OLE DB data provider is required, before a database can become OLE DB compliant. compatible database are located in the Server auditing group section of the Advanced Agent Server Configuration dialog. To display the auditing configuration settings: Using the Adroit Config Editor : Launch the Adroit Config Editor . Click Agent Server Configuration in the right hand pane. Click Advanced Agent Server Configuration in the right hand pane. This displays a page of grouped advanced Agent Server settings. To specify the auditing database: to select the OLE DB compatible database that will store the audit records for this Agent Server. By default an MS Access database file is used. If necessary, display the auditing configuration settings (see above). By default, if the Custom OLE DB connection field is left blank and the Agent Server is started then a MS Access database file, called adroit_audit.MDB, is created in the Work subfolder of the design

By default, if the Custom OLE DB connection field is left blank and the Agent Server is started then a MS Access database file, called adroit_audit.MDB, is created in the Work subfolder of the designated project folder, which is typically C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Configurations\Default \Work. Tip1: It is recommended to use this default database, since this is a single file that can easily be backed up elsewhere. Tip2: If necessary, you can secure this Access database and provide the user/password details in the connection string. Click the browse button to the left of the Custom OLE DB connection field to specify another OLE DB compatible database. For details, see Connecting to an OLE DB database . For instance, you can use a central SQL database for all the Agent Servers on your network, since the identification (Session ID) used for the logged events contain the name of the computer and Agent Server. In this case, if you do not have SQL installed then you can install MS SQL EXPRESS. To stop auditing the Agent Server: this prevents additional records from being added to the auditing database If necessary, display the auditing configuration settings (see above).

ll MS SQL EXPRESS. To stop auditing the Agent Server: this prevents additional records from being added to the auditing database If necessary, display the auditing configuration settings (see above). Clear the Enable checkbox, which is enabled by default. Tip: If you want to analyse your audited data then, we recommend that you install the Adroit Report Suite and specifically the Audit Reports report pack, which provides you with the necessary tools you need to analyse both your Agent Server auditing and tag auditing, where Agent Server auditing includes any activities on the Agent Server, while the tag auditing is concerned specifically with data logged by any Audit agents. Configuring Automatic WGP File Backups Top Configuring Automatic WGP File Backups Adroit WGP files can be automatically backed up when they are saved to ensure that at most only the changes made since the last save will be lost. WARNING! This feature is merely intended to AUGMENT the existing backup system and NOT to REPLACE it i.e. it is still imperative that an efficient backup system is in place! For details, see Creating Backup Procedures . Note: These backup files will be created in the folder in which the WGP file resides, EACH time it is saved, regardless as to whether its contents have been changed or not. To configure automatic WGP file backups Using the Adroit Config Editor : Launch the Adroit Config Editor . Click Agent Server Configuration in the right hand pane. Click Advanced Agent Server Configuration in the right hand pane. This displays a page of grouped advanced Agent Server settings. The following settings are contained within the WGP Versioning group: These files are created when the WGP file is saved for the period of time specified by the Delete WGP backup files older than # days edit box, where # is the required number of days. The default period is 90 days a

e created when the WGP file is saved for the period of time specified by the Delete WGP backup files older than # days edit box, where # is the required number of days. The default period is 90 days and any backup WGP file older than this time will be deleted every time the WGP file is saved. Tip: It is recommended to set this value to the period of your existing Adroit backups, so as to avoid backup duplication. Note: A value of 0 will disable this feature and remove all the backup files on the next save. The minimum number of backup files that will always remain can be specified using the … but keep a minimum of # backup files edit box, where # is the required number of files. This should be used as a failsafe to prevent ALL the previous backups from being deleted if the WGP file is saved after the period specified by the Delete WGP backup files older than # days edit box has elapsed. The default minimum number of files is 3, which ensures that the folder will always contain the 3 most recent backups. The total number of backup file that are created can be limited, by specifying the required number in the … and a maximum limit of # files edit box, where # is the required number o

st recent backups. The total number of backup file that are created can be limited, by specifying the required number in the … and a maximum limit of # files edit box, where # is the required number of files. In this way it is possible to regulate the amount of disk space that is used for these backups. The default number of files is 10, after which the oldest backup file will be deleted each time the WGP file is saved. Note: A value of 0 will remove this limitation, so that a separate backup file will be created each time the WGP file is saved for the specified number of days. For further details, such as the naming format of these automatically created backup copies, see Automatic WGP File Backups . -->

If the Operator tag settings are configured for these categories and the TANK_1_LEVEL.High incident occurs within the Tank01 category (level 4 in the category hierarchy). Then this incident is logged to the database with the operator name of Jaco , as this is the CLOSEST configured Operator tag for this i

Configuring colored value ranges for gauges Top Configuring colored value ranges for gauges If you like you can add colored value ranges to a Gauge control, these can be added to help your operators to immediately determine in which general range of values the current value is which needing to study the gauge closely. text: Configuring Command Agents Top Configuring Command Agents The Command agent can receive textual commands in SMS messages that it is able to remotely configure or "command" Adroit . SMS messages can also be sent either manually or automatically and, if necessary, be sent via another Command agent to another recipient, such as a colleague or escalated up the management chain. This agent requires a device of the GSM_SMS protocol driver, to be added and correctly configured, in order to send and receive SMS messages. For details, see Specifying the GSM_SMS Device . Each Command agent is able to send SMS messages to a single recipient. For details see, Sending SMS Messages or for details on specifying this required phone number, see Specifying the Recipient Phone Number . Note: When the Resend message checkbox is cleared (its default setting) a message will ONLY be sent if the rawvalue of this agent HAS changed when dialog is either updated or closed. This effectively prevents the resending of identical messages. Sent SMS messages can be monitored for auditing purposes and if they are not received and/or responded to within a specified period can also be sent to another recipient via an

of identical messages. Sent SMS messages can be monitored for auditing purposes and if they are not received and/or responded to within a specified period can also be sent to another recipient via another Command agent, which can be used to escalate this message up the management chain, if necessary. For details, see Monitoring Message Receipt and Monitoring Message Response . Note: Although Command agents can also receive SMS messages from their recipient, one or more additional cell phone numbers can also be specified that are able to send SMS messages to it. For details, see Specifying Additional Callers . If a Command agent is required to receive COMMANDS within these received messages, this must be MANUALLY ENABLED. Since once enabled, these commands can be used to obtain and/or control any process value or slot exposed by the Agent Server. For details, see Allowing Commands to be Performed or for details of the available commands that can be performed, see Available Commands . PLEASE NOTE: Once a Command agent is configured to receive commands, scan point licenses are consumed by every unique phone number specified by this agent and/or used to send SMS messages to it. Note:

LEASE NOTE: Once a Command agent is configured to receive commands, scan point licenses are consumed by every unique phone number specified by this agent and/or used to send SMS messages to it. Note: Pseudonyms and macros can also be created to simply the process of specifying these commands by acting as placeholders for part or all of a textual command that is sent to a Command agent. For details, see Using Pseudonyms and Macros . If necessary, it is also possible to configure the following Command agent–specific settings: To specify default format used for displaying real numbers in sent messages . In the Inputs section: Note1: The value of these inputs can either be supplied by another spider or Data spider (e.g. property or data element) via a silk or it can be typed in manually. g. If necessary, use the Minimum and Maximum inputs to specify the range within which a numerical value MUST be specified. Configuring DBLog Agents Top Configuring DBLog Agents Tip: Typically you need to separate the Analog and Digital tags that you want to log into different DBLog agents, due to their unique logging requirements. The DBLog configuration dialog is divided into the following sections: The top checkboxes that determine the general operation of this agent: The Enable checkbox (the BOOLEAN start slot), which allows you to start/stop this agent from logging the listed tags. The Disable on standby checkbox (the BOOLEAN disableOnStandby slot), which allows you to disable this agent, when its Agent Server is part of a cluster and is in standby node - to prevent the logging of DUPLICATE tags. The String logging checkbox (the BOOLEAN strLog slot), when enabled logs the tag values as Strings and not numeric values; this also allows you to log other string slots (this will log the first 79 characters). Note: While DBLog agents typically log Numerical and Digital values or bits, they can be configured to convert ALL values to Strings, by checking the String logging checkbox - but this is NOT recommended for general use, since it requires MORE SPACE to store String values compared to Numerical value

to convert ALL values to Strings, by checking the String logging checkbox - but this is NOT recommended for general use, since it requires MORE SPACE to store String values compared to Numerical values and this can also cause formatting problems. Then the selected Logging method determines which parameters are required and when the list of tags are logged, as follows: Log all on interval : all the listed tags are logged at the specified Logging interval regardless of whether they have changed or not and regardless of their quality. Tip: This method is typically used when logging Analog values. Log on change : only the tags that change are logged, typically when their value or quality status changes. IMPORTANT: To prevent this logging method from logging the tags when their quality status changes, add the following registry value and set it to 1: DisableOnQualityChangeLogging . Note: Only this method allows for the logging of historical putslots. Log all on change : all the listed tags are logged if ANY tag value changes. Note: Tags are ONLY logged when a value of ANY listed tag changes. Log all on trigger value -> zero : all the listed tags are logged when the value of the specifie

are logged if ANY tag value changes. Note: Tags are ONLY logged when a value of ANY listed tag changes. Log all on trigger value -> zero : all the listed tags are logged when the value of the specified Trigger tag goes to zero. Log all on trigger value -> non-zero : all the listed tags are logged when the value of the specified Trigger tag leaves zero. Log all on trigger any value change :all the listed tags are logged when the value of the specified Trigger tag changes value. IMPORTANT: When selecting the Log all on interval method, do NOT add more than 5000 agents to the DBLog agent , otherwise ALL the logged values are ALWAYS be dumped to a .SQL file and not be logged directly to the database, since the total number of logged values exceeds the maximum queue size (5000). More detail: This agent provides a queue of values waiting to be logged to the specified database (or buffer), when the number of items in this queue exceeds 5000, the currently unlogged transactions are dumped to a .SQL file in the C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Configurations\Default \Work folder. These .SQL files can be manually loaded into SQL Enterprise manager and executed to “catch up” this dat

.SQL file in the C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Configurations\Default \Work folder. These .SQL files can be manually loaded into SQL Enterprise manager and executed to “catch up” this data. Each file name uses the following format: DBLogAgentName_Y_M_D_H_M_S.sql. Tip: You can split DBLog agents up to share the load of the agents being logged. Then the Tag list , which is sorted alphabetically, allows you to specify and configure the tags that are logged according to the specified Logging method , as follows: Either manually browse in the required tags, by using the button to both browse in the tag and add it to the list, which is sorted alphabetically - so it may not be added to the end of this list. Tip: You can also use the button to add a blank row to this list and then type in the required tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). . Or configure this list from a CSV Comma Separated Value file containing data, which consists of a number of fields in one or more rows, in which the different fields (values) are typically separated by commas. editor, as follows: Manually add the first tag to the Tag List (since you cannot export an empty list).

in one or more rows, in which the different fields (values) are typically separated by commas. editor, as follows: Manually add the first tag to the Tag List (since you cannot export an empty list). Click the Export... button to export this as a CSV file and open the current CSV editor for you, such as Microsoft Excel, so you can populate this list will all the required tags. Save this CSV file. Click the Import... button and browse for this required CSV file to import the configured tag list. Since, if the change in value is LESS than this value then this value is NOT logged. IMPORTANT: When logging DIGITAL values, ensure that this Value deadband is 0, otherwise NO values will be logged. Then you can specify both the OLE DB database and the table name in which these tags are logged, as follows: Note: While these fields specify SQL, you are able to connect to any OLE DB database. SQL connection string : the required OLE DB connection string to the database where these tag values are t

ollows: Note: While these fields specify SQL, you are able to connect to any OLE DB database. Note: If you specify global , the Global OLE DB connection string of the Agent Server is used, which is specified in the Adroit Config Editor . Typically, you can launch this tool from the Desktop shortcut. Select the Agent Server Configuration Welcome menu item. Select the Advanced Agent Server Configuration option. At the bottom of the dialog, the Global OLE DB connection field is available for you to specify this connection string. SQL table name : the name of the table in this database to log this data, which is Adr_DBLog by default (the STRING tableName slot). that a DBLog agent logs to. More details: DBLog Housekeeping configuration examples: DBLog1 writes data to Table1 and is configured with no housekeeping: So housekeeping will NOT run on Table1, as expected. DBLog2 writes data to Table2 and housekeeping is configured: So the specified housekeeping WILL run on Table2, as expected. DBLog3 and DBLog4 writes data to the same table Table34 - DBLog3 is configured with no housekeeping AND DBLog4 is configured with 30 days housekeeping: So Housekeeping WILL run on Table34 as per DBLog4’s housekeeping configuration for this SHARED table. DBLog5 and DBLog6 writes data to the same table Table56 - DBLog5 is configured with 30 days housekeeping AND DBLog6 is configured with 90 days housekeeping: So Housekeeping will run on Table34 as per DBLog5’s housekeeping configuration and the data older than 30 days will be deleted, since the SHORTEST housekeeping period is always used as this is the period that is reached first for this SHARED table. When this backup folder is being used each DBLog agent creates a daily flat cabinet (.CAB) file of the data that is to be deleted (by the SHORTEST Housekeeping setting if multiple DBLog agents log to the same table). These files are self-extracting SQL scripts, which you need to manually execute against the required SQL database, in order to import your data. PLEASE NOTE: It is up to you to manage the files stored in this folder yourself. ag being logged Value :– the value of the tag being logged Quality : an indication of whether value of this logged tag was good or bad data has a bad status when data is missing, incorrectly reported or extrapolated. . This agent ALSO creates the Adr_DBLog_AgentDetails table, which contains all the agents referenced by all DBLog agents to provide more details about these referenced agents, which can be used to provide more context about them for reports. ar(255): the tag being logged TagDescription – varchar(255): a description of the tag being logged; always equal to AgentDescription unless agent type is Marshal whereupon it contains the description of the bit Units - varchar(255): for Analog agents only OffText - varchar(255): for Digital and Marshal agents only OnText - varchar(255): for Digital and Marshal agents only RawMin - float: Raw (device-scale) minimum scaling limit for Analog agents only RawMax - float: Raw (device-scale) maximum scaling limit for Analog agents only EngMin - float: Engineering minimum scaling limit for Analog agents only EngMax - float: Engineering maximum scaling limit for Analog agents only LoLo - float: Low-low alarm level for Analog agents only Lo - float: Low alarm level for Analog agents only Hi - float: High alarm level for Analog agents only HiHi - float: High-high alarm level for Analog agents only Note: If you do not intend to make use of this table then you can prevent this table from being created by all of your DBLog agents, by adding the following registry value and setting it to 0: DumpAgentDetailsEnabled . text: Configuring Incident (Alarm) Priorities Top Configuring Incident (Alarm) Priorities One way to ensure that your operators ONLY receive IMPORTANT alarms is to prioritise your alarms into categories of importance so that you can filter your incidents, based on their priority. There are two ways to prioritise your incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). : Per Agent: Use this method if ALL the incidents (alarm types) of this agent have the SAME priority. Alternatively, use this method to specify the LOWEST priority for the incidents (alarm types) of this agent and then use the other per-incident method to specify the incidents that differ. Five levels of importance are supported from 0 the lowest up to 4 the highest. To configure an agent-specific priority: Select the required agent in the Agent Configurator dialog. For details, see To Select an Agent . Click the Header button. Specify the required priority level for ALL the incidents (alarm types) of this agent, in the Alarm priority edit box i

figurator dialog. For details, see To Select an Agent . Click the Header button. Specify the required priority level for ALL the incidents (alarm types) of this agent, in the Alarm priority edit box in the lower right corner of the Agent Header dialog, as follows: 0 : lowest 1: low 2: normal 3: high 4: highest The default is 2 (normal). The Alarm agent will discard any alarms that are triggered if its own priority filter is greater than that of the alarmed agent it is monitoring. Per Incident: Use this method if SOME incidents of an agent have DIFFERENT priorities. For instance the High alarm limit of an Analog agent will have a lower priority than the HighHigh alarm limit. Note: The agent priority setting is the default priority used when configuring an incident for the first time, thereafter the incident priority setting is always used. To configure an incident-specific priority: Select the required agent, in other words the agent containing the alarmed alarm type/s. For details, see To Select an Agent . Right click this agent and select the Alarm… menu item. Click on the required alarm type in the Current list of the Alarming dialog. Click the button of the Priority list box, in

To Select an Agent . Right click this agent and select the Alarm… menu item. Click on the required alarm type in the Current list of the Alarming dialog. Click the button of the Priority list box, in the lower right corner of the dialog. Select the required level of priority for this incident, as follows: 0 : lowest 1: low 2: normal 3: high 4: highest The default is 3 (high). For further details about filtering incidents based on their priority level, see About Filtering Prioritised Incidents . -->

Configuring Incident Acknowledgement Top Configuring Incident Acknowledgement Acknowledgment of incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). is typically recommended for alarms i.e. all incidents that require some sort of reaction or attention from the operator. When you create incidents, you can specify whether it needs to be acknowledged in the Alarm List Viewer window. Note: If you are using the AlarmManagement agent, you can extend the acknowledgement of alarms to enforce the need for operators to specify the reason for the incident and if necessary to specify any notes pertaining to this incident too. To enable or disable acknowledgement of incidents: Select the required agent, in other words the agent containing the alarmed alarm type/s. For details, see To Select an Agent . Right click this agent and select the Alarm… menu item. Click on the required alarm type in the Current list of the Alarming dialog. If you require this incident to be acknowledged: Ensure that the Acknowledgement requi

ent and select the Alarm… menu item. Click on the required alarm type in the Current list of the Alarming dialog. If you require this incident to be acknowledged: Ensure that the Acknowledgement required checkbox in the middle of this dialog is checked (its default setting). Tip: You should ONLY enable the acknowledgement of incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). that operators MUST respond to. If you do not require this incident to be acknowledged: Ensure that the Acknowledgement required checkbox in the middle of this dialog is cleared. Note1: The statusAlarmsUnacked agent status bit ( Alarm(s) Unacknowledged checkbox) is set when one or more of the incidents for this agent still require acknowledgement. Note2: The statusAlarmsActive status bit ( Alarm(s) Active checkbox) is set when one or more of the incidents for this agent have not yet returned to normal operating conditions. For further details about acknowledging incidents, see About Alarm Acknowledgement . -->

Configuring levels and layers Top Configuring levels and layers Levels and layers are configured in the Levels and Layers tool window for the current graphic form displayed in the Design workspace . For more details on why you would configure a level or layer for a graphic form and how they work, see Working with levels and layers . The Levels and layers tool window consists of a grid, where the columns represent the levels and the rows represent the layers, which support the following tasks in order of importance: Click for more information about each task: Adding levels : each level can be selected by the end-user of this graphic form to display the associated layers and their visible form components. Note: At runtime, the user can select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. any configured level of a graphic form, so ensure that each level has a unique configuration of layers associated with it. Tip: Ensure that the first level in the grid contains the graphic form components that need to be viewed by default, since this is the default view of the graphic form. Adding layers : each layer should contain a sub-set of visi

evel in the grid contains the graphic form components that need to be viewed by default, since this is the default view of the graphic form. Adding layers : each layer should contain a sub-set of visible form components are need to be selectively hidden or displayed on this graphic form. Note1: After adding a layer you need to associate it with at least one level. Note2: Layers that have not been associated with levels are indicated by cells in the grid, which have the default background color. Tip: If necessary, after you have added a form component to a layer, you can move it to another layer, by right clicking it and selecting its Move to layer item (provided that this graphic form provides two or more layers). Associate layers with levels : so that their visible form components are displayed on the graphic form, when the required level is selected. Tip1: A single layer can be added to any number of levels. Tip2: To quickly determine which layers have been added to each level, each layer or row is assigned its own unique color in this grid when layers are associated with levels. Identifying edited layers : form components are added to the currently edited layer, in the Levels an

layer or row is assigned its own unique color in this grid when layers are associated with levels. Identifying edited layers : form components are added to the currently edited layer, in the Levels and Layers tool window. Identifying visible levels : identify a level as the visible level, in the Levels and layers tool window, to display the form components associated with its layers in the graphic form. Tip: When editing a graphic form, it is recommended to add and identify a level containing ALL the controls that will appear at the same time, so that they can be arranged. Renaming layers : to assist the designers in identifying the controls it contains, since the end-user does not see the layer names. Removing layers : to remove BOTH the layer and its added controls. WARNING! ALL the form components attached to this layer are also removed and cannot be recovered. Therefore save the graphic form before removing any layers. For details, see Saving graphic forms . Renaming levels : to assist the end-user to identify the contents of this level when its graphic form is displayed at runtime. Removing levels : remove levels that are no longer needed or which are associated with the SAME

sist the end-user to identify the contents of this level when its graphic form is displayed at runtime. Removing levels : remove levels that are no longer needed or which are associated with the SAME layers as another level. Hiding or showing configured levels : for instance to hide the levels, if the Levels and Layers tool window is very narrow. Note: This has no effect upon the display of levels within the graphic form itself. -->

Configuring marks for the values of a series Top Configuring marks for the values of a series When using the Series Setup page of the configuration dialog of a charting control, the Series Marks tab allows you to configure Marks or additional labels for each or some of the values for this series. Typically these Marks this will be used by Pie series to display the percentage of each slice, although they can be added to any series. Choose whether you want these marks to be Visible or not and/or specify the other display options. Select the required Marks Style , which determines the format of the displayed label. Select the required display Angle for these marks. Determine whether you want to mark every value or specify how many values to skip in the Draw every spin control. If necessary, use the other display options to configure these marks. Tip: Its recommended that you use the previewed chart to test first these other options first to see if they are desirable or not. -->

To specify the maximum kVA demand limit for this agent: if this limit is exceeded an alarm can be generated. Use the Max demand limit edit box (the mdLimit slot). Tip: If may be useful to specify a value slightly LESS THAN the actual maximum demand limit imposed by your electricity provider, so that there is time for counteractive measures to be taken when this is exceeded. By alarming the ‘MaxDemand’ alarm type for this agent, you can be warned when this occurs. Check the Enable max demand alarm checkbox (the enableMDAlarm slot). To reset the monthly maximum demand calculation: since this agent stores the largest maximum demand calculated over any block period for the current billing period (month), you need to specify when this billing period ends to reset this value. ver any block period for the current billing period (month), you need to specify when this billing period ends to reset this value. Both the day of month and time of day can be specified, as follows: Day of month (0 denotes the last day of month) (the resetDay slot): This edit box specifies the required day at which the monthly values are reset, the default is 0 (the last day of the month). Time of day (the resetTime slot): This spin control specifies the time (hours:minutes:seconds) of the specified day (in 24 hour format) at which the at which the monthly values are reset, the default is 12 am (midnight). Note: The BOOLEAN resetNow slot, if set to one, resets all the calculated values to zero. To specify the instantaneous kVA (apparent power) input: this is required to calculate maximum demand for the current block period and for the current monthly billing period. Specify this input as follows: Either scan the REAL kVA slot of this agent to a PLC that measures the total instantaneous kVA usage and leave the kVA edit box empty. Or specify a REAL tag (agent.slot) value in the kVA edit box (the kVATag slot) that specifies the total instantaneous kVA usage. Tip: Use the browse butto

Tip: Use the browse button to the right of the kVA edit box to locate this tag. For details, see Selecting a Tag Using the Built-in Agent Explorer . To specify the instantaneous kW (real power) input: this is required if you also want this agent to calculate the instantaneous reactive power and/or power factor. Specify this input as follows: Either scan the REAL kW slot of this agent to a PLC that measures the total instantaneous kW usage Or specify a REAL tag (agent.slot) value in the kW edit box (the kWTag slot) that specifies this value. Pulse-based block periods: The time at which the scanned pulse started the current block period. Tip: Alarm the error alarm type for this agent to warn you when the timing of these external block pulses is compromised. Time left (mins) (the blockTimeLeft slot): The available time-in-hand (in minutes) to the end of this block period. In other words, this specifies the available time in which the maximum demand for this block period can still be controlled. Current demand (the demand slot): The actual power that has been used (kVA demand) for this block period. Predicted max demand (the mdPredict slot): This estimates the total power use (kVA demand) for this block period, by using the Current demand (the demand slot) against the remaining time for this block period. Note: If this value exceeds the specified Max demand limit (the mdLimit slot) then the MaxDemand status bit is set if the Enable max demand alarm checkbox (the enableMDAlarm slot) is enabled. Then a

Then alarm the ‘MaxDemand’ alarm type for this agent to warn you when this occurs. Tip: It is possible to use the MaxDemand status bit in a Script agent to control the maximum demand by using it to turn off non-essential equipment. Predicted over/under (the mdOverUnder slot): This displays the difference between the Predicted max demand (the mdPredict slot) and the Max demand limit (the mdLimit slot) for this block period. Time to max demand (mins) (the timeToMD slot): This indicates how long, in minutes, before the Max demand limit (the mdLimit slot) will be reached before the end of the block metered period, at the current demand. Note: If you are running safely, this will ALWAYS indicate the end of the current block period. Optimal KVA (the kVAOptimal slot): The recommended kVA consumption to meet (and NOT EXCEED) the Max demand limit (the mdLimit slot) for this block period. Spare KVA (the kVASpare slot): The spare kVA capacity for current period, which is the difference between the Curr

meet (and NOT EXCEED) the Max demand limit (the mdLimit slot) for this block period. Spare KVA (the kVASpare slot): The spare kVA capacity for current period, which is the difference between the Current demand (the demand slot) and the Optimal KVA (the kVAOptimal slot). This either specifies a negative amount of kVA that needs to be shed (removed) or a positive amount of kVA that can be added to meet (and NOT EXCEED) the Max demand limit (the mdLimit slot) for this block period. MaxDemand Agent Calculations: the MaxDemand agent only performs these calculations when correctly licensed and provided with the necessary inputs. Note: This agent needs a separate OEM a component in Adroit that requires a SEPARATE license BEFORE it can be used, which is added to the Agent Server license by means of an appropriate textual description of this component. license before performing background calculations. Tip: To determine if this agent is correctly licensed, ensure that its Unlicensed status bit is NOT set. kVAr* (the kVArCalc slot): This calculates the instantaneous kVAr (reactive power) value, which requires both the mandatory kVA input (the kVA slot) and optional kW input (the kW slot). For details on how this can save you money, see About Power Factor . TotalKWh (the kVAhTotal slot): This calculates the total real power in KWh (kilowatt-hours) consumed for the maximum demand periods of the current month . TotalKVArh (the kVArhTotal slot): This calculates the total reactive power in KVArh (Kilo Volt Amps Reactive Hours) consumed for the maximum demand periods of the current month, either from the calculated kVAr* value or the optional kVAr input. Current month MD (the mdActual or value slot): This is the highest recorded maximum demand for any block period of the current month. Configuring Monitored Tags Top Configuring Monitored Tags The Tag Monitor utility can display current values of one or more tag values from a particular Agent Server, in tabular and trend format, without having to specifically draw a mimic or create a trend to do so. For details, see Monitoring Tags (Values) . The Tags tabbed page is displayed by default, when this utility is launched. This page contains and manages the list of tags (agent.slot), whose values are monitored by this utility. Interaction with this page is dependent upon whether the status of the tag monitoring process, as follows: Note1: The list of tags configured by this page is saved, when the utility is saved. When the tag monitoring process is started i.e. the Start button is clicked and is currently greyed out. When the tag monitoring process is stopped i.e. the Stop button is clicked and is currently greyed out. text: Configuring Node names and descriptors Top Configuring Node names and descriptors When you Add / Edit a node, you can specify the Node name , which is the literal description used when navigating the defined hierarchy and Node descriptor which is typically a 3 character code to reference the specific contextual area that is represented by this node. Note: The specified descriptor is always CAPITALISED. The Descriptor path specifies all the defined Node descriptors up to the current level and only adds the descriptor of this new node once you define it. This is typically used when creating object instances, whose names and substitution/s use a predefined naming convention that specifies the context in which the instance is created. For details, see Creating contextually sensitive object instances . Note: You are unable to specify any character that is not allowed for agent names. Tip: Any parent or grand parent node that you have not defined a descriptor for will NOT appear in the specified Descriptor path . By default these node descriptors are not separated using the '_' character, however you can click the Configure view in the bottom tool bar of this window and uncheck the Use s

fied Descriptor path . By default these node descriptors are not separated using the '_' character, however you can click the Configure view in the bottom tool bar of this window and uncheck the Use separators checkbox to remove this separator character or specify the required separator character in the Separator edit box. -->

ify one or more of these 4 scaling variables as follows: Right-click the title bar of this spider and select the RawMin , RawMax , EngMin and/ or EngMax items. Configuring the Agent Server Top Configuring the Agent Server The Agent Server is the storage facility for all real time and historical data. For further details, see About Agent Servers . The real time data resides within intelligent objects, known as agents, which exchange messages with other agents or picture objects either from their local host computer or from remote computer nodes elsewhere on the network. For details, see About Agents . Historical data is written to disk where it is available for rapid retrieval and on-line analysis. For details, see Logging Values . The Adroit database (.WGP) file or load file stores almost all of the data and configuration of the Agent Server, including the added agents, their values and their alarming, logging and scanning configuration. For details, see About Adroit Database Files . The Agent Server Configurator creates, manages and stores the configured agents and their slots (values) in the Agent Server. For further details, see the list of available agent types and their slots (values). Open the Agent Configuration dialog, as follows: Tip: This also opens the Adroit Classic UI in the SmartUI Designer, which provides agent-specific men

f available agent types and their slots (values). Open the Agent Configuration dialog, as follows: Tip: This also opens the Adroit Classic UI in the SmartUI Designer, which provides agent-specific menu functions, such as importing and exporting agents. In the SmartUI Designer: Click the Open Configurator tool in the Agent Server group of the Home tab of the SmartUI Designer ribbon. Note: When there is more than one Adroit datasource available, a list is provided to select which Agent Server to configure. The Agent Configuration dialog is displayed within the Classic UI. Note: The Project Explorer can also be used to configure the Agent Server. For details, see The Project Explorer . Before you can create or edit any agents you must be connected to an Agent Server. If necessary, you can manually specify which Agent Server the Configurator should connect to and configure. For details, see Connecting to an Agent Server via the Classic UI . Note1: Only when these changes made to agents are saved, will they be written to the Adroit database file (.WGP) file of the Agent Server. For details, see Saving agents . Note2: These agents can also be exported to CSV files for editing by 3rd part

saved, will they be written to the Adroit database file (.WGP) file of the Agent Server. For details, see Saving agents . Note2: These agents can also be exported to CSV files for editing by 3rd party applications and then imported into the Agent Server. For details, see Exporting and Importing Agents . Related topics Agent Server Connection Methods : Adroit provides three methods for allowing multiple distributed Agent Servers to seamlessly share their agents and the data that they contain. Proxy servers : An Agent Server that creates proxy agents for agents that exist on remote Agent Servers on the same project because it itself does not contain any configured agents. Note: A Proxy Server (an Agent Server that is licensed for ZERO scan points) can proxy an unlimited number of agents, whereas a normal Agent Server is only able to create as many proxy agents as it has scan points and therefore must be licensed for AT LEAST the same number of scan points as the remote Agent Server. Clustering Agent Servers : A mechanism for providing client and server redundancy, previously known as hot standby. For more details on addressing the important issues that affect the operation and confi

stering Agent Servers : A mechanism for providing client and server redundancy, previously known as hot standby. For more details on addressing the important issues that affect the operation and configuration of clustered Adroit Agent Servers, see Important Points to consider when Clustering Agent Servers . For more details on detecting and solving issues that most frequently prevent clustered Adroit Agent Servers from working, see Troubleshooting Clustered Agent Servers . -->

Configuring the auditing and/or authorizing of value changes Top Configuring the auditing and/or authorizing of value changes The SmartUI Server includes the following data element security functionality: Note: This functionality is part of the SmartUI Server and is available even when one does not want to use 21 CFR 11 mode. auditing functionality: to audit ANY data element by completely tracking changes made to its value through the SmartUI . change authorizing functionality: when enabled this requires an additional user to provide authorization before a change can be made (written) to a data element. Tip: If you are employing a 21 CFR 11 compliant project then ensure that you have enabled 21 CFR 11 mode. For more details, see Working with 21 CFR 11 mode . Before your Windows user accounts and/or groups can participate in the auditing and/or authentication of value (data element) changes, they need to be added as "allowed" users and groups on each SmartUI Server. Since these users are required to access the SmartUI Server computer directly then to preserve the integrity of the 21 CFR 11 functionality, these users must only be given minimal rights (from a Windows security context)
