text: e required to access the SmartUI Server computer directly then to preserve the integrity of the 21 CFR 11 functionality, these users must only be given minimal rights (from a Windows security context). Only administrative users may be given extended rights. IMPORTANT: Therefore ONLY specify your system administrator users and/or groups in this the Security Settings page of the SmartUI Server in the Adroit Config Editor , since these users and/or groups have immediate GLOBAL access to every aspect of your project, which includes the ability to write to all of the data elements. For details, see Server security settings . For this reason, you should rather configure your allowed users and groups within the SmartUI Designer, as you can then manually configure the extent of their access. For details, see Adding allowed users and groups . Since, you need to know beforehand exactly which values to audit and/or authorise, you can only configure specific, individual data elements and not entire groups of data elements. In the SmartUI every value is known as a data element of a datasource, so you use data element security to configure the auditing change of values (data elements) and/or their authorization, as follows: IMPORTANT: Unlike the data element security permissions, the auditing and authorizing settings are data element specific and NOT user or group specific. So they are enabled or disabled for ALL the selected users and/or groups. However, ONLY users or groups with the Write Data security permission can authorise changes to a data element. Configuring the DBQuery Agent Top Configuring the DBQuery Agent Configuration of the DBQuery agent is processed via the dialog, as shown below. The agent dialog provides the ability to set several options: (See the Configuration slots option for more information.) Enable or disable the functionality of this particular agent. Disable transactions executed on the standby server. Select the trigger method to use and optionally also the trigger tag. Enter the execution interval value in seconds. Set the auto-reset runNow option. Enter the SQL Server connection string. Enter the required tag list. Enter the required Table name . Enter the WHERE clause containing tag names within an angled bracket (< >) pair. The agent automatically substitutes these tags into values first and then performs the following example SELECT statement transaction: SELECT f3,f4,f5,f6 FROM Table_1 WHERE (f1=12) AND (f2=13) Enter a custom query. Let’s have a look at a few Custom Query examples. If a SELECT query returns more than one record, the agent will use the first record only. Should you want to use the newest record from the result of a SELECT statement, you could use the example custom query as shown belo

rns more than one record, the agent will use the first record only. Should you want to use the newest record from the result of a SELECT statement, you could use the example custom query as shown below: SELECT f3,f4,f5,f6 FROM Table_1 WHERE (f1=12) AND (f2=13) ORDER BY dt DESC Because Adroit only uses the first record returned, the example custom query could effectively be changed to: SELECT TOP 1 f3,f4,f5,f6 FROM Table_1 WHERE (f1=12) AND (f2=13) ORDER BY dt DESC NOTE: Should a custom SELECT query be used then the ‘SQL table name’, ‘WHERE clause’ and ‘Field’ column entries in the tag list will be ignored because you would add this information to the custom query. Custom SELECT queries will substitute the ‘Tagname’ entries in the tag list with values returned from the custom query, therefore it is important to ensure that the custom SELECT query requests the data in the order required by order of the ‘Tagname’ entries. Other Custom Query examples For the query below to work, the tag list should only contain only one entry specifying a tagname. SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM MyTable WHERE f1=12 The ‘Field’ name is disregarded. If more than one tag is specified the agent will assume f

st should only contain only one entry specifying a tagname. SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM MyTable WHERE f1=12 The ‘Field’ name is disregarded. If more than one tag is specified the agent will assume failure with the above query. Delete records The query below will delete all records older than 1st Jan 2019. The query disregards the contents of the tag list in the dialog. DELETE FROM MyTable WHERE dt < “2019-01-01” Insert records The queries below will insert a new record to the table. The queries will disregard the contents of the tag list in the dialog. INSERT INTO MyTable (f1, f2, f3, f4, f5, f6) VALUES (1, 1, 123, 456 ,678, 901) or INSERT INTO MyTable (dt, f1, f2, f3, f4, f5, f6) VALUES (<systeminfo.currenttime>, 1, 1, <f1.value>,<f2.value>,<f3.value>,<f4.value>) Execute Query Automatically The query below can use f1.value tag as a trigger tag to automatically have the DBQuery agent execute every time the tag value changes SELECT date,timestart,timeend FROM shift_adv_sh1 WHERE idx=<f1.value> Running Stored Procedures The query below will execute the spHousekeeping stored procedure EXEC spHousekeeping The query below will execute the spCheckRecords stored procedure with parameter

f1.value> Running Stored Procedures The query below will execute the spHousekeeping stored procedure EXEC spHousekeeping The query below will execute the spCheckRecords stored procedure with parameters as may be required by the stored procedure EXEC spCheckRecords 1,5 For all SELECT queries or stored procedures which return data, these results will be substituted into the tags as specified in the tag list and also as governed by the corresponding field names. If the field names are not supplied by the result, as may happen with stored procedures, you can do one of the following: Simply apply the index number to use e.g. 0, 1 or 2. or Leave the field name empty for the tag entry, The agent will then attempt to use the row number (beginning with 0) of the tag entry as the field name. -->

text: Configuring the Notify Agent to send Email messages Top Configuring the Notify Agent to send Email messages There are two ways in which to send an email message from the Notify agent. BOTH require scanning (not @scanning) the Email-rawValue slot (as output enabled and scan inhibited ) of the applicable Notify agent to the applicable Email driver device address i.e. EMAIL.x where { x = 0, x <= 250 } The number of Email driver devices a system requires is determined, as follows: the required number of FROM email addresses, since each Email driver device uses a single FROM address, from which all the email messages scanned to this device are sent from. the number of Notify agents that send email messages, since each Email driver device can service up to 251 Notify agents. Note: Since multiple Email driver devices can use the SAME FROM address, the system can technically serve an unlimited number of Notify agents. Configuring the Shift agent Top Configuring the Shift Agent Edit an agent of type: Scheduler . Please use the following sequence when adding shift patterns: Entries that contain a Special date or Day of month value must always be specified first. Special date entries must use the format “yyyy/mm/dd” e.g. 2010/04/04. An example of a “special date” is a public holiday which falls on a different day every year e.g. Easter Monday. Day of month entries must use the format “mm/dd”. An example of a “day of month” is a public holiday which falls on the same day every year e.g. New Years day. Note1: Entries containing a Special date cannot contain a Day of month value too. Note2: Entries containing a Special date or Day of month value force (disable) their Day of week value. Tip: Use the DEL key to delete unneeded Special date or Day of month field entries The last entries should be the default shift patterns that ONLY contains a Day of week value and NO Special date or Day of month values. Shift pattern examples: This screenshot exemplifies the required order of entries and provides the following shift patterns: For the 1 st of January of any year. For the 25 th of December for any year. O

ft pattern examples: This screenshot exemplifies the required order of entries and provides the following shift patterns: For the 1 st of January of any year. For the 25 th of December for any year. ONLY on the 4 th of April 2010 For ALL Saturdays and Sundays For ALL normal weekdays Notice how the shift patterns that do NOT contain a Special date or Day of month column are at the END of this list. The Shift agent caters for a maximum of 6 shifts per day. If you need less than 6 shifts, then specify the starting time of the last applicable shift for the unneeded shifts. For instance, if only 3 shifts are used, then specify the starting time of shift 3 as the starting times of shifts 4, 5 and 6. Configuring Windows Security Policies Top Configuring Windows Security Policies The Adroit Security Manager provides the following security policies, which affect the Windows operating system of the computer that these policies are applied to, as follows: Configure Power Users: All Adroit users must, at least, belong to the LOCAL "Power Users" security group over and above the default "User" group; otherwise they are not able to perform all the functions necessary to run Adroit on this computer. For instance: if you are NOT part of the Power Users group, although you will able to start the User Interface, you will not be able to start the Agent Server or the Adroit Setup utility. Also if the Agent Server is installed as a service, then the Agent Server will also start. Note: If you are running a domain and you are configuring the domain controller computer, you do not need to perform this configuration as this computer already has a POWER USERS group and the Adroit users are already assigned to this group. Enable Auto-Logon: If enabled this setting allows other users to start your computer and use the account that you establish to automatically log on. For instance: many SCADA inst

signed to this group. Enable Auto-Logon: If enabled this setting allows other users to start your computer and use the account that you establish to automatically log on. For instance: many SCADA installations create a user that is part of the Adroit Operator security group called DefaultOP, which is used to auto logon to Windows. For this reason, if you choose to create the default groups, this user is created for you; however you need to make this user a member of the Adroit Operators default group yourself. WARNING! Although enabling auto logon makes your computer more convenient to use, it can pose a security risk. Therefore it is recommended that the user account that you specify has the LOWEST access permissions for the computer and the Adroit installation. To BYPASS the Windows automatic logon to log on as a different user: Hold down the SHIFT key after you log off or after Windows XP restarts. Note: This ONLY applies to the first logon attempt of the computer. Replace the Shell: This is the easiest method of creating a restricted workstation for your operators, as this simply replaces the default Explorer shell with the Classic UI. This means that when Windows is launched,

: This is the easiest method of creating a restricted workstation for your operators, as this simply replaces the default Explorer shell with the Classic UI. This means that when Windows is launched, the Classic UI is displayed by default and NOT the Windows Desktop. Tip: By applying the Disable Alt-Tab and Disable Ctl-Esc policies you can run the Classic UI on top of the XP (without removing shell) and STILL prevent your operators from accessing Windows. To enable a security policy: this allows you to specify which of the available security policies you want to apply. Press the Windows key and start typing in Security Manager and select it from the list. If necessary, expand (double click) the Windows Security Options branch in the left hand tree pane. Click on the required option. Ensure that the Apply Setting checkbox is checked. If necessary, perform any additional configuration. IMPORTANT: Simply enabling a policy (option) does NOT change this policy on this computer; you need to APPLY the policy to a specific computer in order to change the security settings of this computer. For details on how to save and/or apply the specified security settings, see Applying Security Polici

text: Connecting to an OLE DB database Top Creating a SQL database connection string Click the ... browse button to the right of this field and use the Data Link Properties dialog to create the required connection string to your SQL Server database. Provider TAB The Data Link Properties dialog specifies the location and the security credentials required to connect to this database. Double-click the Microsoft OLE DB Provider for SQL Server item in the Provider tab of the Data Link Properties dialog. Important: If the computer, on which SQL Server was installed, was renamed, then SQL Server may need to be re-installed. If the computer was renamed after installing SQL Server, then SQL Server must be re-installed, to function correctly. Run the following check: Execute the following T-SQL (Transact-SQL) script in SQL Server Management Studio: SELECT @@SERVERNAME If the resulting server name is different to the actual name of the computer, then the name of the computer has been changed after SQL Server was installed, so you need to reinstall SQL Server. Note: If you need to configure or view this database and its data from remote computers, then you should use a UNC Universal Naming Conventio

text: Server was installed, so you need to reinstall SQL Server. text: Connecting to the distribution computer Top Connecting to the distribution computer The SmartUI Launcher is used to download the files required for the SmartUI Operator application, either over a LAN or the Internet. Tip: For a detailed step-by-step procedure of connecting Operators to a Server over the Internet, see How to Connect to the Server over the Web . To do this, the Launcher needs to connect to a computer that has the SmartUI Distributor service installed and configured, which is typically the SmartUI Server computer. The VIP Distributor service specifies the folder that the Launcher uses to synchronises its installation folder with. For details, see Working with the SmartUI Launcher . Note1: If the distribution computer uses firewall software ensure that the Distributor service has access to the necessary communication port. For details, see Firewall configuration . Note2: Once the Launcher has successfully connected to a distribution computer, these connections settings will automatically be used whenever it is run. Note3: This connection dialog can also be displayed, for instance to connect to another computer, by opening the launcher, selecting File menu and its Conne

l automatically be used whenever it is run. Note3: This connection dialog can also be displayed, for instance to connect to another computer, by opening the launcher, selecting File menu and its Connection item. The following procedure describes how to create a new connection. First ensure that the VIP Distributor service is running on the required computer. To manually start or configure the SmartUI Distributor service: Open the Services applet on the required computer, as follows: click the Start menu, Control Panel , Administrative Tools and the Services item. Locate the VIP Distributor entry in the list. Right-click this item and select Start . Tip: Select Properties… to configure this service to your liking within the Services environment i.e. to determine the Startup type or the Log on account that should be used for this service. To connect to the distribution computer: Run the SmartUI Launcher, as follows: If you have installed the SmartUI Launcher: use the Launcher shortcut on the Desktop by the installation or from within the VIP Launcher r program group. If SmartUI supports the use of the Launcher and you have the Operator or Designer components already installed, then d

the Desktop by the installation or from within the VIP Launcher r program group. If SmartUI supports the use of the Launcher and you have the Operator or Designer components already installed, then double click the SmartUI Launcher executable in the installation folder, which is typically: C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI . The SmartUI Launcher is displayed. If necessary, selecting File menu and its Connection item to display the Connection dialog. If necessary, select how this distribution computer is to be reached i.e. over the LAN or over the Internet. Note: By default, this dialog displays the fields required when connecting to a distribution computer over the LAN. If this connection is required over the LAN: Specify the network name of this required computer that has the SmartUI Distributor service installed and configured in the Computer/URL edit box. Ensure that the LAN or WAN selection is selected. In the Authenticate group, specify the required User and Password , which are required when connecting to this computer. Note: At least the User field needs to be completed, in order for a connection to be created; a Password does not need to be specified. Cli

sword , which are required when connecting to this computer. Note: At least the User field needs to be completed, in order for a connection to be created; a Password does not need to be specified. Click the Connect button, once the necessary details, have been correctly specified. If this connection is required over the Internet: Note: Before a connection can be made over the Internet to the Server, the Web service needs to be installed. For details, see Installing the SmartUI Web Service . Specify the Internet address (URL) of the Web service, which makes this Internet connection possible, in the Computer/URL edit box, which is typically: http://ComputerName/VirtualDirectory/wsdistributor.asmx. Where: ComputerName is the name of the IIS server hosting the distribution service (on which the Web service has been installed) VirtualDirectory is the name of the virtual directory containing the wsdistributor.asmx file, which was specified when installing the SmartUI Web Service , which is typically: SmartUI Tip: The 'http://' prefix and '/wsdistributor.asmx' suffix will be added to this URL on connection, if they have not been specified. For further details, open this web page: http://C

ypically: SmartUI Tip: The 'http://' prefix and '/wsdistributor.asmx' suffix will be added to this URL on connection, if they have not been specified. For further details, open this web page: http://ComputerName/VirtualDirectory e.g. http://localhost/ SmartUI , which can be used to download the Launcher application and also contains instructions on how to connect and download the distribution files too. Note: The SmartUI Web Service does not need to be installed on the same computer as the Distributor service, as long as these two computers can communicate over the LAN. Ensure that the Internet selection is selected. In the Authenticate group, specify the required User and Password , which are required when connecting to this computer. If a proxy server is required for this Internet connection, check the Enable Proxy checkbox and click the Proxy Settings button. This displays the Proxy Settings dialog, so that the necessary connection settings for this Proxy server can be specified, as follows: Specify the network name of this Proxy server or its IP address in the Machine Name or IP edit box. Specify the port that this Proxy Server uses in the Port edit box, this is typically port

follows: Specify the network name of this Proxy server or its IP address in the Machine Name or IP edit box. Specify the port that this Proxy Server uses in the Port edit box, this is typically port 8080. Tip: If necessary, the required port for this proxy server can also be determined from Internet Options (typically launched from the Tools menu in Internet Explorer), by selecting the Connections tab and its LAN Settings… button. If user authentication is required when connecting to this proxy server, then check the Authenticate checkbox and supply the necessary User and Password. Click OK . Click the Connect button, once the necessary details, have been correctly specified. -->

Connecting to the Managed Device Connecting to the Managed Device The SNMPManager agent must connect to the required device and specify the required level of access to its values (SNMP managed objects) before you can monitor and/or manage this device. To connect to a SNMP device: Specify the following settings in the Connection settings section of the Edit SNMP Manager Agent dialog: IP address (STRING ipAddress slot): Specify the IP address of the device that is to be monitored and/or managed by this SNMPManager agent. For details on the requirements and guidelines regarding the use of this agent to monitor and/or manage devices, see Usage Requirements . Tip1: Use the arrow keys to navigate between the digits separated by periods. Tip2: When monitoring the local computer, the following IP address always returns the local address: 127.0.0.1. Port address: this allows SNMP devices to be addressed via a gateway where the IP addresses are not unique and so a unique port address is required. Read comm. (STRING readCommunity slot): If you ONLY want to retrieve (poll) values from this device then specify its read-only SNMP Community String. For further details, see SNMP Community Strings.

. Read comm. (STRING readCommunity slot): If you ONLY want to retrieve (poll) values from this device then specify its read-only SNMP Community String. For further details, see SNMP Community Strings. Tip: Since most equipment ships from the factory with a read-only community string that is set to "public", this is its default value. Write comm. (STRING writeCommunity slot): If you want to write (set) values for this device then specify its read-write SNMP Community String. Timeout (ms) (INTEGER timeout slot): If necessary, specify the maximum time (in milliseconds) to establish a connection to this device. This is 2.5 seconds, by default. Retries (INTEGER retries slot): If necessary, specify the number of attempts to connect to the device, before deeming this device to be unavailable. This is 2 times, by default. Only check the Enable traps checkbox (BOOLEAN trapEnabled slot): if you want to receive SNMP traps from this device. For more details, see About SNMP Traps . Note: If the Update button is clicked after modifying the IP address or Read comm. or WriteRead comm. settings, the agent will attempt to reconnect to the device using these new settings. The Invalid connection check

ate button is clicked after modifying the IP address or Read comm. or WriteRead comm. settings, the agent will attempt to reconnect to the device using these new settings. The Invalid connection checkbox (InvalidConnection status bit) indicates if this agent CAN (if empty) or CANNOT (if checked) connect to the specified device. BUT this checkbox is ONLY validated when you press the Update button or select the Enable polling option for this agent, so it will ALWAYS be CHECKED when the Disable polling option is selected. Note1: If you are monitoring a computer and have NOT installed the SNMP service, then the InvalidConnection status bit will be set. Note2: An invalid connection will delay the closing and opening the Edit dialog, as the agent attempts to establish this connection. -->

Connecting to the Managed Device Connecting to the Managed Device The SNMPMgr agent must connect to the required device and specify the required level of access to its values ( SNMP managed objects management data exposed by SNMP managed devices that might be hardware, configuration parameters, performance statistics, and any other data that directly relates to the operation of this device. ) before you can monitor and/or manage this device. IMPORTANT: Since the SNMPMgr agent supports up to SNMP version 3 and SNMP version 3 supports additional connection settings, therefore you need to know beforehand which SNMP version the device requires before you can connect to it. To connect to a SNMP device: Specify the following settings in the Connection settings section of the Edit SNMPMgr Agent dialog: IP address (STRING ipAddress slot): Type in the IP address of the device that is to be monitored and/or managed by this SNMPMgr agent. For details on the requirements and guidelines regarding the use of this agent to monitor and/or manage devices, see Usage Requirements . he use of this agent to monitor and/or manage devices, see Usage Requirements . Tip1: Use the LEFT and RIGHT arrow keys to quickly move to each number separated by the periods. By default this is 161 the port that is used for SNMP communications. IMPORTANT: Ensure that the specified port is unblocked (enabled) in any firewalls that may exist. Timeout (INTEGER timeout slot): If necessary, specify the maximum time (in seconds) to establish a connection to this device. This is 1 seconds, by default. Version (INTEGER version slot): Select which SNMP version this device supports. This is version 1, by default. Read comm. (STRING readCommunity slot): If you ONLY want to retrieve (poll) values from this device then specify its read-only SNMP Community String. For further details, see SNMP Community Strings. Consistent alarm indication Top Consistent alarm indication To ensure the consistency of your process user interface and that your operators are suitably alerted to the important alarms: Alarm Priorities Alarms should be broken down into 5 priorities each having its own sound and the following associated color: Priority 4 – Highest – Red Priority 3 – High – Yellow Priority 2 – Normal – Orange Priority 1 – Low – Magenta Priority 0 – Lowest – Royal blue - reserved for diagnostics alarms or events. Every alarm priority chosen should have its own unique alarm sound. For instance: by sounding a railroad crossing bell sound for Priority 4 – Highest. IMPORTANT: Ensure that the sounds that are chosen are unique and are therefore not used by any other process or interface in the control room. Displaying Alarm Indications The following visual methods ensure that the maximum amount of information is efficiently displayed by an alarm: Each alarm priority should have an associated geometric shape, which is both simple and unique to each alarm priority. Control Bits (user modifiable) Top Control Bits (user modifiable) Control Bits fan-out, which means that a slot control bit becomes set or reset, whenever the corresponding agent control bit is set or reset. Note: Unlike Condition Bit fan-in, Control Bit fan-out does not use positive logic (nor negative logic, for that matter): when an agent bit is set or reset this action is performed on all its corresponding slot bits. The fan-out doesn’t happen to a derived status word as in the case of fan-in, but to the raw status value. Therefore if a slot control bit is already set when the agent control bit is reset, then this slot control bit will not be restored to its set state but will remain reset along with all the other corresponding slot bits. Global Inhibit . Log Inhibit . Scan Inhibit . Output Initialise . Operator Inhibit . Alarm Inhibit . Output Enable . -->

Converting Adroit Classic UI mimics into SmartUI graphic forms Top Converting Adroit Classic UI mimics into SmartUI graphic forms This topic describes the following best practice process for exporting mimics from the Classic UI and importing these as SmartUI graphic forms: Ensure that your Classic UI mimic is correctly configured Save your mimic in the Classic UI to a XAML file Ensure that the XAML conversion was successful Import this mimic into the SmartUI Ensure that your Classic UI mimic is correctly configured In particular, consider the following points: Note1: Mimics that have been saved in a zoomed state are automatically normalised before the mimic is exported. Note2: Scale picture elements are currently not supported and need to be recreated after importing. Note3: Rotated Rectangle picture elements are imported as polylines and therefore will NOT have rounded corners. Ensure that you have performed the required alignment of your picture elements before exporting the mimic, since the SmartUI uses a different method of aligning objects that takes practice to do. Ensure that all your configured Behaviours are working as desired before exporting the mimic, so that you do not

text: ince the SmartUI uses a different method of aligning objects that takes practice to do. Ensure that all your configured Behaviours are working as desired before exporting the mimic, so that you do not need to reconfigure them after importing the mimic. IMPORTANT: This especially applies to any template mimics that are being exported, because currently if their Behaviours are edited after importing then they lose their functionality and need to be re-configured. More details: during the importing process, SmartUI Template Sets are configured (which employ alternate sets of spider silks for each template), but when these Behaviours are configured after importing, their configuration is automatically changed to use SmartUI Templates instead (which uses a totally different mechanism of templatization, namely the use of graphic form aliases) This means that unless the appropriate aliases are configured, then this Behaviour loses ALL of its functionality until the necessary aliases are configured appropriately. text: Converting output data types Top Converting output data types If an output of a spider does not provide the necessary data type, you can convert it to the required data type and use this converted value instead. For instance if the spider produces a numerical output which you want to display this as a string, you can now convert it to a string and apply string formatting too and then use this converted value instead. The following type conversions are possible , depending on the data type of the selected output: Double: Typically used to convert integer into a floating point value in order to perform number formatting. This does not provide any further configuration options. Drawing point: Typically used to configure any property that accepts X and Y coordinates, such as the Location property of a control. This does not provide any further configuration options. Note: Your output must have the same format as a point, by providing both X and Y coordinates e.g. {x=0,y=5}. Boolean: Typically used to convert floating, integer or String values when a Boolean value is required. This does not provide any further configuration options. String: Typically used for displaying numerical or dat

lly used to convert floating, integer or String values when a Boolean value is required. This does not provide any further configuration options. String: Typically used for displaying numerical or date time values in Text properties, such as in TextBox controls. This provides optional string formatting. See below for procedure. Integer: Typically used to convert floating point values into integers. This does not provide any further configuration options. To add a type conversion for an output Open the required spider workspace. If necessary, display the configuration view of this spider by double clicking its title bar. In the Outputs section, right click the required output and select the required conversion from the Convert Output menu. Note: The available conversions depend upon the data type of the selected output. This adds the selected conversion in the line immediately below this output. If this conversion type supports additional configuration options these can be displayed by double clicking the conversion. String formatting configuration: to format this string value accordingly. For instance to specify how the decimal digits should appear or how what elements of a date ti

double clicking the conversion. String formatting configuration: to format this string value accordingly. For instance to specify how the decimal digits should appear or how what elements of a date time should be displayed and how. Double click the required String conversion. Check the Add String Formatting checkbox in the Conversion configuration dialog. Add the required format string to the Format edit box, as follows: Double click one of the provided formatting options in the Format dialog to add this automatically. Manually specify or edit this format string. If necessary, press the Test button to see how the specified test Value appears when using the specified Format string. For further details and examples of creating format strings, see String formatting syntax . Click the Finish button once you have the required format string. If necessary, connect the output as required. Note: Once a conversion is created for an output this converted value is used and not the raw output value. -->

Copying form components Top Copying form components You can copy added form components either within the same graphic form or to another graphic form. Once copied these form components can then be modified as normal. Click for more details: In addition to copying the selected form components themselves, you can ALSO copy any spiders that have been associated with the properties of these form components and/or any Behaviours that have been configured for this form component - which further reduces the amount of designing required. Creating a WGP file From a 3rd Party Application Top Creating a WGP file From a 3 rd Party Application The Adroit DB Generator creates Adroit agent databases (.WGP files) from information stored in 3 rd party applications, such as front-end devices. Things you need to know beforehand: Have you installed this utility from the Additional Adroit Components installation? Does the required Connector exist for the 3 rd party application that you want to create a .WGP file for? Has this Connector (DLL) file been added to the required Agent Server? Can this Connector be accessed remotely or do you need to use the Adroit DB Generator on the Agent Server computer on which the required 3 rd party application resides. Does this Connector support the use of templates? Templates can be used to customise or fine-tune your agent creation, scanning, logging and/or alarming default settings. How to create a WGP file from a 3 rd party application Press the Windows key and start typing in DB Generator and select it from the list. If necessary, add the required remote Agent Server. Note: ALL the available Connectors of this Agent Server are displayed, whether they can be accessed remotely or not. If ne

Creating Alarm Types Top Creating Alarm Types You can either create alarm types from the Alarm agent for ALL agent types or from the Alarming dialog for the agent type of the specific agent that you are alarming. To create an alarm type a named (abnormal) condition or state of an agent that is defined by which of its status bits are simultaneously ON or OFF, which can also list the slots of this agent to report when this condition occurs. for an agent, you must provide two of the following three components: a descriptive name for the specified condition, this usually takes the form of a descriptive abbreviation. For instance "Overheating" for an Analog agent type or "Tripped" for a Digital agent type. specify which of these status bits must be simultaneously enabled or disabled in order for this condition to occur and if necessary, specify which slots of the agent should be reported (and their order) when the specified condition occurs. alog. Select the required Alarm agent. Click the button above the Available alarm types list. Type the required name for this alarm type in the Alarm Type edit field. You can name each instance and specify the process values that uniquely configure it by using the assigned predefined value substitutions. You can also choose to immediately deploy the instance, fully or partially, or deploy it at a later time. Currently, the Object Model supports the following commonly-used drivers (devices) : Modbus Ethernet, Mitsubishi Q, QnA, L, R and iQF Series Ethernet (3E Frames) , OPC Client and Siemens Ethernet. Creating an Object Template Top Creating or Editing an Object Template To start, use a wizard instance on a graphic form that you have already configured, which is working as required and is already configured with the necessary SCADA configuration (i.e. the scanning, logging, and alarming) plus any other agents that the object needs. Important: Take the necessary time to test that the wizard has been correctly configured and is working optimally. Ensure that it can be scanned, logged and alarmed correctly. Be aware that any mistakes or omissions will be duplicated. So, take care! Tip: If you keep the identical substitution names as those you have used in the wizard, this makes it easier to implement your instances, as you will only need to configure these substitutions once. If you don’t use the same substitutions, you should specify unique substitutions during both the SCADA and Graphical Substitution stages. Next, create a template from the wizard, which incorporates the graphical components of the wizard (and any substitutions that it uses), along with the SCADA configuration that you specify. Now, you can create numerous instances of each that will create unique tags and can b

omponents of the wizard (and any substitutions that it uses), along with the SCADA configuration that you specify. Now, you can create numerous instances of each that will create unique tags and can be scanned, logged and alarmed, as specified by the template. Note: To create an object template, you need to be fully aware of how your SCADA system (Agent Server) is configured. text: Creating Conditional Expressions for Incidents Top Creating Conditional Expressions for Incidents Often incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). are set off in a chain reaction that distracts your operators as they only highlight a problem that has already been identified. First-out or SOE (Sequence Of Events) alarming strives to ensure that each incident is unique and is NOT caused by a condition that your operators have already been alerted to. You can implement first-out alarming by creating conditional expressions for your related incidents, so that if an incident becomes active the monitored condition of this incident (alarm/event) is still in effect and has not yet returned to its normal operating state. , it ONLY enters your alarming system WHEN its conditional expression is SUCCESSFUL. In this way you can disregard the incidents that echo existing problems, so that your operators can focus on the real issues at hand. Note1: If the RESULT of the conditional expression for an incident i

this way you can disregard the incidents that echo existing problems, so that your operators can focus on the real issues at hand. Note1: If the RESULT of the conditional expression for an incident is a NULL or zero value then the incident NEVER enters your alarming system, so your operators will NOT know about it. Note2: If BOTH a delay and a conditional expression is specified for an incident, then the conditional expression is evaluated BEFORE and AFTER the specified delay expires. To configure a conditional expression for an incident: Select the required agent, in other words the agent containing the required alarmed alarm type/s. For details, see Locating an agent . Right click this agent and select the Alarm… menu item. Click on the required alarm type in the Current list of the Alarming dialog. Specify the required expression for this alarm type in the Conditional expression field at the bottom of this dialog. Typically you will create a logical expression, whereby the required tag is followed by a value condition, such as: Logical expression Condition for success Tag(TANKLEVEL.value) = 80 SUCCESSFUL if the tag is equal to the value Tag(TANKLEVEL.value) <> 80 SUCCESSFUL if

tag is followed by a value condition, such as: Logical expression Condition for success Tag(TANKLEVEL.value) = 80 SUCCESSFUL if the tag is equal to the value Tag(TANKLEVEL.value) <> 80 SUCCESSFUL if the tag is not equal to the value Tag(TANKLEVEL.value) > 80 SUCCESSFUL if the tag is greater than the value Tag(TANKLEVEL.value) >= 80 SUCCESSFUL if the tag is greater than or equal to the value Tag(TANKLEVEL.value) < 80 SUCCESSFUL if the tag is less than the value Tag(TANKLEVEL.value) <= 80 SUCCESSFUL if the tag is less than or equal to the value Note: You need to enclose each tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). within the Tag() specifier e.g. Tag(systeminfo.second) IMPORTANT: If a tag is NOT enclosed within a Tag() specifier then this incident will NEVER become active. Tip: When adding a tag to the expression, click the browse button and use the Adroit Agent Browser to locate and copy the required tag for you (then use the CTRL+V shortcut to paste it into the expression). This saves you from having to type in the tag yourself and ensure that there are NO spelling errors. Your expressions can make use of one or more of the following elements: Note1: Multi

Your expressions can make use of one or more of the following elements: Note1: Multiple items are separated by commas ','. (not), & (and), | (or) Arithmetic operators +, -, *, /, % (modulus),^ (power) Parentheses (), {}, [] Scientific notation 3E+10 Constants 2, 3, 50 Functions MIN(4,5), SQR(34) By making use of these elements, you can create expressions that contain more than one tag, such as: (Tag(TANKLEVEL.value) < 20) | (Tag(TANKLEVEL.value) > 80) This will be SUCCESSFUL if the tag (Tanklevel.value) is less than 20 or greater than 80. Creating Conditional Expressions for Incidents Top Creating Conditional Expressions for Incidents Often incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). are set off in a chain reaction that distracts your operators as they only highlight a problem that has already been identified. First-out or SOE (Sequence Of Events) alarming strives to ensure that each incident is unique and is NOT caused by a condition that your operators have already been alerted to. You can implement first-out alarming by creating conditional expressions for your related incidents, so that if an incident becomes active the monitored condition of this incident (alarm/event) is still in effect and has not yet returned to its normal operating state. , it ONLY enters your alarming system WHEN its conditional expression is SUCCESSFUL. In this way you can disregard the incidents that echo existing problems, so that your operators can focus on the real issues at hand. Note1: If the RESULT of the conditional expression for an incident i

this way you can disregard the incidents that echo existing problems, so that your operators can focus on the real issues at hand. Note1: If the RESULT of the conditional expression for an incident is a NULL or zero value then the incident NEVER enters your alarming system, so your operators will NOT know about it. Note2: If BOTH a delay and a conditional expression is specified for an incident, then the conditional expression is evaluated BEFORE and AFTER the specified delay expires. To configure a conditional expression for an incident: Select the required agent, in other words the agent containing the required alarmed alarm type/s. For details, see Locating an agent . Right click this agent and select the Alarm… menu item. Click on the required alarm type in the Current list of the Alarming dialog. Specify the required expression for this alarm type in the Conditional expression field at the bottom of this dialog. Creating contextually sensitive object instances Top Creating contextually sensitive object instances Creating an object instance from a node in the Default context can be particularly useful when its name and substitutions use a predefined naming convention that specifies the context in which the instance is created. Tip: If you drag an existing Object Model template from the Enterprise Manager directly onto the applicable node, then you can skip the step where you need to specify the required template. To make the best use of this feature, you need to: Define the necessary hierarchy of Nodes, which typically represent each specific contextual area and specify each Node descriptor , typically a 3-character reference code for each contextual area. For more information about naming details, see Configuring Node names and descriptors . Define the process variable names if your object employs multiple substitutions. You should ensure that these substitutions are specified in the template and are in the logical order of the defined contextual areas. When an object instance is created in a node, then each defined Node descriptor , up to the current level, are used to define its name and

and are in the logical order of the defined contextual areas. When an object instance is created in a node, then each defined Node descriptor , up to the current level, are used to define its name and its substitutions, as follows: The Map Descriptors to Substitutions dialog lets you do one of two things: Assign the Descriptor path , a string that assigns all the Node descriptors that are separated by 'underscore _' characters to a specific substitution. You can specify which Node Descriptor in the Descriptor path is used for each of these substitutions, if you have created multiple substitutions that are combined to specify the required contextual naming convention, such as {site}_{area}_{section}_...., By default, this dialog immediately assumes that the first substitution maps to the first defined Node descriptor , and the second substitution maps to the second defined Node descriptor and so on, up to the current node level of the displayed object instance. It is most useful when the order of the first substitutions matches the order of the Node Descriptors meaning no further configuration is required. You can, however, manually select the required substitution values, if requir

e order of the first substitutions matches the order of the Node Descriptors meaning no further configuration is required. You can, however, manually select the required substitution values, if required. Tip: The Template Descriptor (if one was specified for this template) the last portion of the default deployed object name, that relates to the object itself and not its context, is also specified as an available option in this list. Note: This step is optional and can be skipped by clicking the Skip button at the bottom of this dialog. In the Create New Instance dialog the default New instance name uses the Descriptor path , a string that specifies all the Node descriptors that are typically separated by '_' characters, and appends the Template Descriptor (if one was specified for this template) the last portion of the default deployed object name, that relates to the object itself and not its context. Note: Typically you will need to edit this default name to provide the unique, detailed name for this object. For detailed steps to create an object instance, see Creating an Object Instance . -->

the required commands to perform the required task in the SQL Query editor, which highlights keywords and makes it easier to customise your queries. Sub-folders can also be created within these folders if necessary. To create a folder in a project itself: Open the required project in the Enterprise Manager . For details, see Opening Projects . Right-click on the required project name or its icon and select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. Create Folder . A folder named ‘Folder’ will be added beneath the project, which can be immediately renamed, if required. To create a sub-folder: Open the required project in the Enterprise Manager . For details, see Opening Projects . If necessary, expand click the plus (+) box to the left of the current icon or name its required existing folder(s), until the required folder is displayed. Right-click on this folder name or its icon and select Create Folder . A sub-folder named ‘Folder’ will be added beneath this folder, which can be immediately renamed, if required. Note1: If the name of the folder you create already exists within this level of the project hierarchy then its name wil

ill be added beneath this folder, which can be immediately renamed, if required. These expressions are saved in the expression slot. Note: You need to insert empty lines to separate multiple expressions. The following example shows two separate expressions as they are displayed in the Expression edit box of the IOT agent dialog: Z=slot(x) + slot(y) status16 = slot(z) > 100 As a side note, the expression slot of the IOT agent would actually be saved as follows: Z=slot(x) + slot(y)\r\n\r\nstatus16 = slot(z) > 100 How to define IOT expressions Note: Any status or controlling IOT slot can be alarmed by creating an IOT Alarm agent to alert the user of an anomaly. Slot></Slots><HeaderSlots></HeaderSlots></IOT> SecsInMinute . expression =status16=slot(secs)>30 Note: This example also shows that you do not need to specify a name for the status bits of an IOT agent in order for them to be used, in this case they need to be referred to using the convention status nn in any expressions that you create (where nn is the required status bit number from 16 to 31). Creating Macros Top Creating Macros Macro can be created to simply the process of specifying commands, since a macro is simply an abbreviation or alias for an ENTIRE command, which once defined, can be used when issuing this command to this Command agent . Before macros can be used in messages, it is necessary to alert this Command agent to their possible existence in its received messages, so that it can correctly interpret them. For details, see Enabling Pseudonyms and Macros . Although macros can provide the most intuitive and the shortest command names, they are also the MOST restrictive, since this entire command must be pre-configured in this Command agent, before it can be used. For this reason, they can be used to further restrict or limit the SET-table commands that can be performed by this Command agent. For details, see Limiting SET Commands . Note1: Pseudonyms can be used as placeholders for individual tags (agent.slot), if required. For details, see Creating Pseudonyms . Note2: Macros, like pseudonyms, are specific to the Command agent in which they are defined and are not global to all Command agents. However when a Command agent is copied, any defined macros and pseu

However when a Command agent is copied, any defined macros and pseudonyms will also be duplicated. For details, see Copying Agents . Creating states Top Creating states Define the required “states” , each of which associate a particular color with either a specific string or value or a range of numeric values or a logical result when comparing one or more input values. When the monitored String, Double or Integer input value/s corresponds to the criteria of a defined state, the spider returns the associated color; thereby providing a visual indication of the value/s. To create a state: If necessary, add and/or select the required Multi-state color spider and/or open its configuration view. For details, see Adding Multi-state color spiders . Double-click the New State entry, in the New Input section. Specify the criteria that must be met for this state in the Enter a State dialog, as follows: For String values, specify the required text value that the default Value input or additional input ( i1 etc.) must match exactly, for instance "True" or "False" for boolean values. Note: Do not specify the required name of this state within quotes. For Integer or Double values, specify the range of values that the default Value or additional input ( i1 etc.) must lie within, as follows: To specify a specific range: connect

state within quotes. For Integer or Double values, specify the range of values that the default Value or additional input ( i1 etc.) must lie within, as follows: To specify a specific range: connect the minimum and maximum values with ":" character, for instance: 5.5:6.5 or -20:-10. To create infinite ranges , you can use one of the following operators: > for instance: >5.5. >= for instance: >=6.5 < for instance: <-20 <= for instance: <=-10 <> for instance: <>7 Note: Ensure that there are NO spaces between the specified numbers and the operator characters. To compare the values of one or more inputs , create a logical expression using the following Boolean operators: Example of a logical expression that compares more than one input values: (Value>3)||(i1<34) Note: If a state uses multiple inputs, these need to be added and the correct values need to be assigned to them before the state can be evaluated. Although these boolean operators are typically used to compare the values of more than one input, you can also use them to define states for the single default Value input, for instance: (Value>23)&&(Value!=25) IMPORTANT: When adding multiple “&&” , “||” and other expressions, each

than one input, you can also use them to define states for the single default Value input, for instance: (Value>23)&&(Value!=25) IMPORTANT: When adding multiple “&&” , “||” and other expressions, each expression MUST be enclosed in parentheses “()” (see the examples above). If these parentheses are left out, these expressions do not evaluate correctly. Creating states Top Creating states Create more than one “state” for a specific String, Double or Integer value, so that when this value falls within a defined state, the spider returns the value associated with this state. To create a range of values associated with a particular value If necessary, add and/or select the required Multi-State spider and/or open its configuration view. For details, see Adding Multi-state spiders . Tip: Double click the title bar of this spider to open its configuration view. In the New Input section, double-click the New State entry. This will display the Enter a State dialog. Define the required state, as follows: For String values, specify the required text value that the Value input must match exactly, for instance "True" or "False" for boolean values. Note: Do not specify the required name of this state within quotes. For Integer or Double values, specify the range of values that the Value input must lie within, as follows: To specify a specific range: connect the minimum and maximum values with ":" character, for instance: 5.5:6.5 or -20:-10. To create infinite ranges, you can use one of the following operators: > for instance: >5.5. >= for inst

e: connect the minimum and maximum values with ":" character, for instance: 5.5:6.5 or -20:-10. To create infinite ranges, you can use one of the following operators: > for instance: >5.5. >= for instance: >=6.5 < for instance: <-20 <= for instance: <=-10 <> for instance: <>7 Note: Ensure that there are NO spaces between the specified numbers and the operator characters. Note: Ensure that the state has been correctly defined, for you are unable to re-define it once it has been added. In which case you will only able to remove it, if it is incorrect. For details, see Removing states . This adds this defined state to the Inputs section, which is NOT associated with any value, by default. Specify the value that is associated with this state, as follows: Either double click the value column to the right of the state definition input name in the Inputs section and type in the required value. Or use another spider or Data spider (e.g. property or data element) to provide this value via a silk. Tip: When creating a silk, it is also possible to simply drag onto the New State entry directly, in the New Input section, to add an input to the Inputs section and connect it to the silk in one ea

k. Tip: When creating a silk, it is also possible to simply drag onto the New State entry directly, in the New Input section, to add an input to the Inputs section and connect it to the silk in one easy step. For details, see Creating silks . Repeat this until all the required states have been defined. -->

Creating the Control Recipes Top Creating the Control Recipes A control recipe name may be selected from the control recipe list. A new name may also be typed into this field. The first control recipe in the list will have a numerical identity number (id) equal to zero. The second control recipe will have a numerical id equal to one, and so on. The master recipe slot currentRecipeId can be used to select a control recipe using its id. Note: Names used in the recipe agent e.g. to define recipes and batches, CANNOT contain the ‘%’ character. Start Control Recipe : Start the execution of the control recipe selected from the Control Recipe List . Only one control recipe per master recipe can be active at once. Stop Control Recipe : Stop the execution of an active control recipe. Add Control Recipe : Add an empty control recipe. Remove Control Recipe : Remove the selected control recipe. Edit Control Recipe : Edit the selected control recipe. See Edit Control Recipe for more information. Test Control Recipe : Test the validity of the selected control recipe. Advanced Control Recipe Properties : Edit the advanced properties of the selected control recipe. -->

Creating the Data Object Top Creating the Data Object For details, see Steps required to Monitor Real-time Data . The first step is creating the Data Object. Visual Basic for Applications includes a language statement, CreateObject , for this purpose. CreateObject needs only the name of the object as its first parameter. The VBA code for creating an Adroit OLE Server Data Object is then: Dim dataObj As Object Set dataObj = CreateObject("AdroitServer") -->

Creating the Requests collection Top Creating the Requests collection For details, see Steps required to Monitor Real-time Data . One of the objects exposed by the Data Object is the Requests collection, a collection of individual descriptions for required real-time data. Each description consists of a tag (or agent name) plus the names of all the slots to be monitored. The slot names are gathered into another collection called the Properties collection. Since the Data Object provides the Requests collection as one of its properties, the VBA code to gain access to the Requests collection is simply: Set reqs = dataObj.Requests A single request consists of the tag plus the names of all slots to be monitored. The Requests object provides a method (function) for the creation of blank sets of fields (the Properties collection). This method is named CreateProperties . VBA allows us to create the Properties collection by directly calling the CreateProperties method, which returns a Properties collection: Set props = reqs.CreateProperties() -->

Creating UDT agent types Top Creating UDT Agent Types The UDT Agent Type Designer creates separate Adroit agent types for each UDT (complex data type) that you require. Duplicate the EXACT structure of each UDT by adding properties (basic data types) and, if necessary, configure status slots for the purposes of alarming. IMPORTANT: UDT agent types must exist on all Adroit computers that require access to the UDT agents from the Configurator. Once you have created one or more UDT agent types, you can import them to other computers. For details, see Importing UDT Agent Types . PLEASE NOTE: Every instance (agent created) of an UDT agent type will consume (number of slots-1) scan points. The other scan point will be consumed if and when its rawValue slot is scanned. Note : You can only create UDTs that are composed of data types that can be represented by Boolean, Integer, Real, Datetime, String (80 characters or less) and VarString values. Array data types are NOT supported. To create a new UDT agent type Press the Windows key and start typing in UDT Agent Type Designer and select it from the list. The UDT Agent Type Designer utility is displayed. Click the Add new UDT agent type... b

ew UDT agent type Press the Windows key and start typing in UDT Agent Type Designer and select it from the list. The UDT Agent Type Designer utility is displayed. Click the Add new UDT agent type... button in the UDT Agent Types section. Specify the required name for this UDT agent type in the Create new UDT type dialog. Tip : Use a short yet suitably descriptive name as this name appears in the list of agent types in Adroit . Note : Once you have added a name you CANNOT rename it later. Click the OK button. Specifying the Properties for your UDT Specify the first property (component data type) of this UDT in the Add new UDT property dialog. Note: A property of a UDT is equivalent to a slot of an agent. Type in the required name of this data type. Note: If necessary, you CAN rename a property later, by selecting the required property and clicking the Rename selected UDT property... button. WARNING! Renaming properties invalidate any configurations using the older slot (property) name. Click the OK button. Open the Type list box and specify the required data type for this property. Tip :Ensure that the Selected UDT Properties section indicates the correct basic Adroit data types to

Click the OK button. Open the Type list box and specify the required data type for this property. Tip :Ensure that the Selected UDT Properties section indicates the correct basic Adroit data types to represent this property. Note : If you cannot find the required data type then contact support so that we can add it for you. Only clear the Readonly checkbox, if you want to prevent the user from editing the value of this property in the agent edit dialog. Only clear the Public checkbox, if you want to hide this property from the agent edit dialog. Click the Add new UDT property... button in the Selected UDT - Properties section and repeat steps 5 to 10 for each of the component data types within this UDT. Note : Please ensure that you add these data types in the EXACT order as they appear in the UDT of the PLC. If necessary, edit the property descriptions. The UDT Agent Type Designer dialog increments the Scan size of the resultant UDT after each property is added or modified. Specifying the Status Bits for your UDT In the Selected UDT - Status Bit section: Select the required status bit/s from the Status bits list, do the following for each, as required: Rename this status bit, by t

the Status Bits for your UDT In the Selected UDT - Status Bit section: Select the required status bit/s from the Status bits list, do the following for each, as required: Rename this status bit, by typing in the required name in the Status bit name edit field - you can use a maximum of 18 characters for this name. Note1: The “Status bit xx” naming convention is ONLY used for display purposes in this dialog. Therefore any status bit that is NOT renamed will not be added as a status bit name within the UDT agent instances. Note2: If a customised status bit name is cleared, the “Status bit xx” naming convention will be re-applied. Specify the required expression to calculate the value of this status bit, in the Status bit expression edit field, which define the state of this UDT that needs to be alarmed. For details, see Creating UDT Status Bit Expressions . Therefore the expected expression result should be True (1) or False (0), Examples of such expressions are: Slot(value) > 95 Slot(Open) & (Slot(value) > 95) The following expression language used for this feature is exactly the same as the expression language used in conditional alarming. If necessary, configure another UDT agent

If necessary, configure another UDT agent by repeating steps 2 to 12. IMPORTANT: Ensure that the Agent Server is stopped. In the New Output section, double click on Constant . This opens the Name Constant dialog. Type in the name of the required constant in the Constant Name edit box. Tip1: You can use any character for the name of this constant. Tip2: This name is case sensitive, because it is an output name. Tip3: It is recommended to use a descriptive name, which is as concise as possible - although the name of the constant is not limited. The specified name is added to the Outputs section. Specify the value of this constant by double-clicking the value column to the right of its name and typing in the required value. Note1: The value of this constant must be numeric. er-defined constant on a graphic form or use it within other spiders, it is necessary to connect it to the required property (Data spider) or spider, by means of a silk. Creating variable data elements Top Creating variable data elements Create variable data elements for any data elements that you need to dynamically the name of and if necessary to configure their values. Example: In this example a variable data element concatenates the {AgentServer}.{PUMP} inputs to dynamically specify the value of any pump on any Agent Server, which are specified via graphic form aliases. To create one or more variable data elements If necessary, add and/or select the required Variable Data Element spider and/or open its configuration view. For details, see Adding Variable Data Element spiders or Selecting spiders or Displaying spider configuration views . ified name in {} to the Inputs section. In the New Output section, double-click the + Variable DE entry. Creating wizards Top Creating wizards You have two main options when creating wizards, typically in the Enterprise Manager window: Either create the wizard from scratch: in this case, right click a project or folder and select Create Wizard . Note: When creating a wizard from scratch, the default size of the wizard is 200 by 200 pixels, since wizards are typically small by nature. If necessary customise this default, by using the Designer.CONFIG setting in the Misc group, called DefaultWizardsize . Or convert an existing graphic form into a wizard: in this case, open the required graphic form and select the Save as Wizard graphic form toolbar button. Then use the Substitution configuration dialog to create ALL the necessary substitutions for this new wizard. Tip: When you substitute a data element that is used in numerous locations within the graphic form, all these locations use the specified substitution name. The graphic form toolbar contains the Optimise Graphic Form size button (at the end), which resizes the wizard to the size of the added controls and vectors, so that there are no overlaps at the top, bottom, left or right sides. -->

Criteria for Creating Tag Groups Top Criteria for Creating Tag Groups Tag groups are primarily used manage the communication settings for the tags whose values need to be communicated to or from the remote Agent Servers via their associated WanServers. For details, see Tag Groups . The following criteria are used for creating different tag groups: Physical location: Tags from different parts of the process or plant, can be placed in different groups. Polling Requirements: Tags that require different poll rates need to be placed in the appropriately configured groups. Communication type (Read/Write requirements): Tags requiring the same read / write ability need to be within the same group, as follows: Tags within Normal groups are only able to have their tag values read i.e. to have one-way communication from WanServer to WanClient Tags within Control groups are able to have their tag values read and written i.e. to have two-way communication from WanServer to WanClient AND also from WanClient to WanServer. -->

Current Operational Status Top Current Operational Status The Tag Monitor utility can display current values of one or more tag values from a particular Agent Server, in tabular and trend format, without having to specifically draw a mimic or create a trend to do so. For details, see Monitoring Tags (Values) . The status bar of this utility displays the following details, concerning the status of the tag monitoring process: The first text box (from the left), displays the operational status of the tag monitoring process i.e. whether it has Started or Stopped . The second text box, displays the operational phase of the tag monitoring process, for instance Editing (when Stopped ) or Monitoring (when Started). Other transitory phases include Opening , Subscribing , Desubscribing , Closing and Delaying . The third text, displays the status of the currently connected Agent Server, for instance AS OK when it is operating correctly or AS ERROR , when it is not. For details, see Connecting to the required Agent Server . The fourth text box displays the total amount of memory committed by the computer, for information purposes only. The fifth text box displays the number of updates being re

the required Agent Server . The fourth text box displays the total amount of memory committed by the computer, for information purposes only. The fifth text box displays the number of updates being received per second, for instance 68 updates @ 1 subs/s. -->

Custom Agent Usage Guidelines Top Custom Agent Usage Guidelines Since the introduction of the Custom agent a number of customers have put this agent to good use, which is what it is there for. But as with all tools there is both a proper and improper way of using them and the method used directly affects the achievable results. Therefore the following points or guidelines are recommended concerning the prudent use of this agent: If the Custom agent is used purely as a pure container agent i.e. no scripting attached, this should not cause any problems. When using large numbers of intelligent Custom agents (those containing scripts): Always monitor the virtual memory usage of the AS.EXE (Agent Server) process (from startup) during the design and commissioning phase - typically by using the Windows Performance Monitor. Since Adroit is a 32 bit application, if you have installed a 64 bit operating system then when you run the default Performance Monitor (PERFMON.EXE) all the counters for Adroit will be missing, because the 64 bit version of PERFMON is being run which can only load 64bit counter dlls! Therefore, in order to force Windows to load the 32 bit version of PERFMON, open the C

droit will be missing, because the 64 bit version of PERFMON is being run which can only load 64bit counter dlls! Therefore, in order to force Windows to load the 32 bit version of PERFMON, open the Command Prompt and specify the following statement: mmc /32 perfmon.msc As this KPI determines when you should convert your intelligent Custom agents into properly written C++ agents, as follows: For 32-bit operating systems , which allocate a maximum of 2 GB per process, when the virtual memory used by the AS.EXE process: exceeds 1.0 GB then you SHOULD convert your intelligent Custom agents to C++ agents. approaches 1.5 GB then you MUST convert your intelligent Custom agents to C++ agents. For 64-bit operating systems , which allocate a maximum of 4 GB per process, when the virtual memory used by the AS.EXE process: exceeds 2.0 GB then you SHOULD convert your intelligent Custom agents to C++ agents. approaches 3.0 GB then you MUST convert your intelligent Custom agents to C++ agents. Always monitor the CPU usage of the AS.EXE process. Natively, the AS.EXE process runs at about 1-2% CPU load, very rarely over 5%. If your custom agent configuration causes the CPU load to exceed 10-20%, t

s monitor the CPU usage of the AS.EXE process. Natively, the AS.EXE process runs at about 1-2% CPU load, very rarely over 5%. If your custom agent configuration causes the CPU load to exceed 10-20%, then you should ALSO consider converting your intelligent Custom agents into properly written C++ agents. Ensure that the code used to create an intelligent Custom agent is optimised. Since EACH instance of this agent uses the SAME CODE to perform its functions. So when the code is poorly written, EVERY error is exacerbated, which can reduce the performance of the entire Adroit system. Custom agents normally have multiple slots scanned, which is no problem in itself. But please ensure that ONLY the required INDIVIDUAL slots are output enabled and NOT the ENTIRE Custom agent. Click for more details: Note: The scan dialog does this by default. Historically, users have simply output enabled the whole agent and this practice was acceptable because, typically, only one slot was scanned in the analog, digital or marshal agents. However, when an agent has multiple slots scanned AND is globally output enabled, any changes to ANY of this agent’s slot values will cause a write message to the scan

alog, digital or marshal agents. However, when an agent has multiple slots scanned AND is globally output enabled, any changes to ANY of this agent’s slot values will cause a write message to the scanning subsystem resulting in scan degradation. In the case of Custom agents the extent of this scanning degradation depends on the number of Custom agents being used and the level of activity on these agents. Note: This rule also applies when configuring scan inhibit. How to Use the Custom Agent Designer -->

To customise the adding of default events to graphic form scripts Create a profile or edit the profile that applies to the current user. Dimmed: prompts the user, when the required control or graphic form is double clicked, as to whether event handler scripting should be added to the graphic form script or not.
