text: Customizing alarm colors Top Customizing alarm colors As in Adroit , you can customise the colors assigned to the alarms, by the AlarmViewer control, to represent their states can be customised. The following Adroit defaults, are initially used by this control: Note: This assumes that the Priority colors setting is NOT being used. The background color indicates whether the alarm is active (set) [red] or inactive (cleared) [green]. Note: This corresponds to the Activity column of the alarm list, which is either 1 if active or 0 if inactive. Tip: The colors of both the selected active and inactive alarms are typically the same as those used in the legacy alarm viewer (light red and light green and both these colors can be customised, via the SelectedActivecolor and SelectedInactivecolor properties. The foreground (text) color indicates whether the alarm is in an unacknowledged [yellow] or acknowledged [white] state. Note: This corresponds to the Acknowledge column of the alarm list, which is either 0 if unacknowledged or 2 if acknowledged. Note: When an alarm condition has returns to normal and is either acknowledged or not (if it requires no acknowledgment), then it is immediately r

h is either 0 if unacknowledged or 2 if acknowledged. Note: When an alarm condition has returns to normal and is either acknowledged or not (if it requires no acknowledgment), then it is immediately removed from the alarm list. To customise the colors used to represent alarm states: If necessary, add this control to the required graphic form. For details, see Adding AlarmViewer controls . In the Design workspace , select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the required AlarmViewer control. Open the Properties tool window. Select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the Alarmcolors property, which is listed in the Alarm category. Click the browse button in the value column to the left of this property. This will display the alarm color selection dialog. Note: Only one color can be selected at a time. EITHER click on the required Foreground or Background button to configure its associated colors. This displays the color dialog to select or define the required color. See Selecting colors . Tip: The color of the button indicates the currently configured color. OR c

nfigure its associated colors. This displays the color dialog to select or define the required color. See Selecting colors . Tip: The color of the button indicates the currently configured color. OR configure the Priority colors section, so that operators can see the alarm priority in addition to its acknowledged state to know which alarms to react to first. Note: These colors are ONLY displayed if the ShowPrioritycolors property is enabled. -->

Customizing alarm columns Top Customizing alarm columns You can customise both the columns and their widths that are displayed by the AlarmViewer control, when listing each alarm. Tip: To quickly display or hide columns, double click the required column to add it to the other list. To customise the alarm columns and/or their widths: If necessary, add this control to the required graphic form. For details, see Adding AlarmViewer controls . In the Design workspace , select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the AlarmViewer control. Open the Properties tool window. Select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the AlarmColumnInfo property, which is listed in the Alarm category. Click the browse button in the value column to the left of this property. This will display the alarm column selection dialog. Example: To hide a column from display: Select the column in the left Visible Columns list that should be hidden. Click the button to add it to the right Hidden Columns list. To display a previously hidden column: Select the column in the right Hidden Columns list th

ft Visible Columns list that should be hidden. Click the button to add it to the right Hidden Columns list. To display a previously hidden column: Select the column in the right Hidden Columns list that should be displayed. Click the button to add it to the left Visible Columns list. To specify the required width of a column: Select the column in the left Visible Columns list. Specify the required number of pixels in the Width field, in the central property pane, the default value depends on the selected column. To change the order in which a column is displayed in this control: Select the column in the left list, whose order of display needs to be changed. Either click the Move up button to move this column up the column listing. This will move to column closer to the left of the control, so that it is more prominent or easier to be displayed. Or click the Move Down button to move this column down the column listing. This will move to column closer to the right of the control, so that it is less prominent or harder to be displayed. -->

Customizing auto logoff settings Top Customizing auto logoff settings Profiles can ensure that the assigned users are automatically logged off the SmartUI Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. after a specific period of inactivity. Note: This is an added security feature often required by particular industries. For instance, this is required to comply with CFR The Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) is the codification of the general and permanent rules published in the Federal Register by the executive departments and agencies of the Federal Government. 21 (Food and Drugs) requirements. Tip: Instead of completely logging off after the inactivity timeout, you can specify a default user that should be logged on instead. To customise the auto logoff settings Note: If you want to DISABLE this auto logoff then uncheck the Logoff users assigned to this profile checkbox, which is checked by default. Create a profile or edit the profile that applies to the current user. Tip: Any user not associated with a profile has the Default profile applied to them. For details, see Default profiles . In the Profile Configuration dialo

he profile that applies to the current user. Tip: Any user not associated with a profile has the Default profile applied to them. For details, see Default profiles . In the Profile Configuration dialog, select the Profile Properties dialog, from the left pane. Ensure that the Logoff users assigned to this profile checkbox is checked. Specify the required period of inactivity, in seconds, during which no mouse or keyboard activity should occur to enforce this log off. By default this is 600 seconds (10 minutes). Instead of completely logging off after the inactivity timeout, you can specify a default user that should be logged on instead - simply check the Revert to Default User checkbox and then specify the required User Name and Password of this default user in the edit boxes. Related links Creating profiles Editing profiles Default profiles Applying profiles to allowed users or groups Working with profiles -->

Customizing connections and work environment Top Customizing connections and work environment When configuring a user profile, the Automatically Update Profile setting saves the following Designer settings: all the SmartUI Server connections made within the Enterprise Manager , using their most recently used settings. the positions of the menus, tool windows and toolbars within the SmartUI Designer when the associated user logs off. any properties and/or events added to the default menu of specific graphic form controls, used when dragging data onto controls. all custom (third party) form components recently added to the Toolbox . WARNING! This setting is applied per profile and not per user. So the work environment and/or connection settings configured for the user who logs off the SmartUI Designer last are displayed for ALL the users of this profile. Customizing report templates Top Customizing report templates A common reason for customizing the GENERIC report templates is to add your company logos to its header. text: Customizing the work environment Customizing the work environment The Smart UI Operator displays configured graphic forms, so they can be operated or interacted with and allows you to customize the working environment, as follows: The display and the amount of interaction that a user has with the Smart UI Operator window, is determined by: the user profile configured for this user in the Smart UI Designer. However, when this is NOT configured to use the default setting (typically this occurs on Windows Server 2003 although can occur on other operating systems that provide this such as Windows XP etc.), then the Agent Server can become unable to read the HASP at start up, which will cause the Agent Server to hang or fail and/or to display HASP exceptions in the Agent Server window. To check whether DEP is enabled on your computer and to ensure that it is appropriately configured for Adroit to function correctly, please perform the following steps: Right click on My Computer and select Properties . Select the Advanced tab and click the Settings button under the Performance heading. This will display the Performance Options dialog. If not, the problem lies elsewhere. Data Logging Compression Methods Top Data Logging Compression Methods Logging values is an event-based function, by default, a value is logged whenever it changes. When logging values, you can specify both a time and value deadband (in the Datalog agent) to reduce the number of records that you log for a value which effectively 'compresses' your log files so you are able to store more data on the same storage medium. Using the Value deadband: Values are ONLY logged if their change in value EXCEEDS the specified deadband value. Hence when the value of a logged point does not exceed the previously logged value by more than the deadband, the value is not logged. Using the Time deadband: One of the following Compression Method algorithms is used to determine which value is logged, if the logged value changes MORE THAN ONCE during the specified deadband period: IMPORTANT: To use a logging Compression Method, you need to use a Time logging deadband that is greater than 0. Actual The logged value is the value at the end of the specified Time deadband. Average a time-weighted average is maintained for all the changes that occur and this is logged at the end of the specified Time deadband.

alue is the value at the end of the specified Time deadband. Average a time-weighted average is maintained for all the changes that occur and this is logged at the end of the specified Time deadband. Minimum The lowest or minimum value is logged at the end of the specified Time deadband. Maximum The highest or maximum value is logged at the end of the specified Time deadband. Of the provided methods, the Average method is recommended, since it calculates a time-weighted average of all the values that were recorded during the Time deadband period and this average is then logged at the end of this period. For this reason a 1-hour average (as opposed to a 1-hour interval raw log) will provide a more accurate representation of what happened in the plant, than the same raw log. Since the raw log value will only represent the instantaneous value in the hour, not the average for the hour. -->

Data Specification Method for Statistical Agent Top Data Specification Method for Statistical Agent The method of data sampling offered by the Statistical agent is called STREAMING, whereby all the collected input values are placed in one sample for analysis. Each input value may be collected on an event basis, and is called a STREAM EVENT. The Stream Event method takes the input agent’s values, either when triggered by another agent, or when its input value changes, and calculates the statistical data (Maximum, Minimum, Average, Standard Deviation, Total and Rate) for all the values collected, treating the values as being part of a single sample. -->

Data Structure of an Agent Top Data Structure of an Agent Most agents are designed to contain multiple items of data, which are referred to as agent attributes. Most of these attributes are accessible to clients of the Agent Server as slots of the agent. For details, see About Agent Data (Slots) . An agent's "state", at any instant in time, is defined as the collective values of all its data. Agents have both generic and type-specific data. Generic or header slots are found in all types of agents. Note: The overall status of an agent can be determined from its status slot, which is common to all agent types. For details, see Agent Status . Examples of header slots are: agentDescription for describing purpose of the agent status a 32 bit word recording agent status Type-specific slots pertain only to agents of the specific type. An agent's "state", at any instant in time, is defined as the collective values of all its data. Agents have both generic and type-specific data. Generic or header slots are found in all types of agents. Note: The overall status of an agent can be determined from its status slot, which is common to all agent types. For details, see Agent Status . Examples of header slots are: agentDescription for describing purpose of the agent status a 32 bit word recording agent status Type-specific slots pertain only to agents of the specific type. Database Behaviour Top Database Behaviour The Database Behaviour functionality provides you with an easy method of accessing data that has been returned after running a database query and the result displayed on a control or vector placed on a graphic form. The database query can be processed in two ways: A Database Query in the Spider Configuration Although you can currently use queries on a graphic form, the setup is normally done in the Spider Configuration. Warning: This setup is sometimes quite complex. Requires you to be a relatively advanced or experienced user to successfully set up a query to link it to a control or vector to achieve the desired result. A Database Query using the Database Behaviour provides the following advantage It removes the complexity you would encounter in the spiders and silks to create and successfully execute queries in an OLEDB Data Source. It automatically determines the spider configuration required for a selected query and query type, and also its target control or vector. It creates the relevant spiders and silks in the background that are required to execute a query successfully. Note: Previously, you were required to go to the Spider Config

target control or vector. It creates the relevant spiders and silks in the background that are required to execute a query successfully. Note: Previously, you were required to go to the Spider Configuration workspace to manipulate spiders and silks manually. It also lets you easily edit a current spider configuration which is related to executing a query. Includes deleting the entire configuration, not leaving any spiders or silks behind that might have to be managed manually. Configuring a database query Current behaviours work on the principle that you must first select a control or vector, which displays the relevant behaviour types available for the selected control or vector. You can select and configure a behaviour required for the control or vector. The above process is not suitable for all Database Behaviour action scenarios and requires modification to allow for a slightly different flow for the following reason: It is possible that without a Database Behaviour action, you may use the current configuration options available with spiders and silks, to successfully execute a query without interacting with a control or vector at all. For example, an Update , Delete or Insert

For example, an Update , Delete or Insert query can be triggered through the following methods, Propagate at Startup or Trigger from event (for example, the Form.Click event) . Configuring query parameters It is possible to create queries where not all the parts of the query are known at the time of creating it. It is especially true that you might want to generate dynamic query results by supplying or inserting different values into the WHERE clause of the query just before the query is executed. To help facilitate this process, the Query Spider currently provides inputs for parameters that can be driven either by a default value or from the output silk of another spider, such as a Property Spider of the Text property of a Textbox or Label control. Warning: This type of configuration is currently a manual process and requires an advanced understanding of spiders to correctly and successfully achieve this. The Database Behaviour solves this by giving all types of users, from beginners to advanced, access to this level of configuration without having to know and understand how to do it manually. The following steps guides you through a simple process to follow and shows you how to configure the source inputs for each parameter in the query: STEP 1: Selecting a query that contains parameters Access to the setup of parameters for a query starts with the sel

w and shows you how to configure the source inputs for each parameter in the query: STEP 1: Selecting a query that contains parameters Access to the setup of parameters for a query starts with the selection of a query that contains parameters. When a valid query is selected, the Parameters tab becomes visible. By default, an error icon indicates that errors exist, implying that values must be provided for the parameters present in the query. The values that must be provided should consist of the following types: The source of the input for the parameter. Component Property is selected by default. The value of the input for the parameter. The parameter is blank by default. The Default value of the parameter. The parameter is blank by default and only applies when the Propagate at startup option is selected. Database Folder Top Database Folder The WanClient application requires a folder to store the files that contain the tag link database, which it manages. For further details on what this database is and what it contains, see Tag Link Databases . By default, this folder is called ‘WanlinkDB’ and is created as a sub-folder off the Adroit installation folder, so its default location is ‘ C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit \WanLinkDB’. However, an alternate location and / or name can be specified for this folder, if necessary, by adding the following registry key to the Adroit registry: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Wanlink Then add the following String value to this registry key and set it to the fully qualified path of the desired folder: (REG_) SZ DatabaseFolder = the fully qualified path of the desired folder e.g. C:\WanClient\Database Note: If this specified folder does not exist, then it will be created as soon as WanClient is launched. WARNING! It is recommended that ONLY advanced computer users should configure the registry, as any mistakes made can severely affect the operation of your computer. -->

Datalog Catchup Slots Omitted by the Configuration Dialog Top Datalog catch-up Slots Omitted by the Configuration Dialog The progress slot: This displays the progress of the current synchronization process as a percentage of datalog agents that have been synchronised on that Agent Server in the cluster. The tagRestoring slot: This displays the datalog agent that is currently being synchronised by the systemDatalog agent. The information slot: This contains general information regarding the synchronization process including error messages if an error occurs or if the synchronization process is stopped unexpectedly, for instance by putting a 0 unto the start slot, or if the cluster partner is unavailable. The realTimeRate slot: This indicates how many points were datalogged by all of the datalog agents in the last second. The catchupRate slot: This indicates the rate at which data points are being merged into the local datalogs from the cluster partner. The totalRate slot: This is the sum of the realTimeRate and the catchupRate slots. The Qfree slot: This represents the percentage of the datalog buffer queue that is currently free. -->

text: Datasource-specific Server settings Top Datasource-specific Server settings The SmartUI Server provides the following settings that apply to specific datasources: Server Scripts datasources The MinimumScriptSchedulingTime SmartUI Server setting specifies the minimum interval time (in seconds) for scheduling of a script in a SmartUI Server Script Datasource. This prevents the CPU on the Server computer from being overused (so that it is not able to attend to critical tasks) and guards against poorly written scripts. The default minimum interval is 30 seconds. OLE DB datasources The OLEDBCommandTimeOut SmartUI Server setting specifies the maximum time, in milliseconds, allowed for the SmartUI OLEDB datasource to respond to an OLEDB command. By default this is set to 10 seconds, although it can be increased for more complex OLEDB commands. -->

Date Agent - Slot Details Top Date Agent - Slot Details The Date Agent stores a date and time value. It has the capability of returning the value in a number of ways as depicted by the slots. If TRUE is put into setTime , the date agent will set itself to the current time. The user may change the time stored in the date agent by writing to any slot, except the asciiTime slot. The user may format the way the date and time stored by the agent is displayed in the asciiTime slot, by setting the format slot in a specific way. Note: You should never externally manipulate the localtime slot of the Date agent from a mimic using an operator action. The localtime slot must be used for viewing the time and the ucttime slot MUST be used for manipulating the datetime value. This is by design of the Date agent only. All other time slots in Adroit can be viewed and edited directly. It is generally a bad idea to store an alphanumeric or broken down time in the Agent Server, because clients may exist in different time zones. This is why all times native to the Agent Server are stored in UTC stands for Coordinated Universal Time, which is a time standard that couples Greenwich Mean Time (GMT), which

n different time zones. This is why all times native to the Agent Server are stored in UTC stands for Coordinated Universal Time, which is a time standard that couples Greenwich Mean Time (GMT), which is based solely on the Earth's inconsistent rotation rate, with the highly accurate International Atomic Time (TAI). time. If clients in different time zones read the same time slot, their time displays should differ. If the conversion to local time is done on the Agent Server level, as it is done in this agent, the user should take care to be totally aware that the time conversion to local time is done in the time zone of that Agent Server, and not in the time zone of the client the user is using. Date and Time Settings Top Date and Time Settings By using the Date and Time option you can change the date, time and time zone of your system's clock. It is important that your system date and time are always accurate as many of the Adroit applications use this to record information and to print reports. For example the Event viewer and Scheduler. To set the date and time . WARNING: Never turn the PC clock backwards because certain internal transactions made after the back-tracking are ignored or rejected due to their timestamp now being "suddenly in the future". This will cause erratic Behaviour in Adroit . The Support Desk cannot deal with problems caused by rolling the system clock backwards. Golden Rule: Don't fiddle with your PC clock!! -->

DbAccess Transaction Scheduling and Triggering Top DbAccess Transaction Scheduling and Triggering This enables the remote execution of the configured transaction by the DbAccess Agent. The following combinations of triggering and scheduling are configured in the dialog box which is displayed after clicking the Edit… button in the main edit window of the DbAccess Agent. The remote-execution mechanisms of the transactions are: Triggering only: This is used when the transactions are only required after a particular condition has been met by the required tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). /s. This requires configuring one or more triggering expressions . When one of the conditions, in the list of triggers, is met – then database transactions are executed by the DbAccess Agent. Scheduling only: This is used when the transactions are required at a set period, which is set by the user. It is also possible to synchronise the start of the scheduling at a specified time. This requires the scheduling to be configured . Triggering and Scheduling: In this case a transaction will be executed when its scheduled and whenever a condition in the list of triggers is met

time. This requires the scheduling to be configured . Triggering and Scheduling: In this case a transaction will be executed when its scheduled and whenever a condition in the list of triggers is met. This requires configuring one or more triggering expressions and configuring the scheduling . (Note the And only if triggered option remains disabled for this option) Scheduling if Triggered: In this case the scheduled transaction will only be executed if a condition in the list of triggers is met at the configured transaction ‘Run Every’ time. This effectively applies a time deadband to the triggering, preventing a flood of triggers that would initiate multiple transactions. This requires configuring one or more triggering expressions and configuring the scheduling and enabling the And only if triggered option. -->

DbAccess Trigger Configuration Top DbAccess Trigger Configuration In order to use triggering as an option, at least one triggering expression is required, which involves a tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). and a triggering condition. Each triggering expression consists of the following columns: Index column: This is added to each trigger automatically and is only used as a means of reference. Trigger column: This contains the tag that is be compared to the triggering condition, to determine when the transactions are to be executed. Either type in the tag directly into this column or click on the column and use the displayed browse button (...) to browse in required the tag. Condition column: This contains the triggering condition, namely: when zero, when non-zero and when changed. Buttons To add a new triggering expression, simply click the button. To remove a triggering expression, click the button. -->

DBQuery Agent Slot Detail Top DBQuery Agent Slot Detail The DBQuery agent contains various slot categories. Select the options below to view more information on each category. DBQuery Configuration slots The following slots are used for configuration and are saved to the WGP file. Slot name Slot type Slot description connection VARSTRING The OLE DB connection string | “global” can be selected to use the Agent Server’s audit connection string. customQuery VARSTRING An option for a valid SQL query statement to be performed on the database connection. If a custom query is specified, this will always be executed instead of the built-in SELECT query statement. disableOnStandby BOOLEAN When set to [1], the slot indicates that the transaction should not be executed on the standby server. enable BOOLEAN When set to [1] the slot is enabled to Start or alternatively, when set to [0] to disable the agent. interval INTEGER An optional number of seconds may be entered that will determine the execution interval of the transaction. A value of [0] (default) disables this feature. method INTEGER Sets a trigger tag check value. You can set method value to one of the following: 0 – Execute the query

ion interval of the transaction. A value of [0] (default) disables this feature. method INTEGER Sets a trigger tag check value. You can set method value to one of the following: 0 – Execute the query when the trigger tag value goes to zero. 1 – Execute the query when the trigger tag value leaves zero. 2 – Execute the query when the trigger tag value changes. The default value is [1]. tableName STRING The name of the table that the built-in SELECT statement should use. This is available only if the custom query is not used. tagList LIST Sets the list of tag values to be retrieved by the built-in SELECT statement. This is available only if the custom query is not used. triggerTag TAGNAME The trigger tag to be used. Indicates the trigger tag used in conjunction with the trigger method. This is available for trigger methods only. pulseWidth INTEGER Edit this slot to set the pulse length of the Status slot: SuccessPulse [StatusBit18] . The pulse length is set in milliseconds (ms). A value of [0] will disable the pulse. Note: Any value less than 5 ms will always cause a minimum pulse width of around 5 ms. The default value is [100] ms. whereClause VARSTRING Sets the WHERE clause that wil

f [0] will disable the pulse. Note: Any value less than 5 ms will always cause a minimum pulse width of around 5 ms. The default value is [100] ms. whereClause VARSTRING Sets the WHERE clause that will be applied to the built-in SELECT statement. DBQuery Information slots The following slots are used for information only and are NOT saved to the WGP file. Slot name Slot type Slot description badTransactions INTEGER A slot value that is incremented after every unsuccessful transaction and denotes the number of bad transactions since starting the agent server. goodTransactions INTEGER A slot value that is incremented after every successful transaction and denotes the number of good transactions since starting the agent server. lastDuration INTEGER A slot value that represents the duration of time in milliseconds that the query took to execute the last transaction. lastError VARSTRING This slot captures the last OLE DB transaction error. Successful transactions will display “None”. lastErrorQuery VARSTRING This slot captures the SQL Query that caused the last OLE DB transaction error. This value is never cleared and is only valid if the FAILED status bit (StatusBit21 ) is currently se

rorQuery VARSTRING This slot captures the SQL Query that caused the last OLE DB transaction error. This value is never cleared and is only valid if the FAILED status bit (StatusBit21 ) is currently set to on [1]. lastQuery VARSTRING This slot captures the last SQL Query that was executed. lastTime TIME This slot captures the last time a transaction was executed. resetRunNow BOOLEAN When set to ‘1’ this slot will cause the agent to automatically reset the runNow slot value to ‘0’ after a transaction has completed. The default value is set to enabled. This should be disabled when the agent communicates the runNow slot value directly to the PLC. runNow BOOLEAN When set to ‘1’ the agent will execute a transaction ONLY if the agent is enabled AND connected to the database. totalTransactions INTEGER This slot tallies the total number of transactions executed since the agent server was last started. DBQuery Runtime slots The following slots are used for runtime operations and are NOT saved to the WGP file. Slot name Slot type Slot description catchupData RAWBYTES For internal use during real-time catch-up. DBQuery Status slots The following slots indicate the status of certain DBQuery age

the WGP file. Slot name Slot type Slot description catchupData RAWBYTES For internal use during real-time catch-up. DBQuery Status slots The following slots indicate the status of certain DBQuery agent functions. Status name Status description Connected Also known as StatusBit16 This slot is set to on [1], if the Agent is connected to the database as of the last transaction. If the agent is not enabled, the slot will always be set off [0]. The slot will be also be set to off [0] should the agent become disconnected from the database. However, this slot will automatically be set on [1] if the agent is enabled and the agent is able to reconnect to the database. Important: It is important to note that some transactions may take up to one minute to transact, if there is a problem with the connection. Disconnected Also known as StatusBit17 This slot is set to on [0], if the Agent is not connected to the database possibly due to a last transaction error or that the database is not available. Note: Be aware that if the agent is not enabled, this slot will always be set on [1]. Failed Also known as StatusBit21 This slot will be set on [1] if the last transaction failed. Will be reset imme

. Note: Be aware that if the agent is not enabled, this slot will always be set on [1]. Failed Also known as StatusBit21 This slot will be set on [1] if the last transaction failed. Will be reset immediately prior to a transaction being executed. FailPulse Also known as StatusBit19 A short pulse is generated on a transaction failure. This slot will be set on [1] for a very short period (approximately 100 ms) , if the last transaction failed. Succeeded Also known as StatusBit20 This slot will be set on [1] if the last transaction succeeded. Will be reset immediately prior to a transaction being executed. SuccessPulse Also known as StatusBit18 A short pulse is generated on a successful transaction. The default length of this pulse can configured using the pulseWidth configuration slot. This slot will be set on [1] for a very short period (approximately 100 ms or as set in the pulseWidth slot) , if the last transaction succeeded. -->

Debugging the script object Top Debugging the script object Before the script object this contains a script and provides its self-contained environment within which it is run. of a Script Engine spider is run, it is first compiled and only if there are no compilation errors, is it executed, after which any run time errors are identified. Note: The script will only run properly once both the compilation and run time errors are fixed. To identify and fix errors in the script object If necessary, select the required Script Engine spider and/or open its configuration view. In the Outputs section, examine both the Errors and Runtime errors outputs, which record both the compilation and the run time errors respectively, which occurred when the script was last run. If either of the numbers displayed by these outputs are not zero, then click the Launch Script Editor button, in the Inputs section. This opens the Script editor and allows you to view the descriptions of these errors in its Output window so that you may be able to locate and rectify them. For details, see Working with the script editor . -->

Debugging Tools in the Status Bar of the Adroit Script Editor Top Debugging Tools in the Status Bar of the Adroit Script Editor The status bar of the Adroit Script Editor is composed of two compartments: The first compartment indicates the current location of the cursor, ONLY when the cursor is moved around the editor window using the keyboard. The cursor location is indicated by the current line number followed by a colon ":", followed by the current column number. Tip: This is useful when locating compilation errors that are indicated by the second compartment. Note: This cursor location is NOT updated when using the mouse to move around the Adroit Script Editor. The second compartment indicates the status of the last script file that was compiled , either indicating: That an error occurred during compilation, giving a description and location of the first error located in the script file e.g. That the file compiled successfully e.g. -->

text: Decrementing numerical values Top Decrementing numerical values Decrease a numerical value by a configurable amount. Note: This action is ONLY performed ONCE irrespective of how many times this spider is triggered, until its input values change or when the required Action Type changes. Tip: This action can change the current template set within the Template Set spider. For details, see Template Set spiders . To decrease a numerical value by a specific amount If necessary, add and/or select the required Operator Action spider and/or open its configuration view. For details, see Adding Operator Action spiders . In the Inputs section: Open the Action Type list box and select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. Decrement . Specify the numeric value on which this action is to be performed, in the Input Value input. Note1: This value can either be supplied by another spider or Data spider (e.g. property or data element) via a silk, for details, see Creating silks , or it can be typed in manually. Note2: Only Boolean or numerical values can be typed in. Tip: When typing in a value manually, double-click the value column to the

, for details, see Creating silks , or it can be typed in manually. Note2: Only Boolean or numerical values can be typed in. Tip: When typing in a value manually, double-click the value column to the right of the input name in the Inputs section and type in the required value. Specify the numeric value by which the Input Value is to be decreased, in the Increment/Decrement Value input, either via a silk or by typing it in manually. When this spider is triggered, the value of the Increment/Decrement Value input is subtracted from to the Input Value input value and this result is assigned to the Output Value output in Outputs section. For details on triggering spiders, see Triggering spiders . Note1: The Boolean Value output in Outputs section, contains the Boolean equivalent of this Output Value output i.e. FALSE when it is zero, otherwise TRUE. Note2: This operation is only performed if the Input Value and Increment/Decrement Value inputs contain numerical / Boolean values. Note3: If a String value is supplied then the spider will try to convert the string value to a number before using it. If it cannot be converted, the input is meaningless and will not be used. -->

Default Alarm Management Queries Top Default Alarm Management Queries The following queries are displayed by the View data and unless otherwise noted the View graph dialogs: Tip: You can change the KPI values that are used by these default queries, so that they better comply with your specific requirements. Click for more details: Click the Edit KPI's button in the Edit AlarmManagement agent dialog; in the Edit Alarm Management KPI values dialog, double click the appropriate KPI (row) to change its value. Current incidents: All incidents whose alarmed conditions are still active and/or which have NOT been fully responded to. In other words they still need to be acknowledged and/or have their required reasons specified and/or have their required notes specified. On the basis of 6 alarms per hour this should never have more than 6 incidents under normal operating conditions or 60 under abnormal operating conditions. Note: This query is NOT displayed by the View graph dialog. Historical incidents: All incidents whose alarmed conditions have returned to normal and which have been fully responded to, if necessary, for the specified period of time. In other words they have been acknowled

ncidents: All incidents whose alarmed conditions have returned to normal and which have been fully responded to, if necessary, for the specified period of time. In other words they have been acknowledged and/or had their required reasons specified and/or had their required notes specified. This can be used to analyse your alarm configuration during set time periods. Note: This query is NOT displayed by the View graph dialog. Historical incidents by operator: Incidents which have been logged against the specified operator. This can be used to analyse the effectiveness of your operators. Note: This query is NOT displayed by the View graph dialog. Historical incidents by category: Incidents which have occurred for a specific category. This can be used to analyse your alarm configuration for specific process areas. Note: This query is NOT displayed by the View graph dialog. Outstanding reasons and notes: All incidents that still need reasons and/or notes specified. Only those current incidents that have their Reasons required and/or Notes required settings enabled are added to this list. Note: This query is NOT displayed by the View graph dialog. Incident count per hour: The total numb

ents that have their Reasons required and/or Notes required settings enabled are added to this list. Note: This query is NOT displayed by the View graph dialog. Incident count per hour: The total number of incidents that occur over each hour of the specified duration. In other words this query returns the number of logged incidents per hour for the specified duration. Typically each number should be between 6 (normal conditions) to 60 (abnormal conditions). But different industries have different standards. Burst rate: The number of incidents that occur in a 10 minute window. Calculation: Burst rate = 6 * Maximum alarm count in a 10 minute period. (this is calculated as a per hour count, hence the 6 *) This is an important measure of the usability of an alarm system and the operator's capability to deal with alarms. Typically this should be between 1 (normal conditions) to 10 (abnormal conditions). But different industries have different standards. Percent upset: The number of hours where there are more than 30 incidents per hour. If you want to specify a more appropriate maximum number of alarms, then change the PUC [Percent upset count] entry in the Adr_AM_UserKPIs table. Calcula

ere there are more than 30 incidents per hour. If you want to specify a more appropriate maximum number of alarms, then change the PUC [Percent upset count] entry in the Adr_AM_UserKPIs table. Calculation: Percent upset = 100 * [Number of hours where alarms exceeds 30/hour]/[Total number of hours]. This is a measurement of alarm overload on operators, as follows: Overloaded > 50% Reactive 25%-50% Stable 5%-25% Robust 1%-5% Predictive < 1%. Priority distribution: The priority distribution for incidents occurring over a period of time. Typically this should be 5% high priority alarms (>Normal priority), 15% medium priority alarms (=Normal priority) and 80% low priority alarms (<Normal priority). But different industries have different standards. Standing alarms: The number of current incidents at the end of an hour. Typically this should be 9. But different industries have different standards. Most frequent alarms (count by type): The most frequent alarms over time, filtered only by the type. The top 20 of these alarms can account for almost 50% of total alarm generation. If properly reviewed, you will find that most of these incidents should not be classified as alarms at all, since

Default profiles Top Default profiles The SmartUI Server automatically creates a standard user profile called ‘Default’ that contains the default settings for the SmartUI Designer and SmartUI Operator. Click for more details: This profile is automatically applied to all the allowed user(s) and/or group(s) configured on the SmartUI Server, unless another profile is applied to them. For details on applying profiles to users, see Using profiles . Note: The Default profile cannot be renamed. Whenever a user logs off, the ‘Default’ profile is immediately applied to the SmartUI Designer or SmartUI Operator. To configure the work environment for all SmartUI Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. users: Edit the profile called Default and change the necessary settings. For details see Editing profiles . To reset the default profile settings: Delete the profile called Default . For details, see Removing profiles . The SmartUI Server then recreates it using the default settings. -->

Default Real Number Formatting Top Default Real Number Formatting If necessary, the default format for real or floating point numbers can be specified, to ensure conformity when these values are reported in messages sent from this Command agent . In addition, by limiting the number of displayed significant places, it is possible to increase the total number of values that can be reported. Note: This setting is ONLY specific to this Command agent only and does not apply globally to all Command agents. To specify the default floating point formatting: Edit the required Command agent. For details, see Editing Agents . This will display the Edit Command agent dialog. If necessary, select the General tab, the default selection. Under the Agent Settings group, specify the required formatting expression in the Default float format edit box, the default is ‘%.2f’ which displays 2 decimal places, although up to 8 decimal places can be displayed, if required. For further details regarding the formatting of floating point numbers, such as the justification and padding of the displayed value, see Formatting a Text Field. -->

Defining colors Top Defining colors You can define the color of a color spider by individually manipulating its A, R, G and B sub-properties. Click for more details: For instance, by driving one or more of these color constituents remotely, you can create a constantly varying color to configure a color property of a graphic form or one of its form components. Note1: The R, G, B color constituents, specify the relative intensity of red, green, and blue respectively in the resultant color. Note2: The A constituent, however, specifies the required transparency of this color, which is only supported by specific color properties e.g. for the Backcolor property of a button. Note3: If any of the R, G or B properties are being remotely driven, you need to preview the graphic form in the SmartUI Designer, before you can view the changing colors. Note4: Only Integer values can be used to specify the values of these constituents, from 0 to 255. To define a color using its ARGB sub-properties If necessary, add and/or select the required color spider and/or open its configuration view. For details, see Adding color spiders . Right-click its title bar and select Add ARGB Properties . Note: Once

ecessary, add and/or select the required color spider and/or open its configuration view. For details, see Adding color spiders . Right-click its title bar and select Add ARGB Properties . Note: Once you add these color sub-properties you cannot remove them from this spider. This adds the following four additional Integer inputs to the Inputs section: Note: All four of these inputs only accept Integer values from 0 to 255. A: The Alpha property, representing the transparency of this color. Transparency determines how much of the background is visible “through” this color. A value of 0 is completely transparent so that only the background and not the specified color will be visible and a value of 255 is not transparent at all. Note: For the following color properties, a value of 0 creates a color that has none of the specified color in it. R: The Red property, representing the red component of the color. G: The Green property, representing the green component of the color. B: The Blue property, representing the blue component of the color. The value of these inputs can either be supplied by another spider or Data spider (e.g. property or data element) via a silk or it can be typed i

roperty, representing the blue component of the color. The value of these inputs can either be supplied by another spider or Data spider (e.g. property or data element) via a silk or it can be typed in manually. For details, see Creating silks . Note: If a String or Double value is typed in, the cell will not accept this input until either this value is removed or an Integer value is entered instead. Tip: When typing in a value manually, double-click the value column to the right of the A , R , G or B input name in the Inputs section and type in the required value. The color input, only displays the color defined by these R, G, B properties and not the A (transparency) property. -->

Defining the required blinking Top Defining the required blinking Configure how the color is required to "blink" in other words to alternate between two pre-defined colors at a specified interval in milliseconds. When this blinking is stopped, another pre-defined color can be displayed. To define the required blinking If necessary, add and/or select the required Blinking spider and/or open its configuration view. For details, see Adding Blinking spiders . In the Inputs section: If necessary, specify the colors of the Oncolor input and/or the Offcolor input, by using their color edit boxes to the right of these inputs. For details, see Using the color edit box to select a color . If necessary, specify the required Interval input, which is the time (in milliseconds) that the Oncolor and Offcolor will each be alternately displayed. Note: The value of this input can either be supplied by another spider or Data spider (e.g. property or data element) via a silk or it can be typed in manually. Tip: When typing in a value manually, double-click the value column to the right of the Interval input name in the Inputs section and type in the required value. Note: The Oncolor and Offcolor color

. Tip: When typing in a value manually, double-click the value column to the right of the Interval input name in the Inputs section and type in the required value. Note: The Oncolor and Offcolor colors will only alternate at the specified Interval when the StartStop input starts the blinking. For details, see Stopping or starting the blinking . -->

Delaying Incidents Top Delaying Incidents Sometimes you do not want incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). to enter your alarming system as soon as they become active the monitored condition of this incident (alarm/event) is still in effect and has not yet returned to its normal operating state. , this is typically for one of the following reasons: To prevent intermittent alarms from flooding your alarm system and distracting your operators from the other more important incidents. To ensure that this alarm is raised when the operator needs to respond to it, not too early and not too late. In these cases, you can configure a delay appropriate for each incident . This delay is simply the number of seconds that the alarm system should wait, once an incident becomes active, before this incident is recognised as being ‘officially’ active and is made known to your operators via the configured Alarm routes. Note1: If the incident is cleared the monitored condition of this incident (alarm/event) ha

recognised as being ‘officially’ active and is made known to your operators via the configured Alarm routes. Note1: If the incident is cleared the monitored condition of this incident (alarm/event) has returned to its normal operating state. before the delay has expired then the incident NEVER enters your alarming system, so your operators will NOT know about it. Note2: This delay must NOT be LESS THAN the scan period of the tag that creates the alarm otherwise the incident will ALWAYS enter your alarming system, and the time delay is ineffective. Note3: If BOTH a delay and a conditional expression is specified for an incident, then the conditional expression is evaluated BEFORE and AFTER the specified delay expires. To configure a delay for an incident: Select the required agent, in other words the agent containing the required alarmed alarm type/s. For details, see Locating an agent . Right click this agent and select the Alarm… menu item. Click on the required alarm type in the Current list of the Alarming dialog. Specify the required delay for this alarm type, in seconds, in the Delay (secs) field at the bottom of this dialog. Note: If this value is zero, the default setting, t

ent list of the Alarming dialog. Specify the required delay for this alarm type, in seconds, in the Delay (secs) field at the bottom of this dialog. Note: If this value is zero, the default setting, then no delay checking is performed and as soon as the incident becomes active it is routed to your operators. -->

Delete a Group Top Delete a Group Tag groups are primarily added to manage the communication settings for the tags whose values need to be communicated to or from the remote Agent Servers via their associated WanServers. Groups are server-specific. For details, see Tag Groups . To delete a group: If necessary launch the WanClient and open the WanClient Configurator, by selecting the Open Configurator item from the File menu. Ensure that the required server is selected in the Select server list box. For details, see Servers . Click the Edit Groups button to display the Edit Groups dialog. In the List of Groups list box, select a tag group that is to be modified. Click the Delete button, this action will need to be confirmed. Note: All tag groups that are deleted will be added to the Recover Deleted Groups list, which is cleared when the database is packed . Click the Ok button to accept the changes made to the list of tag groups or the Cancel button to discard any configuration changes and return to the WanClient Configurator. Note: If the Cancel button is clicked, after deleting a group, the group will remain deleted but using the Recover Groups button can retrieve this group. For

and return to the WanClient Configurator. Note: If the Cancel button is clicked, after deleting a group, the group will remain deleted but using the Recover Groups button can retrieve this group. For details, see Recovering Deleted Groups . -->

Delete a Link Top Delete a Link A tag link or tag mapping, specifies the name of the local and the remote Adroit tag, whose values are to be ‘linked’. This is added to a tag group within a server. For details, see Tag Links . To delete a link: If necessary launch the WanClient and open the WanClient Configurator, by selecting the Open Configurator item from the File menu. Ensure that the required server is selected in the Select server list box. For details, see Servers . Ensure that the required tag group is selected in the Select group list box. For details, see Tag Groups . Select the required link in the WanClient Configurator window and click the Delete Link button. This action will need to be confirmed. Note: Any link that is deleted is permanently removed from the database and cannot be recovered later, unlike tag groups and servers. -->

Delete a Server Top Delete a Server A Server simply stores the necessary communication settings for a specific remote WanServer and its computer, so that the WanClient can connect to this computer and communicate with this WanServer application. For further details, see Servers . To delete a server: If necessary launch the WanClient and open the WanClient Configurator, by selecting the Open Configurator item from the File menu. Click the Edit Servers button to display the Edit Remote Servers dialog. In the List of servers list box, select the required server that is to be deleted. Click the Delete button; this action will need to be confirmed. Note: All servers that are deleted will be added to the Recover Deleted Servers list, which is cleared when the database is packed . Click the Ok button to accept the changes made to the list of servers or the Cancel button to discard any configuration changes and return to the WanClient Configurator. Note: If the Cancel button is pressed, after deleting a server, the server will remain deleted but using the Recover Servers button can retrieve this server. For details, see Recovering Deleted Servers . -->

Delete Queries Top Delete queries Queries provide common tasks for managing your database that is connected to an OLE DB datasource. The Delete Queries can delete records from a specific table or view. Click for more information: If necessary, limit this deletion by defining criteria for fields which must be met before a record is deleted. WARNING! If no constraints are defined then this query will remove ALL the records from a table pr view. Note1: The criteria values can be specified by parameters. Note2: This query is ONLY able to delete the records from a SINGLE table or view. To add and configure a Delete query: Add a Delete Query: Click for generic instructions on how to add, name and specify the creation method for a query: Open the Enterprise Manager . Note: The specified name cannot be the same as any other query that has been already been specified.> Tip: Give this query a meaningful and concise name so that its purpose can be clearly identified - try not to use all 55 characters. If supported by this query category - choose how you want to create this query, by selecting one of the following options: XXX Query Wizard :This default option uses a structured configuration dialog to create the query. This method is especially recommended for those who are not familiar with the SQL querying language. Click Next , once the query is named and the required method of its creation is selected. Configure this Delete query: Note: This configuration dialog does NOT provide a Preview button to prevent records from being incorrectly deleted from your database. Therefore please ensure that you configure the values for these fields correctly. The Constraints dialog is displayed. to delete record/s from a view or table, by selecting the required Table Type option. Select the required view or table from the Select a ... to Delete from list box. The names of tables and views support SQL schemas. Click for more details: The default schema 'DBO' is NOT displayed. But if a table or view is part of a different schema, then the name of this schema is indicated in brackets after the name of the table or view. This means that a table or view can have the SAME name as another table or view as long as it belongs to a different schema. Note: Only ONE table or view can be selected. If necessary, add or remove constraints for the fields of this table in the Constraints dialog. Typically, you constrain values of one or more fields to prevent this table from being needlessly updated. If these constraints will change from user to user then use parameters instead of hard-coded values. Adding or removing constraints for the fields of this table: To add a constraint: Press the Add Constraint button. If this constraint is NOT the first, specify how to relate this constraint to the previous constraints, as follows: AND: This is the default option, which makes this constraint man

Constraint button. If this constraint is NOT the first, specify how to relate this constraint to the previous constraints, as follows: AND: This is the default option, which makes this constraint mandatory. For instance, if there are two constraints with an AND between them, then the data will be restricted by BOTH constraints. OR: Use this option, to make the specified constraint optional. For instance, if there are two constraints with an OR between them then the data can be restricted with EITHER of these constraints. Select the field, whose values you want to limit, from the Field drop-down list box, in the following syntax: [Fieldname]. Note1: This list only displays the selected fields. Note2: If necessary, you can edit the selected field name yourself - in this case ensure that you spell these names correctly. Select the method by which the values of this field are to be constrained or limited from the Constraint drop-down list box. For details, see Available constraint operators . Specify the constraining value or parameter in the Value field. Specify a value if your users will not need to change this criterion, otherwise specify a parameter if your users will need to chan

rs . Specify the constraining value or parameter in the Value field. Specify a value if your users will not need to change this criterion, otherwise specify a parameter if your users will need to change this criterion, for instance, if different users require different values. For details, see Adding parameters . Note: Ensure that the specified Value has the same data type as the specified Field , otherwise the query will not work. Demand Logging Top Demand Logging Batch type processes often require one to log variables only at the end of a batch. In these circumstances, it is not desirable for the data log subsystem to log every change it receives during the execution of a batch. In these cases, Adroit can be configured to only log data values on an exception basis with a configurable time deadband (or maximum logging rate), this is known as (on) demand logging. Configuring demand logging: Use the following three slots of the Datalog agent: Slot Type Description LogNow BOOLEAN The current value is logged to disk every time this slot makes the transition from 0 to 1. Trigger STRING An optional tag (agent.slot) configuration which is monitored for a zero to non-zero transition. When this occurs, a log will take place. Mode INTEGER A variable to control the mode of operation as follows: Normal – change based logging only Demand based logging only Demand and change based logging If necessary, you can ALSO use the Datalog compression algorithm when using Demand logging, by configuring the Support compression algorithm on demand logging global datalogging setting. For details, see Advanced Datalog Configuration (g

talog compression algorithm when using Demand logging, by configuring the Support compression algorithm on demand logging global datalogging setting. For details, see Advanced Datalog Configuration (global settings) . -->

Demand Scanning Top Demand Scanning What is demand scanning and how should it be used? Demand scanning is only supported by NASA This stands for New Adroit Scanning Architecture and describes a sub-class of protocol drivers that are specifically written to take advantage of the scanning improvements and enhancements provided by NASA, such as demand scanning and highly optimised scan tasks. drivers that are specifically written to support it, legacy drivers do not provide this feature. Process values (tags) configured to be demand scanned are only communicated when they are being used (when there are one or more subscriptions or references to these tags). Note: In Adroit, a subscription to a process value essentially means that something else is using it. For instance if this process value is being: alarmed; actively logged; used by another Adroit agent or viewed by an operator. Therefore, demand scanning can reduce the number of process values that are communicated, which are especially useful in the following situations: when you are communicating process values over networks where there is an expense attached to the amount of data that is being transferred like a telemetry system

y useful in the following situations: when you are communicating process values over networks where there is an expense attached to the amount of data that is being transferred like a telemetry system using a GSM network or possibly satellite communications or as a means to improve the throughput (communication speeds) of a belabored network. But demand scanning can ONLY be used for any READ-ONLY process value that is typically ONLY displayed on a mimic (graphic form) or is used by any of its graphic form components like a Behaviour or spider on the graphic form. In other words a process value that is NOT alarmed or logged or used by any other agent. Click for more details: In this case, when the graphic form is opened that contains or references this process value, then the NASA driver will become aware that this graphic form requires this process value and so it will communicate (scan) this value from its front-end device. When this graphic form is closed, then the NASA driver will become aware that this process value is no longer being used and so it will stop communicating (scanning) this value from its front-end device. Note: There is a fair amount of overhead involved for eac

ecome aware that this process value is no longer being used and so it will stop communicating (scanning) this value from its front-end device. Note: There is a fair amount of overhead involved for each demand scanned process value, since the NASA driver has to constantly query the Agent Server to determine when this process value is being used. Therefore due to this implicit overhead only configure process values to be demand scanned that will benefit from demand scanning, in other words, do not configure process values for demand scanning that will NEVER make use of this mechanism (e.g. those that are logged or alarmed). WARNING: If you configure ALL your process values to be demand scanned then you could experience SLOWER system performance and not experience any other benefits since all the process values NOT used by ONLY one thing will ALWAYS be scanned anyway! Tip: You can determine which other agents are using (subscribed to) a tag, by opening the Agent Server Configurator and clicking the Used by… button. Usage scenarios NOT recommended for demand scanning: Demand scanning is NOT recommended for process values that are being alarmed or actively logged or used by another Adro

icking the Used by… button. Usage scenarios NOT recommended for demand scanning: Demand scanning is NOT recommended for process values that are being alarmed or actively logged or used by another Adroit agent. Furthermore, any such tag configured for demand scanning could degrade the overall system performance due to the implicit overhead involved in constantly querying the Agent Server to determine when this process value is being used. Currently when a process value has the Output Enabled scanning setting configured then it is CONSTANTLY being scanned and therefore CANNOT be demand scanned. Demand scanning cannot be used as a strategy to “reuse” your scan points, since as explained above a scanned point license is not relinquished by a demand scanned tag when its tag is not being scanned, since the NASA driver has to constantly query the Agent Server to determine when this process value is being used. We do also NOT recommend the use of demand scanning for a clustered Agent Server that uses shadow scanning and a proxy server to handle requests for its tags from remote clients. Since this could return INCORRECT VALUEs. Therefore use the parallel clustering scanning strategy instea

at uses shadow scanning and a proxy server to handle requests for its tags from remote clients. Since this could return INCORRECT VALUEs. Therefore use the parallel clustering scanning strategy instead. Click for more details: Firstly, when a clustered pair of Agent Servers use shadow scanning, only the Master Agent Server performs the scanning and the Standby Agent Server does not. Secondly, when a client requests a tag from the proxy Agent Server, this proxy Agent Server it is UNABLE to specify which Agent Server partner it retrieves the requested tag from and only retrieves the tag from the first Agent Server in the list, as long as it is in a healthy state. Thirdly, demand scanning is the only type of scanning that requires at least one subscription to exist to the referenced tag before the tag is scanned. For this reason, if a remote client opens a mimic that has a demand scanned tag on it, it is possible for the proxy server to source the requested tag from the Standby Agent Server partner that is NOT being physically scanned (when its name is first in the list), which results in the WRONG VALUE being returned because: the Standby Agent Server is given the subscription to thi

er partner that is NOT being physically scanned (when its name is first in the list), which results in the WRONG VALUE being returned because: the Standby Agent Server is given the subscription to this demand scanned tag, but is unable to service this request because it is NOT performing any scanning and the Master Agent Server does NOT have a subscription to this demand scanned tag (since this subscription was made with the standby Agent Server) and so this tag will NOT be demand scanned! For this reason use parallel scanning instead, which ensures that BOTH the Standby and Master Agent Server scan all the tags and so the value would be demand scanned regardless of which clustered partner is selected by the proxy Agent Server. Demand Scanning Configuration Demand scanning requires a global setting Demand scanning enabled checkbox to be checked in the Driver Configuration page of the Config Editor, which is accessed by clicking the Advanced Driver Options button in the bottom right of this page. This requires an Agent Server restart and sets the following DWORD registry value to 1, from the default value is 0, HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\ Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Workgroup\WG.INI

this page. This requires an Agent Server restart and sets the following DWORD registry value to 1, from the default value is 0, HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\ Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Workgroup\WG.INI\EnableDemandScanning) The device’s ability to support demand scanning is available to the system via the new Boolean demandScanningEnabled slot in the Device agent, which is only enabled when the device (its protocol driver) supports demand scanning. IMPORTANT: Demand scanning is only supported by NASA This stands for New Adroit Scanning Architecture and describes a sub-class of protocol drivers that are specifically written to take advantage of the scanning improvements and enhancements provided by NASA, such as demand scanning and highly optimised scan tasks. drivers that have been written to support it. All other drivers should have the demand scanning checkbox disabled. Note: Since it requires a lot of memory to manage these subscriptions, only enable this global setting if you need it. The Subscriptions active condition bit in the agent header (Status Bit 15 or the statusSubscribed slot) shows whether the agent is actively being subscribed to or not, and all agents that are alarm

t. The Subscriptions active condition bit in the agent header (Status Bit 15 or the statusSubscribed slot) shows whether the agent is actively being subscribed to or not, and all agents that are alarmed, logged or subscribed to by any other agent will have this bit set. Note: This status bit in the agent header dialog only works if global demand scanning is enabled. In other words if global demand scanning setting is NOT enabled, this status bit is ALWAYS off. The scanning configuration dialog now contains a Demand scan checkbox, that is configurable for each scanned item and is saved in the IO flags field. The availability of this checkbox depends on the following: will NOT be visible if the global demand scanning flag is OFF will be visible if the global demand scanning flag is ON, in which case this will: be disabled if the currently selected device driver type does NOT support demand scanning be enabled if the currently selected device driver type supports demand scanning -->

Deployment considerations Top Deployment considerations The SmartUI has been designed to be as open as possible and as such there is no limitation or restriction to the number of different deployment scenarios that are possible. Since any number of Clients are able to connect to any number of Servers. For details about the function of the SmartUI and a description of its component applications, see Working with the SmartUI . Note1: Servers can also be clustered to provide both load balancing and redundancy. For details, see Server clustering . Note2: Click Once allows a user to use a fully fledged SmartUI Operator in Internet Explorer without requiring an initial installation. For details, see Working with Click Once . Possible Client connections: Although there are no restrictions to the number of SmartUI Servers that any one Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. can connect to, the following two constraints determine the maximum number of Clients that any one Server can be connected to: The operating system that is running on the Server computer i.e. any Server that is not running on a Windows Server operating s

e the maximum number of Clients that any one Server can be connected to: The operating system that is running on the Server computer i.e. any Server that is not running on a Windows Server operating system, e.g. Windows Server 2003, is only able to allow 5 Clients to connect to the Server, over the Internet, at any one time. Also if more than 10 Clients are required to connect to the Server, over the LAN, at any one time, it is also recommended to use a Server operating system, as otherwise this may cause performance problems. The licencing of the SmartUI Server i.e. this will determine the total number of possible Clients that can connect to a Server at any one time. Note: The licencing of the Server also determines if the Server has access to any additional components, such as datasources, spiders etc. For more information on licensing the SmartUI Server, see Licensing the Server . Network topology used for Client connections: When connecting Clients to Servers, the most important decision is what network topology should be used to connect the Client to the Server i.e. whether to use the LAN or the Internet. Note: By default, the SmartUI Launcher can be used to deploy and update

cision is what network topology should be used to connect the Client to the Server i.e. whether to use the LAN or the Internet. Note: By default, the SmartUI Launcher can be used to deploy and update the Operator application via the selected network topology. Although this can also be used to deploy and update the Designer and additional components, such as datasources, spiders etc. if necessary. For details, see Working with the Launcher . It is recommended that only the SmartUI Operator application be connected to the Server over the Internet, unless you are using a high bandwidth Internet connection. This is because the Designer, unlike the Operator, requires a two-way flow of data between itself and the Server, when designing graphic forms. If one or more Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. can connect to the Server over the Internet, then the SmartUI Server needs to communicate to IIS and the firewall, if present, will also need to be configured, so that the Server can communicate to IIS and the Clients. For details, see Firewall configuration . Tip: For a detailed step-by-step procedure of connecting Opera

nt, will also need to be configured, so that the Server can communicate to IIS and the Clients. For details, see Firewall configuration . Tip: For a detailed step-by-step procedure of connecting Operators to a Server over the Internet, see How to Connect to the Server over the Web . Note1: The SmartUI Web Service needs to be installed on the web server (IIS computer) to facilitate the communication between the Client and the Server. For details, see SmartUI Installations . Note2: Since the SmartUI Server only needs to communicate to IIS, these applications can be on different computers, which can even be in different domains, providing the necessary trust relationships exists between these computers. Note3: IIS is also required when exposing Web services to the Internet. -->

Design workspace Top Design workspace The Design workspace is the main work area, which is always opened in the center of the SmartUI Designer application window. This contains all the currently open documents. Only one document can be displayed within this window at a time, where it can be viewed and/or configured as required. Note1: Increase the viewing and editing space provided by the Design workspace , depending on how you arrange the tool windows in the work environment.
