text: Designer connection settings Top Designer connection settings This page of the Setting up the Designer component of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog, provides the following settings that specify the default data connection that is established between this SmartUI Designer and the specified SmartUI Server at login: To display this page of settings: When the SmartUI Designer is launched, it needs to log into a SmartUI Server computer, which stores the data configured within the SmartUI Designer. Launch the Adroit Config Editor . The Welcome section is displayed by default, unless multiple configurations have been created, in which case the Configuration page is displayed by default, which needs to be expanded to display the Welcome section. For details, see Working with Configurations . Select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the Setting up the Designer option. Note: If this option does not appear then the SmartUI Designer may not be installed. Select the Connection Settings option. Tip1: You can navigate directly to this page using the left pane of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog. For details

tUI Designer may not be installed. Select the Connection Settings option. Tip1: You can navigate directly to this page using the left pane of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog. For details, see Working with configuration dialogs . Tip2: Press the Next or Previous buttons to display the other pages of settings. Login Server: this specifies the default SmartUI Server computer that this SmartUI Designer connects to during the login process. Note: ONLY the user profiles configured on this specified SmartUI Server can be applied to the users of this SmartUI Designer. To specify the login Server computer name: If necessary, type the required name into the provided edit box. Note : Please ensure that the name of this computer is correctly spelt; otherwise the login process will not succeed. The following are typical login errors that occur when this name is incorrectly specified: “Requested service not found” -> The Server has not completed loading yet “No connection could be made because the target machine actively refused it” -> There is no running server Data communication method: select the required method that data is transferred within the established connection between

because the target machine actively refused it” -> There is no running server Data communication method: select the required method that data is transferred within the established connection between this SmartUI Server and SmartUI Designer. To specify the required communication method: Select the required option. The optimal method depends upon the network (bandwidth) connecting this SmartUI Server and SmartUI Designer, as follows: Subscribe : recommended when using a Local Area Network as this provides the fastest response time by requiring the highest bandwidth. Poll(send all values) : recommended when using a high bandwidth Internet connection. Poll(send most recent values) : recommended when using a low bandwidth Internet connection. For further details concerning these methods, see About connection communication methods . The bandwidth requirements for this connection depends upon a number of factors, such as the update requirements and the size of the graphic forms. However, you can ensure that the selected communication method provides sufficient bandwidth for the needs of your project, by adopting the following recommendations: Keep the graphic form sizes small; for exampl

can ensure that the selected communication method provides sufficient bandwidth for the needs of your project, by adopting the following recommendations: Keep the graphic form sizes small; for example use JPG files instead of BMP files. Plan the graphic forms beforehand with the end-user in mind, including the bandwidth that will be available. Develop an end-to-end prototype to test in a production environment in order to satisfy all requirements (including the communication requirements). Only once this prototype has been successfully tested should the project be completely engineered. Connection status check frequency: specify how often the SmartUI Designer should test that the SmartUI Server connection is still healthy and is not disconnected. To specify the required interval between checking the connection, in seconds: Either type in the required value directly or use the arrows of this spin control to obtain the required value. Tip: There is little reason to change this default value, as this connection monitoring process only consumes a small amount of bandwidth and CPU usage. For details, see Setting up the Designer . For details on displaying all the related SmartUI Designer settings, see the Advanced Designer settings page . -->

king with configuration dialogs . Tip2: Press the Next or Previous buttons to display the other pages of settings. Default script references: specify the list of external assemblies or dynamic linked library (.DLL) files that are automatically added to each script. Note: The longer the list of references, the longer it takes to load and compile every script. Tip: This setting allows 3 rd party users to expose their product-specific assemblies (DLLs) to all their scripts. To add a default script reference: Click the Add button and browse for the required assembly. Note : Ensure that the paths of all of these files are added to the Script references paths setting so they will be located. To remove a default script reference: Select the assembly that is no longer required and press the Remove button. WARNING! The reference to the selected assembly is immediately removed, so ensure that you select the required assembly. Graphic form scripting: to enable or disable the ability to script event handlers to programmatically achieve a more interactive user experience for graphic forms. For further details, see Graphic form scripting . Note: If this functionality is not required then disable

nt handlers to programmatically achieve a more interactive user experience for graphic forms. For further details, see Graphic form scripting . Note: If this functionality is not required then disable it to increase the speed of loading graphic forms. To configure graphic form scripting: Either select Yes to enable or No to disable this setting. Visual Studio debugging: if you have Visual Studio 2010 or later installed, then you can use this application to edit and debug your scripts instead of the generic script editor, which only provides limited debugging functionality. To debug your scripts using Visual Studio: Either select Yes to debug your scripts using Visual Studio or No to use the generic script editor. Note: When debugging your scripts in Visual Studio, the scripts are exported to the ScriptsExport subfolder of the SmartUI ProgramData folder (typically C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI \ScriptsExport) in a Visual Studio-compatible format. Search paths for script references: specify additional paths that contain the assemblies (.DLL files) that are referenced by your scripts. For further details regarding script references, see Managing references . WARNIN

ipt references: specify additional paths that contain the assemblies (.DLL files) that are referenced by your scripts. For further details regarding script references, see Managing references . WARNING! Only specify the locations to assemblies (.DLL files) that you use frequently, since an extensive list will delay the loading and compilation times of all scripts. To add a path that is to be searched: Click the Add button and browse for the required folder. To remove a path from the list: Select the path that is no longer required and press the Remove button. WARNING! The selected path will immediately be deleted, therefore ensure that the required path is selected. Note1: The installation folder and its subfolders are searched by default and so do NOT need to be added to this list. Note2: It is NOT recommended that these locations exist on different computers due to many hindrances, such as security problems and time delays. This page only configures the part of the essential SmartUI Designer settings. For details, see Setting up the Designer . For details on displaying all the related SmartUI Designer settings, see the Advanced Designer settings page . -->

Designing graphic forms Top Designing graphic forms Open a graphic form in the Design workspace to design it. Note: Projects and their folders provide a Preview Graphic Forms option to displays thumbnail snapshots of all the graphic forms located in their immediate or root level to either open the required graphic form or populate the Favorites tool window. For details, see Previewing graphic forms . Tip: The Shapes Wizards & Examples tab of the Designer ribbon, provides access to the shapes, wizards and/or examples of the default Shapes Wizards and Examples project so that you can easily design your graphic forms. For details, see Working with Shapes Wizards and Examples . In particular this contains the Situational Awareness category, which contains sub-categories of wizards that allow you to create process control user interfaces that strive to minimise operator fatigue and increase their response times. For more details, see Situational Awareness (or High Performance SCADA) . Design or configure a graphic form for the following reasons: To provide the functionality or user interface that will allow end-users to interact with and examine the data displayed by the graphic form. T

n or configure a graphic form for the following reasons: To provide the functionality or user interface that will allow end-users to interact with and examine the data displayed by the graphic form. To connect data to this graphic form, gathered from any datasource. If necessary, to manipulate data before it is displayed on the graphic form. Note: A Wizard is a pre-drawn and/or pre-configured (animated) graphical object that can be used to simplify and speed up the task of creating graphic forms. For details, see Working with wizards . The graphic form toolbar provides tools to analyse and/or optimise the structure of your graphic forms. For details, see Optimizing graphic forms or Graphic form statistics . How to design a graphic form: Add form components to the graphic form to create the user interface of a graphic form, which you can do by adding one or more Window Forms or a customised control a visible form component used to display data or accept user input in the graphic form. ee form component. and component a hidden form component that provides additional functionality to this graphic form and some or all of its form components. Note: The TableLayoutPanel control allows you to add and arrange controls in a table, so that these controls can change dynamically as the application environment changes. Device Agent - Database File Format Top Device Agent - Database File Format For a detailed description of any of its slots, see Slot Details . See the agent header slots for the information that is common to all agent types. .WGP File Line Description DRV=string The name of protocol driver DLL, typically an eight-character string RLN=n The size of the binary dump (REG) in bytes. REG=bin_dump A binary dump of the registry configuration of the device. This makes the WGP file more portable between computers, in that if the device entry is not found in the registry it is automatically created. However the onus remains on the user to ensure that the specified driver DLL (DRV) is installed. To remove this REG entry, configure the following settings as such: RLN=0 REG= CNT=n Count of subscription specifications (@ type scanning) SUBS1=string First subscription specification SUBS2=string Second subsription specification ... ... SUBSn=string n th subscription specification CNT=m Count of scanning specifications SCAN1=string First scanning specification SCAN2=string Second scanning specification ... ... SCANm=string m th scanning specification RCV=nnnn Recovery/Cooldown period in millisecond

ng specifications SCAN1=string First scanning specification SCAN2=string Second scanning specification ... ... SCANm=string m th scanning specification RCV=nnnn Recovery/Cooldown period in milliseconds AGS=0 Agent Stop/Start State (0 = Stopped; 1 = Started) -->

Device Information Top Device Information The following attributes are displayed in the information pane at the top of the right windowpane when a configured ( , , ) or un-configured ( ) Device has been selected in the left Installed Drivers and Devices windowpane: Status: This indicates the status of the device itself and will either be: not loaded, no Agent Server connection, stopped or started. Healthy: This indicates status of the communications or scan-tasks assigned to this device, as follows: healthy, indicates that all of its all of its scan-tasks have started successfully. not healthy, indicates that either the selected device has stopped or a problem has occurred when starting this device or there may be a license/HASP problem (to test, run the Agent Server in demo mode). Device Management Settings Top Device Management Settings Each SNMPMgr can manage a single device by getting and/or setting and/or trapping its SNMP managed objects management data exposed by SNMP managed devices that might be hardware, configuration parameters, performance statistics, and any other data that directly relates to the operation of this device. (values). The Poll settings section of the Edit SNMP Mngr Agent dialog, either enables or disables this device management and can specify a rate at which values are retrieved from the managed device and how many values are included in each polling transaction, as follows: PLEASE NOTE: If the Unlicensed checkbox (status bit indicator) is checked, then you need to correctly license your Agent Server before you can run 2 or more SNMPMgr agents. To start managing the device: to start polling (monitoring) and/or writing (controlling) and/or trapping (enabling events) of the OID values of this device. Select the Enable polling option (BOOLEAN start slot). Click the Update button. This sets the Started (status bit 18), which checks the Started checkbox. Note: A scan point is consumed for every unique OID value that is polled, written

OLEAN start slot). Click the Update button. This sets the Started (status bit 18), which checks the Started checkbox. Note: A scan point is consumed for every unique OID value that is polled, written to and/or trapped. WARNING! If a SNMPMgr agent requires more than your available scan points then ALL these OID operations are DISABLED and its Error status bit is set. IMPORTANT: If the InvalidConnection status bit is set (the Invalid connection checkbox is checked), then NONE of these OID operations will be performed as the agent cannot connect to this device To stop managing the device: to stop polling and/or writing and/or trapping OID values of this device and to release the scan point licenses the agent was using for these OID operations. Select the Disable polling option (BOOLEAN start slot). Click the Update button. The Stopped (status bit 17) is set, which checks the Stopped checkbox The Started (status bit 18) is cleared, which clears the Started checkbox. To configure the poll rate: the default rate, in milliseconds, that the agent fetches OID values (that are enabled for polling in the list) and copies these values into their associated tags. Specify the Poll rate (INTEGER

ate: the default rate, in milliseconds, that the agent fetches OID values (that are enabled for polling in the list) and copies these values into their associated tags. Specify the Poll rate (INTEGER scanRate slot) in milliseconds. Note: The lowest rate is 5000 milliseconds (5 seconds). To configure the number of OID values per polling transaction: the number of OID values to retrieve in a single polling transaction, which effectively determines how many transactions are required for each poll. In the Pdu edit box specify the number of OID items to include in a single polling transaction. For instance if you have a list with 15 OIDs and you specify a Pdu of 5 then each poll will require 3 transactions. Note: The device determines how many OID values that it is able to return in a single transaction. To view the activity of this agent: to allow advanced users to use the Datascope window to monitor the state and current activity of this agent. Note: Ensure that you Enable polling before you can monitor this agent. Click the Datascope button. In the Adroit Protocol Driver Monitor dialog, type 1 to select the Datascope option. In the Datascope window, type A to convert the Datascope fr

you can monitor this agent. Click the Datascope button. In the Adroit Protocol Driver Monitor dialog, type 1 to select the Datascope option. In the Datascope window, type A to convert the Datascope from HEX to ASCII. This window displays the current STATE of this agent, where [1] means running and [2] means stopped. The other messages indicate the current activity of the agent, such as tree building, reading writing polling general activity. In general this facility allows you to know if the agent is working or not. Specific Status Bits : Lists the non connection-related errors that the Error status bit can indicate. Connecting to the Managed Device : How to connect to the required device. Usage Requirements : Requirements in order to use this agent. -->

text: Diagnosing the GSM_SMS Device Top Diagnosing the GSM_SMS Device Once a GSM_SMS device has been specified for this Command agent , the following key communication diagnostic indicators are exposed to this Command agent: Note: For details on specifying this device, see Specifying the GSM_SMS Device . Signal Strength: This signalStrength slot is displayed within the Edit Command agent dialog and indicates the strength, in percent, of the current signal of the GSM modem that is being used to transmit and receive the SMS messages. According to the GSM specification, the signal strength must be greater than 29 % to reliably transmit data. Bit Error Rate: This bitErrorRate slot is not displayed within the Edit Command agent dialog and indicates the quality of the communications i.e. a high bit error rate indicates that there is a large amount of interference, in percent. According to the GSM specification, the bit error rate must NOT be greater than 40 % signal strength to reliably transmit data. The SignalError specific status bit monitors the values of BOTH of these slots of the command agent and if either the signalStrength slot is less than 29 % or the bitErrorRate slot is greater tha

ata. The SignalError specific status bit monitors the values of BOTH of these slots of the command agent and if either the signalStrength slot is less than 29 % or the bitErrorRate slot is greater than 40 %, this specific status bit will be enabled. For details, see Specific Status Bits . Note1: If this is checked, it does NOT mean that SMS messages will not be sent or received, it only indicates that the current conditions are unfavorable for their successful receipt or delivery i.e. this should be used for troubleshooting purposes only. Note2: The MsgSendError specific status bit should also be monitored for troubleshooting purposes; this is checked whenever the last message could not be sent due to cell phone network-specific problems, such as signal problems etc. To view the signal strength of the device used by a Command agent: If necessary, add a Command agent. For details, see Adding Agents . Edit the required Command agent. For details, see Editing Agents . This will display the Edit Command agent dialog. Select the Phone tab. Under the ‘ GSM_SMS’ Device Diagnostics group, the value to the right of the Signal Strength (in %) specifies the current percentage strength of the

e Edit Command agent dialog. Select the Phone tab. Under the ‘ GSM_SMS’ Device Diagnostics group, the value to the right of the Signal Strength (in %) specifies the current percentage strength of the signal that is being received by this GSM SMS modem. The progress bar below this represents this signal strength graphically. -->

Diagnostic Counters Screen Top Diagnostic Counters Screen The "Diagnostic Counters" Protocol Driver Monitor screen provides a comprehensive list of counters maintained by Protocol Driver. Example screenshot: These counters are all zeroed when the Agent Server starts, and for some drivers, also when the device agent starts. These diagnostic counters can be used to troubleshoot your device communication problems, by providing the following information: “ Transactions ” increment every-time a transaction succeeds. A transaction fetches one or more data points. “ Retry's ” increment every-time a transaction is retried. xxx errors increment when there is a problem communicating. For example, Write errors increment when DTR signaling is configured but not received; by device failure or the cable not having that line wired in. xxx timeouts increment when no or too little data has been received on the port in the time allotted for a transaction, resulting in a retry. The following describes all the available counters: Transactions: The number of successful transactions performed by this device. Init failures: The number of times this device attempted to initialise or configure the communic

l the available counters: Transactions: The number of successful transactions performed by this device. Init failures: The number of times this device attempted to initialise or configure the communication hardware and failed. Retry’s: The total count of retries performed on read or write operations. Port switches: If a secondary resource is allowed, this count is the number of times the driver switched between primary and secondary channels. Protocol errors: This counter generally indicates invalid device responses, which are not legal or are unrecognised. Percent errors: This is an indication of the communication fault frequency, which is expressed as a percentage. Read errors: The number of times the driver failed to read an expected response. Read timeouts: The number of times the driver failed to receive a response to a request, within the required time. Write errors: The number of times the driver failed to send data because of a hardware problem. Write timeouts: The number of times the driver timed out while waiting to send data because of a hardware problem. Transactions/sec: This represents the number of successful transactions performed per second. Note: These default dri

mes the driver timed out while waiting to send data because of a hardware problem. Transactions/sec: This represents the number of successful transactions performed per second. Note: These default driver performance counters, as well as any driver-specific counters, can also be displayed using the Perfmon agent . This agent is also able to copy the value of these counters into tags, which could then be reported, as required. -->

Digital Agent - Slot Details Top Digital Agent - Slot Details The Digital Agent stores a digital (ON/OFF) value and their text representations. It has the capability of alarming the value, pulsing a value on output, and value inversion. This agent is located in the following file: T_DIGITAL.DLL Slots: Slot Name Type Function catchupData RAWBYTES Internal use only (used for datalog and real-time data catch-up). delay INTEGER Pulse delay in milliseconds enableChange BOOLEAN This is used to enable/disable change monitoring for this agent. initValue BOOLEAN Cold start value invert BOOLEAN Invert flag pulse BOOLEAN Enable pulse output rawValue BOOLEAN Device value state0 STRING State 0 name state1 STRING State 1 name textValue STRING Text value - may be written to, to change the state of the digital. time TIME Value time stamp timePrev TIME Provides the timestamp of the valuePrev slot (the previous value) and is only affected by putslots to the value slot NOT the time slot. This slot is not currently supported in realtime catchup. value BOOLEAN Current value valuePrev BOOLEAN This contains the previous value of the value slot before it was changed. Specific status bits: Note: These are

currently supported in realtime catchup. value BOOLEAN Current value valuePrev BOOLEAN This contains the previous value of the value slot before it was changed. Specific status bits: Note: These are of type BOOLEAN. Bit Number Name Function status bit 16 Off On when the Value is OFF. status bit 17 On On when the Value is ON i.e. non-zero value. status bit 18 Changed Used when change monitoring is enabled (the enableChange slot is set to 1) AND the value (the value slot) CHANGES then this status bit is pulsed (set to 1 and then immediately be set back to 0). Methods of creation: Manual Agents created by default: None For a description of which of these slots are saved to the Adroit database file (.WGP), see: Digital Agent - Database File Format . -->

Disabling silk triggering of spiders Top Disabling silk triggering of spiders By default, each silk connected to the input of a spider can trigger this spider. If this is not desired, then the default triggering of some or all of these silks can be disabled. This can be performed using two methods: Disabling silk triggering per silk: This method is recommended when you need to disable the triggering of particular silk(s) connected to a spider. To disable silk triggering per silk: Open the required spider workspace. Right-click the required silk and select the Silks menu. From the Silks menu select the description of the required silk. This will display a menu of options that apply to the required silk. If a tick mark appears to the left of Trigger Output Spider , select it to remove this tick mark and disable this option. Note: Once this triggering option is disabled, this method will need to be performed again to enable the triggering of this silk. ndicates the status of this property. For details, see Visual property indicators . Disabling Simple File Sharing Top Disabling Simple File Sharing Simple File Sharing is a feature introduced in Microsoft Windows XP, which removes some file sharing security options available in other versions of Windows. This feature is enabled by default. However, if this feature is enabled, it prevents the Designer from accessing remote Server information and so is unable to connect to and login to any remote Servers. Note: This only needs to be performed when the Windows XP Professional computer is part of a Windows workgroup, since Simple File Sharing always remains disabled for computers joined to domains. To disable Simple File Sharing in Windows XP: Either open My Computer from the Windows XP Desktop or open up the Windows Explorer (use the WindowsKey+E shortcut). The appropriate window will be displayed. Open the Tools menu and select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the Folder Options... option from this menu. A new Folder Options window will be displayed. Click on the View tab and locate the Use Simple File Sharing (Recommended) checkbox in the Advanced Settings list. Tip: The checkbox should be at or near

new Folder Options window will be displayed. Click on the View tab and locate the Use Simple File Sharing (Recommended) checkbox in the Advanced Settings list. Tip: The checkbox should be at or near the bottom of this list. Ensure this checkbox is not checked. Click OK to close the Folder Options window. The settings for Simple File Sharing are now updated; no computer reboot is required. -->

Disabling Simplified File Sharing Top Disabling Simplified File Sharing By default Windows XP, VISTA and Windows 7 enables simplified file sharing. This setting must be DISABLED on clustered Agent Server computers because it interferes with the inter-communication between the clustered Agent Servers by making incorrect assumptions regarding this communication. If this setting is ENABLED on a clustered Agent Server computer then under certain conditions one of the cluster partners does not see/detect the presence of its cluster partner. In other words, one cluster partner detects both Agent Servers, while the other detects only itself. This causes the master-standby switchover to fail, resulting in an unstable cluster configuration. How to disable this simplified file sharing setting: Open Windows Explorer. (Click the Start menu, Programs, Accessories and Windows Explorer item.) Open the Tools menu. Select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. Folder Options… Example: In the Folder Options dialog, select the View tab. Scroll to the bottom of the Advanced settings list. For Windows XP: Ensure that check box next to the Use s

own as clicking. Folder Options… Example: In the Folder Options dialog, select the View tab. Scroll to the bottom of the Advanced settings list. For Windows XP: Ensure that check box next to the Use simple file sharing (Recommended) setting is empty. Example: If this is not empty, then click it to clear the tick. For VISTA and Windows 7: Ensure that check box next to the Use Sharing Wizard (Recommended) setting is empty. Example: If this is not empty, then click it to clear the tick. Click the OK button. -->

Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). (alarms) are stored in alarm lists, which allow them to be displayed and/or acknowledged, typically by using Alarm List Viewer windows in the Classic UI which connect to a SINGLE alarm list at a time. Both the Alarm agent and AlarmList agent provide alarm lists, with the following differences: While the alarm list of an Alarm agent contains ALL the incidents of the agents that it is monitoring, an AlarmList agent ONLY contains the incidents of the agents that are specifically routed to it. ONLY the alarm list of an AlarmList agent allows users to LOCALLY acknowledge alarms. BOTH alarm lists (of an AlarmList and Alarm agent) allow users to GLOBALLY acknowledge alarms. Typically AlarmList agents are only required when you want to view alarms by process area or device. Displaying both existing and updated dataset data Top Displaying both existing and updated dataset data By default, when connecting data elements of type dataset tabular data or data that is contained within one or more tables; each table contains one or more columns and each column consists of one or more rows. to a property of a control, all the data contained within the dataset is initially displayed and thereafter only the newly added or updated data is displayed. This configuration is typically suited to datasets whose values change frequently. However if the existing data remains unchanged then only the most recently updated data will be displayed, by default. For instance, if events are being logged to a database, only the new events will be displayed. In this case, it is possible to append any newly updated data to the end of the existing data that has already displayed within the required control on the graphic form. WARNING! If this control is configured to append updated data to the displayed data and the data changes constantly, each change will be displayed separately as another row within the control, which could complicate the viewing of this data, unnecessarily. Docking tool windows Top Docking tool windows Tool windows are dockable, as such they have both a floating and docked display mode. When a tool window is docked, it is attached to the Designer application by means of a docking area, which is usually along any of the four borders of the Design workspace window. To dock a tool window: Locate and open the required tool window. For details, see Accessing tool windows . Note: Ensure that this tool window is not being auto hidden, if so deactivate this feature first. For details, see Automatically hiding and showing tool windows . Drag the window into the required window and use the overlay menu items (namely ) to dock this window appropriately - only the supported overlay menu options indicate where this window will be placed. This will display a shadow over the selected tool window, indicating where this window will be docked - if correct then release the mouse button to accept this position. Example: Note: The position of the mouse pointer, not the edges of the tool window that you are dragging, determines which overlay menu option you select. Tip1: To move a tool window without snapping it into place or docking it, press CTRL or SHIF

r, not the edges of the tool window that you are dragging, determines which overlay menu option you select. Tip1: To move a tool window without snapping it into place or docking it, press CTRL or SHIFT while dragging it to the location you desire. Tip2: Double-clicking the title bar of a docked window will also free the entire group so that it can be re-docked as required. Double-clicking it again docks it in its former position. Tip3: Double-clicking the tab of a grouped window, frees this window from the group so that it can be re-docked as required. Double-clicking it again docks it in its former position. Driver monitor launcher options dialog Top Driver Monitor Launcher Options Dialog This dialog is either accessed by clicking the Options… button in the Driver Monitor Launcher or by selecting the Options… menu item from the System menu. This is configured as follows: Device icon update speed: This specifies how fast the device icons update in the Device Name list of the Driver Monitor, this can either be set to: Fast (0.05 sec), Medium (0.1 sec), Slow (0.5 sec) or be Disabled. Command line options: Additional command-line options can also be added to this edit box and allows you automatically display and/or configure the driver monitoring screen that you always want to view by default. Turn off datascope mode when DrvMon exits: This checkbox, which is checked by default, if checked this will stop the driver from producing the Datascope text when Driver Monitor has closed, in order to reduce the CPU load. This is especially important for fast drivers. -->

DSC EnvisaLink Ethernet Driver DSC EnvisaLink Ethernet Driver Overview This document describes the setup of, and the communication protocol implemented in the Adroit protocol driver, with the following logic unit: DSC EnvisaLink. Device Configuration Configuration Selection Enable Secondary – Enables secondary configuration for dual redundant Controllers. This setting is disabled for this driver. Primary / Secondary – Select the primary or secondary button depending on which connection you wish to configure. This setting is disabled for this driver. 1 Adroit Protocol Driver Setup Manual IP Settings IP Address – The IP Address that will be used for communicating with the controller. Passwords Please note. Passwords are encrypted using 16 bit key encryption before being stored in the registry. TPI Password – Enter your envisalink webpage password here DSC Master Code – Enter the DSC alarm panel’s master code. This is used to arm and disarm the alarm panel. DSC Installer Code – Enter the DSC alarm panel’s installer code. This is used when configuring the alarm panel. Internal Settings Note. This driver has an internal thread which handles the scanning. Changing these settings, change

DSC alarm panel’s installer code. This is used when configuring the alarm panel. Internal Settings Note. This driver has an internal thread which handles the scanning. Changing these settings, change the frequency in which the scanning thread adds the following to the read queue. Keep alive poll frequency (ms) – This is the time delay between keep alive polls. This value is measured in milliseconds and must be between 1000 and 10000. Status poll frequency (ms) – This is the time delay between status polls. This value is measured in milliseconds and has a minimum of 10000ms. Set alarm system time from SCADA – If this checkbox is checked, the alarms panel’s system time will be set with the time from the Adroit agent server. Time update frequency (m) – The time on the alarm panel may drift, if “Set alarm system time from SCADA” is check, the alarm panel’s system time will be updated with this frequency. Timeout (ms) – If the driver does not receive a valid response from the device within this period (measured in milliseconds), the port will be closed. Note. Dual mode tags Top Dual mode tags When using tags within control groups, it is recommended to also add these tags to normal groups too, so that these tags become ‘dual mode’ tags. However, the ORDER in which these groups are defined within the WanClient tag link database is important, as follows: The normal group is defined ABOVE the control group: This will update the local Agent Server with the current tag value within the remote Agent Server on the appropriate WanServer computer first. The normal group is defined BELOW the control group: This is akin to making the client Agent Server the master for this tag, in that the current tag value within the local Agent Server on the WanClient computer will always be sent first. Note: Tags within control groups can be written to a remote WanServer Agent Server, to update their tag values. This is in addition to merely receiving their tag values, as is the case within normal groups. However, in BOTH cases, dual mode tags enable the Mark bad scan bad indication methodology to be successfully employed when using the On comms start event. For further details, see Scan Bad Indication Methodologies . -->

DumpConfig Agent - Slot Details DumpConfig Agent - Slot Details The DumpConfig agent simply stores the configuration of specific agents in an OLE DB database. This agent is located in the following file: T_DUMPCONFIG.DLL Note: You can only add ONE DumpConfig agent. Slots: Slot Name Type Function catchupData RAWBYTES Internal use only (used for real-time data catch-up) connection VARSTRING The connection string to the specified OLE DB database (preferably MS SQL). dumpnow BOOLEAN When set to TRUE (1) this forces the agent to dump all the currently configured agent configurations to the specified database. enable BOOLEAN When set to TRUE (1) this enables the agent to start dumping agent configurations to the specified database. list LIST The Agent type configuration list, which specifies the agent types and/or their slots and/or the agent instances to dump to the database. schedule INTEGER If set to a number greater than 0, then this number specifies the hourly interval that will be used to trigger this agent to dump the specified agent configurations to the database but if set to 0 this disables this method of triggering this agent. trigger STRING The tag (agent.slot) with a Boolean

to trigger this agent to dump the specified agent configurations to the database but if set to 0 this disables this method of triggering this agent. trigger STRING The tag (agent.slot) with a Boolean, integer or real value so that whenever the value of this slot changes to a non-zero value, the specified agent configurations are dumped to the database. Specific status bits: Note: These are of type BOOLEAN. Bit Number Name Function status bit 16 ConnectionError Set to TRUE (1) when the connection with OLE DB source cannot be established - for troubleshooting. status bit 17 TransactionError Set to TRUE (1) when any transaction error with SQL occurs - for troubleshooting. status bit 18 DumpBusy Set to TRUE (1) when a dump begins and set to FALSE when dump is complete – for monitoring. Methods of creation: Manual Agents created by default: None

Edit a Group Top Edit a Group Tag groups are primarily added to manage the communication settings for the tags whose values need to be communicated to or from the remote Agent Servers via their associated WanServers. Groups are server-specific. For details, see Tag Groups . To edit a group: If necessary launch the WanClient and open the WanClient Configurator, by selecting the Open Configurator item from the File menu. Ensure that the required server is selected in the Select server list box. For details, see Servers . Click the Edit Groups button to display the Edit Groups dialog. Note: This dialog can also be used to delete groups . In the List of Groups list box, select a tag group that is to be modified. In the Group Title edit box, specify a name for this tag group, which must not be more than 90 characters in length. The Group Type list box, ONLY specifies the communication type originally selected for this group, as follows: Normal: This should contain tag links, whose local values (located in the Agent Server, residing on the WanClient computer) should ONLY be fetched (read) from the specified remote tag values via the required WanServers. Control: This should contain tag l

ues (located in the Agent Server, residing on the WanClient computer) should ONLY be fetched (read) from the specified remote tag values via the required WanServers. Control: This should contain tag links, whose local values (located in the Agent Server, residing on the WanClient computer) can be BOTH fetched (read) from AND sent (written) to the specified remote tag values via the required WanServers. In the Poll Period edit box, specify the rate in seconds at which the WanClient should request this WanServer for changes to the tag links within this tag group. The default value of 0 implies "as fast as possible" and specifies a 1 second polling rate. Note: Poll periods can be specified from 1 to 2000 seconds. Uncheck the Enabled checkbox, if the tag links within the tag group is not to be communicated to for a period, but will be required in the future and so should not be deleted. Click the Ok button to accept the changes made to the list of tag groups or the Cancel button to discard any configuration changes and return to the WanClient Configurator. -->

Edit a Link Top Edit a Link A tag link or tag mapping, specifies the name of the local and the remote Adroit tag, whose values are to be ‘linked’. This is added to a tag group within a server. For details, see Tag Links . To edit a link: If necessary launch the WanClient and open the WanClient Configurator, by selecting the Open Configurator item from the File menu. Ensure that the required server is selected in the Select server list box. For details, see Servers . Ensure that the required tag group is selected in the Select group list box. For details, see Tag Groups . Either double click the required link in the WanClient Configurator window or select the link and then click the Edit Link button. This will display the Edit Link dialog. In the Remote Tag edit box, specify a name of the required Adroit tag, located in the Agent Server residing on the WanServer computer. In the Local Tag edit box, specify a name of the required Adroit tag, located in the local Agent Server, residing on the WanClient computer. The Method list box, is disabled, since this only applies to tags within normal groups, in which case the WanServer will return the current value of the specified remote tag.

Edit a Server Top Edit a Server A Server simply stores the necessary communication settings for a specific remote WanServer and its computer, so that the WanClient can connect to this computer and communicate with this WanServer application. For further details, see Servers . To edit a server: If necessary launch the WanClient and open the WanClient Configurator, by selecting the Open Configurator item from the File menu. Click the Edit Servers button to display the Edit Remote Servers dialog. Note: This dialog can also be used to delete servers . In the List of servers list box, select the required server that is to be modified. In the Full server title edit box, specify a name for the server, not more than 90 characters in length. The Database name field ONLY displays the CSV filename that was specified for this server to store its tag groups and tag links. In the IP Address edit box, either specify the exact IP address of the WanClient computer or specify the network name of this computer instead. Note: If the computer name is specified then the WAN requires a LMHOSTS file or a WINS server to resolve the computer name into its corresponding IP address. The Port field, displays t

mputer instead. Note: If the computer name is specified then the WAN requires a LMHOSTS file or a WINS server to resolve the computer name into its corresponding IP address. The Port field, displays the port address that is being used by WanLink, which can be modified, if necessary. The Connect timeout edit box is not currently used. In the Transaction timeout edit box, specify the time in seconds before a requested transaction made to the server fails. The default value of 5 is required for fast networks and a value from 15 – 20 can be used for slower networks. In the Retries edit box, specify the number of reties to be automatically attempted when attempting to establish a connection to this WanServer computer. In the Ping timeout edit box, specify the period in seconds to wait after the communications fail before the client will retry to establish communications. Uncheck the Enabled checkbox, if this server is not to be communicated to for a period, but will be required in the future and so is not to be deleted. Click the Ok button to accept the changes made to the list of servers or the Cancel button to discard any configuration changes and return to the WanClient Configurator.

Editing graphic elements Top Editing graphic elements After adding one for more graphic elements can be edited as follows: Note: Graphic elements need to be selected before they can be edited. For details, see Selecting graphic elements . Tip: The RoundedRectangleRadius property, specified in pixels, adds support for rounded corners for the following graphic elements: Rectangle, Text, Picture and Button - by default this is 0 (disabled), except for Button which is 2. Values from 5 onward result in rounded corners. Moving: Drag the selected graphic elements and/or controls to their required location. Note1: By default, when moving a selection, it snaps (jumps) to the snaplines (displayed in blue) of the other form components, so as to be aligned with these components. This means that you are not able to place this selection in certain places on the graphic form. Note2: When moving a selection, the X and Y axis displacement (in pixels) of the current position relative to its original position is displayed next to the center-point in red, so that you can know when to release the mouse button. ition is displayed next to the center-point in red, so that you can know when to release the mouse button. Sizing: The current selection provides sizing handles small boxes that appear around the perimeter of a selected item, which if dragged changes the size of this item. When the mouse cursor passes over a sizing handle it changes into a double-headed arrow ( ), indicating the directions in which the selection can be sized. Note: When resizing Text graphic elements, the text itself will ALSO be resized. Tip: To draw perfect squares and circles, hold down the CTRL key while resizing their graphic elements. Rotating: Use the rotation handle above the center of the vector as its rotation site for rotating the selection. When the mouse cursor approaches the outer edge of the rotation site it changes into a rotation cursor ( ), which when dragged rotates the selection clockwise or anti-clockwise. Note1: Each selection provides a center-point indicated by a circle ( ) around which it rotates. If

es into a rotation cursor ( ), which when dragged rotates the selection clockwise or anti-clockwise. Note1: Each selection provides a center-point indicated by a circle ( ) around which it rotates. If necessary, drag this center-point to another position before rotating the selection. Note2: When rotating a selection, the angle (in degrees) of the current rotation relative to its original position is displayed next to the center-point in red, so that you can know when to release the mouse button. Clockwise rotation is positive and anti-clockwise rotation is negative. Note3: If necessary, the center-point can be reset by right-clicking and selecting the Reset Center-point item. Graphic elements provide a task menu, opened by clicking its icon, which also contains a Reset Center-point item. Editing nodes: Graphic elements that are collections of basic shapes have nodes at the start and end of each constituent, represented as a small square box ( ). Nodes allow these constituent shapes to be moved, deleted and added. For instance the Polyline which is made up of separate lines, the Spline is made up of curves. Nodes are edited using the node pointer ( ), as follows: Move nodes by drag

be moved, deleted and added. For instance the Polyline which is made up of separate lines, the Spline is made up of curves. Nodes are edited using the node pointer ( ), as follows: Move nodes by dragging them, if the node is attached to two constituents BOTH of them will readjust to their new starting or ending position. Delete nodes by pressing CTRL and clicking the required node, this removes the constituents attached to this node. Add nodes by pressing SHIFT and selecting the existing node that is to be the start or end of the new constituent. This adds the new node on top of the selected node, which needs to be dragged to the required position. elements . Other important properties: Location and size - to dynamically adjust the size and location of this graphic element at runtime. StartPoint and EndPoint: adjusts the size and location of a Line. Rectangle: adjusts the location and dimensions of a Rectangle, Ellipse, Scale and Text. Closed: closes a Polyline or Spline if set to True - this automatically joining the beginning and ending points. ScaleType: changes the displayed scale of a Scale. This also means that the text will not rotate and will remain horizontal regardless of the rotation of this Text vector. Tip: You can use the TemplateGOContextNav control to display the graphic forms associated with the nodes and/or added to the nodes of this Default context. For details, see TemplateGOContextNav controls . To edit the Default context: Select the Default context from the list of contexts to the left of the bottom tool bar of this window. lick the Edit button in the bottom tool bar of this window to create your own logical organisation of your objects and/or other data, by either: You can then either Save the recent changes made to this Default context since it was last saved or Cancel these changes, by selecting the appropriate tool from the bottom tool bar of this window. manually create the necessary hierarchy of nodes , which are like folders in the Context View, each of which typically represent a specific contextual area and can contain additional nodes or a graphic form associated to them or have data elements and/or object model objects added to them: Add or Edit a node to specify the Node Name , which is the literal description used when navigating the defined hierarchy and Node Descriptor , which is typically a 3 character code to reference the specific contextual area that is represented by this node. This dialog then displays the 32 bits of the Agent Status word that contains configuration and run-time status information about the agent. text: Editing the Master Recipe Top Editing the Master Recipe Firstly, select a Step from the Master Recipe list. Enter new information into the Ingredient (Tag) , Verification (Tag) or Tag/Value field. To update the master recipe data select any other field. Effective Alarm Characteristics Top Effective Alarm Characteristics The characteristic of an effective alarm is that it should be: Relevant: requiring acknowledgment and corrective action i.e. NOT an event that can simply be ignored. Unique: does not duplicate another alarm and is not a secondary consequence of a previous alarm. Timely: is not triggered too long before any response is needed or too late to do anything. For instance, when monitoring for over temperature the High alarm is the most important event, not the High-High alarm because the damage is probably already done at this point! Prioritised: indicates the importance with which the operator deals with the problem. Understandable: has a message that is clear and easy to understand. Diagnostic: identifies the problem that has occurred. Advisory: indicates the action that is to be taken. Focusing: draws attention to the most important issues. While the AlarmManagement agent can ensure that the first four characteristics are met, the last 4 characteristics are supported within the Classic UI by assigning a document to each incident that is accessible from the alarm viewer. For details about using the AlarmManagement agent

met, the last 4 characteristics are supported within the Classic UI by assigning a document to each incident that is accessible from the alarm viewer. For details about using the AlarmManagement agent, see Quick Start to Configure and Record Incidents (Alarms/Events) . For details about specifying a document for incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). , see Configuring Incidents . -->

The left Status section contains the following items: The associated ISO 14617 representation, if one exists for this item of equipment One or more of the following status indicators and their meanings: Operating mode : Automatic (PLC) control or Field-based control and/or Hand (Manual control) Warning (a fault or alarm) Interlock (a safety, process and/or start interlock is in effect) Simulation (PLC function block works but does not start the equipment) Maintenance (manual control with PLC control interlocks overridden) One or more common equipment-specific interlocks and/or faults The top right panel, allows one to change how this item of equipment is controlled and, if necessary, operate this equipment, as follows: The Control Mode section: Auto: The equipment is controlled by the PLC. Electrical equipment templates Top Working with Electrical equipment templates In MAPS each piece of electrical equipment requires an associated template. For complex items of equipment consisting of more than one piece of electrical equipment, like conveyors, create a unit for item of equipment and associate all their component-electrical equipment to individual MAPS templates. You can also create custom (user-defined) templates too. Default Electrical equipment templates : the templates of the electrical equipment provided by MAPS . Template naming convention: The first section is the abbreviated or full name of the equipment e.g. DOL (Direct on line motor) or VALVE. The second section can further classify the equipment e.g. for valves _S_ indicates 'single actuating and _D_ indicates 'double actuating'. The second or third section of the template will be _B_ (basic), _S_ (standard) or _A_ (advanced), indicating the level of complexity or diagnostic information provided by this template. For each piece of equipment there can be up to 3 templates, each providing different levels of complexity or diagnostic information, the names of these templates indicate the provided level of co

ate. For each piece of equipment there can be up to 3 templates, each providing different levels of complexity or diagnostic information, the names of these templates indicate the provided level of complexity as follows: _B_ (basic), _S_ (standard) or _A_ (advanced). IMPORTANT: The greater the level of complexity provided by a template, the more signals are required for this item of equipment, which therefore increases the number of the required SCADA tags. This can increase the size and cost of your Adroit licence, as in Adroit you pay for each tag that you scan to a PLC. So ensure that you assign the templates to your equipment carefully. The third or fourth section provides the version of this template e.g. v1_0 stands for version 1.0 Each MAPS template: Provides one or more SCADA graphical representations providing an intelligent faceplate. Enabling data entry Top Enabling data entry To configure the dialog provided by the Data Entry to allow users to enter a data value at runtime and to specify whether this value change is logged or confirmed. Note1: Only single-value data can be entered using this spider i.e. tabular (dataset) data cannot. Enabling Pseudonyms and Macros Top Enabling Pseudonyms and Macros Pseudonyms and macros act as placeholders for part or all of a textual command that is sent to a Command agent . For details, see Using Pseudonyms and Macros . Before these can be used, however, it is necessary to specify whether a Command agent should examine its received messages for pseudonyms and/or macros, so that these can be correctly interpreted. To alert a Command agent to possible pseudonyms and macros in received messages: If necessary, add a Command agent. For details, see Adding Agents . Edit the required Command agent. For details, see Editing Agents . This will display the Edit Command agent dialog. Select the Pseudonyms and Macros tab. Ensure that the Expand pseudonyms in messages checkbox, is checked. Note: Once this checkbox is checked, the ExpandPseudos specific status bit for this agent will also be checked, to indicate that any pseudonyms and macros specified in a received message will be correctly interpreted and any outgoing messages will have the pseudonyms replaced with the full tag. For details, see Specific Status Bits . -->

text: Enabling the Monitoring of OID Values Enabling the Monitoring of OID Values The SNMPManager agent can poll (monitor) OID values from the managed device. Each OID value that you want to monitor is retrieved from the device at the required poll rate and copied into the selected tag, so that this tag can be alarmed, trended (reported), logged and/or manipulated etc. within Adroit . Note: You can also manually poll (obtain the value of) ANY OID value in the device. For details, see Manually Polling OID Values . To enable the polling of a selected OID value: This assumes that the Edit SNMP Manager Agent dialog is displayed and the required OID is in the list. Click the Name field of the required OID to select this row in the list. Click the Browse tag button and use the built-in agent explorer to create and/or select the Tag that will contain this value. For details, see Select a Tag Using the Built-in Agent Explorer. Note: Ensure that the selected agent type can store the data of this OID value. For help on this, see SNMP Object Value Return Types. text: Adroit : Endress & Hauser Promag 800 Email Driver Endress & Hauser Promag 800 Email driver Introduction This driver is designed to provide an interface for Promag 800 flow meters. The data is sent in the form of an email containing a csv attachment. Once the email is received it is decoded to expose the values contained in the attachment and body of the mail. Inbox management is provided through a backup box and an unknown/todo box, where email messages can be moved as appropriate. Messages older than a configured amount of days may be set for auto deletion. A separate Adroit device has to be created for each flow meter with the station ID being set equal to the serial number of the flow meter as per the CSV file that get emailed. There is a resource id allocated automatically on configuration, new devices will attempt to find a compatible configuration (those that share an inbox for example) any others will create a new resource, selecting a resource in the dialogue will load the current configuration for that box, if the device is saved (On OK) any changes will be save with an appropriate warning. Resource ID can be deleted with appropriate warnings if it might affect other devic

ent configuration for that box, if the device is saved (On OK) any changes will be save with an appropriate warning. Resource ID can be deleted with appropriate warnings if it might affect other devices. Offline devices and unknown (unconfigured) devices will have their emails moved to the UNKNOWN box if the MOVE radio is applied. Else if DELETE was selected unconfigured emails will be deleted. And offline device emails will be left in the main INBOX. 1 Adroit : Endress & Hauser Promag 800 Email Driver Configuration Dialog Mail server settings (*Resource key) (the parameters Identified by the * define a resource common to all devices that share those parameters, any change to any other parameter in this group will be changed for all devices using this mailbox.) *Mailbox Type – Choose IMAP or POP depending on your server type. Enhanced Data Logging Top Enhanced Data Logging The data logging sub-system of Adroit provides the following enhancements: Improved performance : using the datalog change queue to improve the data logging sub-system performance. Demand logging : configuring Adroit to only log data at specific times or events, such as at the end of a batch. Multiple log sets : instead of specifying only a single rate and period per datalog agent configuration, you can create multiple log sets within a single datalog agent. Improved Integrity : the Agent Server ALWAYS honors the data log settings as found in the agent database (WGP) file to prevent Datalog agent exceptions. Advanced Datalog Configuration (global settings) : all the global settings that affect the operation of the data logging sub-system can be configured from a single dialog, whenever a user logs a tag. To Minimise the Risk of Datalog Corruption from a Power Failure . -->

EnvisaLink™ TPI Programmer's Document DEVELOPER DOCUMENTATION VERSION 1.08 February 10, 2017 1.0 Overview The EnvisaLink™ Third Party Interface (TPI) consists of a set of commands and responses designed to allow third-party command and control applications to interface directly with the EnvisaLink™ module and in turn the security system, over a TCP/IP connection. The goal in releasing this programmer's interface is not only to allow existing home-automation software greater interaction with the EnvisaLink module, but also to encourage the development of third-party applications on mobile platforms. 2.0 Connecting to the Envisalink™ 2.1 Hardware Connections Please refer to Envisalink installation or “Quick Start” document. 2.2 TCP Connection The Envisalink acts as a server for the TCP connection and the user application is the client. The Envisalink listens on port 4025 and will only accept one client connection on that port. Any subsequent connections will be denied. The Envisalink will close the connection if the client closes its side. To initiate a connection, the application must first start a session by establishing a TCP socket. Once established the TPI will send a 5053 comma

l close the connection if the client closes its side. To initiate a connection, the application must first start a session by establishing a TCP socket. Once established the TPI will send a 5053 command (See section 3.0 for a detailed description of the protocol) requesting a session password. The client should then, within 10 seconds, send 005 login request. The 005 command contains the password which is the same password to log into the Envisalink's local web page. Upon successful login, the Envisalink's TPI will respond with the session status command, 505, and whether the password was accepted or rejected. If a password is not received within 10 seconds, the TPI will issue a 5052 command and close the TCP socket. The socket will also be closed if the password fails. Once the password is accepted, the session is created and will continue until the TCP connection is dropped. Note, as with all network communications, it is possible the TCP socket could be lost due to a network disruption, or an exception at either the client or server end. Application programmers are advised to include some handling for dropped connections. The Poll command (000) is a useful command to test of the

ion, or an exception at either the client or server end. Application programmers are advised to include some handling for dropped connections. The Poll command (000) is a useful command to test of the connection is still alive. Alternately, an application could watch for the period time broadcast (510) which is issued by the panel every 4 minutes. Enivsalink 3 vs Envisalink 4 Difference The Envisalink 3 only supports 6 ASCII digits for a password but the Envisalink 4 supports 10. IMPORTANT: Envisalink Application Firewall As of Envisalink 4 (1.0.102) and Envisalink 3 (1.12.180) the Envisalink has an internal firewall that will block all TPI connections that originate outside of the network segment it resides upon. This is to protect users who expose their Envisalinks to the public Internet either by mistake or ignorance. This feature can be disabled by changing the default user's password from “user” to any other password, 4 characters or longer. 3.0 Detailed Description of the Feature Set 3.1 Communications Protocol All data is sent as hex ASCII codes. The transmission from will consist of the following: CCC DDD…DDD CKS CR/LF CCC => 3 Digit Command This tells the module or the app

DDD…DDD => Data Byte(s) This is the data that may be needed for the command. For example, after the Partition Arm command (030), the application must specify which partition should be armed (1-8). CKS => Checksum The checksum is calculated by adding the hex value of all command and data digits, and truncating the result to 8 bits. The upper and lower nibbles of the result are converted to ASCII characters before sending. Evaluation Options for Expressions Top Evaluation Options for Expressions There are two options available to you in this group, whether the expression is to evaluate continuously or only when triggered by a change in the trigger input slot. If the continuous option is selected then a new result will be generated whenever any of the inputs change or even if the expression itself changes. By design, a triggered Expression agent will always generate subscription updates for the value slot even if the value slot has not actually changed, which can lead to unnecessary Agent Server CPU loads and network traffic when remote UI clients have been deployed. These unnecessary subscription updates can be disabled, by adding the PropagateTrigger registry value. Note: When selecting the Continuous option ensure that there are no cyclic relationships between outputs and inputs. If such cyclic dependencies exist for a continuously evaluating expression Adroit is likely to become unresponsive. -->

text: Example of using Notify agents to send pager or SMS messages Top Example of using Notify agents to send pager or SMS messages Note: By using the Email driver, Notify agents can also send email messages. For details, see Configuring Notify agents to send email messages. Consider the scenario of a plant with an existing Adroit configuration. The existing Adroit configuration must be extended to provide support for the routing of only certain important alarms to various personnel. The plant consists of four dams that are modeled using the four analog agents, dam_level_1, dam_level_2, dam_level_3 and dam_level_4. Each of the analog agents are currently alarmed on the high and high-high alarm limits using route 2 of the alarm agent, dam_level_alarms. Route 2 sends alarms to an alarm list agent, dam_level_alarm_list, and to the local event log. The high-high alarms for the analog agents, dam_level_1 and dam_level_2 are very important to Harry and Sally and they would like these alarms to be routed to their cellular phones when these alarms become active. Both Harry and Sally have cellular phones on the Vodacom network. Larry is concerned about the high-high alarm of dam_level_1. He has a

metadata.title: Example of using Notify agents to send pager or SMS messages

text: routed to their cellular phones when these alarms become active. Both Harry and Sally have cellular phones on the Vodacom network. Larry is concerned about the high-high alarm of dam_level_1. He has a cellular phone on the MTN network. However, neither Harry, Sally nor Larry want the remaining plant alarms to be routed to their cellular phones, that is, the alarms for dam_level_3 and dam_level_4. In order to access the cellular or pager network, install the user-defined protocol driver in the Drivers section of the Adroit setup program. Then add a device for each cellular network. Name these devices, for instance, VODACOM and MTN. Both devices will make use of a modem installed on the Agent Server computer. Notice that each Pager device represents a cellular or pager service network, while each Notify agent represents a person to be notified. Create three Notify agents to represent each person, Harry, Sally and Larry; namely HARRY, SALLY and LARRY. Edit each Notify agent and insert that person’s cellular-phone number in the field entitled "User Code". The cellular number required in this field is the number excluding the 082 or 083 network code. The alarm can be transmitted the ins

metadata.title: Example of using Notify agents to send pager or SMS messages

text: t person’s cellular-phone number in the field entitled "User Code". The cellular number required in this field is the number excluding the 082 or 083 network code. The alarm can be transmitted the instant it occurs by checking Transmit an Alarm when it is raised . Each alarm routed to a Notify agent will be kept in a separate list of alarms for each Notify agent. An alarm will be removed from the list only when it has been cleared and acknowledged. It is also possible to send the list periodically to keep people informed of alarms that have not been cleared or acknowledged. The format of the alarm record structure can also be specified as desired. Scan the "rawValue" slot of the Notify agents using the relevant pager devices. HARRY.rawValue and SALLY.rawValue will be scanned using the VODACOM device. LARRY.rawValue will be scanned using the MTN device. Start each device. It is possible to test the device configuration by sending a message to each person. Simply set the "value" slot of each Notify agent to any string value and verify the message gets through to each cellular-phone. Now modify the alarm routes for the alarm agent, dam_level_alarms. Edit the alarm agent and add a new

text: each Notify agent to any string value and verify the message gets through to each cellular-phone. Now modify the alarm routes for the alarm agent, dam_level_alarms. Edit the alarm agent and add a new route, route 3. It is important to note that the new route includes the routing information of route 2 (the alarm list agent dam_level_alarm_list and the local event log), that is, the new route should be a superset of the old route. This ensures that the operation of the plant from an operators point of view is unaffected by adding in the cellular phone destinations. When the operators acknowledge alarms in the manner that were practiced before, the acknowledgement will be sent to the additional cellular phone destinations. Add the Notify agents HARRY and SALLY to the ‘Output’ list of route 3. The alarm routing configuration of the high-high alarms for the analog agents, dam_level_1 and dam_level_2, must be altered from route 2 to route 3. To cater for Larry, edit the alarm agent, dam_level_alarm, and add a new route, route 4. Ensure that this route includes the alarm routing information of route 2. Example of altered precedence: Consider the expression: v1 | v2 & v3 These operator precedence rules say that & has precedence over | So this IS the same as: (v1 | (v2 & v3)) However, you add a ! to one of the variables, this appears to influence this precedence ! Consider the expression: !v1 | v2 & v3 According to the operator precedence rules this should be the same as ((!v1) | (v2 & v3)) However, this is not the case, it is actually treated as the following by expression agents: (((!v1) | v2) & v3) Do if true – else stay the same v1? v2 : v99 IF v1 TRUE, value = v2, ELSE value = old value (v99) Logic expression !v1 & !v2 means value IS (NOT v01) AND (NOT v02) ( e.g. if v1=1 and v2=1, then v99=0) v11| v12 means value IS v11 OR v12 Nested expression v01 <= v02 ? 0 : (v01 >= v03)?1 : v99 means: Turn a digital on then value goes too low, but leave it on until the value goes above the HI, with: v1=input value, v2=lo and v3=hi Totaliser expression (v0

01 <= v02 ? 0 : (v01 >= v03)?1 : v99 means: Turn a digital on then value goes too low, but leave it on until the value goes above the HI, with: v1=input value, v2=lo and v3=hi Totaliser expression (v02==v06) && (v03==v07) ? 0 : v99 + v01 means IF (v02 EQUALS v06) AND (v03 EQUALS v07) THEN value IS 0 ELSE value IS value PLUS v01 Ramp expression v01 ? (v99 + 0.05) : v99 means IF v01 TRUE THEN value IS value PLUS 0.05 ELSE value IS value (i.e. no change) Control expression (!v02| v03) ? !v04 : v04 means IF (NOT v02 OR v03) TRUE THEN value IS NOT v04 ELSE value IS v04 Prioritization expression (v01<<0) | (v02<<1) | (v03<<2) | (v04<<3) means value IS v01 SHIFTED 0 BITS LEFT OR v02 SHIFTED 1 BITS LEFT (i.e. multiplied by 2) OR v03 SHIFTED 2 BITS LEFT (i.e. multiplied by 4) OR v04 SHIFTED 3 BITS LEFT (i.e. multiplied by 8) Angular expression atan(v01/v02) means ANGLE IN RADIANS whose TANGENT is v01 DIVIDED by v02 Power expression pow2(v03) means v03 RAISED TO THE POWER OF 2 (i.e. squared) Remainder expression v1%v2 means v01 MODULUS v02 ( e.g. if V01=34 and v02=5, v99=4) Exponentiation expression exp(v1) means NATURAL LOG BASE ‘e’ RAISED TO THE POWER v01 (ev01 ) ( e.g. if v1=4 then 2.7182

ainder expression v1%v2 means v01 MODULUS v02 ( e.g. if V01=34 and v02=5, v99=4) Exponentiation expression exp(v1) means NATURAL LOG BASE ‘e’ RAISED TO THE POWER v01 (ev01 ) ( e.g. if v1=4 then 2.7182818284= 54.59815003) Note: v01 may not exceed 422 Raising the power exp( v2 * log(v1) ) v1 RAISED TO THE POWER OF v2 i.e. v1v2 Bitwise negation expression ~v1 means 1’S COMPLEMENT OF V01 ( e.g. if v1= 1, v99 = –2) -->
