text: Execute Command Behaviours Top Execute Command Behaviours This Behaviour can be applied to controls and graphic elements (vectors) to perform the following commands: Note: You CANNOT test Execute Command behaviour that perform graphic forms operations (opening, closing etc.) in the SmartUI Designer in Run mode, this functionality is only available in the SmartUI Operator. If you try to do so, an alert informing you of this is displayed. Tip: If necessary, more than one Execute Command Behaviour (command) may be assigned to perform additional commands. To add a command to a control or vector: Add or edit an Execute Command Behaviour to display its configuration dialog. Select the required command from the Command list and configure it as follows: Start application: to launch an application and specify any required parameters, you configure this command as follows: Application Name: browse in the required application. By default this specifies an absolute path. Check the Exclude path checkbox to specify a relative path, from the folder in which the Client executable is being run from, which is typically the installation folder. IMPORTANT: You need to ensure that this application is l

ckbox to specify a relative path, from the folder in which the Client executable is being run from, which is typically the installation folder. IMPORTANT: You need to ensure that this application is located in the specified path of your Operators and/or Web Operators. Parameters: specify any parameters required by this application. Open graphic form : to open a specific graphic form, you configure this command as follows: Graphic Form: click the browse button to launch the Graphic Form Selection dialog to select the required graphic form from the configured projects on the available SmartUI Servers. Open As : specify how the graphic form opens, as follows: Modal Form : the graphic form opens as a separate window that requires the user to interact with it or close it before being able to continue using the application. This is the default selection. Modeless Form : the graphic form opens as a separate window that allows the user to interact with it and also return to a previous task without closing it. Tab Page : the graphic form opens as a another tabbed page within the workspace. Replace : the graphic form replaces the currently displayed graphic form. Template Graphic Object : th

hout closing it. Tab Page : the graphic form opens as a another tabbed page within the workspace. Replace : the graphic form replaces the currently displayed graphic form. Template Graphic Object : the graphic form is opened within a specific Template Graphic Object control. This option displays the TemplateGO field to specify the name of the required TemplateGO or TemplateGONavToolbar control, from the list - assuming that one or more of these controls have been added to the graphic form on which this Execute Command Behaviour is on. Position : specify where, on the screen, the graphic form opens, as follows: Center of Screen : opens the graphic form in the center of the screen (the default setting). Location : uses the Location settings to specify the required X and Y position of the top left hand corner of the graphic form. Mouse cursor : opens the graphic form at the current position of the mouse cursor Template Set : specify which pre-configured template set to activate, when this graphic form opens. Level : specify which pre-configured level to show, when this graphic form opens. size : specify the dimensions of the opened graphic form, as follows: By default, this conforms t

graphic form opens. Level : specify which pre-configured level to show, when this graphic form opens. size : specify the dimensions of the opened graphic form, as follows: By default, this conforms to the size of opened graphic form. If you check the Custom checkbox then specify the required Width and Height dimensions of the opened graphic form. Note1: The Advanced View provides an Aliases tab for this Open Graphic Form command, which lists any configured aliases of the specified graphic form, so that these values can be set either by specific data elements or by static values. This tab can be used to Drive alias values with wizard substitutions or Pass alias values from parent to child SmartUI Templates . Note2: If the specified graphic form does not exist (for instance if it was typed in incorrectly or if this Behaviour was copied from another project), then when this Behaviour is performed in the SmartUI Operator, it opens the specified graphic form containing the text 'graphic form not found'. IMPORTANT: The default action for values entered into the Aliases tab of the Advanced View has been changed to always specify the text that is either manually entered or browsed in, unl

rm not found'. IMPORTANT: The default action for values entered into the Aliases tab of the Advanced View has been changed to always specify the text that is either manually entered or browsed in, unless the Use Tag Value checkbox is checked, at which time it will try to resolve the required data element value from the entered (typically browsed in) text. Therefore when passing substitutions or aliases, in curly {} brackets, ensure that the Use Tag Value checkbox is NOT checked, which is its default setting. Tip: If necessary this graphic form can be opened within a specific TemplateGO a Template Graphic Object control that displays a graphic form and connects data elements to any aliases of this graphic form. control on this graphic form. Close graphic form : to either close a specific graphic form or the currently open graphic form, you configure this command as follows: Either specify the required graphic form to close, as follows: Graphic Form: click the browse button to launch the Graphic Form Selection dialog to select the required graphic form from the configured projects on the available SmartUI Servers. Or check the This form checkbox to close the graphic form that is curr

Graphic Form Selection dialog to select the required graphic form from the configured projects on the available SmartUI Servers. Or check the This form checkbox to close the graphic form that is currently open, when this command is performed. Print graphic form : to send the currently displayed graphic form to the default printer. If you check the Show Print Dialog option, then your users can choose which printer is used to print this graphic form and/or which print settings are used when printing this graphic form, such as the required page orientation. Otherwise you the currently displayed graphic form will be sent to the default printer. Log off : to log off the current Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. user, you configure this command as follows: No further configuration is required to simply log off the current user. If you have configured an auto-login account for this Client, then you can check the Auto login checkbox to automatically log in again using the specified auto-login user credentials. This, in effect, performs a “switch user” operation for the pre-configured auto-login user. Log on : to perf

gin checkbox to automatically log in again using the specified auto-login user credentials. This, in effect, performs a “switch user” operation for the pre-configured auto-login user. Log on : to perform a “switch user” operation by logging in another user, you configure this command as follows: Username: either type in the name of the required Allowed or Impersonated user or use the browse button to use the User Browser to specify this user name. Password: type in the required password of the selected user. If necessary, click the Advanced View button to specify some or all of the following additional configurable options: Confirmation: provide pre and/or post confirmation for this command, by selecting one or both of the following checkboxes: Log action : logs (records) this command in the Application event log for forensic or audit trail purposes. Confirm action : pops up a yes/no confirmation message box before the command is performed. Security: ensure this action is only performed when the designated user/s and/or group/s are logged on, as follows: Either click the browse button to specify a String data element, which contains the names of the required users and/or groups. Execute Command spiders Top Execute Command spiders The Execute Command spider can run an application (.EXE), command file (.CMD) or a batch file (.BAT) when the spider is triggered and also allows command-line parameters to be specified, if required. Note: This launching can be confirmed and/or logged to the event log - see the spider inputs for more details. To add this spider to the spider workspace . To run an application or batch file . Configuration Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider. Note: Menu items that are enabled will have a tick mark to the left of them. Detail View: This can be used to display the configuration view of this spider, so its name, description, inputs and outputs can be configured. For details, see Working with spider configuration views . Tip: Double-click the title bar of the spider to display or hide the configuration view of the spider. Delete Spider: This can be used to remove this spider from the spider workspace. For details, see Removing spiders . Trigger Spider From Event: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by means of an event. For details, see Triggerin

he spider workspace. For details, see Removing spiders . Trigger Spider From Event: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by means of an event. For details, see Triggering a spider from an event . This is disabled by default. Enable Silk Triggering: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by any silks that are attached to the inputs of this spider. For details, see Triggering spiders . This is enabled by default. Propagate Outputs At Startup: This enables the spider to supply the silks connected to its outputs with values as soon as its spider workspace enters into running mode. For details, see Working with spider workspaces or Sending spider outputs at startup . This is disabled by default. Trigger Now!: This will cause this spider to immediately be triggered. Inputs and outputs: This describes the available inputs and outputs displayed by the default configuration view of this spider. Execute Statements Top Execute Statements Queries provide common tasks for managing your database that is connected to an OLE DB datasource. The Execute Statements can perform the predefined stored procedures or user-functions of the database, which are listed by the Procedures branch. Export Compressed Event Log Files Top Export Compressed Event Log Files Ensure the Event logs tick box is ticked. Ensure the Compress tick box, below the Event logs tick box, is ticked so that the event log files are backed up to a single compressed file (events.zip) in the backup directory. Note: This compressed file is in the standard Winzip format and the component event files are stored with their full backup path information from the root. These backed up event logs, consist of the three Operating System event log files, namely: application.evt, security.evt and system.evt. Note: These event log files can be viewed using the Event Viewer application in the Administrative Tools program group. -->

Export Master Recipe Top Export Master Recipe This exports the master recipe and all of its control recipes to a .CSV file. Note: This exporting can also be achieved by setting the recipe agent’s " exportName " slot to the full path and filename of the CSV file that is to be exported. If used in conjunction with the " importname " slot, it is now possible to redefine the contents of the master and control recipes completely. But if control recipe names are changed then their respective batch numbers will be reset to zero. -->

Exporting and Importing controls Top Exporting and importing controls You can export one or more configured controls for reuse, by importing them into the same or other graphic forms. Click for more details: In this way it is possible to create a library of commonly used controls, whose properties are fully or partially configured – instead of creating these controls from scratch each time they are required. Note: Only the controls and their MANUALLY configured properties can be exported, in other words any spiders, Behaviours or other methods that are used to configure their properties will NOT be exported. To export controls: Select the required control/s. For details, see Selecting controls . Right-click and select the Export Selection menu option. This will display the Save As dialog. Note: An Invalid Selection error message is displayed if no controls are currently selected when this option is used. Browse for the required folder and then type in the required file name and press the Save button. Note1: The name and especially the extension of this file is immaterial and does not affect the importing process. Note2: If only a file name is specified then the .XML file extension

he Save button. Note1: The name and especially the extension of this file is immaterial and does not affect the importing process. Note2: If only a file name is specified then the .XML file extension is provided. This will save the selected controls to the specified file. Note: When these controls are imported, their location depends upon where the cursor is in this graphic form. To import controls: Ensure that the Windows Explorer and the SmartUI Designer application windows are positioned in such a way that the exported file containing the required controls is visible in Windows Explorer and the required graphic form into which these controls are to be added is also visible in the SmartUI Designer. Drag the file containing the exported controls from Windows Explorer into the required graphic form in the SmartUI Designer. Note: The imported controls are initially added to this graphic form in the SAME position from which they were exported. The imported controls are immediately selected so that they can be moved to another location, if necessary. Note: Only the attributes of the imported controls are imported. -->

text: Exporting and Importing Groups and Users Top Exporting and Importing Groups and Users If you need to create the same groups and/or users on more than one computer, such as when you use a Workgroup, then the Adroit Security Manager utility can reduce this management overhead as follows: Create the necessary groups and/or users on one computer. Export these users and groups via the Adroit Security Manager to a users.ini file Launch the Adroit Security Manager on the required computer and import these users and groups, which do not exist on this computer, from this users.ini file. This functionality makes configuring Adroit security on a workgroup a lot easier, since you can simply create all the Adroit users and their groups ONCE and import these on ALL the other computers in your workgroup. To export the created groups and users: this allows you to export all the groups and the users on this computer and the groups that each user is a member of OR to only export the Adroit groups and Adroit users that have been created on this computer and their group memberships. Press the Windows key and start typing in Security Manager and select it from the list. Open the Tools menu. Click on th

metadata.title: Exporting and Importing Groups and Users

text: roit users that have been created on this computer and their group memberships. Press the Windows key and start typing in Security Manager and select it from the list. Open the Tools menu. Click on the Export … menu item. Click Yes to export ALL the groups and users and their group memberships on this computer. This ALSO exports the local Power Users group and the Adroit users that are members of this group, if the Configure Power Users option has been applied. Click No to ONLY export the Adroit groups and Adroit users and their Adroit group memberships that are configured on this computer. Click Cancel to NOT export ANY groups and users. The exported groups and users, if any, are saved to a file called export.users.ini , which is typically located in the Adroit installation folder, which is typically C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit . If necessary rename this file and copy it to the required Adroit computer/s that you would like to identically configure their Adroit users and groups and then import this file using their Adroit Security Manager utility. text: Exporting and Importing project translation tables Top Exporting and Importing project translation tables Export the project translation table to an Excel spreadsheet (.XLS) file so you or a professional translator can translate the various entries of both the Graphic Form and Data tabs of the project translation table, which you can them re-import. You can also export this project translation table from one project and import this or the translated file into another project or another project on another computer. To export a project translation table: Open the required project in the Enterprise Manager . For details, see Opening Projects . Double-click its Translation object or its icon . This displays the Translation configuration dialog , which can be maximised and/or manually resized as required . Right click the Properties column heading and select Export Translation . Tip: You can also click the Export button. Select the path and file name of the required Excel spreadsheet (.XLS) file. Click the Save button. The entire project translation table is saved to this file both the Graphic Form and Data tabs of this table are saved to separate pages within this file . To import a pr

metadata.title: Exporting and Importing project translation tables

text: file. Click the Save button. The entire project translation table is saved to this file both the Graphic Form and Data tabs of this table are saved to separate pages within this file . To import a project translation table: ensure that you are able to access the location in which the required Excel spreadsheet (.XLS) file. Open the required project in the Enterprise Manager . For details, see Opening Projects . Double-click its Translation object or its icon . This displays the Translation configuration dialog , which can be maximised and/or manually resized as required . Right click the Properties column heading and select Import Translation . Tip: You can also click the Import button. Select the required path and file name of the required Excel spreadsheet (.XLS) file. WARNING! Ensure you select the correct file as the contents of this file REPLACES the existing entries of both the Graphic Form and Data tabs of the project translation table. Click the Open button. The existing translations of both the Graphic Form and Data tabs of the project translation table are REPLACED with the imported entries. -->

text: Exporting categories and their incidents Top Exporting categories and their incidents The Categories tree of the AlarmManagement Agent edit dialog allows you to add and configure categories and incidents. You can use the Export button to save and/or edit these categories and incidents in a .CSV file editor instead. Benefits: Ability to bulk add and/or configure categories and/or their incidents. Note: If necessary, you change the category of an incident to another existing category, in which case this new Category ID is applied to any occurrences in the current and historical tables. Ability to save your existing configuration to import this configuration into another AlarmManagement agent (in this case save this .CSV file to the name of the required agent first before importing it). To export/import categories and their incidents: this described the process involved when bulk configuring the categories and/or incidents of the Categories tree for an AlarmManagement agent. Click the Export button in the AlarmManagement Agent edit dialog. Note: A message box is displayed if there is nothing to export. This exports a .CSV file to the Work subfolder of your designated project folder, w

This file typically has the same name as this AlarmManagement agent. If you have MS Excel installed then this file opens in it, otherwise it opens in your default .CSV file editor. Save this file, once you have performed the necessary changes to it and closed your .CSV editor. Click the Import button in the AlarmManagement Agent edit dialog. Exporting charts Top Exporting charts This exports the current chart as an image file and/or to export the current chart configuration settings as a template file(.ten) and/or to export the charted data to a file. Note: The (Toolbar) ExportChartButtonVisible property needs to be enabled to display this toolbar button. To export the chart: Click the Export Chart toolbar button from the toolbar of the required charting control to display the TeeChart Export configuration dialog. To export the chart as a picture: this saves the current chart as an image, either in one of the supported image file formats and/or to the clipboard so that it can be pasted into another application. Select the Picture tab. If necessary, specify the required Format of the image file If necessary, use the Options tab to specify whether the colors are to be left unchanged ( Default ) or set to Grayscale . If necessary, use the size tab to specify the required Width and Height of the image in pixels and if you want to Keep aspect ratio or not. Either click Copy to copy the currently configured image to the clipboard. Or click Save... to specify required path and filename of the currently selected Format . To ex

to Keep aspect ratio or not. Either click Copy to copy the currently configured image to the clipboard. Or click Save... to specify required path and filename of the currently selected Format . To export the current chart configuration settings: this can save these settings and the current series data to a template file (.TEN), which can be imported into another charting control so that it can have the same look and feel. Select the Native tab. If necessary, you can Include Series Data along with the chart configuration settings. Check the File size checkbox to obtain an estimate of the size of this template file. Either click Copy to copy the chart configuration settings to the clipboard. Or click Save... to specify required path and filename of the template (.TEN) file. To import a chart configuration settings template file, which configures the chart accordingly, see Importing chart templates . To export the data of the charted series: this can save this data to one of the following file types: text, xml, an html table or an Excel spreadsheet file. Select the Data tab. Select the required Series from list box. Specify the file Format for this data from the 4 options. Specify wh

g file types: text, xml, an html table or an Excel spreadsheet file. Select the Data tab. Select the required Series from list box. Specify the file Format for this data from the 4 options. Specify what other elements to include with the data, such as: Point Index: to display a zero based index of the charted values. Point Labels: to display the labels of the data points, if currently specified by the charted values. Header: This adds a row at the beginning of this file that describes the columns. Specify the delimiting character to use within the specified file Format , if necessary. Either click Copy to copy the currently configured data to the clipboard. Or click Save... to specify required path and filename of the selected file Format . Tip: The Advanced View of the Style tab when configuring Line and FastLine series allow you to specify the required Value Format and DateTime Format of the exported values. Click the Close button when you have finished the exporting operations. -->

Exporting datasources Top Exporting datasources Instead of manually duplicating a datasource from one SmartUI Server to another, you can export the datasource and its configuration to a file and then import this datasource into another SmartUI Server from this file. This is useful for datasources that have extensive configuration, such as OLE DB datasources with many configured queries and/or stored procedures. This can also be used to save time and ensure that clustered Servers have exactly the same datasource configuration. Note: It is not recommended to export or import the datasources within the Management and Projects datasource categories. To export a datasource: Select the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager , as follows: Open the Enterprise Manager . Navigate to Servers > [Server Name] . Tip: The connection name is prefixed by the SmartUI Server computer name. If necessary, expand the Datasources category. Right-click the relevant datasource name or icon and select Export Datasource . This will display the Browse For Folder dialog. Select and/or create the required folder in which this exported datasource should be saved and then press the OK button. This adds

t Export Datasource . This will display the Browse For Folder dialog. Select and/or create the required folder in which this exported datasource should be saved and then press the OK button. This adds two files to this location, which have the same name as the selected datasource and the following extensions: .DSINFO and .DSINFOINDEX. Note: It is essential that BOTH of these files remain in the same folder in order for this datasource to be successfully imported. For further details on importing datasources, see Importing datasources . -->

Exporting graphic form translations Top Exporting local graphic form translations to the project You can export translations from the graphic form translation table (the Translation window) for the additional languages you have added (NOT from the Graphic Form Language column whose header is bold and underlined). This should only be performed when all or most of the textual strings of the Graphic Form Language column match those in the global project translation table. IMPORTANT: ONLY the translation entries (rows) of the exported language are exported, whose Graphic Form Language column entries MATCH in BOTH the graphic form and project translation tables! Note1: Any translations in the global translation table which do not exist in the Graphic Form Language column of this graphic form translation table will remain unchanged. Note2: You can only export ONE language of translations from the graphic form translation table at a time. To export all the translations for an entire language This assumes that you have added the required languages performed their translations. Ensure that the required graphic form is opened and displayed in the Design workspace . Ensure that the project tr

This assumes that you have added the required languages performed their translations. Ensure that the required graphic form is opened and displayed in the Design workspace . Ensure that the project translation table contains the Graphic Form Language column and that all or most of these textual strings match those in the global project translation table. This can be best achieved by using the Fetch operation of the project translation table for this graphic form. For details, see Fetching translation strings from graphic forms . Open the Translation tool window. . Right-click on the heading or one of the cell in this language column and select Export Language to Project Translation Table . Note: You cannot export the Graphic Form Language column, hence this command is not provided by it. ONLY the translation entries (rows) of the exported language are exported, whose Graphic Form Language column entries MATCH in BOTH the graphic form and project translation tables. This will display a confirmation dialog, that displays the success or failure of this export operation. Click the Finish button to close the translation table. For details on using these translations in other graphic for

confirmation dialog, that displays the success or failure of this export operation. Click the Finish button to close the translation table. For details on using these translations in other graphic forms of this project, see Importing global project translations or Pushing translations to graphic forms . -->

Exporting graphic forms Top Exporting graphic forms In order to reuse or backup existing graphic forms, it is possible to export graphic forms from the Enterprise Manager to a local or networked hard disk using Windows Explorer. Note1: This can only be performed if the currently logged on user has the necessary security permissions. For details, see Securing projects . Note2: An exported graphic form can be imported into any project. For details, see Importing graphic forms . To export a graphic form to the hard disk: In the SmartUI Designer: Open the required project in the Enterprise Manager . For details, see Opening Projects . If necessary, expand click the plus (+) box to the left of the current icon or name its required existing folder(s), until the required folder is displayed. Right-click on this graphic form or its icon and select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. Copy . In Windows Explorer: Either create or select the folder that will contain this graphic form. Right-click on this folder and select Paste . Tip: Graphic forms can also be exported by dragging them from the Enterprise Manager into the required f

t the folder that will contain this graphic form. Right-click on this folder and select Paste . Tip: Graphic forms can also be exported by dragging them from the Enterprise Manager into the required folder in the Windows Explorer. Note: Each saved graphic form, is entirely self-sufficient, containing all the data that it requires, such as spiders, levels and layers and translations. -->

Exporting MAPS projects to and importing them from Excel Top Exporting MAPS projects to and importing them from Excel The main purpose or use of this Export to / Import from Excel functionality is to allow you to bulk configure your MAPS project after creating it using the MAPS project wizard. For instance, when creating a plant with 100 conveyors, it may be useful to add one conveyor using the MAPS project wizard and then export the project and bulk configure the other 99 conveyors in Excel and then import this modified project. Note: You need Microsoft Excel 2003 or later installed before you can use this functionality. Tip: We recommend that you first use the MAPS Project wizard to create at least one Plant Area, PLC, Unit and Equipment – to understand the required syntax and requirements for the fields on each of the worksheets of this Excel file. To export a project to Excel: Right click the required MAPS project in the MAPS window and select the Export to Excel option. Specify the path and file name of the required Microsoft Excel Spreadsheet (.xls file). This creates and populates a separate worksheet for each hierarchical component of this MAPS project. Note: If you make mi

This exported configuration can be viewed and/or edited in a compatible XML Spreadsheet program such as Microsoft Excel and re-imported later into this or another spider workspace. Exporting the Alarming Configuration Top Exporting the Alarming Configuration If necessary, you can save the entire configuration of the Adroit alarming sub-system in a single table of the alarm management database, for analysis. This gives you access to your alarm agent configuration, which previously you could only view through associated agents. To export the Adroit alarming configuration to the AM database: Edit your AlarmManagement agent. Click for more details: Select the name of this AlarmManagement agent. For details, see Locating an agent . Right click and select the Edit... menu item. This will display the Edit AlarmManagement Agent dialog. Click the Export alarm cfg button in the Edit AlarmManagement agent dialog. Click Yes when the confirmation dialog is displayed. The AlarmManagement agent creates the Adr_AM_AlarmConfigurationDump table in its associated OLE DB database and populates it with the alarming configuration. The created Adr_AM_AlarmConfigurationDump table provides the following fields: Idx (Integer), used to sort the table; Process (a 30 character String) representing the applicable Agent Server; AlarmAgent (a 30 character String); Incident (a 80 character S

es the following fields: Idx (Integer), used to sort the table; Process (a 30 character String) representing the applicable Agent Server; AlarmAgent (a 30 character String); Incident (a 80 character String); Description (a 80 character String); Route (Integer); AlarmLists (a 80 character String); Devices (a 80 character String); Outputs (a 80 character String); Eventlogs (a 80 character String); Priority (Integer); AlarmDelay (Integer); Acknowledge (Integer); Condition (a 80 character String); InhibitUntil (a 20 character String). -->

Exporting the OID List Exporting the OID List The OID list contains all the OIDs for the managed device, whose values you select to monitor and/or control. If necessary, you can export this list of OIDs to a .CSV file, for one of the following reasons: To bulk add and/or configure OIDs (in this case modify this file in a .CSV file editor and then import it into the SNMPManager agent). To save your existing OID configuration, so that this can be imported into another SNMPManager agent (in this case save this .CSV file to the name of the required agent first before importing it). To bulk configure the OID list: Note: You need to Disable polling before you can export the OID list. Click the Export button in the SNMPManager agent edit dialog. This exports the current list of OIDs to the following .CSV file: The file is placed in the Work subfolder of your designated project folder, which is typically C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Configurations\Default \Work. The file uses the following naming convention: SNMP_ SNMPManagerAgentName_OIDlist.csv, where SNMPManagerAgentName is the name of your SNMPManager agent e.g. SNMP_SNMP001_OIDList.csv. Example: The following is an exampl

following naming convention: SNMP_ SNMPManagerAgentName_OIDlist.csv, where SNMPManagerAgentName is the name of your SNMPManager agent e.g. SNMP_SNMP001_OIDList.csv. Example: The following is an example of an exported list of OIDs: Open this file in a .CSV file editor, such as MS Excel. The exported file contains the following columns: Enabled: A Boolean value that specifies whether this OID (value) is polled (returned) from the device. Writeable: A Boolean value that specifies whether this OID is written to the device. OID: This is either the numeric format of the OID of the device or ‘General Object’ if this refers to a general or calculated statistic common to all devices. Exposing properties Top Exposing properties Use the Hidden Property spider to expose and/or manipulate properties of the specified object that are normally hidden. These properties will either be displayed as inputs, if they are writable and/or outputs, if they are readable. To expose the required properties of the selected object Note: It is only possible to expose properties once an object has been selected. For details, see Selecting the required object . Select the required Hidden Property spider. Right-click its title bar and select Expose Object Properties . The Property Browser configuration dialog is displayed to expose one or more of the properties of the specified Object input for this spider. To manually specify one or more properties: In the Expose Object Properties dialog on the right: Specify the name of the required property in the Property Name edit box. Note: Property names are case sensitive, if the specified case is incorrect this property will not be recognised and therefore cannot be manipulated. Clear the checkboxes, which determine whether you want this property to have an associated input and/or output, as follows: Clear the CanRead checkbox, if the specifie

therefore cannot be manipulated. Clear the checkboxes, which determine whether you want this property to have an associated input and/or output, as follows: Clear the CanRead checkbox, if the specified property cannot be read from (e.g. a write only property), this will prevent this property from being added to the Outputs of this spider. Clear the CanWrite checkbox, if the specified property cannot be written to (e.g. a read only property), this will prevent this property from being added to the Inputs of this spider. Click the Add button. This adds the specified property to the Added Inputs and/or the Added Outputs columns, depending on which checkboxes were cleared. If necessary, add another property manually or select an existing property instead. Click the Finish button, once all the required properties have been added. To select one or more existing properties: In the Expose Object Properties dialog on the right: Either click the View Properties button, to immediately display the existing properties for the specified object in the Select Properties dialog on the right. Note: The tree of properties will only be displayed if the properties of this object are already known by th

existing properties for the specified object in the Select Properties dialog on the right. Note: The tree of properties will only be displayed if the properties of this object are already known by the reflection spider. If they do not appear, then click the Browse button and manually locate the assembly that defines these properties instead. Or click the Browse button, to manually locate the assembly, which defines the properties of the specified object. For example the System.Windows.Forms.dll assembly, could be browsed in for a Windows Control. The properties defined by the selected assembly are then displayed in the Select Properties dialog on the right. Note: The onus is upon the user to ensure that the correct assembly is selected. In the Select Properties dialog on the right: If necessary, expand the tree until the necessary properties are exposed. Select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the checkboxes of the required properties, so that they are ticked . Note: Do not click on the names of the properties themselves. Click the Finish button to add these selected properties to the spider. -->

Expression spiders Top Expression spiders The Expression spider can create user-defined calculations. Click for more information: This calculation is a sequence of operators and their operands the term(s) or sub-expression(s) that an operator acts upon. , which are evaluated and resolved to produce the result. Click for more details: This is a cumulative expression. For details, see Working with expressions . The operators have both an associativity the order in which an operator acts upon its operand(s). See operands. and precedence (defining the order in which their operands are evaluated). See the Available operators . In addition to numbers, input variables (i#), output variables (j#) and other sub-expressions, these operands can also include mathematical functions. See the Available mathematical functions . Note1: Add the necessary input and/or output variables to the spider first and manually assign their values initially to quickly debug the expression and ensure that it evaluates correctly. For details, see Adding input variables or Adding output variables . Note2: You are unable to complete entering an expression that contains input and output variables that do not yet exi

es correctly. For details, see Adding input variables or Adding output variables . Extended SQL Querying Top Extended SQL Querying If no row identifier is specified, then the selected (update, delete or retrieve) transaction could return multiple records and even if a row identifier was specified, the first record returned was always used for the transaction. Note: It is assumed that the user is familiar with the SQL querying language and is able to perform SQL queries unassisted. However it is also possible to specify which record is to be returned first, by adding the following commands to the SQL Query in the Identify Row edit box: In order for the DBAccess agent to use the first sorted record, append the following commands: $ORDER BY fieldname In order for the DBAccess agent to use the last sorted record, append the following commands: $ORDER BY fieldname DESC Note1: "fieldname" refers to the name of the field by which the table will be sorted in ascending order (from the largest to the smallest) Note2: Only add the "$" character if this is the ONLY SQL query command. Furthermore, the SQL query in the Identify Row edit box, for both the retrieve and delete transactions, supports free SQL format queries, these are identified from the normal SQL queries by star

mand. Furthermore, the SQL query in the Identify Row edit box, for both the retrieve and delete transactions, supports free SQL format queries, these are identified from the normal SQL queries by starting the SQL query with two ‘$’ characters. Note: The update and insert transactions do not support free SQL format queries. This is an example of a free SQL format delete query: $$DELETE FROM tablename WHERE fieldname=value1 OR fieldname=value2 Note: The "tablename" does not need to match the name of the table, currently specified in the Table name edit box. This is an example of a free SQL format retrieve query: $$SELECT fieldname1,fieldname2 FROM tablename WHERE fieldname3=value ORDER BY fieldname4 DESC Note1: The field name(s) used after the SELECT keyword (fieldname1, fieldname2), in retrieve queries must be the same as the field names specified in the tag to field mapping grid. Note2: The "tablename" does not need to match the name of the table, currently specified in the Table name edit box. Note: To test the syntax of the SQL query in the Identify Row edit box, click on the Trigger now button, then click the Details… button and check that this transaction succeeded in this dial

edit box. Note: To test the syntax of the SQL query in the Identify Row edit box, click on the Trigger now button, then click the Details… button and check that this transaction succeeded in this dialog box. -->

Extracting Logged Data Top Extracting Logged Data Adroit uses a data extraction facility called Extract which retrieves information from an AgentGroup consisting only of DataLog agents (see Grouping Agents Together ), or from a single DataLog agent, for a specified time period. Tip: To provide decimal resolution for real logged values that are retrieved using this Extract utility, use the ExtractFloatResolution registry value. The data is then converted into a CSV (comma separated value) file format, which can be opened by a third, party application such as Microsoft Excel and formatted to create reports. When using the Extract utility to transfer logged data from Adroit to an external system for further processing, you can reorder and/or remove some of the default CSV columns, as follows: Use the command line parameter: -COL to define the required subset and/or ordering of these default columns in the CSV file. Simply append the lowercase letters that represent each default columns to the end of this -COL command line parameter, in their required order. The following lowercase letters: d, t, n, c, v, u, q represent the following respective default columns: Date, Time, (tag)Name, D

the end of this -COL command line parameter, in their required order. The following lowercase letters: d, t, n, c, v, u, q represent the following respective default columns: Date, Time, (tag)Name, DesCription, Value, Units, Quality. Usage example: -COLctv will produce an output CSV file that ONLY contains the Description, Time, Value columns in this order. Note: The existing keywords -TERSE, -UCT, -UNIT still work as they did before. Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations Top Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations Calculation duration The OEE agent uses a background engine to update the monitored KPI or OEE in real-time. Any changes made to the input slots, determines how this background engine does its calculations. Note: Ensure that your Adroit license has specified the required number of OEE agents, which are specified in groups of 10. WITHOUT specifying the licensed number of OEE agents, only one instance of an OEE agent has its background engine enabled. All other agents will appear not to be running. By default, the agent records the OEE or KPI based on shift numbers, which are determined by the Shift agent specified by the Shift tag field of the edit dialog ( shiftAgent slot). For details, see Configuring the Shift agent . At the end of each shift the OEE or KPI is recorded and automatically reset for the start of the next shift. If you want to use the agent for recording the OEE or KPI on a “per batch” basis, then: Disable the autoReset slot of the agent (uncheck the Shift auto-reset checkbox of the edit dialog) and Programmatically reset the agent at the end of every batch. Note: The action of re

metadata.title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations

text: ” basis, then: Disable the autoReset slot of the agent (uncheck the Shift auto-reset checkbox of the edit dialog) and Programmatically reset the agent at the end of every batch. Note: The action of resetting the agent, automatically creates an OEE data snapshot entry before resetting the data. Tip: If the KPI or OEE is affected by the type of product being produced, then use different OEE agents for the different products. Running time KPI calculations are performed against runtime. Therefore the OEE agent uses the BOOLEAN running slot (or the optional BOOLEAN tag reference runningTag ) that informs the agent whether the process (or machine) is running. Running time is typically automatically incremented by the agent while this BOOLEAN value is ON. IMPORTANT: The OEE agent only supports BOOLEAN tags - so you cannot use an expression value tag. Note: The OEE agent expects that this slot will be OFF if the available slot is OFF. If not, runtime will continue to increment even though availability is OFF. However, it is possible that the process/machine is running but there is no physical production because, for example, a gear has stripped. This causes the measurement variable (the in

metadata.title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations

text: lability is OFF. However, it is possible that the process/machine is running but there is no physical production because, for example, a gear has stripped. This causes the measurement variable (the input1 slot) to remain static or go to zero i.e. inactive. If the measurement variable (the input1 slot) remains inactive for a configurable amount of time then the OEE agent will stop incrementing the running time and will raise a downtime alarm status. As long as the input1 slot is changing AND is not zero, the agent assumes that the process/machine is active and increments the running time. Therefore the actual production time is determined by a combination of the running slot and an active input1 slot. Available time Whereas KPI calculations are performed against runtime, OEE calculations are calculated against the time that the process/machine is available for production. The OEE agent therefore uses the BOOLEAN available slot (or the optional BOOLEAN tag reference availableTag ) to determine the maximum available time. This slot should be ON when the machine/process is supposed to be running. If the process/machine is under maintenance or operators are at lunch/tea, this slot shoul

metadata.title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations

text: ermine the maximum available time. This slot should be ON when the machine/process is supposed to be running. If the process/machine is under maintenance or operators are at lunch/tea, this slot should be OFF. Tip: This slot can be controlled by the output of a Scheduler agent that is configured with the applicable maintenance/lunch/tea times etc. For details, see Configuring the Scheduler agent . Complex mode and KPI calculation To allow for KPIs that have one measurement divided by another measurement (other than time), such as kWh/ton- the OEE agent supports a second measurement input slot ( input2 ). For normal OEE and KPI calculations, input2 is not used and the input type is set to Unused (0), by default. In this case the input1 slot is divided by time. In this case: KPI% = (Total for the Shift for input1/Run time)/Target KPI If the Input type 2 field (the type2 slot) is NOT set to Unused (0), then the OEE agent is said to be in complex mode. Note: OEE agents operating in complex mode CANNOT calculate OEE. In this case: KPI% = (Total for the Shift for input1/Total for the Shift for input 2)/Target KPI OEE calculations The OEE agent performs OEE calculations using the followin

metadata.title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations

text: mode CANNOT calculate OEE. In this case: KPI% = (Total for the Shift for input1/Total for the Shift for input 2)/Target KPI OEE calculations The OEE agent performs OEE calculations using the following formula: OEE% = Quality% * Performance% * Availability% Where: Quality% = Quality factor(%) * ((Total for the Shift - Reject Count)/Total for the Shift) Performance% = Total for the Shift/(Design capacity (per hour) * Run time) Availability (hours)% = Run time/Available time Availability Percent of scheduled production (to measure reliability) or calendar hours 24/7/365 (to measure equipment utilization), that equipment is available for production. Calculated as the equipment uptime (actual production – see 2.5 above) divided by the time that the equipment was available (see 2.3 above) for use. Performance Percent of total parts produced against the design capacity (optimal production rate) per time frame. Quality Percent of good sellable parts out of total parts produced per time frame multiplied by the Quality factor % value. Quality factor Quality can be calculated in many ways, depending on the type of process and the variables/information available to calculate quality. Therefor

metadata.title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations

text: multiplied by the Quality factor % value. Quality factor Quality can be calculated in many ways, depending on the type of process and the variables/information available to calculate quality. Therefore, the OEE agent calculates the quality using the reject and total counts for the shift, which is multiplied by an external quality factor, expressed as a percentage. This Quality factor % value (the qualityFactor slot) is the external quality factor whose value (0 to 100) must be driven externally. The default value is 100%. -->

Calculated as the equipment uptime (actual production – see 2.5 above) divided by the time that the equipment was available (see 2.3 above) for use. Performance Percent of total parts produced against the design capacity (optimal production rate) per time frame. Quality Percent of good sellable parts out of total parts produced per time frame multiplied by the Quality factor % value. Nothing lower will be accepted and will be replaced with 15 seconds. For this reason, the actual time specified for each scan point is ignored. _____________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ ATQMS-DRVR-DOC-D_FAG.docx P a g e | 5 2. This lists the names of all the tables in the DataBinder associated with the selected VIZNETDataBinder component. Select Fill from the Functions list. In the Event Trigger section Select the object and its event that triggers this function. This is typically a control added to the graphic form, such as a Button control, which uses its Click event to perform the action. For details, see Triggering a spider from an event . -->

FileBrowser controls Top FileBrowser controls The FileBrowser control typically allows SmartUI users to display to view, edit, upload and/or delete documents pertaining to ALL the ISA S88 / S95 hierarchical levels of your SmartUI project or to simply view the documents within a specific folder on the SmartUI Server computer. In other words, you need to use this control if your users need to access and/or manage documents ( click for more details: for instance, you could add Excel worksheets, PDFs, and/or JPGs to provide easy and controlled access to product specifications, standard operating procedures, drawings etc. ) associated with the entire site (MAPS Project) or plant area or unit at runtime within the SmartUI Operator. Since SmartUI natively only opens allows documents associated to each specific item of equipment. To add this control to a graphic form : A control needs to be added to a graphic form before it can be used and configured. Note: The FileBrowser control is located in the Custom section of the Toolbox window. What you need to do before you can use the FileBrowser control: Add this control to the required graphic form. If you intend to use this to display the docu

n the Custom section of the Toolbox window. What you need to do before you can use the FileBrowser control: Add this control to the required graphic form. If you intend to use this to display the documents of a SmartUI project, then ensure that the ProjectName property of this control specifies the name of the required SmartUI project. If you simply want to displays all the documents in a specific folder, then ensure that the DocumentPath property of this control specifies the required path to this directory on the SmartUI Server computer. End-user interaction: To operate this control : This describes how users view, edit, upload and/or delete documents provided by the FileBrowser control, at runtime. -->

The default filter string is * which displays all available agents. Open the Agent Configuration dialog, as follows: Tip: This also opens the Adroit Classic UI in the SmartUI Designer, which provides agent-specific menu functions, such as importing and exporting agents. In the SmartUI Designer: Click the Open Configurator tool in the Agent Server group of the Home tab of the SmartUI Designer ribbon. Note: When there is more than one Adroit datasource available, a list is provided to select which Agent Server to configure. The Agent Configuration dialog is displayed within the Classic UI. Examples of valid filtering expressions: * (or an empty string) - to display all agents *AREA1 - to display all agents ending in AREA1 AREA1* - to display all agents beginning with AREA1 *AREA1* - to display all agents containing AREA1 in any part of the agent name Note: The filtering expressions are not case sensitive. The filter string i

- to display all agents beginning with AREA1 *AREA1* - to display all agents containing AREA1 in any part of the agent name Note: The filtering expressions are not case sensitive. The filter string is enforced as soon as the Filter edit box loses focus – for instance by clicking the magnifier button, to the left of the Filter edit box. -->

Filtering event log files Top Filtering event log files The EventViewer control exposes the events recorded in an event log file, so that these events can be monitored. Effective monitoring of events requires the filtering out of unnecessary or unimportant events. This control is also able to filter Adroit specific data. The EventViewer control provides the following methods of filtering an event log file: If an event log file is connected to this EventViewer control by dragged it onto the DataSource property, then the Filter Dataset configuration dialog can be used to specify filters. For details, see Filtering datasets . If an event log file is connected to this EventViewer control by means of its ConnectionInformation property then you can filter these events by a specific Source . For details, see Connecting event log files to EventViewer controls . Design-time filtering: This involves the creation of filter strings that are saved in the FilterString property of the EventViewer control and are therefore ALWAYS applied when this control is displayed. For details, see Design-time filtering of event log files . Run-time filtering: If enabled, this involves the creation of on-the-f

trol and are therefore ALWAYS applied when this control is displayed. For details, see Design-time filtering of event log files . Run-time filtering: If enabled, this involves the creation of on-the-fly filter strings by your users that are NOT saved. For details, see Run-time filtering of event log files . Note: You can use BOTH the design-time and run-time methods of filtering simultaneously. -->

Floating tool windows Top Floating tool windows Tool windows are dockable, as such they have both a floating and docked display mode. When a tool window is floated, it becomes a separate window, with a thin title bar and can appear anywhere on your screen that CANNOT be docked. To float a tool window: Locate and open the required tool window. For details, see Accessing tool windows . Note: Ensure that this tool window is not being auto hidden, if so deactivate this feature first. For details, see Automatically hiding and showing tool windows . Double-click the title bar of this docked window, which makes this a separate window, with a thin title bar and can appear anywhere on your screen. Tip: This window will be re-docked in its previous position when its title bar is double clicked again. Note1: A floating tool window is always on top of all other windows and can be resized as required. Note2: It is possible to float both a single tool window or grouped tool windows in the same way. For details, see Grouping tool windows . Note3: Floating tool windows provide a number of methods for conserving space in the within the work environment, however they do not support auto-hiding - hen

For details, see Grouping tool windows . text: General Description Top General Description Wanlink allows data to be replicated over a slow or Wide Area Network (WAN) from one Agent Server to another. The word "replicate" is key to understanding the operation of Wanlink. In other words, Wanlink allows remote Agent Servers to behave as if they were normal remote nodes on a Local Area Network (LAN), because data can be read from the Agent Server and also written back. But the transmission and reception of this data behaves in an indirect manner, and not directly as a normal remote node would, since speed is the most important limiting factor when communicating across a WAN. Wanlink, is comprised of two components, namely the WanClient and the WanServer , where the WanClient component performs all the tag and communication configuration so that one WanServer to have multiple WanClient connections. Therefore a computer running an Agent Server and a WanServer, can act as a data concentrator and only send the relevant, requested data to a number of remote Agent Server computers, each with their own WanClient. This is far more efficient, since the data replication to these WanClient computers can either be full or partial (depending o

a number of remote Agent Server computers, each with their own WanClient. This is far more efficient, since the data replication to these WanClient computers can either be full or partial (depending on the remote WanClient’s configuration) thereby increasing efficiency. Related links Quick Start How to use Wanlink -->

GET Commands Top GET Commands Function: To obtain the value of any tag (agent.slot) exposed by the Agent Server. Note1: This command must be enabled by the Command agent , which it is sent to, before it can be performed, because it can create a security risk through the remote retrieval of process values. For details, see Specifying Permitted Commands . Note2: Both the command and its parameters are NOT case-sensitive; commands have only been capitalised for ease of reference. The decision of which of the following command formats to use, is essentially a tradeoff between the prior configuration in the Command agent and the required amount of typing, when specifying the SMS command itself: Note1: It is also possible to retrieve the values of tags automatically, for instance, to remotely monitor the status of important process values. For details, see Automatic Sending of Values . Note2: Both the command and its parameters are NOT case-sensitive; commands have only been capitalised for ease of reference. Basic command syntax: GET, tagName In this case, tagName is the name of the tag whose value is to be displayed. For instance: get,dig_01.value This is the simplest format of this co

ease of reference. Basic command syntax: GET, tagName In this case, tagName is the name of the tag whose value is to be displayed. For instance: get,dig_01.value This is the simplest format of this command, which requires the least prior configuration in the Command agent, it is able to retrieve the value of any tag, however it does require the most typing when specifying the command. Pseudonym usage: GET, pseudonym In this case, a pseudonym or alias needs to be created, beforehand, for the required tag (agent.slot). For instance, assuming that a pseudonym called ‘dig01v’ is created to represent ‘DIG_01.value’, this command can be specified as: get,dig01v Although pseudonyms save on the typing when specifying the command, ONLY the tags that have defined pseudonyms for this Command agent can be used. For details on creating and using pseudonyms, see Creating Pseudonyms . Macro usage: macro In this case, a macro or alias needs to be created, beforehand, for the entire GET command. For instance, assuming that a macro called ‘Pump1?’ is created to represent ‘get,dig_01.value’, then this command can simply be specified as: "Pump1?". Although macros provide short yet intuitive command na

stance, assuming that a macro called ‘Pump1?’ is created to represent ‘get,dig_01.value’, then this command can simply be specified as: "Pump1?". Although macros provide short yet intuitive command names, they require the most pre-configuration in this Command agent and are therefore most restrictive. For details on creating and using macros, see Creating Macros . The received SMS message, adheres to the following format: <GET RESPONSE> tagName = value Where tagName is the name of the tag (agent.slot) whose value is displayed, i.e. the pseudonym or macro, if used, is replaced with the actual tag name. Note1: Invalid requests, for instance for the values of tags that do not exist, will be preceded by <GET FAILURE> instead. Note2: If the default formatting of real numbers has been configured for this Command agent, this format will be used to display real or floating-point values. For details, see Default Real Number Formatting . -->

Getting to know the Collections Top Getting to know the Collections WOSA/XRT Data Objects make extensive use of the OLE collection construct. A collection is an object that is implemented such that a well-known set of methods exists for iterating over the collected sub-objects. The defined Behaviours provide for enumeration, addition, deletion, and access via index. A collection contains only objects of the same class. The way collections are named is to typically call the collection the plural of the collected object name. For example, if we create a collection of objects of class Tag, we would name the collection Tags. In this way, VBA language constructs can take advantage of them, since VBA implements a language semantic known as For Each...In . Glossary Glossary @scan (pronounced at-scan), which is a method of linking the value of one tag to another, by scanning the required tag value directly. active the monitored condition of this incident (alarm/event) is still in effect and has not yet returned to its normal operating state. agent an instance of an agent type, that stores data and typically provides the ability to operate or act on this data. agent group an agent that facilitates the logical grouping of other agents. For example, an AgentGroup agent could contain all agents related to a specific section of a plant, or all agents required for a specific report. alarm the process of monitoring an agent for the occurrence of a specific abnormal condition or state (alarm type). alarm type a named (abnormal) condition or state of an agent that is defined by which of its status bits are simultaneously ON or OFF, which can also list the slots of this agent to report when this condition occurs. alarming strategy a set of guidelines or a plan to optimise the configuration of the alarming of agents. Once created it can easily be transferred and adapted for other projects, as required. aspect ratio a ratio or comparison of its w

es or a plan to optimise the configuration of the alarming of agents. Once created it can easily be transferred and adapted for other projects, as required. aspect ratio a ratio or comparison of its width to its height. The screen resolution determines the aspect ratio of a monitor. More than one screen resolution can have the SAME aspect ratio e.g. the following screen resolutions 800×600, 1024×768 and 1280×960 all share the SAME aspect ratio of 4:3. Behaviours can be assigned to picture elements to display process values either actually or graphically to provide a dynamic visual indication of events taking place in the process. block period the interval over which your electricity provider monitors your maximum demand, which is typically 30 minutes. Boolean a value that only has two discrete states, 0 (FALSE) or 1 (TRUE). cleared the monitored condition of this incident (alarm/event) has returned to its normal operating state. Graphic form statistics Top Graphic form statistics When designing large graphic forms, especially when more than one person has designed it, it can become difficult to determine at first glance the number of components that have been added. Therefore the Designer provides the Statistics button in the graphic form toolbar, which displays a dialog that reports the number of vector objects and windows controls used to create the user interface and the number of spiders and silks used to animate this user interface along with the size and name of this graphic form and the time and date at which it was last saved. Note: The graphic form needs to be saved first before these statistics can be displayed. Possible uses for these graphic form statistics are: As a diagnostic tool to identify possible inefficiencies in the design of the current graphic form, that could be affecting its loading time . Digital I/O can be scanned into a multistate, by specifying the first digital module in the controller, as input or output, if output is used, all positions will become outputs. When writing to the value, only the output modules on the board get updated. Refresh and controller-enable are header items, i.e. they are not actual I/O points. They do however count as scan points. and controller-enable are header items, i.e. they are not actual I/O points. They do however count as scan points. All non-configured positions are assumed by the driver to be inputs. Header items  The special address mnemonic for a Boolean or Digital slot is supplied to initiate configuration refresh on demand: “UPDATE”. Issuing a digital write with a value of 1 will initiate steps 2 & 3 of the startup sequence described in Operation. This address will return zero if scanned. This will refresh the configuration of all the enabled controllers.  The special address mnemonic “ENABLE n” will allow enabling and disabling of scanning for a specific module “n”, as an enable tag. This virtual variable can also be driven from the driver setup dialog. If the dialog is used to change the value, the digital tag (if scanned) associated with the variable will also update. A value of 1 = enabled, and zero (checkbox off) = disabled. The enable tags get saved in the system registry database for each device, if the device gets deleted in the setup program, this information is thus lost. Grouping Agents Together Top Grouping Agents Together An Agent Group is a logical grouping of agents, contained within an AgentGroup agent, either for user convenience or to identify a section or a function of a plant. For example, all the I/O agents associated with Boiler No. 1, or all DataLog agents needed to compile, say, a Production shift report could be placed in groups. This has already been done for each of the agent types and for the three pre-defined agent groups of BASIC, ADVANCED and SYSTEM as determined by the postload Adroit database file . An Agent Group can also be used to control several agents contained within a group. For example, the control bits of an Agent Group agent can be used as a way of setting or resetting the equivalent bits for all agents in the group. An agent can belong to more than one Agent Group and these may be displayed by selecting the agent type from the Type list box and its specific name from the Tags list box and then clicking the Groups button. A list of current Groups to which the agent belongs is shown. Note: Any agents that have been browsed into the agent, e.g. the agents used in an Expression agent, or the agent used to trigger the Co

. A list of current Groups to which the agent belongs is shown. Note: Any agents that have been browsed into the agent, e.g. the agents used in an Expression agent, or the agent used to trigger the Counter agent, will appear in the Current groups list, prefaced by an asterisk (*) e.g. *TRIGGER. These ARE NOT group names. Similarly, the membership list of a given Agent Group can be displayed by selecting the group from the Group drop down list box, whereupon the members will be listed in the Tags list box. The AgentGroup Agent To create a new agent group . Adding agent types to an agent group : this adds one or more agent types to an AgentGroup agent. Adding agents to an agent group : this adds one or more agents to an AgentGroup agent. Listing the contents of an agent group : this displays the agents and agent types that have been added to an AgentGroup agent. -->

Grouping tool windows Top Grouping tool windows Tool windows can be grouped together or tab-docked into the same window. This automatically creates a tab, at the bottom of this grouped tool window, by which each of the windows can be accessed. Click for more details: This and other techniques can be used to conserve space within the work environment. For details, see Arranging tool windows . To add tool window/s to one or more grouped tool windows: Locate and open the required tool window or group of tool windows. For details, see Accessing tool windows . HASP Troubleshooting Top HASP Troubleshooting Typically, Adroit is licensed via a HASP software protection key, which is programmed in accordance with the required licence. PLEASE NOTE: When Data Execution Prevention (DEP) is incorrectly configured, this can cause the Agent Server to be unable to read the HASP, at start up causing the Agent Server to hang or fail and/or to display HASP exceptions in the Agent Server window. For further details, see Data Execution Prevention (DEP) Configuration . When Adroit cannot read the HASP details: IMPORTANT: Do not do this via a remote desktop session as this does not allow the reading of the HASP. Check which version of the HASP drivers are installed by doing the following: Browse to the following folder in Windows Explorer: C:\Program Files (x86)\Adroit Technologies\Common Open a Command Prompt in this folder – this is most easily done by holding down SHIFT and right clicking the Common folder In the Command Prompt type the following command: haspdinst.exe -info Click Yes if a UAC confirmation box pops up for Sentinel and wait after a while the Sentinel Run-time Environment Installer dialog should appear. Take note of the version number in

aspdinst.exe -info Click Yes if a UAC confirmation box pops up for Sentinel and wait after a while the Sentinel Run-time Environment Installer dialog should appear. Take note of the version number in the title bar. Browse to the HASP driver download available for Adroit 10 on the Adroit website and compare this version with the version of your installed HASP drivers. If this Sentinel Run-time Environment Installer dialog does not appear or the version number is less than the latest HASP drivers – then download and install the latest HASP drivers install for Adroit 10 from the Adroit website, the downloaded file is called LatestHASPDrivers.exe. If the currently installed HASP drivers are newer than the ones contained in the LatestHASPDrivers.exe, then we suggest that you manually uninstall your existing HASP drivers – by running the haspdinst.exe –r command (see steps a - c above) and then running the LatestHASPDrivers.exe to install this HASP driver instead. If you still are struggling to remove your existing HASP drivers, then run the following command to manually remove your HASP drivers: haspdinst.exe -purge (see steps a - c above) and then re-run the LatestHASPDrivers.exe. If t

to remove your existing HASP drivers, then run the following command to manually remove your HASP drivers: haspdinst.exe -purge (see steps a - c above) and then re-run the LatestHASPDrivers.exe. If this does not help, then it is possible under extremely rare conditions, the HASP or its parallel or USB port may have failed/blown. Header Slots Top Agent Header Slots All agents types, regardless of their function, have header attributes that are assigned and managed by the Agent Server. These slots are identifiable by the fact that their names are all prefixed with word agent . Note1: The overall status of an agent can be determined from its status slot, which is common to all agent types. For details, see Agent Status . Note2: The first bit in the status word, statusBit00 ( statusBad) , is the only bit an application needs to monitor to determine the integrity of this agent. For details, see Agent or Slot Integrity Monitoring (Bad Handling) . Note2: The remaining slots for each agent are specific to the agent type. For details, see Agent Type and Slot Reference . Hidden Property spiders Top Hidden Property spiders The Hidden Property spider exposes and/or manipulates properties of the specified object that are normally hidden. These properties are either displayed as inputs, if they are writable and/or outputs, if they are readable. To add this spider to the spider workspace . To select the object whose properties will be exposed . To expose the required properties of the selected object . Note: You can only expose properties once you select an object. To remove unnecessary input and/or output properties . Configuration Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider. Note: Menu items that are enabled will have a tick mark to the left of them. Detail View: This can be used to display the configuration view of this spider, so its name, description, inputs and outputs can be configured. For details, see Working with spider configuration views . Tip: Double-click the title bar of the spider to display or hide the configuration view of the spider. Delete Spider: This can be used to remove this spider from the spider workspace. For details, see Removing spiders . Trigger Spider From Event: This ena

y or hide the configuration view of the spider. Delete Spider: This can be used to remove this spider from the spider workspace. For details, see Removing spiders . Trigger Spider From Event: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by means of an event. For details, see Triggering a spider from an event . This is disabled by default. Enable Silk Triggering: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by any silks that are attached to the inputs of this spider. For details, see Triggering spiders . This is enabled by default. Propagate Outputs At Startup: This enables the spider to supply the silks connected to its outputs with values as soon as its spider workspace enters into running mode. For details, see Working with spider workspaces or Sending spider outputs at startup . This is disabled by default. Trigger Now!: This will cause this spider to immediately be triggered. Hiding and displaying available tool windows Top Hiding and displaying available tool windows The View tab of the Designer ribbon displays the list of icons of the tool windows currently available in the SmartUI Designer application window, which can be used to hide or display these windows - hovering over each icon displays the associated name of the tool window. For a list of the available icons and which tool windows they represent, see Available tool windows . This and other techniques can be used to conserve space within the work environment. For details, see Arranging tool windows . To hide an available tool window: Open the View tab of the Designer ribbon. If the entry IS selected (icon has a yellow background): click this item to turn it off (the background changes from yellow to white). Tip: It is also possible to access the required tool window itself and click the close icon on its title bar. Note: This will only hide and not remove this tool window from Designer application window. To display a hidden tool window: Open the View tab of the Designer ribbon.
