text: Hiding or displaying Header slots Top Hiding or displaying Header slots You can display or hide the common Header slots of each agent within the connected Agent Server of an Adroit datasource. Click for more information: Note: This ALSO displays or hides the Header slots of the GROUP agents, which if displayed are listed in the *Group Slots list beneath each agent type, that has configured agents. These slots are usually used for general overview displays, to easily monitor the statuses of all the configured agents. For instance, by monitoring the statusAlarmed slot for the Analog GROUP agent, it is possible to determine whether one or more of the configured Analog agents are currently alarmed. Note: If the Adroit datasource is currently opened, this change will only take effect once it is refreshed or closed and reopened. To display the Header slots of agents within an Agent Server: Select the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager , as follows: Open the Enterprise Manager . Navigate to Servers > [Server Name] . Tip: The connection name is prefixed by the SmartUI Server computer name. If necessary, expand the Datasources category. Right-click the name of the required Ad

. Navigate to Servers > [Server Name] . Tip: The connection name is prefixed by the SmartUI Server computer name. If necessary, expand the Datasources category. Right-click the name of the required Adroit datasource or its icon and ONLY if you see a menu item called Include Header Slots then select it. When an agent is expanded in the Enterprise Manager it will also display its Header slots too. This will also change the name of this option to Exclude Header Slots . To hide the Header slots of agents within an Agent Server: Select the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager , as follows: Open the Enterprise Manager . Navigate to Servers > [Server Name] . Tip: The connection name is prefixed by the SmartUI Server computer name. If necessary, expand the Datasources category. Right-click the name of the required Adroit datasource or its icon and select Exclude Header Slots . When an agent is expanded in the Enterprise Manager it will NOT display its Header slots. This will also change the name of this option to Include Header Slots . Note: You can also display or hide these common Header slots, by default, by configuring the Boolean AdroitIncludeHeaderSlots Server setting ac

change the name of this option to Include Header Slots . Note: You can also display or hide these common Header slots, by default, by configuring the Boolean AdroitIncludeHeaderSlots Server setting accordingly. For details on accessing this setting, see Advanced Server settings . -->

Hiding or showing configured levels Top Hiding or showing configured levels You can hide or display the configured levels of a graphic form. Note: This has no effect upon the display of levels within the graphic form itself. To hide or show configured levels Open and display the required graphic in the Design workspace . Open the Levels and Layers tool window. For details, see Accessing tool windows . Click the second column of the grid to display or to hide the configured levels (columns). Tip: The symbols displayed by this second column, indicate whether the levels are currently displayed or hidden . -->

Hiding spider configuration views Top Hiding spider configuration views You often need to hide the spider configuration views, to provide room to work within the spider workspace. Click for more details: Once the configuration view is hidden, the spider will usually display its distinctive icon beneath its title bar. Note: Data spiders disappear from view when their configuration view is hidden. To hide the configuration views of all the spiders in the spider workspace: If necessary, open the required spider workspace. Either press the Collapse All Spiders toolbar button, from the spider workspace toolbar. Or right-click the spider workspace and select the Collapse All Spiders menu item. This makes it easier to rearrange and add other spiders. Although it is also possible to automatically arrange the spiders too. For details, see Rearranging spiders . Tip: This is the best method of closing a large number of spider configuration views at once, although Data spider configuration views are not as easy to reopen. To hide the configuration view of any particular spider or Data spider: Open the required spider workspace. Select the required spider. For details, see Selecting spiders . R

re not as easy to reopen. To hide the configuration view of any particular spider or Data spider: Open the required spider workspace. Select the required spider. For details, see Selecting spiders . Right-click the title bar of this spider and select Detail View . Tip: You can also double-click the spider title bar. The configuration view collapses upward and expands to the left and downward from the position of the title bar of the icon of the spider. -->

Hiding unselected spiders and regions Top Hiding unselected spiders and regions Use the Hide Unselected Spiders/Regions spider workspace display option to simplify an otherwise cluttered spider workspace. Click here for more information: In addition to hiding ALL the unselected spiders and regions directly associated with the currently selected spider or region or form component, there are 3 other selective hiding filters. For instance, consider a scenario when Alias spiders are in conjunction with Variable Data Element spiders to connect the required data elements, so most of the spiders would be connected. Note1: When a spider is located or manually selected in the spider workspace, with this option enabled, then only it and the spiders that it is connected to will be displayed, in accordance with the currently specified hiding filter. For details, see Finding spiders . Note2: If the graphic form itself, is selected, then all the spiders which are connected by silks to properties of this graphic form and its form components will be displayed. But any standalone spiders or spiders which are not connected to any form components will not be displayed, such as Script Engine spiders.

Historical Data Catch Up of the Newly Added Standby Server Top Historical Data Catch Up of the Newly Added Standby Server When a standby server joins a cluster, the historical data stored on the master server must be mirrored over to the standby server. This is done in an intelligent manner by only copying over the data that it requires, that is, the data stored by the master during the period that the newly added standby server was down. Note: This is only possible if the cluster Agent Servers have their system time synchronised . This data catch-up is performed by the SystemDataLog agent, called systemDl. For details, see The SystemDatalog Agent . Note: For performance reasons, the SystemDatalog agent ONLY provides the Time datalog catchup method, of catching up the data between two specified date/times. -->

This can also create CSV files too, to make this historical data available to third party applications such as Microsoft Excel and formatted to create reports. For details, see Datalog backup and retrieval . Extracting Logged Data Adroit uses a data extraction facility called Extract that retrieves information from an AgentGroup consisting of DataLog agents, or from a single DataLog agent, for a specified time period. The data is then converted into a CSV (comma separated value) file format that can be opened by a third party application such as Microsoft Excel and formatted to create reports. Merging Data Logs Adroit also provides a utility for merging values from a .CSV file into an existing historical database of DataLog agents . Therefore, the “back off time” time has been replaced by a hardcoded timing/backoff mechanism for reconnecting to PLC’s. The hardcoded algorithm is dependent on the number of configured devices in groups of 10. The value is 10 seconds for the first 10 devices + 20 seconds for each multiple of 10 devices or part thereof thereafter. For example, 26 PLC's will take up to 50 (10+20+20) seconds to reconnect. HMI Mode Top HMI Mode HMI mode is a lower cost, simpler version of Adroit and SmartUI , which is a stand-alone solution that supports the addition of up to 2 clients. This cannot be incorporated into a larger distributed project and does not support redundancy. HMI mode is licensed via the HASP and provides for a cost-effective, bulk implementation of HMI software. The Hasp agent LICENCE has a read-only slot called "HMIMode". If a HMI mode HASP is present then the slot value will be 1, otherwise it will be 0 for standard Agent Servers. HMI mode is therefore one of the components of an Adroit license. HMI mode is typically configured on installation. However, you can create configurations using the Full or HMI mode by using the Configuration dialog of the Adroit Config Editor utility. Note: You can only see if the current (active) configuration is running in Full or HMI mode, after checking the Allow Multiple Configurations checkbox. When using multiple configurations (when engineering multiple projects), you can specify which configurations run in Full or HMI mode, depending upon your project's requirements. This allows you to easily switch between projects (configurations) running

multiple projects), you can specify which configurations run in Full or HMI mode, depending upon your project's requirements. This allows you to easily switch between projects (configurations) running in Full or HMI mode. You can also create additional configurations that are based on existing ones, as needed. Note: If you have only installed the Agent Server and not the SmartUI Server, then you can manually put the Agent Server in and out of HMI mode by configuring the HMIMode registry value (this requires restarting the Agent Server). if the Agent Server is licensed for HMI and Adroit has not been configured for HMI mode the Agent Server will display a message box that it cannot continue and it will terminate. The user must either enable the HMI configuration or change the HASP. if Adroit has been configured for HMI mode and the Agent Server is not licensed for HMI, then the Agent Server will continue in HMI mode. An HMI licensed Agent Server has the following restrictions: ONLY loads the following agent types: Primitive agents: Boolean, Integer, Real The following primitive agent types have also been added to HMI mode: Real and Integer, however these agents (including Boolean) s

s the following agent types: Primitive agents: Boolean, Integer, Real The following primitive agent types have also been added to HMI mode: Real and Integer, however these agents (including Boolean) should ONLY be used where efficient use of memory is required. PLEASE NOTE: These legacy primitive agents do not support Alarming and other SCADA functionality, use Analog/Digital agents instead! Basic agents: Analog, Counter, Date, Digital, Expression, Marshal, String, StringList and Timer IMPORTANT: Each Marshal agent used, consumes 16 scan license points. How MAPS implements the S88 / S95 hierarchy Top How MAPS implements the S88 / S95 hierarchy The ISA S95 standard divides the manufacturing enterprise into: plant floor automation control, MES and ERP. This standard focuses on MES and ERP, as its goal is to seamlessly coordinate business and production processes. The ISA S88 standard, originally created for batch processes, can be used to structure ANY process. This standard focuses on plant floor automation control. BOTH standards share a SIMILAR hierarchy describing the structure of automation projects, as follows: MAPS implements (and enforces) the following extended physical model: Note: These hierarchical categories ALL have a 1 to many relationship with their components i.e. a Site can contain MANY Areas, an Area can contain MANY Process Cells (PLCs) etc. The Site level is the MAPS project. So you will have one MAPS project per site. For example, XYZ Foods. The Area level is the defined Plant area/s of the MAPS project. For example, Batching Plant. The Process Cell level is the PLC/s of each defined plant area. For example, BATCHING PLC. The Unit level is the collection/s of equipment items within each PLC. Typically these rel

metadata.title: How MAPS implements the S88 / S95 hierarchy

text: e, Batching Plant. The Process Cell level is the PLC/s of each defined plant area. For example, BATCHING PLC. The Unit level is the collection/s of equipment items within each PLC. Typically these relate to the plant area-specific operations, such as Filling, Packing, Flocculation etc. For example, Batching. However, you can ALSO create a unit for each item of complex equipment i.e. equipment that consist of more than one Electrical or Instrumentation item, such as conveyors. The Equipment module and the Control module levels are NOT separately implemented because this is not supported by the PLC programming architecture. These levels are the defined items of equipment that are classified into either the Electrical or Instrumentation categories for each of the defined units. -->

text: How Maximum Demand is Calculated Top How Maximum Demand is Calculated Maximum demand or peak kVA demand is an additional cost for most non-domestic power users. Your kVA usage is averaged over a “block” period, ONLY during defined periods of the day when electricity consumption is high. Block periods are typically 30 minutes but could be anywhere from 15-60 minutes in duration. If you are in doubt about the block period that is applicable for you, please speak to your electricity provider for clarification. The block period with the highest kVA value, over the duration of the current billing period (month), is your maximum electricity demand. Maximum demand calculation example: Assuming that the power consumption on a plant over a block period of 30 minutes is comprised of 5 different episodes of consumption as follows: 800 kVA for 5 minutes 200 kVA for 5 minutes 400 kVA for 10 minutes 800 kVA for 8 minutes 1500 kVA for 2 minutes Adroit calculates the maximum demand for that 30 minute period as follows: ((800*5) + (200*5) + (400*10) + (800*8) + (1500*2)) / 30 = 613.33 kVA During each of the above five episodes the predicted maximum demand would have been: Episode1: (800*30) / 30 =

period as follows: ((800*5) + (200*5) + (400*10) + (800*8) + (1500*2)) / 30 = 613.33 kVA During each of the above five episodes the predicted maximum demand would have been: Episode1: (800*30) / 30 = 800 kVA Episode2: ((800*5) + (200*25)) / 30 = 300 kVA Episode3: ((800*5) + (200*5) + (400*20)) / 30 = 433.33 kVA Episode4: ((800*5) + (200*5) + (400*10) + (800*10)) / 30 = 566.66 kVA Episode5: ((800*5) + (200*5) + (400*10) + (800*8) + (1500*2)) / 30 = 613.33 kVA If this agent had a configured maximum demand limit of 600 kVA and the Enable max demand alarm checkbox is enabled, then the MaxDemand status bit would have been on during episodes 1 and 5. How to Alarm Process Values Top How to Alarm Process Values In Adroit , your process values (tags) are stored as slots within agents. You therefore alarm your process values by alarming the agent in which they reside. To alarm an agent (process value): For instance: we will alarm an agent called ANA001 of the Analog agent type, using the defaultAlarmAgent: the Alarm agent that is created by default by Adroit . How to chart and/or report data from a database Top How to chart and/or report data from a database This document describes the procedure for trending/charting and/or reporting/displaying data that has been logged: by using the DBLog agent of Adroit - although this how can be adapted for ANY data logging method. to a MS SQL database that is connected to a SmartUI Server via an OleDB datasource Prerequisites Note: This document assumes that the reader has a basic working knowledge of using SQL databases and using databases in SmartUI . Have Adroit 8 (MAPS 3) or later installed. Note: If you are using a version later than this then this how to will probably also apply to your version too, although some dialogs and/or commands may have changed slightly. Configuring the DBLog agent The DBLog agent is a bulk OLE DB logging agent for typically logging Analog and/or Digital values to a specific table in a database for later retrieval. This provides various different logging methods, such as “log on change”, “log on interval” etc. For a detailed description of configuring the DBLog agent, see Configuring DBLog Agents . Tip: Typically you need to separate the Analog and Digital tags that yo

text: log on change”, “log on interval” etc. For a detailed description of configuring the DBLog agent, see Configuring DBLog Agents . Tip: Typically you need to separate the Analog and Digital tags that you want to log into different DBLog agents, due to their unique logging requirements. Once the DBLog Agent has been configured and enabled, it creates table /s in the specified database with the following fields: id : a unique indexing identifier dt : the Timestamp of the logged value Tagname : the name of the tag being logged Value :– the value of the tag being logged Quality : an indication of whether value of this logged tag was good or bad data has a bad status when data is missing, incorrectly reported or extrapolated. . This agent ALSO creates the Adr_DBLog_AgentDetails table, which contains all the agents referenced by all DBLog agents to provide more details about these referenced agents, which can be used to provide more context about them for reports. How to cluster Servers Top How to cluster SmartUI Servers SmartUI Servers should be clustered to provide: redundancy to ensure continued operation in the event that one or more fail. load balancing to handle their combined workload evenly Redundancy is achieved by ensuring that each of the SmartUI Servers in the cluster has exactly the same project data source files as well as configuration files. In other words, it is necessary to configure one Server within the cluster and then duplicate its settings to all the others. Note : Any number of Servers can belong to the same cluster. Load balancing is achieved by ensuring that each of the SmartUI Operators (that use the Servers in this cluster) provide the connection settings of all the Servers in the cluster. In other words, it is necessary to configure one Operator and duplicate its settings to all the others. Each SmartUI Server uses UDP broadcasts to inform its cluster aware Operators of its availability and load. The load of each Server is determined by the number of SmartUI Clients that are currently connected to it. Each cluster aware Operator maintains a list of Servers for ALL the clusters that it connects to. The list is per

ver is determined by the number of SmartUI Clients that are currently connected to it. Each cluster aware Operator maintains a list of Servers for ALL the clusters that it connects to. The list is periodically updated by the SmartUI Operator, which obtains the availability and load of these Servers from their broadcasts. Cluster aware Operators automatically switch over to the Server with the lightest load. Upon login, if the default Server (cluster partner) is NOT available then a cluster aware Operator will search for an available cluster partner. Note : Clustered Servers currently ONLY share the workload generated by their Operator clients. The following procedure is recommended to cluster multiple Servers together: IMPORTANT: The screenshots and specified configuration settings relate to an OLD version of the SmartUI product and so your specific settings and screens may differ. Configure the SmartUI Server computers that will be added to the cluster. Configure the SmartUI Operators that will make use of the Servers in this cluster. Perform additional configuration of these SmartUI Operators when load balancing is required . Back to top Configuring SmartUI Server Computers that

that will make use of the Servers in this cluster. Perform additional configuration of these SmartUI Operators when load balancing is required . Back to top Configuring SmartUI Server Computers that Make up the Cluster Select a SmartUI Server computer, which will be used to as the template for the cluster on which all the necessary configuration will be initially performed and then copied to ALL the other Server machines in the cluster . Perform the following configuration on this computer: Run the SmartUI Config application and open the SmartUI Server or SmartUI Service configuration under the Advanced section, depending upon whether this Server is being run as a service or not. Ensure that its ServerName property is set to the name of the cluster . Figure 1: Locating the ServerName property for a SmartUI Server Run the SmartUI Server and SmartUI Designer and ensure that ALL the projects and data sources have been set up and finalised. Close the Designer and Server. Now ensure that the following components are copied from this Server computer to all the Server computers in this cluster : The Data and Projects folders. The VIPServer.exe.config and VIPService.exe.config files. If n

he following components are copied from this Server computer to all the Server computers in this cluster : The Data and Projects folders. The VIPServer.exe.config and VIPService.exe.config files. If necessary, configure the following settings that configure the UDP broadcasts that inform cluster aware Operators of the availability and load of each cluster partner: The BroadcastEnabled Server setting enables (the default setting) or disables these UDP broadcasts. The BroadcastTimePeriod Server setting specifies the time, in milliseconds, between broadcasts, which is 2 seconds (2000 milliseconds) by default. Although decreasing this setting reduces the network traffic it also prevents the Operators from quickly responding to changes in Server load and/or availability. The BroadcastPortRange Server setting specifies the UDP port range which the Server uses for its broadcasts, by default this is 11000-11010. IMPORTANT : If you CHANGE this setting for a Server then you need to change the BroadcastPortRange setting of each Client that you want to receive these broadcasts from this Server. Back to top Configuring the SmartUI Operators that Use the Servers in this Cluster Select an SmartUI

oadcastPortRange setting of each Client that you want to receive these broadcasts from this Server. Back to top Configuring the SmartUI Operators that Use the Servers in this Cluster Select an SmartUI Operator computer, which will be used as the template for all the Operator clients that are to connect to this cluster, on which all the necessary configuration will be initially performed and then will usually be copied to the other Operator clients. Run the SmartUI Config application on this Operator computer and open the SmartUI Operator configuration page under the Advanced section. Ensure that the Cluster Settings group of properties are configured, as follows: Figure 2 : Locating the Cluster Settings group of properties for a SmartUI Operator The ClusterEnabled property must to be set to true Since a SmartUI Operator can be configured to connect to more than one cluster, the ClusterNames property is a comma separated list, which specifies the names of each of the clusters that this SmartUI Operator can connect to. In this case as we only want to connect to one cluster, this should be set to Cluster1. The last and most important setting is the ClusterServers setting, which contai

SmartUI Operator can connect to. In this case as we only want to connect to one cluster, this should be set to Cluster1. The last and most important setting is the ClusterServers setting, which contains a comma separated list of the Servers that form part of the cluster. This list is in the following format: “clustername~computername~port~connectionmechanism~ communicationmechanism;…” Since it is possible for the Servers that make up a cluster to either be located on the LAN or hosted on the Internet, this determines how these Servers are described by this setting, as follows: An example of a Server connection string for a LAN cluster server is: Cluster1~Computer1~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE An example of a Server connection string for an INTERNET cluster server is: Cluster1~http://201.201.201.1~80~WEBSERVICEDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE_POLL In our example, all the Servers that form part of the cluster exist on the LAN, and more specifically on three computers – Computer1, Computer2 and Computer3. For this reason this ClusterServers setting will appear as follows: Cluster1~Computer1~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE; Cluster1~Computer2~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE; Cluster1~Computer

Computer3. For this reason this ClusterServers setting will appear as follows: Cluster1~Computer1~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE; Cluster1~Computer2~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE; Cluster1~Computer3~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE However, if all the Servers that form part of this cluster existed on the Internet, and more specifically on three computers with the following IP addresses– 201.201.201.1, 201.201.201.2 and 201.201.201.3. Then this ClusterServers setting will appear as follows: Cluster1~http://201.201.201.1~80~WEBSERVICEDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE_POLL; Cluster1~http://201.201.201.2~80~WEBSERVICEDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE_POLL; Cluster1~http://201.201.201.3~80~WEBSERVICEDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE_POLL Ensure that this configuration file ( VIP Operator.exe.config ) is copied to and used by ALL the SmartUI Operator clients that will connect to this cluster. Note : This is possible since these SmartUI Operator clients connect to a single cluster. However, if different Operators are required to connect to different clusters, it may be necessary to manually configure their configuration files individually, depending upon the complexity required. Back to top Additional Configuration of

red to connect to different clusters, it may be necessary to manually configure their configuration files individually, depending upon the complexity required. Back to top Additional Configuration of Operators for Load Balancing When configuring load balancing, it is often useful to group the SmartUI Operators that connect to a cluster into more than one set. Then modify the ClusterServers setting for each of these sets, so that the order in which they connect to the Servers within the cluster differ. For example, if we have three sets of SmartUI Operators that need to connect to this cluster, then each of their CONFIG files could be configured with three different ClusterServers settings. In this way each SmartUI Operator in the three different sets connects to a different SmartUI Server on start up. For instance: Set 1 Cluster1~Computer1~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE; Cluster1~Computer2~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE; Cluster1~Computer3~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE Set 2 Cluster1~Computer2~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE; Cluster1~Computer3~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE; Cluster1~Computer1~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE Set 3 Cluster1~Computer3~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBS

r1~Computer2~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE; Cluster1~Computer3~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE; Cluster1~Computer1~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE Set 3 Cluster1~Computer3~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE; Cluster1~Computer1~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE; Cluster1~Computer2~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE IMPORTANT NOTES The INITIAL connection for the SmartUI Operator MUST have a running SmartUI Server. In other words, if a SmartUI Operator is configured to connect to the SmartUI Server on Computer3, this SmartUI Server MUST be running, otherwise the initial log on of this SmartUI Operator will fail. From then on if this SmartUI Server fails, this SmartUI Operator will hunt until it finds an active connection. The speed at which this occurs is determined by its switch-over time. This switch-over time is the time taken for a SmartUI Operator to become aware that its current connection has failed and to search for and connect to another SmartUI Server. This is configured by the ClientPingInterval setting of the SmartUI Operator, which is grouped under the ConnectionSettings in the SmartUI Operator.exe.config file. The ClientPingInterval setting determines how often the SmartUI Ope

PingInterval setting of the SmartUI Operator, which is grouped under the ConnectionSettings in the SmartUI Operator.exe.config file. The ClientPingInterval setting determines how often the SmartUI Operator will query the Server for an active connection and its configuration has the following effect upon the performance of the Operator: If this interval is too frequent interval, this will increase client-server chatter and use up bandwidth unnecessarily. If this interval is too infrequent interval, then the SmartUI Operator will take a long time to realise that the Server it is currently connected to is no longer available. A ping interval between 5 and 10 seconds should suffice for most cluster configurations. -->

In this way, each user can customise the values trended using an associated LineChart control, according to their requirements. Note: The TrendConfigurator is a SEPARATE control from the LineChart control and requires an associated LineChart control to trend its configured sets of series. Since this control is intended for use in a SCADA environment, it provides support for the physical structure of automation projects as described by the ISA S95 and S88 standards, so when specifying which values (tags) need to be trended, the following drop-down lists are available for use: Note: Of these levels only the Pen is mandatory, both the Area and Device levels can be hidden if needed. text: How to configure graphic form security Top How to configure graphic form security Typically graphic forms are secured (access to them is controlled) by the projects in which they are created. However, when designing graphic forms in the Designer, it is also possible to limit the interaction and viewing capabilities of particular users within the graphic forms too. This is achieved by specifying which users have access to which properties exposed by the controls that have been added to the graphic form. text: How to configure the OEE agent to calculate a KPI Top How to configure the OEE agent to calculate a KPI This explains the recommended method of configuring your Adroit system to calculate a KPI Key Performance Indicator, a quantifiable measurement that measures how well something is accomplishing its goals and objectives. for specific equipment (machine/s) and/or an entire plant (process). KPIs are either: simple : some production value over time such as ton/hr, total produced or actual run-hours, etc. [KPI% = (Total input1/Run time)/Target KPI] OR complex : one production value against (divided by) another production value, such as kWh/ton. [KPI% = (Total input1/Total input2)/Target KPI] Note: If the SECOND variable is not specified, then the FIRST variable is automatically divided by time. The KPI can either compare actual performance with benchmark (optimum) figures or compare shift performances. For instance you could compare today’s total performance with that of the previous day and/or today's shifts with those of the previous day. text: How to configure user security Top How to configure user security The SmartUI security system is user-centric and operates on top of the traditional Windows operating system security, using a configurable sub-set of the existing users and groups on each Server computer, known as the "allowed" users and groups. This process requires the following steps: Create the necessary user accounts on the SmartUI Server computer . Add the users to the list of allowed users of the SmartUI Server computer . Configure access to the added datasources, where necessary . For the purposes of this example only two users are required to be allowed to log into this SmartUI Server, namely the Operator (which should belong to the group “Users”) and the Administrator (which should belong to the group “Administrators”). How to Connect to the SmartUI Server over the Web Top How to connect to the Server over the Web This describes the recommended procedure to connect Operators to a Server over the Internet, as follows: The SmartUI Web Service must be installed on a web server or ‘Internet PC, which provides Internet connectivity between the Server and its clients. Installing the SmartUI Web Service . Since SmartUI Operators are typically deployed using the SmartUI Launcher application, the VIP Distributor service must be started on the SmartUI Server computer. Starting the SmartUI Distributor service . This is used together with the SmartUI Launcher application, as follows: Note : This also provides a good way of testing whether the Internet connectivity is working. The VIP Distributor service identifies a "distribution" folder on its computer. The SmartUI Launcher then connects to the computer that is running the VIP Distributor service and is able to download all files and folders that have been placed in the "distribution" folder and allows any downloaded executables to be launched. Test that the SmartUI Web Service is working externally, via the Internet. Testing Internet connection to the SmartUI Server . text: How to create a parameterised database query and view it in a DataGrid control Top How to create a parameterised database query and view it in a DataGrid control Queries can be performed on an OLE DB compliant database to produce a sub-set of data, which comply with the specified requirements of the query. This is useful to create different views or sets of the data, so that the displayed data can be uniquely adapted to the need. OLE DB is an open standard for accessing data from a variety of sources – both relational and non-relational data. An OLE DB datasource exposes the data contained within an OLE DB compliant database or data store as fields within one or more tables. IMPORTANT: The screenshots and specified configuration settings relate to an OLD version of the SmartUI product and so your specific settings and screens may differ. Queries can only be added once an OLE DB datasource is required for the required OLE DB compliant database. Adding an OLE DB datasource The criteria of these queries can also be parameterised, so that results produced by the query can vary dynamically, depending upon the specified values of the parameters. text: How to create a Wizard that contains a Template pop up Top How to create a Wizard that contains a Template pop-up Introduction We have received many queries about how to create wizards that contain a pop-up that needs to “inherit” or use the tag data that is substituted when the user drops the wizard down on the form. This is a complex requirement but not an unusual one. This requires knowledge of some more advanced concepts of using and understanding “Aliases” which are essentially variables that can be passed between forms. They are an extremely powerful aspect of the product and once understood will help to minimise configuration of complex projects where there are many of the same objects to monitor. By way of example you may have many identical distributed pump stations in a water distribution system. You would like to have a single graphic that represents a pump station, which when you need to view the data and say click on a navigation button, at runtime, pops up a template mimic that is populated with the relevant real-time data from the selected pump station. In addition you might want to have some “template” trends and sub faceplates that would be launched by say clicking

In addition you might want to have some “template” trends and sub faceplates that would be launched by say clicking on a particular pump. This is all possible using the same ideas and technology. Tip: Wizards that display one or more SmartUI Templates can use their substitutions to drive the values of the aliases of these child SmartUI Templates. For details, see Driving aliases with wizard substitutions . Prerequisites Have Adroit 8 (MAPS 3) or later installed. text: How to effectively log your data Top How to effectively log your data Like any SCADA system one of the essential requirements of Adroit is to log values, so that they can be retrieved for long term analysis and reporting purposes. At first it would appear that this process is relatively simple, but the logging of values has evolved over the years into a fairly complex sub-system that requires a guide such as this one for you to use this effectively. For instance, in the past it was potentially necessary to log the same tag using different logging rates and log sizes and even different destinations so multiple log sets could be created within a single datalog agent. Now these multiple log sets are no longer required due to subsequent improvements made to the datalogging sub-system. When recording or logging the values contained in agents in the Agent Server, the first decision you need to make is the logging method that best suits your logging requirements. Configuring the effective logging rate It is important to understand that a value is only logged when it changes and then ONLY when this value meets the conditions imposed by the specified Deadbands , which can be used: to eliminate the nuisance values or noise that can clutter up a log file without providing any meaningful change in value or to reduce the number of records that you log for a value which effectively 'compresses' your log files so you are able to store more data on the same storage medium. So the effective logging rate is determined by configuring the Time... and/or Value deadbands, as follows: Using the Value deadband: Values are ONLY logged if their change in value EXCEEDS the specified deadband value. Hence when the value of a logged point does not exceed the previously logged value by more than the deadband, the value is not logged. Using the Time deadband: One of the following Compression Method algorithms is used to determine which value is logged, if the logged value changes MORE THAN ONC

Note: To use a logging Compression Method, you need to use a Time... logging deadband that is greater than 0. Actual : the logged value is the value at the end of the specified Time deadband (the default). Average : a time-weighted average is maintained for all the changes that occur and this is logged at the end of the specified. Minimum : the lowest or minimum value is logged at the end of the specified Time deadband. Maximum : the highest or maximum value is logged at the end of the specified Time deadband. text: How to effectively log your data Top How to effectively log your data Like any SCADA system one of the essential requirements of Adroit is to log values, so that they can be retrieved for long term analysis and reporting purposes. At first it would appear that this process is relatively simple, but the logging of values has evolved over the years into a fairly complex sub-system that requires a guide such as this one for you to use this effectively. For instance, in the past it was potentially necessary to log the same tag using different logging rates and log sizes and even different destinations so multiple log sets could be created within a single datalog agent. Now these multiple log sets are no longer required due to subsequent improvements made to the datalogging sub-system. When recording or logging the values contained in agents in the Agent Server, the first decision you need to make is the logging method that best suits your logging requirements. Adroit provides the following methods of storing data: IMPORTANT: If rapid logging is required, then use the Datalog agent to log to the propriety Adroit database. Proprietary Adroit log files: This logging method uses the Datalo

Proprietary Adroit log files: This logging method uses the Datalog agent and has been specifically designed for the needs of the SCADA industry to provide improved HIGH SPEED logging performance, typically achieving sub-second logging rates. You should always use this logging method if you need REAL-TIME trending of your data within Adroit itself, such as in a chart on a graphic form. Note: Unlike in previous versions of Adroit the logging to databases by the Datalog agent is disabled by default in Adroit 10 to force users to use the DBLog agent, which has been specifically designed for this task A table in an OLE DB database : This logging method is ideally suited for logging slow moving data and NOT for high speed logging and can use the following two agents, depending upon your intended reason for storing the data: IMPORTANT: BOTH these logging methods are MUCH SLOWER than when using the Datalog agent due to the inherent inefficiencies of the OLE DB interface, in interfacing with remote databases. Batch processing : In this case, use the DbAccess

Batch processing : In this case, use the DbAccess agent , which is ideally suited for batch processing as it allows you to define your table structure and then map agents to the various fields, so that you can log both TEXT and NUMERIC values separately to create a single record per batch and then requires that you specify the unique trigger to log this batch. However, the DbAccess agent is not suited to logging a large number of tags to a database as it requires that you specify a trigger for each record that you intend to log and does not provide any tag importing functionality. Bulk logging of NUMERIC or DIGITAL tags : In this case, use the DBLog agent , which has been specifically designed to efficiently log large numbers of primarily NUMERIC (e.g. Analog) or DIGITAL tags to databases, by providing bulk triggering mechanisms and tag importing functionality and even housekeeping functionality to ensure that only the most current data is stored in the database. However, the DBLog agent is not suited to batch processing as it uses a predefined database table so it is more difficult to group the values that belong to the same batch and it can ONLY log TEXT by converting all the logged values to Strings . When logging to proprietary Adroit log files: As previously stated this is a fast logging method facilitated by the Datalog agent that is designed to provide improved logging performance, by using datalog (.LDG) files to store the active logged data and log backup (.LDB) files that store the historical data. You should always use this logging method if all you need to do is to display (report) your data within Adroit itself, such as in a chart on a graphic form. When configuring the Datalog agent, firstly select the required data-logging Mode , which depends upon how this process value is being used as follows: Continuous: the default setting, where Adroit logs data values as and when the value changes and then ONLY when this value meets the conditions imposed by the specified Deadbands (see below for more details

text: uous: the default setting, where Adroit logs data values as and when the value changes and then ONLY when this value meets the conditions imposed by the specified Deadbands (see below for more details). This is the default setting as this mode typically applies to most process variables, whose values you want to record for trending etc. Demand: Adroit only logs a data value when the LogNow or Trigger is activated and then ONLY when this value meets the conditions imposed by the specified Deadbands (see below for more details). This mode typically applies to batch type processes, to prevent the logging of every change it receives during the execution of a batch and only log the value at the end of a batch, in this case: The Trigger edit field, allows a String tag (agent.slot) to be specified, which is monitored for a zero to non-zero transition, at which time a log occurs (provided it complies with the . When this occurs, a log occurs provided this value meets the conditions of the specified deadbands. The Log Now button is provided for manually triggering the logging. Both: this is a hybrid mode that uses both the Continuous and Demand data logging modes. Configuring the effective

text: ified deadbands. The Log Now button is provided for manually triggering the logging. Both: this is a hybrid mode that uses both the Continuous and Demand data logging modes. Configuring the effective logging rate It is important to understand that a value is only logged when it changes and then ONLY when this value meets the conditions imposed by the specified Deadbands , which can be used: to eliminate the nuisance values or noise that can clutter up a log file without providing any meaningful change in value or to reduce the number of records that you log for a value which effectively 'compresses' your log files so you are able to store more data on the same storage medium. So the effective logging rate is determined by configuring the Time... and/or Value deadbands, as follows: Using the Value deadband: Values are ONLY logged if their change in value EXCEEDS the specified deadband value. Hence when the value of a logged point does not exceed the previously logged value by more than the deadband, the value is not logged. Using the Time deadband: One of the following Compression Method algorithms is used to determine which value is logged, if the logged value changes MORE THAN ONC

metadata.title: How to effectively log your data

text: the deadband, the value is not logged. Using the Time deadband: One of the following Compression Method algorithms is used to determine which value is logged, if the logged value changes MORE THAN ONCE during the specified deadband period: IMPORTANT: When using the Demand Mode , you need to configure the Support compression algorithm on demand logging global datalogging setting via the Advanced... button, in order to use these Datalog compression algorithms. Note: To use a logging Compression Method, you need to use a Time... logging deadband that is greater than 0. Actual : the logged value is the value at the end of the specified Time deadband (the default). Average : a time-weighted average is maintained for all the changes that occur and this is logged at the end of the specified. Minimum : the lowest or minimum value is logged at the end of the specified Time deadband. Maximum : the highest or maximum value is logged at the end of the specified Time deadband. If you are using the Time... deadband to compress your log file to store more data then the Average method is recommended, since it calculates a time-weighted average of all the values that were recorded during the Time d

text: Time... deadband to compress your log file to store more data then the Average method is recommended, since it calculates a time-weighted average of all the values that were recorded during the Time deadband period and this average is then logged at the end of this period. In other words a 1-hour average (as opposed to a 1-hour interval raw log) will provide a more accurate representation of what happened in the plant, than the same raw log. Since the raw log value will only represent the instantaneous value in the hour, not the average for the hour. It is important to know that a value is only logged when it changes and when this change in value meets the conditions imposed by the specified Deadbands because this means that the specified Length... of the datalog (.LDG) file is only an estimation, which assumes that this value will change substantially at the effective rate of logging determined by the deadbands, however: if the value changes less than the effective rate of logging, then this log file will contain data for more than the specified duration but if the value changes more often than the effective rate of logging, these changes will not be recorded. The Datalog agent al

text: en this log file will contain data for more than the specified duration but if the value changes more often than the effective rate of logging, these changes will not be recorded. The Datalog agent allows for a maximum of 53000000 records. This means that the specified datalog Length... (or period) and Time... deadband combination may not exceed 53000000 records. This corresponds to a maximum of 1010.9 MB of data at 20 bytes per record, which means 613 days at 1 second or 30 days at 50 ms. Note: The minimum Time... deadband allowed is 10 ms which only provides a maximum Length... (or period) of 6.13 days of logged data. Furthermore, you can use Out of limit logging to bypass this process and immediately log any out of limit values (values that are not within their specified operating range), by ignoring the effective rate of logging, which is specified by the Time... deadband and using the faster log rate specified by the Out of limit logging -> Time... setting instead. In other words, as soon as the logged value that is being logged, enters or leaves its user-specified limit range it is logged unconditionally, and continues to be logged at the new time deadband as specified by the

metadata.title: How to effectively log your data

text: as soon as the logged value that is being logged, enters or leaves its user-specified limit range it is logged unconditionally, and continues to be logged at the new time deadband as specified by the Out of limit logging time setting ( Time... ). This allows the Datalog agent to catch short spikes whose duration is less than the normal time deadband logging interval ( Deadbands -> Time... ) Usage Example: A customer wants to monitor his incoming voltage of 220 V. Previously, without using out of limit monitoring: he would create a Datalog agent to log this voltage tag at a logging rate of 1 second for a period of 1 week. So, in this case, this Datalog agent is configured ( Length = 7 days and Deadbands Time = 1 sec) to log all changes to the voltage at 1 second and always keep one week's worth of this data. Using out of limit monitoring: since he is actually not that interested in logging this voltage, if it remains within its normal operating voltage range of 215-225 volts, as long as the voltage is within this value range he is happy to log it at a far slower rate - say 10 seconds. But when the voltage breaches this range, then he wants this Datalog agent to log this value at 1

How to log the communication of a driver Top How to log the communication of a driver Introduction When troubleshooting potential driver problems, it is essential to understand exactly how the specific device of an installed driver is communicating between Adroit and the specified front-end device. Adroit provides a utility known as the Driver Monitor that is used for just this purpose and one of its functions allows it to display the Datascope window, which allows you to view and log the exact communication messages and errors as they occur between Adroit and the specified front-end device. This procedure describes how to create an HTML log file of the communication messages and errors as they occur between Adroit and the specified front-end device. So that if you are not a driver expert, you can email this log file to Adroit support, who will then be able to assist you with your driver problem. The advantage of an HTML log file over a text file is that this file format preserves the color of the Datascope window, which makes the troubleshooting process easier. Prerequisites Have Adroit 8.4 or later installed. Note: If you are using a version earlier than this, then the method use

text: How to manually specify Total ON or OFF time Top How to manually specify Total ON or OFF time One application of the Counter agents is to monitor device running/stopped bit to display motor running hours. Due to control system starts, stops, backups and communication breaks, it is often necessary to manually specify the Total On Time (and/or Total Off Time) as an operator entry function. So that the Counter agent must resume counting from the new value. The Total On Time and Total Off Time, is saved by the Counter agent in its rawOnTotal and rawOffTotal slots as a millisecond based time value. In other words 1 hour = 3600000 milliseconds. Therefore in order to create a button to allow an operator to specify the Total On Time of a Counter agent, you need to add the following THREE Operator Action behaviours to it: The first operator action sets the contpause slot of this Counter agent to 0. The second operator action allows the operator to type in a new value rawOnTotal in milliseconds (where 1 hour = 3600000 milliseconds). The third operator action sets the contpause slot of this Counter agent to 1. -->

This document aims to describe the three COMMUNICATION mechanisms and two CONNECTION mechanisms that SmartUI provides, each intended to optimise the use of a specific network infrastructure: Minimum requirements Graphic form size: 50-100 kb. Computer: Pentium IV with 512MB RAM. Bandwidth: 512KB/sec [slower GPRS/3G links may still provide acceptable response times] Install the latest available version of SmartUI Start your SmartUI Server and SmartUI Designer and log in to the SmartUI Server. Communication mechanisms Subscribe A LAN based communication mechanism where the SERVER will PUSH data to the CLIENT. This mechanism is the fastest and the CLIENT will receive changes as they happen on the SERVER. This mechanism does not optimise bandwidth usage, but is the fastest. Subscribe-Poll A communications mechanism

metadata.title: How to optimise performance for remote clients over slow networks

text: chanism is the fastest and the CLIENT will receive changes as they happen on the SERVER. This mechanism does not optimise bandwidth usage, but is the fastest. Subscribe-Poll A communications mechanism that can be used on a LAN/WAN or the Internet. This mechanism does NOT PUSH any data to the CLIENT, but relies on the CLIENT to POLL for the data. ALL the changes since the last POLL cycle will be retrieved from the SERVER. This mechanism attempts to reduce latency by minimising round-trips to the SERVER. Poll A communications mechanism that can be used on a LAN/WAN or the Internet. This mechanism does NOT PUSH any data to the CLIENT, but relies on the CLIENT to POLL for the data. Only the LAST change will be retrieved from the SERVER for each interested data point e.g. if there has been 5 changes to a set point, only the last change will be fetched (the most recent change). This mechanism attempts to reduce latency by minimising round-trips to the SERVER. It will also try to optimise bandwidth usage by retrieving as little data as possible. TIP : On slower networks, opt to use the SUBSCRIBE-POLL mechanism first and then the POLL mechanism. Configurable settings: The following setting

Configurable settings: The following settings can be applied to the communication mechanisms on the SmartUI Client applications (Designer and/or Operator): ClientPollTime : The time (in seconds) which will be used to POLL the SERVER for any changes. ClientPingInterval : An “IsAlive” period in which the CLIENT will determine whether the SERVER is still available. Connection mechanisms: SmartUI offers the following TWO connection mechanisms that can be used with some or all of the communication mechanisms, as follows: MAINDATAPROVIDER A direct, binary connection to the SERVER using a proprietary protocol. The channel can be encrypted using some of the configuration options discussed below. The communication to the SERVER is normally on port 9000. All three communication mechanisms may be used. WEBSERVICEDATAPROVIDER An indirect, Web Service (XML) connection to the SERVER via IIS. Packets are compressed before they are made available to the CLIENT. The communication to the SERVER is normally via IIS on port 80 and then from IIS to

text: ervice (XML) connection to the SERVER via IIS. Packets are compressed before they are made available to the CLIENT. The communication to the SERVER is normally via IIS on port 80 and then from IIS to the SERVER on port 9000. Only the SUBSCRIBE-POLL and POLL mechanisms may be used. Configurable settings: The following settings can be applied to the connection mechanisms on BOTH the SmartUI Server and Client applications (Designer and/or Operator): NetworkBindAddress : This setting determines which subnet the SERVER and CLIENTS communicate on and is required for computers with multiple network cards or IP ranges . Note : ALL CLIENTS and SERVERS that need to communicate must have this setting specified in order to communicate with each other. Example : SERVER has TWO IP’s: 10.10.10.9 and 196.248.23.1; Client has TWO IP’s: 10.10.10.101 and 192.168.1.2; If both need to communicate set the SERVER NetworkBindAddress to: 10.10.10.9 and the CLIENT’s NetworkBindAddress to: 10.10.10.101; The following settings can ONLY be applied to the connection mechanisms on the SmartUI Server: BroadcastEnabled : This setting causes the SERVER application to broadcast it’s availability to the subnet and is

metadata.title: How to optimise performance for remote clients over slow networks

text: owing settings can ONLY be applied to the connection mechanisms on the SmartUI Server: BroadcastEnabled : This setting causes the SERVER application to broadcast it’s availability to the subnet and is ONLY required for clustered systems, so DISABLE this setting if not in a clustered SmartUI environment.. This setting only applies to the local subnet and does NOT apply to Internet/WAN connected CLIENTS. Note : This setting INCREASES general network traffic. ServerPort : This setting specifies the port that the SERVER listens for incoming connections. Note : If this port is changed, make sure it is changed on the CLIENT as well. Caching: Caching can optimise the transfer of data between the CLIENT and the SERVER. For instance, if a graphic form that has been cached is opened by the Client, this graphic form is loaded from the local cache instead of retrieving it from the Server via the Internet/LAN so it opens quickly. There are TWO main caching techniques, both of which are configured on the CLIENT: Using the DataElementCachingEnabled setting : This method determines whether the SERVER contains a more recent version of an object than the CLIENT: If it does, the CLIENT cache will be

metadata.title: How to optimise performance for remote clients over slow networks

text: n the CLIENT: Using the DataElementCachingEnabled setting : This method determines whether the SERVER contains a more recent version of an object than the CLIENT: If it does, the CLIENT cache will be updated. If it does not, the CLIENT will simply use the object from it’s local cache. In other words, a cached graphic form will ONLY be loaded by the Client if it remains unchanged when it is opened again. In other words, no further design changes have been made to this graphic form that is stored on the Server. Note : This method requires a roundtrip to the SERVER. Using the DataElementCachingRetrieveRegardless setting : This method retrieves the cached object (if it exists) regardless of whether a more recent version exists on the SERVER. Note : This method is faster as it does NOT require a roundtrip to the SERVER. This greatly improves the user experience but requires the additional administrative overhead of ensuring that the local cache is updated to include any changes made to the graphic forms of the project/s that it displays AND then copy this updated local cache to all the Operators that use this project/s. How to prevent multiple users from simultaneously editing the same graphic form Top How to prevent multiple users from simultaneously editing the same graphic form If multiple users or engineers develop graphic forms in project datasources, it is necessary to ensure that they cannot overwrite each others work by both accidentally editing the same graphic form at the same time. To this end, it is necessary to use the data element security infrastructure, provide by SmartUI , to ensure that there is only one person who can write to a project at a time. The following configuration is required: Initial Windows Security Setup You need to ensure that each engineer logs in with his/her own unique user onto the SmartUI Designer. Furthermore, each of these users must have the necessary rights to modify the security settings on data elements for the project datasource. In this case: Create windows users for each person who needs to edit graphic forms in the windows user management system tool. Create a new user group called ‘designer users’ and assign all the users you created in the previous step to this group. For further details, see How to configure user security . text: How to reuse graphical components Top How to reuse graphical components A common practice in projects is to modularise components to reuse them elsewhere, as follows: Design-time reuse : in this case, graphic forms or portions of graphic forms, behave like advanced controls that are added to other graphic forms to speed up the creation of their user-functionality. Run-time reuse : in this case, complete pre-configured graphic forms allow you to change which values they display or allow user to interact with, at runtime. Prerequisites Have Adroit 8 (MAPS 3) or later installed. Note: If you are using a version later than this then this how to will probably also apply to your version too, although some dialogs and/or commands may have changed slightly. Design-time reuse Wizards: Wizards allow you to reuse the same graphical object and its assigned Behaviours (if any), over and over again, with different values (data elements), without having to recreate this object from scratch ever time. In other words, a wizard is a reusable design-time object, much like a Windows control. Also wizards have the facility to update their instances that have been added to graphic forms to their current

In other words, a wizard is a reusable design-time object, much like a Windows control. Also wizards have the facility to update their instances that have been added to graphic forms to their current configuration, when they are modified after having been used. For details, see How to create and use wizards . Use the Favorites tool window, which: allows you to create your own custom set (library) of your favorite graphic forms and wizards, which you frequently use. helps to speed up the process of designing your graphic forms, since you can directly drag these from this tool window onto your graphic forms without having to find them in their relevant projects. Note: Projects and their folders provide a Preview Graphic Forms option to displays thumbnail snapshots of all the graphic forms located in their immediate or root level to either open the required graphic form or populate the Favorites tool window. For details, see Previewing graphic forms . Manually create and manage a library of graphical components : Another method of design-time reuse is creating a library of graphical components that can be copied and pasted to the required graphic forms and then connecting the necessa

of graphical components : Another method of design-time reuse is creating a library of graphical components that can be copied and pasted to the required graphic forms and then connecting the necessary values to the properties of these components. In this case, you can export the required graphical components to XML files and then simply drag the file into a graphic form that is being designed in the SmartUI Designer. For details, see How to export a graphical component to a XML file . Although this reduces the amount of repetition required, it does not eliminate the task of reconnecting the data every time to every new component. Furthermore, should the specification of a component change (say its look and colors) then the user would need to go and manually update every instance of this component. Mapping spiders : Facilitates the simple connection of data to the required properties of this reusable graphical component. In other words, this eliminates the process of manually locating the properties of the reusable graphical component, in order to provide their values with live data. Template GOs : By using a TemplateGO control, a graphic form can behave as a reusable graphical component. The fundamental difference between a graphic form and a SmartUI Template is that a SmartUI Template has aliases, some of which are automatically created, which allow data elements within Behaviours and/or spiders to be dynamically driven. Back to top How to create and use wizards A Wizard is a pre-drawn and/or pre-configured skeleton of graphical objects and their assigned Behaviours (if any), which has placeholders (substitutions) for data elements, which can simplify and speed up the task of creating graphic forms. But, instead of directly specifying the values that drive these Behaviours, these are replaced with value or static text placeholders (substitutions). Each time a wizard is inserted into a graphic form, a dialog is displayed whereby values must be specified for all the substitutions that occur within this wizard. For instance, instead of redrawing a pump or a motor, each time one is required, a wizard can be created and simply inserted wherever a pump or motor is needed, at which time you link the required data elements (values) to its pre-defined substitutions. You have two main options when creating wizards, typically in the Enterprise Manager window: Either create the wizard from scratch:

he required data elements (values) to its pre-defined substitutions. You have two main options when creating wizards, typically in the Enterprise Manager window: Either create the wizard from scratch: in this case, right click a project or folder and select Create Wizard . Note: When creating a wizard from scratch, the default size of the wizard is 200 by 200 pixels, since wizards are typically small by nature. If necessary customise this default, by using the Designer.CONFIG setting in the Misc group, called DefaultWizardsize . Or convert an existing graphic form into a wizard: in this case, open the required graphic form and select the Save as Wizard graphic form toolbar button. Then use the Substitution configuration dialog to create ALL the necessary substitutions for this new wizard. Tip: When you substitute a data element that is used in numerous locations within the graphic form, all these locations use the specified substitution name. The graphic form toolbar contains the Optimise Graphic Form size button (at the end), which resizes the wizard to the size of the added controls and vectors, so that there are no overlaps at the top, bottom, left or right sides. Now design the

ise Graphic Form size button (at the end), which resizes the wizard to the size of the added controls and vectors, so that there are no overlaps at the top, bottom, left or right sides. Now design the graphical components of your wizard as you would a normal graphic form. When you get to the point of where you must specify data elements (values), e.g. when creating a behaviour, instead of browsing in a data elements you simply type in the substitution name with curly brackets around the name, e.g. {PUMP}. For details, see Working with Wizard substitutions . After saving the wizard, you simply drag the wizard from the Enterprise Manager onto the graphic form where you want to use this wizard, at which point you’ll be prompted to assign valid data elements to the substitutions you specified in your wizard. Back to top Mapping Spiders Ultimately, data is connected to properties of controls or vectors, to animate them. However, it is not always easy to know which property to connect the data to, especially considering the number of properties that a control can expose. Mapping spiders can be used to simply this process, by providing a central location where the data for a reusable graphical component can be connected, without needing to manually locate the required properties. In other words, the user ties the data to the inputs of the Mapping spider, which are custom-named so that it is easy to identi

e connected, without needing to manually locate the required properties. In other words, the user ties the data to the inputs of the Mapping spider, which are custom-named so that it is easy to identify which data point goes to which input. This is made possible because the Mapping spider consists of input output pairs, so the user who creates the reusable graphical component also creates the Mapping spider and the required input-output pairs, which are named appropriately. Back to top Template Graphic Objects While it is possible to use a Mapping spider to simplify the mapping of data to the properties of reusable graphical components, it would still be necessary to update every instance of this graphical component should a global change be required. This can be prevented, however, by using template graphic forms. There is a control called a TemplateGO control, which has the unique ability to contain another graphic form. By using this control, it is possible to reuse a graphic form as a component in another graphic form. Since this reusable component is actually a reference to another graphic form and not a copy of a reusable component, making changes to the reusable form can result in that change immediately becoming available in all the

mponent is actually a reference to another graphic form and not a copy of a reusable component, making changes to the reusable form can result in that change immediately becoming available in all the places where this graphic form is used. Furthermore, just as reusable components allow data to be connected to them to animate them, it is also possible to create a reusable graphic form that can have data connected to it via the TemplateGO control. This is accomplished, through the Aliases property of the graphic form, which can contain any number of user defined data entry points to the graphic form. In other words any of the properties of the controls used on the graphic form can be exposed by this Aliases property. Then when a TemplateGO control contains this graphic form, the Aliases property of the TemplateGO control exposes the Aliases property in this contained graphic form and the data entry points that have been configured so that data can be connected to them. In this case the property spider associated with the Aliases property provides a central location from which data can be connected to these exposed entry points, much like the Mapping spider. IMPORTANT: The screenshots and specified configuration settings relate to an OLD version of the SmartUI product and so your specific settings and screens may differ. This method of setting and triggering spiders is useful in the following scenarios: To ensure that a spider in triggered only after all input parameter value(s) have been set. When you have more than one spider that needs to be triggered and the relevant spiders must always be triggered in a specific order. When the input parameter value(s) of the spider is so complex that it can only be calculated using script. When the output data of a spider is needed in your script for further processing. text: How to use the ICMP agent to ensure the availability of a networked device Top How to use the ICMP agent to ensure the availability of a networked device The ICMP or PING agent uses the Internet Control Message Protocol to determine the existence of a remote device on the network. By continuously polling the specified remote IP address, this agent is therefore able to identify potential network problems as they occur by generating alarms when errors are obtained when attempting to contact the specified remote IP address and/or when the round trip time The time to send an ICMP message to the network device and receive a reply. exceeds specified High and High-high times. Things you need to know or do before you can assess the availability of a networked device: Ensure that the network supports the Internet Control Message Protocol. Ensure that you know the IP address of the required device and that this IP address does not change. ONLY IP addresses can be specified, so if you need to contact a web address, you need to resolve this to an IP address first. To ensure the availability of a device on a network: Edit an agent of type: ICMP . If necessary, add an agent of the required type,

text: How to use the IOT agent to define an object Top Defining the structure of an IOT agent Configuration This agent does not possess any default status slots and is required to be configured externally. The IOT agent is basically not usable until it’s configuration is defined by using either the addSlot or the xmlSlots slot. Configuration of the agent slots is not currently supported by the agent dialog, however, you may import a XML slot definition file that defines the slots for any single IOT agent. It is typically called from an external source, for example, a browser or 3rd party application. Creating the structure of an object You should provide an appropriate name and then add the required IOT agent, which will enable the code that interfaces to the IOT device to identify it. As only this code knows the identification of the IOT device, it should use the addSlot OR xmlSlots slots of this agent to programmatically create the slots as required. Using the addSlot The format for this slot is as follows: slottypeidx,slotname[,slotdescription[,slotvalue]] Where: slottypeidx : is a slot type index as follows: 0 : boolean (1/0) 1 : integer (4 byte signed integer) 2 : real (8 byte float

text: lot is as follows: slottypeidx,slotname[,slotdescription[,slotvalue]] Where: slottypeidx : is a slot type index as follows: 0 : boolean (1/0) 1 : integer (4 byte signed integer) 2 : real (8 byte float) 3 : string (79 characters) 4 : time 5 : tagname (67 chars) (see “Use of Tagname type slots” below) 10 : varstring (any number of characters) slotname : any valid slotname not exceeding 15 characters and not containing the characters $ @ , \ & % * ? slotdescription : any 79 character description describing the agent (object) instance slotvalue : any suitable slot value conforming to the slot type index above Using the xmlSLot This XML structure requires that you always specify: the name and description of the IOT agent in the <IOT> section. the name, description and values of each slot that you require in the <Slots> section, where: The slot name is any valid slot name not exceeding 15 characters and does not contain the characters $ @ , \ & % * ? The slot description is any 79 character description that describes the purpose of this property. The slot type is one of the following (case sensitive) values: Boolean : a 1 or a 0 Integer : a 4 byte signed integer Real : an 8 byte floatStr

The slot type is one of the following (case sensitive) values: Boolean : a 1 or a 0 Integer : a 4 byte signed integer Real : an 8 byte floatString : 79 characters Time : Win32 64-bit FILETIME Type Name : 67 chars. For more details, see How to use Tagname type slots . VarString : any number of characters Status bits, you can specify status bits in the <HeaderSlots> section, where only the status bit name is required. Note: You should note, however, that you do not need to specify a name for the status bits of an IOT agent for them to be used. Example of the XML structure The following is an example of the required XML structure for the xml slot of the IOT agent with custom text shown in blue for ease of reference: <IOT Name=" Fridge1 " Description=" Fridge in kitchen "><Slots><Slot Name=" value " Description=" Temperature " Type=" Real "> 20 </Slot></Slots><HeaderSlots><Slot Name=" hi "/></HeaderSlots></IOT> Alternatively, with Revision 7 or later of iot.dll, you should use <IOT><SlotDefinitions><Slot Name=" value " Description=" Temperature "Type="Real"> 20 </Slot></SlotDefinitions><HeaderSlots><Slot Name=" hi "/></HeaderSlot

For more details, see How SmartUI implements the S88 / S95 hierarchy . The MAPS project wizard in the SmartUI Designer provides a “first principal” approach of using the MAPS Project Wizard, showing how MAPS uses the S88/S95 extended physical model hierarchy to organise equipment. text: How to use the Scanning Monitor Utility Top How to Use the Scanning Monitor Utility The Scanning Monitor utility is particularly useful in tuning polled driver's polling intervals. However, OPC Server devices not in "sync-poll mode", and telemetry applications will find this utility less useful. For details of the user interface of this utility, see Scanning Monitor Utility . Tip: The Scanning Monitor utility can generate a report of your current scanning configuration of an Agent Server to indicate how well it has been configured. For details, see Creating and using the Scan Configuration Report . After understanding the user interface of the program and selecting the required device from the Device List , one really needs to only look at 2 things, the "effective" scan rate (rate at which the driver actually returns data), and the polling rate you intended it to use, these 2 values are in column 5 and 6 of the Scan Job List . If the effective rate is consistently greater than the intended rate, you have a scanning backlog. Find the scan jobs with the shortest scan-times, as you select each one, check how many tags (scan points) are scanned in that task in the Tag List , which is i

metadata.title: How to use the Scanning Monitor Utility

text: nded rate, you have a scanning backlog. Find the scan jobs with the shortest scan-times, as you select each one, check how many tags (scan points) are scanned in that task in the Tag List , which is immediately below the scan job list. Consider the communications bandwidth cost of having a task with only one I/O point; at this point one can make the scan-interval of an expensive point longer to remedy this. If all tasks are responding slower than their intended intervals, then a re-evaluation of all the scan-times is needed. For further details concerning the scanning optimization benefit of grouping scanned data, see Scanning Optimization Tips . Since the right-click commands within the Scan Job List that change scan rates are not permanent (in other words saving the Adroit agent database will not save these online changes), it is necessary to perform the following procedure to make any changes permanent: To make permanent scan rate changes: Backup your Adroit agent database file (.WGP). For details, see Backing Up Agent Database Files . Stop the required device agent , and wait a few seconds for any backlogged polling to cease. Export the Device agent type , i.e. click the No but

When the next agent type message box is displayed, click Cancel , to stop the exporting process. This file will contain four columns or comma-separated values, from left to right as follows: Address, agent.slot, Scanning Interval (period), Deadband Increase the scan-times on all I/O points, particularly those that are not fast moving within your process. You will want to increase all of your tags poll rates up until the average "effscanrate" value, or increase most of them to double that value and leave just a few scanning quickly. Save and close this CSV file. In the User Interface, edit the required Device agent . Remove all the scan points from this device (unscan them).
