text: How to use the SNMPMgr agent to Manage a Device Top How to use the SNMPMgr agent to Manage a Device This agent can both monitor and manage devices on a network, by using the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP). Examples of devices that can be monitored using SNMP include routers, switches, hubs, UPSs, printers, modems and computers. Things you need to know or do before you can manage a device: ensure that you know which SNMP version the device supports and that you know all of its connection settings. Since the SNMPMgr agent supports up to SNMP version 3 and SNMP version 3 supports additional connection settings. ONLY if this device is a computer, ensure that you have installed and configured the SNMP service on this computer. For details, see Installing the Windows SNMP Service or SNMP Service Security Configuration . IMPORTANT: NEVER run the Windows SNMP Trap (listener) service because it conflicts with the Adroit SNMP trap functionality! Note: This agent does NOT require the Windows SNMP Service to function, this service is ONLY required on each computer that this agent monitors. please ensure that the device and your Agent Server license, complies with the specified SNMPM

text: How to use VIP Version VIP Version The VIP Version application is a diagnostic tool that obtains the versions of all the .DLL and .EXE files in a folder (including its sub-folders) and can export this version list to a .CSV file. This also displays the currently installed VIP version. This is a troubleshooting tool, so that users can email the .CSV file of the file versions of their VIP installation to support, so that support can quickly tell if the installed files are the latest or which files may be causing the current problem. How to use VIP Version: Launch the VIP Version application. By default, this immediately obtains the versions of the files in this folder (and its sub-folders). If necessary, specify another folder whose file versions you want to obtain, as follows: either by using the Browse Folder toolbar button or the File menu, Browse Folder... option. Wait until all the versions of ALL the applicable files in this folder are obtained. The progress bar at the bottom should indicate 100%, as follows: Note : Although some file version numbers are separated by commas ',' these are converted to periods '.' when this list is exported. If necessary, re-check the file versio

d indicate 100%, as follows: Note : Although some file version numbers are separated by commas ',' these are converted to periods '.' when this list is exported. If necessary, re-check the file version numbers of the selected folder and its sub-folders, as follows: either by using the Check File Versions toolbar button or the File menu, Check File Versions option or the bottom right hand corner button. Export the current list of files and their versions to a .CSV file, as follows: either by using the Export to CSV toolbar button or the File menu, Export to CSV option. How to use Wanlink Top How to use Wanlink Wanlink allows data to be replicated over a slow or Wide Area Network (WAN) from one Agent Server to another. In other words, it allows remote Agent Servers to behave as if they were normal remote nodes on a Local Area Network (LAN). The following diagram and explanation, briefly describes how Wanlink works and how it is configured: Where: Computer 1 is the "primary" Agent Server (AS1), which obtains its IO from its remote outstations. WanServer is also running on this computer, which is connected to AS1, no other configuration is required. When a remote Agent Server connects to the primary Agent Server using Wanlink, the remote WanClient will connect to and upload its configuration to the WanServer . The WanServer will then establish connection to the primary computer’s Agent Server (AS1) and communication based on this configuration will commence from then on. Computer 2 is a Remote node, which is able to view and control data on (AS1) directly because it on the same LAN. Note : Since this computer does not have its own Agent Server, it directly accesses the primary computer’s Agent Server (AS1). Computer 3, 4 are the "remote Agent Server

ly because it on the same LAN. Note : Since this computer does not have its own Agent Server, it directly accesses the primary computer’s Agent Server (AS1). Computer 3, 4 are the "remote Agent Servers", these Agent Servers (AS3), (AS4), may or may not have local data derived from other IO sources. WanClient needs to be running on each of these computers. The Configuration file of each WanClient , must essentially specify how to communicate to the WanServer and which local tags in these remote Agent Servers (AS3), (AS4) need to be "linked" to tags that reside in the primary Agent Server (AS1) and the communication settings to its WanServer connected to the primary Agent Server (AS1). Note: It is not necessary to link to all the tags in the primary Agent Server (AS1), only link those tags that are required. The WanClient configuration, is performed using the WanClient Configurator , in the following order: A server must be added , which contains the configuration necessary to communicate with the WanServer computer, the primary Agent Server (AS1) in this case and it specifies the database that will contain the links that need to be communicated. Note: This server is "remote" in that

e with the WanServer computer, the primary Agent Server (AS1) in this case and it specifies the database that will contain the links that need to be communicated. Note: This server is "remote" in that it is on the other side of the WAN from the computer that is running WanClient . Now the tags that are required to be linked must be grouped and these groups must be added . The following criteria need to be considered, when group the tags into groups: The primary consideration should be the type of communication is required between the two Agent Servers: Select a Normal group, for links that require a one-way communication, so that the remote Agent Servers (AS3), (AS4) are only able to view the value of a "linked" tag and any changes made to this tag will not be made to its associated tag on the primary Agent Server (AS1). Select a Control group, for links that require a two-way communication, so that the remote Agent Servers (AS3), (AS4) are able to modify the value of a "linked" tag and its associated tag on the primary Agent Server (AS1) will reflect this change. Note: With this method of linking a remote Agent Server ( Computers 3 and 4 ) can operate as if it was a remote node (

d its associated tag on the primary Agent Server (AS1) will reflect this change. Note: With this method of linking a remote Agent Server ( Computers 3 and 4 ) can operate as if it was a remote node ( Computer 2 ) of the primary Agent Server it is being connected to ( Computer 1 ). The secondary consideration is the poll rate of the tags or the rate at which the WanClient will ask for changes from the WanServer , which only affects tag links that have been configured to be polled (this is described below). Once the tag groups have been created, the specific tag links must be added to their respective groups. When creating tag links, the following methods of linking can be used: Polling , in which case the WanClient will ask for changes to this tag from the WanServer at a fixed rate, so that in this case the WanClient will requests the tag from the primary Agent Server (AS1) every x seconds. This method also requires tags with the same poll period to be grouped in the same group. Subscribed , in which case the WanClient will only ask for changes to this tag from the WanServer on startup and when the value of the tag changes, this is recommended for critical data, since it is a more e

bed , in which case the WanClient will only ask for changes to this tag from the WanServer on startup and when the value of the tag changes, this is recommended for critical data, since it is a more efficient method of linking tags over a WAN. Note: This is also possible to manually edit the CSV files in which the links , tag groups and servers are stored, in order to perform bulk configurations etc. PLEASE NOTE 1: The full tag description must be specified when configuring a remote or local link in the WanClient e.g. "MYDIGITAL.rawValue" If the slot name is omitted, the tag link will fail. PLEASE NOTE 2: Historical data cannot be transferred over Wanlink, only current runtime values will be sent and retrieved. It is possible for a linked tag on a remote Agent Server (AS3),(AS4) to be logged as usual, but then Wanlink connection must be maintained at all times to ensure that no "holes" in the remote datalogs occur. -->

Port switches: If a secondary resource is allowed, this count is the number of times the driver switched between primary and secondary channels. Protocol errors: This counter generally indicates invalid device responses, which are not legal or are unrecognised. Percent errors: This is an indication of the communication fault frequency, which is expressed as a percentage. Read errors: The number of times the driver failed to read an expected response. Read timeouts: The number of times the driver failed to receive a response to a request, within the required time. Write errors: The number of times the driver failed to send data because of a hardware problem. Write timeouts: The number of times the driver timed out while waiting to send data because of a hardware problem. ICMP Agent - Database File Format Top ICMP Agent - Database File Format For a detailed description of any of its slots, see Slot Details . See the agent header slots for the information that is common to all agent types. .WGP File Line Description ADDR==nnn.nnn.nnn.nnn IP address of the network device. ENABLED=n A Boolean value indicating whether ICMP message will be sent to the network device or not. RETRIES=n How many times you want to query the availability of the network device before determining that it is unavailable. TIMEOUT=nnnn How long you want to wait, in milliseconds, to receive a response from the device before you determine that this device is unavailable. LSTEX=nnnnnnnnnn nnnnnnnn UTC stands for Coordinated Universal Time, which is a time standard that couples Greenwich Mean Time (GMT), which is based solely on the Earth's inconsistent rotation rate, with the highly accurate International Atomic Time (TAI). Note: Only after a layer is identified as being the edited layer, will visible form components be attached to it. To identify the layer that is being edited Display the configured layers of the required graphic form: Open and display the required graphic form in the Design workspace . Open the Levels and Layers tool window. For details, see Accessing tool windows . In the grid, click a row heading. This causes the following symbol to be displayed on the left of the row heading and the name of the layer will also become bold and underlined. -->

Identifying visible levels Top Identifying visible levels Only one level can be identified as visible, in the Levels and layers tool window, which means that its associated layers and their visible form components are displayed in the graphic form. Tip: When editing a graphic form, create a level containing all the controls that will appear at the same time, so that they can be arranged. For details, see Arranging controls . To identify the level that is visible Configure the levels of the required graphic form: Open and display the required graphic form in the Design workspace . Open the Levels and Layers tool window. For details, see Accessing tool windows . If necessary, display the configured level(s). For details, see Hiding or showing configured levels . In the grid, click a column heading. This displays the following symbol on the left of the column heading and the name of the level also becomes bold and underlined. Ignoring Delayed SET Commands Top Ignoring Delayed SET Commands Once SET commands are enabled for a Command agent , additional restrictions can be imposed on these commands to further ensure that they are not misused to create a serious security and/or operational risk. For details, see Specifying Permitted Commands or Additional SET Command Restrictions . One of the additional restrictions is to specify the period for which these commands are of valid for, which is calculated from the time the message is originally sent. Any SET commands, whose SMS messages are received after this period has elapsed will not be processed by the Command agent. This is to prevent SMS messages that have been lost or delayed by the network from being inappropriately acted upon. To specify the period of validity for SET commands: If necessary, add a Command agent. For details, see Adding Agents . Edit the required Command agent. For details, see Editing Agents . This will display the Edit Command agent dialog. If necessary, select the General tab, the default selection. Under the Commands group, ensure that the Enable commands and Allow ‘Set’ commands checkboxes are checked to allow this Command agent

log. If necessary, select the General tab, the default selection. Under the Commands group, ensure that the Enable commands and Allow ‘Set’ commands checkboxes are checked to allow this Command agent to perform SET commands. Under the Extended ‘Set’ Configuration group, specify the required period of validity, in minutes, in the Time (in minutes) edit box beneath the Ignore ‘Set’ commands older than title, the default is 0 minutes. -->

One of the additional restrictions is to specify the period for which these commands are of valid for, which is calculated from the time the message is originally sent. Any SET commands, whose SMS messages are received after this period has elapsed will not be processed by the Command agent. This is to prevent SMS messages that have been lost or delayed by the network from being inappropriately acted upon. To specify the period of validity for SET commands: If necessary, add a Command agent. For details, see Adding Agents . Edit the required Command agent. For details, see Editing Agents . Implementing SNMPManager Agents Implementing SNMPManager Agents Each SNMPManager agent can manage a single device, by getting, setting and/or trapping its OID values. PLEASE NOTE: It is very important to set up Windows firewall, or any other similar network security product, correctly to allow SNMP traffic. Failing to do this will result in the inoperability of the SNMPManager agent. For further details on the requirements and guidelines regarding the use of this agent, see Usage Requirements . To implement SNMPManager agents to monitor a physical industrial network: Before setting up the SNMPManager agent, decide which devices you need to monitor. In other words determine the (SNMP) network topology. Tip: It is recommended to create a mimic to visualize the network, because this also assists in quickly detecting of the source of network bottlenecks too. Example of a typical SNMP monitoring mimic: It is recommended to create a mimic to visualize the (SNMP) network topology, not only because it helps in deciding which devices are going to be monitored but more importantly, because the source of bottlenecks can then easily be detected on such a mimic. Import Master Recipe Top Import Master Recipe This is used to import a master recipe and its associated control recipes from a .CSV file. Note: When importing recipes, the CSV file that is being imported CANNOT contain ‘%’ characters, if these characters are present then the file will not be imported. After selecting the appropriate CSV file, click OK to import the master recipe and the requested control recipes. The master recipe is always imported, and the existing master recipe is overwritten. Select an option under Control Recipes: to regulate which control recipes to import. The options are: Import All . Import all of the control recipes in the CSV file. Any already existing control recipe will be overwritten. New control recipes will be added. Import New . Import only new control recipes. Hence, no existing control recipe will be overwritten. Import None . No control recipes found in the CSV file will be imported. Note: This importing can also be achieved by setting the recipe agent’s " importName " slot to the full path and filename of the CSV file that is to be imported. -->

General charting properties: properties that display the charting toolbar, enable the chart to configured in runtime and change the main title of this chart, amongst others Property Function AntiAliased This Boolean property, which is True by default, uses antialiasing to smooth the edges of the drawn chart. DataLegendDigits This Integer property allows you to specify the number of significant places to use when values are rounded off in the data Legend. Direct2DMode This Boolean property, which is False by default, uses GDI+ to chart the data, which is slower as the charting is only performed by the CPU and by the graphics card. Important Points to consider when Clustering Agent Servers Top Important Points to consider when Clustering Agent Servers Clustering in Adroit , previously known as hot standby, consists of a pair of Agent Servers (known as the master and standby) running a replicated agent database (WGP file) on the same project. More details: The master server services all the I/O and client tasks, while the standby server replicates the master server. If the master server or computer fails, the standby server takes over as master and its clients and scanning tasks take appropriate action. The following issues are important when implementing an Adroit cluster: Ensure that both Agent Server computers (and their clients) have their system time synchronised, for clustering to work effectively. For details, see Time Synchronization of an Adroit Cluster . Ideally both Agent Servers, in the cluster, should be in the same Windows domain. If your Agent Server has a cluster partner that is on a DIFFERENT domain or on DIFFERENT sides of a router/switch, then ensure that you are using an explicit connection to connect to this remote Agent Server. See Agent Server Connection Methods . When naming the two Age

metadata.title: Important Points to consider when Clustering Agent Servers

text: in or on DIFFERENT sides of a router/switch, then ensure that you are using an explicit connection to connect to this remote Agent Server. See Agent Server Connection Methods . When naming the two Agent Servers that you want to be a clustered pair, if you have a preference for a specific Agent Server to act as master, then ensure that the name of this Agent Server is alphanumerically lower than the name of the Agent Server that will be the standby partner e.g. if the preferred master Agent Server is called AS1 then the standby Agent Server should be called AS2. Ensure that you configure both Agent Server processes, in an Adroit cluster, to have the same (identical) Windows security permissions. If using the Agent Server Service on one of both of your clustered Agent Servers, ensure that the user account under which the Agent Server Service is running has network access to the partner machine. IMPORTANT: It is NOT sufficient that a user logged in on the Agent Server can access the remote machine through explorer since this applies to his / her user account. Ensure that you DISABLE simplified file sharing on your clustered Agent Server computer, because this interferes with the inter

metadata.title: Important Points to consider when Clustering Agent Servers

text: e machine through explorer since this applies to his / her user account. Ensure that you DISABLE simplified file sharing on your clustered Agent Server computer, because this interferes with the inter-communication of clustered Agent Servers. For details, see Disabling Simplified File Sharing . Ensure that your chosen method of providing communication from Adroit to/from your PLCs or RTUs can support your desired clustering-scanning method. For details, see the following chart: Communication Hardware and Cluster Server I/O Modes . Adroit Clustering does not support the run-time creation of agents on both Agent Servers. Note: Certain agent types on a cluster server require synchronization of internal data structures with their master partner. For details, see Real-time Catch-up . It is recommended that identical copies of the agent database (.WGP) files are manually replicated on both clustered Agent Server computers. Click for more details: Typically Agent Server configuration is not shadowed across to the Standby computer, unless the agent database (.WGP) file used by both Agent Servers in the cluster is browsed in using the UNC file notation i.e. \\ComputerName\Drive\pathName. In

metadata.title: Important Points to consider when Clustering Agent Servers

text: hadowed across to the Standby computer, unless the agent database (.WGP) file used by both Agent Servers in the cluster is browsed in using the UNC file notation i.e. \\ComputerName\Drive\pathName. In this case this shared WGP file should not reside on either of the clustered Agent Server computers. But we do NOT RECOMMEND the use of a SHARED WGP file as this creates a potential single point of failure if the computer containing this WGP file fails OR if the network connection to this computer fails. Therefore we recommend that identical copies of the WGP files are manually copied between the clustered Agent Server computers and that Auto-Load Filename field of the Adroit Configuration Setup utility (PSEXE) is configured to point to the local copy of this WGP file. Tip: This provides the added benefit of being able to use the standby server for extending the WGP configuration, then once the user is happy that the extended configuration is working correctly, the standby WGP file can then be deployed on the master Agent Server computer. Ensure that you configure the following fundamental Agent Server settings for both of your clustered Agent Server partners, as follows: Using the Adroit Config Editor : Launch the Adroit Config Editor . Click Agent Server Configuration in the right hand pane. Click Agent Server Configuration again in the right hand pane. In the WGP (Auto-Load) File field, typically specify the local copy of the manually replicated agent database (.WGP) file [OTHERWISE specify the SHARED WGP file, specified using the UNC file notation i.e. \\ComputerName\Drive\pathName - which is NOT RECOMMENDED - see the relevant point above for details). In the Project Name field, specify the SAME name. In the Agent Server Name field, specify a DIFFERENT name. In the Agent Server Type field, select ‘Cluster Server’. Click the Options… button to the left of the Agent Server Type field (that is now selectable) to display the clustering-specific settings. In the Cluster Name field, specify the SAME cluster name Configure the desired Server master mode assignment strategy that is, either manual or automatic. Important TemplateGO properties Top Important TemplateGO properties Although a TemplateGO control appears to have the same properties as a standard graphic form, it also exposes the following additional properties: Note: These properties can be viewed and configured in the Properties tool window. Property / (Category) Function Autosize This Boolean property determines whether this control will automatically resize itself to display a graphic form, if this control is smaller than the graphic form that it contains. This is disabled (False) by default. AutoScroll This Boolean property either enables or disables scrollbars that appear if the control is smaller than the graphic form that it contains. This is disabled (False) by default. Note1: Its sub-properties determine how much smaller the graphic form needs to be before these scrollbars appear. Note2: By enabling the Autosize property this control will initially be resized to the size of the graphic form it contains, after which its size can be adjusted as necessary. Aliases This property exposes any specified aliases of the hosted graphic form (properties of its form components), so that values can be assigned to them, if required.

e can be adjusted as necessary. Aliases This property exposes any specified aliases of the hosted graphic form (properties of its form components), so that values can be assigned to them, if required. For details, see Working with aliases . AutoResize This Boolean property enables or disables the automatic resizing of the control to fit the size of the graphic form that it is hosting. This feature is disabled (False) by default. GraphicForm Although this property can be used to specify which graphic form is contained by this control it is not generally recommended because the specified graphic form will ONLY be loaded at runtime. In other words, the specified graphic from will ONLY be displayed when the graphic from containing the control is opened in Run mode or when using the Operator. This property also requires the required graphic form to be manually linked to it. For details on using this property, see Connecting TemplateGO controls to graphic forms . GraphicFormPath This is the generally recommended method of specifying which graphic form is contained by this control. Click on the provided browse button and browse in the graphic form that you want to contain within this cont

generally recommended method of specifying which graphic form is contained by this control. Click on the provided browse button and browse in the graphic form that you want to contain within this control. The specified graphic form will immediately be displayed in this control in the Design viewing mode, so that any further configuration can easily be performed. For details on using this property, see Connecting TemplateGO controls to graphic forms . MaxDepth Given that the TemplateGO is a control within a graphic form, that can contain a graphic form itself, it is possible for circular references to be created i.e. for this control to display its own graphic form. In this case, instead of opening an infinite number of graphic forms, this Integer property specifies the maximum number of instances of each graphic form that can be opened. For instance if MaxDepth is set to 2 and GraphicFormA contains TemplateGOControlA, which hosts GraphicFormB containing TemplateGOControlB, which hosts GraphicFormA – then 2 instances of GraphicFormA and 2 instances of GraphicFormB will be opened. Run This Boolean property is able to start and stop the spider engine (spider workspace), associated wit

GraphicFormA – then 2 instances of GraphicFormA and 2 instances of GraphicFormB will be opened. Run This Boolean property is able to start and stop the spider engine (spider workspace), associated with the graphic form that this control is hosting. By default, this is enabled (True) so that the spider workspace of the contained graphic form is started. Importing datasources Top Importing datasources Instead of manually duplicating a datasource from one SmartUI Server to another, you can export the datasource and its configuration to a file and then import this datasource into another SmartUI Server from this file. This is useful for datasources that have extensive configuration, such as OLE DB datasources with many configured queries and/or stored procedures. This can also be used to save time and ensure that clustered Servers have exactly the same datasource configuration. Improved Performance Top Improved Performance In Adroit data logging is a synchronous activity in that it is done internally on the same thread that creates the value change. Click for more details: For example, plant changes arrive into Adroit via one of the many scan threads. When a scan agent (or thread) has detected a value change, the thread updates the agent as well as any Agent Server clients interested in the information because of their subscription to this value. The datalog agent is one such client. Depending on the: size of the data log file speed of the hard disk available memory and other factors Writing the new value to disk (or to Window’s file caching subsystem) may take a long time. This affects the ability of the thread to timeously update the Agent Server with any other ‘real-time’ changes from the same scan transaction. Click for more details: For example, suppose 256 words of digital information changes every second, that is, 4096 discrete digital points changing per second. The scan agent must be able to effectively update every agent well within 240 uS per agent if it is going to be able to maintain the configured one-second-transaction rate. A sluggish data

per second. The scan agent must be able to effectively update every agent well within 240 uS per agent if it is going to be able to maintain the configured one-second-transaction rate. A sluggish data logging sub-system will definitely prevent this from happening. All changes arriving at the data logging subsystem are now added to a "datalog change queue". Click for more details: This mechanism is similar to the real-time update mechanism within Adroit , however; now the updates that occur because of historical logging requirements do not affect the throughput of the remaining real-time updates. This is a fast operation and releases the calling thread immediately. A separate, asynchronous thread reads the data from the queue and sends the change to the data logging mechanisms. From the above it is obvious that the size of the queue must be such that it is able to handle the maximum spike of changed values that a plant can expect. The maximum number of changes is generally proportional to the number of logged tags. This queue is global and has a default size of 500Kb, which allows for an approximate spike of 11000 changes. It is possible that the sustained (not the instantaneous) ra

to the number of logged tags. This queue is global and has a default size of 500Kb, which allows for an approximate spike of 11000 changes. It is possible that the sustained (not the instantaneous) rate of plant changes will exceed the rate at which the data logging subsystem is able to operate. Example: In this case, the Agent Server is simply not capable of handling the data logging requirement - the PC and/or its subsystems will require upgrading or the data logging task musts be split over separate Agent Servers. Tuning Parameters This data log system buffer queue size can be changed by clicking the Advanced button in the Datalog agent edit dialog , use the Datalog system buffer size (Kb) field to specify the required buffer queue size. It is recommended to use the buttons to increase/decrease this value in 64 KB increments/decrements. -->

Incident Icon colors Top Incident Icon colors The color of the incident icon indicates whether reasons and/or notes are required or not for this incident, as follows: The white icon means that no reasons or notes are required. The yellow icon means that ONLY reasons must be specified. The blue icon means that ONLY notes must be specified. The red icon means that BOTH reasons and notes must be specified. These colored icons indicate what the operator MUST specify for an incident before it is removed from the Adr_AM_CurrentIncidents table and is added to the Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents table. Note: Even though reasons and/or notes may not be required, they can still be specified. Example: Categories tree shows a hierarchical structure of the categories, while the top right-hand Incidents list displays all the incidents in the selected category and the bottom right-hand category/incident details list displays the selected category/ incident configuration. Note: The incident details list is disabled when more than one incident is selected. -->

Increasing Logging Periods Top Increasing Logging Periods When the logging period is increased when using the Adroit proprietary logging, ensure that the WGP file is saved and the Agent Server is restarted, at least once to allow the necessary LGD file compressions to occur, for the following reasons: Note: This is NOT required when reducing the logging period. When the logging period is increased: The datalog subsystem create new space at the end of the existing LGD file and copy all existing history to this new space. The datalog subsystem also marks the old space as unused. On the next startup of the Agent Server, all the LGD files that contain unused regions will be compressed out. -->

Increasing the virtual memory available to the Agent Server Top Increasing the virtual memory available to the Agent Server The Agent Server and Agent Server Service processes can use up to 3GB of virtual memory on 32 bit Windows XP and Server 2003 and up to 4GB on certain 64 bit operating systems. Previously, these processes were limited to only 2GB. This feature allows users to extend their WGP file configuration and is particularly useful when your current Agent Server process is approaching the 1.6GB virtual memory limit, as measured by Performance Monitor (NOT Task Manager!). Implementation on a 32 bit operating system: 32 bit operating systems have a maximum of 4GB of addressable memory space. By default, Windows allows only 2GB per process and uses the other 2GB for Windows itself. To change this default, you need to do the following: On 32 bit Windows Vista and later versions of Windows: Use the IncreaseUserVA element in BCDEdit . Click for more details: In other words specify the following command: BCDEdit /set [{ID}] increaseuserva Megabytes , where: The /set command sets a boot entry option value in the boot configuration data store. The {ID} is the GUID that is associat

text: the following command: BCDEdit /set [{ID}] increaseuserva Megabytes , where: The /set command sets a boot entry option value in the boot configuration data store. The {ID} is the GUID that is associated with the boot entry. If you do not specify an {ID}, the command modifies the current operating system boot entry. The increaseuserva Megabytes specifies the amount of memory, in megabytes, that is available per proceess. This variable can have any value between 2048 (2 GB) and 3072 (3 GB) megabytes in decimal notation. Windows uses the remaining address space (4 GB minus the specified amount). Using the full 3 GB for this option CAN potentially cause the Agent Server (and/or other Windows applications) not too work, if Windows requires MORE THAN 1GB for dealing with this process. For instance: if the configuration of the Agent Server is such that the size of network packets between Adroit client and server components are too large, then Windows requires more memory for itself to handle the networking layers. In these cases, limit the amount of additional memory available to the process and hence increase the amount of memory available to Windows. On 32 bit Windows Server 2003 and Wi

text: Incrementing numerical values Top Incrementing numerical values Increase a numerical input by a configurable amount. Note: This action is ONLY performed ONCE irrespective of how many times this spider is triggered, until its input values change or when the required Action Type changes. Tip: This action can change the current template set within the Template Set spider. For details, see Template Set spiders . To increase a numerical value by a specific amount If necessary, add and/or select the required Operator Action spider and/or open its configuration view. For details, see Adding Operator Action spiders . In the Inputs section: Open the Action Type list box and select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. Increment . Specify the numeric value on which this action is to be performed, in the Input Value input. Note1: This value can either be supplied by another spider or Data spider (e.g. property or data element) via a silk, for details, see Creating silks , or it can be typed in manually. Note2: Only Boolean or numerical values can be typed in. Tip: When typing in a value manually, double-click the value column to the

, for details, see Creating silks , or it can be typed in manually. Note2: Only Boolean or numerical values can be typed in. Tip: When typing in a value manually, double-click the value column to the right of the input name in the Inputs section and type in the required value. Specify the numeric value by which the Input Value is to be increased, in the Increment/Decrement Value input, either via a silk or by typing it in manually. When this spider is triggered, the value of the Input Value input is added to the Increment/Decrement Value input value and this result is assigned to the Output Value output in Outputs section. For details on triggering spiders, see Triggering spiders . Note1: The Boolean Value output in Outputs section, contains the Boolean equivalent of this Output Value output i.e. FALSE when it is zero, otherwise TRUE. Note2: This operation is only performed if the Input Value and Increment/Decrement Value inputs contain numerical / Boolean values. Note3: If a String value is supplied then the spider will try to convert the string value to a number before using it. If it cannot be converted, the input is meaningless and will not be used. -->

Indicators Top Indicators An indicator graphically indicates the value of the associated process variable without actually displaying its value. Analogue Indicators Purpose: to graphically indicate the current value of an analogue (floating point) process variable (PV), by means of a sliding pointer along a horizontal or vertical range defined by the currently specified Maximum and Minimum engineering span of this Analogue process variable, while also indicating its currently specified normal operating range. Description: A horizontal or vertical rectangle, whereby: the normal operating range (the values between the High and Low alarm limits) is filled in light blue and the minimum and maximum allowable range (the values between the High High and the High and the Low Low and the Low alarm limits) are filled in dark grey and the minimum and maximum extremes (the values between the Engineering Maximum and the High High alarm limit and the Engineering Minimum and Low Low alarm limit) are filled in black and the current value is indicated by means of dark blue triangle sliding pointer and ONLY if the statsPeriod slot of the Analog agent representing this process variable is configured,

filled in black and the current value is indicated by means of dark blue triangle sliding pointer and ONLY if the statsPeriod slot of the Analog agent representing this process variable is configured, then a directional arrow may also be displayed indicating the current direction of trend i.e. an arrow pointing up when the value is going up or another arrow pointing down when the value is going down or no arrow at all when the value is stable. For more details, see Calculating statistics from Analog values . PLEASE NOTE: This direction of trend is ONLY calculated by the Analog agent representing the process variable, when its statsPeriod slot is set to the required sampling period, we recommend a value of 10 (minutes), since the default value of 0 DISABLES the calculation of these statistics, since if used excessively they can affect performance. Tip: You can also configure the optional statsDirDev slot specify an optional minimum deviation or deadband to ensure that this trending direction only indicates significant changes in value (we recommend setting this value to 0.05). ction only indicates significant changes in value (we recommend setting this value to 0.05). The following analogue indicators are available: Horizontal analogue indicators, where the minimum range is on the left and the maximum range is on the right and the sliding pointer is on the bottom, in the following sizes: wzdAnalogueIndicator_Small_Horizontal_v01: a small horizontal analogue indicator wzdAnalogueIndicator_Medium_Horizontal_v01: a medium horizontal analogue indicator wzdAnalogueIndicator_Large_Horizontal_v01: a large horizontal analogue indicator Vertical analogue indications, where the minimum range is on the bottom and the maximum range is on the top and the sliding pointer is on the right, in the following sizes: wzdAnalogueIndicator_Small_Vertical_v01: a small vertical analogue indicator wzdAnalogueIndicator_Medium_Vertical_v01: a medium vertical analogue indicator wzdAnalogueIndicator_Large_Vertical_v01: a large vertical analogue indicator Required values: Note: When this wizard is added to a graphic form, all these values are MANDATORY and therefore must ALL be specified. Installing a Protocol Driver Top Installing a Protocol Driver Launch the Adroit Config Editor . Click Agent Server Configuration in the right hand pane. Click Driver Configuration in the right hand pane. Click the Install new driver button. This displays the DriverInstallList dialog to allow new protocol drivers to be installed, by creating a list of available Adroit drivers from the installation path or the previously specified path. If the Adroit driver setup files cannot be found in the installation or previously specified path, then click the browse button to manually locate the disk or folder containing the protocol drivers. Click the name of the driver ( ) to install. This copies the associated driver files into the Adroit system folder and opens the associated driver documentation. PLEASE NOTE: Read this driver documentation carefully, as it specifies which devices are supported, how to configure the driver, how to scan using the driver, diagnostic tips and any relevant protocol information. -->

Installing Internet Information Services Top Installing Internet Information Services The SmartUI Web Service and Click Once requires Microsoft Internet Information Services (IIS) to be installed. For details, see Installing the SmartUI Web Service or Working with Click Once . When using a Windows desktop operating systems, such as Windows 7, it may be necessary to install IIS as it is not part of the default installation. However, when using a Server operating system IIS is installed by default. To install IIS on Windows 7: IMPORTANT: Simply selecting IIS is NOT enough on Windows 7 - you need to manually check ALL the ALL of the sub-components of its Application Development Features component. Note: Ensure that the Windows system files are located in the same location as when the operating system was installed, for instance, if having installed from the local drive ensure that the Windows installation media is in this drive. Select the Start menu, Control Panel and Programs and Features item. Select the Turn Windows features on or off link, on the left side of this applet. This will display the Windows Features dialog. Click the checkbox to the left of the Internet Information Ser

es item. Select the Turn Windows features on or off link, on the left side of this applet. This will display the Windows Features dialog. Click the checkbox to the left of the Internet Information Services component. This only selects some of its components by default - indicated by a filled checkbox. Double click the Internet Information Services component to expand its options. Expand the World Wide Web Services option. Expand its Application Development Features option. Ensure that there is a tick box next to ALL of the sub-components of this Application Development Features component. Tip: Once all the sub-components are ticked, a tick appears next to the Application Development Features component. Example Click the OK button to install this component. Close the open dialog boxes. To install IIS on Windows XP: Note: Ensure that the Windows system files are located in the same location as when the operating system was installed, for instance, if having installed from the local drive ensure that the Windows installation media is in this drive. Select the Start menu, Settings , Control Panel and Add or Remove Programs item. This will display the Add or Remove Programs applet. Sele

ensure that the Windows installation media is in this drive. Select the Start menu, Settings , Control Panel and Add or Remove Programs item. This will display the Add or Remove Programs applet. Select the Add or Remove Windows Components button, on the left side of this applet. This will display the Windows Components Wizard dialog. In the Windows Components Wizard dialog, scroll down until the Internet Information Service (IIS) component is visible. Click the tick box next to the Internet Information Service (IIS) component. Note: Ensure that there is a tick in this tick box. Example Click the Next button to install this component. Click the Finish button to close the Windows Components Wizard dialog and also close the Add or Remove Programs applet. -->

For details on using this application, see Working with the SmartUI Launcher . By default, this installation does not require the user to have Administrative rights. WARNING! This installation does NOT install the files required for the SmartUI Operator itself. Note1: Ensure that the computer complies with the software and hardware requirements for the Operator. ose all programs. Open the required web browsing application and type in the required address that specifies the SmartUI Web Service of the required Server. Installing WanServer as a Service Top Installing WanServer as a Service The WanServer can run either as a standard Application or as a Service within Windows. The advantage of running this as a Service is that then the WanServer does not shutdown when the current user logs off. Instrumentation equipment templates Top Working with Instrumentation equipment templates In MAPS each piece of instrumentation equipment requires an associated template. text: INTRAC : INTRAC 2000 INTRAC 2000 driver Overview The INTRAC 2000 protocol for Adroit communicates to a INTRAC 2000 Central Interface Unit (CIU) via a serial rs232 port that receives data from remote outstations. The protocol allows both polling for data as well as receiving data on exception (i.e. data is received asynchronously when a value changes at an outstation). Protocol Manufacturer Motorola. Wiring No Intrac CIU (25 pin RS-232C male) Computer Interface (25 pin RS-232C female) 1 2 - Transmit 2 - Receive 2 3 – Receive 3 – Transmit 3 7 – Signal Ground 7 – Signal Ground Driver Installation and Setup The driver is installed by picking the INTRAC driver from the drivers directory. The INTRAC.DLL and the INTRAC.DOC are then copied into the Adroit directory. After installation of the driver, the user may then create and configure devices for the INTRAC driver. Printed 1 INTRAC : INTRAC 2000 Device Configuration Devices At a minimum, you must create at least one device for every port being used. However, you may choose to create a device for a group of transmitters. Device configuration dialog Port Select the port through which you are going to communicate. Baud Rate The baud can be

ing used. However, you may choose to create a device for a group of transmitters. Device configuration dialog Port Select the port through which you are going to communicate. Baud Rate The baud can be selected. Other parameters are fixed at the standard rate of 7 data, 1 stop, and odd parity. Timeout This field gives the waiting time if not end of message is received once a start of message is received. It is recommended that this value be kept at 1000. Moxa Cluster Support Check this option when running on a MOXA virtual port in a cluster environment. It will allow to purge the port when in standby and in shadow mode, as the MOXA unit stops functioning in this mode. Data keeps filling the buffer seeing that the driver does not do any reading from the port and eventually becomes unresponsive! Hard Purge Does a call to the COM PORT to purge all the data on it. (Preferred Method) Soft Purge Continue to read data from the port and just discard it. Close serial port on fail With a transaction failure closes the port and re-opens it by default but for some virtual ports it becomes an issue so we allow not closing the port in this case. Printed 2 INTRAC : INTRAC 2000 Download & Driver Pa

ion failure closes the port and re-opens it by default but for some virtual ports it becomes an issue so we allow not closing the port in this case. Printed 2 INTRAC : INTRAC 2000 Download & Driver Parameters These Download parameters are explained in the appendix. Driver Parameters Interrogate on Startup – All outstations are interrogated on agent server load. Hot Standby – The driver does not send any data to outstations but only receives data and updates its database. This parameter can be toggled by using system tag number 9. Delay Between AI’s – To slow AI’s down – not really required since driver only polls after a RI is received. Acknowledge Delay – An AA message is sent only after this specified delay , so that more than 1 group can be acknowledged at once. Printed 3 INTRAC : INTRAC 2000 Scanning System Tags is: SY: B Where: SY – System. B – Bit number (0 - 15) Boolean Support Only These bits represent the following: (Configure Pulsed Items – these bits must be configured as pulsed items as they indicate the condition on a raising edge) Bit 0 - 'BS' Radio channel busy. - Configure Pulsed Bit 1 - 'CB' Check back (indication only). - Configure Pulsed Bit 2 - 'OF' Overflow ala

lsed items as they indicate the condition on a raising edge) Bit 0 - 'BS' Radio channel busy. - Configure Pulsed Bit 1 - 'CB' Check back (indication only). - Configure Pulsed Bit 2 - 'OF' Overflow alarm. Any other message received will clear this bit. It is like a NAK NAK message - Configure Pulsed Bit 3 - 'RS' Request for restart for CIU. - Configure Pulsed Bit 4 - 'CM' Channel monitor received. - Configure Pulsed Bit 5 - 'TX' received after a control. Bit 6 - 'RI' request interrogation received. Bit 7 - The CIU is OFF LINE, no CK for 5 minutes. Bit 8 - Forced CIU download. - Configure Pulsed Bit 9 - Hot Standby Toggle. - Configure Pulsed Bit 10 - Force AI even if RI not received (RI outstanding reset)- Configure Pulsed Bit 11 - Force DW even if TX not received (TX outstanding reset)- Configure Pulsed Bit 12 – 15 - Unused Outstation Status Tags: OS: St: Gr: [B:] AI Where: OS – Outstation. St – Outstation Number Gr – Group/s A , BCH , CD , ABCDEFTGH, etc B – Bit number (0 – 15) AI – Auto Interrogation rate in minutes, 0 time disables auto interrogation. Boolean & Integer Support (Multi State). Bit 0 - AC power failure Bit 1 – Group A communication failure Bit 2 - Group B communicat

to Interrogation rate in minutes, 0 time disables auto interrogation. Boolean & Integer Support (Multi State). Bit 0 - AC power failure Bit 1 – Group A communication failure Bit 2 - Group B communication failure Bit 3 - Group C communication failure Printed 4 INTRAC : INTRAC 2000 Bit 4 - Group D communication failure Bit 5 - Group E communication failure Bit 6 - Group F communication failure Bit 7 - Group G communication failure Bit 8 - Group H communication failure Bit 9 – Manual Poll does Auto Interrogate on demand. (Tag must be output enabled) Bit 10 – 15 – Unused. Group Data Tags: GD: St: Gr: [B] [T] Where: GD – Group Data St – Outstation Number Gr – Group A,B,C,D,E,F,G or H B – Bit number – 0- 7 T – Analogue type N or C Boolean, Integer and Real Support. For digital tags a maximum of 8 scan points from a Group can be scanned. For analogues a group can be scanned in as either Normal(N) or as a Counter(C). Scanning of integers made of 2 groups is to be scanned individually and calculated using an expression agent. Digital Ouput Tags: DO: St: Gr: [B] [T] Where: DO – Digital Output St – Outstation Number Gr – Group A,B,C,D,E,F,G or H B – Bit number T – Digital Output type – SM,SL,

lated using an expression agent. Digital Ouput Tags: DO: St: Gr: [B] [T] Where: DO – Digital Output St – Outstation Number Gr – Group A,B,C,D,E,F,G or H B – Bit number T – Digital Output type – SM,SL,PN or PR SM - Single Momentary : the outputs to be toggled are set to 1 and the rest of the bits to 0. These bits are to be configured as pulsed items. The output is only triggered on a rising edge. 8 bits are used for every group. SL - Single Latched : a latched command ,the outputs to be set on are set to 1 and the outputs to be reset are set to 0. After the transaction the bits remains in their respective states. Outputs are sent both on rising and falling edges.8 bits are used for every group. PN - Paired Normal : If a bit is set, the data transmitted is a 1 and 0 ,and a bit is reset the data transmitted is a 0 and 1. 4 bits are used for every group. PR - Paired Reverse : If a bit is set, the data transmitted is a 0 and 1 ,and if a bit is reset the data transmitted is a 1 and 0. Printed 5 INTRAC : INTRAC 2000 Analogue Ouput Tags: AO: St: Gr: [B] [T] Where: AO – Analogue Output St – Outstation Number Gr – Group A,B,C,D,E,F,G or H Integer and Real Support. Message protocol Datascope

d 5 INTRAC : INTRAC 2000 Analogue Ouput Tags: AO: St: Gr: [B] [T] Where: AO – Analogue Output St – Outstation Number Gr – Group A,B,C,D,E,F,G or H Integer and Real Support. Message protocol Datascope messages are displayed in hex or ASCII. All messages are displayed whether that transmitter is configured or not. Messages of devices not configured are displayed in the first devices protocol monitor. The INTRAC protocol is ASCII. The structure of transactions is as follows: Read analogue/digital Inputs Auto Interrogate: <STX><AI><ADR><AG><RG><ETX><CS><CR><LF> CIU reply’s <STX><AN><ADR><G><DAT><ETX><CS><CR><LF> Auto Acknowledge: (Auto Acknowledge once requested groups data arrives) <STX><AA><ADR><RG><ETX><CS><CR><LF> (Acknowledge Messages) <ACK><ACK><CR><LF> <NACK><NACK><CR><LF> Direct Word - Outputs: <STX><DW><ADR><G><DAT><ETX><CS><CR><LF> (Download parameters Px where x is 1,2,3,4,5) Printed 6 INTRAC : INTRAC 2000 <STX><PP><DAT><DAT><DAT><DAT><ETX><CS><CR><LF> CIU reply’s (Acknowledge Messages) <ACK><ACK><CR><LF> <NACK><NACK><CR><LF> (Spontaneous Data) <STX><DT><ADR><G><DAT><ETX><CS><CR><LF> (Failed Groups on Interrogate) <STX><FL><ADR><AG><ETX><CS><CR><LF> (Busy/Check/OverFlow/Requ

The CIU can address up to 512 stations out of a total of 2048 different remote stations in an INTRAC 2000 system. The parameter determines the number of systems among which the 2048 remote stations are to be allocated. If 1-4 systems are being used, the value “4” is assigned to this parameter, i.e. maximum 512 stations per system. If 5-8 systems are used, the value “8” is assigned, i.e. maximum 256 stations per system. If 9-16 systems are used, the value “16” is assigned, i.e. maximum 128 stations per system. System Address (0-3 or 0-7 or 0-15). Default value 0. Each system assigned to a CIU requires an identification address between 0 and 3. If 2-4 systems are being used, each system must be assigned a separate address between 0 and 3. If 5-8 systems are being used, each system must be assigned a separate address between 0 and 7. If 9-16 systems are being used, each system must be assigned a separate address between 0 and 15. Introduction Top General Description Many Adroit users have various complex devices that contain one or more value properties. Ordinarily, in order for users to represent these complex devices, multiple instances of analog, digital or other common agent types, would be used to represent a single device. For example, your process may make use of a particular drive type; let’s call it Drive Type XYZ. Multiple drives of this type exist in your process. This drive type has a couple of properties, for example Start, Stop, Running, Tripped, Speed and Temperature, requiring each of these values to be mapped to four digital and two analog agents respectively, therefore 10 of these drives would mean 60 agents. Would it not be better to use a single agent representing a complete drive and containing the 6 items of information in 6 slots of the agent, so that, in this example only 10 agents would need to be used instead of 60? The Custom agent, has been designed to do just this, it is a generic agent type used to create user-defined agent types, by means of the Custom Agent Designer, and must not be used in its generic format. But in addition to representing, simple "container" agents, which

gent type used to create user-defined agent types, by means of the Custom Agent Designer, and must not be used in its generic format. But in addition to representing, simple "container" agents, which simply contain or encapsulate the values of a number of previous agents in a single user-defined agent, the Custom agent is also able to provide VB Scripting (or Java Scripting) intelligence to the agent to drive (control) other derived slots of this custom agent. For example, we can add an extra slot to this agent for defining a high temperature alarm value. The script would monitor the actual temperature such that when the temperature exceeds this value a status bit is set for alarming purposes. We can also set a Trip status bit when the Tripped signal is switched on. Furthermore, we can also disable the drive from starting if the temperature is too high. Note: Any derived Custom agent, containing a Script engine, will require a scan point license. Tip: Custom agents created via the Custom Agent Designer that require scripting intelligence now provides support for JavaScript (.jav file) or you can choose to use the existing VBScript (.vbs file). This drive type XYZ example will be us

om Agent Designer that require scripting intelligence now provides support for JavaScript (.jav file) or you can choose to use the existing VBScript (.vbs file). This drive type XYZ example will be used to explain the process of creating a user-defined agent using the Custom Agent Designer. The user-defined agent, created by the Custom Agent Designer, is known as a custom derived agent and will have the following three files associated with it: t_CustomDerivedAgentName.dll t_CustomDerivedAgentName.csv t_CustomDerivedAgentName.vbs / t_CustomDerivedAgentName.jav Note: This file is only required if this custom derived agent has scripting intelligence. Where, CustomDerivedAgentName suitably describes this agent type and is not the same as an existing agent name. Related links How to Use the Custom Agent Designer Custom Agent Usage Guidelines -->

Introduction to spiders and silks Top Introduction to spiders and silks Spiders and silks are essentially a visual programming language, which can transfer and/or manipulate data, typically by means of drag and drop. Spiders communicate and/or manipulate data from a set of inputs to a set of outputs, when they are triggered. A list of available spiders . Silks connect spiders together and can be grouped into template sets, which control how data is transferred between spiders. Spiders, silks and template sets are configured using a spider workspace, which can either be run on the Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. or the Server, depending upon their required application. For further details, see Working with spider workspaces . Note: The spider workspace is actually a spider engine as it has both a running and a stopped state. The transfer and/or manipulation of data can only occur while the spider workspace or spider engine is running. Although the potential use and areas of application for spiders are diverse, spiders and silks are primarily used to animate graphic forms by connecting data to the properties o

der engine is running. Although the potential use and areas of application for spiders are diverse, spiders and silks are primarily used to animate graphic forms by connecting data to the properties of graphic forms and their form components, which occurs on the Client. Click for more details: By using spiders, it is possible to provide a rich interactive environment for the end-user of a graphic form, without necessarily needing to write any scripting at all. This is provided, in part, by the ability of spiders to be operated or triggered by means of events or actions either performed by another spider or performed by a user on a control attached to the graphic form. In this way users are able to perform custom and/or complicated manipulation of data elements, literally at the touch of a button or a click of a checkbox etc. For details, see Animating graphic forms . Spiders are either added manually or automatically during the process of creating silks. Silks are created by dragging, as follows: You can either drag from an item in the explorer tree(s), which border the spider workspace or from a spider. You are then able to drag to either another item in an explorer tree or to ano

as follows: You can either drag from an item in the explorer tree(s), which border the spider workspace or from a spider. You are then able to drag to either another item in an explorer tree or to another spider. -->

To toggle the Boolean state of a numerical value If necessary, add and/or select the required Operator Action spider and/or open its configuration view. For details, see Adding Operator Action spiders . In the Inputs section: Open the Action Type list box and select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. Toggle Boolean . Specify the numeric value on which this action is to be performed, in the Input Value input. Note1: This value can either be supplied by another spider or Data spider (e.g. property or data element) via a silk, for details, see Creating silks , or it can be typed in manually. Note2: Only Boolean or numerical values can be typed in. text: IO Flags Top IO Flags In an effort to simplify the scanning configuration, the following legacy status slots that used to affect how a slot (value) was scanned: Scan Inhibit, Output Enable and Output Initialise are no longer stored in the header of the each agent for each of its slots. Note: The advanced header dialog no longer displays these statuses and putslots to these status bits are also disabled. Instead these settings are now stored in the scanning configuration of the Device agent in the Agent Database (.wgp) file along with the other scanning related settings, such as the scan address, scan rate etc, as an IO flags setting. Hence the Tag Scanning Configuration dialog contains an IO flags column in the list of scanned tags. Note: There is no slot that contains these IO flags, since they are now stored in the tag list of scanned values of a Device agent. When loading a Agent Database (.wgp) file from a previous version of Adroit, Adroit 10 uses the saved status bit information to configure the IO flags setting of all the Device agents and when the Agent Database (.wgp) file is saved then these status bits are switched OFF in the Agent Database (.wgp) file. Therefore Adroit

to configure the IO flags setting of all the Device agents and when the Agent Database (.wgp) file is saved then these status bits are switched OFF in the Agent Database (.wgp) file. Therefore Adroit 10 Agent Database (.wgp) file are NOT backwardly compatible! IMPORTANT: When starting the Adroit 10 Agent Server for the first time and loading a Agent Database (.wgp) file from a previous version, devices will most likely NEVER show healthy once all the devices are started. You need to save the Agent Database (.wgp) file FIRST and then restart the Agent Server and then you should see all the devices going healthy. The IO flags setting is a bit mask as follows: Value Bit Description Default 1 0 Input disabled ON supercedes the legacy statusScanInhibit flag at the agent and slot level. Any legacy WGP file that has the statusScanInhibit flag set, will force Bit 0 OFF. Note1: This setting is the INVERSE of the Input disabled (Scan inhibited) checkbox, when scanning a tag. Note2: You can still use the statusScanInhibit header slot of an agent to prevent any configured scanning of the agent from occurring. 2 1 Output enabled OFF supercedes the legacy statusOutputEnable flag at the agent and

use the statusScanInhibit header slot of an agent to prevent any configured scanning of the agent from occurring. 2 1 Output enabled OFF supercedes the legacy statusOutputEnable flag at the agent and slot level. Any legacy WGP file that has the statusOutputEnable flag set, will force Bit 1 ON. Note: This setting is enabled by checking the Output enabled checkbox, when scanning a tag. 4 2 Output initialise OFF supercedes the legacy statusScanInitialise flag at the agent and slot level. Any legacy WGP file that has the statusScanInitialise flag set, will force Bit 2 ON. If this bit is set, an initial value will be scanned out from the agent at startup, or after any communications failure and subsequent recovery. Note: This setting is enabled by checking the Output initialise checkbox, when scanning a tag. 8 3 Demand scan OFF New functionality – requires that the global configuration for demand scanning is enabled and that the currently selected device driver type supports demand scanning. The IO flags setting is a sum of the values whose associated bit is ON. So for a newly scanned tag, the default of bit 0 (enable reads) applies, in which case IO flags is 1. If bit 0 (enable reads)

g. The IO flags setting is a sum of the values whose associated bit is ON. So for a newly scanned tag, the default of bit 0 (enable reads) applies, in which case IO flags is 1. If bit 0 (enable reads) and 2 (output initialise) are ON then the IO flags is 5 (1 + 4). For more details on demand scanning, see Demand Scanning . -->

IPEnableHeartbeat Top IPEnableHeartbeat WARNING: Registry settings are recorded as ADVANCED information and should not be used unless you understand exactly how these will affect the operation of your Adroit installation, IF YOU HAVE ANY DOUBTS, PLEASE CONTACT Adroit SUPPORT, BEFORE CHANGING THE REGISTRY. When using sockets as the communication mechanism between the Agent Server and its clients, the socket heartbeats will always occur, as clients will PING the Agent Server every 10 seconds. ISO Shapes Top ISO Shapes ISO symbols are recommended to represent your common plant equipment to promote pattern recognition, since these simple obvious shapes are easy to recognise immediately without needing any labeling. Also any labeling that is added for your plant equipment should not be intrusive (highly visible) as they only serve to distract your operators from other more important information. IMPORTANT: Move away from labeling every item of equipment with their tag names or point IDs as these are NOT important and only add unnecessary visual clutter and . Furthermore muted colors should ideally be used by these plant equipment representations to indicate whether they are started or stopped. Previously it was common to use green to indicate the started state and red to indicate the stopped state. While these colors were visually appealing they only served to increase the mental fatigue of the operators and especially the red stopped state would distract them any alarm conditions that they actually do need to pay immediate attention to. Issues related to using Remote Desktop to Run Adroit Top Issues related to using Terminal Clients (Remote Desktop) to Run Adroit Problems running the Agent Server You cannot start the Agent Server as an application by using the Windows Remote Desktop (a terminal client). This is because Windows does not support USB ports when you use the Remote Desktop application, so any USB HASP is effectively invisible to the Agent Server. Note: This is not a problem when starting the Agent Server as a service from within a Remote Desktop. The resources (e.g. printer etc) of the computer used to remote desktop into the Agent Server computer are used by the Agent Server NOT the resources on the Agent Server's computer. This means that when you terminate the remote desktop session, these resources become unavailable which causes problems. Problems running Adroit Client Applications Adroit has terminal client (remote desktop) connection licencing rules whereby every Adroit client application takes a (remote node) connection licence regardless. An Adroit client is ANY application that makes a connection to an Agent Server, for instance: Classic User Interface Agent Configurator Adroit utilities, suc

text: emote node) connection licence regardless. An Adroit client is ANY application that makes a connection to an Agent Server, for instance: Classic User Interface Agent Configurator Adroit utilities, such as the Agent Browser Any Adroit OLE Automation (MISSRVR) or ActiveX client application. If the Classic User Interface is started from within a remote deskop session, and the Configurator is opened – then TWO connection licenses are required; otherwise either the Configurator and/or UI will be unable to connect to the Agent Server. Since BOTH the UI and the Configurator require their OWN connection licences when started using remote desktop. This change ALSO prevents the use of remote desktop for perform maintenance especially on stand-alone (no remote connection licences) installations. Since UIs cannot be restarted via Remote Desktop and/or the Configurator is unable to connect to the Agent Server. For this reason, Adroit has attempted to redress this limitation by NOT enforcing connection licences for the console user’s session. Large Scalable Agent Server Networks Top Large Scalable Agent Server Networks This network configuration typically contains a large number of Agent Servers that are required to share information as if they were part of the same project so that any one Agent Server can directly gain access to any of the other Agent Server. However, maintaining a grid of fully connected Agent Servers can potentially be resource intensive, for the following reasons: Many Agent Servers within a network all broadcasting their presence - many IT administrators do not like this. Many Agent Servers within a network all on the same project causing large agent tables to be transmitted in a "one to many" relationship. Large agent tables are generally created when agents are added or deleted. Note: This is a problem for slower (10MB, WLAN) networks where bandwidth was at a premium especially if the network is not dedicated to SCADA operations. However, 100MB networks handle this easily. In this case, we recommend that you use the method, in which you can divide these Agent Servers into their own projects (or have each Agent Server in its own project if necessary), then use the list method for connecting these

that you use the method, in which you can divide these Agent Servers into their own projects (or have each Agent Server in its own project if necessary), then use the list method for connecting these Agent Servers and/or projects together. For further details of this and the other methods of connecting Agent Servers together, see Agent Server Connection Methods . If these Agent Servers are in different domains then you need to use explicit Agent Server connections. Click for details: For instance, consider this situation in which each section in a plant has its own Agent Server and its own local Classic UI and where all of these plant section Agent Servers are connected to a central gateway computer (known as a proxy server ), which also has its own local (or remote) Classic UIs. In this case The central gateway computer requires explicit Agent Server connections to be created for each of the plant section Agent Servers. Each plant section Agent Server, will only require explicit Agent Server connections to those servers from which data is required i.e. if its local Classic UI refer to tags, which are located on other plant section Agent Servers. Diagram Key The central gateway com

Server connections to those servers from which data is required i.e. if its local Classic UI refer to tags, which are located on other plant section Agent Servers. Diagram Key The central gateway computer = the grey circle. Each plant section Agent Server = a clear circle. -->

The Welcome section is displayed by default, unless multiple configurations have been created, in which case the Configuration page is displayed by default, which needs to be expanded to display the Welcome section. For details, see Working with Configurations. Select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the Setting up the Launcher option. Select the Connection Settings option. Tip1: You can navigate directly to this page using the left pane of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog. For details, see Working with configuration dialogs. Tip2: Press the Next or Previous buttons to display the other pages of settings. This page is divided into the following three sections: The type of network used to connect the Distribution computer

Tip2: Press the Next or Previous buttons to display the other pages of settings. This page is divided into the following three sections: The type of network used to connect the Distribution computer to your clients. The network identification and login to the Distribution computer. Additional configuration options and the Apply button that creates the customized Launcher executable. You can either connect to the Web Service using: LAN or WAN Internet, if this is selected then you can specify the required proxy server settings, as follows: Check the Enable Proxy checkbox. Then either specify the Machine Name or IP address and Port used by your proxy server. If necessary, provide the required User and Password for your Proxy Authentication Details . Specify the name of the required Computer name or the URL required to connect to the Web Service: If necessary, provide the required User and Password for your Authentication Details for this computer. Tip: Click the Test Connection button to check that you are able to connect to this computer using the specified information. If necessary, the Launcher installation can prompt for its required extraction path, by default this is: C:\Progr

o check that you are able to connect to this computer using the specified information. If necessary, the Launcher installation can prompt for its required extraction path, by default this is: C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI If necessary, you can automatically run the Launcher after extraction - by default this option is checked. Click the Apply button to create your customized Smart UI Launcher executable, which is called VIP Launcher Setup.exe and is created in the Smart UI Web Service installation folder ( C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI\Webservice ). -->

Launching Alternatives Top Launching Alternatives Certain applications (including utilities) support command-line parameters, which allow various configuration settings to be performed as soon as the application is launched. A number of alternatives are available when launching an application with command-line parameter(s), the correct one to use depends upon the required frequency of using the same command-line parameters: Infrequent or once-only use: In this case it is recommended to launch the application using the Run dialog. For details, see Using the Same Command-line Options Infrequently . Frequent use: In this case it is recommended to create another shortcut for this application, especially if it is necessary to launch the required program with more than one command-line parameters configuration. For details, see Using the Same Command-line Options Frequently . Permanent use: In this case it is recommended to modify the installation shortcut for this application itself. For details, see Using the Same Command-line Options Permanently . -->

Launching Wanlink Components Top Launching Wanlink Components Wanlink components are installed into the Adroit folder as part of the complete Adroit installation, alternatively its WanClient and WanServer components can be selectively installed during a custom installation. Note: Only one WanClient and WanServer can be launched on a computer. If there is an already an existing WanClient or WanServer running on a computer, then if either program is run again, a warning will appear reminding the user than only one instance of each application is allowed. Tip: Both the WanClient and WanServer applications can be started before the Agent Servers have started. Therefore once the Agent Servers are started/restarted the applications will resume communications as expected. Press the Windows key and start typing in the required application name and select it from the list, in this case: Adroit Wanlink Client , this launches the WanClient application. Adroit Wanlink Client Auto-start , this launches the WanClient application, with the "/start" command-line parameter, so that it automatically starts its communication process . Adroit Wanlink Server , this launches the WanServer . Note: If the

ches the WanClient application, with the "/start" command-line parameter, so that it automatically starts its communication process . Adroit Wanlink Server , this launches the WanServer . Note: If the WanServer is started with the " /p:nnn" command-line parameter, then it will be able to change the port on which the server is to operate (default 51114). Where nnn specifies the required port. To specify the port on which the Wanlink Server is to operate, the following DWORD registry value is provided: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\WanlinkServerPort (default value 51114). This setting can also be overridden with the /p:nnnn command-line parameter. If the /persist command-line parameter is used the /p:nnnnn value will be saved to the registry. Adroit Wanlink Server Service Setup , this launches the Wanlink Server Service Setup . This also supports the Wanlink Server command line parameters when this service is started e.g. net start adrwanwerver /p:51115. For details of these components, see Wanlink components . -->

Laying out controls in a TableLayoutPanel Top Laying out controls in a TableLayoutPanel Each control that is added to a TableLayoutPanel becomes a child control that inherits several additional properties, which when used together with its existing properties can assist in its layout within this table, as follows: Note: The TableLayoutPanel provides a number of properties that can be used for designing its layout. For details, see Important TableLayoutPanel properties . Tip: Being a table, this TableLayoutPanel control can easily expand, by adding additional rows and/or columns to accommodate new controls, without you needing to manually re-configure the alignment of the other controls. Stretching and aligning controls You can use the Anchor property of the control to align to a particular side (e.g. Left will stick it to the Left side). Using opposing anchors, the control can be stretched. E.g. Anchor=Left|Right will stretch to fill the width. The Dock property works in a similar manner.
