Licensing methods Top Available SmartUI Licensing methods The SmartUI Server can be licensed by one of the following methods , which are listed in the ORDER that the Server LOOKS for its license: Note1: The license for the FIRST licensing method that is detected is used to license the SmartUI Server Note2: ONLY when NONE of these licensing methods are found, does the SmartUI Server considers itself NOT to be licensed. HASP license: In this case, the SmartUI Server is licensed by a HASP software protection key, which is inserted into the USB port of the computer on which the Server is running. This HASP is programmed in accordance with your specific license agreement. Click for more details: The Server continuously checks that the HASP key is present. If the HASP key cannot be found after 3 retries (which are logged to the Application event log) the Server shuts down displaying a 'HASP cannot be found' message. WARNING! If this HASP key is lost, the cost of replacement is the current full value of the corresponding license fee. We recommend, therefore, that you consider insuring this item against loss or theft. Note1: If the licence is updated or modified then the HASP key must be r

ll value of the corresponding license fee. We recommend, therefore, that you consider insuring this item against loss or theft. Note1: If the licence is updated or modified then the HASP key must be reprogrammed to reflect the changes. Note2: You can use the SAME HASP to license BOTH Adroit and SmartUI , however, this requires a 4K “green” USB HASP. Advantage: The MAIN advantage of this licensing method is PORTABILITY, as unlike a soft license which is bound to a specific computer, you can install and use the Server ANY computer provided that you plug your HASP into one of its USB ports. Soft license: In this case, the SmartUI Server is licensed by a software license to a SINGLE computer and only remains valid while certain hardware and software or system characteristics of this computer remain unchanged. Limited Time License HASP Top Limited Time License HASP IMPORTANT: When a HASP is not detected when the Agent Server is started and the Agent Server is not being otherwise licensed, then the Agent Server will automatically run in limited time license mode. Use the limited time license HASP if the Agent Server is not currently licensed. This runs the Agent Server with a 120 minute operating license with 20000 scan points and 2 remote connections. When this period of time ends, the scanning of devices will stop and any remote server connections will be lost and not reconnected. Typically this can be launched from the Adroit Start menu by clicking on the Start menu, Programs , Adroit 10 , and clicking the Adroit Agent Server (timed license) item. Although it is also possible to launch the Agent Server with the following command line parameter: –demo e.g. C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit \as.exe –demo There are message boxes and event log entries explaining these important events. Also the HASP agent provides the following status bits that indicate events relating to the use of this mode of licensing the Agent Server: TimedLicence : ON when the Agent Server is running in tim

s. Also the HASP agent provides the following status bits that indicate events relating to the use of this mode of licensing the Agent Server: TimedLicence : ON when the Agent Server is running in time license mode, which automatically occurs when the Agent Server is started and the HASP cannot be found. TimedLicenceExpired : ON when the Agent Server is running in time license mode and the timed license period has expired, so the Agent Server needs to be restarted to re-enable scanning. Note : To run the Agent Server Service in timed license mode, use the /-demo startup option, which is specified AFTER installing the Agent Server service, as follows: EITHER open CMD.exe and type in the following command: "net start agentserver /-demo" OR open the Services applet (in Administrative Tools), right click the AgentServer service, select Properties and specify –demo in the Start parameters edit field, then click the Start button and the Ok button. LineChart controls Top LineChart controls These controls are typically used to trend live data by displaying one or more series of points that are usually connected to form lines. Note: You can create template charting controls, since the applicable Series values of chart controls support the use of curly brackets {} to create aliases for SmartUI Templates or data element substitutions for wizards. How to chart data within a line chart: this describes the recommended procedure for creating a line chart on a graphic form to report your data. This assumes that you have already added the necessary datasources to expose the data that you want to chart. If necessary, add this control to the required graphic form. For details, see Adding Charting controls . Click the Series Setup heading in the left pane of the chart configuration dialog to display the Series Setup dialog. Add the series that you want to chart and specify the data that each series should represent and if necessary specify the various options that affect how the series is charted. Linking controls to BindingSource components Top Linking controls to BindingSource components Once you have added a VIZNETDataBinder component to a graphic form and associated it with a DataBinder DataBinders allow you to create a sub-set of the data contained within an OLE DB datasource to provide constant bi-directional communication with this database. This means that unlike the data returned by Select queries, this data can be viewed and/or modified and updated if it changes. , other controls can access the data of the View and/or tables of this DataBinder by being linked to the respective BindingSource Allows other controls and components on the graphic form to access the data of their associated table or View. Typically created by the VIZNETDataBinder component for each table and View of its associated DataBinder. component. The following BindingSource components are created: A single View BindingSource component, which ONLY allows its data to be viewed and not modified, which adheres to the following naming convention: bsView[OLE DB Datasource Name][DataBinderName]_[DataBinderName]. For instance: bsViewMyOLEDBMyDatBndr_MyDatBndr, where the datasource is 'MyOLEDB' and the Dat

heres to the following naming convention: bsView[OLE DB Datasource Name][DataBinderName]_[DataBinderName]. For instance: bsViewMyOLEDBMyDatBndr_MyDatBndr, where the datasource is 'MyOLEDB' and the DataBinder is 'MyDatBndr'. A BindingSource component for each table within this DataBinder, which allows both viewing and modification of its data and adheres to the following naming convention: bs[OLEDB Datasource Name][DataBinderName]_[Table Name]. For instance: bsMyOLEDBMyDatBndr_Sales Staff, where the datasource is 'MyOLEDB' and the DataBinder is 'MyDatBndr' and the table name is 'Sales Staff'. Prerequisites for linking controls to BindingSource components: Determine the field/s that you want the control to view and/or modify. Identify the BindingSource component that contains these field/s and provides the required interaction. Associate the appropriate databinding property of this control with this BindingSource component. Loading Agents Top Loading Agents The Agent Server automatically loads the .WGP file defined in the Agent Server Configuration dialog of the Adroit Setup utility. If there is a POSTLOAD.WGP file this too will be loaded. Further agents can be loaded from other .WGP files whenever the user wishes. Locating saved data Top Locating saved data The following topic describes how to locate all the data that is saved to disk: Note: Each Configuration is completely separate or insular, containing its own files, application settings and/or registry keys. For details, see Working with Configurations . Tip: The Adroit Config Editor provides a System Backup and Restore feature that can backup and restore your SmartUI and/or Adroit user-configuration. For details, see System Backup and Restore . Server data files: Note: It is necessary to backup all of this data to completely backup the Server. For details, see Backing up Server data . Server-specific configuration: This contains all the SmartUI Server configuration that only has meaning for this Server, such as its security configuration and the added datasources and their configuration. This data is saved to the ‘ServerData’ files. For details, see Saving data files . By default, these files are located in the Data subfolder of the Default configuration folder (typically C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI\Configurations\Default \Data), although this location can be customised. For details, see Server directory settings .

configuration folder (typically C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI\Configurations\Default \Data), although this location can be customised. For details, see Server directory settings . Note: If these files are removed then all the security configuration and added datasources will be removed for this Server. However the profiles and projects may still exist. Profiles: This contains all the profiles created for this Server and their configuration, which is saved separately so that these profiles can be easily replicated to other Servers, if necessary. For details, see Locating saved profiles . Projects: Each project that is created is saved in separate folders, with the exact structure of the project being maintained, to easily locate your graphic forms, so that they can be backed up, copied and/or moved. For details, see Locating saved projects . Client data files: Each Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. is also able to save or cache data that it requests from the SmartUI Server, however unlike the SmartUI Server this data does not need to be saved and is saved voluntarily to improve its response

ver. is also able to save or cache data that it requests from the SmartUI Server, however unlike the SmartUI Server this data does not need to be saved and is saved voluntarily to improve its response time from the Server. This data is saved to the ‘CACHE’ and 'CACHEINDEX' files. These files will always be located in the Caching sub-folder of the SmartUI ProgramData folder (typically C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI \Caching), if the (Caching) DataElementCachingEnable setting is enabled (set to True) for the Client. For details on accessing this setting, see Advanced Designer settings or Advanced Operator settings as applicable. Currently this only applies to graphic forms for SmartUI Operators. g) DataElementCachingRetrieveRegardless setting, then the SmartUI Operator will ALWAYS load a cached graphic form from the local cache REGARDLESS of the subsequent changes that have been made to it, since the cache was last updated. Locking datasources Top Locking datasources Due to the client-server model of SmartUI more than one user can modify the same datasource exposed by a SmartUI Server. But if you want to be the only user that is able to modify a datasource, then you can lock this datasource in the Enterprise Manager . Click for more details: Note1: Only users that have the necessary security permissions can do this. For details, see Securing datasources . Note2: Although other users are unable to modify a locked datasource, they can still view and display this datasource. Note3: A locked datasource can either be unlocked by the same user who locked the datasource or by any user with global security access to this SmartUI Server (typically an Administrator). Note4: You can identify a locked datasource in the Enterprise Manager by its red text . Note5: A datasource remains locked until it is unlocked, so it remains locked even when the user that has locked it has logged off the SmartUI Server. For details, see Unlocking datasources . To lock a datasource: Select the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager , as follows: Open the Enterprise Manager . Navigate to Servers > [Server Name] . Tip: Th

Logged Data Values CSV File Format Top Logged Data Values CSV File Format Note: Backup (LGB) files can be created when logging to the Adroit proprietary datalog (.LGD) files so that this historical data can be retrieved by the datalogging system when needed. This can also create CSV files too, to make this historical data available to third party applications such as Microsoft Excel and formatted to create reports. For details, see Datalog backup and retrieval . After you have exported data logged values to a CSV Comma Separated Value file containing data, which consists of a number of fields in one or more rows, in which the different fields (values) are typically separated by commas. file, this file provides the following columns: date , time , value , comment The purpose of the comment field is to label each data log entry indicating how and when the value was derived. For every session, defined as the period between startup and shutdown of the Agent Server, Adroit always marks the first and last entries in the log as the post startup and last known values. Note1: To prevent logging the POST_STARTUP value after an Agent Server restart, configure the Disable first datalog entries

text: first and last entries in the log as the post startup and last known values. Note1: To prevent logging the POST_STARTUP value after an Agent Server restart, configure the Disable first datalog entries on startup of agent server global datalogging setting. See Advanced Datalog Configuration (global settings) . Note2: Post startup values apply to all datalogs regardless of whether their input tag is scanned or not. All intermediate values will be marked as normal or bad. When retrieving data for viewing or analysis, the requested interval time may not coincide with the actual logging time. Therefore, Adroit calculates the values that occur between the recorded values either by estimation (if between sessions) or interpolation (if within the same session). Logging Alarms to a SQL Database Top Logging Alarms to a SQL Database Tip: the EventLogging agent provides a simpler method for logging incidents to a SQL (OLE DB compatible) database. For details, see Configuring EventLogging Agents . In Adroit , an EventOutput agent can be used to log alarm events to a SQL database. This requires the following main steps: Creating the SQL database and its associated ODBC data source , which is used by the EventOutput agent to refer to this SQL database. Create your SQL Database and save it. Tip: It is recommended to limit the size of the table and field names as ONLY 80 characters is available to represent the comma delimited list of these names in the EventOutput agent. Open the Start menu and select Run… Type “odbcad32.exe” into the Run dialog and click OK . Click on the System DSN tab in the ODBC Data Source Administrator dialog. Click the Add... button. Double-click the SQL Server entry in the Create New Data Source dialog. Tip: This should be the last entry in the list. Specify the name of this ODBC data source in the Name field of the Create a New Data Source to SQL Server dialog. In this example the following name is used: AdrEvtSQL Note:

metadata.title: Logging Alarms to a SQL Database

text: e last entry in the list. Specify the name of this ODBC data source in the Name field of the Create a New Data Source to SQL Server dialog. In this example the following name is used: AdrEvtSQL Note: This name will be used to specify this Access database, when configuring the EventOutput agent. Specify the required SQL Server computer in the Server field and click Next to advance to the next configuration page. For more information on configuring the entries on both this and the subsequent pages, click the provided Help button. Tip: It is HIGHLY RECOMMENDED to test that the specified data source is able to connect to the specified SQL database. This can be done by clicking the Test Data Source button on the Finish page. Click OK and OK again to close the ODBC Data Source Administrator dialog. Note: Please ensure that you are able to add records to the table that these events are to be sent to. This can be achieved through a simple utility such as Microsoft Query. If you are in doubt as to how to go about this, speak to your SQL administrator. text: to how to go about this, speak to your SQL administrator. Adding and configuring an EventOutput agent to log alarms to this SQL database. Open the Agent Configurator dialog. Add a new EventOutput agent and click the Edit button. In the Printer Type field, select the SQL option. You will notice that the "Printer Name" and "Setup Data" fields immediately default to a simple form of help. These defaults can be re-created by deleting the contents of the respective field, exiting the dialog box and re-entering. In the Printer Name field, enter the ODBC data source name that refers to the required SQL database, followed by the username and password required to log on to this database as set up in SQL. Note: Ensure that commas separate these three items. Since no username or password has been specified in this case, this field is simply: AdrEvtSQL,joe,mypassword In the Setup Data field, enter the table name (specified in the SQL database) followed by a comma delimited list of the required field names. Note: The MAXIMUM size of this Setup Data field is 80 characters, therefore ensure that the table and field names are small enough to all fit. Tip: It is recommended to add the fields ONE a

Any problem with any field will prevent records from being added to the database i.e. no warning messages are displayed. Problem areas are the widths of text field; date fields and specific field formatting. In this case this field, after three testing iterations is: Evnts,AgtFld,AgtData,EvtTime , where Evnts refers to the table name. . If this is enabled (True) then use the Event Log message input to specify the text that is displayed by the logged event. This is '[{2}] changed the value of {3} from {0} to {1}' by default. When specifying this text, the following placeholders can be used: {0}: The Default Value . {1}: The newly entered value. Tip: The formatting of the values specified by {0} and {1} can also be customised to display decimals etc. for details, see Working with value formatting . {2}: The user name, of the currently logged in user, when the value was changed. {3}: The name of the spider or data element, whose value has been changed. Logging events to the event log Top Logging diagnostic events to the event log When diagnosing the SmartUI Server, it is possible to log diagnostic information to the event log, which is typically logged to the Application event log category on the local Server computer. These events are typically used for troubleshooting the setting up and licensing the SmartUI Server and establishing the required security, profiles, datasources and projects. Note: Both the computer on which this event log resides and the event log category in which these events are logged are user-configurable. For details on configuring these settings, see General Server settings . When using the event log it may be necessary to clear these events either to pinpoint a current problem by only displaying the most current events or to prevent it from becoming too big. The manner in which these events can be viewed and/or cleared, depends upon how the Server has been launched, as follows: If the Server is being run as an application then the Activity Monitor can be used. To use the Activity Monitor to display the logged events: Open the Activity Monitor Launch the Server as an application by clicking the Start menu,

Logging Values Top Logging Values How to effectively log your data : guides you to use the fairly complex logging sub-system effectively. How to Log a Tag (agent.slot) : describes the procedure for logging process values in Adroit . The Datalog agent should ONLY be used for proprietary logging and the datalog period ( Length... ) should not exceed what is required for operational trending purposes. In other words, should an operator only need to see 24 hours of trend data to properly monitor and control his plant then the datalog period should only be set for 1 day. Historical data (i.e. data outside of the datalog period), if requested, will be retrieved from the backup files, if required. Therefore the logging to ADO (SQL) databases by the Datalog agent is disabled by default (the SQL... button of the Datasource field is hidden in the Edit Datalog agent dialog). This is to force users to use the DBLog agent instead, which logs data to SQL more efficiently. Note: The DBLog agent is a bulk OLE DB logging agent for typically logging Analog and/or Digital values to a specific table in a database for later retrieval that supercedes SQL logging via the Datalog agent. For details, see T

bulk OLE DB logging agent for typically logging Analog and/or Digital values to a specific table in a database for later retrieval that supercedes SQL logging via the Datalog agent. For details, see The DBLog Agent . Although if the Agent Server loads a legacy WGP file that ALREADY contains an ADO datalogging configuration, then the SQL... button of the Datasource field will be visible in the Edit Datalog agent dialog. Note: Multiple log sets are no longer required as Adroit provides the DBLog agent that should make SQL logging via the Datalog agent redundant. Also you no longer need multiple proprietary sets with increasing periods and larger time deadbands, since Adroit provides a new datalog backup feature with full trend-retrieval support. When recording or logging the values contained in agents in the Agent Server, first decide on the logging method that best suits your logging requirements. Adroit provides the following methods of storing data: Note: The Disable logging on standby setting is now configured PER datalog SET. So you can disable an OLE DB logging set WITHOUT disabling any proprietary logging sets, which typically do not require this setting as each Agent Server l

y setting is now configured PER datalog SET. So you can disable an OLE DB logging set WITHOUT disabling any proprietary logging sets, which typically do not require this setting as each Agent Server logs to their own datalog files. Proprietary Adroit log files: This logging method has been specifically designed for the needs of the SCADA industry to provide improved logging performance, typically achieving sub-second logging rates. Previously, when logging to the Adroit proprietary datalog (.LGD) files, the Adroit datalogging system only provided the historical logged data existing in the .LGD file and was unable to provide historical data from the SystemDatalog-created .CSV datalog backup files. Now each Datalog agent can create their own backup (.LGB) files to automatically retrieve this data, if required by trends (charts) or other requests for historical data. For details, see Datalog backup and retrieval . This method stores original Adroit timestamps (a Windows FILETIME structure which represents the number of 100 nanosecond intervals since Jan 1 1601), which provide millisecond resolution for each recorded value. Note: When accessing these timestamps by using the OLE automat

which represents the number of 100 nanosecond intervals since Jan 1 1601), which provide millisecond resolution for each recorded value. Note: When accessing these timestamps by using the OLE automation interface, this millisecond resolution is lost because the data type used to store this value is unable to store milliseconds. Each log file has a maximum of 53 million records, which can provide at least 30 days of logging at a log rate of 50 milliseconds! This rate is determined by configuring the required Time and/or Value Deadbands. Note: If the logging period is increased ensure that this change is saved and the Agent Server is restarted, at least once, to allow the necessary LGD file compressions to occur. For details, see Increasing Logging Periods . Note: If you export and delete Datalog agents that use Adroit 's proprietary log files, ensure that you restart the Agent Server before re-importing - so that they can remove the areas that they currently use in the LGD files. Click for more details: Multiple Datalog agents can potentially use a single LGD file, so when you delete a Datalog agent using proprietary logging all that happens is the area of the file that was used by

for more details: Multiple Datalog agents can potentially use a single LGD file, so when you delete a Datalog agent using proprietary logging all that happens is the area of the file that was used by the deleted Datalog agent is marked as unused and will be compacted at the next Agent Server startup. Therefore if you re-create the Datalog agent in the same Agent Server session, the LGD resource simply adds the space required for the newly added Datalog to the end of the LGD file i.e. it does not re-use the old area that has been marked as unused. This can cause the LGD file to become too big, resulting in errors such as an error message asking you to check your Datalog agent configuration (in Agent Server window you may also get a Datalog agent dll exception) and your Datalog agents may not start. When you restart the Agent Server , the old areas of the LGD file are compacted and room is left to re-create the datalogs. This logged data can be retrieved for viewing , used in trends, or exported as comma separated variable (CSV) files . In Adroit terminology, a value is referred to as a tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). , therefore ‘to log a value’ is the same as saying ‘to log a tag’. For a brief introduction to Adroit terminology, see Agents, Slots, Tags and their relation to Values . Note: For further details concerning the agents responsible for managing this logging of data and links to these storage facilities and for other logging functionality, see Logging Agents . Note: It is also possible to log multiple tags simultaneously i.e. to log multiple agents of the same type, using the most recently specified logging configuration. Since a total of 65534 devices may be added and used for any one installed protocol driver, the following configuration options are possible: One protocol driver, with one configured device (logical connection) communicating to one physical device. In some drivers, the communications are synchronised via this common port. Many protocol drivers, each with one or more configured devices (logical connections) communicating to many physical devices, via several ports. RGAM Station Address: This two-digit number indicates the address of the RGAM to which the message has to be sent. Op-code: The op-code identifies the type of information that is requested by the user. This could be any one of the opcodes described in the previous section (Supported addresses). the type of message to send (Read or Write message). The Adroit Lovato RGAM serial driver only supports ‘Read’ messages; thus, the operator will always be a question mark (‘?’). Data: The data that the user wants to write to the unit. Because this driver doesn’t support write functionality, the data portion will always be omitted. Start checksum: The ampersand character (‘&’) indicates the start of the message checksum. Checksum: The checksum is two characters wide and is the lowest significant byte of the algebraic sum of the single bytes that are transmitted, starting from the RGAM station address to the last data byte. Message stop: The closing bracket (‘)’) indicates the end of the message. Note: This number must never be greater than the number in the first column of the System.CSV file. Server Enabled: This stores the enabled status of the server, if the server is enabled this is 1, otherwise if the server is disabled this is 0. Server Deleted: This stores the deleted status of the server, if the server is deleted this is 0, otherwise if the server is not deleted this is 1. If the server is deleted then it will be added to the list of servers to be recovered, until the Pack Database file menu item is executed, after which it is permanently removed from this file. Server Title: This stores the name that has been given to the server, which must not more than 90 characters in length. Server Database: This stores the name of the CSV file, that is also stored in the database folder . This file stores all the tag groups and tag links that belong to the server. IP Address: This stores the IP address of the WanClient computer or its computer name (

Port: This stores the IP port that is used by Wanlink for communications and this can only be set to 51114. Retries: This stores the number of times that communications are to be reattempted when the communications to this WanServer fail. Ping Period: This stores the period in seconds to wait after the communications to this WanServer fail before the WanClient will retry to establish communications. Connect Timeout: This is not being used. Transaction Timeout: This stores the time in seconds before a requested transaction made to the server fails. Making Operators cluster-aware Top Making SmartUI Operators cluster-aware SmartUI Servers can be clustered to handle their combined workload evenly and to provide continued operation in the event that one or more fail. For details on configuring a clustered Server ( cluster partner a Server that belongs to a particular cluster. See Cluster. ), see SmartUI Server clustering . Cluster partners are only able to service SmartUI Operator clients that have been made aware of their cluster, by configuring a number of their Operator-specific settings. For details on accessing these settings, see Advanced SmartUI Operator settings . Example: ClusterName =Cluster1 ClusterServers =Cluster1~Machine1~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE;Cluster1~Machine2~ 9000 ~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE;Cluster1~Machine3~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE This will make this SmartUI Operator aware of a cluster named "Cluster1", and allow it to connect to the cluster partners that are running on Machine1, Machine2 and Machine. Each of these Servers are communicating by means of Subscribe, via the default Server Port 9000 and will have "Cluster1" as their ServerName setting. Also, the default connection settings for thi

ine. Each of these Servers are communicating by means of Subscribe, via the default Server Port 9000 and will have "Cluster1" as their ServerName setting. Also, the default connection settings for this Operator are: DefaultConnection = Machine1 DefaultConnectionType = MAINDATAPROVIDER DefaultCommunicationMode = SUBSCRIBE Note: That these settings match those used for the first Server, specified in the ClusterServers setting. Tip: It is recommended that this configuration be performed once and then copied to all the Operators that need to be made aware of the cluster(s). Simply copy the two sections of this .CONFIG file, ConnectionSettings and ClusterSettings , to the other SmartUI Operator .CONFIG files. Management Information Tools Top Management Information Tools A number of tools are provided with Adroit to facilitate the organization and communication of information from operations to management. Data can either be taken live from the Agent Server or collected from historical Data Logs. The data is then manipulated and reported by third party applications to provide relevant management information quickly. The tools have been designed to retrieve data from Agent Servers belonging to more than one project, providing management with the ability to get an overall view of their operations. They use several data retrieval methods listed below: DbAccess Agent The DbAccess Agent that provides a link between Adroit and various external databases, by using OLE DB technology. It is ideally used in applications where data inside the Agent Server is periodically written to a database (such as at the end of a batch job) for reporting reasons. It is not suited for fast logging of data. OLE Interface (MISSRVR) This OLE Server Interface , formerly known as the MISSRVR, forms the standard API (Application Programming Interface) for Adroit Agent Servers. Adroit Server ActiveX Control The Adroit

face (MISSRVR) This OLE Server Interface , formerly known as the MISSRVR, forms the standard API (Application Programming Interface) for Adroit Agent Servers. Adroit Server ActiveX Control The Adroit Server ActiveX Control (adroitx.ocx) is provided as an alternative to the current Adroit Server OLE interface. While it honors the current OLE Server interface, its prime feature is that of supporting subscriptions via an event interface. Merging Data Logs : merges values from a CSV file into an existing historical database of DataLog agents Putting Values into Agents : enables a specific value to be written to a specific agent’s slot a value (attribute) or field within an agent that can be retrieved and/or set. . Managing Message Queues Top Managing Message Queues The Command agent uses a message queue because the sending and receiving of SMS messages are not instantaneous. This message queue provides temporarily storage, especially when a large number of SMS messages need to be sent at any one time or a large number of Command agents are using the same GSM SMS modem. If necessary, the total number of messages that can be stored in this queue can be limited, although once the queue is filled, any further messages that arrive will not be sent. It is therefore recommended to keep the default setting, of 0, which does not limit this queue length, since a large message queue does not pose a performance issue. It is also possible to purge all the messages from this queue, for instance, for testing purpose or when the message queue has been filled with unwanted or unnecessary messages. Note: These settings are ONLY specific to this Command agent only and do not apply globally to all Command agents. To specify the maximum number of queued messages: Edit the required Command agent. For details, see Editing Agents . This will display the Edit Command agent dialog. If necessary, select the General ta

o specify the maximum number of queued messages: Edit the required Command agent. For details, see Editing Agents . This will display the Edit Command agent dialog. If necessary, select the General tab, the default selection. Under the Agent Settings group, specify the required maximum number of messages in the Queue size edit box. Note: Any integer number from 0 to 1000 can be specified, the default being 0 i.e. an unlimited queue length. Tip: It is recommended to keep the default of 0 i.e. unlimited queue length. To remove all the messages that are currently in the queue: Edit the required Command agent. For details, see Editing Agents . This will display the Edit Command agent dialog. If necessary, select the General tab, the default selection. Under the Agent Settings group, click the Empty Queue button. WARNING! All messages currently in the queue will be removed and will need to be re-sent. Tip: This can also be performed through the direct manipulation of its Boolean emptyQueue slot. -->

text: Manual Master Mode Assignment Top Manual Master Mode Assignment In manual mode, the systemInfo.serverMode slot is completely controlled by the user. Rules and implications There cannot be more than one master server in a cluster. Hence making a server master will immediately switch the other server to standby mode. The serverMode and serverState slots between Agent Servers and within an Agent Server are not replicated. All other server and client clustering operations will operate as normal given the slot values, irrespective of whether a manual or automatic master mode assignment method is used. For instance, the automatic switching UI will track the first healthy master server in its list even if the UI detects more than one healthy master server, when connected to more than one cluster. Suggested method of operation As suggested in the above scenarios, start all or part of the cluster servers. Set the desired master server as master through the various means available to set the serverMode slot (one way would be to use the dialog in the options-preferences-connection menu item). The automatically assigned clients switch their connection to the new master server. Adding a new clu

verMode slot (one way would be to use the dialog in the options-preferences-connection menu item). The automatically assigned clients switch their connection to the new master server. Adding a new cluster server to the cluster will have no effect on the system. All cluster information and operations including the historical synchronization can be viewed and managed within the UI by using the cluster-controlling graphic form. See the Active Cluster Control tab of the System Management graphic form in the System Information project. -->

Note: The following calculation can calculate the incoming (or outgoing) bandwidth for each network card of the monitored computer in kilobits per second. Technical explanation of this calculation: The network bandwidth is an accumulative value of the number of bits that are either received (incoming) or sent (output) from the specified network card. Therefore, its current value must be calculated by subtracting it from the previous value, which is performed by the rate slot of the Statistical agent. These bits are recorded as octets and so need to be multiplied by 8 before this value displays the number of bits, then the value needs to be divided by 1024 so that it is displayed as kilobits. The Analog agent performs this conversion, since its Device Span (raw) Maximum value of the Analog agent is set to 10000000000000, to ensure that this value will not be exceeded. Its Engineering Span (eng) Maximum value is set to 78125000000, because this is the Device Span Maximum value multiplied by 8 and divided by 1024. Manually Edit Groups Top Manually Edit Groups Tag groups are primarily added to manage the communication settings for the tags whose values need to be communicated to or from the remote Agent Servers via their associated WanServers. Groups are server-specific. For details, see Tag Groups . If it is necessary to bulk configure a large number of groups at one time, they can be manually edited. To manually edit groups: Groups are stored in the user-specified database filename of their applicable Server, specified when adding a server . This .CSV file is located within the database folder and contains all the specific configuration of the tag groups and their tag links that have been configured within the specific server. The first 6 lines of the file are comment lines. The first two lines show both the name and IP address of the server, to which these tag groups and tag links are associated. The next four lines then provide configuration specific information. The columns, required when configuring a tag group, in the order that they appear in the file: [GROUP]: This is used to identify that a tag group, as opposed to a tag link, is being specified. Note: This must not be any spaces be

nfiguring a tag group, in the order that they appear in the file: [GROUP]: This is used to identify that a tag group, as opposed to a tag link, is being specified. Note: This must not be any spaces before the [GROUP]’ indication. Group Title: This stores the name that has been given to this tag group, which must not more than 90 characters in length. Group Enabled: This stores the enabled status of the group, if the group is enabled this is 1, otherwise if the group is disabled this is 0. Group Deleted: This stores the deleted status of the group, if the group is deleted this is 0, otherwise if the group is not deleted this is 1. If the group is deleted then it will be added to the list of groups to be recovered, until the Pack Database file menu item is executed, after which it is permanently removed from this file. Poll Period: This stores the rate in seconds at which the WanClient should request this WanServer for changes to the tag links within this tag group. The default value of 0 implies "as fast as possible" and the rate will depend on the total number of configured groups. Buffer size: This is not being used. Group Type: This stores the communication type required by the t

0 implies "as fast as possible" and the rate will depend on the total number of configured groups. Buffer size: This is not being used. Group Type: This stores the communication type required by the tag links within the group. A Normal group, indicated by a 0, only permits the values of the tags links within this group to be fetched from the WanServer so that the values on the WanClient are updated accordingly. A Control group, indicated by a 2, also permits the tags links within this group to also send changes from the WanClient to the WanServer. -->

Manually Edit Links Top Manually Edit Links A tag link or tag mapping, specifies the name of the local and the remote Adroit tag, whose values are to be ‘linked’. This is added to a tag group within a server. For details, see Tag Links . If it is necessary to bulk configure a large number of tag links at one time, they can be manually edited. To manually edit links: Links are stored together with groups in the user-specified database filename of their applicable Server, specified when adding a server . This .CSV file is located within the database folder and contains all the specific configuration of the tag groups and their tag links that have been configured within the specific server. The first 6 lines of the file are comment lines. The first two lines show both the name and IP address of the server, to which these tag groups and tag links are associated. The next four lines then provide configuration specific information. Note: Tag links can only be entered into this file below a configured tag group [GROUP]-entry, to which they are then associated. The columns, required when configuring a tag link, in the order that they appear in the file: Local Tag: This stores the name of t

onfigured tag group [GROUP]-entry, to which they are then associated. The columns, required when configuring a tag link, in the order that they appear in the file: Local Tag: This stores the name of the required Adroit tag, located in the local Agent Server, residing on the WanClient computer. Remote Tag: This stores the name of the required Adroit tag, located in the Agent Server residing on the WanServer computer. Link Enabled: This stores the enabled status of the link, if the link is enabled this is 1, otherwise if the link is disabled this is 0, and this tag link is not to be communicated to. Link Method: This stores the communication method by which values are transferred between the two Agent Servers. A Polled link, indicated by a 0, involves the use of a polling period in which the values are to be fetched. A Subscription link, indicated by a 1, involves changes being fetched only when they change. -->

Manually Polling OID Values Manually Polling OID Values There are a number of methods of polling (monitoring) the values of SNMP managed objects within the connected device. Note: A scan point is consumed for every unique OID that is polled. To manually poll ANY OID of the device: this can be used to monitor OIDs that you do not normally need to view. Typically this will be used to view the OIDs associated with an SNMP trap (event) that is received from the device. Set the oid slot to a valid OID, in numeric format, for this managed device. The value of the OID is returned in the oidValue slot. To manually poll ALL the OIDs in the list: this will immediately retrieve the values of all the OIDs in the list and sets their corresponding tags to the new values. For instance, this could be set from a button on a mimic. Set the pollAllNow slot to 1. Note1: The value of any OID that does NOT have an associated Tag in this list will NOT be returned. Note2: This polling occurs immediately, over and above the normal poll cycle. To manually poll ALL the OIDs in the list that are NOT enabled for automatic polling: this will immediately retrieve that values of all the OIDs in the list that do n

and above the normal poll cycle. To manually poll ALL the OIDs in the list that are NOT enabled for automatic polling: this will immediately retrieve that values of all the OIDs in the list that do not have their E fields checked and sets their corresponding tags to the new values. Set the pollManualNow slot to 1. Note1: The value of any OID that does NOT have an associated Tag in this list will NOT be returned. Note2: This polling occurs immediately, over and above the normal poll cycle. -->

Mapping spiders Top Mapping spiders The Mapping spider maps or connects inputs to outputs, through the creation of mapping pairs, so that each input has an associated and identically named output. Click for more details: This spider acts as a connection interface for reusable graphics to which the data, required for the display and animation of the graphic, can be connected. In other words this spider eliminates the need of painstakingly connecting the required data to each of the various properties and other spider inputs, every time this graphic is re-used. This configuration can be performed once for all, by simply creating the necessary mapping pairs and connecting their outputs to these properties and other spider inputs. Then, when the graphic is re-used, the data is simply connected to the inputs of this Mapping spider, which correspond to its already connected outputs. To add this spider to the spider workspace . To add (and configure) one or more mapping pairs . To remove unnecessary mapping pairs . Configuration Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider. Note: Menu items that are enabled will have a tick mark to the le

cessary mapping pairs . Configuration Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider. Note: Menu items that are enabled will have a tick mark to the left of them. Detail View: This can be used to display the configuration view of this spider, so its name, description, inputs and outputs can be configured. For details, see Working with spider configuration views . Tip: Double-click the title bar of the spider to display or hide the configuration view of the spider. Delete Spider: This can be used to remove this spider from the spider workspace. For details, see Removing spiders . Trigger Spider From Event: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by means of an event. For details, see Triggering a spider from an event . This is disabled by default. Enable Silk Triggering: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by any silks that are attached to the inputs of this spider. For details, see Triggering spiders . This is enabled by default. Propagate Outputs At Startup: This enables the spider to supply the silks connected to its outputs with values as soon as its spider workspace ente

see Triggering spiders . This is enabled by default. Propagate Outputs At Startup: This enables the spider to supply the silks connected to its outputs with values as soon as its spider workspace enters into running mode. For details, see Working with spider workspaces or Sending spider outputs at startup . This is disabled by default. Trigger Now!: This will cause this spider to immediately be triggered. This default configuration view of this spider, contains the following sections: New Input , this section contains the input types configured for this spider. New Input Function New Mapping Pair This will display the New Mapping Pair configuration dialog, so that the mapping pair can be named. Then an input and output with the specified name is added to the Inputs and Outputs sections of the spider. For details on adding and configuring mapping pairs, see Adding mapping pairs . Master Recipe Top Master Recipe The Master Recipe consists of all the process variables or "ingredients" and the sequence in which they are to be downloaded. It is here that the procedure and associated tag names will be defined. The following are the components of the Master Recipe: Step: Both master and control recipes consist of sequences of steps. Each step is numbered, and if any new steps are inserted or deleted, the steps are renumbered consecutively. It is important to note that any GOTO STEP references must be manually edited if there has been any change to the order or number of steps. Ingredient: An agent and slot corresponding to the process variable to be set or downloaded to a front end device (e.g. PLC). The keyword <NONE> when used as an ingredient indicates that no process variable will change for the step. This allows a phase action to take place without having to set any process variable. The ingredient must either be a valid agent and slot having one of the slot types STRING, BOOLEAN, INTEGER, REAL, or a null entry <NONE> when a control Phase Action entry is needed. Verification: This is the means of verifying the values written to a front-end device (e.g. PLC).

es STRING, BOOLEAN, INTEGER, REAL, or a null entry <NONE> when a control Phase Action entry is needed. Verification: This is the means of verifying the values written to a front-end device (e.g. PLC). It is represented by an agent.slot that is read after a definite period of the ingredient value being downloaded. This value must be a valid slot. If the value of this slot does not match the value written to the ingredient slot, verification fails. The verification check occurs at the end of a phase. Phase Boundary: Any step that has a Phase Action marks the end of a phase. Phase: A phase consists of all steps executed between phase boundaries. Phase Actions and Tag/Value : A phase always ends with a Phase Action , and therefore may have several ingredient steps preceding it. Specific Status Bits . -->

Mathematical Operators for Expressions Top Mathematical Operators for Expressions Primary elements are primitive members of expressions like constants, variables or functions. Terms are separable parts of expressions, and can be signed terms or the product, quotient or modulus of two signed terms. Expressions are well-formed strings of terms, composed of symbols representing constants, variables, operators and relationships. Comments may follow an expression using C and C++ syntax (i.e. // comment or /* comment */). The order of precedence TYPICALLY begins at the top of the table, and is the same within each box. IMPORTANT : There are cases when certain operators do NOT follow their prescribed order of precedence - so please use parentheses to enforce the required precedence in your expressions. Example of altered precedence: Consider the expression: v1 | v2 & v3 These operator precedence rules say that & has precedence over | So this IS the same as: (v1 | (v2 & v3)) However, you add a ! to one of the variables, this appears to influence this precedence ! Consider the expression: !v1 | v2 & v3 According to the operator precedence rules this should be the same as ((!v1) | (v2 & v3))

! to one of the variables, this appears to influence this precedence ! Consider the expression: !v1 | v2 & v3 According to the operator precedence rules this should be the same as ((!v1) | (v2 & v3)) However, this is not the case, it is actually treated as the following by expression agents: (((!v1) | v2) & v3) Primary elements: NUMBER // Adroit real constant VARIABLE //variable input (V01, V02) mathFunc (primary) //mathematical function – primary //unary minus(result is negative of its operand) + primary //unary plus(result is same as its operand) ! primary //logical NOT ~ primary //bitwise NOT (1’s complement) Terms: primary / primary //division primary * primary //multiplication primary % primary //remainder (modulus) Expression relationships: term + term //addition term – term //subtraction term >> term //right shift (divide by 2) term << term //left shift (multiply by 2) term < term //less than term > term //greater than term <= term //less than or equal to term >= term //greater than or equal to term == term //equal term != term //not equal term & term //bitwise AND term ^ term //bitwise exclusive OR term | term //bitwise inclusive OR term && term //logical AND term || term

than or equal to term == term //equal term != term //not equal term & term //bitwise AND term ^ term //bitwise exclusive OR term | term //bitwise inclusive OR term && term //logical AND term || term //logical OR term ? expression:expression //conditional expression -->

Maximum Demand Quick Start Top Maximum Demand Quick Start This explains the recommended method of configuring your Adroit system to monitor your maximum demand. Before you can monitor your maximum demand, you need the following: To know when your electricity provider monitors your maximum demand. To know the maximum kVA demand limit imposed by your electricity provider, above which you are required to pay penalties. To know the block period duration used by your electricity provider to monitor your maximum demand. A front-end device (PLC) that monitors the pulse sent from your electricity provider to signal the start of each block period. [Otherwise, you can disable block pulses and allow to agent to determine block periods automatically based on current time instead.] A front-end device (PLC) that monitors the total kVA that your process uses. To monitor your maximum demand: Only enable this agent when maximum demand is being monitored Create a Scheduler agent, for instance called MDPERIODS, to specify the periods of high power use during which your electricity provider monitors your maximum demand. Contact your electricity provider for this information. For details, see Configuri

ERIODS, to specify the periods of high power use during which your electricity provider monitors your maximum demand. Contact your electricity provider for this information. For details, see Configuring the Scheduler agent . Edit an agent of type: MaxDemand . If necessary, add an agent of the required type, as follows: In the SmartUI Designer: Select the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager , as follows: Open the Enterprise Manager . Navigate to Servers > [Server Name] . Tip: The connection name is prefixed by the SmartUI Server computer name. If necessary, expand the Datasources category. If necessary, expand the required Adroit datasource or its icon . If necessary, expand the AgentGroup tree. Right click the required agent type , which are listed alphabetically, and select Create Tag . Specify the required Tag Name or agent name. The following rules apply when naming agents: Agent names have a maximum of 27 characters. Agent names cannot be the same as the names used for Agent Types or for Agent Groups. Agent names cannot use the following characters: Space Percent % Comma , Period . back slash \ Dollar $ If necessary, provide an optional Description that describes

r Agent Types or for Agent Groups. Agent names cannot use the following characters: Space Percent % Comma , Period . back slash \ Dollar $ If necessary, provide an optional Description that describes the purpose or describes the value of this tag (agent) for ease of reference. Click the Finish button. If necessary, locate the required agent, as follows: In the SmartUI Designer: Select the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager , as follows: Open the Enterprise Manager . Navigate to Servers > [Server Name] . Tip: The connection name is prefixed by the SmartUI Server computer name. If necessary, expand the Datasources category. If necessary, expand the required Adroit datasource or its icon . If necessary, expand the AgentGroup tree. If necessary, expand the required agent type , which are listed alphabetically. Locate the required agent , which is also listed alphabetically beneath their applicable agent type. In the Enterprise Manager window: right click this agent and select Configure . In the Edit MaxDemand Agent dialog: Check the Enable OR use tag checkbox (the enable slot) Click the browse button to the left of the Enable OR use tag checkbox and select the Scheduler

t Configure . In the Edit MaxDemand Agent dialog: Check the Enable OR use tag checkbox (the enable slot) Click the browse button to the left of the Enable OR use tag checkbox and select the Scheduler agent you created and its value slot (MDPERIODS.value) to only enable this agent when your electricity provider monitors your maximum demand. For details, see Selecting a tag from the Agent Explorer . Configure the other maximum demand-specific settings Specify the duration of the block period that your electrical provider uses, in minutes, in the Block period (mins) edit box (the blockPeriod slot). For instance, 30 minutes. Check the Enable block pulses checkbox (the blockPulseEnable slot) Specify the maximum kVA demand limit for this agent, in the Max demand limit (the mdLimit slot) edit box. Tip: If may be useful to specify a value slightly LESS THAN the actual maximum demand limit imposed by your electricity provider, so that there is time for counteractive measures to be taken when this is exceeded. Check the Enable max demand alarm checkbox (the enableMDAlarm slot) to enable the MaxDemand status bit when the predicted maximum demand exceeds this specified maximum demand limit. Le

is is exceeded. Check the Enable max demand alarm checkbox (the enableMDAlarm slot) to enable the MaxDemand status bit when the predicted maximum demand exceeds this specified maximum demand limit. Leave the default Reset configuration, unless you do NOT want to reset the current month’s calculations at midnight on the last day of the month. Click OK and close the configuration dialog of the MaxDemand agent. Configure the maximum demand-specific alarms for this agent Alarm the ‘PulseError’ alarm type for this agent, so that you will know if the timing of these external block pulses are compromised i.e. as soon as a pulse does not occur at the period specified by the Block period (mins) value. Alarm the ‘MaxDemand’ alarm type for this agent, so that you will know when the maximum demand limit is exceeded. Scan the relevant values of this agent to the appropriate front-end device Scan the BOOLEAN blockPulse slot of this agent to a value in a PLC that monitors the pulse sent from your electricity provider to signal the start of each block period. Scan the REAL kVA slot of this agent to a value in a PLC that measures the total instantaneous kVA usage. If you ALSO want to calculate the

ctricity provider to signal the start of each block period. Scan the REAL kVA slot of this agent to a value in a PLC that measures the total instantaneous kVA usage. If you ALSO want to calculate the instantaneous power factor and reactive power component then also scan the REAL kW slot of this agent to a PLC that measures the total instantaneous kW usage. Display important values You could display some or all of the following MaxDemand agent slots: mdLimit : the maximum kVA demand limit for this agent. mdActual : the highest recorded maximum demand for any block period of the current month. demand : the actual power that has been used (kVA demand) for this block period. mdPredict : estimates the total power use (kVA demand) for this block period, by using the demand slot against the remaining time for this block period. mdOverUnder : displays the difference between the Predicted max demand (the mdPredict slot) and the Max demand limit (the mdLimit slot) for this block period. timeToMD : indicates how long, in minutes, before the Max demand limit (the mdLimit slot) will be reached before the end of the block metered period, at the current demand. Note: If you are running safely, th

: indicates how long, in minutes, before the Max demand limit (the mdLimit slot) will be reached before the end of the block metered period, at the current demand. Note: If you are running safely, this will ALWAYS indicate the end of the current block period. kVAOptimal : the recommended kVA consumption to meet (and NOT EXCEED) the Max demand limit (the mdLimit slot) for this block period. kVASpare : the spare kVA capacity for current period, which is the difference between the Current demand (the demand slot) and the Optimal KVA (the kVAOptimal slot). This specifies a positive or negative amount of kVA that needs to be removed or added to meet (and NOT EXCEED) the Max demand limit (the mdLimit slot) for this block period. Example: For instance, you can create a mimic that allows a manager to know that at the current consumption ( demand slot) that: the configured maximum demand (the mdLimit slot) will be reached in 12 minutes ( timeToMD slot) which is 3 minutes before the end of the period (the blockTimeLeft slot - timeToMD slot) and 30kW of load needs to shed (the kVASpare slot is a negative number) to not exceed the maximum demand OR if the process is running safely that 45kW o

period (the blockTimeLeft slot - timeToMD slot) and 30kW of load needs to shed (the kVASpare slot is a negative number) to not exceed the maximum demand OR if the process is running safely that 45kW of load can be added (the kVASpare slot is a positive number) to meet the maximum demand) for this block. If necessary, use this agent to control your maximum demand If you want to control the maximum demand by using this agent, then use the MaxDemand status bit of this agent to turn off non-essential equipment via a script. Since this status bit is ONLY set when the Enable max demand alarm checkbox is enabled and the predicted maximum demand exceeds this specified maximum demand limit. Related Links: Configuring the MaxDemand agent : A comprehensive description of all the configuration options provided by the MaxDemand agent. How Maximum Demand is Calculated : To better understand this value and see how it is calculated. About Power Factor : To describe the cost implications of this value. -->

Merging Data Logs Top Merging Data Logs Adroit provides a means of merging values from a .CSV file into an existing historical database of DataLog agents. The .CSV file may have been originally created by the EXTRACT utility, or by choosing the EXPORT... button in the Datalog Retrieval dialog, or by using a text editor to modify existing files taking care to adhere to the format. The syntax of the command is as follows: merge mc.as,csvfile > jnlfile The abbreviations and examples are as follows: Note: No spaces are required between arguments. Message Sending and Processing Slots Top Message Sending and Processing Slots The Command agent provides the following slots that are responsible for processing commands and sending SMS messages, which can be externally manipulated if required: The lastMsgReceived slot: the most recent data received by this slot, even if identical to its previous contents, will cause it to BOTH process the data and then to send this processed data to the rawValue slot. Note1: If this slot receives a command, which has been enabled for this Command agent, then this command will be performed before it is sent to the rawValue slot. For details on enabling commands, see Specifying Permitted Commands . Note2: If pseudonyms and macros have been configured and enabled for this agent, then they can be also used when specifying this data. For details, see Using Pseudonyms and Macros . The value slot: the most recent data received by this slot will also be sent to the rawValue slot. Since this is a standard 80-character String slot and NOT a VARSTRING slot, like these other lastMsgReceived and rawValue slots, other agents are able to be @ scanned to it, so that their STRING slots can be sent by the Command a

haracter String slot and NOT a VARSTRING slot, like these other lastMsgReceived and rawValue slots, other agents are able to be @ scanned to it, so that their STRING slots can be sent by the Command agent instead. The lastMsgReceivedTime slot displays the time of the last message received. The lastMsgReceivedTimeStr slot displays the time of the last message received, as a (var)string. For instance, the value slot of the Command agent can be @scanned to the rawValue slot of a Notify agent, so that the Notify agent's alarm message can be sent to the recipient of the Command agent instead. For details, concerning @scanning, see Scanning from a Slot of Another Agent . The rawValue slot: this sends the most recent data received by this slot to its associated GSM_SMS device and as it leaves the Command agent, this data will also be placed in its lastMsgSent slot. For details on associating a GSM_SMS device with a Command agent, see Specifying the GSM_SMS Device . Note1: This rawValue slot is also exposed as the Raw value edit box provided at the bottom of the Edit Command agent dialog. For details on displaying this dialog, see Editing Agents . Note2: When the Resend message checkbox is

s also exposed as the Raw value edit box provided at the bottom of the Edit Command agent dialog. For details on displaying this dialog, see Editing Agents . Note2: When the Resend message checkbox is cleared (its default setting) a message will ONLY be sent if the rawvalue of this agent HAS changed when dialog is either updated or closed. This effectively prevents the resending of identical messages. Tip: The lastMsgSentTime slot displays the time of the last message sent. These slots can either be modified programmatically, via scripting or manually, such as by exposing the required slot and sending messages to it directly by exposing it on a mimic and associating a Data Entry, Operator Action Behaviour to it. For details, see Adding an Operator Action Behaviour or its Data Entry action. -->

Overview This driver supports the Mitsubishi 3E Frames protocol, with communication to the Q/QnA/L/R and FX5 Series CPU’s. The 2nd Generation driver allows for the following features: a) Improved performance due to optimizations on mixed I/O to the same protocol area being transacted only once removing redundant transactions. b) Support for multiple channels, where due scan tasks are balanced over available channels, reads and writes are interlaced to prevent starvation. c) Demand scanning support, where read only I/O that is not on a mimic / graphic form and not logged or alarmed and not output enabled will be removed from the scanning system , the applicable tasks will dynamically be reduced in size and can merge into fewer scan tasks. For improved network performance and reliability, it is recommended that you install 2 network adapters into your PC. Use the first adapter for Adroit to Adroit and all other Windows connectivity. The first adapter may have all the default installation bindings. Use t

that you install 2 network adapters into your PC. Use the first adapter for Adroit to Adroit and all other Windows connectivity. The first adapter may have all the default installation bindings. ooting It is possible that by modifying the default settings, that the watchdog sent by the driver may not arrive in the PLC, thus causing the PLC to “intermittently” reset our connection to the PLC. Ensure that the timer in the PLC (which runs for 120 seconds by default) is at least double the setting used by the driver. If the driver channel is backlogged (ie the driver is too busy with polling tasks), the watchdog may also be delayed,as it is not a foreground process in the driver. Driver backlogging or queing is easily detectable by setting a value in register in the PLC, and then timing how long it takes to receive a feedback via another tag which was scanned to the same register. he same route now automatically use a new path as well. This means that 2 devices on separate “paths” may communicate simultaneously for better speed. 3.3. Network Delay Note Applies to RS-232/422 gateway use only. The network delay is an optional instituted delay, inserted before a different station is polled on the same Data master-path. Using a value of zero will disable this feature. The network delay or quiet time is needed to allow a slave to detect the end of the communication cycle. A Modbus slave interprets a 2.5 character time delay at the end of a message as a signal that communication has been broken off, and thus allows communication to be initiated by the master to a new slave. By default, the Adroit driver does not implement this delay or network quiet time. To calculate the necessary time use the following formula, we have used 5 characters instead of 2.5 as this is always good engineering practice. 11 bits per byte have been used. 1/Baudx11x5. e.g. For a baud-rate of 2400, 1/2400 x11x5= 0.022916. or 23 ms. For a baud-rate of 19200, 1/19200 x11x5= 0.002863. or 3 ms. Devices using separate Data master paths will not wait using this network quiet time, so that all 422

Dynamic IP via DNS Lookup (Disabled until required) When Dynamic IP via DNS is enabled, the driver will launch a thread that will attempt to lookup an IP address when retries are exhausted and found to be failing. This lookup process will continue indefinitely until the Agent Server is stopped. It will not block a connection or the Agent Server read/writes which will continue on existing connection parameters until changed by a successful lookup, which will then save those new parameters. This mode can be used on connections that are on the internet and have a dynamic IP such as when using ADSL that change IP address once a day. Ensure the following Boolean properties of this charting control are enabled: ToolbarVisible , TimeDetailsButtonVisible and TimeDetailsButtonEnabled . Note: Any configuration of the charted time period that is performed in runtime will not be saved. Select the Modify the time details toolbar button from the toolbar. To modify the charted time details at runtime: use the Time Details tab to configure the charted time period and interval for a real-time or required charted time period for a historical trend. Modifying fonts Top Modifying fonts To use the Font spider to modify an existing font by independently adjusting certain of its attributes. By driving one or more of these font attributes remotely, you can create a constantly varying font, when configuring a font property of a graphic form or one of its form components. Note: The font attributes that can be individually manipulated are: Regular , Bold , Italic , Font size , Underline and Strikethrough . To modify a font by adjusting certain attributes If necessary, add and/or select the required Font spider and/or open its configuration view. For details, see Adding Font spiders . Right-click its title bar and select Add ARGB Properties . Note: Once you add these properties you cannot remove them from this spider. This adds the following six additional Integer inputs to the Inputs section: Regular: This Boolean attribute, if set to True, removes any Bold or Italic formatting specified for the font. Note: For this reason, you cannot set both the Regular and Bold or Italic properties at the same time. Bold: This Boolean attribute, if set to True, displays the font in Bold . Italic: This Boolean attribute, if set to True, displays the

both the Regular and Bold or Italic properties at the same time. Bold: This Boolean attribute, if set to True, displays the font in Bold . Italic: This Boolean attribute, if set to True, displays the font in Italic . Font size: This Double attribute, specifies the point size of the specified font. Underline: This Boolean attribute, if set to True, will cause the font to appear with underlines. Strikethrough: This Boolean attribute, if set to True, will cause the font to appear with a horizontal line through it. Note: You are unable to set both the Underline and Strikethough properties at the same time. The value of these inputs can either be supplied by another spider or Data spider (e.g. property or data element) via a silk or it can be typed in manually. For details, see Creating silks . Note: The Font size can be specified by a Double, whereas only Boolean values can be used to specify the values of the Regular , Bold , Italic , Underline and Strikethrough font attributes. If other values are typed in, the cell will not accept this input until either this value is removed or the required value is entered instead. Tip: When typing in a value manually, double-click the value colu

values are typed in, the cell will not accept this input until either this value is removed or the required value is entered instead. Tip: When typing in a value manually, double-click the value column to the right of the Regular , Bold , Italic , Underline , Font size or Strikethrough input name in the Inputs section and type in the required value. Note: If you unchecked the Grouped option when adding the wizard to this graphic form, then the controls and/or vectors behave, as normal, and so their values cannot be re-substituted. Substitution Assignment : to change the substitution assignments (you can also click the Substitutions graphic form toolbar button) to display the Substitution Assignment dialog. For details, see Working with substitutions . Load source wizard : this opens the wizard that was originally used to create this wizard instance in a separate window of the Design workspace Open source wizard location : this opens the project and/or folder in the Enterprise Manager that contains the wizard that was originally used to create this wizard instance. Create Object Template : create an Object Model Template from this wizard instance, which creates an advanced wizard that also configures the r

that was originally used to create this wizard instance. Create Object Template : create an Object Model Template from this wizard instance, which creates an advanced wizard that also configures the required SCADA-related configuration, such as the required scanning, alarming and logging of this object. Monitor the Local Agent Server Top Monitor the Local Agent Server Using the Adroit Configuration Setup : Press the Windows key and start typing in Classic Setup and select it from the list. Click on the Drivers tab and right click in the Installed Drivers and Devices list. If the Monitor Local Agent Server option is enabled, a tick ( ) appears next to it, in which case the local Agent Server will be looked for every 5 seconds until it is found. Once the Agent Server is detected, both the device icons ( , , ) in the Installed Drivers and Devices list and in their information panes will indicate the status of the device in the Agent Server. This option is enabled by default. Note: It is only possible to stop or start running devices via the Agent Configurator, alternatively use the Project Explorer . Using the Adroit Config Editor : This functionality is currently not provided. -->

Monitoring a network using SNMPMgr Agents Top Monitoring a network using SNMPMgr Agents Each SNMPMgr agent can manage a single device, by getting, setting and/or trapping its OID values. PLEASE NOTE: It is very important to set up Windows firewall, or any other similar network security product, correctly to allow SNMP traffic. Failing to do this will result in the inoperability of the SNMPMgr agent. For further details on the requirements and guidelines regarding the use of this agent, see SNMPMgr Agent Usage Requirements . To implement SNMPMgr agents to monitor a physical industrial network: Before setting up the SNMPMgr agent, decide which devices you need to monitor. In other words determine the (SNMP) network topology. Tip: It is recommended to create a mimic to visualise the network, because this also assists in quickly detecting of the source of network bottlenecks too. In the case of the network described by this mimic, it would be necessary to configure seven SNMPMgr agents on the computer running the Agent Server. In other words one SNMPMgr agent is required for each networked device that you need to manage. Configure each of these SNMPMgr agents to get and/or set the requ

metadata.title: Monitoring a network using SNMPMgr Agents

text: the computer running the Agent Server. In other words one SNMPMgr agent is required for each networked device that you need to manage. Configure each of these SNMPMgr agents to get and/or set the required OID values of their devices. For details, see Configuring SNMPMgr Agents . Once the monitoring process has begun, the SNMPMgr agent will start: Polling : to receive values from the device and copy them into the associated tags. Which you can then trend, alarm or log in Adroit : For instance, it is possible to trend object information such as bandwidth; alarm certain conditions on the network, such a computer becoming unavailable and log information, which allows you to determine at which point in history an error or certain condition of the network has occurred, such as its degree of congestion etc. Writing: to change values of the device when the value of their associated tags change. Trapping: to receive events from the device, which are placed in a queue that you will typically interrogate by means of a script and respond to the important ones. -->

In this case you need to: Enable change monitoring for the Analog or Digital agent, as follows: Either edit the agent and check its Enable change monitoring for this agent checkbox or set its BOOLEAN enableChange slot to 1. When enabled, this feature will instantaneously pulse (set and then immediately reset) the Changed specific status bit of this agent. Note1: The valuePrev slot contains the previous value (the value slot) of this agent. Note2: The timePrev slot that provides the timestamp of this previous value ( valuePrev slot) and is only affected by putslots to the value slot NOT the time slot. This slot is not currently supported in realtime catch-up.
