Monitoring digital values Top Monitoring digital values Monitor a digital (Boolean) value, so that you can record the number of On (1) and Off (0) events that occur and the individual and total time of these events. Note: At any time during the monitoring period, click the Reset button to reset all of the output values to 0 and restart their counters. To monitor a digital (Boolean) value If necessary, add and/or select the required Counter spider and/or open its configuration view. For details, see Adding Counter spiders . In the Inputs section: Drag the required data element and/or property (Data spider) or output from a spider onto the Digital Input input. For details, see Creating silks . Note: Ensure that the data type of this value is Boolean, i.e. either 0 or 1, since any other numerical value will not record any events. Set the Start Stop input to 1, to begin the monitoring period. The monitored period will end when this Start Stop input is set to 0 or any other value except for 1. Note: The value of this input can either be supplied by another spider or Data spider (e.g. property or data element) via a silk or it can be typed in manually. Tip: When typing in a value manuall

1. Note: The value of this input can either be supplied by another spider or Data spider (e.g. property or data element) via a silk or it can be typed in manually. Tip: When typing in a value manually, double-click the value column to the right of the Start Stop input name in the Inputs section and type in the required value. The following outputs in the Outputs section are calculated for this value, during the monitored period: Note: The times are displayed in the following format: hours:minutes:seconds. Tip: At any time, you can reset these counters (set the values of all the outputs to 0 and restart their counters). Off Counts: The total number of incidents or events when the Digital Input was in the Off state (0) over the monitored period or since the last reset. Current Off Time: When the Digital Input is currently in the Off state (0), this value displays the actual time of this duration, which is incremented every second, while Digital Input remains in the Off state. Last Off Time: This displays the last duration of time, during the monitored period or since the last reset, when the Digital Input was in the Off state (0). Total Off Time: The total time at the Digital Input

ime: This displays the last duration of time, during the monitored period or since the last reset, when the Digital Input was in the Off state (0). Total Off Time: The total time at the Digital Input has spent in the Off state (0), this is effectively the sum of all the Last Off Time periods during the monitored period or since the last reset. On Counts: The total number of incidents or events when the Digital Input was in the On state (1) over the monitored period or since the last reset. Current On Time: When the Digital Input is currently in the On state (1), this value displays the actual time of this duration, which is incremented every second, while Digital Input remains in the On state. Last On Time: This displays the last duration of time, during the monitored period or since the last reset, when the Digital Input was in the On state (1). Total On Time: The total time at the Digital Input has spent in the On state (1), this is effectively the sum of all the Last On Time periods during the monitored period or since the last reset. -->

Monitoring Message Receipt Top Monitoring Message Receipt One of the methods in which SMS messages sent by a Command agent can be monitored, for auditing purposes, is to require a delivery report to be sent by the recipient as soon as the SMS messages arrives, which logged to the event log. This audit method verifies that the message has been delivered to the recipient’s device. Furthermore, a minimum time period can also be specified in which this delivery report must be received. If this is exceeded then this SMS message can be sent via another Command agent to someone else. In this way it is possible to escalate this message either to a colleague or up the management chain, as is necessary. Note1: It is also possible to ensure that the recipient receives and is aware of a message and, if necessary that this recipient responds within an appropriate time otherwise the message is escalated. For details, see Monitoring Message Response . Note2: For details on specifying the recipient for a Command agent, see Specifying the Recipient Phone Number . The lastMsgReceivedTime slot displays the time of the last message received. The lastMsgReceivedTimeStr slot displays the time of the las

r a Command agent, see Specifying the Recipient Phone Number . The lastMsgReceivedTime slot displays the time of the last message received. The lastMsgReceivedTimeStr slot displays the time of the last message received, as a (var)string. To log delivery reports for all the sent messages: If necessary, add a Command agent. For details, see Adding Agents . Edit the required Command agent. For details, see Editing Agents . This will display the Edit Command agent dialog. Select the Phone tab. Under the SMS Delivery Confirmation group, ensure that the Require delivery report checkbox is checked. Note: Once this checkbox is enabled, the delivery report of all messages that are sent from this Command agent are always logged i.e. this is independent on whether a timeout is configured. To specify the maximum delivery delay and the required escalation Command agent: If necessary, add a Command agent. For details, see Adding Agents . Edit the required Command agent. For details, see Editing Agents . This will display the Edit Command agent dialog. Select the Phone tab. Under the SMS Delivery Confirmation group, ensure that the Require delivery report checkbox is checked. Specify the maximum

ts . This will display the Edit Command agent dialog. Select the Phone tab. Under the SMS Delivery Confirmation group, ensure that the Require delivery report checkbox is checked. Specify the maximum delay period, in minutes, in its Timeout (in minutes) edit box. Note: This delay can only be specified in multiples of 10, however any number less than 10 but greater than 4 will rounded up to the next 10 automatically. Specify the Command agent, which is to be sent the SMS message when this timeout expires, in the Escalation tag edit box. Tip: It is recommended to use the browse button to the right of this edit box, to select and/or add the required Command agent, as this only displays the Command agents currently configured for this Agent Server. -->

ghtweight, report by exception, ISO-standard pub-sub messaging protocol specifically designed for the Internet of Things. The MQTT network consists of publishers, subscribers and a broker. The publishers will publish or send information to the broker, the broker will then relay those messages to the subscribers. The broker is the “middleman” in the network and could be situated in the cloud. A publisher/subscriber are the clients on the network and are linked together by topics. Each Adroit agent can be a publisher and/or subscriber, and acts as a client on the network. If Adroit is a publisher, then it will write values out to other subscribers (when the tag is scanned using Output enabled). When Adroit is a subscriber, then it waits for data on a specific topic from any publisher to that topic. There are three parts of an MQTT transmission: Message: This is the data that is passed through the broker to all clients subscribed to a specific topic on the MQTT network. Topic: Some brokers support topic strings with a maximum of 128 levels and a maximum length of 250 bytes, so an MQTT client connection that exceeds those limits will be closed. QoS: Quality of Service, ensures delivery

s support topic strings with a maximum of 128 levels and a maximum length of 250 bytes, so an MQTT client connection that exceeds those limits will be closed. QoS: Quality of Service, ensures delivery to connected clients: a. At most once - The published message is sent once, and if it does not arrive it is lost. b. At least once - Guarantees that the published message arrives, but there may be duplicates. c. Exactly once - Guarantees that the publish message arrives and that there are no duplicates. 1.1. MultiMedia Agent - Slot Details Top MultiMedia Agent - Slot Details The MultiMedia Agent uses the Windows Multi-media Control Interface (MCI), so that it can "play" .WAV files, .MID files and .AVI files, being sound, Midi and Video for windows respectively. This is meant for audio alarms, but can be used for many other purposes. A typical setup will be for the user to record his own .WAV files and configure a MultiMedia agent to play them. It functions in the same way as the Beeper agent in that the start slot should be non zero for it to play. Priority has no effect. This agent is located in the following file: T_MULTIMEDIA.DLL Slots: Slot Name Type Function dataPersist BOOLEAN Save counter on shutdown. element VARSTRING The full pathname to the multi-media file to be played, e.g. C:\WINNT35\CHIMES.WAV. The Configuration Dialog allows the user to Browse for this file, or type its name explicitly. errMsg STRING Explanation of the error code in the error slot, if applicable. errMsgCont STRING If the explanation of an error does not fit into the errMsg slot, it is continued here. error INTEGER Error Code, e.g. when the element specified isn’t found, or the relevant multi-media device

STRING If the explanation of an error does not fit into the errMsg slot, it is continued here. error INTEGER Error Code, e.g. when the element specified isn’t found, or the relevant multi-media device and drivers aren’t installed. repeat BOOLEAN Repeat the multi-media element over and over again when this is TRUE, until start is 0 or the agent is reset. If this is not TRUE, it will only play once and then switch itself off. reset BOOLEAN When set to True (1) this resets the MultiMedia agent, which causes its start slot to become zero. start INTEGER Starts the MultiMedia agent. This is a counter and can be incremented or decremented. Specific status bits: None Methods of creation: Manual Agents created by default: None For a description of which of these slots are saved to the Adroit database file (.WGP), see: MultiMedia Agent - Database File Format . -->

Multiple Log Sets Top Multiple Log Sets Note: Multiple log sets are no longer required as Adroit provides the DBLog agent that should make SQL logging via the Datalog agent redundant. Also you no longer need multiple proprietary sets with increasing periods and larger time deadbands, since Adroit provides a new datalog backup feature with full trend-retrieval support. Instead of specifying only a single rate and period per datalog agent configuration, you can create multiple log sets within a single datalog agent. In other words, if you need to log a given tag (agent.slot) at different sample/window settings, you can simply create multiple log sets with these different permutations for the SAME tag, without creating separate datalog agents for each permutation. Click for the advantages of using log sets: The advantage of using multiple log sets is this case is that it prevents cumbersome configuration reduces the number of required datalog agents and subsequently decreases the memory requirements and thereby improves performance. Multiple log set usage example: For example, a user may wish to log a tag at 1 second for 2 days, and at 10 seconds for 7 days, and at 60 seconds for 30 d

equirements and thereby improves performance. Multiple log set usage example: For example, a user may wish to log a tag at 1 second for 2 days, and at 10 seconds for 7 days, and at 60 seconds for 30 days and at 1 hour for 365 days. Each of these interval/period specifications constitutes a log set. In the above diagram, two log sets are used for each of the two logged tags. The first log set may be at 1 second for 2 days and the other, 10 seconds for 7 days. It is possible to configure these sets in various combinations. For instance, all the slower logging rates for all tags may be logged to one file while the faster logging rate for all tags logged to another separate file. Alternately, the file for each tag (or set of tags) may be distinct from another tag (or another set of tags) even though each tag may have multiple sets of logging. Thirdly, it is also possible to place all logging into one central file. The data for each datalog agent can be extracted and saved to a CSV file for analysis. When multiple log sets are used, the data for each log set can be extracted and saved to a separate CSV file. Data log clients (for example, trends and OLE method calls) will always retriev

analysis. When multiple log sets are used, the data for each log set can be extracted and saved to a separate CSV file. Data log clients (for example, trends and OLE method calls) will always retrieve data from a matching sample rate set. If there is no matching sample rate set, data will be retrieved from the best matching set. The matching criteria will take the requested rate and period into account. Therefore, trend windows configured at trend rates that match the data log rate will ensure that the data from an actual set is always displayed as long as the required period is within that set. Configuring multiple log sets . -->

Multiply and Divide spiders Top Multiply and Divide spiders The Multiply and Divide spider multiplies and/or divides numerical values. Click for more details: This multiplies the numerators (the multiplying values) and the denominators (the dividing values) to create products for each. The final value is calculated by dividing the numerator product by the denominator product. If necessary, an offset can also be added; in which case a total offset is calculated by adding the offset values together, which is then added to the final value. This spider can ONLY multiply and divide NUMERICAL values. If a string value is supplied then the spider will try to convert the string value to a number before using it. If it cannot be converted, the input is meaningless and will not be used. To add this spider to the spider workspace . To add one or more numerator values . To add one or more denominator values . To add one or more offset values . To remove unnecessary numerator, denominator or offset values . MultiState Data Model Top MultiState Data Model The MultiState agent models a logic table or truth table , which can be used to define the operating and control sequence for equipment and is typically used to control drive groups. Its logic or truth table has the following properties: Up to a maximum of 16 discrete states, such as, for example, Group Auto Ready and OFF, Group in hold, etc. Each state can have a description text up to 64 characters long. A maximum of 16 inputs , various unique combinations of which are used to define the discrete states. These inputs can originate from any Boolean, Integer, or Real data, but will be converted to Boolean TRUE/FALSE indications on being stored in a MultiState agent. MultiState inputs can be sourced either from agents, such as existing Digital agents or directly from PLC registers. This latter option is facilitated by the ability to scan directly into MultiState agent’s inputs (. rawValue slot) without going through an interposing conditioning agent like a digital, and can yield some very substantial benefits in terms of reducing the total number of agents that need to be engineered for a project. Any number of Boolean outputs , can be

ning agent like a digital, and can yield some very substantial benefits in terms of reducing the total number of agents that need to be engineered for a project. Any number of Boolean outputs , can be set TRUE or FALSE on attainment of a particular state. A current state variable, containing the agent’s currently active state. Because there are a maximum of 16 states, 16 agent- Specific Status Bits are used to hold the current state. This approach, namely having a separate bit dedicated to each state, leads to a smooth integration with the Classic user interface multicolor Behaviour, by allowing a different text, line and/or background color for each discrete state. In addition, these bits can be individually alarmed using existing Adroit alarming mechanisms, which means a wide variety of alarm strategies can be developed. If a Multistate input bit is driven by a Digital agent in addition to being scanned to the field, then this input bit will reflect the state of this Digital agent, ignoring any changes made to this Multistate agent’s "rawValue" slot from the field. Note: It is recommended that the Marshal agent be used for this type of application instead. A current state string,

gnoring any changes made to this Multistate agent’s "rawValue" slot from the field. Note: It is recommended that the Marshal agent be used for this type of application instead. A current state string, containing the state description text for the MultiState agent’s currently active state. Each state therefore has the following properties: A state number (1 -16), corresponding to the state’s bit position in the MultiState agent’s status word. A state description text string up to 64 characters long. A 16-bit input-true mask, defining which, if any, of the 16 inputs need to be TRUE for the state to be active (see Common Status Bits ). A 16-bit input-false mask, defining which, if any, of the 16 inputs need to be FALSE for the state to be active. An output-true list, comprising any number of Boolean agent.slots that are automatically set TRUE on attainment of the state. An output-false list, comprising any number of Boolean agent.slots that are automatically set FALSE on attainment of the state. -->

Naming Agents Top Naming Agents Each agent (instance of an agent type) is referred to by its own unique name, so Adroit will not permit an agent name to be used twice within an Agent Server. Usually this name is defined by the user when the agent is created. However, some agents are created by Adroit itself, in which case a name is usually automatically generated. Note: It is important to adhere to the agent naming convention, when naming agents. For details, see Agent Naming Convention . Agent Naming in a Distributed System Furthermore, because of the distributed nature of Adroit it is possible for multiple Agent Servers to be part of the same project, so that Adroit cannot prevent agent names from being duplicated. Therefore, the following two approaches can be taken to resolve the potential duplication of names in a distributed installation when referencing agents: Either the user can ensure all agent names on all Agent Servers are unique, perhaps by keeping a master list. Adroit will assist the user with a prompt to warn him that he is adding a duplicate agent name, with an option to continue or not, whenever he attempts to add an agent name that exists on another Agent Server.

I also assume that some terms related to the operation of Adroit such as proxies and subscriptions make sense at a simple level at least. A working knowledge of scanning is also assumed. The problem Currently we identify 2 short-comings in the Adroit scanning philosophy, these are largely offset by simplicity of configuration, and some automated reasoning in our drivers. However for the more advanced customer who wants total control, and the best possible performance we identify the following.  Double-polling of data when packing in the Front-end has overlaps  Continued polling of data that is not needed in the client at times. We will now lay out the reasons for the problems, and then move onto a proposal in the next section. Unde

Front-end has overlaps  Continued polling of data that is not needed in the client at times. We will now lay out the reasons for the problems, and then move onto a proposal in the next section. Understanding these problems is imperative to the design of a solution. Double-polling: This occurs because the driver always maps I/O addresses that are near to each other into one large task. This happens automatically in the driver based on an optimization algorithm which tries to fetch the largest legal blocks (PDU length) of data since this is the optimal method. This causes a hitch because of a presentation problem. For instance data in an Analog tag in Adroit has 8-byte IEEE float presentation, data in a counter would have 4-byte long. If I/O addresses for these 2 types is interspersed, the driver has to create 2 tasks in order to return the data to Adroit, one for the IEEE presentation, and another for the 4-byte long. Nothing however stops the driver from creating one physical task for both, and converting for both presentations (this may include Booleans and Strings) in memory, saving communications bandwidth. Continuous polling: The scanning sub-system continues to poll for data

r both, and converting for both presentations (this may include Booleans and Strings) in memory, saving communications bandwidth. Continuous polling: The scanning sub-system continues to poll for data even if it is not required. The only current work-around is to create a separate device agent for each plant segment, and scan those tags from it. Then, when the data is not required, stop the device agent. This situation is quite complex, and as a system grows with time, the benefits of this type of configuration are typically eroded by people placing more un-necessary tags on mimics, which causes these scan tasks to run again when only 1 item is needed. Limited data types: Currently the Adroit scanning subsystem is limited to scanning Boolean, Integer, Real and String[80] data types only. The new architecture will break this limitation allowing for datetime and longer strings data types to New Adroit Scanning Architecture (NASA) Page 3 of 15 Last printed 11/15/2017 8:19 AM be communicated as well. User Defined Types, discussed later, will also be supported in that the scanning subsystem. New architecture NASA requires changes in two areas of Adroit’s scanning subsystem: New device a

ed as well. User Defined Types, discussed later, will also be supported in that the scanning subsystem. New architecture NASA requires changes in two areas of Adroit’s scanning subsystem: New device agent A new Device class (called Device_NASA) inherits from the current Device class in the device agent to handle the new architecture. The Device_NASA class does NOT require the use of scan agents. The responsibility for scheduling scan tasks are now demoted to the protocol driver as explained later. The Device_NASA class implements a callback method defined by the CAdroitProtocolDriverCallbacks class which will allow NASA drivers to call back into the device agent. On creation of a device agent, the decision to use the legacy device class or the new class takes place in the Device agent’s construct() API call whereby the driver DLL would be tested for the existence of a new export function called CreateAdroitProtocolDriver, otherwise falling back to the legacy ProtDrvCreate. If CreateAdroitProtocolDriver exists, it implies that the protocol driver is compliant to the new scanning architecture and will be controlled by an instance of Device_NASA. In order to cater for on demand pollin

oitProtocolDriver exists, it implies that the protocol driver is compliant to the new scanning architecture and will be controlled by an instance of Device_NASA. In order to cater for on demand polling, a scan flag bit mask will be introduced for each scanned item that will denote the type of scanning required for each scanned tag. These are: Bit 0 = enable reads Bit 1 = enable writes Bit 2 = output initialize Bit 3 = demand scan It is envisaged that write-only tags will never be marked bad. The scanned Adroit tag type is NOT passed to the driver. The driver shall return all values as COleVariant’s and the Device_NASA class shall be responsible for converting these returned values into the required Adroit type. The driver issues callback to the Device_NASA class in much the way OPC callbacks work viz an array of tag handles, an array of timestamps, an array of variant values and an array of qualities. Obtaining KPI Values Top Obtaining KPI Values One of the possible uses of the database of incidents logged by your AlarmManagement agent/s is to determine how well your process or your operators are meeting the KPIs Key Performance Indicators, quantifiable measurements that measure how well an organization or individual is accomplishing its goals and objectives. that you have set for them regarding alarming . The AlarmManagement agent provides the Integer kpiCalcRate slot that sets the maximum rate at which the KPIs should be calculated, in minutes, to improve the performance of this agent, which by default is set to 1. If this slot is set to 0 then KPI calculations are NEVER executed on new or changed alarm occurrences and so also added the Boolean kpiCalcNow slot that pulses to allow users to perform a KPI calculation at any time, especially when they have set the kpiCalcRate slot to 0. The AlarmManagement agent automatically calculates the following KPIs: The kpi24Hrs slot records the number of alarms per hour for the current 24 hour period. The kpiMonth slot records the number of alarms per hour for the current month. The kpiPrev24Hrs slot records the number of alarms per hour

he number of alarms per hour for the current 24 hour period. The kpiMonth slot records the number of alarms per hour for the current month. The kpiPrev24Hrs slot records the number of alarms per hour for the previous 24 hour period. The kpiPrevMonth slot records the number of alarms per hour for the previous month. The kpiPrevShift slot records the number of alarms per hour for the previous shift. The kpiShift slot records the number of alarms per hour for the current shift. The kpiTotal slot records the number of alarms per hour for the all incidents found in the database. Furthermore, the AlarmManagement agent provides you with the ability to obtain the values of 6 user-defined KPIs. IMPORTANT: Each KPI must be a SELECT query that is performed on the database of logged incidents that returns a SINGLE numeric value called kpi . Obtaining KPI Values Top Obtaining KPI Values One of the possible uses of the database of incidents logged by your AlarmManagement agent/s is to determine how well your process or your operators are meeting the KPIs Key Performance Indicators, quantifiable measurements that measure how well an organization or individual is accomplishing its goals and objectives. that you have set for them regarding alarming . The AlarmManagement agent provides the Integer kpiCalcRate slot that sets the maximum rate at which the KPIs should be calculated, in minutes, to improve the performance of this agent, which by default is set to 1. If this slot is set to 0 then KPI calculations are NEVER executed on new or changed alarm occurrences and so also added the Boolean kpiCalcNow slot that pulses to allow users to perform a KPI calculation at any time, especially when they have set the kpiCalcRate slot to 0. The AlarmManagement agent automatically calculates the following KPIs: The kpi24Hrs slot records the number of alarms per hour for the current 24 hour period. The kpiMonth slot records the number of alarms per hour for the current month. The kpiPrev24Hrs slot records the number of alarms per hour

he number of alarms per hour for the current 24 hour period. The kpiMonth slot records the number of alarms per hour for the current month. The kpiPrev24Hrs slot records the number of alarms per hour for the previous 24 hour period. The kpiPrevMonth slot records the number of alarms per hour for the previous month. The kpiPrevShift slot records the number of alarms per hour for the previous shift. The kpiShift slot records the number of alarms per hour for the current shift. The kpiTotal slot records the number of alarms per hour for the all incidents found in the database. Furthermore, the AlarmManagement agent provides you with the ability to obtain the values of 6 user-defined KPIs. OEE Agent - Slot Details Top OEE Agent - Slot Details The OEE Agent allows you to EITHER calculate the OEE for the monitored equipment and/or plant. Since targeting the three key OEE factors simultaneously, can effect significant improvements in production. OR measure a specific KPI Key Performance Indicator, a quantifiable measurement that measures how well something is accomplishing its goals and objectives. . In other words, individual OEE agents can be applied to any component or part of a process for which a variable denoting a measurement of output is available. KPIs are typically the measurement of some production value over time OR one production value against (divided by) another production value. OEE Agent - Slot Details Top OEE Agent - Slot Details The OEE Agent allows you to EITHER calculate the OEE for the monitored equipment and/or plant. Since targeting the three key OEE factors simultaneously, can effect significant improvements in production. OR measure a specific KPI Key Performance Indicator, a quantifiable measurement that measures how well something is accomplishing its goals and objectives. . In other words, individual OEE agents can be applied to any component or part of a process for which a variable denoting a measurement of output is available. KPIs are typically the measurement of some production value over time OR one production value against (divided by) another production value. OID List OID List The SNMPManager agent can manage a device by getting and/or setting SNMP managed objects (OID values) from a single device on the network. All the selected OIDs are added to the list in the Edit SNMP Manager Agent dialog. Tip: You can use the Export button to save and/or bulk configure these OIDs within a .CSV file. For details, see Exporting the OID List . Each OID in this list contains the following columns: I (Index): The zero-based integer index of this SNMP object in this list. Note: This index is used to select and/or configure OIDs in this list from outside of this agent. For details, see Externally Accessing the OID List . E (Enable): This checkbox determines whether the OID value will be copied into the specified Tag at the applicable rate, so that it can be monitored. For details, see Enabling the Monitoring of OID Values . W (Writable): This checkbox determines whether this OID value will be changed when the value of the specified Tag changes. For details, see Enabling the Changing of Values . Note: Please ensure that the returned data type can be written to. For details, see: SNMP Object Value Return Types. OID (Object Identifier): The OID of this SNMP

see Enabling the Changing of Values . Note: Please ensure that the returned data type can be written to. For details, see: SNMP Object Value Return Types. OID (Object Identifier): The OID of this SNMP object depends on the type of selected object: A General SNMP object: This field simply states "General Object". For details, see Selecting General SNMP Objects . A Browsed SNMP object: This field specifies the unique numeric description of this OID. For further details, see Selecting Browsed SNMP Objects . OLE DB Datasources Top OLE DB datasources An OLE DB datasource exposes the data contained within an OLE DB compliant database or data store. This data is contained within fields in one or more tables. For a practical example of using Select queries one of which uses parameters, which are supplied by controls on a graphic form, see How to chart and/or report data from a database . For an example of using a DataBinder to read and/or write data in a database to and/from a control on a graphic form, see How to write and or read database data from a control . Click for more details: OLE DB is an open standard for accessing data from a variety of sources — both relational and non-relational data including: mainframe and hierarchical databases; e-mail and file system stores; text and graphical data and custom business objects etc. An OLE DB data or service provider is required, before a database or data store can become OLE DB compliant. This data provider ensures that the database shares its data in a uniform or consistent manner using OLE DB. This datasource is added to and configured within the Datasources category of the required Server connection in the Enterprise Manager . For more

data in a uniform or consistent manner using OLE DB. This datasource is added to and configured within the Datasources category of the required Server connection in the Enterprise Manager . For more details, see Adding OLE DB datasources . Click for advanced OLE DB datasource usage information: This datasource can be updated, locked or removed, if necessary. For details, see Updating datasources , Locking datasources or Removing datasources . Instead of manually duplicating an OLE DB datasource from one Server to another, especially when many queries and/or stored procedures have been configured, it is possible to export and import the required datasource. For details, see Exporting datasources . When connecting to a SQL database, the table, view, stored procedure and user function names support schemas. Click for more details: The default schema 'DBO' is NOT displayed. But if a table, view, procedure or function has a different schema name, then this is indicated in brackets after the name of the table, view, procedure or function. This means that you can now have a table, view, procedure or function with the same name as another table, view, procedure or function as long as it b

e name of the table, view, procedure or function. This means that you can now have a table, view, procedure or function with the same name as another table, view, procedure or function as long as it belongs to a different schema. Note1: This datasource provides the following as its data elements: its tables, their fields and any queries which have been created. Note2: Currently both the Client and Server computers need the required OLE DB data provider to be installed. Both computers also need access to the required data store in order to establish a connection to it. Note3: If necessary, the access to this OLE DB datasource, its data and/or queries can be controlled. For details, see Securing datasources . Note4: Each table is monitored at an individually configurable interval for new or updated data by the Server. Note5: Queries can be executed, by using Special Function spiders. Also, if using SQL, please ensure that all time based queries adhere to the universal date time standard for SQL, which is yyyy-mm-dd. For details, see Executing queries and stored procedures . OLE Server Interface Top OLE Server Interface (MISSRVR) The OLE Server Interface allows third party client applications to interact with standalone or distributed Agent Servers. Because OLE is a programming-language-independent standard, third party applications can be written in any OLE enabled development environment, such as Visual Basic™, (VBA) Visual Basic for Applications™, Borland Delphi™, PowerBuilder™, C++, etc. Note: The Adroit Server ActiveX Control (adroitx.ocx) is provided as an alternative to this OLE Server interface. See Adroit Server ActiveX Control . Monitoring Real-time Data describes the steps you need to take to provide continuously updating real-time data for your application. The examples are shown in VBA for ease of understanding. The Adroit Automation Interface describes the OLE Automation or Programmability Interface for Adroit OLE Server Data Objects, which is a set of OLE Automation methods and properties exposed by the Data Objects. These methods are callable as functions and these properties are settable/gettable as variables by container applications. Note1: Adroit also provides a scripting interface, namely the Adroit system object . This is not the

le as functions and these properties are settable/gettable as variables by container applications. Note1: Adroit also provides a scripting interface, namely the Adroit system object . OLE Server Interface API for Adroit Agent Servers Top OLE Server Interface (MISSRVR) API for Agent Servers This OLE Server Interface Specification forms the standard API (Application Programming Interface) for Agent Servers. It effectively defines a contract, by means of which third party client applications can interact in a rich variety of ways with standalone or distributed Adroit configurations. Because OLE is a programming-language-independent standard, third party applications can be written in any OLE enabled development environment, such as Visual Basic™, (VBA) Visual Basic for Applications™ , Borland Delphi™, PowerBuilder™, C++, etc. It is an implementation of the Windows Open Services Architecture, Extensions for Real-time Market Data (WOSA/XRT) standard, as created by the Open Market Data Council For Windows (Microsoft Part Number 098-54432). Unlike other WOSA standards such as MAPI, ODBC, and TAPI, WOSA/XRT does not require new APIs to be defined, nor does it require any production code from Microsoft (other than the OLE DLLs). This is possible because WOSA/XRT leverages the existing architecture and binary standard provided by OLE. Specifically, WOSA/XRT uses the exist

Omron : Sysmac C200H OMRON SYSMAC C200H protocol driver Overview The Adroit Omron protocol driver provides serial connectivity using RS-232 or RS-422 to omron host link modules The C200 and C1000 ,CS1 series amongst others, as well as KEYENCE PLC and Process-Plus modules are supported in this driver. Device configuration Note: The most commonly used settings are for multi-link system operation with station zero even when on RS232. A baud rate of 19200 is suggested if the default of 9600 does not work. Re-start your agent server after changing any of these settings for them to take effect. PLC Details Multi-link System Select to enable multiple link protocol on a RS-422 line. If this option is selected, the Link Unit number must be entered in the ‘PLC Station ID’ field. Single-link System Select to disable multiple link (for point to point communication). PLC Station ID Host Link unit number for multi-link (multidrop) connections PLC Type Applicable SYSMAC PLC types. The PLC type selected will apply to the primary and secondary port if available. This selection currently has no affect on communications. Local Details Port The available serial ports on the machine. Baud Rate The spee

ed will apply to the primary and secondary port if available. This selection currently has no affect on communications. Local Details Port The available serial ports on the machine. Baud Rate The speed of data transmission. Any of the following Baud Rates may be specified 300, 600, 1200, 2400, 4800, 9600, 19200 or 38400. 1 Adroit Protocol Driver Setup Manual Format The transmission format used for the port. Retry The number of times that Adroit will try to gain communication with a PLC before failing a transaction. Time-out The time that Adroit will wait for a valid response from a PLC before failing a transaction (Read or Write). Advanced dialog The settings visible in the advanced dialog should only be modified to optimise configuration. Maximum frames The number of frames that Adroit will grow transactions to. A larger number reduces the number of poll records used, but will reduce performance if the scan points are widely scattered. Force PLC into monitor mode Allow the Driver to put the PLC into monitor mode on startup as well as whenever the PLC mode is changed to run. If at any stage the driver attempts to write to PLC memory and fails because the PLC is in run mode this opt

ut the PLC into monitor mode on startup as well as whenever the PLC mode is changed to run. If at any stage the driver attempts to write to PLC memory and fails because the PLC is in run mode this option will allow the driver to set the PLC mode while running. The driver will fail to write values to PLC memory if it is in run mode. The settings in the advanced dialog will be applied to primary and secondary configurations. Overview OPC (OLE for Process Control) is a standard specification that makes it possible for automation/control software applications and field systems/devices to interoperate and communicate data between each other. To learn more about what OPC is, visit the OPC foundation website http://www.opcfoundation.org/ The OPC Client driver for Adroit communicates to OPC servers that expose at least the OPC DA Custom Interface Version 1.0A. The driver is compatible with OPC DA Version 2.0. As of revision 56 of the driver, it is not version 3.0 compatible. PLEASE NOTE It is very important that Adroit users updating to revision 56 of the OPC client driver re-check all their OPC client device settings as things have changed since. lient device settings as things have changed since. Read especially the setting “Override default DCOM security (for callbacks)” below. By default, older versions of this driver had this setting hardcoded as enabled. Also make a note of newly introduced settings (such as “auto recovery”) and make sure you understand what is being provided for in this new version. “Auto recovery” was not a feature available in older versions of the driver. 1.1. OPC Definitions Top OPC Definitions OPC is short for OLE (Object linking embedding) for Process Control, it is a software technology designed, like OLE to allow different applications to exchange data, more specifically allowing an I/O server developed by a 3rd party to communicate to any SCADA. This allows a SCADA Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition, used to monitor and control an industrial plant or process and its related equipment. such as Adroit to use the same I/O server as any other SCADA, eliminating the need for each SCADA to have its own drivers or I/O server for a device. The technology allows for an OPC item ( scan point a scan point licence that is consumed from your Adroit license when information is being manipulated. ) to be read by a SCADA and, if enabled to do so, to also write to the OPC item. An OPC Item: is a string, uniquely describing an individual data element residing in an OPC server. It may be up to 80 characters long, and structured hierarchically typically using a period "." to separate each level. OPC Data Types: OPC is based on OLE, which uses Variants for all data transferred in transactions. A Variant is basically a block of data preceded by so

ally using a period "." to separate each level. OPC Data Types: OPC is based on OLE, which uses Variants for all data transferred in transactions. A Variant is basically a block of data preceded by some information indicating the actual type of data in the block. A program will automatically convert Variants received to a data type that it is familiar with. Conversions are standardised, and automatically occur in high-level programming languages. An OPC Server is a data source or I/O Server, conforming to the OPC Data Access Specification e.g. the Adroit OPC Server . An OPC Client is an application, which uses the data provided by an OPC server, such as HMI software. -->

OPC Server Security Issues Top OPC Server Security Issues Note: If you still experience issues even after following this procedure, then consult the Configuring OPC DCOM Settings.pdf document in the Adroit Documentation folder of the Adroit DVD , which provides a clear description of the configuration of all the required DCOM settings. OPC client applications are generally unable to connect to remote OPC servers due to DCOM and Windows security reasons. We therefore recommend that both the OPC clients and OPC server computers reside within the same domain to reduce the possible security issues. If this is not possible then please: ensure that the required user accounts (and their passwords) are configured on all OPC client and server computers and ensure that any change to these access details (a user name and/or password) are replicated to all these computers. We also recommended that you configure the lowest or minimum level of DCOM security for both OPC client and server computers, as follows: These settings prevent the domain configuration and the login user names and passwords of each computer from affecting the OPC client to OPC server connection. OPC client applications are generally unable to connect to remote OPC servers due to DCOM and Windows security reasons. We therefore recommend that both the OPC clients and OPC server computers reside within the same domain to reduce the possible security issues. If this is not possible then please: ensure that the required user accounts (and their passwords) are configured on all OPC client and server computers and ensure that any change to these access details (a user name and/or password) are replicated to all these computers. OPC Server Troubleshooting Top OPC Server Troubleshooting See OPC Server Security Issues ,since these are the most prevalent issues relating to the use of OPC. If for no obvious reason: You are losing OPC communications when running Adroit (or any OPC client application) on a Windows XP computer . It takes 30-45 seconds to connect to a remote OPC Server This is caused by a problem on Windows XP operating systems that allows you to add datagram DCOM protocols, even though these operating systems do not support datagram protocols for DCOM. To resolve this, remove the datagram protocols from the DCOM protocols, so that ONLY connection-orientated protocols are listed, as follows: Launch the Component Services Administrative tool. For Windows 2000: From the Start menu, select Programs , Administrative Tools and then click Component Services OR run DCOMCNFG and the refer to step 4. For Windows XP: From the Start menu, select Settings , Control Panel , Administrative Tools , then click Component Services . In the console tree of the Component Services Administrative tool, right-click the computer on which you want to configure the protocols to display the menu. Click the Properties menu i

ent Services . In the console tree of the Component Services Administrative tool, right-click the computer on which you want to configure the protocols to display the menu. Click the Properties menu item to display the Computer Properties dialog box. Click the Default Protocols tab. If any Datagram protocol (UDP/IP or IPX) are listed, then select each one and click Remove . If you do not have any of the connection-orientated protocols in the list, click Add to display the Select DCOM Protocol dialog box. Choose Connection-orientated TCP/IP Protocol as the protocol sequence, and then click Ok . Repeat step 7 to add other connection-orientated protocols to the default protocol. Move the Connection-orientated TCP/IP Protocol to the top of the list. Restart the computer for these changes to take effect. For more information on this subject refer to http://support.microsoft.com/default.aspx?scid=kb;EN-US;q245197 and/or http://support.microsoft.com/default.aspx?scid=kb;EN-US;q242022 -->

To learn more about what OPC UA is, visit the OPC foundation website https://opcfoundation.org/about/opc-technologies/opc-ua/ The OPC UA client driver for Adroit communicates to OPC servers that expose an OPC UA interface. Connectivity The OPC UA client driver communicates with OPC UA Servers in accordance with the OPC UA Specification whose details are beyond the intended scope of this document. Driver Installation and Setup If the Adroit OPC UA Client driver is not installed, you will need to install it. Installation of this driver for the first time will install the OPC Foundation’s OPC UA reditributables if not already installed on your PC. The following files will be installed agent server folder:  d_opc_ua.dll  d_opc_ua.doc  opcuabrowser.exe as well as the following 3rd party dependency files:  libeay32.dll  libxml2.dll  TB5CPP.dll  TB5OT.dll  TB5STACK.dll  TB5UTIL.dll If any of these files is not in the agent directory, then the driver did not install properly. OPC UA Instance Certificates The OPC UA specification requires that all UA clients have an instance certificate that positively identifies client to the server. The instance certifi

install properly. OPC UA Instance Certificates The OPC UA specification requires that all UA clients have an instance certificate that positively identifies client to the server. The instance certificate for Adroit OPC UA is automatically created on the agent server PC when the OPC UA Protocl driver DLL is loaded by PSEXE or AS.EXE for the first time. The instance certificate can also be created manually by executing the %ProgramData%\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\certs\create_instance_certificate.bat file which is found in the folder. Once the batch file has completed, the following folders will have been created under the certs folder: crl issuer own private Adroit OPC UA CLIENT Protocol Driver 2018/10/16 3 rejected trusted The cert_adroit_client.der file will be found in the certs/own folder and the private_key_adroit_client.pem file will be found in the certs/private folder. Select these two files for the instance certificate entries above. Furthermore, the cert_adroit_client.der file needs to be copied to the trusted certificate folder of the OPC UA Server/s that you will be communicating to. Conversely, the OPC UA Server instance certificate needs to be copied to the Adroit sys

e needs to be copied to the trusted certificate folder of the OPC UA Server/s that you will be communicating to. Conversely, the OPC UA Server instance certificate needs to be copied to the Adroit system folder for two way authentication. The certificate types should be the same. OPC UA Server Certificates The OPC UA specification requires that all UA clients trust the server certificate for the OPC UA server that they are connecting to. By default, server certficates will be place in the %ProgramData%\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\rejected folder when a client connects to the OPC UA server for the first time. These must be manually copied to the %ProgramData%\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\trusted folder before a successful connection will be allowed. The dialog has 3 different modes depending on the authentication type selected. ollows for anonymous authentication: Adroit OPC UA CLIENT Protocol Driver 2018/10/16 4 Username authentication looks as follows: Certificate authentication looks as follows: On selecting the […] button for ‘Endpoint URL’ you will be presented with the “Connect to Server” dialog discussed later. User certificates need to be issued by a 3rd party certification authority. Timestamp source – Local, Server or Source. Default is Server  Server – When the OPC server sends a value the driver, whether by exception or from being polled, the OPC server return two timestamps, the timestamp that the server received the value, or the timestamp that the Adroit OPC UA CLIENT Protocol Driver 2018/10/16 5 device/source received the value, by selecting this radio button, the driver will update values with the servers timestamp.  Source – The driver will update values with the device/source timestamp as mentioned above. (NB, do not use this timestamp option if the communication protocol connecting to the device does

mestamp.  Source – The driver will update values with the device/source timestamp as mentioned above. (NB, do not use this timestamp option if the communication protocol connecting to the device does not supply a timestamp)  Local – If this option is selected, the driver will update values with the timestamp of when the driver receives the value. Polled – OPC clients by nature receive data “by exception” from OPC Servers. However, you can use OPC for polling data from front end devices. To learn more about what OPC UA is, visit the OPC foundation website: https://opcfoundation.org/about/opc-technologies/opc-ua/ The OPC UA client driver for Adroit communicates to OPC servers that expose an OPC UA interface. 1.1. Connectivity The OPC UA client driver communicates with OPC UA Servers in accordance with the OPC UA Specification whose details are beyond the intended scope of this document. 1.2. Operating charting controls Operating charting controls This topic briefly explains how end-users are able to interact with charting controls, in run-time i.e. typically when its graphic form is opened in the Smart UI Operator. General charting control interaction: Charting toolbar : This toolbar allows your end-users to print and/or preview the chart, change the magnification of the charted data, rotate the chart and if necessary chart additional data, amongst other actions. Tip: You can hide or show this user toolbar, by using the following shortcut: CTRL+M. Note: Enable the (Appearance) ToolbarVisible property of this charting control to display this toolbar. The appearance of certain tools are also controlled by Boolean properties. Chart interaction: Users can interact with the plot area of the chart, as follows: Display or hide series: Check or clear the relevant checkboxes in the series legend (on the chart), if these appear. Zooming in: To zoom into a particular region of a chart Click the top left most corner of the area that needs to be magnified or enlarged in the trend. Hold the left mouse button down and drag down towards the bottom right hand corner of the required are

t Click the top left most corner of the area that needs to be magnified or enlarged in the trend. Hold the left mouse button down and drag down towards the bottom right hand corner of the required area. This will display a dashed box that defines the area of the graph that will be enlarged. Release the left mouse button once the required area has been defined. Tip: The toolbar button provides generalized zooming functionality, by decreasing the scaling by 10%. Note: When using a Line or XYPlot to trend real-time values, the width (Interval) of the chart cannot be changed when zooming. Tip: When using a Line or XYPlot to trend real-time values, scroll back by one interval and then zoom in. Panning (moving the trended data): Right-click and drag to move to data that is above, below, to the left or right of the current chart area. Note: This is especially useful if you have zoomed into historical data when using a Line or XYPlot to trend real-time values. Reset zooming and panning (return to original magnification and location): Click anywhere in the graph, hold the left mouse button down and drag upwards towards the top left hand corner and release the left mouse button. Note: Ensure

to original magnification and location): Click anywhere in the graph, hold the left mouse button down and drag upwards towards the top left hand corner and release the left mouse button. Note: Ensure that a sizable area has been defined before releasing. Tip: It is also possible to use the Zoom home functionality provided by the toolbar to reset the zooming. Line and XYPlot charting control interaction: Trending of data: The Line and XYPlot charting controls can trend live data, as follows: When the charting control is displayed in run-time any historical data for the data elements connected to its series, is fetched from the relevant datasource(s) and displayed. Note: The configuration of the TimeInfo property determines whether this charting control displays real time or historical trending. For details, see Important charting control properties. If this charting control has been configured for real time trending, then as the current data is received from the relevant datasources, this data is immediately plotted. Note: The rate at which the data is fetched is dependent upon the configuration of its Interval property. If this charting control has been configured for historical t

his data is immediately plotted. Note: The rate at which the data is fetched is dependent upon the configuration of its Interval property. If this charting control has been configured for historical trending, then only the data recorded for these data elements during the specified period of time will be displayed. Note: The charted time period can also be altered at runtime, however any changes made will NOT be saved. For details, see Modifying chart time at runtime . Charting data legend: The data legend is typically displayed beneath Line and XYPlot charting controls to provide statistical information about the series: Each of the following columns, which are listed from left to right, can be sorted and resized, as required: Series: The names of the charted series of data. Minimum: The lowest value of each series for the currently displayed “window” of charted data, which is updated continuously. Maximum: The highest value of each series for the currently displayed “window” of charted data, which is updated continuously. Average: The average value of each series for the currently displayed “window” of charted data, which is updated continuously. Note: When the Scroll line to view

d data, which is updated continuously. Average: The average value of each series for the currently displayed “window” of charted data, which is updated continuously. Note: When the Scroll line to view historical values toolbar option is enabled, two additional columns are added to the legend after this column, namely Historical and Time , which display the value and the date and time of the historical value currently selected by the scroll line. Current: The current or last value of each series of charted data, which is updated continuously. Count: The number of values/points plotted by the current series. Std Dev: The standard deviation of the current series or a measure of the degree of variance within this series. Errors: When doing historical trending, this displays any historical data retrieval errors for this series. Note: Enable the (Appearance) DataLegendVisible property of this charting control to display this toolbar. Tip: The height of this legend and the widths of these columns can also be configured using the DataLegend properties of the charting control. -->

Operating FileBrowser controls Top Operating FileBrowser controls This topic briefly explains how end-users can view, edit, upload and/or delete documents provided by the FileBrowser control, at runtime. To open a document: navigate to and double click the document, just like when using Windows Explorer. To add a document: right click the required folder and select the Upload Document item. SmartUI transfers the file that you browse in to the SmartUI Server. To edit a document: open (double-click) a file and make the necessary changes and save and close it. SmartUI transfers this modified file to the SmartUI Server, ensuring that the SmartUI Server is always updated with the latest changes. To delete a document or folder: right click it and select the Delete menu item and then click the Yes button on the confirmation dialog. WARNING! This removes the selected files and/or folders and their sub-folders from the SmartUI Server – so use this with caution! To refresh the display of part or the entire folder tree: right click the required folder and select the Refresh item. Note: If this is applied to a folder, then all of its sub-folders are also refreshed. This displays all the files

the entire folder tree: right click the required folder and select the Refresh item. Note: If this is applied to a folder, then all of its sub-folders are also refreshed. This displays all the files that you have added and removes any files/folders that you have deleted. -->

Therefore if you want to maintain separate lists of sets for your TrendConfigurator controls, then rename this variable of each TrendConfigurator control in the The Setting Name to use to load and save the Set configuration to the Users Profile field of the General Settings tab of the TrendConfigurator Setup dialog (the UserProfileSetting property). For each Pen (tag or value) that you select to be trended as part of a set, you can specify the following: IMPORTANT: You need to click the Save Set button (on the right of the TrendConfigurator control ) after adding or configuring one or more series to this list, to save these changes to the current set (as specified by the Set Name drop-down list on the right of the TrendConfigurator control). Otherwise when you close this graphic form, the new serie

is list, to save these changes to the current set (as specified by the Set Name drop-down list on the right of the TrendConfigurator control). Note: You may need to click the Refresh Chart button to view with any series that you add to the current set. Operator Action spiders Top Operator Action spiders The Operator Action spider performs various operations on a numerical input, such as increasing or decreasing it by a configurable amount; setting it to TRUE (1 i.e. non-zero) or to FALSE (0) or inverting its current Boolean state accordingly. Operator connection settings Operator connection settings This page of the Setting up the Operator component of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog, provides the following settings that specify the default data connection that is established between this Smart UI Operator and the specified Smart UI Server at login: To display this page of settings: When the Smart UI Operator is launched, it needs to log into a Smart UI Server computer, which stores the data configured within the Smart UI Operator. Launch the Adroit Config Editor . The Welcome section is displayed by default, unless multiple configurations have been created, in which case the Configuration page is displayed by default, which needs to be expanded to display the Welcome section. For details, see Working with Configurations. Select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the Setting up the Operator option. Note: If this option does not appear then the Smart UI Operator may not be installed. Select the Connection Settings option. Tip1: You can navigate directly to this page using the left pane of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog. For detail

t UI Operator may not be installed. Select the Connection Settings option. Tip1: You can navigate directly to this page using the left pane of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog. For details, see Working with configuration dialogs. Tip2: Press the Next or Previous buttons to display the other pages of settings. Login Server: this specifies the default Smart UI Server computer that this Smart UI Operator connects to during the login process. Note: ONLY the user profiles configured on this specified Smart UI Server can be applied to the users of this Smart UI Operator. To specify the login Server computer name: If necessary, type the required name into the provided edit box. Note : Please ensure that the name of this computer is correctly spelt; otherwise the login process will not succeed. The following are typical login errors that occur when this name is incorrectly specified: “Requested service not found” -> The Server has not completed loading yet “No connection could be made because the target machine actively refused it” -> There is no running server Data communication method: select the required method that data is transferred within the established connection betw

made because the target machine actively refused it” -> There is no running server Data communication method: select the required method that data is transferred within the established connection between this Smart UI Server and Smart UI Operator. To specify the required communication method: Select the required option. The optimal method depends upon the network (bandwidth) connecting this Smart UI Server and Smart UI Operator, as follows: Subscribe : recommended when using a Local Area Network as this provides the fastest response time by requiring the highest bandwidth. Poll(send all values) : recommended when using a high bandwidth Internet connection. Poll(send most recent values) : recommended when using a low bandwidth Internet connection. For further details concerning these methods, see About connection communication methods . The bandwidth requirements for this connection depends upon a number of factors, such as the update requirements and the size of the graphic forms. However, you can ensure that the selected communication method provides sufficient bandwidth for the needs of your project, by adopting the following recommendations: Keep the graphic form sizes small; fo

ver, you can ensure that the selected communication method provides sufficient bandwidth for the needs of your project, by adopting the following recommendations: Keep the graphic form sizes small; for example use JPG files instead of BMP files. Plan the graphic forms beforehand with the end-user in mind, including the bandwidth that will be available. Develop an end-to-end prototype to test in a production environment in order to satisfy all requirements (including the communication requirements). Only once this prototype has been successfully tested should the project be completely engineered. Connection status check frequency: specify how often the Smart UI Operator should test that the Smart UI Server connection is still healthy and is not disconnected. To specify the required interval between checking the connection, in seconds: Either type in the required value directly or use the arrows of this spin control to obtain the required value. Operator customization Smart UI Operator customization User profiles can customize the default display and permitted user interaction within the Smart UI Operator window. Note: You can also specify default Smart UI Operator settings are applied before a user logs on. For details, see Default Operator user interface settings or Operator command line arguments . To customize the Smart UI Operator display and user interaction: In the Smart UI Designer, create a profile or edit the profile that applies to the current user. Tip: Any user not associated with a profile has the Default profile applied to them. In the Profile Configuration dialog, select the Operator Settings dialog, from the left pane. Select the required setting to highlight the row and then configure this setting. Tip: It is also possible to double-click either the setting name or its value cell to expand or highlight numerical values selections or select the next value within the lists. Edit : for Adroit datasources ONLY, this option opens the Adroit Agent Configurator with this tag (agent) selected (if it can be found), so that it can be edited. Note: Since this option ONLY applies to Adroit datasources and even then t

his option opens the Adroit Agent Configurator with this tag (agent) selected (if it can be found), so that it can be edited. Note: Since this option ONLY applies to Adroit datasources and even then the editing of tags in the Smart UI Operator poses a security risk, so the display of this option is controlled via the AllowEditTags Boolean setting of the Operator Settings page of the profile dialog, which is False (hidden) by default. Customizable Smart UI Operator settings and their required configuration AllowEditTags: this setting applies, when linking tags from Adroit datasources to controls and vectors of graphic forms. In this case, this option determines whether your Operator users have the ability to edit the exposed Adroit tags, which are displayed either through the use of Show (All) Information or the Bad tag status indicators. For details on these tag exposing mechanisms, see Working with Show (All) Information and Bad tag status indicators . IMPORTANT: This option is disabled (False) by default, due to the security risk posed by allowing your operators to edit tags on the fly. AlwaysOnTop: to enable or disable the initial display of the Smart UI Operator window to be ab

ed (False) by default, due to the security risk posed by allowing your operators to edit tags on the fly. AlwaysOnTop: to enable or disable the initial display of the Smart UI Operator window to be above all other applications. By default this is disabled (False). CanClose: to allow users to close the Smart UI Operator window (True) or not (False). Configuration: Click the drop-down list box button at the right of this field and select the required value. Note: If the user CANNOT close the Smart UI Operator window, the close button will still appear in the top left hand corner but will not work. DefaultGraphicFormLevel: to select which level is initially displayed by the graphic form, specified by the DefaultGraphicFormPath setting. Configuration: Type in or paste (right click and select Paste ) the required level name or leave this field blank to select the first level, as usual. Note: If the specified level does not exist in this graphic form, then the first level is selected. DefaultGraphicFormPath: to select the default graphic form that is displayed when the Smart UI Operator window opens. Configuration: Click the browse button at the right of this field to launch the Graphic

tGraphicFormPath: to select the default graphic form that is displayed when the Smart UI Operator window opens. Configuration: Click the browse button at the right of this field to launch the Graphic Form Selection configuration dialog to locate this graphic form from its required project within the correct Server or leave this field blank. DefaultGraphicFormTemplateSet: to select which template set is initially activated in the graphic form, specified by the DefaultGraphicFormPath setting. Configuration: Type in or paste (right click and select Paste ) the required template set name or leave this field blank to select the "Default" template set, as usual. Note: If the specified template set does not exist in this graphic form, then the "Default" template set is selected. FullScreen: to display the title bar at the top of the Smart UI Operator window (False) or not (True). Configuration: Click the drop-down list box button at the right of this field and select the required value. ShowContextMenu: to allow users to display the right-click menu in the Smart UI Operator window (True) or not (False). Note: This menu can close the Smart UI Operator window, configure its always-on-top pr

ontextMenu: to allow users to display the right-click menu in the Smart UI Operator window (True) or not (False). Note: This menu can close the Smart UI Operator window, configure its always-on-top property and toggle the Operator mode i.e. to hide or display the Levels and Layers window. Configuration: Click the drop-down list box button at the right of this field and select the required value. Note: If this setting is disabled, this ALSO disables the Ctrl+0 and Ctrl+T shortcuts to entirely prevent this menu from being displayed in the Smart UI Operator. ShowMaximize: to allow users to maximize the Smart UI Operator window (True) or not (False). Configuration: Click the drop-down list box button at the right of this field and select the required value. ShowMinimize: to allow users to minimize the Smart UI Operator window (True) or not (False). Configuration: Click the drop-down list box button at the right of this field and select the required value. StartupBorderStyle: to specify the window type used for the graphic forms, which determine how users can interact with each graphic form window. Configuration: Click the drop-down list box button at the right of this field and select

window type used for the graphic forms, which determine how users can interact with each graphic form window. Configuration: Click the drop-down list box button at the right of this field and select one of the following styles: Note: Each style has its own pre-set properties, experiment with these styles as necessary. FixedSingle: This has a title bar and frame, therefore you are able to close, move, minimize or maximize this window, although you are unable to resize it. Fixed3D: Similar to FixedSingle , except that it has a 3D frame, which makes its contents seem sunken. FixedDialog: Similar to FixedSingle , except that its a dialog. Sizable: Similar to FixedSingle , except that you are also able to resize this window. FixedToolWindow: Similar to FixedSingle , except its a dockable window that you are unable to resize. SizableToolWindow: Similar to Sizable , except that its a dockable window. StartupLocation: to MANUALLY set the location of the Smart UI Operator window on the screen, by specifying the required position of the top left corner of the window in pixels. Tip: The StartupWindowPosition setting provides preset system-dependent startup positions. Configuration: These pix

by specifying the required position of the top left corner of the window in pixels. Tip: The StartupWindowPosition setting provides preset system-dependent startup positions. Configuration: These pixel measurements are measured relative to the top left corner of the screen. The first digit specifies the leftmost (X) position and the second the topmost (Y) position. Either specify both positions separated by a comma or expand this setting and specify these positions separately. Note1: Only integer values can be used when specifying these positions. Note2: This setting is overridden if the StartupWindowPosition setting is NOT set to Manual . StartupSize: to set the maximum dimensions of the Smart UI Operator window on the screen, by specifying the required window size in pixels. Configuration: These pixel measurements are relative to the size of the screen. The first digit specifies the width of the window and the second digit specifies its height. Either specify both dimensions separated by a comma or expand this setting and specify these dimensions separately. Note: Only integer values can be used when specifying these positions. StartupWindowPosition: to set the location of the S

ed by a comma or expand this setting and specify these dimensions separately. Note: Only integer values can be used when specifying these positions. StartupWindowPosition: to set the location of the Smart UI Operator window on the screen, by selecting one of the preset system-dependent startup positions. Configuration: Click the drop-down list box button at the right of this field and select one of the following preset system-dependent startup positions: Manual: This is the default option, which uses the StartupLocation setting to determine the location of the Smart UI Operator window on the screen at startup. CenterScreen: This option overrides the StartupLocation setting and positions the Smart UI Operator window in the centre of the screen. WindowsDefaultLocation: This option overrides the StartupLocation setting and cascades the Smart UI Operator window at the Windows default location on the screen. WindowsDefaultBounds: This option overrides the StartupLocation setting and positions the Smart UI Operator window at the Windows default location on the screen and has its bounds determined by the Windows default. CenterParent: This option overrides the StartupLocation setting and

ns the Smart UI Operator window at the Windows default location on the screen and has its bounds determined by the Windows default. CenterParent: This option overrides the StartupLocation setting and positions the Smart UI Operator window in the centre of its parent form, which is not applicable in this case. Note: These startup positions, with the exception of Manual , typically use the currently selected active monitor (monitor with the mouse cursor) when dual monitors are being used, which is determined by the windows video driver. Tip: It is recommended that this setting either be set to Manual (default) or CenterScreen . StartupWindowState: to select the initial state of the Smart UI Operator window - in other words should this window be maximized, normal or minimized. Configuration: Click the drop-down list box button at the right of this field and select the required state. For details, see Working with Configurations. Select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the Setting up the Operator option. Note: If this option does not appear then the Smart UI Operator may not be installed. Select the Login Settings option. e Login Settings option. Tip1: You can navigate directly to this page using the left pane of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog. For details, see Working with configuration dialogs. Default login user name: specify the name of the most prevalent user of this Smart UI Operator, which the login dialog always displays. To specify the default login username: If necessary, type the required name into the provided edit box. Note : Ensure this user name is correctly spelt, otherwise it needs to be manually corrected before this, user can login. Automatic login of the default user: in a single-user or non-secure environment, you can save time launching the Smart UI Operator, by having the necessary login details automatically specified. To configure automatic login: Either select Yes to enable or No to disable this setting. WARNING! Since this setting bypasses Smart UI security, this setting is only recommended when security is not important, such as when one user uses this Smart UI Operator exclusively. However, this facility can prevent users of the Smart UI Operator from knowing the password of t

re the display of the automatic login option: Either select Yes to enable or No to disable this setting. Note : Hide (disable) this setting when the Operator has more than one user to ensure the security of Smart UI . This page only configures the part of the essential Smart UI Operator settings. For details, see Setting up the Operator . For details on displaying all the related Smart UI Operator settings, see the Advanced Operator settings page . -->

g with configuration dialogs. Tip2: Press the Next or Previous buttons to display the other pages of settings. Default script references: specify the list of external assemblies or dynamic linked library (.DLL) files that are automatically added to each script. Note: The longer the list of references, the longer it takes to load and compile every script. Tip: This setting allows 3 rd party users to expose their product-specific assemblies (DLLs) to all their scripts. To add a default script reference: Click the Add button and browse for the required assembly. Note : Ensure that the paths of all of these files are added to the Script references paths setting so they will be located. To remove a default script reference: Select the assembly that is no longer required and press the Remove button. WARNING! The reference to the selected assembly is immediately removed, so ensure that you select the required assembly. Search paths for script references: specify additional paths that contain the assemblies (.DLL files) that are referenced by your scripts. For further details regarding script references, see Managing references. WARNING! Only specify the locations to assemblies (.DLL files) that you use frequently, since an extensive list will delay the loading and compilation times of all scripts.
