Out of limit data logging Top Out of limit data logging Out of limit monitoring enables Datalog agents to immediately log out of limit values (values that are not within their specified operating range), by ignoring the normal time deadband value and using the faster log rate specified by the out of limit time deadband instead. In other words, as soon as the logged value that is being logged, enters or leaves its user-specified limit range it is logged unconditionally, and continues to be logged at the new time deadband as specified by the Out of limit logging time setting ( Time... ). This allows the Datalog agent to catch short spikes whose duration is less than the normal time deadband logging interval ( Deadbands -> Time... ) Usage Example: A customer wants to monitor his incoming voltage of 220 V. Previously, without using out of limit monitoring: he would create a Datalog agent to log this voltage tag at a logging rate of 1 second for a period of 1 week. So, in this case, this Datalog agent is configured ( Length = 7 days and Deadbands Time = 1 sec) to log all changes to the voltage at 1 second and always keep one week's worth of this data. Using out of limit monitoring: sinc

talog agent is configured ( Length = 7 days and Deadbands Time = 1 sec) to log all changes to the voltage at 1 second and always keep one week's worth of this data. Using out of limit monitoring: since he is actually not that interested in logging this voltage, if it remains within its normal operating voltage range of 215-225 volts, as long as the voltage is within this value range he is happy to log it at a far slower rate - say 10 seconds. But when the voltage breaches this range, then he wants this Datalog agent to log this value at 1 second intervals. So, in this case, this Datalog agent is configured ( Length = 7 days and Deadbands Time = 10 sec and Out of limit monitoring Time = 1 sec and Upper limit = 225 and Lower limit = 215). Note: In this case he will be able to catch short voltage spikes whose duration whose duration are less 10 seconds, the normal logging interval. Out of limit data logging Top Out of limit data logging Out of limit monitoring enables Datalog agents to immediately log out of limit values (values that are not within their specified operating range), by ignoring the normal time deadband value and using the faster log rate specified by the out of limit time deadband instead. In other words, as soon as the logged value that is being logged, enters or leaves its user-specified limit range it is logged unconditionally, and continues to be logged at the new time deadband as specified by the Out of limit logging time setting ( Time... ). This allows the Datalog agent to catch short spikes whose duration is less than the normal time deadband logging interval ( Deadbands -> Time... ) Usage Example: A customer wants to monitor his incoming voltage of 220 V. Previously, without using out of limit monitoring: he would create a Datalog agent to log this voltage tag at a logging rate of 1 second for a period of 1 week. So, in this case, this Datalog agent is configured ( Length = 7 days and Deadbands Time = 1 sec) to log all changes to the voltage at 1 second and always keep one week's worth of this data. Using out of limit monitoring: sinc

talog agent is configured ( Length = 7 days and Deadbands Time = 1 sec) to log all changes to the voltage at 1 second and always keep one week's worth of this data. Using out of limit monitoring: since he is actually not that interested in logging this voltage, if it remains within its normal operating voltage range of 215-225 volts, as long as the voltage is within this value range he is happy to log it at a far slower rate - say 10 seconds. But when the voltage breaches this range, then he wants this Datalog agent to log this value at 1 second intervals. So, in this case, this Datalog agent is configured ( Length = 7 days and Deadbands Time = 10 sec and Out of limit monitoring Time = 1 sec and Upper limit = 225 and Lower limit = 215). Note: In this case he will be able to catch short voltage spikes whose duration whose duration are less 10 seconds, the normal logging interval. Overview Top Working with the SmartUI The primary purpose of the SmartUI is to provide a web enabled, data visualization tool that is able to collaborate with data from a number of sources. The data can be accessed and manipulated from one or more local, LAN or Internet clients. The data can be secured at the data element level on a per user basis for read/write/no access. CAD type tools are provided for the design of graphic forms (mimics) that contain a mixture of vector drawing and windows components for visualizing and manipulated the data. Stand-alone operator environments then allow access to these graphic forms via a smart client application. Overview of the SmartUI architecture: The SmartUI consists of three main components: The Server: this is the "data portal" - it aggregates data from a number of disparate sources via "datasource plug-ins" which convert data from the outside world into a generic SmartUI format called a "data element". The Server also contains datasources designed to hold all user information and configured graphic forms. The Designer: this is used to configure datasources and data elements in the Server and allows for the design of graphic forms to visua

igned to hold all user information and configured graphic forms. The Designer: this is used to configure datasources and data elements in the Server and allows for the design of graphic forms to visualise and interact with the data. The Operator: this is a “smart client”, which allows access to the configured graphic forms for the viewing and manipulation of data, over a LAN or over the Internet. The Click Once Operator allows a user to use a fully fledged Operator, which is downloaded via Internet Explorer and runs normally, as a separate application. The reasons for having two Client applications: The Operator has been designed to be able to provide across the Web reporting The future Win CE version of the Operator Ability to combine both when designing The real world problems that SmartUI solves: It’s a real time data portal Real time data over the Internet Secure open client architecture (OEM extensibility) Roaming user profiles Internationalization (translation) of mimics Full UI and Server scripting Containment of ActiveX, .NET & 3rd-party controls in mimics Web Service compatible - both as a consumer and provider -->

Performance Monitoring Top Performance Monitoring The PerfMon agent has been created for measuring the performance of your own computer or other computers on a network. On each computer, you can view the Behaviour of objects such as the Agent Server, processors, memory, cache, threads, and other processes. Since Adroit is a 32 bit application, if you have installed a 64 bit operating system then when you run the default Performance Monitor (PERFMON.EXE) all the counters for Adroit will be missing, because the 64 bit version of PERFMON is being run which can only load 64bit counter dlls! Therefore, in order to force Windows to load the 32 bit version of PERFMON, open the Command Prompt and specify the following statement: mmc /32 perfmon.msc Each of these objects has an associated set of counters that provide information on such things as device usage, queue lengths, delays, as well as information used for throughput and internal congestion measurements. Up to 16 counters can be added to a single PerfMon agent. The values of these counters are updated every second. The following list provides an overview of what you can do with the PerfMon agent to view the performance of objects: L

o a single PerfMon agent. The values of these counters are updated every second. The following list provides an overview of what you can do with the PerfMon agent to view the performance of objects: Log the data from the configured counters. The values of the counters can also be assigned to other Adroit tags, such as Analog agents, which can then be alarmed whenever this value goes over or under a user-defined value etc. Create a trend of the configured counters. The following performance counters are added, by default, to first PerfMon agent created: CPU load i.e. \\Processor(_Total)\\% Processor Time Agent Server CPU load i.e. \\Process(as)\\% Processor Time Total memory used i.e. \\Memory\\Committed Bytes Agent Server memory usage i.e. \\Process(as)\\Private Bytes Agent Server put slots i.e. \\Agent Server(name (project))\\PutSlots -->

Phase Actions and Tag/Value of a Master Recipe Top Phase Actions and Tag/Value of a Master Recipe A phase always ends with a Phase Action , and therefore may have several ingredient steps preceding it. A phase action can be any of the following keywords: GOTO STEP <step number>; DELAY <milliseconds> or VARIABLE. A GOTO STEP action will cause an active recipe to jump to the step given in the Tag/Value field. The Tag/Value for a GOTO STEP action may either be an explicit step number or an agent.slot that holds the step number. A DELAY action will delay the execution of an active recipe by the number of milliseconds given in the Tag/Value field. Note: The Tag/Value for a DELAY action may either be an explicit delay time or an agent.slot that holds the delay time. A VARIABLE action will alter recipe execution based on the value of the agent.slot given in the Tag/Value field, as follows: Slot value Action 0 Wait until the slot value changes to a value between 1 and 6 and then perform the action associated with this number 1 Go to next step 2 Go to previous step 3 Go to first step 4 Go to last step 5 Perform verification failure rollback 6 Stop recipe execution Note: the Tag/Value for a

The Tag/Value field may also be an explicit number between 0 and 6. This is usually done to force the end of a phase and thus ensure verification checking to take place. -->

text: Philosophy for End User Applications Top Philosophy for End User Applications The general philosophy is for the user to create an instance of a coarse grained object, and then instruct the object to create many finer grained objects inside itself. A coarse grained object corresponds to a connection to a known Agent Server, either running on the same computer as the application, or some other computer on a local- or wide-area network. In WOSA/XRT terminology, a coarse grained object is a Data Object , and a fine-grained object is a Request Object . A Request object formally describes the pieces of information we require from the Data object. It consists of data that identifies the information we want, plus data which names the specific fields related to that information. For real time Adroit data this corresponds to an agent and the associated slots we are interested in, whereas for historical data, it corresponds to a time and the associated agent.slots we are interested in. The individual fields of each request are stored as a Properties Collection . A single Request collection can hold many Request objects at once. Once we have created requests on the Data Object, the easiest way

dual fields of each request are stored as a Properties Collection . A single Request collection can hold many Request objects at once. Once we have created requests on the Data Object, the easiest way to get at the required data is to ask the object to paste links to the data into our containing application, which needs to be able to process the paste. When the links are pasted onto the application, the application activates the links, and the Data object supplies the application with ongoing updates. In addition to the basic WOSA/XRT features described above, our OLE server provides a number of Adroit -specific extensions. These include the provision of an output mode that permits the poking of values from a container application to an Agent Server, the ability to fetch values in a one-off fashion from an Agent Server, the ability to connect to a remote Agent Server, the ability to create and remove agents in an Agent Server, etc. -->

PID Alarm Limits Top PID Alarm Limits The PID agent type provides alarming capabilities for both the PV (process value) and the %Error or the percentage deviation of the PV from the SP (the required set-point). As such it is possible to define L, LL, H and HH for the PV and an H and HH alarm for the %Error, for each instance of the PID agent. The L (low)and H (high) inner alarms are the first warning that a process value has moved outside its acceptable range, and implies that corrective action must be taken, by the control algorithm, as soon as possible. The LL (low low) and HH (high high) outer alarms are the second warning that the process value has moved further from its acceptable range and reached the second alarm limit. This implies that the first warning has been ignored and urgent and immediate corrective action, by the control algorithm, is now required. Note: that whenever the LL alarm is on, the L alarm must by definition already be on. Similarly, whenever the HH alarm limit is reached, the H alarm limit will already have been passed. The alarm will not be cleared until the process value goes past the limit. When the value of the PValue or Error slot of the agent reache

t is reached, the H alarm limit will already have been passed. The alarm will not be cleared until the process value goes past the limit. When the value of the PValue or Error slot of the agent reaches one or more of these configured limits, the agent will set the relevant specific status bit . Any Alarm agent subscribing to the PID agent will detect these status bits. -->

Method PokeWithTime(Agent, Slot : string; Value : variant; Timestamp : datetime) : boolean; This method changes the historical value of a tag. Note: This can ONLY be used to change PAST values of tags NOT current or future values. However, a value that is the SAME as the previous time sample will NOT be accepted. For instance, if a value is being logged hourly and the value at 10:00 is 1 then you will be unable to set the 11:00 value to 1. But if the value at 10:00 is 0 then you will can set the 11:00 value to 1. Parameters: Agent: the name of the agent or tag (agent.slot) whose value is to be changed. Slot: the name of the slot whose value is to be changed. This parameter is ignored if the Agent parameter contains a tag. Value: the required value. Timestamp: the (historical) time when this value was changed. Returns: If the call is successful the function returns TRUE else it returns FALSE. Use LastError / LastErrorNum to determine the cause of failure. -->

Primary / Secondary – Select the primary or secondary button depending on which connection you wish to configure. 3.1.2. Bold top line – Top 2 lines of sign in bold Bold bottom line - Lines 3 & 4 in bold _____________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ ATQMS-DRVR-DOC-POLY_ETH.docx P a g e | 7 Auto centre text – Text centres itself on the sign Display code (style)- Controls the way that text appears on the display. Auto centre text – Text centres itself on the sign Display code (style)- Controls the way that text appears on the display. Line width Specify the line width (maximum of 40) in characters wide that the display is. This will only affect datascope text displayed. 3.1.3. Sign Settings Use acknowledgments – The driver should request and wait for the ACK from the sign. If this option is on, and the sign must acknowledge in order for the driver to be able to determine if the communication is working. This option may not work on most signs, if the RS232 transmit from the sign is not connected. Send PC time to sign – The driver will send the local time to the Sign each time a message is sent. Allow multiple sign clients – The driver will disconnect and reconnect with each message sent, this will allow use in a cluster or situation where 2 devices control the sign content. 3.1.4. Local Details IP Address – TCP/IP address of the sign. Port – The port used at this IP address to communicate. y - The number of times that Adroit will try to gain communication with a PLC before failing a transaction. If the sign does not have an internal clock (requires time sent from PC) and temperature sensor, these options have no effect. Apply Button – Use this button to save the settings without leaving the dialog, you may use the dialog to customise the sign appearance (any setting in the sign details group) and then send a message to the sign straight away from Adroit to see the effects of the selections. _____________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ ATQMS-DRVR-DOC-POLY_ETH.docx P a g e | 8 4. Supported Addresses 4.1. Addresses The driver will scan a string slot using an address mnemonic made up of an alphabetic and numeric characters, e.g. : “FRED001” The string will be converted to upper case and is used by the driver to identify each message apart. PLEASE NOTE THE SCAN-RA

mnemonic made up of an alphabetic and numeric characters, e.g. : “FRED001” The string will be converted to upper case and is used by the driver to identify each message apart. PLEASE NOTE THE SCAN-RATE MUST BE ZERO! 4.2. Scanning You may use a notify agent to scan, put a Sign address of 1 into the user code of the notify agent, and then scan the rawValue slot to the driver. Each notify agent can thus address a sign uniquely. The default address for a sign (since usually only one sign will be on the Ether-Pad) is 1. _____________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ ATQMS-DRVR-DOC-POLY_ETH.docx P a g e | 9 5. Protocol Definition and Considerations 5.1. Message Details You must manually address a sign when not using the Notify agent by inserting the station/sign number in at the beginning of the string followed by a comma, e.g.: “5,East-dam level high”, will address the sign #5 with the message “East-dam level high”. Control codes may be sent to the sign using the character ‘` ’, same key as the tilde ‘~ ’ on the keyboard, the driver converts this to the control code 28, thus the message “Call `FAdroit” Would display

trol codes may be sent to the sign using the character ‘` ’, same key as the tilde ‘~ ’ on the keyboard, the driver converts this to the control code 28, thus the message “Call `FAdroit” Would display with only “Adroit” flashing. 5.1.1. Control Codes are: F : Flash Characters E : Enlarge Characters R : Change Colour to Red (Color signs only!) G : Change Colour To Green (Color signs only!) Y : Change Colour to Yellow (Color signs only!) M : Multicolour – i.e.: Top Red Center Yellow Bottom Green and applies to everything after the `M (Color signs only!) D : Return To Default Setting – i.e.: Normal Red Letters Not Flashing. (All the above settings are cleared) T : Turn background on (applies to entire message, and also to subsequent messages) t : Turn background off (applies to entire message, and also to subsequent messages) 5.1.2. Background Colors. The sign background can be enabled by sending a `T to the sign, this is a toggle that effects all subsequent messages. Using `t (lower-case T) turns the background off. The background setting code may appear anywhere in the message (it gets removed) and will affect the entire message. Background for certain colors may not be permissible

T) turns the background off. The background setting code may appear anywhere in the message (it gets removed) and will affect the entire message. Background for certain colors may not be permissible depending on the sign used. 5.1.3. Style Notes When using “scroll” style, the 1st line displayed in multi-line displays will not scroll, use the BOLD style or control code to scroll all the text. 5.1.4. Longer Messages Long messages up to 180 characters are possible using the continuation character ` (same as for control codes) at the end of a message. All messages sent to the same scan address (E.g. NAME 0) are appended up to the above limit. The last message must not end in the control code; this triggers the sending of the built-up long message. E.g. Scan a notify agent from NAME 1, and then add the text “Hello world`”, and send it, then add “ how are you today`” and lastly add “?”. All 3 messages will be concatenated and sent as one. “Hello world how are you today?” ___________________

Post Installation Configuration Top Post Installation Configuration Wanlink is installed into the Adroit installation folder as part of the complete Adroit installation, alternatively its WanClient and WanServer components can be selectively installed during a custom installation. For details of these components, see Wanlink Components or for details of launching these components, see Launching Wanlink Components . The following post-installation configuration actions can be performed on each Wanlink components: WanServer If the shortcut used to launch the WanServer includes the " /p:nnn" command-line parameter, then it will be able to change the port that this WanServer uses to communicate to the necessary WanClients (default 51114). Where nnn specifies the required port. The WanServer can also be installed to run as a Service within Windows . The advantage of this is that then the WanServer does not shutdown when the current user logs off. The WanServer also generates a WanServer.ini file which can be used when troubleshooting its communicating. WanClient If the shortcut used to launch the WanClient the "/start" command-line parameter, then it will automatically start its communi

file which can be used when troubleshooting its communicating. Predictive vector drawing Top Predictive vector drawing To speed up the adding of vectors, from the Vectors list of the Toolbox tool window to a graphic form, the following vectors support predictive drawing: Note: The following only applies when the vector is initially added to the graphic form. When you add an Ellipse to a graphic form and attempt to draw a circle (trying to create the same width and height) then a circle will be drawn [you can also hold down CTRL to do this]; otherwise an ellipse is drawn. When you add a Rectangle to a graphic form and attempt to draw a square (trying to create the same width and height) then a square will be drawn [you can also hold down CTRL to do this]; otherwise a rectangle is drawn. When you add a Line to a graphic form, if you attempt to draw a horizontal line, then a perfectly horizontal line is drawn and if you attempt to draw a vertical line, then a perfectly vertical line is drawn; if you actually want an angled line to be drawn then hold down SHIFT to override this predictive drawing. Printing Alarms Top Printing Alarms Before a new printer may be used, you must ensure that the host computer has the correct BIOS setting. The Parallel Port Mode must indicate Normal or Standard (SPP), NOT Enhanced (EPP). For further details see To set up a new printer. Note1: Typically, in order to perform line-by-line printing, no Windows driver should be installed at all, since the Windows spooler will internally cache printing until it has an entire page, so as to reduce CPU load while printing. However, specific printer drivers may be able to disable this spooling or page-caching method, and can thus work too. Note2: It is also possible to prevent the EventOutput agent from outputting events when its clustered Agent Server is in standby mode, so that the output destination does not receive duplicate entries, by adding the DisableEventOutputOnStandby value to the registry. Note3: The Time column of the EventOutput agent now supports MILLISECONDS. In the Configurator dialog box, select EventOutput from the Agent Type drop down list. ect EventOutput from the Agent Type drop down list. A list of agents is displayed in the Agent Tag list box. Select an agent and click on the Edit button. The EventOutput Agent dialog box is displayed. Ensure that the Activate option is set to No. Select the type of printer connection from the Printer Type list box: PARALLEL, PRINT or SERIAL, where: The PARALLEL and SERIAL options are for printers connected to local PC where the Agent Server is running. Such printers must NOT be configured in Print Manager as it creates a conflict in resource usage and hence will not work. The PRINT option is for printers that are configured in Windows' Printer manager and are usually page based and shared by other users . WHEN USING THIS OPTION, DO NOT SELECT LINE BY LINE PRINTING or you will waste paper . Process Vessels Top Process Vessels Purpose: when it is necessary to depict the level of a vessel to operators without undue emphasis or distractions. Description: a simple vessel with a vertical orientation, that provides a trend of its analogue level, between its maximum and minimum operating range: The trend of the analogue level is a bold black line. The Maximum operating range limit is a thin grey line at the top. The Minimum operating range limit is thin grey line at the bottom. The rolling time span of this trend is displayed in the base of the tank, which is 2 hours. wzdProcessVessel_Small_v01: a small process vessel wzdProcessVessel_Medium_v01: a medium process vessel wzdProcessVessel_Large_v01: a large process vessel Required values: Note: When this wizard is added to a graphic form, all these values are MANDATORY and therefore must ALL be specified. Production Charts Top Production Charts Purpose: when operators need to know how a production value is performing against a set target value: this charts the production value and a straight line graph of the set target value for the specific production period. Description: a line chart with a value axis on the left and a time axis on the bottom, with a straight line in blue drawn from 0 to the specified target value, representing the required production rate and the production value is indicated by means of a grey filled area, so that its actual production rate can be monitored relative to its required production rate. Note: This production value is only displayed if its value is being logged or if it constantly changes over the specified time period. User interaction: Click the clock glyph in the top right corner of this wizard to configure the current Production Parameters , as follows: Choose how the period of observing this production value is determined, by specifying the End Production Time , by using one of the following methods: Current to End Time : specify the future dated end time from the Current time (now), by typically typing in the required digits. Progress tool window Top Progress tool window This tool window tool windows are dockable windows, which provide several arrangement options to increase the size of the Design workspace window used for designing graphic forms. displays the progress of any Client-Server communication to determine if a (lengthy) process has completed. Project Backup and Restore Top Project Backup and Restore Note: This SHOULD be used to transfer project files to and from an engineering workstation. Currently the backup and restore provided by the Adroit Config Editor is SYSTEM-wide, that is why it is called SYSTEM backup and restore, where ONLY a specific CONFIGURATION, including ALL of its configuration settings, is backed up and restored at a time, as it is primarily intended to be a disaster-recovery fail safe. In other words, this functionality does NOT support selective restoration, which ONLY backs up your projects and their related files, such as their wizards and graphic forms. Currently you need to do the following, in order to perform a selective backup and restore: Note: This partial restoration functionality will be added to the product in a future release. Backing up project files: On the SmartUI Server computer that contains the projects you want to copy: Open the SmartUI Designer. Ensure that you save any graphic forms that are currently open in the Designer, which belong to these projects (assuming you want these changes to be copied). Click on the Configuration tab of the Designer ribbon. Click the Open Projects

s that are currently open in the Designer, which belong to these projects (assuming you want these changes to be copied). Click on the Configuration tab of the Designer ribbon. Click the Open Projects Folder tool, opens the folder containing the configured projects, in Windows Explorer, since these projects are on the same computer. In Windows Explorer: Backup the relevant projects and/or specific folders and their files, either by directly copying them to the required backup directory or zipping them up into an archive. Restoring project files On the SmartUI Server computer where you want to copy the backed up projects: Open the SmartUI Designer. Ensure that you close any graphic forms that are currently open in the Designer, which belong to these projects that you are restoring. Click on the Configuration tab of the Designer ribbon. Click the Open Projects Folder tool, to open the folder containing the configured projects, in Windows Explorer, since these projects are on the same computer. Note: You do not need to shut down the SmartUI Designer and Server. In Windows Explorer: Copy the backed up projects into this folder: If you intend to replicate an entire project then delete i

puter. Note: You do not need to shut down the SmartUI Designer and Server. In Windows Explorer: Copy the backed up projects into this folder: If you intend to replicate an entire project then delete it first If you are copying a partial project (such as some of its folders) then overwrite the existing files. You can also backup and restore any datasources that your projects use too, which is useful for datasources that have extensive configuration, such as OLE DB datasources. For details on these procedures, see Exporting datasources or Importing datasources . -->

Note: The Description is typically used by the tooltip of the specific component in the tree, equipment descriptions are also added as comments to the PLC program. Proprietary Data Logging to Disk Top Proprietary Data Logging to Disk Adroit provides extensive proprietary historical data logging facilities . As with scanning, any slot of any agent can be configured to have its values historically logged, subject to the proviso that they are of slot type Real , Integer , Boolean or 79 character String (this length excludes the mandatory zero terminator character). When logged, the values are time stamped and are made available, via a DataLog agent , to any client . Examples of data log clients would be historical trends, the extract utility, OLE-aware 3 rd party applications such as external spreadsheets for reports etc. Historical values can be stored in one or more data files, each file containing the values of one or more DataLog agents. Note: If you export and delete Datalog agents that use Adroit 's proprietary log files, ensure that you restart the Agent Server before re-importing - so that they can remove the areas that they currently use in the LGD files. Click for more details: Multiple Datalog agents can potentially use a single LGD file, so when you delete a Datalog agent using proprietary logging all that happens is the area of the

the LGD files. Click for more details: Multiple Datalog agents can potentially use a single LGD file, so when you delete a Datalog agent using proprietary logging all that happens is the area of the file that was used by the deleted Datalog agent is marked as unused and will be compacted at the next Agent Server startup. Therefore if you re-create the Datalog agent in the same Agent Server session, the LGD resource simply adds the space required for the newly added Datalog to the end of the LGD file i.e. it does not re-use the old area that has been marked as unused. This can cause the LGD file to become too big, resulting in errors such as an error message asking you to check your Datalog agent configuration (in Agent Server window you may also get a Datalog agent dll exception) and your Datalog agents may not start. When you restart the Agent Server , the old areas of the LGD file are compacted and room is left to re-create the datalogs. Previously, when logging to the Adroit proprietary datalog (.LGD) files, the Adroit datalogging system only provided the historical logged data existing in the .LGD file and was unable to provide historical data from the SystemDatalog-created .C

etary datalog (.LGD) files, the Adroit datalogging system only provided the historical logged data existing in the .LGD file and was unable to provide historical data from the SystemDatalog-created .CSV datalog backup files. Now each Datalog agent can create their own backup (.LGB) files to automatically retrieve this data, if required by trends (charts) or other requests for historical data. For details, see Datalog backup and retrieval . TWO files are created for each proprietary log, the .LDG file, which stores the raw data and its associated .LGI file, which is the lookup index file. The total amount of disk space required for data logging depends on the following factors: the number of data files used the number of agents being data logged the total number of values logged per agent the sampling time and length of time each value is logged for. Note: Any datalogs that cause their .LGD file to be greater than 2 GB will fail to start and user is notified accordingly and an associated eventlog entry is also created. During logging, each DataLog agent will write to its pre-allocated dynamic buffer area in a data file and will overwrite itself from the beginning after it reaches th

d eventlog entry is also created. During logging, each DataLog agent will write to its pre-allocated dynamic buffer area in a data file and will overwrite itself from the beginning after it reaches the end of the buffer. The Datalog agent allows for a maximum of 53000000 records. This means that the specified datalog Length... (or period) and Time... deadband combination may not exceed 53000000 records. This corresponds to a maximum of 1010.9 MB of data at 20 bytes per record, which means 613 days at 1 second or 30 days at 50 ms. Note1: The minimum Time... deadband allowed is 10 ms which only provides a maximum Length... (or period) of 6.13 days of logged data. Note2: When retrieving data from classic (legacy) trends the maximum number of datapoints that can be trended is 99999 therefore, for example, only 27.77 hours of data can be retrieved at 1 second on a classic (legacy) trend. PLEASE NOTE: Adroit ’s proprietary logging uses an in-built logging factor, which reduces the specified logging period by 80%. UNLESS a clean installation of Adroit is installed, in which case this logging factor is NOT applied. For details, see Adroit Logging Factor . Note: If the logging period is inc

logging period by 80%. UNLESS a clean installation of Adroit is installed, in which case this logging factor is NOT applied. For details, see Adroit Logging Factor . Note: If the logging period is increased ensure that this change is saved and the Agent Server is restarted, at least once, to allow the necessary LGD file compressions to occur. For details, see Increasing Logging Periods . Tip: If you use datalog backups, which create .LDB files, then you can extend the potential amount of logged data without creating larger log files. In this case, while the active log (LGD) file can remain small, the log backup (.LDB) files can store historical data for much longer time periods. For details, see Datalog backup and retrieval . A data log file is composed of many buffers, one for each DataLog agent. Being event based, the speed at which each buffer is written depends on how often the value in the agent slot being logged changes, and its deadband. If necessary, the data log file can be periodically archived by file copy. Historical data can later be retrieved for viewing , used in trends, or exported as comma separated variable (CSV) files , a format recognised by many commercial spre

riodically archived by file copy. Historical data can later be retrieved for viewing , used in trends, or exported as comma separated variable (CSV) files , a format recognised by many commercial spreadsheet and database packages. Adroit supports the merging of external data into existing log files , and logged data is accessible via OLE. Disk size estimation for the data log . Data Logging Compression Methods . -->

The total amount of disk space required for data logging depends on the following factors: the number of data files used the number of agents being data logged the total number of values logged per agent the sampling time and length of time each value is logged for. Note: Any datalogs that cause their .LGD file to be greater than 2 GB will fail to start and user is notified accordingly and an associated eventlog entry is also created. d eventlog entry is also created. During logging, each DataLog agent will write to its pre-allocated dynamic buffer area in a data file and will overwrite itself from the beginning after it reaches the end of the buffer. The Datalog agent allows for a maximum of 53000000 records. This means that the specified datalog Length... (or period) and Time... deadband combination may not exceed 53000000 records. This corresponds to a maximum of 1010.9 MB of data at 20 bytes per record, which means 613 days at 1 second or 30 days at 50 ms. Note1: The minimum Time... deadband allowed is 10 ms which only provides a maximum Length... (or period) of 6.13 days of logged data. Note2: When retrieving data from classic (legacy) trends the maximum number of datapoints that can be trended is 99999 therefore, for example, only 27.77 hours of data can be retrieved at 1 second on a classic (legacy) trend. Protocol Drivers Top Protocol Drivers Adroit has created a large number of protocol drivers that use Windows device drivers to communicate to a wide range of front-end devices e.g. Programmable Logic Controllers PLCs, RTUs etc. If necessary, specialised drivers can be developed. Before a protocol can be used to provide communication to a front-end device, it needs to be installed. Each protocol driver, provides the following services: The configuration of hardware I/O addresses to be scanned from the front-end device. The communication of these configured addresses to and from the hardware I/O. Note: Protocol Drivers using proprietary hardware adapters will require the relevant Windows driver for the adapter. Although an installed protocol driver provides the means of communication, the communication to each FED front-end device, which is a device that is accessed directly by the user, such as a PLC or RTU. is performed by a device added to an installed protocol driver to communicate using this protocol to a specific front-end device - in other words a logical connection to this FED. that you need to be add to the installed protocol driver. These devices are essentially logical con

sing this protocol to a specific front-end device - in other words a logical connection to this FED. that you need to be add to the installed protocol driver. These devices are essentially logical connections to the front-end devices they communicate to and a total of 65534 devices may be added and used for any one installed protocol driver. Note1: The protocol driver configuration for each device is saved in the system registry; therefore it is necessary to reconfigure the devices if they are to be run on another computer. Note2: You may use as many different protocol drivers and devices as you wish, until the sum of their scanned points exceeds your licensed number of scan points. For details, see Scan Points . NASA, stands for New Adroit Scanning Architecture and describes a sub-class of protocol drivers that are specifically written to take advantage of the scanning improvements and enhancements provided by NASA, such as demand scanning and highly optimised scan tasks. For more details, see Demand Scanning . ails, see Demand Scanning . Related topics: Scanning (communication) overview Logical and Physical Device Configurations How to install a protocol driver How to add and configure a device for an installed protocol driver Diagnosing installed Protocol Drivers and their configured Devices -->

Proxy Servers Top Proxy Servers A proxy server is an Agent Server that creates proxy agents for agents that exist on remote Agent Servers on the same project because it itself does not contain any configured agents. Since it only contains Proxy agents, it will not support scanning, alarming or datalogging. Proxy servers generally use an empty WGP file. IMPORTANT: If your proxy Agent Server is running as a service, then ensure that the user profile that the Agent Server service uses to log onto the computer HAS the necessary rights to browse the network and connect to the other Agent Servers. This should NOT be the default Local System account. See Configuring Agent Server Service User Profile. Note: A Proxy Server (an Agent Server that is licensed for ZERO scan points) can proxy an unlimited number of agents, whereas a normal Agent Server is only able to create as many proxy agents as it has scan points and therefore must be licensed for AT LEAST the same number of scan points as the remote Agent Server. Proxy servers are used in environments where one or more clients need information from multiple Agent Servers. A client can only connect to one Agent Server so this server must hav

emote Agent Server. Proxy servers are used in environments where one or more clients need information from multiple Agent Servers. A client can only connect to one Agent Server so this server must have the capability to create proxies where needed. Proxy servers are also useful in environments where a user wishes to remove the burden of servicing multiple clients from an Agent Server. Those clients are connected to a proxy server and the remote server(s) then only services the proxy server leaving it more processor and network time for it's SCADA functions. Note: If your proxy server needs to proxy information from a remote Agent Server that is on a DIFFERENT domain or on DIFFERENT sides of a router/switch, then ensure that you are using an explicit connection to connect to this remote agent server. See Agent Server Connection Methods . All Agent Server types (Standalone, Cluster aware and cluster servers) have the capability to create proxy agents for agents that exist on remote agents servers on the same project. Cluster and Cluster Aware servers acting as proxy servers, have the unique feature of creating proxy agents even if there are more than one agent of the same name in a n

s servers on the same project. Cluster and Cluster Aware servers acting as proxy servers, have the unique feature of creating proxy agents even if there are more than one agent of the same name in a network of clustered Agent Servers. Therefore cluster proxy servers must be used if there are cluster servers on the same project. A Standalone server acting as a proxy server will not create proxies agents if two or more agents of the same name are found on a network. Therefore standalone proxy servers should only be used where there are no cluster servers on the same project. -->

Publishing run-time versions of graphic forms Top Publishing run-time versions of graphic forms Once a graphic form has been designed and is working as required, you can publish a run-time version for use in the Operator only. We recommend that you publish your graphic forms since this creates an optimised run-time version for the Operator. This process strips out the design-time information from the graphic form to reduce the size and complexity of the graphic form that is sent to the Operator, which also improves its loading time. Therefore two versions of the graphic form are stored: the typical design-time graphic form (a .viz file) that also contains all the information required to edit the graphic form and the published run-time graphic form (a .opv file) which is the stripped down Operator only version. However if a graphic form has not been published, the Operator will load the design-time graphic form. IMPORTANT: When you save the design-time graphic form (the .viz file) you REMOVE the published run-time graphic form (the .opv file) and need to republish it. This is by design, to allow you to revert to using the design time version if the publishing process has removed fun

This is by design, to allow you to revert to using the design time version if the publishing process has removed functionality that you requried. Note: If a run-time graphic form does not exist then the Operator will load the design-time graphic form. The following Publishing Settings can be specified when publishing the run-time version: Preserve container objects that have Behaviours : by default, part of the run-time optimization process removes container objects (these are the generic containers for wizards), since removing these containers reduces the size and complexity of the graphic form. However if Behaviours have been directly configured on these containers (such as a visibility Behaviour) then these Behaviours will not work after the graphic form has been published. In this case check this checkbox to preserve these container objects and their Behaviours. To publish a run-time version of a graphic form: Click the Save and Publish toolbar button (that appears above the graphic form in the Design workspace ). -->

Putting Values into Agents Top Putting Values into Agents Adroit provides a utility that performs a putslot operation. The putslot utility enables a specific value to be written to the target agent’s slot. Alternatively, a value obtained from another agent’s slot, by dereferencing it with an asterisk (*) prefix, can be used in the putslot expression both for the target agent’s name and the put value. It can be scheduled to start a process, allowing the scheduler to trigger commands (e.g. print, scan etc.) and to drive mimics and dynamic pictures. The syntax of a Putslot command is as follows: putslot [-ccomputer.server],[*]agent.slot,[*]value[,time] Note1: DO NOT insert spaces between arguments [ ] means optional. Note2: By default a connection to a local Agent Server is assumed, but if a computer.server is specified, prefix it with –c. Symbol Description Example computer computer name -cMSP-1 server Agent Server West-Plant agent target agent ANALOG01 or *OTHER (asterisk dereferences tag) slot target slot RawValue value value to put or ~ to toggle value if Boolean slot 90.0 or "a string" or *ANOTHER.VALUE (asterisk dereferences tag) or ~ (~ absent = set value of slot) time time of

ag) slot target slot RawValue value value to put or ~ to toggle value if Boolean slot 90.0 or "a string" or *ANOTHER.VALUE (asterisk dereferences tag) or ~ (~ absent = set value of slot) time time of change 04/10/1998 14:00:00 (dd/mm/yyyy hh:mm:ss) Note: The command line input is now case-sensitive when changing the values of STRING slots. Examples: putslot boo01.value,1 putslot boo01.value,~ putslot int01.value,123,04/10/1998 14:00:00 putslot -cMSP-1.West-Plant,int01.value,123,04/10/1998 14:00:00 putslot str01.value,"hello" putslot ana01.value,*ana02.value Configuring the same slot of multiple agents If necessary, create the required Agentgroup or simply use the pre-defined Agentgroups for the defined Agent types. Configure this agentgroup as a bulk-editing group, as follows: Open the Agent Configurator window. Ensure that the Advanced checkbox is checked, in the Agent type section. Select the AgentGroup agent type from the Type list box. Double click the name of the required agentgroup e.g. Datalog. Select the Bulk editing of agent type : XXX option (where XXX refers to this agent type). Note: This option is ONLY enabled if this agentgroup has one or more agents in it of the SAME

up e.g. Datalog. Select the Bulk editing of agent type : XXX option (where XXX refers to this agent type). Note: This option is ONLY enabled if this agentgroup has one or more agents in it of the SAME agent type. Click the OK button. Specify the name of this agentgroup in the putslot command (instead of the required agent name). For example, to start all the Datalog agents at once (by setting their start slot to 1), you can specify the following putslot command: putslot datalog.start,1 -->

Putting Values into Agents Top Putting Values into Agents Adroit provides a utility that performs a putslot operation. The putslot utility enables a specific value to be written to the target agent’s slot. Alternatively, a value obtained from another agent’s slot, by dereferencing it with an asterisk (*) prefix, can be used in the putslot expression both for the target agent’s name and the put value. It can be scheduled to start a process, allowing the scheduler to trigger commands (e.g. print, scan etc.) and to drive mimics and dynamic pictures. The syntax of a Putslot command is as follows: putslot [-ccomputer.server],[*]agent.slot,[*]value[,time] Note1: DO NOT insert spaces between arguments [ ] means optional. Note2: By default a connection to a local Agent Server is assumed, but if a computer.server is specified, prefix it with –c. text: Radar Plots Top Radar Plots Purpose: to create a Pattern Recognition Object (PRO) that expresses the relationship between a number of related process variables as a shape instead of as a series of numbers, because the brain can remember shapes far more than sets of numbers. Typically radar plots are used to monitor and describe important (serious) process conditions, so that preventative action can be taken to prevent their reoccurrence. Description: the radar plot consists of a sequence of equi-angular spokes, called radii, with each spoke representing a process variable. A line is drawn connecting the data values for each spoke which produces the resultant shape. The length of these radii or spokes are determined by the difference between the specified maximum and minimum setpoints, as follows: Minimum Setpoint : sets the value of the origin (centre-point), therefore typically ensure that this value will encompass the smallest of the specified process variables. Maximum Setpoint : sets the outer value of all the radii, therefore typically ensure that this value will encompass the largest of the specified process variables. wzdRadarPlot_3_v01 : a radar plot for three related proce

RDC SYSTEMS : REPORTER 8102 Printed 17-Aug-20 1 RDC8102 driver Overview The RDC8102 protocol for Adroit communicates to a Reporter 8102, which is designed to receive transmitter codes in a control room or operate as a stand alone intelligent repeater. Product obtainable from Radio Data Communications (Tel 011 616 7685) The protocol is an exception based protocol driver in that data is received asynchronously when a value changes on an outstation. Wiring Wiring between the RS232 port and the modem is standard RS232. Please consult your REPORTER 8102 documentation for additional particulars on setting up the hardware. Driver Installation and Setup The driver is installed by picking the RDC8102 driver from the drivers directory. The RDC8102.DLL and the RDC8102.DOC is then copied into the agent directory. After installation of the driver, the user may then create and configure devices for the RDC8102 driver. Device Configuration Devices At a minimum, you must create at least one device for every port being used. However, you may choose to create a device for a group of transmitters. RDC SYSTEMS : REPORTER 8102 Printed 17-Aug-20 2 Device configuration dialog Port Select the port through

every port being used. However, you may choose to create a device for a group of transmitters. RDC SYSTEMS : REPORTER 8102 Printed 17-Aug-20 2 Device configuration dialog Port Select the port through which you are going to communicate. The baud rate is fixed at 9600,8,1,N. Prefix This field is only used when the protocol is configured to communicate in alpha prefix mode. In all other modes this field is ignored. Scanning Due to the system operation, all scanned tags must be output enabled, pulsed, and cold started to zero. The reasoning follows: The scanning sub-system keeps a record of the last received value for optimization, and thus will not re-send an alarm “on” until it goes “off” again. By output enabling the tag, when the tag goes to “zero” the scanning system updates it’s last known value with the zero (“off”), thus when the alarm on (“one”) condition arrives again, it gets put into the tag as expected. By the same reasoning, cold-start will initialize the tags to zero (“off”), so that all current alarms are clear. In addition, stopping and starting a device agent causes the driver to zero all scanned values, and the tags. The driver keeps a last known value for the alarm

), so that all current alarms are clear. In addition, stopping and starting a device agent causes the driver to zero all scanned values, and the tags. The driver keeps a last known value for the alarms, which is cleared on device start, this last known value gets “OR”ed with an incoming alarm, thus giving the SUM of alarms received to the tag. Effectively this “copy” of the value allows the driver to keep track of the tags’ value. This function naturally only works correctly if the tag was output enabled, so that when bits in the tag clear (go off) the driver will also clear them at the same instant in time. Outstation Data The driver processes the following data received: 0 - Alarm 1 - Lock up 2 - Open up 3 - Emergency 4 - Telemetry 1 5 - Telemetry 2 6 - Telemetry 3 7 - Telemetry 4 8 - Mains Fail RDC SYSTEMS : REPORTER 8102 Printed 17-Aug-20 3 9 - Mains Restore 10 - Engineer Test 11 - Customer Duress 12 - Medical Alert 13 - Fire Alarm 14 - Telemetry 5 15 - Telemetry 8 Data received in any mode will be processed according to the above list. In Chubb mode only bits(0-7) will be activated. Digital inputs Digital tags (Boolean slots) that are scanned from Outstations can be scanned in

any mode will be processed according to the above list. In Chubb mode only bits(0-7) will be activated. Digital inputs Digital tags (Boolean slots) that are scanned from Outstations can be scanned into Digital tags The format of the address string is as follows: CN: TTTT: B Where: CN – stands for code number. TTTT – Code number of transmitter B – Bit number (0 - 15) Analogue / Multistate inputs If scanned into a Multistate agent than the 16 slots represent the digital status of that transmitter. The format of the address string is as follows: CN: TTTT Where: CN – stands for code number. TTTT – Code number of transmitter When scanned into an integer, the value of the integer will represent the status of the outstation by a number ranging from 1 to 65535 with the value 0 representing no alarms. Message protocol Datascope messages are displayed in hex or ascii. All messages are displayed whether that transmitter is configured or not. Messages of devices not configured are displayed in the first devices protocol monitor. e first devices protocol monitor. Thus this protocol will have 1 byte more than the above 3 protocols. For the data to be valid the prefix defined must match the prefix defined in the device. Read Only Scanning Strategy Top Read Only Scanning Strategy This scanning the process of communicating a value (slot), typically to and/or from a front-end device (FED). configuration is the normal mode of operation for read only scanning. Where users should not modify the values of tags within the Agent Server manually otherwise the value of these tags in the Agent Server will be out of sync with their process values i.e. their values in the front end device (PLC). For details of all the scanning strategies offered, see Scanning Strategies or for further details on the effect of combining the available global and tag-specific scanning settings, see The Effect of Combining Scanning Settings . Required global scanning settings: MonitorStatus can be set, in which case any values which have been manually modified in the Agent Server, will be overwritten with the process value, on the next read. This setting can be configured within the Advanced Scanning Settings dialog, by checking the Allow changes in scan-inhibit and output-enable to affect the tag immediately checkbox. Note: For this strategy, the settings of both ForceOutputs and SyncProcessToServerOnFirstScan are immaterial. Requ

low changes in scan-inhibit and output-enable to affect the tag immediately checkbox. Note: For this strategy, the settings of both ForceOutputs and SyncProcessToServerOnFirstScan are immaterial. Required tag-specific scanning settings: Output Enable = 0 Scan Inhibit = 0 Operation of strategy: When the Agent Server is started, the Agent Server receives the values of these scanned tags from the front-end devices (PLCs). When a device stops or starts, the Agent Server receives the values of these scanned tags from the front-end devices (PLCs). When the communications have been restored after a device has failed, the Agent Server receives the values of these scanned tags from the front-end devices (PLCs). If a value of one of these scanned tags is changed in the Agent Server, this value is overwritten by the value in the front-end device (PLC) Note: Depending on the driver being used, MonitorStatus may need to be set, for this to be the case. If a value of one of these scanned tags is changed externally, the Agent Server receives this value from the front-end device (PLC). -->

Real-time Catch-up Top Real-time catch-up Certain agent types on a cluster server require synchronisation of internal data structures with their Master partner. This process is called real-time catch-up. When a cluster partner starts up and it's Master server is available, this synchronisation takes place while the standby server is loading up. Note: Real-time catch-up is not associated with shadowing and datalog catch-up. The following agent types support real-time catch-up: Analog , Digital , Counter , Expression , IOT , MaxDemand , PID , Scheduler and Statistical . How the Real-time catch-up process works The Real-time catch-up is a process that applies to clustered Agent servers only and not to stand-alone servers. The process occurs during the start up of a standby agent server, if a master agent server is already running. If this is the case, then every agent that is loaded from the WGP file and also supports real-time catch-up will request the current state of the agent from the master server and then synchronise itself. The WGP file is loaded in two phases: First, all the agents are loaded from the WGP file. Each agent is initialised synchronously. During this phase each ag

master server and then synchronise itself. The WGP file is loaded in two phases: First, all the agents are loaded from the WGP file. Each agent is initialised synchronously. During this phase each agent subscribes to other agents when required by expression agents. It is during this phase that the agent will synchronise itself, using real-time catch-up with the same agent in the master agent server. On completion of phase 2 above the agent server then enters the ready state. As an illustration of real-time catch-up: Let’s assume we have an analog agent called TANKLEVEL. The saved value of TANKLEVEL in the WGP file is very likely to be an old value (for example, 25%) that was relevant at the time the WGP file was last saved. The current real-time value in the process is very likely to be different (let’s say 55%) from the saved value of 25%. The TANKLEVEL agent in the newly started standby agent server will then synchronise its slot values with those of the master during the agent initialization phase. Both servers should now reflect 55% for the TANKLEVEL.value . Take note of following In scenarios where Adroit installations only save their WGP files after a configuration change, i

ialization phase. Both servers should now reflect 55% for the TANKLEVEL.value . Take note of following In scenarios where Adroit installations only save their WGP files after a configuration change, it is important to realise that: Adroit does not automatically save WGP files on shutdown of the agent server unless it is specifically configured to do so. It is then very likely that the WGP files contain old saved values which makes the requirement for real-time catch-up a very important process. Installations where a cluster is setup to extend the configuration on the standby server should execute the following procedure: Let’s call the maser server AS1 and the standby server AS2. Save the WGP file on the standby server AS2. Switch the standby AS2 to master, resulting in AS1 becoming the standby. Stop the standby agent server which is now AS1. Copy the WGP file from standby AS2 to master AS1. Restart the standby server AS1. Optionally, once AS1 is back up and running correctly, switch AS1 back to master if this is the preferred master agent server. When the synchronisation has completed, the agent server values contained in the newly copied WGP file may still be a few minutes old an

S1 back to master if this is the preferred master agent server. When the synchronisation has completed, the agent server values contained in the newly copied WGP file may still be a few minutes old and will require further real-time catch-up to finalise current process values. -->

Rearranging spiders Top Rearranging spiders and regions The Rearrange All Spiders/Regions spider workspace option, can neatly and logically arrange the spiders, regions and silks to illustrate the flow of data. Click for more details: For instance, in the case of the Spider Configuration tool window, the flow of data is illustrated via the silks and the other spiders in the middle from/to the Data spiders (data elements and/or properties) which are hidden and only appear as origins or destinations of the silks. To rearrange spiders and regions in a spider workspace: If necessary, open the required spider workspace. Either press the Rearrange All Spiders/Regions toolbar button, from the spider workspace toolbar . Or right-click the spider workspace and select the Rearrange All Spiders/Regions menu item. Note1: This immediately hides any open configuration views and rearranges the spiders, regions and silks in this spider workspace. Note2: This arranges the spiders so that no overlapping of the full sized spider icons will occur even if Small Spider Icons display option is currently selected from the spider workspace toolbar. -->

Reasons for categorizing your incidents Top Reasons for categorizing your incidents By default, all the incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). assigned to the alarm routes that use this AlarmManagement agent are added to the _ Uncategorised category of its Categories tree. Typically you will create and use categories for your incidents for one or both of the following reasons: The more incidents in the _Uncategorised category, the harder it becomes to differentiate between these incidents. For this reason, you can create other categories to distinguish between the following: different areas or sections of your process, such as crushing, flocculation etc. different equipment within each of these areas and if necessary down to the individual tag level. Adding categories allows you to easily query (analyse) or report ONLY the incidents that you are interested in, instead of ALL the incidents, so that you can manage this data more effectively. Categories also allow you to provide the name of th

(analyse) or report ONLY the incidents that you are interested in, instead of ALL the incidents, so that you can manage this data more effectively. Categories also allow you to provide the name of the Operator that is responsible for the incidents allocated within it (and if necessary its sub-categories). This name is logged with these incidents, for auditing purposes. Therefore, this setting only applies to categories that represent areas of your process that have different operators overseeing them. The default _Uncategorised category is simply provided to make you aware of the incidents that you have not categorised. Therefore this category does NOT allow you to assign an operator name to these logged incidents. Tip: To quickly categorise your incidents, click the Learn alarms (incidents requiring acknowledgement) and/or Learn events (incidents NOT requiring acknowledgement) buttons to add ALL the applicable unassigned incidents, that are routed to this alarmmanagement agent, to the _Uncategorised category. -->

Rebuild the List of Installed Drivers and Devices Top Rebuild the List of Installed Drivers and Devices Using the Adroit Configuration Setup : Press the Windows key and start typing in Classic Setup and select it from the list. Recipe Agent Overview Top Recipe Agent Description A recipe is a statement of the ingredients and procedures necessary for the making or compounding of some preparation or formulation. It defines how the control system is to process its raw materials to make the desired product and byproducts. In Adroit , this is achieved by the Recipe agent which provides the means for automatically downloading information to process variables. These variables allow a plant to produce the final product. Mundane tasks can be automated saving time and removing the element of human error. In common with modern industry practice (SP88), the recipe agent consists of a master recipe and one or more control recipes. Note: Names used in the recipe agent e.g. to define recipes and batches, CANNOT contain the ‘%’ character. The Master Recipe consists of all the process variables or "ingredients" and the sequence in which they are to be downloaded. It is here that the procedure and associated tag names will be defined. Each Control Recipe will contain specific quantities and values for customizing the Master Recipe for a given production run, thus allowing a plant to produce variants of its base product; for

efined. Each Control Recipe will contain specific quantities and values for customizing the Master Recipe for a given production run, thus allowing a plant to produce variants of its base product; for example, differing colors of paint, different flavors of cola. For each master recipe, there may be one or more Control Recipes. For example, the Master Recipe could describe a Fruit Juice mixing plant. Several Control recipes would provide the data to manufacture various flavors and mixtures of fruit juice such as Orange, Mango, Pineapple, Mango and Orange, Pineapple and Orange etc. The Adroit recipe system allows: Each Control recipe to be assigned a batch identification. Accumulation of batch histories through event logging. Downloading of process variables that are of type Boolean, Integer, Real or String. The sequence of execution to be delayed by a specified amount of time, to be paused until a desired condition in the plant is met, or to be redirected to another step. Master recipes and Control recipes to be imported or exported to files using the comma separated variable (CSV) format, for ease of viewing and editing by 3rd party products (e.g. Excel). The progress of a working

The progress of a working recipe to be monitored. Verification of the values scanned out to PLC. Optional Rollback can be performed should the verification fail. -->

Recommendations for using TableLayoutPanel controls Top Recommendations for using TableLayoutPanel controls Microsoft recommends that you use the TableLayoutPanel control sparingly. Note: You should NOT use it in all situations that require a resizable layout. The following list describes layouts that benefit most from using the TableLayoutPanel control: Layouts in which there are multiple parts of the form that resize proportionally to each other. Layouts that will be modified or generated dynamically at run time, such as data entry forms that have user-customizable fields added or subtracted based on preferences. Layouts that should remain at an overall fixed size. For example, you may have a dialog box that should remain smaller than 800 x 600, but you need to support localised strings. The following list describes layouts that do not benefit greatly from using the TableLayoutPanel control: Simple data entry forms with a single column of labels and a single column of text-entry areas. Forms with a single large display area that should fill all the available space when a resize occurs. An example of this is a form that displays a single PropertyGrid control. In this case, use anc

s. Forms with a single large display area that should fill all the available space when a resize occurs. An example of this is a form that displays a single PropertyGrid control. In this case, use anchoring, because nothing else should expand when the form is resized. These recommendations have been taken as-is from the Best Practices for the TableLayoutPanel Control http://technet.microsoft.com/en-us/subscriptions/downloads/ms171689(v=vs.85).aspx ) Note: Avoid nesting TableLayoutPanels not only does this make it harder to debug your layouts but can also reduce your performance when resizing the graphic form. We recommend that you plan your intended layout of controls beforehand, when using this control. IMPORTANT: When you DELETE a TableLayoutPanel control an error occurs because it is only PARTIALLY removed at design time, so you need to save, close and reopen the graphic form to complete the removal of this control and its added controls. WARNING: Immediately after deleting a TableLayoutPanel control, although this control and/or the added controls may remain on the graphic form, any further configuration of them will be lost as these will be removed the next time you save and r

Recommended Method of Importing Alarm Agents Top Recommended Method of Importing Alarm Agents Since the configuration of each alarm agent is stored in THREE interrelated files , this can complicate the method of bulk-configuring Alarm agents as these files MUST be correctly sorted so that they will correctly relate to one another. For details, see Importing Alarm agents . The following method of importing Alarm agents, however, is recommended as it does away with the need of ensuring that these files are correctly sorted: Export the required Alarm agent(s). For details, see Exporting Agents . Design their TYPLST and ROUTLST files first. For details of the formats of these CSV files, see Type List CSV File Format or Route List CSV File Format . Perform a selective import of each alarm agent, only importing these files. In other words, click No when the Import Alarm agent dialog is displayed and then only select the xxxxx-TYPLST.CSV file and xxxxx-ROUTLST.CSV (where xxxxx represents the name of the Alarm agent). Re-export the required Alarm agent(s). Design the AGNTLST file using the indexes as per the newly exported TYPLST file. For details of the formats of this CSV files, see Agen

text: name of the Alarm agent). Re-export the required Alarm agent(s). Design the AGNTLST file using the indexes as per the newly exported TYPLST file. For details of the formats of this CSV files, see Agent List CSV File Format . Perform a selective import of each alarm agent, only importing the AGNTLST file. Note: If you import a list of alarm types list into an existing Alarm agent, it is recommended that this Alarm agent is deleted and then re-created to quickly clear its list of already configured alarms, as these may conflict with the new alarm types. Tip: In addition to being able to select which of the three configuration files will be imported; the manual import option is also able to select DIFFERENT import files, other than the default files created on export. For this reason, it is possible to design a single TYPLST file, containing the default alarm types required by ALL alarm agents. Then import this file, using manual importing, into all the configured alarm agents. This not only saves configuration time, but also ensures that all the Alarm agents will have the same alarm types. -->

text: Recommended System and/or Adroit Configuration Guide Top Recommended System and/or Adroit Configuration Guide The following is the recommended order in which to set up the system. Note: When asked to reboot after installing anything or changing a setting, do so by selecting the "Reboot later" option, and then shutdown-&-restart the system manually. Install your Operating System, which should be NT-based from Windows XP onwards, verify that it has been installed correctly. Contact your network administrator if this is not the case. Install the network card and the required network protocol and verify that the computer is connected to the network. Contact your network administrator if this is not the case. Install all hardware drivers, including the required printer drivers and verify that the hardware devices are working and that it is possible to print to all the required printers (both those that are physically connected to the computer and those that are available over the network). Contact your network administrator if this is not the case. Configure the graphics card with at least a resolution of 800 x 600 with 65535 colors. Open the System applet in the Control Panel, optimise

metadata.title: Recommended System and/or Adroit Configuration Guide

text: Contact your network administrator if this is not the case. Configure the graphics card with at least a resolution of 800 x 600 with 65535 colors. Open the System applet in the Control Panel, optimise performance for background applications for the Agent Server computer and configure the virtual memory paging file, keep the Initial and the maximum size the same to avoid page file fragmentation. Recommended size is 300 MB or at least twice the physical RAM. Also set system recovery options to reboot automatically on a fault. Re-start the operating system at least once before installing Adroit . Ensure that the computer complies with the specified hardware and software requirements, before installing Adroit . For details, see Removing scanned values from a device . Step Two: Remove the configured device from its protocol driver, as follows: Using the Adroit Config Editor : Launch the Adroit Config Editor . Click Agent Server Configuration in the right hand pane. Click Driver Configuration in the right hand pane. Right click the required Device ( ) of an installed Protocol Driver ( ) in the Installed Drivers and Devices list and select Remove from the menu. This will immediately remove the selected device, provided that all of its scanned points have been removed from the current Adroit database (.WGP) file. If this is NOT the case, then the device is not removed and a message box will display this warning instead. -->

Step Two: Remove the configured device from its protocol driver, as follows: Using the Adroit Configuration Setup : Press the Windows key and start typing in Classic Setup and select it from the list. Click on the Drivers tab and the required configured Device ( , , ) in the Installed Drivers and Devices list and then Click the Remove ( ) button. This will display the Protocol Driver Device confirmation dialog, which reports the name of the device to be deleted; click either the Yes or No button, as required. Tip: This can also be displayed by right clicking on the required configured Device ( , , ) in this list and selecting Remove Device from the menu. Note: This device will only be removed, if all of its scanned points have been removed from the current Adroit database
