text: Removing added and subtracted values Top Removing added and subtracted values Remove unnecessary adding or subtracting values. To remove unnecessary adding or subtracting values If necessary, select the required Summation spider and/or open its configuration view. Right-click the unnecessary value that is being added ( Add value# ) or subtracted ( Subtract value# ) in the Inputs section, where # is a unique number starting from 1 and select Delete . WARNING! The selected value is immediately removed from the spider and any silks that are connected to it; therefore ensure that the correct value has been selected. Note: You are able to remove every input in the Inputs section, if necessary. -->

Removing Alarm Types Top Removing Alarm Types You can ONLY remove alarm types from the Alarm agent. Note: You can ONLY remove an alarm type that you have not configured for alarming. If you DO attempt to remove an alarm type that is being used. The following Agent Server Error message is displayed “Bad Slot Parameters”. To remove an alarm type: Edit the required Alarm agent, as follows: Select the name of this Alarm agent. For details, see To Select an Agent . Right click and select the Edit... menu item to display the Edit Alarm Agent dialog. Select the Types tab from the Edit Alarm Agent dialog. Select the required agent type from the Agent Type drop down list box. Select the alarm type that you no longer require from the Available Alarm Types list Click the Delete button. -->

Removing Alarm Types Top Removing Alarm Types You can ONLY remove alarm types from the Alarm agent. Note: You can ONLY remove an alarm type that you have not configured for alarming. If you DO attempt to remove an alarm type that is being used. The following Agent Server Error message is displayed “Bad Slot Parameters”. To remove an alarm type: Edit the required Alarm agent, as follows: Select the name of this Alarm agent. For details, see To Select an Agent . Right click and select the Edit... menu item to display the Edit Alarm Agent dialog. Select the Types tab from the Edit Alarm Agent dialog. Select the required agent type from the Agent Type drop down list box. Select the alarm type that you no longer require from the Available Alarm Types list Click the Delete button. -->

Removing aliases Top Removing aliases Aliases that are no longer required by a graphic form can be removed. To remove an alias from a graphic form: Ensure that the required graphic form is opened and displayed in the Design workspace . In the Design workspace , select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the graphic form itself. Open the Properties tool window. Select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the Aliases property, which is listed in the VIZNET Extended category. Click the browse button in the value column to the left of this property. This will display the Aliases configuration dialog. Select the unwanted alias. Click the Remove button. Note: If this alias is connected to any properties, then these links will also be removed. WARNING! The selected alias will immediately be removed. Click the Finish button when all the required aliases have been removed. -->

Removing allowed groups Top Removing allowed groups If necessary, group(s) used by Server security can be removed. To remove a group from the allowed groups list Expand the Security component of the required SmartUI Server, as follows: Open the Enterprise Manager . For details, see Accessing tool windows . If necessary, expand click the plus (+) box to the left of the current icon or name Servers . If necessary, expand the name of the required Server connection . Tip: The connection name is prefaced by the SmartUI Server computer name. If necessary, expand the Management category. Click the plus box to the left of the Security icon . Tip: It is also possible to display the security components by double-clicking on this name or icon. Expand the Users and Groups icon . Expand the Groups icon . Right-click the Allowed Groups icon or its name and select Set Allowed Groups . The Set Allowed Groups configuration dialog is launched. Select the name of the required group from the Selected Groups list. Click the >> button to add this group to the Available Groups list. Tip: You can also remove groups by double-clicking the required group in the Selected Groups list. Repeat this for all the

ps list. Click the >> button to add this group to the Available Groups list. Tip: You can also remove groups by double-clicking the required group in the Selected Groups list. Repeat this for all the groups that you want to remove. Tip: It is also possible to remove groups from the Allowed Groups list by expanding the Allowed Groups icon , right-clicking the required group name or its icon and selecting Remove Allowed Group . -->

Removing allowed users Top Removing allowed users If necessary, the user(s) used by Server security can be removed. To remove a user to the allowed users list Expand the Security component of the required SmartUI Server, as follows: Open the Enterprise Manager . For details, see Accessing tool windows . If necessary, expand click the plus (+) box to the left of the current icon or name Servers . If necessary, expand the name of the required Server connection . Tip: The connection name is prefaced by the SmartUI Server computer name. If necessary, expand the Management category. Click the plus box to the left of the Security icon . Tip: It is also possible to display the security components by double-clicking on this name or icon. Expand the Users and Groups icon . Expand the Users icon . Right-click the Allowed Users icon or its name and select Set Allowed Users . The Set Allowed Users configuration dialog is launched. Select the name of the required user from the Selected Users list. Click the >> button to add this user to the Available Users list. Tip: You can also double-click the required user in the Selected Users list. Repeat this for all the users that you want to remove. Ti

Click the >> button to add this user to the Available Users list. Tip: You can also double-click the required user in the Selected Users list. Repeat this for all the users that you want to remove. Tip: It is also possible to remove users from the Allowed Users list by expanding the Allowed Users icon , right-clicking the required user name or its icon and selecting Remove Allowed User . -->

Removing connections Top Removing connections If necessary, unwanted connections can be removed within the Enterprise Manager of the SmartUI Designer. WARNING! The selected connection will be removed; even if its data is being used within the SmartUI Designer e.g. by a spider. Note: The default or login connection cannot be removed. For details, see Specifying the default connection . To remove a connection: Open the Enterprise Manager . For details, see Accessing tool windows . If necessary, expand click the plus (+) box to the left of the current icon or name Servers . Right-click the name or icon of the required Server connection and select Remove connection . Tip: The connection name is prefaced by the SmartUI Server computer name. -->

Removing constants Top Removing constants Remove any constants that you no longer need. To remove unnecessary constants If necessary, select the required Constant spider and/or open its configuration view. In the Outputs section, right-click the constant that is no longer required and select Delete . WARNING! The selected constant is immediately removed from the spider and any silks that are connected to it; therefore ensure that the correct constant has been selected. -->

Removing custom form components Top Removing custom form components If necessary, you can remove any custom form component from the Toolbox tool window, when it is no longer needed. Click for more information: Note1: This will only remove these form components from being displayed within the Toolbox , so that can no longer be selected when designing graphic forms. Note2: To completely remove these form components from your computer, it is necessary to navigate to the folder specified by the CustomControlsRelativePath setting of the Designer and remove the required files manually. For details on accessing this setting, see Advanced Designer settings . WARNING! It is your responsibility to ensure that you only remove the files associated with the custom form components that you want to remove. To remove custom form components from the Toolbox: If necessary, open the Toolbox tool window in the SmartUI Designer. Right-click an existing category heading and select Add Controls . Note: The category, in which a form component is added, is dependent upon which form component is selected and NOT upon the category that is right-clicked. This displays the Custom Controls dialog, which alphabe

ategory, in which a form component is added, is dependent upon which form component is selected and NOT upon the category that is right-clicked. This displays the Custom Controls dialog, which alphabetically lists all the form components located within the specified custom controls folder (and its sub-folders). Tip1: Use the Name , Namespace , Assembly and/or Directory columns within this dialog to locate the required form components, as needed. Tip2: Select the column heading of a column to sort the list using this column and to change the sorting order between ascending and descending order. If you cannot see a checkbox for the required control, click the Browse .NET Control button and browse to the file location, typically within the plugins folder and select the DLL of this control and click Open . This adds a checkbox for this control to the Custom Controls dialog. Uncheck the checkbox(es) of all the custom form component(s) that you no longer want to appear in the Toolbox tool window and click Finish . Tip: Double-clicking on a row, within this dialog, will check or empty its checkbox. The form component(s), whose checkboxes were cleared will be removed from the Toolbox tool

ndow and click Finish . Tip: Double-clicking on a row, within this dialog, will check or empty its checkbox. The form component(s), whose checkboxes were cleared will be removed from the Toolbox tool window. Note: If all the custom form components within a custom category were removed, the custom category will also no longer appear in the Toolbox tool window either. -->

Removing customised spider inputs Top Removing customised spider inputs Any custom input created for a spider can be removed from the Inputs section of its configuration view, if necessary. Click for more details: Note1: Only the inputs that have been created using the New Input section can be removed from the spider. Note2: If the input that is removed is still connected to other spider by a silk, this silk will also be removed. To remove a custom input for a spider Open the configuration view for the required spider. For details, see Displaying spider configuration views . If necessary, navigate the spider workspace until you can see the Inputs section. Right-click the input that is no longer required and select Delete . WARNING! The selected input is immediately removed from the spider; therefore ensure that the correct input has been selected. -->

Removing customised spider outputs Top Removing customised spider outputs Any custom output created for a spider can be removed from the Outputs section of its configuration view, if necessary. Click for more details: Note1: Only the outputs that have been created using the New Output section can be removed from the spider. Note2: If the output that is removed is still connected to any other spider by a silk, this silk will also be removed. To remove a custom output for a spider Open the configuration view for the required spider. For details, see Displaying spider configuration views . If necessary, navigate the spider workspace until you can see the Outputs section. Right-click the output that is no longer required and select Delete . WARNING! The selected output is immediately removed from the spider; therefore ensure that the correct output has been selected. -->

Removing datasources Top Removing datasources Datasources that are no longer required can be removed in the Enterprise Manager from the Datasources category of the required SmartUI Server connection. For details, see Working with datasources or Working with connections . Note1: Only users that have the necessary security permissions can do this. For details, see Securing datasources . Note2: When you remove a datasource, you only remove the connection to its data and NOT the data itself, unless a Virtual datasource is being removed. To remove a datasource: Open the Enterprise Manager . For details, see Accessing tool windows . If necessary, expand click the plus (+) box to the left of the current icon or name Servers . If necessary, expand the name of the default Server connection . For details on connections, see Working with connections . Tip: The connection name is prefaced by the Server computer name. Right-click the Datasources category and select Delete Datasource . Select the required name from the displayed list of datasources. Click the Yes button when the confirmation dialog is displayed. -->

Removing folders Top Removing folders Folders can be removed from a project in the Enterprise Manager , as long as they do not contain graphic forms or subfolders. Note: This can only be performed if the currently logged on user has the necessary security permissions. For details, see Securing projects . Tip: You can only remove folders that are empty. If you want to remove a folder that contains graphic forms, you need to remove them first. For details, see Removing graphic forms . To remove a folder: Open the required project in the Enterprise Manager . For details, see Opening Projects . If necessary, expand click the plus (+) box to the left of the current icon or name its required existing folder(s), until the required folder is displayed. Right-click on this folder name or its icon and select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. Delete Folder . -->

Removing graphic forms Top Removing graphic forms Graphic forms can be removed from your project in the Enterprise Manager . WARNING! When you delete a graphic form from your project, it is removed from your system. We recommend that you see Tips for removing graphic forms from projects before you remove any graphic form from your project. Note: This can only be performed if the currently logged on user has the necessary security permissions. For details, see Securing projects . To remove a graphic form from a project: Open the required project in the Enterprise Manager . For details, see Opening Projects . If necessary, expand click the plus (+) box to the left of the current icon or name its required existing folder(s), until the required folder is displayed. Right-click on this graphic form or its icon and select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. Delete Graphic Form . -->

Removing Incidents Top Removing Incidents Since you can only assign an incident to a SINGLE category, you may want to remove an incident from one category and assign it to another. In this case either: drag the incident to the required category, this reassigns this incident immediately or select the required incident/s in the top right hand Incidents list and click the Delete Incident button. The deleted incident/s will be added to the _Uncategorised category when they re-occur. To permanently remove an incident from an AlarmManagement agent: either remove this alarm type for this agent (add it to the Available list) OR reassign this incident to a route NOT assigned to a route on which this AlarmManagement agent is allocated BEFORE deleting it from the database. -->

Removing Incidents Top Removing Incidents Since you can only assign an incident to a SINGLE category, you may want to remove an incident from one category and assign it to another. In this case either: drag the incident to the required category, this reassigns this incident immediately or select the required incident/s in the top right hand Incidents list and click the Delete Incident button. The deleted incident/s will be added to the _Uncategorised category when they re-occur. To permanently remove an incident from an AlarmManagement agent: either remove this alarm type for this agent (add it to the Available list) OR reassign this incident to a route NOT assigned to a route on which this AlarmManagement agent is allocated BEFORE deleting it from the database. -->

Removing input and output variables Top Removing input and output variables To remove unnecessary input or output variables - no longer used by the current script object this contains a script and provides its self-contained environment within which it is run. of the Script Engine spider . To remove unnecessary input or output variables: If necessary, select the required Script Engine spider and/or open its configuration view. For details, see Selecting spiders or Displaying spider configuration views . Right-click the unnecessary variable in either the Inputs or Outputs section and select Delete . WARNING! The selected variable is immediately removed from the spider and any silks that are connected to or from it; therefore ensure that the correct variable has been selected. Note: You are only able to remove the variable inputs and outputs i.e. var # , where # is a unique number starting from 1. -->

Removing input and output variables Top Removing input and output variables Remove input and/or output variables that are no longer needed. WARNING! Ensure that you do not remove any input or output variable that is still being referenced in the expression, otherwise the expression will not be evaluated. To remove unnecessary input and/or output variables If necessary, select the required Expression spider and/or open its configuration view. Right-click the unnecessary i# input in the Inputs section and/or the unnecessary j# output in the Outputs section, where # is a unique number starting from 1 and select Delete . WARNING! The selected variable is immediately removed from the spider and any silks that are connected to or from it; therefore ensure that the correct variable has been selected. -->

Removing languages from graphic forms Top Removing languages from graphic forms Remove unneeded languages from the graphic form translation table. Note: The Graphic Form Language column (whose header is bold and underlined) CANNOT be removed. To remove a language from a graphic form translation table Ensure that the required graphic form is opened and displayed in the Design workspace . Open the Translation tool window. For details, see Accessing tool windows . Right-click on a column heading of the language you want to remove and select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. Delete . WARNING! This will immediately remove the selected column; therefore ensure that the correct column is selected before selecting this menu option. -->

Removing languages from projects Top Removing languages from projects Remove languages from the project translation table that are no longer required by the users of the graphic forms in this project. To remove a language from a global translation table Open the required project in the Enterprise Manager . For details, see Opening Projects . Double-click its Translation object or its icon . This displays the Translation configuration dialog , which can be maximised and/or manually resized as required . Right-click on the required column heading and select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. Delete Language . WARNING! This immediately removes the selected column from both the Graphic Form and Data tabs of the project translation table; therefore ensure that you select the correct column. Note: You cannot remove the last language from the a project translation table. -->

Removing layers Top Removing layers Remove layers, whose form components are no longer needed or that are identical to those on another layer on the graphic form. WARNING! When you remove a layer from a graphic form, EACH control a visible form component used to display data or accept user input in the graphic form. See form component. and graphic element a form component that typically provides drawing functionality for the graphic form. See form component. attached to this layer are also removed and cannot be recovered . Tip: Save the graphic form before removing any layers. For details, see Saving graphic forms . To remove a layer Display the configured layers of the required graphic form: Open and display the required graphic form in the Design workspace . Open the Levels and Layers tool window. For details, see Accessing tool windows . In the grid, right-click the row heading of the required layer and select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. Delete Layer . The confirmation dialog is displayed; click Yes to remove this layer, INCLUDING its attached controls and graphic elements from this graphic form. Note: You can

also known as clicking. Delete Layer . The confirmation dialog is displayed; click Yes to remove this layer, INCLUDING its attached controls and graphic elements from this graphic form. Note: You cannot remove the last layer from in grid. Note: The row below the deleted row becomes the edited layer of this graphic form - so any visible form component that is subsequently added to this graphic form will be attached to this layer. -->

Removing levels Top Removing levels Remove any levels that you no longer need. To remove a level Configure the levels of the required graphic form: Open and display the required graphic form in the Design workspace . Open the Levels and Layers tool window. For details, see Accessing tool windows . If necessary, display the configured level(s). For details, see Hiding or showing configured levels . In the grid, right-click the column heading of the required level and select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. Delete Level . WARNING! This immediately removes this level, so ensure that you right-click the correct column. Note1: You are unable to remove the last level in the grid. Note2: The column to the right of the column being removed, becomes the visible level for this graphic form. For details, see Identifying visible levels . -->

Removing mapping pairs Top Removing mapping pairs Remove mapping pairs that are no longer required from the Mapping spider to avoid confusion. To remove unnecessary mapping pairs If necessary, select the required Mapping spider and/or open its configuration view. Right-click the unnecessary mapping pair name in either the Inputs or Outputs section and select Delete . WARNING! The selected mapping pair is immediately removed from BOTH the Inputs or Outputs sections of the spider and any silks that are connected to or from them; therefore ensure that the correct mapping pair has been selected. -->

Removing numerator, denominator and offset values Top Removing numerator, denominator and offset values Remove unnecessary numerators (the multiplying values), denominators (the dividing values) and/or offset values. To remove unnecessary numerator, denominator or offset values If necessary, select the required Multiply and Divide spider and/or open its configuration view. Right-click the unnecessary numerator ( Numerator# ), denominator ( Denominator# ) or offset ( Offset# ) value in the Inputs section, where # is a unique number starting from 1 and select Delete . WARNING! The selected value is immediately removed from the spider and any silks that are connected to it; therefore ensure that the correct value has been selected. Note: You are able to remove every input in the Inputs section, if necessary. -->

metadata.title: Removing numerator, denominator and offset values

text: Removing performance counters Top Removing performance counters Remove unnecessary or useless performance indicators. To remove unnecessary performance counters If necessary, select the required Performance Counter spider and/or open its configuration view. In the Outputs section, right-click the performance counter that is no longer required and select Delete . WARNING! The selected output is immediately removed from the spider and any silks that are connected to it; therefore ensure that the correct output is selected. -->

Removing profiles Top Removing profiles Remove unnecessary user profiles. Note: This can only be performed if the currently logged on user has the necessary security permissions. To remove a profile Select the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager , as follows: Open the Enterprise Manager . Navigate to Servers > [Server Name] . Tip: The connection name is prefixed by the SmartUI Server computer name. If necessary, expand the Management category. Click the plus box to the left of the Profile icon . Tip: It is also possible to display the profiles by double-clicking on this name or icon. Right-click the required name of the profile or its icon and select Delete . WARNING! When you remove a profile, all of its customised configuration settings will be removed from your system. Click the Yes button to confirm that this profile is to be removed. -->

Removing projects Top Removing projects Projects which are no longer needed can be removed in the Enterprise Manager . WARNING! When you remove a project, this will remove all of its folders, graphic forms and the global translation table from your system. We recommend that you see Tips for removing graphic forms from projects before removing any project. Note: This can only be performed if the currently logged on user has the necessary security permissions. For details, see Securing projects . To remove a project: Select the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager , as follows: Open the Enterprise Manager . Navigate to Servers > [Server Name] . Tip: The connection name is prefixed by the SmartUI Server computer name. Right-click the Projects category and select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. Delete Datasource . From the displayed list of projects, select the required project name. Click the Yes button when the confirmation dialog is displayed. -->

Removing properties Top Removing properties Remove previously exposed hidden properties of the selected object, that are no longer required. To remove unnecessary input and/or output properties If necessary, select the required Hidden Property spider and/or open its configuration view. Right-click the unnecessary property input or output in the Inputs or Outputs section and select Delete . WARNING! The selected property is immediately removed from the spider and any silks that are connected to or from it; therefore ensure that the correct property is selected. Note: You are able to remove all the outputs and all the inputs except for Object . -->

Removing Pseudonyms and Macros Top Removing Pseudonyms and Macros Pseudonyms and macros act as placeholders for part or all of a textual command that is sent to a Command agent . For details, see Using Pseudonyms and Macros . It is also possible to remove any pseudonyms and/or macros that have been created and are no longer required. To remove unnecessary pseudonyms and/or macros: Edit the required Command agent. For details, see Editing Agents . This will display the Edit Command agent dialog. Select the Pseudonyms and Macros tab. Select the required pseudonym and/or macro and click the Remove pseudonym or macro button to delete this entry. WARNING! This will immediately remove the currently selected row. Tip: It is possible to immediately undo this removal by clicking the Refresh button, although once the Update or OK buttons are clicked this row will be permanently removed. -->

Removing Pseudonyms and Macros Top Removing Pseudonyms and Macros Pseudonyms and macros act as placeholders for part or all of a textual command that is sent to a Command agent . For details, see Using Pseudonyms and Macros . It is also possible to remove any pseudonyms and/or macros that have been created and are no longer required. To remove unnecessary pseudonyms and/or macros: Edit the required Command agent. For details, see Editing Agents . This will display the Edit Command agent dialog. Select the Pseudonyms and Macros tab. Select the required pseudonym and/or macro and click the Remove pseudonym or macro button to delete this entry. WARNING! This will immediately remove the currently selected row. Tip: It is possible to immediately undo this removal by clicking the Refresh button, although once the Update or OK buttons are clicked this row will be permanently removed. -->

Removing scaled values Top Removing scaled values Remove any values that you no longer want to scale according to the global scaling factor configured for this Scaling spider. To remove scaled values If necessary, select the required Scaling spider and/or open its configuration view. Right-click the unnecessary value ( RawValue# ) in the Inputs section, where # is a unique number starting from 1 and select Delete . WARNING! The selected value is immediately removed from the spider in addition to the corresponding Engineering Value# output from the Outputs section and any silks that are connected to these items; therefore ensure that the correct value has been selected. Note: You are able to remove every input in the Inputs section, if necessary. -->

Removing script objects Top Removing script objects Script objects that are no longer required can be removed from the Server Scripts datasource in the Enterprise Manager . WARNING! Once a script object is deleted, this will remove the associated script and the list of associated external assemblies, although this will not remove the associated references themselves. Note: This can only be performed if the currently logged on user has the necessary security permissions. For details, see Securing datasources . To remove a script object: Select the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager , as follows: Open the Enterprise Manager . Navigate to Servers > [Server Name] . Tip: The connection name is prefixed by the SmartUI Server computer name. If necessary, expand the Datasources category. Click the plus box to the left of the Server Scripts datasource or its icon . Tip: It is also possible to display the script objects by double-clicking on this name or icon. Right-click the required name of the script object or its icon and select Delete Script . The confirmation dialog is displayed; click Yes to remove this script object from your system. -->

Removing silks Top Removing silks If a silk is no longer required, it can be removed from the spider workspace. Note: This will also remove any Data spider (data element or property) connected to this silk. To remove a silk from the spider workspace: Open the required spider workspace. If necessary navigate the spider workspace using the scroll bars, until you can see the required silk. Right-click this silk and select the Silks menu. This will list all the silks that are represented by the currently selected line. Each silk is described as follows: SourceSpiderName.outputname -> DestinationSpidername.inputname.. From the Silks menu select the description of the required silk. From the displayed menu of options for this silk, choose the Delete option. WARNING! The selected silk and any attached Data spider(s) will immediately be removed from the spider workspace. To remove all the silks from a spider workspace: If necessary, open the required spider workspace. Right-click the spider workspace and select Delete All Silks... . Click the Yes button when the confirmation dialog is displayed. All the silk(s) and all the Data spider(s) are removed from this spider workspace. -->

Removing silks from template sets Top Removing silks from template sets Remove silks from a template set so that they will not be enabled when this template set is activated. This prevents their connected spiders from performing their functions. WARNING! Any silk not associated with any template set will never be enabled. To remove an existing silk from one or more template sets Open the required spider workspace. If necessary navigate the spider workspace using the scroll bars, until you can see the required silk. Right-click this silk and select the Silks menu. This lists all the silks represented by the currently selected line, as follows: SourceSpiderName.outputname -> DestinationSpidername.inputname. From the Silks menu select the description of the required silk. From the displayed menu of options for this silk, select the Template Sets menu. This display the names of the available template sets of this spider workspace. Ensure that there is NOT a tick mark to the left of name of every template set that you want to remove this silk from, if not select the name of this template set. Note: Any template set without a tick mark, will disable this silk when it is activated, thereb

every template set that you want to remove this silk from, if not select the name of this template set. Note: Any template set without a tick mark, will disable this silk when it is activated, thereby effectively preventing the spiders that this silk connects from operating. Unless the silk is associated with the 'Default' template set, in which case it will ALWAYS be enabled. Tip: Clicking the name of the template set will add or remove its tick mark. Repeat this procedure, if necessary, until there is no tick mark to the left of name of every template set that you want to remove this silk from. -->

Removing simulated data outputs Top Removing simulated data outputs Remove the simulated data outputs that you no longer require. To remove unnecessary simulated data outputs If necessary, select the required Simulation spider and/or open its configuration view. Right-click the unnecessary simulated data output in the Outputs section and select Delete . WARNING! The selected simulated data output is immediately removed from the spider and any silks that are connected to or from it; therefore ensure that the correct simulated data output has been selected. Note: You are able to remove all the outputs, if necessary. -->

Removing spiders Top Removing spiders If a spider is no longer required, it can be removed from the spider workspace. Click for more details: When a spider is removed from the spider workspace, the following items are also removed: All the silks connecting this spider to and from other spiders in the spider workspace. Any Data spiders connected to this spider. To remove a spider from the spider workspace: If necessary, open the required spider workspace. Select the required spider. Tip: You can also press the DELETE key. Right-click the title bar of this spider and select Delete Spider . WARNING! The selected spider and any attached silk(s) and Data spider(s) will immediately be removed from the spider workspace. To remove all the spiders from a spider workspace: If necessary, open the required spider workspace. Right-click the spider workspace and select Delete All Spiders... . text: Replicating profiles Top Replicating profiles If necessary, you can create one or more standard profiles for all of your SmartUI Servers by replicating them. To replicate profiles Create and configure the required profiles on a single Server. For details, see Creating profiles and Configuring profiles . Ensure that these profiles are appropriately configured and that they are saved. For details, see Saving the Server . Copy the required Profile data files from this SmartUI Server to the required folders of the other Servers. For details on the required data files and their location, see Locating saved profiles . This will immediately add these profiles to these SmartUI Servers. Note: It will still be necessary to ensure that the correct users and/or groups are assigned to each of these profiles on each of the SmartUI Servers. -->

Replication Top Replication While catch-up deals with the requirement for a new server being added to the cluster to be a mirror image at the current point in time, replication is concerned with how changes that occur as a result of external influences on the cluster are dealt with. For instance, external changes affecting the cluster members can occur from a Adroit client application or from Agent Server scan inputs. Client changes are typically a result of changing a set point from within a UI. All these sources of change are replicated to all Agent Servers in the cluster in order to maintain the mirror image state of the clustered servers. Two instances of configuring replication within a cluster are: Client Runtime Transaction Shadowing : All transactions initiated by a client on a server are shadowed to the other server in the cluster to provide total data replication. Parallel scanning : Each cluster server is configured to replicate the scanning tasks to provide scan task replication, that is, each server performs scanning as if it were a normal server. This is an alternative to automatically shadowing the scanned data. -->

Requirements for Distributed Systems Top Requirements for Distributed Systems If the installation is to form part of a distributed Adroit system with the ability to share data across the network within one project (i.e. it is not a simple standalone system) then it is essential that the following requirements are met: Check that all computers belong to the same Network Workgroup or Domain Using Adroit Configuration Setup , check that all Agent Servers are configured as part of the same project by ensuring the Agent Servers have the same Project Name. Note: Project names must not be longer than 8 characters, nor contain any embedded spaces. When more than one project name is being used on the same network, ensure that the first 3 characters are unique. Click the Project Options button, and ensure that Enable remote servers to automatically detect this server is checked. The checkbox Explicit Additional Server Connections should remain unchecked initially. Ensure that each computer within the same project has a unique name for its local Agent Server. Note: The name " Adroit " is given by default, and if more than one Agent Server with this name is started, the message "Cannot start d

n the same project has a unique name for its local Agent Server. Note: The name " Adroit " is given by default, and if more than one Agent Server with this name is started, the message "Cannot start duplicate AS" will be displayed. (This message is also displayed when more than one Agent Server is started on a computer.) If duplicate agent names exist in the Agent Servers, the one on the local Agent Server will be used. It is therefore advisable to ensure that agent names are unique over the whole project. For details, see Naming Agents . Check that each computer has a HASP software protection key fitted Check that each computer has every Adroit user set up identically by its local User Accounts applet , so that the same User Names and Passwords exist on all the computers in the project. Verify that the Number of Connections (go to the Options/Agent Information menu option) equals the number of computers on the project that have an Agent Server running. Check that all devices that are to be scanned have been installed using the Drivers dialog during the Configuration Setup procedure described earlier. Check that the physical memory is 25% more than the committed memory (see Total C

to be scanned have been installed using the Drivers dialog during the Configuration Setup procedure described earlier. Check that the physical memory is 25% more than the committed memory (see Total Commit Charge in the Performance tab of the Task Manager). Verify on each computer, using the Agent Server Configurator or Agent Browser that an AgentGroup tag exists for each Agent Server in the project. For example, for a project name ‘Juice’ consisting of 3 Agent Servers called PLANT_A, PLANT_B and PLANT_X, you will see PLANT_A and PLANT_B as AgentGroup tags if you pull down the Group list box in PLANT_X’s Configurator. For additional assistance, see Trouble-shooting . -->

Devices of certain protocol drivers also provide the following functionality (as specified in their protocol driver documentation ): Reset the device, so that it will close and re-open its connection to the connected front-end. Note: This will only work for the current device, if its protocol driver supports this functionality. Switch the device, which causes the device to switch the connection from the primary to the secondary connection Note: This will only work for the current device, if this secondary connection has been configured and if its protocol driver supports this functionality.. To reset or switch a device: If necessary, display the Tag scanning configuration dialog, either by editing the required Device agent or when scanning an agent . RestartOnZeroChannels Top RDAdminName WARNING: Registry settings are recorded as ADVANCED information and should not be used unless you understand exactly how these will affect the operation of your Adroit installation, IF YOU HAVE ANY DOUBTS, PLEASE CONTACT Adroit SUPPORT, BEFORE CHANGING THE REGISTRY. PLEASE NOTE: When working on a 64 bit operating system, remember to add "\Wow6432Node" to the path of each registry setting after "\SOFTWARE", for instance: "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Adroit Technologies". Remote Desktop (RDP) clients can now get a free node connection to obtain engineering access to the Agent Server, by designating a virtual client running as a defined user to be considered as the local client. This is done by specifying the username of this defined user by adding and configuring the following WG.INI registry string value: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Workgroup\WG.INI (REG_SZ) RDAdminName = Windows username of the required user. By default this registry entry does not exist and therefore all Remote Desktop (RDP) clients are subject to node licensing. This registry value must be created and set to the required username to esta

By default this registry entry does not exist and therefore all Remote Desktop (RDP) clients are subject to node licensing. This registry value must be created and set to the required username to establish free connections for that user. The reason for this RDAdminName feature is because typically the concept of a local Agent Server in a virtual environment does not exist as the Agent Server process is available to ALL virtual clients. However, local Agent Server connections are important to allow engineering access to the Agent Server in exactly the same way as this occurs on a physical computer. Therefore, this RDAdminName feature allows users to designate a virtual client running as a defined user to be considered as the local client. -->

Restoring Adroit Data Files Top Restoring Adroit Data Files Ensure that the backed up files are copied (if uncompressed) or extracted (if compressed) into their applicable data folders. Note: Refer to the backup profile if it exists, for the list of the Adroit data paths that were backed up. -->
Restoring Adroit System Files Top Restoring Adroit System Files Ensure that the backed up files are copied (if uncompressed) or extracted (if compressed) into the Adroit installation folder. -->

Restoring Compressed Files Top Restoring Compressed Files This compressed file is in the standard Winzip format; the component files are stored with their full path information from the root. Therefore use WinZip or a product that can open WinZip files to extract these files into their original folders, wherever possible. Note: Event log files are stored with their actual backup location path from the root. -->

Restoring Registry Files Top Restoring Registry Files Two registry files are backed up, namely, the global Adroit registry settings and the Adroit registry settings specific to the current user. Execute (double-click on) the required registry file to restore its registry settings. -->

Restoring Uncompressed Files Top Restoring Uncompressed Files In this case, use Windows Explorer or a similar product to copy the required files from their backup folder to their required destination folder. -->

Reversing Input Slot Order Top Reversing Input Slot Order It may be necessary, due to external constraints, to read the 16 bit input rawValue into the 16 Boolean input slots V01-V16 in reverse order, so that V01 becomes the Least Significant Bit of the rawValue .slot. This can be achieved by making the Registry Key ReverseMultiStateBits FALSE (i.e. set to 0) for WG.INI. The default is always TRUE (i.e. set to 1) making v01 the Most Significant Bit. To reverse input slots order (v1 to v16) within the MultiState agent. -->

Routing to Audio Devices Top Routing to Audio Devices Routing an alarm to an audio device has the effect of incrementing or decrementing the specified slot that must be of type boolean or integer. New alarms cause the slot value to be incremented, and acknowledgment of these alarms will cause the value to be decremented. If the start slot of the Beeper agent is used, it will activate a repetitive beeping sound in the PC speaker. The sound pitch will become higher each time the start slot is incremented by a new alarm, and will be lowered when an alarm is acknowledged and the slot decremented. The priority of a Beeper agent determines the interval between beeping i.e. a high priority will beep faster than a lower priority Beeper agent. If the start slot of a MultiMedia agent is used, this will activate the configured multi-media file. These files may be any Windows compatible multi-media standard such as .WAV, .AVI, .MID and .RMI. Alternatively, integer slots of any other agent type may be used to keep a count of active and unacknowledged alarms. To route the alarm to an audio device . To remove a current audio device . -->

Running the Main Subroutine Top Running the Main Subroutine The Script agent executes a single subroutine, or "main" subroutine. This main subroutine can be executed in one of four different ways, namely: On demand, by manually poking ( putslotting ) a one into the runNow slot. While the main subroutine is running any new request for it to run will be ignored. To stop the main subroutine from running, poke a zero into the runNow slot. This method will cause the script to be recompiled, as it needs to be re-initialised after termination. By scheduling , which is based on a simple schedule; e.g. execute every hour starting from midnight on the 1 st of January. By triggering , which is based on a list of tags. Each trigger has an identification number that corresponds to its position in the list of triggers. The first tag in the list has an identification number equal to one, etc. Reordering this list will change the trigger identification numbers. To determine from within your script the value of a trigger or the tag that triggered the script, use the system object denoted by Adroit . By using a combination of scheduling and triggering . For instance, using scheduling on condition th

value of a trigger or the tag that triggered the script, use the system object denoted by Adroit . By using a combination of scheduling and triggering . For instance, using scheduling on condition that triggering has occurred, will apply a time dead band to the triggering of the script, e.g. run every five seconds but only if a tag in the trigger list has changed. This prevents a flood of triggers initiating multiple executions. -->

text: Saving changes made to connected Servers Top Saving changes made to connected Servers Apart from creating graphic forms, the SmartUI Designer is able to configure any of the connected SmartUI Servers. Click for more details: For this reason, it is also possible to save the changes that are made to each of the connected SmartUI Servers from within the SmartUI Designer itself. In other words, the SmartUI Server’s data can be saved without requiring direct access to the SmartUI Server application. In addition to making remote configuration of the SmartUI Server possible, this also allows the SmartUI Server to be configured when it is being run as a service. Note: The SmartUI Server can also be automatically save its data. For details, see Saving the SmartUI Server . To save changes made to a connected Server: Open the Enterprise Manager . For details, see Accessing tool windows . If necessary, expand click the plus (+) box to the left of the current icon or name Servers . Right-click the name or icon of the required Server connection and select Save Server Data . -->

text: Saving data files Top Saving data files Data that is saved by the SmartUI adheres to the following format: Note: For details on the data that is saved by the SmartUI , see Locating saved data . Data is always saved to two files without extensions: FileName and FileNameINDEX, where: FileName is where the data is actually stored and the INDEX file is used when referencing its data. In addition to these two files, two backup files usually exist, which are prefixed with the word BAK: FileNameBAK and FileNameINDEXBAK, where these files are copies of the last version of these saved data files. Therefore if currently saved data becomes corrupted, then these files can be used to return to the previously saved data. Note1: These backup files need to be manually renamed before their data can be read by the Server. Note2: When backing up the data it is not recommended to backup these files. -->

Saving graphic forms Top Saving graphic forms It is important to save graphic forms frequently while you design them to ensure that you will not lose any changes that are made. However the Designer provides the following additional options other than simply saving the contents of the current graphic form: Note: A graphic form also allows the user to decide whether any recent changes made to it, should be saved, when it is closed. To save a graphic form: Click the Save toolbar button (that appears above the graphic form in the Design workspace ) or press CTRL+S. To save a graphic form with a different name: Click the Save As toolbar button (that appears above the graphic form in the Design workspace ). To convert a graphic form into a wizard: Open the required graphic form and select the Save as Wizard graphic form toolbar button (that appears above the graphic form in the Design workspace ). For more details about wizards, see Working with wizards . Then use the Substitution configuration dialog to create ALL the necessary substitutions for this new wizard. To publish a run-time version of a graphic form: Click the Save and Publish toolbar button (that appears above the graphic for

ion dialog to create ALL the necessary substitutions for this new wizard. To publish a run-time version of a graphic form: Click the Save and Publish toolbar button (that appears above the graphic form in the Design workspace ). We recommend that you publish your graphic forms since this creates an optimised run-time version for the Operator. This process strips out the design-time information from the graphic form to reduce the size and complexity of the graphic form that is sent to the Operator, which also improves its loading time. For more details, see Publishing run-time versions of graphic forms . -->

Saving spider workspaces Top Saving spider workspaces Save the spider workspace to ensure that any recent changes will not be lost, such as: any spiders, silks or template sets that are added or configured. Note: Whenever the spider workspace is saved, any Data spiders that have no silks connected to them will also be deleted. In order to save a spider workspace, the document that is associated with the spider workspace must be saved. If the spider workspace is in the Spiders Configuration tool window, then the graphic form that is currently displayed in the Design workspace needs to be saved. For details, see Saving graphic forms . Note: If the associated document is closed, before any changes are saved, a confirmation dialog will be displayed asking whether these changes are required to be saved or not. -->

Saving the Current Backup Configuration for Later Re-use Top Saving the Current Backup Configuration for Later Re-use Either If the current backup configuration will be used most often, then click the Set defaults button to save these settings as the default settings, which will be used, when the "Default" backup profile is selected. Or If the current backup configuration describes a less-frequent backup, then create a backup profile for this. -->

Saving the Server Top Saving the SmartUI Server The SmartUI Server is a "data portal" which exposes data from a number of disparate sources that are both external and internal to it. Save the Server for the following reasons: To save all the datasources connected to it. Note1: Each datasource specifies which of its items are required to be saved. Note2: The SmartUI Server saves the complete datasource, including any Server configuration options, which have been performed via the SmartUI Designer. To save any changes that have been made to internal sources of data, which consist of Client-specific data that is managed by the Server. This includes the security and profile configuration and any projects that have been created. Note1: For details on where these and any other data files that are saved by SmartUI can be located, see Locating saved data . Note2: For details on how to automate backing up the Server data, see Backing up Server data . Methods of saving the Server’s data: Automatically: Typically the SmartUI Server will be automatically saved when it is closed (or when the service is stopped), however this can increase the time taken for the Server to shutdown. This automatic

ically: Typically the SmartUI Server will be automatically saved when it is closed (or when the service is stopped), however this can increase the time taken for the Server to shutdown. This automatic saving can either be enabled or disabled by configuring the SaveServerOnShutdown Server setting. For details on accessing this setting, see Advanced Server settings . Note: It is usually NOT recommended to disable this automatic saving when the Server is running as a service. For details, see Launching the SmartUI Server . In addition the SmartUI Server is also able to save its data continually, according to a user-configurable frequency, which by default saves this data every 2 hours. For details, see Server saving settings . Manually: You can save the SmartUI Server manually, from within the SmartUI Designer, which configures the SmartUI Server, as follows: Open the Enterprise Manager . For details, see Accessing tool windows . If necessary, expand click the plus (+) box to the left of the current icon or name Servers . Saving the Tag Monitor Utility Top Saving the Tag Monitor Utility The Tag Monitor utility can display current values of one or more tag values from a particular Agent Server, in tabular and trend format, without having to specifically draw a mimic or create a trend to do so. By default the list of the monitored tags are saved in the ‘default_tags.txt’ file located in the folder in which the utility is run, however it is possible to create different tag lists for different servers, simply by start the utility with a suitably named command-line parameter. mand-line parameter. For details, see Launching the Tag Monitor Utility . The following additional operational parameters are also saved, per tag list, in the ‘adrmonitor.ini’ file that is located in the folder in which the utility is run: The currently connected Agent Server. Scan Bad Indication Methodologies Top Scan Bad Indication Methodologies Each WanClient is able to determine how the scan bad status of all the tags that it communicates is set within its local Agent Server. This is a global setting, in that it applies to ALL the tag values that are communicated by this WanClient, irrespective of the number of WanServers that these values are communicated to and / or from. This is configured within the Tag bad philosophy group of the WanClient Configurator dialog, which is launched by selecting Open Configurator from the File menu. Note: Although these are actually ‘scan bad’ indication methodologies, whenever the ‘scan bad’ status bit is set for a tag, this will result in this tag being marked ‘bad’ i.e. its ‘bad’ status bit will also be set. Therefore the terms ‘scan bad’ and ‘tag bad’ can be used synonymously. The following four events can be used to determine how the scan bad status of these tags are set within the Agent Server that is on the WanClient computer: On comms start: This event occurs when the WanClient begins communicating the tag values to and / or from the WanClients specified within its tag link database. On comms fail: This event

ent computer: On comms start: This event occurs when the WanClient begins communicating the tag values to and / or from the WanClients specified within its tag link database. On comms fail: This event occurs when the communication of the WanClient to and / or from its listed WanClients is halted unexpectedly. On comms stop: This event occurs when the communication of the WanClient to and / or from its listed WanClients is stopped. On client shutdown: This event occurs when the WanClient application itself is exited i.e. the WanClient.exe is shut down. . For each of these four events, one of the following scan bad indication methodologies can be selected: Do nothing: This leaves the current status of the scan bad bit for all of the communicated local Agent Server tags unchanged. Mark bad: This sets the scan bad bit for all of the communicated local Agent Server tags to ON. Mark healthy: This sets the scan bad bit for all of the communicated local Agent Server tags to OFF. The Include control tags checkbox, can also be checked or cleared to include or exclude the tags within control groups for each of these scan bad indication methodologies. However the following needs to be taken co

ntrol tags checkbox, can also be checked or cleared to include or exclude the tags within control groups for each of these scan bad indication methodologies. However the following needs to be taken cognisance of when this option is enabled: If the tag is currently marked bad, WanClient will mark it healthy (set its scan bad status bit to ON) when it receives a valid value update from the required WanServer. Since the values of tags within control groups are NOT received from the WanServer, the Mark bad methodology must NEVER be configured for tags within control group, when using the On comms start event, as this will result in the ‘scan bad’ bit ALWAYS being set for these tags. When the WanClient starts up, control tags are assumed to have dirty values until a value is received from the WanServer. Updates from a WanServer that fail to putslot in the local Agent Server will also cause values to be "dirty" again. Dirty values are NOT sent to WanServer to prevent "blind" value changes. Then again, this methodology CAN be used, if these tags are configured as dual mode tags i.e. tags that are members of BOTH a control and a normal group. For further details, see Dual mode tags . Scan Jobs within Selected Devices Top Scan Jobs within Selected Devices The Scanning Monitor utility provides information on the scanning (communications) configuration for a particular Agent Server, so this information can be used to manually fine-tune the scanning subsystem to achieve optimal performance. For details, see Monitoring Scanning in Adroit . The list in the middle of this utility, displays the scan jobs for the selected device or devices within the devices list, directly above this list. For details, see Devices within Selected Agent Server Database . Note1: Any configured @scans will NOT appear in this utility because scan agents are NOT involved in @scanning functionality - these are simply internal slot-to-slot subscriptions that change in real time mode. Note2: Scan jobs are automatically created by Adroit to group the scanned tags together in such a way as to minimise scanning load and to maximise throughput. For details on how to assist with this process, see Scanning Optimization Tips . ng Optimization Tips . This list, consists of the following columns: Scan job: This identifies the name of scan job for the selected device(s) in the devices list. The other columns indicate the following attributes of this scan job: Started: This is 1 when this scan job has started. Comms status: This is one of three possible values: Unknown: scanning has not yet started. Bad: scanning has started but there are some unsuccessful transactions or bad scan items, if this is the case, check your configuration and cabling. Healthy: scanning has started and is successful. Required rate: This indicates the rate at which the scan job is expected to scan the front-end device. Note: A value of zero means that this scan job is exception based and does not poll or request its front-end device for changes to its data. Effective rate: This indicates the rate at which the scan job is actually scanning the front-end device. text: Scan Point Licensing Exceptions Top Scan Point Licensing Exceptions Scan point licenses or 'scan points' are just one of the components of an Adroit license. These are consumed when information is being manipulated in some way. Their typical usage is when communicating (scanning) a value to a front-end device. However, there are a number of other consumers of scan point licenses, as follows: Note: This is in accordance with the generally adopted Adroit policy, where information is provided freely, but where you are obliged to pay for the service of manipulating information. Each DbAccess and Script agent consumes a single scan point license to run. This license is checked before doing a DbAccess transaction for the first time (on a per agent basis) or running the Script for the first time (on a per agent basis) and is only returned when the agent is deleted. Any derived Custom agent, containing a Script engine, will consume a scan point license. Any pokes performed (i.e. an operation that changes the value of an agent.slot) using either the Adroit OLE Automation Interface ( MISSRVR ) or the Adroit ActiveX component will consume a scan point license for each unique tag (agent.slot)

hat changes the value of an agent.slot) using either the Adroit OLE Automation Interface ( MISSRVR ) or the Adroit ActiveX component will consume a scan point license for each unique tag (agent.slot) that is "poked". Also, as the AlarmTag, LogTag and ScanTag functions all use pokes internally, calls to these functions will also consume scan point licenses. Also the FetchChanges & FetchValues functions of the Adroit ActiveX component also consume scan point licenses for the same reason. Any tag (agent.slot) writes from the Adroit OPC Server will consume one scan point license per unique tag. Once a Command agent has been allowed to perform commands, scan point licenses are consumed by every unique phone number specified by this agent and/or used to send SMS messages to it. For details, see Specifying Additional Callers . The SNMPMgr agent consumes a scan point for each unique OID value that is monitored, written and/or trapped. Any agent created for a UDT agent type created by the UDT Agent Type Designer consumes (number of slots-1) scan points. The other scan point will be consumed if and when its rawValue slot is scanned. -->

Scanning Deadband Configuration Tips Top Scanning Deadband Configuration Tips A significant change or noise filter can be specified in the Deadband field when a tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). is being scanned to a FED front-end device, which is a device that is accessed directly by the user, such as a PLC or RTU. . Scanning Diagnostics Tips Top Diagnosing Scanning Problems Adroit protocol drivers communicate via standard serial ports, network cards, and other proprietary mechanisms. These ports, cards or devices are collectively referred to as resources in the Adroit protocol drivers. These resources should always be tested using a proper diagnostic tool before being used for the first time. Once it is established that the communications resource is in working order, further fault testing may be carried out. Networks The simplest way of testing a network card is to check whether shared resources like printers and shares are visible to the computer, once the LAN software has loaded on the computer. If the card is not used to communicate on the LAN, then the configuration program for the card can be run, and used to test the card. To do this, the computer must be clean booted so that no drivers are loaded when the diagnostic software runs. Other plug-in cards Plug in cards may be supplied with diagnostic software or in some cases with only a sample program. If neither the diagnostic software, nor the sample application can communicate then the card or hardware configuration may be at fault. Sca

nostic software or in some cases with only a sample program. If neither the diagnostic software, nor the sample application can communicate then the card or hardware configuration may be at fault. Scanning-troubleshooting resources: Golden Rules for Scanning : general scanning tips Configuration Problems : The most commonly experienced fault in the first-time use of any communications link is incorrect configuration. TroubleShooting Communication Problems : how to determine the cause of a communication failure. Scanning Troubleshooting FAQ : answers to commonly experienced problems/issues associated with scanning. Scanning-issue Checklist before Contacting Support : a checklist of steps to try to resolve this issue yourself AND if you cannot then this provide the steps you need to take to adequately report your scanning issue to support. text: Scanning Interval Configuration Tips Top Scanning Interval Configuration Tips A scanning interval can be specified in the Scan rate (ms) field when a tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). is being scanned to a FED front-end device, which is a device that is accessed directly by the user, such as a PLC or RTU. . This is used to specify the time, in milliseconds, which will elapse before this value is communicated to or from this device. For details on scanning tags, see How to scan a tag or Scanning tags for general scanning information. Note: This field should ONLY be specified when configuring POLLED devices, since event-based or TELEMETRY devices do not use setting when communicating. Please consider the following recommendations when configuring this scanning interval: It is good practice to make your scan-interval longer, for polled drivers, because this minimises the queuing of tasks to be performed by the driver. Scan-tasks are created by Adroit (not the driver) whenever the scan-interval expires. Once a scan task has been created it is given to the driver, where it joins the queue of existing tasks. Hence when scan-times are too short, the queue o

he driver) whenever the scan-interval expires. Once a scan task has been created it is given to the driver, where it joins the queue of existing tasks. Hence when scan-times are too short, the queue of existing scan-tasks to performed by the driver increases, which cause configuration-tasks, such as the adding or removal of scan-points or the starting/stopping of the devices, to arrive at the back of this same queue. If the scan-intervals are configured to be longer, then the queue of scan-tasks is reduced, so that the configuration-tasks can be dealt with sooner. Note: The length of the task queue also affects control actions or writes, to the device, which are usually not prioritised to the front of the queue. By slowing the scanning sufficiently, pauses can be created in which nothing is happening, which can be filled by a fast-scanning task. However there is a limit to the number of fast scanning tasks that can be accommodated i.e. if a large amount of fast scanning is required then more sluggish scanning is required too. Therefore, as scan tasks are added, the scanning intervals need to be constantly adjusted and increased to cater for the increased traffic. For details on gro

For details on grouping scanned data together with similar scanning intervals, see Scanning Optimization . Drivers interlock all communications on a communication resource (e.g. COM1) so that it is not possible for the driver to do 2 polls at the same time on a port, but is possible to do 2 polls at the same time on 2 different ports. Note: In this example RTU (Remote Terminal Unit) could also mean any other front-end device, such as a PLC. This means that the request to a RTU #1 has to complete before the request for data from RTU #2 starts. But if RTU #1 responds very slowly, the driver may timeout before this response has been given and so will query RTU #2 for a response but receive the response from RTU #1 instead. Hence the driver loses synchronization as a result of this confusing traffic. Although this problem can be prevented by making the scan-times longer, it would be better to make the timeouts longer to accommodate any late responses, since then no performance is lost when the RTU responds

Scanning Optimization Top Scanning Optimization The optimization of scanning the process of communicating a value (slot), typically to and/or from a front-end device (FED). typically involves grouping data correctly within front-end devices, so as to prevent fragmentation of the data that usually creates a bottleneck for communication performance. Usually I/Os acquired from the plant are not needed by the SCADA, but are intermingled with the SCADA I/O. Therefore, it is recommended to allocate separate memory space in the controller for SCADA tags and the internal I/O. Although determining how much memory to reserve is never easy, it is recommended to plan correctly in this area. Certain front-end devices, such as Siemens controllers, make this process easier by using addressable data blocks or files that can grow in size. By scanning tags, whose slots belong to the same data type, which has contiguous addresses in the front-end device, will ensure that this device will require the least number of transactions to communicate its tags. For details, see Contiguous Scanning . Note: The reason for this is that a separate Scan agent is generally created by this device's Device agent, for

t number of transactions to communicate its tags. For details, see Contiguous Scanning . Note: The reason for this is that a separate Scan agent is generally created by this device's Device agent, for a block of manageable contiguous addresses, the size of which is dependent upon the protocol being used to transfer this data to and from Adroit . When grouping data, ensure that the various data types are separated, such as Analogs and Digitals, examples of such groups are: Digital Inputs, Analog Inputs, Digital Outputs, Analog SPs etc. It is also recommended to further differentiate data with respect to their required scan rate. Typically Analog values for I/O, such as temperatures can be grouped together as these values generally change very slowly. Although, Digital data must always be scanned quite fast, it is possible to differentiate between feedback and event digitals that must be polled very fast and digitals that indicate situations that need not be acted on right away, such as a high level indicator that takes 15 minutes to overflow. Note: When scanning tags, remember that it is the data type of the SLOT that is being scanned that determines which group it should be scanned

a high level indicator that takes 15 minutes to overflow. Note: When scanning tags, remember that it is the data type of the SLOT that is being scanned that determines which group it should be scanned to and not its AGENT name. For details of optimizing the scanning for an Analog agent, see Analog Scanning Optimization Example . The following examples illustrates how various types of data types could be grouped: Note: Scan times of less than 1000 ms should only be used if the driver can poll fast enough. Using faster scan times may adversely affect communications error recovery and the sending of controls to the front-end device. A further tip to optimise scanning in Adroit: Save the WGP and then restart the Agent Server to potentially reduce the number of required Scan agents. Reason: It is only when saving the Adroit agent database (.WGP) file that the Adroit scanning sub-system sorts the scan list into the optimal order, but this .WGP file is only read again when the Agent Server is restarted. Example: After successively importing and deleting scanned items a system required 69 Scan agents. By simply saving the WGP file and restarting the Agent Server, without doing anything els

restarted. Example: After successively importing and deleting scanned items a system required 69 Scan agents. By simply saving the WGP file and restarting the Agent Server, without doing anything else, Adroit only required 30 Scan agents! -->

Scanning Overview Top Scanning Overview Scanning in Adroit refers to the sending of or the communication of values between Adroit tags (agent.slot) and the front-end devices in the field, such as a PLC a Programmable Logic Controller or programmable controller is a digital computer used for the automation of industrial processes. , RTU an Remote Terminal Unit is a device installed at a remote location that collects data and transmits this data back to a central station, or master. etc. Since each front-end device can use a different protocol a set of rules or conventions governing the exchange of information between a computer and a front-end device. or language for communication, Adroit has developed a driver a DLL that interfaces Adroit to front end devices, these are the only Adroit components that are device specific. for each of these different protocols, which allow Adroit to communicate to these front-end devices by adding and configuring a for each. For further details, see Understanding Protocols and Protocol Drivers . Once installed, a protocol driver provides the protocol or language to communicate to front-end devices that use this protocol. However, it is necessary to

erstanding Protocols and Protocol Drivers . Once installed, a protocol driver provides the protocol or language to communicate to front-end devices that use this protocol. However, it is necessary to add a device added to an installed protocol driver to communicate using this protocol to a specific front-end device - in other words a logical connection to this FED. for each front-end device through which the communication actually occurs. Each device is essentially a logical connection to the front-end device that it is communicating to. For further details, see About Protocol Drivers . NASA, stands for New Adroit Scanning Architecture and describes a sub-class of protocol drivers that are specifically written to take advantage of the scanning improvements and enhancements provided by NASA, such as demand scanning and highly optimised scan tasks. For more details, see Demand Scanning . In other words, while the installed protocol driver is the language that needs to be communicated, the devices are the actual translators that use this language to communicate between the front-end devices and Adroit . As any translator needs to be able to communicate to and speak the language of eac

e devices are the actual translators that use this language to communicate between the front-end devices and Adroit . As any translator needs to be able to communicate to and speak the language of each party in order to correctly translate, the device needs to be configured in the following TWO locations, to ensure this: Front-end device communication , this is performed by the ‘device’ that is added to the required installed protocol driver in the Adroit Configuration Setup utility. For details, see Adding Devices . This ‘device’ is then configured to communicate to the required front-end device, according to the protocol-specific requirements laid out in the documentation installed with this Adroit protocol driver. For details, on displaying this documentation, see Display Protocol Driver Documentation . Adroit communication , this is performed using an associated Device agent, which is ONLY added to the Agent Server, when a ‘device’ (see step 1) is selected to communicate or scan a value within Adroit . For details, see Device agents . This Device agent configures the communication settings of the required values (agent.slot), through the use of Scan agents which it dynamically

value within Adroit . For details, see Device agents . This Device agent configures the communication settings of the required values (agent.slot), through the use of Scan agents which it dynamically creates, configures and deletes, as needed. Scanning Overview Top Scanning Overview Scanning in Adroit refers to the sending of or the communication of values between Adroit tags (agent.slot) and the front-end devices in the field, such as a PLC a Programmable Logic Controller or programmable controller is a digital computer used for the automation of industrial processes. , RTU an Remote Terminal Unit is a device installed at a remote location that collects data and transmits this data back to a central station, or master. etc. Since each front-end device can use a different protocol a set of rules or conventions governing the exchange of information between a computer and a front-end device. or language for communication, Adroit has developed a driver a DLL that interfaces Adroit to front end devices, these are the only Adroit components that are device specific. for each of these different protocols, which allow Adroit to communicate to these front-end devices by adding and configuring a for each. For further details, see Understanding Protocols and Protocol Drivers . Once installed, a protocol driver provides the protocol or language to communicate to front-end devices that use this protocol. However, it is necessary to

Scanning Tags Using Contiguous Addresses Top Scanning Tags Using Contiguous Addresses This method of scanning or communicating values is only effective when more than one agent of the same agent type need the same slot to be communicated by the same device using contiguous scan addresses. For instance, if you need to scan the rawvalue slot of more than one Analog agent to the same device, using the same scanning configuration settings. To scan a number of tags to continuous addresses in the same device: Create the required scanning template, by simply scanning the first tag, as normal to the first address of the required contiguous range of addresses. For details, see How to scan a tag . This will specify the following: the agent type, the slot, the Device, the starting address and if necessary the Scan rate and/or Deadband. If necessary, it is also possible to specify if the output enable and/or scan inhibit bits need to be set.
