Note: The Connector used by the Adroit DB Generator utility to connect to the required source (3 rd party application) determines whether templates can be used or not. Usage Example: You can create a scanning template per front end device that provides the default communication parameters required for this specific device. Each time an agent is scanned to this device then these default settings can be used to save your users engineering time. Default templates: The _ScanningDefault template is added for you, providing the Adroit default settings, which you can customise accordingly. Each scanning template allows you to provide default settings for one or more of the following scanning parameters: The slot (value) to be scanned: if this slot is provided by the agent that you want to scan, will be selected by default. The Adroit default for this is the rawVa

of the following scanning parameters: The slot (value) to be scanned: if this slot is provided by the agent that you want to scan, will be selected by default. The Adroit default for this is the rawValue slot. The rate at which the value should be scanned, in milliseconds. This is the amount of time that will elapse before this value is communicated to or from this Device. The Adroit default for this is 1 second (1000 milliseconds) The applicable scanning deadband value, which can prevent unnecessary communication, as any CHANGE in value LESS than this deadband limit will NOT be communicated. In Adroit this is not specified, by default (0). The scan inhibit status, if set this will prevent the scanned value from being changed by the Device ( FED front-end device, which is a device that is accessed directly by the user, such as a PLC or RTU. ). The Adroit default for this is OFF (0). The output enabled status, if set this will allow the scanned value to be written to the Device to change the value in the FED. Scanning Troubleshooting FAQ Top Scanning Troubleshooting FAQ This topics provides answers to commonly experienced problems/issues associated with scanning: Q: When the Agent Server is started, 3 beeps are heard and the Agent Server disappears. Why does this happen? A: The 3 beeps are produced when a driver is NOT loaded by the Agent Server, which can occur because of the following reasons: the driver has not been configured and therefore cannot load properly the port is already in use or does not exist some other resource has run out. Look for the devices in the Adroit Setup drivers tab, and check the amount of free disk space. Make sure you do not have a folder in your installation directory with the same name as the device. Q: When writing to a register, the value does not change, why? A: This can be due to writing to an input; a driver automatically disallows writing values to inputs, since they are most likely not supported in that protocol. In the Modbus driver, for instance you cannot write to digital input 1XXXXX registers, nor to the analog input 3XXXX registers. A driver in most cases does not generate an error/alarm, but simply fails the transaction. This is noticeable b

cannot write to digital input 1XXXXX registers, nor to the analog input 3XXXX registers. A driver in most cases does not generate an error/alarm, but simply fails the transaction. This is noticeable by the tag greying out in the mimic, and then becoming healthy on the next scan. Note: Whenever you perform a write using any polled (not telemetry) driver, Adroit automatically queues that item/task for reading afterwards Q: The driver software does not run, and I do not get any messages explaining what is wrong. Where do I look now? A: The first place to look in event of an error is the Windows event log. Look at the last few entries in the Application and System event logs for more details on a problem. Often a problem is the result of an error reported a little further back in the log. Q: An error message appears about a buffer overrun in the protocol driver monitor just before the comms dies. What does this mean? A: Buffer overruns and underruns are caused when the buffer on the serial card overflows. This is because character reception and transmission relies on the CPU emptying the buffer as the computer receives characters in the line. If the computer is busy with some other tas

card overflows. This is because character reception and transmission relies on the CPU emptying the buffer as the computer receives characters in the line. If the computer is busy with some other task (which happens all the time in windows), the buffer is not serviced often enough. The solution is to use a card with a buffered UART (FIFO buffer). This provides a 16-byte buffer as opposed to the 1-byte buffer common in older cards. Q: I have a serial card with a Buffered UART of FIFO but I still get overruns, why? A: The serial card driver for Windows may not have detected the FIFO. Use the Ports applet in Control Panel to enable the use of the FIFO. Delete the affected ports, and re-boot. The operating system will auto-detect the FIFO on the port and add it in. If it is not added in, you may edit the port settings and go to the advanced dialog which allows changing IRQ’s etc. Check the box at the bottom of the dialog, in order to enable the FIFO. Q: I get error messages such as parity error or framing error in the driver monitor window, followed by communications failure. A: In this case, characters on the line are being corrupted or badly sent. To correct the problem, lower the b

error or framing error in the driver monitor window, followed by communications failure. A: In this case, characters on the line are being corrupted or badly sent. To correct the problem, lower the baud-rate on both devices. Q: The (any serial) driver is not running. When I run the Agent Server, the message "Error load completion agent [BOILER1]." appears. Although no driver or hardware configuration was changed, there is no longer any communication. A: Make sure the mouse is plugged into the correct port. If the mouse is on the port the driver would use, the mouse will work but the Adroit driver will not. To correct this problem, either swap the mouse back and re-boot, or re-configure the driver to use the free port, and re-start Adroit . Q: Why does scanning not work for certain Analog agents? A: Please ensure that you scan the raw value slot and NOT the Engineering value as this can cause scanning to fail because the scanned value is out of range. Q: When I access a device agent, all I receive are event log entries about the failed device and the need to restart the Agent Server. A: This indicates that a device has not been attached at startup and as a result, its scanning conf

ll I receive are event log entries about the failed device and the need to restart the Agent Server. A: This indicates that a device has not been attached at startup and as a result, its scanning configuration is not loaded. This occurs for intermittent Windows/PC resource/device unavailability/conflict at the time of Agent Server startup. The Agent Server needs to be restarted to gain access to these resources or to sort out a resource conflict; for example, your RAS connection (or other software) is still active which is using the same COM port as your device configuration. Q: When I install a protocol driver, it is copied without errors but does not appear in the "Available protocol drivers" list. A: A number of our Adroit drivers rely on 3rd party components being installed, if they are not, then you get the above symptoms. This is because the driver available list in setup uses the driver, which also uses the missing 3rd party component. Examples are: Allen Bradley RSLINX, Eagle, Lonworks, Modbus plus (+), Siemens H1, Siemens L2 and Siemens S7 Functions among others. In such cases, the required hardware and accompanying software must be installed (preferably before the driver)

Lonworks, Modbus plus (+), Siemens H1, Siemens L2 and Siemens S7 Functions among others. In such cases, the required hardware and accompanying software must be installed (preferably before the driver). Note: Many network (Ethernet, H1 and TCP/IP) drivers also require the installation of the Windows TCP/IP protocol. If in doubt, open the relevant driver documentation file found in your Adroit system folder for more information. Q: Communication to the PLC is lost intermittently. A: This is a possible driver device failure. Reinstall or update with a new driver. -->

A: The serial card driver for Windows may not have detected the FIFO. Use the Ports applet in Control Panel to enable the use of the FIFO. Delete the affected ports, and re-boot. The operating system will auto-detect the FIFO on the port and add it in. If it is not added in, you may edit the port settings and go to the advanced dialog which allows changing IRQ’s etc. Check the box at the bottom of the dialog, in order to enable the FIFO. Q: I get error messages such as parity error or framing error in the driver monitor window, followed by communications failure. A: In this case, characters on the line are being corrupted or badly sent. To correct the problem, lower the b

error or framing error in the driver monitor window, followed by communications failure. A: In this case, characters on the line are being corrupted or badly sent. To correct the problem, lower the baud-rate on both devices. Q: The (any serial) driver is not running. When I run the Agent Server, the message "Error load completion agent [BOILER1]." appears. Although no driver or hardware configuration was changed, there is no longer any communication. A: Make sure the mouse is plugged into the correct port. If the mouse is on the port the driver would use, the mouse will work but the Adroit driver will not. To correct this problem, either swap the mouse back and re-boot, or re-configure the driver to use the free port, and re-start Adroit . Q: Why does scanning not work for certain Analog agents? A: Please ensure that you scan the raw value slot and NOT the Engineering value as this can cause scanning to fail because the scanned value is out of range. Q: When I access a device agent, all I receive are event log entries about the failed device and the need to restart the Agent Server. A: This indicates that a device has not been attached at startup and as a result, its scanning conf

ll I receive are event log entries about the failed device and the need to restart the Agent Server. A: This indicates that a device has not been attached at startup and as a result, its scanning configuration is not loaded. This occurs for intermittent Windows/PC resource/device unavailability/conflict at the time of Agent Server startup. The Agent Server needs to be restarted to gain access to these resources or to sort out a resource conflict; for example, your RAS connection (or other software) is still active which is using the same COM port as your device configuration. Q: When I install a protocol driver, it is copied without errors but does not appear in the "Available protocol drivers" list. A: A number of our Adroit drivers rely on 3rd party components being installed, if they are not, then you get the above symptoms. This is because the driver available list in setup uses the driver, which also uses the missing 3rd party component. Examples are: Allen Bradley RSLINX, Eagle, Lonworks, Modbus plus (+), Siemens H1, Siemens L2 and Siemens S7 Functions among others. Scheduling and Triggering Scripts Top Scheduling and Triggering Scripts This enables the remote execution of the main subroutine by the Script agent. The following combinations of triggering and scheduling can be configured: Triggering only: This is used when the execution of the script is only required after a particular condition, defined within the script, has been met by one or more of the tags within Adroit . This requires checking Run when one of the following tags change and then configuring one or more triggers . Scheduling only: This is used when the execution of the script is required at a set time period, which is set by the user. It is also possible to synchronise the start of the scheduling at a specified time. This requires the configuring the scheduling . Ensure that both the, only if one of the following tags change and Run when one of the following tags change options, are unchecked. Triggering and Scheduling: In this case the script is executed when its scheduled to and when a value of the one of the triggers change. This requires configuring one or more triggers and configuring the scheduling . Only the, Run when one of the following tags change option, should be

nd when a value of the one of the triggers change. This requires configuring one or more triggers and configuring the scheduling . Only the, Run when one of the following tags change option, should be checked. Scheduling if Triggered: In this case the script is only executed when it is scheduled to, if a value of the one of the triggers also change. This effectively applies a time deadband to the triggering, preventing a flood of triggers that would initiate multiple executions. This requires configuring one or more triggers and configuring the scheduling . Only the, only if one of the following tags change option, should be checked. Note: An event is logged if a script is executed that contains compilation errors, preventing it from being run. However, this event could result in the event log from being flooded, therefore ensure that the event log is closely monitored and that any buggy scripts are either fixed or disabled ASAP! -->

Scheduling Commands and Utilities Top Scheduling Commands and Utilities Commands and utilities can be scheduled to run today, tomorrow, or on a particular day of the week or month at a specified time using the Scheduler. Typical examples of its use would be executing a batch file, starting a backup procedure, printing a report, archiving a file, extracting logged data or doing a putslot operation. The Scheduler utility also provides dialog boxes to assist in specifying the required details for the Adroit putslot , extract (datalogs) and merge (datalogs) operations. For details, see Specifying the Scheduled Command or Utility . Tip: This utility provides extensive use of tooltips to provide context sensitive help. If unsure about the function of a checkbox or list box hold the mouse pointer over it until the tooltip is displayed. To schedule a command or utility: Launch the Scheduler . Specify the command or utility that should be scheduled . Specify when this command or utility should be executed . Add these specified details to the list of scheduled entries (this also describes how to manage this list of scheduled entries). Write the details of this scheduled command or utility to

be executed . Add these specified details to the list of scheduled entries (this also describes how to manage this list of scheduled entries). Write the details of this scheduled command or utility to the registry . Note: Since this information is written to the registry, it is not necessary for the Scheduler to remain running in order to schedule the specified entries. -->

Scheduling script objects Top Scheduling script objects When a script is required to perform routine services that are required at specific time periods, you can schedule these server scripts to automatically be triggered at the correct times. Tip: The connection name is prefixed by the SmartUI Server computer name. If necessary, expand the Datasources category. Click the plus box to the left of the Server Scripts datasource or its icon . Tip: It is also possible to display the script objects by double-clicking on this name or icon. Right-click the required name of the script object or its icon and select Script Scheduling . The Schedule Script configuration dialog is launched Specify the required Schedule Type from this list, as follows: Interval: the default option, to trigger this script every ## seconds, as specified by the Trigger the script every spin control. The default value of 0 does NOT trigger the script IMPORTANT: In order to use the Interval Schedule Type, you must specify an interval that is >= the Minimu

the Trigger the script every spin control. The default value of 0 does NOT trigger the script IMPORTANT: In order to use the Interval Schedule Type, you must specify an interval that is >= the MinimumScriptSchedulingTime setting in the Server and Service .CONFIG file [in the DatasourceSettings group]. One Time: to Trigger the script at the following Date and Time , which you specify as follows: select the required date and/or time unit and either type in the required unit or use the spin control's arrows to select this. Daily: to Trigger the script Daily at the following time , which you specify as follows: select the required time unit and either type in the required unit or use the spin control's arrows to select this. Weekly: to Trigger the script Weekly, synchronised at the following Date and Time , which you specify as follows: select the required date and/or time unit and either type in the required unit or use the spin control's arrows to select this. ript Monthly, synchronised at the following Date and Time , which you specify as follows: select the required date and/or time unit and either type in the required unit or use the spin control's arrows to select this. If you need this script to be performed as soon as the Server starts up, then check the Trigger on startup checkbox. Specify the user account ( User Name and Password ) that this script should be run under, in the Run the script under the following user section. Script Procedures Top Script Procedures When a Has script engine Custom agent is derived the following empty procedures are created, which can either be left empty– to not provide a script engine or they can be coded to provide any additional functionality for this agent: OnCompiled() Code that is executed every time the Agent Server detects a change in the script code. This procedure can be used to initialise any global variables. OnLoadComplete() Code that is executed once an agent has been loaded from the WGP file. This procedure can contain code to initialise slot values. OnChange(slotid, value) Code that is executed every time a slot value is changed. This procedure should contain code that requires execution depending on the slot and value thereof being changed, e.g. setting status bit slots. OnUpdate(slotid, value) Code that is executed every time a Tagname type slot receives a subscription update. This procedure should contain code that requires execution depending on the subscription received. OnBackground() Code that is executed every second in the background. This procedure should contain time-dependant and/or simulation code. -->

Secondary Port Enabled Top Secondary Port Enabled Adroit drivers can make use of a secondary port to cater for the possible failure of some communications hardware component. For this to be effective, the hardware used by the secondary port should be totally separate (e.g. extra serial card and cable). A device goes into recovery whenever a Read or Write transaction fails. This failure is a 3-step process: Adroit requests an update from the front-end device. Timeout Phase : the request is sent to the front end device, and times out or gives an invalid response. Retry Phase: Step 2 is repeated for the number of retries configured. If the retries are exhausted and there is still no valid response, the Adroit driver will use the secondary port if it is configured when this step is reached. This involves a port switchover, and only occurs once in any transaction. The driver then runs through Steps 2 and 3 using the secondary port. If, at some later time, the secondary port should fail, communications will switch back to the primary port, and will continue through the primary hardware if this has been repaired. After which scanning resumes immediately. However, there is also an Alternat

munications will switch back to the primary port, and will continue through the primary hardware if this has been repaired. After which scanning resumes immediately. However, there is also an Alternate Secondary Port Enabled scenario where the same PC port / resource is used but with different PLC ports / resources. -->

Timeout Phase : the request is sent to the front end device, and times out or gives an invalid response. Retry Phase: Step 2 is repeated for the number of retries configured. If the retries are exhausted and there is still no valid response, the Adroit driver will use the secondary port if it is configured when this step is reached. This involves a port switchover, and only occurs once in any transaction. The driver then runs through Steps 2 and 3 using the secondary port. If, at some later time, the secondary port should fail, communications will switch back to the primary port, and will continue through the primary hardware if this has been repaired. After which scanning resumes immediately. However, there is also an Alternat

munications will switch back to the primary port, and will continue through the primary hardware if this has been repaired. After which scanning resumes immediately. However, there is also an Alternate Secondary Port Enabled scenario where the same PC port / resource is used but with different PLC ports / resources. -->

Depending upon the sensitivity of this data and/or the exposed functionality, you may need to control the access to these items. Both the datasource itself and its data can be secured using the data element security. For details, see Working with data element security . This allows one to specify which user(s) and/or group(s) are allowed to view, configure and remove these items and/or who is able to configure their security settings. For details on how to control the access to the datasource and its data elements, see Assigning security permissions to data elements . Security configuration Top Security configuration The SmartUI security system is user-centric and operates on top of the traditional Windows operating system security. This is made possible by using a configurable sub-set of the existing users and groups on each Server computer, known as the "allowed" users and groups, which provide the first or foundational level of ALL security and user management within the SmartUI ; hence their creation is mandatory for every Server. For further details on configuring roaming profiles to manage user management, see Working with profiles . Note: On each Server, it is also possible to give specific users and groups total or global security access to the Server and it is recommended to use these group(s) and/or user(s) to administer its security. For details, see Assigning global security to groups and users or Configuring SmartUI Server security . Tip: As a further security precaution, it is possible to prevent users from using a domain user name and password, by configuring impersonated user names and passwords, which do not natively exist on the domain itself. In other words, unless a user is either an allowed user or a member of an allowed gro

password, by configuring impersonated user names and passwords, which do not natively exist on the domain itself. In other words, unless a user is either an allowed user or a member of an allowed group he/she will be unable to login to the Server and use the SmartUI . For this reason, the necessary user accounts and/or groups need to be created within Windows first. For details, see Working with user accounts and groups . Tip: To save time when launching a Client, it is possible to specify automatic login settings that will be used whenever the Client is launched. For details, see Automatically logging into SmartUI Servers . -->

In the Choose a Sampling Method dialog, select the required data collection method, as follows: Note1: The selected data collection method applies to all the subsequently added values. Selecting colors Selecting colors A color edit box is used to configure a color, which displays the currently selected color in a color box on the left and on the right of the definition of this color. This color definition is either a color name or a custom color represented by at least three comma-separated numbers from 0 to 255, which indicate the proportions of the red, green and blue primary colors respectively. Note: If the color edit box currently displays a known color name, then double-clicking on it will display the next known color name in alphabetical order. To select a color from a location on the screen: this allows you to directly obtain the color from any location on the screen. Right click the list box to the right of the required color edit box (square). Hold down the right mouse button, so that the cursor changes to . Drag the mouse to the required location on the screen that has the color that you want Release the right mouse button to select this color. This will display a drop-down list button at the f

Click the required tab and select the required color. The color-selection dialog consists of the following three tabs: System: This displays the colors specified by the Advanced Appearance settings of your system. To change your Advanced Appearance color settings: Open the Desktop. Right-click and select Properties The Display Properties dialog is displayed. Click the Appearance tab. Click the Advanced button. The Advanced Appearance dialog is displayed. Either click in the sample window or use the Item list box to select elements and change their colors. Note: If you change your Advanced Appearance settings, the colors displayed in this System tab will change accordingly. Web: This displays colors commonly used when designing web applications. Click on this drop-down list button, to display the color-selection dialog. Click the Custom tab. Selecting General SNMP Objects Selecting General SNMP Objects The General tab of this SNMP Objects Browser contains a collection of commonly used statistics for device management. Note: You CANNOT write to the items you select from this General tab. To select an item from the General tab: Ensure that the General tab of the SNMP Objects Browser dialog is selected. Check the checkbox next to the required item. This immediately adds this item to the OID list of this SNMPManager agent, which is differentiated from browsed objects (those selected from the Browse tab), as follows: their OID field is simply "General Object", their Name field is prefaced by [G#], where # typically specifies the order of this object in this General tab. The statistics provided by this tab are divided into the following two groups: General objects for computers only: SNMP managed objects that are computer-specific and can only be used when monitoring computers. In this case a number of specific usage requirements need to be met first. For details, see Usage Requirements . The statistics provided by this group is further classified into the following sub-groups: Incoming network traffic: these statistics are

s need to be met first. For details, see Usage Requirements . The statistics provided by this group is further classified into the following sub-groups: Incoming network traffic: these statistics are generally used to determine the status of the network received by the specified computer. Note: These calculated statistics ONLY use the SNMP objects that refer to the FIRST network card on the monitored computer, so if there are more than one network cards these statistics will not present the full picture. Bandwidth (kbit per second): This statistic measures the currently utilised networking bandwidth that is being received by the computer, in kilobits per second. Note: If the monitored computer has more than one network card, it may be necessary to perform this bandwidth calculation manually for the other network cards. For details, see Manual Network Bandwidth Calculation . Unicast packets per second: This statistic measures the number of packets received by the computer per second, which are ONLY intended for this computer. Note: Unicast packets are packets that ONLY have a SINGLE device as their destination Non-unicast packets per second: This statistic measures the number of bro

ich are ONLY intended for this computer. Note: Unicast packets are packets that ONLY have a SINGLE device as their destination Non-unicast packets per second: This statistic measures the number of broadcast packets received by the computer per second. Note: Non-unicast packets are broadcast packets meant for all devices or a group of devices on a network. Errors per minute: This statistic measures the number of packet errors received by the computer per minute. Outgoing network traffic: these statistics are generally used to determine the status of the network away from the specified computer. Note: These calculated statistics ONLY use the SNMP objects that refer to the FIRST network card on the monitored computer, so if there are more than one network cards these statistics will not present the full picture. Bandwidth (kbit per second): This statistic measures the currently utilised networking bandwidth, which is being sent out of the computer, in kilobits per second. Note: If the monitored computer has more than one network card, it may be necessary to perform this bandwidth calculation manually for the other network cards. For details, see Manual Network Bandwidth Calculation .

itored computer has more than one network card, it may be necessary to perform this bandwidth calculation manually for the other network cards. For details, see Manual Network Bandwidth Calculation . Unicast packets per second: This statistic measures the number of unicast packets sent out of the computer per second. Note: Unicast packets are packets that ONLY have a SINGLE device as their destination. Non-unicast packets per second: This statistic measures the number of broadcast packets sent out of the computer per second. Note: Non-unicast packets are broadcast packets meant for all devices or a group of devices on a network. Errors per minute: This statistic measures the number of packet errors sent out of the computer per minute. System information: these are generally applicable computer management statistics. System available memory: This statistic measures the available RAM, on the computer being monitored, in Megabytes. For instance, this can determine whether this computer is under-performing or in other words is currently over-utilising its resources or not. Available hard drive space (C:\): This statistic measures the available hard drive space on the <C:\> drive, on th

under-performing or in other words is currently over-utilising its resources or not. Available hard drive space (C:\): This statistic measures the available hard drive space on the <C:\> drive, on the computer being monitored, in Megabytes. Since the majority of Adroit -related information is stored on the <C:\> drive, this statistic can be used to determine when a computer is running out of storage space. Adroit processes: these are commonly used Adroit applications that may be running on the specified computer. Agent Server (as.exe): This Boolean value can be used to determine the current status of the Agent Server process on the device being monitored. For instance, when used to monitor a computer that is designated to run the Agent Server, this value can be used to trigger an alarm when the Agent Server is shut down. Classic User Interface (adroit.exe): This Boolean value can be used to determine the current status of the Classic User Interface process on the device being monitored. For instance, when used to monitor a computer that is designated to run the Classic User Interface, this value could also trigger an alarm when this is shut down. General objects for most devices:

d. For instance, when used to monitor a computer that is designated to run the Classic User Interface, this value could also trigger an alarm when this is shut down. General objects for most devices: SNMP managed objects that are generally provided by all devices. Host name: This statistic displays the textual (network) name of the device being monitored. Host description: This statistic displays the textual system description of the device being monitored, which includes the processor type and operating system employed on this device. System uptime: This statistic measures the time (in hundredths of a second) since the network management portion of the device was last re-initialized, in other words, since its SNMP service has been restarted. While some of these items are individual OIDs, others are calculations using the values of one or more OIDs. It is also possible to perform these calculations yourself within Adroit . Selecting SNMP Objects Selecting SNMP Objects The SNMPManager agent is able to get and/or set SNMP managed objects (each of which is an OID) from a single device on the network. The SNMP Objects Browser can specify the required OIDs. Click for more details: Note1: You need to connect to the device to use this SNMP Objects Browser . Note2: You need to Enable polling before you can use this SNMP Objects Browser . Note3: If you cannot connect to the device then you can add OIDs manually. For details, see Adding OIDs Manually . Note4: Not all devices allow you to browse their OIDs. Launch the SNMP Objects Browser: click the Browse OID to add button in the Edit SNMP Manager Agent dialog. Note: A message box is displayed if the agent cannot connect to the device, indicating that the connection is invalid. The SNMP Objects Browser contains 2 tabs, each of which provide a different view of the values contained within this device, as follows: General: This tab provides a collection of commonly used statistics for device management. Although some of these items are individual OIDs, others are calculations using the values of one or more OIDs. For more details, see Selecting General SNMP Obje

used statistics for device management. Although some of these items are individual OIDs, others are calculations using the values of one or more OIDs. For more details, see Selecting General SNMP Objects . Note: You CANNOT write to items you select from the General tab. Browser: This tab can browse for device-specific OIDs from the device's MIB hierarchy. For more details, see Selecting Browsed SNMP Objects . Note: You can read/write to OID values that you select from the Browser tab. -->

Server clustering Top SmartUI Server clustering How to cluster SmartUI Servers SmartUI Servers can be clustered to provide both load balancing and redundancy. Any number of SmartUI Servers can belong to the same cluster, in which case, they are known as cluster partners. Essentially, all cluster partners ( SmartUI Servers within a cluster), act as if they were a single Server, which means that certain characteristics of ALL the cluster partners in a cluster must be IDENTICALLY configured, as follows: Server name: this also becomes the name of the cluster to which these cluster partners belong, for instance, all the SmartUI Servers whose Server Name is "MyCluster", belong to the "MyCluster" group of cluster partners. For details on configuring this setting, see General SmartUI Server settings . Server configuration: this configuration encompasses the profiles, security, projects and all datasources that have been configured. For details on configuring the locations for these items, see SmartUI Server directory settings . Tip: It is recommended that you specify a shared network folder on RAID (failsafe disk) in which you provide the license and configuration files for all the cluster

SmartUI Server directory settings . Tip: It is recommended that you specify a shared network folder on RAID (failsafe disk) in which you provide the license and configuration files for all the cluster partners to refer to. Alternatively, these locations can be identically configured on each cluster partner, so that the required configuration is performed on one cluster partner and then copied to the other cluster partners. System time: cluster partners need to be time synchronised, so that the same timestamp will be set regardless of which cluster partner performs the operation. Tip: Use time synchronizing software to do this, such as the NET TIME command, provided by the Windows operating system, which sets the time of the local computer to that of a specified remote computer. Example of use: The following example will set the time of the local computer to that of Computer1 (providing that it is in the same domain): NET TIME \\Computer1 /SET /Y The /Y option allows this command to be performed automatically without needing to be confirmed first, so that this command can then be added to a command (.CMD) file that could be run on startup or as often as needed. Microsoft Windows sec

performed automatically without needing to be confirmed first, so that this command can then be added to a command (.CMD) file that could be run on startup or as often as needed. Microsoft Windows security configuration: this means that any user who logs in to a specific clustered SmartUI Server, must be able to log in to all the other cluster partners, using the same user name and password. Network location of users and groups: this means that all the cluster partners must be either be physically located in the same network domain or else must be members of a Workgroup that has the same security configuration on each of the cluster partners. This allows the same users and groups to secure these SmartUI Servers. For details of configuring this settings, see Server security settings . IMPORTANT: For clustering to work correctly, only one Server can run on a specific machine at any point in time. Currently cluster partners ONLY share the workload (load) generated by their SmartUI Operator clients that are cluster-aware, in which case they handle their combined load evenly and to provide continued operation in the event that one or more fail. Each SmartUI Server uses UDP broadcasts to

r clients that are cluster-aware, in which case they handle their combined load evenly and to provide continued operation in the event that one or more fail. Each SmartUI Server uses UDP broadcasts to inform each SmartUI Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. of its availability and/or load. The load of each SmartUI Server is determined by the number of SmartUI Clients that are currently connected to it. This broadcast system can be disabled and both the range of UDP ports used for this broadcast and the frequency of broadcasts can be configured, as follows: The BroadcastEnabled SmartUI Server setting enables (the default setting) or disables these UDP broadcasts. The BroadcastTimePeriod SmartUI Server setting specifies the time, in milliseconds, between broadcasts, which is 2 seconds (2000 milliseconds) by default. Although decreasing this setting reduces the network traffic it also prevents the SmartUI Operators from quickly responding to changes in Server load and/or availability. The BroadcastPortRange SmartUI Server setting specifies the UDP port range which the Server uses for its broadcasts, by default this

quickly responding to changes in Server load and/or availability. The BroadcastPortRange SmartUI Server setting specifies the UDP port range which the Server uses for its broadcasts, by default this is 11000-11010. IMPORTANT: If you CHANGE this setting for a SmartUI Server then you need to change the BroadcastPortRange setting of each SmartUI Client that you want to receive these broadcasts from this Server. Each cluster aware SmartUI Operator maintains a list of SmartUI Servers for ALL the clusters that it connects to. The list is periodically updated by the SmartUI Operator, which obtains the availability and load of these Servers from their broadcasts. Cluster aware SmartUI Operators automatically switch over to the SmartUI Server with the lightest load. Upon login, if the default SmartUI Server (cluster partner) is NOT available then a cluster aware Operator will search for an available cluster partner. For details on how to make an SmartUI Operator aware of one or more clusters, see Making SmartUI Operators cluster-aware . -->

For details, see Specifying Permitted Commands or Additional SET Command Restrictions . One of the additional restrictions is to force the Command agent to only perform SET commands that use pseudonyms or macros to control or limit which tags can have their values modified i.e. tags can no longer be typed in by the user issuing the SET command. In this way it is possible to limit the possible misuse, malicious and otherwise that could be achieved. For details of the various usage formats of this command, see SET Commands . Note: In addition to being a further security precaution, this also simplifies the process of setting process values. To further restrict the usage of SET commands: If necessary, add a Command agent. Note1: This command must be enabled by the Command agent , which it is sent to, before it can be performed, because it can create a serious security and operational risk through the remote modification of process and control values. For details, see Specifying Permitted Commands . Note2: Due to the seriousness of the potential security and operational risk, additional settings are provided to further restrict the usage of this command. For details, see Additional SET Command Restrictions . Note3: Both the command and its parameters are NOT case-sensitive; commands have only been capitalised for ease of reference. The decision of which of the following command formats to use, is usually a tradeoff between the prior configuration in the Command agent and the required amount of typing, when specifying the SMS command itself: Note1: Both the command and its parameters are NOT case-sensitive; commands have only been capitalised for ease of reference. Note2: When using this command, it is the responsibility of the user to specify a value of the correct slot type for the tag (a

se-sensitive; commands have only been capitalised for ease of reference. Note2: When using this command, it is the responsibility of the user to specify a value of the correct slot type for the tag (agent.slot) that is being modified. Basic command syntax: SET, tagName, value In this case, tagName is the name of the tag whose value is to be displayed and value is the required value for this tag. For instance: set,dig_01.value,1 This is the simplest format of this command, which requires the least prior configuration in the Command agent, it is able to modify the value of any tag, however it does require the most typing when specifying the command. Note: If the Only ‘Set’ by pseudonym setting has been enabled, then this command can ONLY be performed using pseudonyms or macros and NOT by typing in the name of required tag directly. For details, see SET Command Usage Restriction . Pseudonym usage: SET, pseudonym, value In this case, a pseudonym or alias needs to be created, beforehand, for the required tag (agent.slot) and value is the required value for this referenced tag. For instance, assuming that a pseudonym called ‘dig01v’ is created to represent ‘DIG_01.value’, this command ca

r the required tag (agent.slot) and value is the required value for this referenced tag. For instance, assuming that a pseudonym called ‘dig01v’ is created to represent ‘DIG_01.value’, this command can be specified as: set,dig01v,1 Although pseudonyms save on the typing when specifying the command, ONLY the tags that have defined pseudonyms for this Command agent can be used. For details on creating and using pseudonyms, see Creating Pseudonyms . Macro usage: macro In this case, a macro or alias needs to be created, beforehand, for the entire SET command. For instance, assuming that a macro called ‘Pump1ON’ is created to represent ‘set,dig_01.value,1’, then this command can simply be specified as: "Pump1ON". Although macros provide short yet intuitive command names, they require the most pre-configuration in this Command agent and are therefore most restrictive. Set Time Period Top Set Time Period The Set Time Period is a generic dialog box that is used to specify time ranges. Under Period Type , one or more of the following options may be available: Start + Interval displays a period from a fixed start time forward in time at a specified interval. End - Interval displays a period from a fixed end time backwards in time at a specified interval. Start to End displays a period from a fixed start time to a fixed end time with a specified interval, and can be used to filter out alarms. Current - Interval displays a real time period with the specified interval. Note: If used for a trend, Adroit will attempt to fetch historical trend data if it exists to fill in the trend window. Datum +/- Interval - displays a period from a fixed datum forwards or backwards in time at a specified interval. Datum - Interval - displays a period from a fixed datum backwards in time at a specified interval. Interval - for DataLog agent Length and Time configuration. Time - for EventOutput agent Time Printing setting. Under Period Details , one or more of the following options may be available: For the Start and End , Date and Time fields, click in the appropriate f

me - for EventOutput agent Time Printing setting. Under Period Details , one or more of the following options may be available: For the Start and End , Date and Time fields, click in the appropriate field, and select the required date and time digits. -->

Setting up the Adroit Agent Server Top Setting up the Agent Server When Adroit is installed, it creates default settings for your Adroit project, which it is recommended that you configure these settings for each of the Agent Servers required by your SmartUI project. Typically one Agent Server is required per plant Area, but this is not always the case. On each computer that has the Adroit Agent Server installed: Using the Adroit Config Editor : Launch the Adroit Config Editor . Click Agent Server Configuration in the right hand pane. Click Agent Server Configuration again in the right hand pane. Configure the Agent Server Parameters Agent Server Type: Usually the default selection of Stand-alone/Distributed Server is required for a typical installation; but this also provides the following options: Cluster Aware Server: This is required when you need stand-alone Agent Servers to operate with an Adroit Active Cluster pair (a set of hot-standby Agent Servers) in a distributed project. Since you are otherwise unable to have multiple Agent Servers with the same name in a Project. Shift Agent - Slot Details Top Shift Agent - Slot Details The Shift agent determines the current shift number as defined by a configurable shift pattern, which can then be used by other agents. Instead of configuring the shift pattern information into each instance of these agents. This agent is located in the following file: T_SHIFT.DLL Slots: Slot Name Type Function catchupData RAWBYTES For internal use connection VARSTRING If specified, the shifts are added to the Adr_Grouping_Details table as the shifts occur in real time, which is used by Adroit SCADA Intelligence. Note: If you specify global , the Global OLE DB connection string of the Agent Server is used, which is specified in the Adroit Config Editor . Typically, you can launch this tool from the Desktop shortcut. Select the Agent Server Configuration Welcome menu item. Select the Advanced Agent Server Configuration option. At the bottom of the dialog, the Global OLE DB connection field is available for you to specify this connection string. data RAWBYTES Encoded data about the current shift for internal use by Adroit agents. day REAL The day value for the current shift – overnight shifts will have previous day’s number fr

nection string. data RAWBYTES Encoded data about the current shift for internal use by Adroit agents. day REAL The day value for the current shift – overnight shifts will have previous day’s number from midnight until end of shift info STRING Current shift information string in the format e.g. 2010/03/17 Shift 2, 08:00 hours from 10:00 to 18:00 number INTEGER The current shift number pattern LIST A list of time shift patterns where each entry contains the following parameters: SpecialDate – a string value in the format yyyy/mm/dd that denotes a specific unique date. Empty string denotes not used DayOfMonth – an integer value in the format mmdd that determines a special recurring holiday e.g. 1225 for 25 December. Value of 0 denotes not used DaysOfWeek – an integer bit mask representing Monday to Sunday Shift1StartTime … Shift6StartTime – a real value that denotes the hour of the day for the start of shift 1 … 6. shiftEndTime TIME Stores the ending time of the current shift. shiftStartTime TIME Stores the starting time of the current shift. Specific status bits: Note: These are of type BOOLEAN. Bit Number Name Function status bit 16 ShiftEnd Pulsed on at the end of every shift to al

ime TIME Stores the starting time of the current shift. Specific status bits: Note: These are of type BOOLEAN. Bit Number Name Function status bit 16 ShiftEnd Pulsed on at the end of every shift to allow interested parties to perform shift end operations. status bit 17 InvalidShift On when the shift pattern entry for the current time is not found. status bit 18 ConnectionError On when the OPTIONAL OLEDB connection string, if specified, is invalid. Methods of creation: Manual Agents created by default: None For a description of which of these slots are saved to the agent database file (.WGP), see: Shift Agent - Database File Format . -->

The TSAP format is 01.02.(Default is 03.03) The first byte(01) is the Service Number or also known as Connection Resource number. The number represents the following: 01 – STEP 7 Connection 02 – SCADA Connection to S7-200 03 – SCADA Connection to S7-300/400 The second byte(02) represents the CPU destination where the 0 is the rack number and the 2 is the slot number. Default values per PLC type will then most likely look like this: S7-200 – 02.00 – As S7-200 does not have RACK and CPU position it is thus 00. S7-300 – 03.02 – The PSU takes slot 1 and the CPU takes slot 2. S7-400 – 03.03 – The PSU takes slot 1 and 2 and the CPU slot 3. SIMPDRV - Adroit Simulation Protocol Driver Top SIMPDRV - Adroit Simulation Protocol Driver The Adroit simulation protocol is a software only emulation of a Siemens S5 PLC, and is provided solely for the purposes of testing and demonstration. This is particularly useful when a PLC and communications hardware is for some reason unavailable. It uses the Siemens S5 addressing scheme, which can be written to and read from. However, there is the limitation whereby only tags of the same type (Boolean, Integer, Real, String) can be mapped to the same address, otherwise the simulator will assign separate memory locations for each tag. Siemens S5 PLC data address types supported by the simulator are: For example, if you map a Digital tag to DB10:DW2.2, you may not assume that mapping an Analog tag to DB10:DW2 will actually map to the same simulated PLC address, even though the address points to the same place in the simulated PLC. Note: The Protocol Driver Monitor cannot be used on this driver. Groups of selected tags can be configured in one step, across Data Block boundaries. For example, if you scan DB4:255 the next address will now be DB5:0 and not remain at DB4:255. The default address

The default address is DB2:0. DB0 and DB1 are reserved for system use. Automatically Incrementing Scanned SIMPLC Values: To simulate a dynamic situation, the values in memory are automatically incremented, for every scan, by the DB number. Situational Awareness (or High Performance SCADA) Top Situational Awareness (or High Performance SCADA) This is a minimalistic standard of user interface design, which has come about through years of research and trial and error. This standard moves away from the brightly colored and the almost photo-realistic process design of the past which used bright colors that while at the outset were visually appealing, proved in practice to only distract the operators from the process they were monitoring. Therefore this situational awareness standard (also known as High Performance HMI) strives at all times to create user interface elements that only present the operator with the information they need to discern exactly what is going on in the process they are operating, for this reason: most of the colors are muted and bright colors are ONLY used to indicate issues that require IMMEDIATE attention. great use is made of trends as these are visually efficient in relaying the necessary information without the operator needing to scrutinise reams of values and then calculate themselves how these values related to their normal operating conditions. In other words this operator interface design

on without the operator needing to scrutinise reams of values and then calculate themselves how these values related to their normal operating conditions. In other words this operator interface design strives to minimise user fatigue and increase their response times, as follows: Clarity : uncluttered displays using simple, easy to understand graphics, where abnormal conditions are clear, prominent and consistently distinguishable and only the most important information is displayed. The process layout should correspond to how the operators envisage the process and not how managers like to view it. Typically use grey backgrounds to minimise glare and avoid the gratuitous use of animation, process lines and the outlines of the process equipment should be dark grey or black, so that emphasis is provided by differing line thicknesses and not color. Consistency : consistent and intuitive methods of navigation, data manipulation and graphics functions need to be employed, involving the minimum number of mouse clicks, typically no more than 3 clicks to get to any level of detail. Consistent visual and color coding of alarm indication and other events. For details, see Consistent alarm in

mum number of mouse clicks, typically no more than 3 clicks to get to any level of detail. Consistent visual and color coding of alarm indication and other events. For details, see Consistent alarm indication. Use a consistent hierarchical structure providing the progressive exposure of detailed information. Feedback : important actions should require confirmation, such as two levels of confirmation to change critical set points to minimise the possibility of mistakes. Consistent alarm indication : the applicable situation awareness wizards use the same numbers and colors and graphical symbols to indicate your alarms. Situational Awareness design elements : the available sub-categories of wizards that can be used to design your process control mimics. Guidelines to implement situational awareness : a recommended continual process to ensure the success of your redesign of your process control mimics. -->

Slot Status Words Top Slot Status Words In addition to an overall agent status word, which shows the status as determined by the status of the individual slot, there is also a status word for each slot of an agent. This is an advanced feature that can provide better monitoring and control of the agent. The bit allocations and meanings for the slot status words are exactly the same as they are for the overall agent status. For details, see Agent Status and Slot Status . Note: The first bit in the status word, statusBad , is the only bit an application needs to monitor to determine the integrity of an agent or slot. For details, see Agent or Slot Integrity Monitoring (Bad Handling) . These slot statuses may be accessed by appending the relevant status slotname after the agent and slot, e.g. ANA01.status.statusBit00. Note: These bits can be viewed and/or set via the Slot Status configuration dialog, by clicking the Advanced button in the Agent Header configuration dialog. -->

Slot Types Top Slot Types Slot types define the type of data that can be stored within a slot, which is an externally accessible attribute of an agent. For further details, see About Agent Data (Slots) . The supported slot types are: Type Description BOOLEAN Boolean TRUE/FALSE Indication INTEGER 32-bit signed integer REAL IEEE double precision floating point value STRING 80-byte ASCII string TIME Win32 64-bit FILETIME TAGNAME 68-byte ASCII string AGENTID Adroit AgentId struct. RAWBYTES A sequence of bytes whose contents are known to the agent only. (Agent specific data) LIST Adroit List Slot AGENT For future use. VARSTRING An unlimited-length ASCII string (first 4 bytes contain the length) HEADER Agent header structure NOTYPE Undefined type. Note: The RAWBYTES slot is ONLY for internal use of the agent and does NOT provide any other functionality. -->

PLEASE NOTE: When working on a 64 bit operating system, remember to add "\Wow6432Node" to the path of each registry setting after "\SOFTWARE", for instance: "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Adroit Technologies". To define how the alarming subsystem treats current alarms if an agent’s statusalarmInhibit slot is set to one and the agent is currently in alarm and/or unacknowledged, add the following DWORD registry value and configure it appropriately: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Workgroup\WG.INI\ (REG_)DWORD SmartInhibit Configure this value as follows: SmartInhibit = 0 The alarm, if active, will remain active. The alarm, if unacknowledged, will remain unacknowledged. The effect of the above is …. NOTHING changes SmartInhibit = 1 The alarm, if active, will be cleared with reported data set to "Inhibited". The alarm, if unacknowledged, will be globally acknowl

dged. The effect of the above is …. NOTHING changes SmartInhibit = 1 The alarm, if active, will be cleared with reported data set to "Inhibited". The alarm, if unacknowledged, will be globally acknowledged with reported data set to "Inhibited". The combination of the above actions will make the alarm disappear off the list This is the default operation . SmartInhibit = 2 The alarm, if active, will be cleared with reported data set to "Inhibited". So the alarm list would show alarm as not active. The alarm acknowledge status remains unchanged, regardless of whether it has already been acknowledged or not, globally or locally. -->

SNMP Community Strings Top SNMP Community Strings SNMP Community strings are like a user name or password that provide specific access to the SNMP managed objects management data exposed by SNMP managed devices that might be hardware, configuration parameters, performance statistics, and any other data that directly relates to the operation of this device. ( OID SNMP managed Object IDentifier, which describes the exact location of this value in the SNMP structure for its device. values) of a device. If the community string is correct, the device responds with the requested information. Otherwise the device simply discards the request and does not respond. The following three types of community strings determine the management commands that can be used, all of which are supported by Adroit: SNMP Read-only community string – this only allows information (OID values) to be retrieved from the managed device. Note: By convention, most equipment ships from the factory with a read-only community string set to "public". SNMP Read-Write community string – this allows information (OID values) to be retrieved from and modified within the managed device. SNMP Trap community string – this allow

ity string set to "public". SNMP Read-Write community string – this allows information (OID values) to be retrieved from and modified within the managed device. SNMP Trap community string – this allows SNMP Traps to be sent from a managed device. Traps are configured on a device to report when an error or specific event occurs. For instance, a common trap is the ‘Authentication Failure’ trap, that is sent when an incorrect community string is sent to a device. Note: Up to 16 community strings can be defined per device. Tip: Each device in a network can have its own unique set of community strings, although it may simplify network management if every device uses the same set of community strings. -->

(values) have an associated Object Identifier (OID), which describes the exact location of this object within the tree-like structure of the MIB SNMP Management Information Base, this is a database that lists uniquely described and organises SNMP managed objects hierarchically. of its device. Integer32: An integer variable, between -2^31 (-2147483648 decimal) and 2^31-1 (2147483647 decimal) inclusive. This should typically be stored in an Integer agent. This is writable . Unsigned 32-bit value: An integer variable, between 0 and 2^32-1 (4294967295 decimal) inclusive. This should typically be stored in a Real agent. This is writable . 32-bit counter: A counter variable that is a non-negative integer which increments until it reaches a maximum value of 2^32-1 (4294967295 decimal), when it wraps around and starts increasing again from zero. This should typically be stored in a Real agent. This is writable . 32-bit gauge: A gauge variable that represents a non-negative integer, which may increase or decrease, but shall never exceed a maximum value. ify the IP address of the Agent Server computer that contains the agent used to monitor this computer. SNMPManager Agent Usage Requirements SNMPManager Agent Usage Requirements The following usage requirements must be met before the SNMPManager agent can monitor and/or manage your network devices: The device must have a SINGLE (FIXED) IP address. Note1: ONE SNMPManager agent CANNOT connect to MULTIPLE devices (IP addresses). Note2: You CANNOT specify an IP address that is ALREADY configured for another SNMPManager agent! The device (computer) must be ACCESSIBLE on the network (able to be PINGed). You ONLY need to run the SNMP service on a computer that you want to monitor using the SNMPManager agent. IMPORTANT: NEVER run the Windows SNMP Trap (listener) service because it conflicts with the Adroit SNMP trap functionality! Note: This agent does NOT require the Windows SNMP Service to function, this service is ONLY required on each computer that this agent monitors. So to monitor a computer, you will typically need to install the SNMP service - because this component is NOT included in the STANDARD installation of Windows (and/or Server) operating systems. e STANDARD installation of Windows (and/or Server) operating systems. For details, see Installing the Windows SNMP Service. SNMPMgr Agent Usage Requirements Top SNMPMgr Agent Usage Requirements The following usage requirements must be met before the SNMPMgr agent can monitor and/or manage your network devices: Typically the device must have a SINGLE (FIXED) IP address or at least a unique port address so that this SNMP devices can be uniquely addressed via a gateway. Note1: ONE SNMPMgr agent CANNOT connect to MULTIPLE devices (IP addresses). Note2: You CANNOT specify an IP address that is ALREADY configured for another SNMPMgr agent! The device (computer) must be ACCESSIBLE on the network (able to be PINGed). You need to know which SNMP version the device supports and you also need to know all of its connection settings. Since the SNMPMgr agent supports up to SNMP version 3 and SNMP version 3 supports additional connection settings. ONLY WHEN MONITORING A COMPUTER: you need to run the SNMP service on this computer. Spark Lines Top Spark Lines Purpose: when operators only need to be aware of how a process variable (PV) behaves with respect to its normal operating range. Description: A small unlabelled trend of a process variable whose normal operating range is shaded in a color, which does not display the actual value: User interaction: None. wzdSparkLine_v01 : trends an analogue process variable Required values: Note: When this wizard is added to a graphic form, all these values are MANDATORY and therefore must ALL be specified. Tip: These values are listed in the order they are specified in the wizard. Browse in the Analog agent name (although this can specify the value slot, but no other slot name) representing the process variable (PV) that is to be monitored e.g. ana001.value Browse in the maximum normal operating range of this process variable, typically this is the high alarm limit (the hi slot) of the Analog agent e.g. ana001.hi Browse in the minimum normal operating range of this process variable, typically this is the low alarm limit (the lo slot) of the Analog agent e.g. ana001.lo -->

text: Specific Status Bits of the DbAccess Agent Top Specific Status Bits of the DbAccess Agent The DbAccess Agent has the following specific status bits: statusBit16 Disconnected ON if there is no connection to the database. statusBit17 Connected ON if there is a connection to the database. statusBit18 Transaction error ON if a transaction with the database fails. Note: This status slot is turned off before executing a new transaction but it is also possible to explicitly turn it off, via a script, before executing a transaction. statusBit19 Overrun error ON if the transaction time took longer than the scheduled delay period. i.e. runTime in seconds > schedulePeriod in seconds. Works only for scheduled transactions. statusBit20 Connection error ON if there is a problem connecting to the database. statusBit21 Transaction success ON if a transaction with the database succeeds. Note: This status slot is turned off before executing a new transaction but it is also possible to explicitly turn it off, via a script, before executing a transaction. It is important to alarm the Transaction error and Overrun error as these indicate any problems associated with a DbAccess Agent. The alarm type cre

metadata.title: Specific Status Bits of the DbAccess Agent

text: off, via a script, before executing a transaction. It is important to alarm the Transaction error and Overrun error as these indicate any problems associated with a DbAccess Agent. The alarm type created for alarming DbAccess Agents should use the information slot in the "Reported Data" field as this may indicate useful error information. If the error is too long to be displayed in an alarm list or an event viewer, edit the agent and click on the Details button to get a better description. -->

text: Specific Status Bits of the DBLog Agent Top Specific Status Bits of the DBLog Agent The following status bit indicates whether the connection to the specified OLE DB database is healthy or not, as follows: statusBit16 ConnectionError On when an OLEDB error occurs – either the specified connection string is invalid OR a transaction error has occurred. If this is ON and the connection string is VALID, then you can use the following VARSTRING slots of this agent to determine the possible cause of error, as follows: lastError : The last OLE DB transaction error. lastErrorQuery : The query that caused the last OLE DB transaction error. statusBit17 TransactionError On when an error occurred during the last transaction to the specified OLE DB database, this can either be alarmed or displayed. statusBit18 QueueFilling On when there is more than 1 item in queue, which could be indicative of a slow database link. statusBit19 QueueDump This is pulsed On, when the number of items in the queue (waiting to be logged) exceeds a 1000 and these items are dumped to a SQL file, which requires manual intervention to "catch-up" this lost data. Note1: If this occurs it is usually indicative of a problem

text: Specific Status Bits of the Expression Agent Top Specific Status Bits of the Expression Agent When the value slot of the Expression agent changes, the agent will set one of its specific status bits in the agent’s status word to describe the current value that is produced by the expression. Any agent subscribing to the Expression agent can then detect these status bits. The 6 specific status bits of the Expression agent can be used to describe the Value calculated for the expression, as follows: statusBit16 Equal to zero On when expression = 0. statusBit17 Greater than zero On when expression > 0. statusBit18 Less than zero On when expression < 0. statusBit19 Greater than or equal to zero On when expression >= 0. statusBit20 Less than or equal to zero On when expression <= 0. statusBit21 Contains bad data On when there is an error in the expression. -->

text: Specific Status Bits of the ICMP Agent Top Specific Status Bits of the ICMP Agent The ICMP or PING agent uses the Internet Control Message Protocol to determine the existence of a remote device on the network. Any IP network device is able to send, receive and process ICMP messages. These messages are only used for troubleshooting network problems and not to transfer data. The most common use of the ICMP protocol is by the PING diagnostic utility. The following status bits of this agent can be used for diagnosing the existence of the specified remote device on the network, as follows: statusBit16 Healthy On when the last ICMP message was sent to and received from the network device successfully. statusBit17 General_Failure On when there is any failure preventing the network device from being accessed. This value is cleared when the device becomes accessible (Healthy). statusBit18 Destination_Unreachable On when the failure is caused because the destination IP address is not reachable on the current network, for instance when no routing is available to reach this IP address range. This value is cleared when the device becomes accessible (Healthy) or when a timeout failure occurs. st

metadata.title: Specific Status Bits of the ICMP Agent

text: n the current network, for instance when no routing is available to reach this IP address range. This value is cleared when the device becomes accessible (Healthy) or when a timeout failure occurs. statusBit19 Destination_Timeout On when the failure is caused because no response has been received from the remote device within the configured timeout value. This value is cleared when the device becomes accessible (Healthy) or when the remote device becomes unreachable. statusBit20 High On when the last round trip time The time to send an ICMP message to the network device and receive a reply. (INTEGER roundTripTime slot) is GREATER THAN OR EQUAL to the Round trip time: high alarm value (ms) (INTEGER hi slot). statusBit21 high-High On when the last round trip time is GREATER THAN OR EQUAL to the Round trip time: high-high alarm value (ms) (INTEGER hiHi slot). statusBit22 Busy On when an ICMP message is in the process of being sent and/or received from the network device. -->

text: Specific Status Bits of the Script Agent Top Specific Status Bits of the Script Agent The Script agent has the following specific status bits: statusBit16 Idle ON if the main subroutine is not running. statusBit17 Running ON if the main subroutine is running. statusBit18 Compilation error ON if there is an error in the compilation of any of the specified module files. statusBit19 Runtime error ON if the an error occurs in any of the subroutines during execution of the script. statusBit20 Overrun error ON if the execution time of the main subroutine took longer than the scheduled delay period. i.e. runTime in seconds > schedulePeriod in seconds. text: Specific Status Bits of the Timer Agent Top Specific Status Bits of the Timer Agent The Timer agent is able to perform one of three commonly used timing operations. The following status bits can determine, whether the configured timer is running or has expired: statusBit16 Running On if the timer is enabled i.e. the timer is operating. statusBit17 Expired On when the timer has terminated, which is timing operation-specific, as follows: The pulse width time expires, when configured as an on timer. For details, see Configuring On Timers . The delay time expires, when configured as an on delay timer. For details, see Configuring On Delay Timers . The timer is not running, when configured as a pulse generator. For details, see Configuring Pulse Generators . Note: The operational status of the timer must not be confused with the value slot of this agent, since these are sometimes independent elements i.e. the timer is not necessarily off when its value is FALSE. For details of the timing operations performed by this agent, see Timer agent . -->

text: Specifying Additional Callers Top Specifying Additional Callers Once a Command agent has been linked to a device, it is possible to specify one or more additional cell phone numbers that are able to send SMS messages to it, in addition to the configured recipient phone number. For details, see Specifying the GSM_SMS Device or Specifying the Recipient Phone Number . However it is ONLY when the Command agent has been enabled to perform commands that commands received from these phone numbers will be performed. For details, see Allowing Commands to be Performed . WARNING! Once the Command agent is configured to receive commands, scan point licenses are consumed by each unique phone number that is able to send an SMS command to this Command agent i.e. by both the configured recipient phone number and these additional cell phone numbers that are specified or used to send SMS messages to it. There are two methods by which these additional callers can be specified: Anonymous access: This requires the least configuration, although it provides unrestricted access in that anyone who phones the recipient will be able to send commands to this Command agent. For details, see Configuring Anonymo

ires the least configuration, although it provides unrestricted access in that anyone who phones the recipient will be able to send commands to this Command agent. For details, see Configuring Anonymous Caller Access . PLEASE NOTE: In this case EVERY unique caller who phones the recipient and issues a command to the Command agent will consume a scan point license, which will not be released until the Agent Server is shutdown. Authorised access: This requires the cell phone numbers of all the callers who are allowed to issue commands to this Command agent to be added to the Cmd phone numbers list. However, only these additional callers are able to ‘command’ this agent and hence will consume scan licenses. For details, see Configuring Authorised Caller Access . Note: This list can hold a maximum of 10 numbers. Tip: Since these commands are able to obtain and/or control any process value or slot exposed by the Agent Server, it is recommended to BOTH specify the authorised phone numbers AND to limit these command-able phone numbers for security reasons. -->

text: Specifying Permitted Commands Top Specifying Permitted Commands Once a Command agent has been allowed to perform commands, NONE of the available commands are selected by default, since certain commands pose a greater security and operational risk than others. For this reason it is necessary to specify exactly which commands each Command agent are able to perform. For details on allowing a command agent to perform commands, see Allowing Commands to be Performed . To select which commands a Command agent is able to perform: Edit the required Command agent. For details, see Editing Agents . This will display the Edit Command agent dialog. If necessary, select the General tab, the default selection. Under the Commands group, ensure that the Enable commands checkbox is checked. Check or clear, the checkboxes next to the available commands, listed beneath each of the following checkboxes, as required: Note: For details of the available commands that can be performed, see Available Commands . Allow ‘Get’ commands: If checked, this will allow this agent to retrieve the value of any tag (agent.slot) exposed by the Agent Server and the GetCommands specific status bit for this agent will also

Allow ‘Get’ commands: If checked, this will allow this agent to retrieve the value of any tag (agent.slot) exposed by the Agent Server and the GetCommands specific status bit for this agent will also be checked, to indicate this. For details, see GET Commands or Specific Status Bits . Note: This command does not pose a security risk since process values are only received. Allow ‘Set’ commands: If checked, this will allow this agent to modify the value of any tag (agent.slot) exposed by the Agent Server and the SetCommands specific status bit for this agent will also be checked, to indicate this. For details, see SET Commands . WARNING! Since this command can cause a serious security and operational risk, additional settings are provided to further restrict its usage. For details, see Additional SET Command Restrictions . Allow ‘Ack’ commands: If checked, this will allow this agent to globally and/or locally acknowledge alarms that have been reported by an agent within the Agent Server. The AckCommands specific status bit for this agent will also be checked, to indicate this. For details, see ACK Commands . Note: This command DOES pose a security risk since alarms can be acknowledg

. The AckCommands specific status bit for this agent will also be checked, to indicate this. For details, see ACK Commands . Note: This command DOES pose a security risk since alarms can be acknowledged remotely. -->

text: Specifying the OLE DB table or view or databinder polling interval Top Specifying the OLE DB table or view or databinder polling interval Each table or view or configured databinder of an OLE DB datasource is monitored by the Server at a specified interval for any changes that have been made to its data. Click for more information: In other words, whether existing data has been changed or new data that has been added. If this data has changed since the last monitored interval then all this data will be resent to the applicable Client(s). For this reason, it is essential that this monitoring interval is correctly configured to prevent the needless sending of large amounts of data. lobal affects all devices) Items configured in this group are common to all outstations using the same serial port.
