Start Communications Top Start Communications Either if the Start Comms item in the File menu is selected after the WanClient is launched or if the WanClient is started with the "/start" command-line parameter, this will initiate the following sequence of events: A check is made to ensure that there is an Agent Server that is currently running on the local computer. If this fails, this error is reported in the WanClient message window and an appropriate warning message is displayed. The main database is loaded The main database is opened. If the main database does not contain any configured servers then this error is reported in the WanClient message window. WanClient then connects to the local Agent Server The database is then closed WanClient then begins the process of connecting to the configured servers by PINGing them. When a WanServer responds to the PING, the WanClient will send it its list of tags that it needs to subscribe to and the required polling periods of each tag. The WanClient will then request from the connected WanServers their changed data. Note: As soon as an error is reported, this communication process terminates. When the WanClient starts up, control tags ar

anClient will then request from the connected WanServers their changed data. Note: As soon as an error is reported, this communication process terminates. When the WanClient starts up, control tags are assumed to have dirty values until a value is received from the WanServer. Updates from a WanServer that fail to putslot in the local Agent Server will also cause values to be "dirty" again. Dirty values are NOT sent to WanServer to prevent "blind" value changes. -->

Starting the Agent Server Top Starting the Agent Server Start up and log onto Windows. Note: If necessary, ensure that the HASP is in place. For details, see Adroit Licensing . Start the Agent Server by selecting the Agent Server icon in the Start , Programs , Adroit 10 menu. The Agent Server window will appear minimised, in a location dependent upon its Minimise to tray setting . Open this, if you wish to see the loading messages: Allow the Agent Server to complete the loading process. This is shown by the message loading complete. Note: the status bar displays the percentage of physical memory being used by the system. When this is greater than 100 % then all the physical memory is being used, requiring the use of virtual memory (the paging file), which will slow down the performance of the system and of the Agent Server. Ideally, this figure should not exceed 75%. Minimise the Agent Server window by selecting its minimise button or command. Now launch the required client application to view and configure the agents within the Agent Server. To troubleshoot this process, see Startup difficulties . -->

In this case, the size of this graphic form is the actual size that the end-user will see too. To statically resize a graphic form in the Designer workspace: Open the required graphic form. Click on the graphic form itself to cause the eight sizing handles small boxes that appear around the perimeter of a selected item, which if dragged changes the size of this item. Retry - The number of times that Adroit will try to gain communication with a meter before failing a transaction. rite). Network/port Idle – time in seconds to wait between transactions, (values 1-15). This time applies to all Reads and Writes out to the meter. WARNING Channels are dynamically ordered from the smallest period to the largest. If you add a channel or edit a channel in the meter, the SCADA MUST take this into account that channels positions could move. Example: channel 1 period = 10 minute sample rate, channel 2 = 30 minute sample rate, now you add channel 3 = 5 minute rate, then channel 3 will become channel 1 in memory, and the old 1 and 2 will become 2 and 3 respectively. So, if channel 1 was VOLTS, and channel 3 was VARS, the next profile read, channel 1 would have VARS instead of VOLTS. This is like swapping two digital jumpers on a digital output card without telling the SCADA engineer to update the user interface – a wrong indication is presented. SurfaceChart controls Top SurfaceChart controls These controls are typically used to plot surfaces or three dimensional charts, from points that are plotted from three sets of values. In other words one set provides the X or horizontal coordinate and the other provides the Y or vertical coordinate of each point and the third set provides the Z or height dimension. A typical usage is if you have a curve and you want to see how this curve changes from day to day. In this case the X = period (e.g. 12am-12pm); Y = value and Z = date time e.g. number of days. Note: You can create template charting controls, since the applicable Series values of chart controls support the use of curly brackets {} to create aliases for SmartUI Templates or data element substitutions for wizards. Synchronizing Distributed Adroit Installations Top Synchronizing Distributed Adroit Installations IMPORTANT: It is compulsory that Adroit Distributed systems are time synchronised , since clustering and other important aspects of Adroit are compromised by an unsynchronised system. This can be accomplished by ensuring that the W32Time service is enabled and working. If so, Active Directory domain member computers will automatically synchronise with the domain controller, however, Workgroup computers must ensure that they are synchronised to the same source. Also ensure that the country selection in the Regional Settings in the Control Panel is the same on all the computers. CAUTION: If the system clock is set back, the mimics, alarming and datalogging may appear to cease working and look as if the system has frozen. This is because Adroit will discard any time stamped data that is older than that currently held in the User Interface; since it always displays or records the latest events it receives. When the system clock reaches the time it was set back, the mimics, alarms and datalogging will come alive again. -->

TableLayoutPanel controls Top TableLayoutPanel controls The TableLayoutPanel control allows you to add and arrange controls in a table, so that these controls can change dynamically as the application environment changes. Each cell in this table typically contains a single control. Note: While you can add a container control such as a Panel to add multiple controls in a cell this can complicate your layouts. Using this control provides the following advantages: it changes dynamically as the application environment changes. In other words, the added controls can proportionally resize, when the parent control is resized or text length changing due to localization etc. you can add any Windows Forms control to a cell in this TableLayoutPanel control, allowing you to construct sophisticated layouts controls can span (cross) multiple rows and columns, which also allows you to construct sophisticated layouts being a table, this control can easily expand, by adding additional rows and/or columns to accommodate new controls, without you needing to manually re-configure the alignment of the other controls through the use of row and column styles, you can specify how the Height (row style) or

ns to accommodate new controls, without you needing to manually re-configure the alignment of the other controls through the use of row and column styles, you can specify how the Height (row style) or Width (column style) should be calculated However, Microsoft recommends that you use the TableLayoutPanel control sparingly and provides the following Recommendations for using TableLayoutPanel controls . IMPORTANT: When you DELETE a TableLayoutPanel control an error occurs because it is only PARTIALLY removed at design time, so you need to save, close and reopen the graphic form to complete the removal of this control and its added controls. WARNING: Immediately after deleting a TableLayoutPanel control, although this control and/or the added controls may remain on the graphic form, any further configuration of them will be lost as these will be removed the next time you save and reopen this graphic form. Tag Groups Top Tag Groups The WanClient application initiates communications to one or more WanServer applications to fetch or send values of Adroit tags that occur in the Agent Server that is also running on the WanClient computer. These tags are organised using one or more groups, which primarily manage their required communication settings. Although there are other criteria that can be used when organizing tags into groups. For details, see Criteria for Creating Tag Groups . While the groups provide the tag-specific communication settings, servers provide the group-specific communication settings to access the required WanServers. Therefore groups are server-specific i.e. they can only be configured after the required server(s) have been configured. For details, see Configuring Servers . Tag-specific Scanning Settings Top Tag-specific Scanning Settings These settings are the scanning-specific Control bits , which are usually configured in the required agent's header . These settings apply to all the scanned slots of the agent for which they are configured. Note1: Changes made to these settings ONLY take effect when the device(s) used to scan the slots of the configured agent(s) is restarted. Note2: By this usage "scan" implies "reading", hence "scanOutput" implies "writing’. Output Enable: If this bit is set, it will enable the agent to update the PLC (front-end device). This does not affect the agent from being updated by the PLC (front-end device). Slot name: statusScanOutputEnable or statusBit09. Scan Inhibit: If this bit is set, it will stop the agent from being updated by the PLC (front-end device). This does not affect the agent from updating a PLC (front-end device). Slot name: statusScanInhibit or statusBit08. Output Initialise: If this bit is set, an initial value will be scanned out from the agent at startup, or after any communications failure and subsequent recovery. Slot name: statusScanInitialise or statusBit11. -->

Tags within Selected Scan Jobs Top Tags within Selected Scan Jobs The Scanning Monitor utility provides information on the scanning (communications) configuration for a particular Agent Server, so this information can be used to manually fine-tune the scanning subsystem to achieve optimal performance. For details, see Monitoring Scanning in Adroit . The list at the bottom of this utility, displays the tags (scan points) grouped within the selected scan job or jobs within the scan job list, directly above this list. For details, see Scan Jobs within Selected Devices . Note: Scan jobs are automatically created by Adroit to group the scanned tags together in such a way as to minimise scanning load and to maximise throughput. For details on how to assist with this process, see Scanning Optimization Tips . This list, consists of the following columns: Tag: This identifies the name of tag (agent.slot) or scan point contained within the selected scan job(s) in the scan job list. The other columns indicate the following attributes of this scan point: Device address: This is the address of the front-end device to which or from which the value of this tag will be written or read. This addres

umns indicate the following attributes of this scan point: Device address: This is the address of the front-end device to which or from which the value of this tag will be written or read. This address is device-specific. Job offset: This indicates the offset of the item within its scan job. Bit offset: This is a legacy value, which generally shows a value of zero. Deadband: This indicates the specified deadband value for the tag Output enabled: This is 1 when the tag is output enabled, which allows this tag to write new values to the front-end device. Note: A value of Global! , indicates that the entire agent has been output enabled instead of just the slot that is being scanned. This can cause a problem when more than one slot of the same agent is being scanned, for when ANY of the scanned slot values change, a write message will be sent to the scanning subsystem, which can lead to scan degradation. Scan inhibited: This is 1 when the tag is scan inhibited, which prevents the front-end device from changing the value of this tag. This is normally used in conjunction with 'output enabled' to configure a write only tag. Note: A value of Global! , indicates that the entire agent has b

d device from changing the value of this tag. This is normally used in conjunction with 'output enabled' to configure a write only tag. Note: A value of Global! , indicates that the entire agent has been scan inhibited instead of just the slot that is being scanned. This can cause also lead to scan degradation when more than one slot of the same agent is being scanned. Scan bad: This is 1 when a problem has occurred with the scan point. In polled drivers, scan bad is generally true for all tags in the job and/or device. If so, check the configuration and cabling. Supported commands: When this list is right-clicked, the following option is displayed: Refresh: this will update ALL the lists with the latest scanning configuration. This also known as inhibiting an alarm. ) alarming temporarily when you are performing maintenance on a plant section or a particular item of equipment or when an alarm indicator is not functioning correctly or is being tested. Depending upon the scope of the required shutdown and the configuration of your alarming, you are able to temporarily suspend alarming in the following two ways: Globally per Alarm agent: this option should only be used when an Alarm agent ONLY manages all the alarming of the plant section that is being shutdown or the plant item/s that are being shutdown for maintenance or repair. Test Control Recipe Top Test Control Recipe Test the validity of the selected control recipe. The following errors that will cause recipe execution to fail are reported: Error message - "Control recipe ingredient [ agent.slot ] not found". The control recipe ingredient was not found in the Agent Server. The agent has either not been added or is misspelled. Error message - "Master [ agent.slot ] and control recipe [ agent.slot ] ingredients are not equal". The control recipe ingredient for a step must be the same as the master recipe ingredient. In this case, check that the control recipe is valid for the current master recipe. Error message - "Control recipe ingredient must be a Boolean, Real, Integer, String or a VarString". The control recipe ingredient type is not supported. (a VarString is a character array whose size can be variable - see document AU-05 "Agents Types and Structures") Error message - "Control recipe ingredient value [ value ] is invalid". This occurs when attempting to set a control recipe ingredient to an illegal value, e.g. setting a real number to a string. -->

The Accumulator Agent Top The Accumulator agent The Accumulator Agent gets its name from the type of process values that it monitors and operates in three ways: It retrieves an input value that normally accumulates over time and is always increasing in value. It uses this value to calculate the difference, or its change in value, between successive events or over a specific time or interval. Finally, it calculates the total for a period based on a predefined trigger or time interval. Operation When the agent is first enabled, it works as follows: If the intervalMode slot property is set to 4, a new period will commence immediately. If the intervalMode slot property is set to 3, the period will commence immediately but will end at the next synchronised period. At the end of every period, the value is saved as lastValue and the new value is calculated as inputValue minus startValue . If a SQL Server connection is configured, a new record is added to the history table (see History below) containing the period end time, the value for the period as well as the current inputValue . A new period commences immediately and the startValue (=inputValue) is recorded. Configuration The minimum

containing the period end time, the value for the period as well as the current inputValue . A new period commences immediately and the startValue (=inputValue) is recorded. Configuration The minimum required configuration for the Accumulator agent: Define an inputTag OR scan the inputValue and then enable the agent. Define a triggerTag and triggerMode OR a method of driving the trigger slot. Trigger event When a trigger event occurs: The agent subtracts the previous interval input value from the current input value to determine the value differential for the current period. This results in a value which represents “the total production for the last hour or shift or day and so-on” . It then calculates the rate of change in value, which is the differential value for the current period divided by the interval of this period (value per hour) . Alarming You can also configure alarm limits for both the differential value and rate of change in value for the current period, which will monitor the current value or rate against these alarm limits: high-high high low low-low Any infringement of these alarm limits causes the agent to set its corresponding status bit , which can also be alarme

the current value or rate against these alarm limits: high-high high low low-low Any infringement of these alarm limits causes the agent to set its corresponding status bit , which can also be alarmed. History To maintain a history of these periodic counts/totals, you should connect the Accumulator agent to a SQL Server database: Each record captures the start and end times of the period, the start and end values and the differential value for the period. To provide automatic management of this data, then a housekeeping period can be defined to ensure that it keeps the most relevant or most recent records only. If a valid connection and table is specified, the History table is created as follows: Column name Type Description idx Int Auto incrementing index dt datetime Period end date and time value float Calculated value for period accumulator float The accumulator reading (inputValue) at the end of the period Further Information For further details, read the following topics: Configuring Accumulator Agents - How to configure some or all of the functionality for an Accumulator agent. The Accumulator Agent Top The Accumulator agent The Accumulator Agent gets its name from the type of process values that it monitors and operates in three ways: It retrieves an input value that normally accumulates over time and is always increasing in value. It uses this value to calculate the difference, or its change in value, between successive events or over a specific time or interval. Finally, it calculates the total for a period based on a predefined trigger or time interval. Operation When the agent is first enabled, it works as follows: If the intervalMode slot property is set to 4, a new period will commence immediately. If the intervalMode slot property is set to 3, the period will commence immediately but will end at the next synchronised period. At the end of every period, the value is saved as lastValue and the new value is calculated as inputValue minus startValue . If a SQL Server connection is configured, a new record is added to the history table (see History below) containing the period end time, the value for the period as well as the current inputValue . A new period commences immediately and the startValue (=inputValue) is recorded. Configuration The minimum

containing the period end time, the value for the period as well as the current inputValue . A new period commences immediately and the startValue (=inputValue) is recorded. Configuration The minimum required configuration for the Accumulator agent: Define an inputTag OR scan the inputValue and then enable the agent. Define a triggerTag and triggerMode OR a method of driving the trigger slot. Trigger event When a trigger event occurs: The agent subtracts the previous interval input value from the current input value to determine the value differential for the current period. This results in a value which represents “the total production for the last hour or shift or day and so-on” . It then calculates the rate of change in value, which is the differential value for the current period divided by the interval of this period (value per hour) . Alarming You can also configure alarm limits for both the differential value and rate of change in value for the current period, which will monitor the current value or rate against these alarm limits: high-high high low low-low Any infringement of these alarm limits causes the agent to set its corresponding status bit , which can also be alarme

the current value or rate against these alarm limits: high-high high low low-low Any infringement of these alarm limits causes the agent to set its corresponding status bit , which can also be alarmed. History To maintain a history of these periodic counts/totals, you should connect the Accumulator agent to a SQL Server database: Each record captures the start and end times of the period, the start and end values and the differential value for the period. To provide automatic management of this data, then a housekeeping period can be defined to ensure that it keeps the most relevant or most recent records only. The Adroit Project Explorer Utility Top The Adroit Project Explorer Utility The Adroit Project Explorer configures and manages both local and distributed Adroit projects. For details, see Project Explorer . This essentially consists of the following two windowpanes: A tree windowpane on the left, displays the various objects in a hierarchical manner , such as found in the Windows Explorer. Note: Right-click in this windowpane, to display a menu of commands applicable to the currently selected item . A grid windowpane on the right, whose contents are dependent upon on the item currently selected in the tree. Note: The grid provides the following standard configuration options . The Project Explorer window can be adapted to your working environment, as follows: Change the width of these windowpanes by clicking below the windowpanes where the division between the two windowpanes is required, in the grey portion at the bottom of the window from the left side of the dialog to the Refresh button. Click the Park button, on the bottom left corner of the window, to move the Project Explorer window off the screen, to view and edit other windows, so that only its right border is visible on th

tton. Click the Park button, on the bottom left corner of the window, to move the Project Explorer window off the screen, to view and edit other windows, so that only its right border is visible on the left side of the screen. The Agent Server Window Tray Icon Top The Agent Server Window Tray Icon Normally, when the Agent Server window is minimised, it appears in the task bar along with any other currently open program, such as on start up. But if the Minimise to tray command, in the Agent Server window's Options menu , is selected, then the Agent Server window appears as a tray icon in the bottom right of the screen, whenever it is minimised. Note: If the Minimise to tray command is selected then on the next startup the AS will immediately startup as a tray icon, similarly if this is disabled then on the next startup the AS will startup as an AS window. The green light indicates that the Agent Server is running. The red light indicates that the Agent Server is shutting down. For instance, all agents belonging to the north side of a process plant could be grouped in the NORTH_PLANT agent group. Agent groups may, and usually do, have overlapping memberships (i.e. an agent is allowed to belong to more than one group). For details, see Grouping Agents Together . Normal mode, the AgentGroup agent simply acts as a container for the agents grouped with it, and does not modify its status if any of its group member’s status changes. Fan in status bits mode, the AgentGroup agent will set its status bits in accordance with the status bits of its members. Only one member agent needs to set a given status bit for it to be "fanned in" to the AgentGroup’s status bit. Bulk editing of agent type mode, this is only possible if all the agents contained by the AgentGroup are of the same type, any changes made to an AgentGroup agent’s control status bits will "fan-out" to the same control bits belonging to the members of the group. It will also route any of their significant events to one or more alarm lists, printers or event logs. Each Agent Server has one instance of the Alarm agent already created called defaultAlarmAgent . However, additional Alarm agents may be created to provide easier management of alarm filtering and messaging loading. Tip: If necessary, bulk-alarming configuration can be performed. For details, see Importing Alarm Agents . The AlarmManagement Agent Top The AlarmManagement Agent Alarm Management is an important aspect of process control required to counteract inefficient alarming. Alarm management allows you to create an alarming system that alerts the operator to the most relevant alarm for the current incident. In this case fewer alarms are more effective as the human mind can only focus on a few things at a time. For details, see About Alarm Management . The AlarmManagement agent logs all incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). and their details, including their time of occurrence, their time of acknowledgement and the time at which they were cleared to a database. This repository of incidents allows you to: generate statistics from the data produced by the alarming system. This allows you to have efficient and meaningful incident reviews to identify and remove nuisance alarms by analysing the counts, frequencies, durations and acknowledgement times of alarms. measure KPIs to improve your alarming configurat

meaningful incident reviews to identify and remove nuisance alarms by analysing the counts, frequencies, durations and acknowledgement times of alarms. measure KPIs to improve your alarming configuration. For details, see Obtaining KPI Values . For the recommended method of implementing the AlarmManagement agent to configure and record your active the monitored condition of this incident (alarm/event) is still in effect and has not yet returned to its normal operating state. incidents so that you can improve your alarming configuration, see Quick Start to Configure and Record Incidents (Alarms/Events) . Note1 : You can only add ONE AlarmManagement agent. Note2: Ensure that your Adroit license is licensed to enable your AlarmManagement agent to function. Tip: An unlicensed AlarmManagement agent can log your historical acknowledged alarms. For details, see Historical Alarm mode . Multiple Agent Servers may log incidents to the same database thereby unifying alarm management for the enterprise. However, in this case please ensure that your AlarmManagement agent is uniquely named as each incident is logged using the name of its assigned AlarmManagement agent. Repeating this process at

prise. However, in this case please ensure that your AlarmManagement agent is uniquely named as each incident is logged using the name of its assigned AlarmManagement agent. Repeating this process at regular intervals will eventually create relevant alarms, which result in the following benefits: Improves the operator environment, workload and efficiency Avoids unplanned outages Improves plant reliability The review process must be a repetitive and cyclical process, for the following reasons: Alarms are generally added without prior forethought Your process changes over time Your equipment changes and degrades over time Seasonal changes The AlarmManagement agent is designed to help you implement the first 3 of t he following 5 phases of ongoing Alarm Management: Alarm and Event Archiving: although already accomplished by Adroit , this is improved by the new AlarmManagement agent. Alarm and Event Analysis: this is main function of the new AlarmManagement agent Alarm Rationalisation: this exercise is performed by the user after the analysing the alarms/events. Dynamic Alarm Management: this is the automated tuning of alarms, currently not supported by the AlarmManagement agent. Predi

The AlarmManagement Agent Top The AlarmManagement Agent Alarm Management is an important aspect of process control required to counteract inefficient alarming. Alarm management allows you to create an alarming system that alerts the operator to the most relevant alarm for the current incident. In this case fewer alarms are more effective as the human mind can only focus on a few things at a time. For details, see About Alarm Management . The AlarmManagement agent logs all incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). and their details, including their time of occurrence, their time of acknowledgement and the time at which they were cleared to a database. This repository of incidents allows you to: generate statistics from the data produced by the alarming system. This allows you to have efficient and meaningful incident reviews to identify and remove nuisance alarms by analysing the counts, frequencies, durations and acknowledgement times of alarms. measure KPIs to improve your alarming configurat

meaningful incident reviews to identify and remove nuisance alarms by analysing the counts, frequencies, durations and acknowledgement times of alarms. measure KPIs to improve your alarming configuration. For details, see Obtaining KPI Values . The Alias Agent Top The Alias Agent An alias is an assumed or "false" name of another agent. By containing a reference to the agent it is aliasing, the Alias agent appears to have the same Behaviour and state information of the agent it is referencing, differing only in its identity. Aliases can be very useful when attaching Behaviours to picture elements, which are to be repeatedly reused for different scenarios, such as recipes, particularly if the source agent is unknown. By simply reconfiguring the Alias agent to reference the desired agent for each scenario, the need to re-edit all the Behaviours on each picture element is eliminated. For example, a rectangular picture element with fill Behaviour supplied by tag ALI01 can be switched from REC01 to REC02 by simply re-editing the Alias agent or by dynamically changing the contents of the Alias agent’s tagname slot from REC01 to REC02 using the Operator Action, Data Set Behaviour. To access the slots of the Alias agent directly (as opposed to the slots of the agent it is aliasing), preface it with a % symbol to override its de-referencing. Note: that when browsing the slots of an Alias agent using the Agent Explorer, you will not

pposed to the slots of the agent it is aliasing), preface it with a % symbol to override its de-referencing. Note: that when browsing the slots of an Alias agent using the Agent Explorer, you will not be able to see this slot. Instead, the % symbol and the tagname slot must be typed in manually into the relevant Behaviour dialog. E.g. %ALI01.tagname Note: Alias agents may not be scanned. Alias Agent - Slot Details . The Analog Agent Top The Analog Agent An Analog agent stores a real (floating point) value that provides the following functionality: Scaling its value according to user defined minimum and maximum scaling settings. These scaling parameters are typically only specified, when a front-end device contains this value. The Analog agent provides support for up to 51 bit numbers, in that the new maximum range is 2,000,000,000,000,000 for unsigned numbers or -1,000,000,000,000,000 to 1,000,000,000,000,000 for signed numbers. Note: To reduce the loss of accuracy in scaling caused by IEEE conversion issues, the Analog agent bypasses the scaling calculation, when the scaling is 1:1. Monitoring its value against one or more of the following value-specific alarm limits: low-low, low, high, high-high and/or rate of change. Any infringement of these alarm limits causes the agent to set its corresponding status bits, which can be alarmed. Specifying the engineering units used to measure this value. Monitoring its value for changes, where any change in value causes the agent to log an event and set a status bit, which can be alarmed. Calculating statistics from the value slot every second, for a sp

nitoring its value for changes, where any change in value causes the agent to log an event and set a status bit, which can be alarmed. Calculating statistics from the value slot every second, for a specific rolling period (specified in minutes). For details, see Calculating statistics from Analog values . Recording the time this value changes, which is saved to the time slot a value (attribute) or field within an agent that can be retrieved and/or set. of this agent Reverse polarity scaling and the remote configuration of the alarm limits Square root extraction for the linearization of flow signals, Alarm deadband settings for the high and low alarm limits A cold start value initialization option when starting the Agent Server. For details on how to configure some or all of this functionality for an Analog agent, see Configuring Analog Agents . IMPORTANT CHANGE FOR ANALOG AGENTS: Changed the default method of handling what happens when the rawvalue slot goes out of range (either exceeds the rawMax value or is lower than the rawMin value), from now this causes the Analog agent to set the new OutOfRange status bit (which can be alarmed if needed). This is to prevent the entire agent

s the rawMax value or is lower than the rawMin value), from now this causes the Analog agent to set the new OutOfRange status bit (which can be alarmed if needed). This is to prevent the entire agent from being marked at as being bad, as happened previously, which causes all the instances of this value to be greyed out (disabled) on the mimics which display them. Note: If you prefer the legacy method of marking the agent bad (setting the statusAgentBad condition bit) when the rawvalue slot goes out of range, then you need to add the OutOfRangeEqualsAgentBad registry setting. Typically Analog agents should be used for tank levels or any process value stored in a front-end device that needs to be scaled (converted) to and from its engineering value and/or that needs to be closely monitored and/or alarmed. If you ONLY want to store a real (floating point) value then use the Real agent instead. Note: For those of you running a clustered Agent Server, this agent supports real-time catch-up so even if the master Agent Server fails, the standby will seamlessly continue with the current configuration settings including its scaling and alarm limit settings. The ARec Agent Top The ARec Agent The ARec agent or "Associated digital Record" agent, is a fancy version of the Multistate agent that enables the configuration of up to 255 states using truth table type logic on up to 32 bits. These 32 bits can be mapped to individual digital tags or the complete 32 bit value can be scanned from an external value. Each state can be configured to test a mask of the bits for ON, OFF or DON'T CARE conditions and can also be tested for timeouts and can be used to set status bits. In addition, each state, or timed out state, can be configured to set or clear one or more of the 32 input bits, allowing this agent to be used as a sequence controller. It is also possible to configure the AREC agent as a numerical sequence , to display text, similar to the StringList agent, except that the AREC supports up to 255 sequence steps and enables these steps to set its status bits. To edit or configure an AREC agent . Configure a Truth Table . Configure the I/O Bits . Configure the States . Configuration a Numerical Sequence . Configure the Sequence Steps . Specific Status Bits . ARec Agent - Slot Details . ARec Agent - Database File Format . -->

The Audit Agent Top The Audit Agent This agent supplements the auditing or logging of the Agent Server sessions and selected activities performed during these sessions to an OLE DB database. Use the Audit agent to specify one or more tags that you want to monitor for ANY change in value. When a value changes, for any reason, the agent logs this change of value to the audit database. In other words, EVERY value change for EVERY specified tag is logged, regardless of whether Adroit or a PLC or something else causes this change in value. For this reason, it is essential that you ONLY specify the process tags whose EVERY change in value is important to the running of the process . Typically you will audit set points or alarm levels, but not temperature or level values. In other words, do not specify process tags whose values that are required to change frequently as part of the normal operation, as these will simply flood your database with unnecessary records. Tip: If you want to analyse your audited data then, we recommend that you install the Adroit Report Suite and specifically the Audit Reports report pack, which provides you with the necessary tools you need to analyse both your

your audited data then, we recommend that you install the Adroit Report Suite and specifically the Audit Reports report pack, which provides you with the necessary tools you need to analyse both your Agent Server auditing and tag auditing, where Agent Server auditing includes any activities on the Agent Server, while the tag auditing is concerned specifically with data logged by any Audit agents. Each changed value is logged to the Activity table of the audit database, which records the following: The action i.e. Tag value change The process tag that is changed i.e. agentName.slotName The change in value i.e. oldValue to newValue Information common to all the other records, such as the date and time of this action, the Agent Server computer and the currently logged on username. The Backup Directory Structure when Overwrite is disabled Top The Backup Directory Structure when Overwrite is Disabled The specified backup path is the root path under which the folders containing the individual backups are stored. Each backup is contained within a folder, named by the date and time at which it was made. text: The Basics of the OLE Server Interface Top The Basics of the OLE Server Interface (MISSRVR) The Adroit OLE server objects leverage OLE infrastructure. This may seem daunting to an end user, but the use of OLE actually makes an end user’s life easier. When talking about objects, a whole litany of terminology tends to arise. In OLE, the coarse grained entities are typically referred to as objects and containers. The words of the great OLE architect, Tony Williams, define these best. He says: "There are things, and there are places to put things". The "things" are the objects. The "places" are containers. In our case, the "things" or objects are local or remote Agent Server(s), and the "places" or containers are shrink wrapped or custom applications, written using Visual Basic™, Delphi™, PowerBuilder™, or any other OLE-aware application development platform. WOSA/XRT forces us to address another piece of terminology: OLE Automation. Extending Tony’s quote, we can say: "There are things, places to put them, and ways to talk to them". The way we talk to a thing (object) is OLE Automation. OLE Automation is simply a way for software, structured as an OLE object, to expose internal functi

text: The Beeper Agent Top The Beeper Agent The Beeper agent provides simple audio output using the built-in PC loudspeaker and is usually controlled by an Alarm agent. The beeping sound is started when the value in the start slot is set to an integer greater than zero. The pitch or tone of the beeping sound depends on the contents of the start slot, and will become higher as it is incremented. The Alarm agent puts a value equal to the number of current unacknowledged alarms into this slot, to indicate that more than one agent is in alarm at the same time. Note: The pitch increases each time a new alarm is signaled, and decreases when an alarm is acknowledged. When the start slot is set to zero, or the reset slot is pulsed, the beeping sound will stop. The beeping sounds will become more urgent (i.e. interval between beeps will decrease) if the Beeper agent’s priority is increased from 0 to 4. This is a useful feature if you wish to route high priority alarms with high priority settings to one Beeper agent and low priority alarms with low priority settings to another Beeper agent. Normally, the contents of the start slot will not be saved to the loadfile (WGP file, by clicking the Save t

ne Beeper agent and low priority alarms with low priority settings to another Beeper agent. Normally, the contents of the start slot will not be saved to the loadfile (WGP file, by clicking the Save toolbar button or File menu item when the Configurator window is selected or when the Agent Server is Shutdown (if the SaveonExit advanced option is enabled). To save the contents of this slot, check the Store values when saving checkbox, which sets the dataPersist slot to 1. Beeper Agent - Slot Details . Beeper Agent - Database File Format . -->

The Command Agent Top The Command Agent The Command agent can send and receive SMS messages, by using a device of the GSM_SMS protocol driver to bypass the scanning subsystem with its imposed scanning limitation of 79 character strings, so that the full 160-character SMS message length can be used. Its name is derived from its ability to also receive commands within these textual messages, which can manage Adroit remotely. Note: The sole function of this new GSM_SMS driver is to send and receive SMS messages to and from a SMS GSM modem. For details, see About the GSM_SMS driver . For details, concerning the configuration and use of this agent, see Configuring Command Agents . This agent, unlike the Notify agent, provides the following functionality: Note: If necessary, this agent can be used to SMS alarms received by the Notify agent instead. For details, see Message Sending and Processing Slots . The ability to BOTH send and receive SMS messages of up to the full 160 character SMS message limit, instead of being restricted to only 79 characters. Send SMS messages to a single recipient, manually, programmatically or automatically to remotely monitor the status of important process

sage limit, instead of being restricted to only 79 characters. Send SMS messages to a single recipient, manually, programmatically or automatically to remotely monitor the status of important process values. For further details, see Sending SMS Messages . Sent SMS messages can also be monitored for auditing purposes. If they are not received and/or responded to within a specified period they can also be sent to another recipient via another Command agent, such as a colleague or even escalated up the management chain, if necessary. Receive SMS messages from the one or more cell phones and, if necessary, perform commands to remotely supervise and control your process and configure Adroit , for instance, by acknowledging alarms or fetching or setting process values etc. For details, see Allowing Commands to be Received or for details of the available commands that can be performed, see Available Commands . PLEASE NOTE: Once the Command agent is configured to receive commands, scan point licenses are consumed by every unique phone number that is able to send an SMS command to this Command agent i.e. by both the configured recipient phone number and any additional cell phone numbers tha

icenses are consumed by every unique phone number that is able to send an SMS command to this Command agent i.e. by both the configured recipient phone number and any additional cell phone numbers that are specified or used to send SMS messages to it. For details, see Specifying Additional Callers . This is in accordance with the generally adopted Adroit policy, where information is provided freely, but where you are obliged to pay for the service of manipulating information. Pseudonyms can also be used when specifying commands, to simplify the process of specifying commands by providing shorter aliases for the names of commonly referenced tag (agent.slot) names. In addition to this macros can also be used to provide shortened aliases for commonly used commands. For details, see Using Pseudonyms and Macros . Command Agent - Slot Details . Command Agent - Database File Format . Each of the 100 devices have a unique cell phone i.e. the ONLY way to identify which device is sending the SMS is from its cell phone number,, hence the need to create one Command agent per device. -->

The Configuration grid Top The Configuration grid The Configuration grid, consists of the following fields, which displays information about the Adroit configuration of the selected computer, as follows: Note: The grid provides the following standard configuration options . For instance any cell entries that are displayed in blue, in the grid, can be both edited or replaced . The first untitled field numbers the information items in the grid. Item: This field specifies the configuration item, which is being displayed. Setting: This field specifies the current configuration of the specified item. The following list describes what the listed Configuration Items refer to: Server type: This field, specifies the current type of Agent Server that is running on the selected computer, as follows: Type 0 - Cluster Server: In this case master or standby mode assignment is necessary and duplicate databases need to maintained on each. Type 1 - Cluster aware server: In this case Proxy agents are created if remote duplicate tags are found. Type 2 - Stand-alone server: In this case Proxy agents are not created if remote duplicate tags are found. Server name: This field specifies the configuration

eated if remote duplicate tags are found. Type 2 - Stand-alone server: In this case Proxy agents are not created if remote duplicate tags are found. Server name: This field specifies the configuration of the Agent Server name to be used when it starts up. This must be unique across the same network and when more than one Agent Server is being used within a project, ensure that the first 7 characters are unique. The Coordinate Agent Top The Coordinate Agent The Coordinate agent was created to work in conjunction with our GIS platform, which runs on top of the SmartUI. The agent lets users to configure the location, in terms of GPS coordinates, for any asset under their control and to store this information on the GIS platform. The latitude (lat_DD) and longitude (lng_DD) slots can be set permanently as a record of an asset in a permanent position. These slots can also be set dynamically via scanning to record and display the current location of a moving asset. Configuration Configuration of the Coordinate agent is via the dialog, as shown below. The dialog shows the static coordinates of Johannesburg as on the world map. Typically the coordinates of an asset would be scanned to contain the current location of the asset. The Geofence warning and alarm areas can be defined as either a circle or as a polygon. Click the Geofence type property then select Radius (circle) or Polygon from the drop-down list. When defining a polygon Geofence, you need to specify any number of points that defines the Geofence. Click the Geofence Warning Co-ords property options button ..., click the + button then e

wn list. When defining a polygon Geofence, you need to specify any number of points that defines the Geofence. Click the Geofence Warning Co-ords property options button ..., click the + button then enter the coordinates in the dialog. The example below shows four coordinates that define the boundaries of the polygon for the warning Geofence. When defining a circle Geofence, you need to specify only two items of information. Click the Geofence Warning Co-ords property options button ..., click the + button then enter the coordinates in the dialog. The first entry specifies the centre point of the circle and the second entry specifies the radius of the circle in metres. The example below shows the centre of the Geofence as -26,-28 with a radius of 1km (1000m) . The longitude of the second entry is disregarded and should always be 0. The Counter Agent Top The Counter Agent The Counter agent takes data from any Input Tag’s BOOLEAN slot and calculates the time spent On (1) and the time spent Off (0), counts the number of On and Off events, and totalises the On and Off time. There is a Counter Wizard to demonstrate its operation, which can be found in the Samples\Wizards folder under the Adroit system folder, typically C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit \Samples\Wizards. The alarm limits associated with these times, are indicated by its specific status bits . Note1: The Counter agent supports real-time catch-up . Note2: Use agent persistence files to prevent Counter agents from losing their statistical data, instead of saving the Agent database (.WGP) file frequently. For further details, see Agent Persistence Files . How to manually specify Total ON or OFF time : how to allow operators to manually specify the Total On Time (and/or Total Off Time) of a Counter agent. To configure a Counter agent . Counter Agent - Slot Details . Counter Agent - Database File Format . Note1: The Counter agent contains the offRunHours and onRunHours slots that convert the millisecond values of rawOffTotalTime and rawOnTotalT

nt - Slot Details . Counter Agent - Database File Format . Note1: The Counter agent contains the offRunHours and onRunHours slots that convert the millisecond values of rawOffTotalTime and rawOnTotalTime into hours. Note2: It is also possible to manually change the OnCount and OffCount slot values, if necessary e.g. by using Putslot.exe . -->

The DataLog Agent Top The DataLog Agent Note: Any datalogs that cause their .LGD file to be greater than 2 GB will fail to start and user is notified accordingly and an associated eventlog entry is also created. Adroit provides extensive historical logging facilities, this includes the existing proprietary data logging via the DataLog agent and the DBLog agent , which is a bulk OLE DB logging agent for typically logging Analog and/or Digital values to a specific table in a database for later retrieval. Note: If you export and delete Datalog agents that use Adroit 's proprietary log files, ensure that you restart the Agent Server before re-importing - so that they can remove the areas that they currently use in the LGD files. Click for more details: Multiple Datalog agents can potentially use a single LGD file, so when you delete a Datalog agent using proprietary logging all that happens is the area of the file that was used by the deleted Datalog agent is marked as unused and will be compacted at the next Agent Server startup. Therefore if you re-create the Datalog agent in the same Agent Server session, the LGD resource simply adds the space required for the newly added Datalog to

ompacted at the next Agent Server startup. Therefore if you re-create the Datalog agent in the same Agent Server session, the LGD resource simply adds the space required for the newly added Datalog to the end of the LGD file i.e. it does not re-use the old area that has been marked as unused. This can cause the LGD file to become too big, resulting in errors such as an error message asking you to check your Datalog agent configuration (in Agent Server window you may also get a Datalog agent dll exception) and your Datalog agents may not start. When you restart the Agent Server , the old areas of the LGD file are compacted and room is left to re-create the datalogs. IMPORTANT: When modifying and/or creating Datalog agents via an exported CSV file, leave the UID column empty. Note: Multiple log sets are no longer required as Adroit provides the DBLog agent that should make SQL logging via the Datalog agent redundant. Also you no longer need multiple proprietary sets with increasing periods and larger time deadbands, since Adroit provides a new datalog backup feature with full trend-retrieval support. As with scanning, any slot of any agent can be configured to have its values histori

ds and larger time deadbands, since Adroit provides a new datalog backup feature with full trend-retrieval support. As with scanning, any slot of any agent can be configured to have its values historically logged, providing that it is a Real , Integer , Boolean or 79 character String (this length excludes the mandatory zero terminator character). The agent is created by selecting the Log button in the Configurator dialog. When logged, the values are time stamped and are made available, via a DataLog agent, to any client. Examples of data log clients are historical trends, the extract utility, OLE-aware 3 rd party applications etc. Note: If an Agent Server, in HMI mode , is being used, then data logging is restricted to 24 consecutive hours. To Minimise the Risk of Datalog Corruption from a Power Failure . Advanced Datalog Configuration : global settings that affect the operation of the data logging sub system. Historical Data Management . Note: Backup (LGB) files can be created when logging to the Adroit proprietary datalog (.LGD) files so that this historical data can be retrieved by the datalogging system when needed. This can also create CSV files too, to make this historical da

gging to the Adroit proprietary datalog (.LGD) files so that this historical data can be retrieved by the datalogging system when needed. This can also create CSV files too, to make this historical data available to third party applications such as Microsoft Excel and formatted to create reports. For details, see Datalog backup and retrieval . Viewing logged data . Exporting logged data to a CSV file . DataLog Agent - Slot Details . DataLog Agent - Database File Format . -->

The Date Agent Top The Date Agent Date agents are particularly useful when used in conjunction with Extract , the historical log extraction utility, in which case slots of Date agents can be used to reference dates and times, instead of cumbersome command-line parameters. The Date agent holds in its slots the localTime , universal UTC stands for Coordinated Universal Time, which is a time standard that couples Greenwich Mean Time (GMT), which is based solely on the Earth's inconsistent rotation rate, with the highly accurate International Atomic Time (TAI). time, the time since 00h00 1st Jan 1970 as an integer (cTime) , and a breakdown of the local time into year , month , day , hour , minute , second and millisecond slots. The format slot governs the way in which the date and time are displayed in the asciiTime slot. Triggering the setTime slot causes the agent local time to be updated by the system clock. Any change to a slot (except the asciiTime slot) will cause all the slot values to be updated to their relevant values. Note: You should never externally manipulate the localtime slot of the Date agent from a mimic using an operator action. The localtime slot must be used for vi

to be updated to their relevant values. Note: You should never externally manipulate the localtime slot of the Date agent from a mimic using an operator action. The localtime slot must be used for viewing the time and the ucttime slot MUST be used for manipulating the datetime value. This is by design of the Date agent only. All other time slots in Adroit can be viewed and edited directly. The format argument consists of one or more codes , which are preceded by a percent sign (%). Note: An additional flag (#) may prefix any formatting code after its % symbol. Date Agent - Slot Details . Date Agent - Database File Format . -->

The DbAccess Agent Top The DbAccess Agent The DbAccess Agent provides a link between Adroit and various external databases such as Access, SQL Server, FoxPro and Oracle, by using OLE DB technology, supported by Microsoft. OLE DB connectivity means that Adroit can connect to any OLE DB provider, unlike ODBC that was only created to provide access to relational databases. The DbAccess Agent allows Adroit to share its information with 3rd party applications that use databases to store information. These 3rd party applications may be responsible for optimised control, reporting, MES, ERP or many other enterprise solutions. As each DbAccess agent is responsible for a transaction on a row in a database, it allows the user to specify how and where he wants the data to be stored which is ideal for reporting. Note: If a connection fails, due to network problems etc. the DbAccess agent will recover and continue transacting. The DbAccess agent allows the following transactions to be performed: new rows can be added to an existing table; existing rows can be updated with current information; specific rows or the entire table can be deleted and data can be retrieved from the table inserted into

The DbAccess Agent Top The DbAccess Agent The DbAccess Agent provides a link between Adroit and various external databases such as Access, SQL Server, FoxPro and Oracle, by using OLE DB technology, supported by Microsoft. OLE DB connectivity means that Adroit can connect to any OLE DB provider, unlike ODBC that was only created to provide access to relational databases. The DbAccess Agent allows Adroit to share its information with 3rd party applications that use databases to store information. The DBLog Agent Top The DBLog Agent This agent is a bulk OLE DB logging agent for typically logging Analog and/or Digital values to a specific table in a database for later retrieval. In other words, instead of logging each Analog and/or Digital value separately, you can simply specify a list of tags to log and either export/import this list from a CSV Comma Separated Value file containing data, which consists of a number of fields in one or more rows, in which the different fields (values) are typically separated by commas. file or browse in this list individually in the required DBLog agent. This agent also provides: a Logging method list box to select the required methods for specifying when and how the listed tags are logged. a String logging checkbox (the BOOLEAN strLog slot), which when enabled logs the tag values as Strings and not numeric values; this also allows you to log other string slots (this will log the first 79 characters). a Housekeeping section to specify how long, in days, that you want to store your logged tags. n days, that you want to store your logged tags. This depends upon the storage capacity you have available for your database and how useful this data becomes to you the older it gets. The DBQuery Agent Top The DBQuery Agent The DBQuery agent provides a robust and efficient methodology for asynchronously executing OLE DB transactions. The agent was created to supersede the DBAccess agent and consequently provides more powerful control by giving you direct access to the query to be executed. The agent is designed to perform SELECT transactions on a database easily and can be configured to perform any other SQL Query transaction using the custom query option. The agent can also be configured to run manually, triggered by a tag or run periodically. The agent can also be configured to execute stored procedures. Configuration Configuring the DBQuery agent Configuration of the DBQuery agent is processed via the dialog, as shown below. The agent dialog provides the ability to set several options: (See the Configuration slots option for more information.) Enable or disable the functionality of this particular agent. Disable transactions executed on the standby server. Select the trigger method to use and optionally also the trigger tag. Enter the execution interval value in seconds. Set the auto-reset runNow option. Enter the SQL Server connection string. Enter the requi

the trigger method to use and optionally also the trigger tag. Enter the execution interval value in seconds. Set the auto-reset runNow option. Enter the SQL Server connection string. Enter the required tag list. Enter the required Table name . Enter the WHERE clause containing tag names within an angled bracket (< >) pair. The agent automatically substitutes these tags into values first and then performs the following example SELECT statement transaction: SELECT f3,f4,f5,f6 FROM Table_1 WHERE (f1=12) AND (f2=13) Enter a custom query. Let’s have a look at a few Custom Query examples. If a SELECT query returns more than one record, the agent will use the first record only. Should you want to use the newest record from the result of a SELECT statement, you could use the example custom query as shown below: SELECT f3,f4,f5,f6 FROM Table_1 WHERE (f1=12) AND (f2=13) ORDER BY dt DESC Because Adroit only uses the first record returned, the example custom query could effectively be changed to: SELECT TOP 1 f3,f4,f5,f6 FROM Table_1 WHERE (f1=12) AND (f2=13) ORDER BY dt DESC NOTE: Should a custom SELECT query be used then the ‘SQL table name’, ‘WHERE clause’ and ‘Field’ column entries in th

: SELECT TOP 1 f3,f4,f5,f6 FROM Table_1 WHERE (f1=12) AND (f2=13) ORDER BY dt DESC NOTE: Should a custom SELECT query be used then the ‘SQL table name’, ‘WHERE clause’ and ‘Field’ column entries in the tag list will be ignored because you would add this information to the custom query. Custom SELECT queries will substitute the ‘Tagname’ entries in the tag list with values returned from the custom query, therefore it is important to ensure that the custom SELECT query requests the data in the order required by order of the ‘Tagname’ entries. Other Custom Query examples For the query below to work, the tag list should only contain only one entry specifying a tagname. SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM MyTable WHERE f1=12 The ‘Field’ name is disregarded. If more than one tag is specified the agent will assume failure with the above query. Delete records The query below will delete all records older than 1st Jan 2019. The query disregards the contents of the tag list in the dialog. DELETE FROM MyTable WHERE dt < “2019-01-01” Insert records The queries below will insert a new record to the table. The queries will disregard the contents of the tag list in the dialog. INSERT INTO MyTable (f1,

MyTable WHERE dt < “2019-01-01” Insert records The queries below will insert a new record to the table. The queries will disregard the contents of the tag list in the dialog. INSERT INTO MyTable (f1, f2, f3, f4, f5, f6) VALUES (1, 1, 123, 456 ,678, 901) or INSERT INTO MyTable (dt, f1, f2, f3, f4, f5, f6) VALUES (<systeminfo.currenttime>, 1, 1, <f1.value>,<f2.value>,<f3.value>,<f4.value>) Execute Query Automatically The query below can use f1.value tag as a trigger tag to automatically have the DBQuery agent execute every time the tag value changes SELECT date,timestart,timeend FROM shift_adv_sh1 WHERE idx=<f1.value> Running Stored Procedures The query below will execute the spHousekeeping stored procedure EXEC spHousekeeping The query below will execute the spCheckRecords stored procedure with parameters as may be required by the stored procedure EXEC spCheckRecords 1,5 For all SELECT queries or stored procedures which return data, these results will be substituted into the tags as specified in the tag list and also as governed by the corresponding field names. If the field names are not supplied by the result, as may happen with stored procedures, you can do one of the following:

cified in the tag list and also as governed by the corresponding field names. If the field names are not supplied by the result, as may happen with stored procedures, you can do one of the following: Simply apply the index number to use e.g. 0, 1 or 2. or Leave the field name empty for the tag entry, The agent will then attempt to use the row number (beginning with 0) of the tag entry as the field name. Agent Slots DBQuery Configuration slots The following slots are used for configuration and are saved to the WGP file. Slot name Slot type Slot description connection VARSTRING The OLE DB connection string | “global” can be selected to use the Agent Server’s audit connection string. customQuery VARSTRING An option for a valid SQL query statement to be performed on the database connection. If a custom query is specified, this will always be executed instead of the built-in SELECT query statement. disableOnStandby BOOLEAN When set to [1], the slot indicates that the transaction should not be executed on the standby server. enable BOOLEAN When set to [1] the slot is enabled to Start or alternatively, when set to [0] to disable the agent. interval INTEGER An optional number of seconds ma

be executed on the standby server. enable BOOLEAN When set to [1] the slot is enabled to Start or alternatively, when set to [0] to disable the agent. interval INTEGER An optional number of seconds may be entered that will determine the execution interval of the transaction. A value of [0] (default) disables this feature. method INTEGER Sets a trigger tag check value. You can set method value to one of the following: 0 – Execute the query when the trigger tag value goes to zero. 1 – Execute the query when the trigger tag value leaves zero. 2 – Execute the query when the trigger tag value changes. The default value is [1]. tableName STRING The name of the table that the built-in SELECT statement should use. This is available only if the custom query is not used. tagList LIST Sets the list of tag values to be retrieved by the built-in SELECT statement. This is available only if the custom query is not used. triggerTag TAGNAME The trigger tag to be used. Indicates the trigger tag used in conjunction with the trigger method. This is available for trigger methods only. pulseWidth INTEGER Edit this slot to set the pulse length of the Status slot: SuccessPulse [StatusBit18] . The pulse le

conjunction with the trigger method. This is available for trigger methods only. pulseWidth INTEGER Edit this slot to set the pulse length of the Status slot: SuccessPulse [StatusBit18] . The pulse length is set in milliseconds (ms). A value of [0] will disable the pulse. Note: Any value less than 5 ms will always cause a minimum pulse width of around 5 ms. The default value is [100] ms. whereClause VARSTRING Sets the WHERE clause that will be applied to the built-in SELECT statement. DBQuery Information slots The following slots are used for information only and are NOT saved to the WGP file. Slot name Slot type Slot description badTransactions INTEGER A slot value that is incremented after every unsuccessful transaction and denotes the number of bad transactions since starting the agent server. goodTransactions INTEGER A slot value that is incremented after every successful transaction and denotes the number of good transactions since starting the agent server. lastDuration INTEGER A slot value that represents the duration of time in milliseconds that the query took to execute the last transaction. lastError VARSTRING This slot captures the last OLE DB transaction error. Successf

slot value that represents the duration of time in milliseconds that the query took to execute the last transaction. lastError VARSTRING This slot captures the last OLE DB transaction error. Successful transactions will display “None”. lastErrorQuery VARSTRING This slot captures the SQL Query that caused the last OLE DB transaction error. This value is never cleared and is only valid if the FAILED status bit (StatusBit21 ) is currently set to on [1]. lastQuery VARSTRING This slot captures the last SQL Query that was executed. lastTime TIME This slot captures the last time a transaction was executed. resetRunNow BOOLEAN When set to ‘1’ this slot will cause the agent to automatically reset the runNow slot value to ‘0’ after a transaction has completed. The default value is set to enabled. This should be disabled when the agent communicates the runNow slot value directly to the PLC. runNow BOOLEAN When set to ‘1’ the agent will execute a transaction ONLY if the agent is enabled AND connected to the database. totalTransactions INTEGER This slot tallies the total number of transactions executed since the agent server was last started. DBQuery Runtime slots The following slots are used

cted to the database. totalTransactions INTEGER This slot tallies the total number of transactions executed since the agent server was last started. DBQuery Runtime slots The following slots are used for runtime operations and are NOT saved to the WGP file. Slot name Slot type Slot description catchupData RAWBYTES For internal use during real-time catch-up. DBQuery Status slots The following slots indicate the status of certain DBQuery agent functions. Status name Status description Connected Also known as StatusBit16 This slot is set to on [1], if the Agent is connected to the database as of the last transaction. If the agent is not enabled, the slot will always be set off [0]. The slot will be also be set to off [0] should the agent become disconnected from the database. However, this slot will automatically be set on [1] if the agent is enabled and the agent is able to reconnect to the database. Important: It is important to note that some transactions may take up to one minute to transact, if there is a problem with the connection. Disconnected Also known as StatusBit17 This slot is set to on [0], if the Agent is not connected to the database possibly due to a last transaction

ransact, if there is a problem with the connection. Disconnected Also known as StatusBit17 This slot is set to on [0], if the Agent is not connected to the database possibly due to a last transaction error or that the database is not available. Note: Be aware that if the agent is not enabled, this slot will always be set on [1]. Failed Also known as StatusBit21 This slot will be set on [1] if the last transaction failed. Will be reset immediately prior to a transaction being executed. FailPulse Also known as StatusBit19 A short pulse is generated on a transaction failure. This slot will be set on [1] for a very short period (approximately 100 ms) , if the last transaction failed. Succeeded Also known as StatusBit20 This slot will be set on [1] if the last transaction succeeded. Will be reset immediately prior to a transaction being executed. SuccessPulse Also known as StatusBit18 A short pulse is generated on a successful transaction. The default length of this pulse can configured using the pulseWidth configuration slot. This slot will be set on [1] for a very short period (approximately 100 ms or as set in the pulseWidth slot) , if the last transaction succeeded. -->

The Device Agent Top The Device Agent Device agents are used to manage the Adroit -specific communication settings of one or more tags (agent.slot) for a device that has already been added to an installed protocol driver. This device is typically a logical connection to a front-end device, with which it communicates. For further details concerning the role this agent plays in communicating values, see the Scanning Overview . For this reason, Device agents cannot simply be added to the Agent Server like other agents. Instead its associated ‘device’ must first be added to an installed protocol driver. For details, see About Protocol Drivers . Then it is only when this device, which appears in the Device list in the Tag scanning configuration dialog, is selected when scanning a tag (agent.slot), for the first time, that a Device agent with the same name is added to the Agent Server. For details, see Scanning Adroit tags . NASA, stands for New Adroit Scanning Architecture and describes a sub-class of protocol drivers that are specifically written to take advantage of the scanning improvements and enhancements provided by NASA, such as demand scanning and highly optimised scan tasks. Fo

ub-class of protocol drivers that are specifically written to take advantage of the scanning improvements and enhancements provided by NASA, such as demand scanning and highly optimised scan tasks. For more details, see Demand Scanning . The purpose of a Device agent is simply to manage the Adroit tags that have been scanned to it and their communication to and from its associated front-end device, as follows: The Device agent automatically creates Scan agents, which generally contain a manageable amount of tags that are scanned to contiguous addresses. Each Scan agent manages the scanning configuration of their assigned Adroit tags, such as their poll rate, deadband, timestamps etc. For details, see Configuring Device Agents . Note1: The Device agent also removes these Scan agents when Adroit tags are unscanned from it. Note2: Since Scan agents are created dynamically, it is not recommended to use their slots in other agents, such as Expression agents, since their names are not fixed. The Device agent also exposes the ‘device’ created in the Adroit Configuration Setup utility, through which the communication actually occurs to its front-end device. So it is able to stop and start

The Device agent also exposes the ‘device’ created in the Adroit Configuration Setup utility, through which the communication actually occurs to its front-end device. So it is able to stop and start the communication to and from this front-end device and configure its communication settings, if necessary. For details, see Configuring Device Agents . -->

The Digital Agent Top The Digital Agent A Digital agent stores a Boolean a value that only has two discrete states, 0 (FALSE) or 1 (TRUE). value that provides the following functionality: Monitoring the current state of this value and setting its On or Off status bits accordingly, which can be alarmed. User-configurable textual descriptions of its two states. Monitoring its value for changes, where any change in value causes the agent to log an event and set a Changed status bit, which can be alarmed. Recording the time this value changes, which is saved to the time slot of this agent. Inverting the Raw value (typically this is the value that is scanned from the front-end device). A cold start value initialization option when starting the Agent Server. A pulsed output option to specify a user-configurable delay to maintain its ON state. For details on how to configure some or all of this functionality for a Digital agent, see Configuring Digital Agents . Typically Digital agents should be used for Boolean process values stored in a front-end device that may need to be inverted first and/or which needs its states to be closely monitored and/or alarmed. If you ONLY want to store a Bo

be used for Boolean process values stored in a front-end device that may need to be inverted first and/or which needs its states to be closely monitored and/or alarmed. If you ONLY want to store a Boolean value then use the Boolean agent instead. Note: For those of you running a clustered Agent Server, this agent supports real-time catch-up so even if the master Agent Server fails, the standby will seamlessly continue with the current configuration settings. For details of the specific status bits of this agent that indicate the current state of this value and other agent-specific conditions that can be alarmed or directly displayed on a mimic to indicate when these conditions occur, see Specific Status Bits of the Digital Agent . For a description of how this agent can be used to create a half hour average of a process input, see To Create a Half Hour Average of a Process Input . For a description of all the slots (values) contained in this agent, see Digital Agent Slots . For a description of how this agent is saved in the Adroit database (.WGP) file, see Digital Agent Database File Format . -->

The DumpConfig Agent Top The DumpConfig agent The DumpConfig agent is used for reporting purposes only and is a special report that exists in the Adroit Pack of our Adroit Report Suite. The sole function of this agent is to periodically record a snapshot (or a dump, or a record) of the current configuration of certain agent types. The snapshot record is saved to specific tables in an OLE DB database that will allow reports to be generated. An example of its use is to report on agents in the context of their configuration at the time of the report, or it may be used to audit changes made to specific agents. Warning: You can only add ONE DumpConfig agent. This agent is located in the following file: T_DUMPCONFIG.DLL How it works When the agent is enabled, the agent will wait for one of three events to happen before performing a snapshot: The occurrence of the next hourly period. The very first period is synchronised to midnight, meaning that if you specify an hourly interval of 8, the first snapshot will occur at 08h00 or 16hoo or at 00h00, whichever occurs first. After that, the snapshot will occur every subsequent 8 hours. A manual snapshot can be requested via the dumpNow slot A n

rst snapshot will occur at 08h00 or 16hoo or at 00h00, whichever occurs first. After that, the snapshot will occur every subsequent 8 hours. A manual snapshot can be requested via the dumpNow slot A non-zero value trigger event of a selected trigger tag, when one is specified. Configuration Configuring this agent provides the following options: Select the agent types to be recorded. For each agent, you can specify CSV strings of specific and also which instances are to be recorded. By default, these entries are specified as [*] to indicate all slots and all instances are selected. Should you want to select only A1 and A2 agent instances, for example, then the entry would read A1, A2 Optionally enable snapshots for the alarming and scanning configurations. Set the hourly interval at which these snapshots should be recorded. Specify a trigger tag for snapshot recording. Enter the database connection string where these snapshot tables are to be created.
