The DumpConfig Agent Top The DumpConfig agent The DumpConfig agent is used for reporting purposes only and is a special report that exists in the Adroit Pack of our Adroit Report Suite. The sole function of this agent is to periodically record a snapshot (or a dump, or a record) of the current configuration of certain agent types. The snapshot record is saved to specific tables in an OLE DB database that will allow reports to be generated. An example of its use is to report on agents in the context of their configuration at the time of the report, or it may be used to audit changes made to specific agents. Warning: You can only add ONE DumpConfig agent. This agent is located in the following file: T_DUMPCONFIG.DLL How it works When the agent is enabled, the agent will wait for one of three events to happen before performing a snapshot: The occurrence of the next hourly period. The very first period is synchronised to midnight, meaning that if you specify an hourly interval of 8, the first snapshot will occur at 08h00 or 16hoo or at 00h00, whichever occurs first. After that, the snapshot will occur every subsequent 8 hours. A manual snapshot can be requested via the dumpNow slot A n

rst snapshot will occur at 08h00 or 16hoo or at 00h00, whichever occurs first. After that, the snapshot will occur every subsequent 8 hours. A manual snapshot can be requested via the dumpNow slot A non-zero value trigger event of a selected trigger tag, when one is specified. Set the hourly interval at which these snapshots should be recorded. Specify a trigger tag for snapshot recording. Enter the database connection string where these snapshot tables are to be created. Click on the options below to read more detailed information. text: The Effect of Using Shadowed Cluster Servers with Drivers Top Using Shadowed Cluster Servers with Drivers Note: Asynchronous or non-polling exception-based (telemetry) drivers are particularly affected by shadowed cluster servers. When a second cluster partner, is started, it will start in standby mode and then any Classic UIs configured to attach to this newly started server will display any tags that are linked to "telemetry" device(s) as being "greyed-out" or marked bad. This is by design, since Adroit has no way of knowing what which of these tags are healthy at startup because of the unsolicited nature of these telemetry drivers. Therefore Adroit errs on the side of caution and greys out all the tags, this also protects the shadow system from mismatched databases in the cluster. Note: Normally, this should only be a problem on the UI of an unmanned cluster node, which is configured to connect locally, since all other remote UIs should be tracking the master. When the clustered servers are both online and the standby is "bad" because it has been started up later than the master, try one of the following: Stop and restart the affected devices on the master server. Swap master an

Note: Events logged to this database CANNOT be viewed in the Event Log Viewer window. Typically, events include undesirable states, process values and the malfunction of control devices. Logged events are used to analyse process conditions over a specified period. Some of the types of events that can be logged by Adroit include: incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. The Expression Agent Top The Expression Agent The Expression agent can create powerful user-defined calculations. Note1: The Expression agent supports real-time catch-up . text: The Frame Agent Top The Frame Agent A Frame agent can store 32 character strings (in slots V01 to V32 ), each string having a length of up to 79 characters (this length excludes the mandatory zero terminator character). These character strings are indexed (from 1 to 32) and the current string being pointed to by the Index is duplicated in the Value field. By suitable indexing, the text string in the value slot can be made to change in a predetermined manner. For example, the Frame agent FRA01 has the four character strings cold , cool , warm and hot edited into its slots v01, v02, v03 and v04. If the value in FRA01.index slot is 4, then the character string hot will be duplicated in the FRA01.value slot. In this way, by subscribing to another agent’s integer slot type, the Frame agent can translate the subscribed value into an appropriate meaningful text message using its indexing Behaviour. Frame Agent - Slot Details . Frame Agent - Database File Format . -->

The ICMP Agent Top The ICMP or PING Agent The ICMP or PING agent uses the Internet Control Message Protocol to determine the existence of a remote device on the network. Any IP network device is able to send, receive and process ICMP messages. These messages are only used for troubleshooting network problems and not to transfer data. The most common use of the ICMP protocol is by the PING diagnostic utility. By continuously polling the specified remote IP address, this agent is therefore able to identify potential network problems as they occur by generating alarms when errors are obtained when attempting to contact the specified remote IP address and/or when the round trip time exceeds specified High and High-high times. This round trip time is the time that it takes to send an ICMP message to the remote IP address and to receive its reply. How to use the ICMP or PING agent to ensure the availability of a networked device Specific Status Bits of the ICMP Agent : this describes the status bits of this agent that can be used for diagnosing the existence of the specified remote device on the network. ICMP Agent - Slot Details ICMP Agent - Database File Format -->

The IOT Agent Top The IOT agent The term Internet of Things (IOT) is an abstract concept that refers to an ever-growing network of physical objects that use an Internet Protocol (IP) address for Internet communication between these objects and other Internet-enabled devices and systems. This implies connecting any device with an interface to the Internet and also possibly to each other. IOT is expected to offer advanced connectivity of devices, systems, and services that goes beyond machine-to-machine (M2M) communications and covers a variety of protocols, domains, and applications. The interconnection of these embedded devices (including smart objects), is expected to support automation in many technological fields. Creating a specific IOT Agent As an example, let’s create an IOT agent called 2KVAPUMP. All that is required is to first copy the default Adroit IOT agent x_iot.dll to a new file called t_2KVAPump.dll in the Adroit system folder, which is typically found at C:\Program Files (x86)\Adroit Technologies\Adroit . The newly copied agent type is then available to Adroit. A newly created IOT agent can represent any object containing multiple properties or slots. Currently, the

s (x86)\Adroit Technologies\Adroit . The newly copied agent type is then available to Adroit. A newly created IOT agent can represent any object containing multiple properties or slots. Currently, the IOT agent does not support real-time catch-up . Management slots By default, The IOT agent in itself does not contain any useful slots that are usable for end-user process purposes. It does, however, contain four management slots that may be used to build up the structure of the IOT agent after it has been created. Select the Agent Specific Slots option below to view more information. The xmlSlots slot When this agent is created, it only contains the management slots, one being the xmlSlots slot which is used to create and configure the user-defined slots. This agent does not have any default status slots. The structure of this agent is defined only once in XML stands for Extensible Markup Language, which defines a set of rules for encoding documents in a format that is both human-readable and machine-readable. format after the agent instance is created and saved in the Agent database (.WGP) file. Expression slot The IOT agent provides a multi-line expression engine to calculate the defined slot values and status bit conditions, which are saved in the expression slot. The expression engine is similar to the expression engine used by UDP-Based Protocol (UDT) agents for manipulating status slot values (See the “ Creating UDT Status Bit Expressions ” topic). However, the IOT agent lets users create multi-line expressions where each unique expression is used to drive a single IOT slot or a single status slot. See the following related topics How to use the IOT agent to define an object to externally define the structure of the object Configuration This agent does not possess any default status slots and is required to be configured externally. The IOT agent is basically not usable until it’s configuration is defined by using either the addSlot or the xmlSlots slot. Configuration of the agent slots is not currently supported by the agent dialog, however, you may import a XML slot definition file that defines the slots for any single IOT agent. ration of the agent slots is not currently supported by the agent dialog, however, you may import a XML slot definition file that defines the slots for any single IOT agent. It is typically called from an external source, for example, a browser or 3rd party application. Creating the structure of an object You should provide an appropriate name and then add the required IOT agent, which will enable the code that interfaces to the IOT device to identify it. As only this code knows the identification of the IOT device, it should use the addSlot OR xmlSlots slots of this agent to programmatically create the slots as required. Using the addSlot The format for this slot is as follows: slottypeidx,slotname[,slotdescription[,slotvalue]] Where: slottypeidx : is a slot type index as follows: 0 : boolean (1/0) 1 : integer (4 byte signed integer) 2 : real (8 byte float) 3 : string (79 characters) 4 : time 5 : tagname (67 chars) (see “Use of Tagname type slots” below) 10 : varstring (any number of characters) slotname : any valid slotname not exceeding 15 characters and not containing the characters $ @ , \ & % * ? slotdescription : any 79 character description describing the agent (object) ins

The slot description is any 79 character description that describes the purpose of this property. The slot type is one of the following (case sensitive) values: Boolean : a 1 or a 0 Integer : a 4 byte signed integer Real : an 8 byte floatString : 79 characters Time : Win32 64-bit FILETIME Type Name : 67 chars. For more details, see How to use Tagname type slots . The IOT Agent Top The IOT agent The term Internet of Things (IOT) is an abstract concept that refers to an ever-growing network of physical objects that use an Internet Protocol (IP) address for Internet communication between these objects and other Internet-enabled devices and systems. This implies connecting any device with an interface to the Internet and also possibly to each other. IOT is expected to offer advanced connectivity of devices, systems, and services that goes beyond machine-to-machine (M2M) communications and covers a variety of protocols, domains, and applications. The interconnection of these embedded devices (including smart objects), is expected to support automation in many technological fields. Creating a specific IOT Agent As an example, let’s create an IOT agent called 2KVAPUMP. All that is required is to first copy the default Adroit IOT agent x_iot.dll to a new file called t_2KVAPump.dll in the Adroit system folder, which is typically found at C:\Program Files (x86)\Adroit Technologies\Adroit . Expression slot The IOT agent provides a multi-line expression engine to calculate the defined slot values and status bit conditions, which are saved in the expression slot. The expression engine is similar to the expression engine used by UDP-Based Protocol (UDT) agents for manipulating status slot values (See the “ Creating UDT Status Bit Expressions ” topic). However, the IOT agent lets users create multi-line expressions where each unique expression is used to drive a single IOT slot or a single status slot. See the following related topics How to use the IOT agent to define an object to externally define the structure of the object Configuration This agent does not possess any default status slots and is required to be configured externally. The IOT agent is basically not usable until it’s configuration is defined by using either the addSlot or the xmlSlots slot. Configuration of the agent slots is not currently supported by the agent dialog, however, you may import a XML slot definition file that defines the slots for any single IOT agent. It is typically called from an external source, for example, a browser or 3rd party application. Creating the structure of an object You should provide an appropriate name and then add the required IOT agent, which will enable the code that interfaces to the IOT device to identify it. As only this code knows the identification of the IOT device, it should use the addSlot OR xmlSlots slots of this agent to programmatically create the slots as required. Using the addSlot The format for this slot is as follows: slottypeidx,slotname[,slotdescription[,slotvalue]] Where: slottypeidx : is a slot type index as follows: 0 : boolean (1/0) 1 : integer (4 byte signed integer) 2 : real (8 byte float) 3 : string (79 characters) 4 : time 5 : tagname (67 chars) (see “Use of Tagname type slots” below) 10 : varstring (any number of characters) slotname : any valid slotname not exceeding 15 characters and not containing the characters $ @ , \ & % * ? slotdescription : any 79 character description describing the agent (object) ins

characters) slotname : any valid slotname not exceeding 15 characters and not containing the characters $ @ , \ & % * ? slotdescription : any 79 character description describing the agent (object) instance slotvalue : any suitable slot value conforming to the slot type index above Using the xmlSLot This XML structure requires that you always specify: the name and description of the IOT agent in the <IOT> section. the name, description and values of each slot that you require in the <Slots> section, where: The slot name is any valid slot name not exceeding 15 characters and does not contain the characters $ @ , \ & % * ? The slot description is any 79 character description that describes the purpose of this property. The slot type is one of the following (case sensitive) values: Boolean : a 1 or a 0 Integer : a 4 byte signed integer Real : an 8 byte floatString : 79 characters Time : Win32 64-bit FILETIME Type Name : 67 chars. Expressions Once the slots have been defined, you create expressions to specify the value of one or more of the specified IOT agent slot and the required condition that needs to be met to enable each of the specified status bits by using the expression slot. The expression slot is a multi-line expression engine, where multiple expressions are separated by blank lines. For more information, see Creating IOT Expressions . Using Tagname Type Slots in an IOT Agent to subscribe to external tags Tagname type slots are used in an IOT agent when the IoT The Internet of Things (IoT) is the concept of connecting any device with an on and off switch to the Internet (and/or to each other). device needs to subscribe to external tags, such as systeminfo.second . When using Tagname type slots, there is a rule that must be applied: The Tagname slot must be immediately followed by the IOT agent slot that will ultimately contain the value of the specified tag. The Marshal Agent Top The Marshal Agent The Marshal agent is designed to replace the popular marshalling function of the Multistate agent, by gathering discreet binary data from its 16 bit rawvalue or value slot. By giving each of the individual bits the full functionality of a digital agent, the Marshal agent exceeds the former capabilities of a marshalled mode Multistate Agent. These bits can then be alarmed, pulsed, named, and the 1 and 0 states of each bit can be named (on/off, open/closed etc). Tip: You can implement and use the MarshalAlarmMode registry value, to specify the type of information reported in the description field for Marshal agent alarms. Only the ON state is reflected in the status bit header slots of the agent and therefore the alarming subsystem has been extended to allow the alarming of status bits that are ON or OFF. The rawvalue and value relationship can also be reversed i.e. mirrored. To address the individual properties of each bit in the Marshal agent, e.g. from a mimic, used the following convention: MarshalAgentName.BitName.slot , e.g. MSH1.Switch.Value - will address the Value slot of the Switch bit inside the MSH1 Marshal agent. The MaxDemand Agent Top The MaxDemand Agent What is maximum demand and why should you monitor it? . The MaxDemand agent predicts the maximum kVA demand for the current block period the interval over which your electricity provider monitors your maximum demand, which is typically 30 minutes. so you can create alarms if the predicted consumption exceeds a predefined limit. This enables you to control the electricity consumption during each block period and prevent your actual “maximum demand limit” from being exceeded. For details on how to use this agent to monitor your maximum demand, see Maximum Demand Quick Start . Usually, control entails turning off machines which do not affect the main production process or which are not essential. While the primary aim of this agent is to monitor your power usage, it can also automate the control of your electricity consumption. In other words you can use its MaxDemand status slot in a script or expression agent to perform the necessary remedial actions. The MaxDemand agent can also calculate your instantaneous power factor, which also has the potential to save you money. Note: For those of you running a clustered Agent Server, this agent sup

actions. The MaxDemand agent can also calculate your instantaneous power factor, which also has the potential to save you money. Note: For those of you running a clustered Agent Server, this agent supports real-time catch-up so even if the master Agent Server fails, the standby will seamlessly continue monitoring your maximum demand. Related topics: Configuring the MaxDemand agent : To explain the various configuration options. Specific Status Bits : To describe how you can use the provided status bits of this agent. How Maximum Demand is Calculated : To better understand this value and see how it is calculated. About Power Factor : To describe the cost implications of this value. This agent also provides the following additional slots: kVAOptimal , mdOverUnder and timeToMD . See MaxDemand Agent - Slot Details . -->

The OEE Agent Top The OEE Agent What is OEE? Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) is a measurement of how effectively a single piece of equipment, or a group of equipment, and even how an entire factory is being utilised. OEE is percentage determined by the cumulative impact of the following three factors: Availability : is the percentage of the actual running time of the monitored equipment and/or factory. So this factor is decreased by the activities that cause unplanned downtime. Performance : is the percentage of how often the monitored equipment and/or factory performs at optimum speed. So this factor is decreased by the all the factors preventing the equipment and/or factory from running at optimal speed. Quality : is the percentage of good quality items produced by the monitored equipment and/or factory. So this factor is decreased by the amount of produced waste or bad quality and scrapped items. OEE% = Availability% x Performance% x Quality% This OEE percentage takes into account all losses in downtime, speed and quality and can therefore be used for analysis and benchmarking. Why use the OEE agent? The OEE agent can : EITHER calculate the OEE for the monitored equipment

ount all losses in downtime, speed and quality and can therefore be used for analysis and benchmarking. Why use the OEE agent? The OEE agent can : EITHER calculate the OEE for the monitored equipment and/or plant. Since targeting the three key OEE factors simultaneously, can effect significant improvements in production. How to configure the OEE agent to calculate OEE OR measure a specific KPI Key Performance Indicator, a quantifiable measurement that measures how well something is accomplishing its goals and objectives. . In other words, individual OEE agents can be applied to any component or part of a process for which a variable denoting a measurement of output is available, as follows: Note: The number of OEE agents that you can add to your Agent Server is determined by the OEE Count parameter of your Adroit license. KPIs are typically the measurement of some production value over time OR one production value against (divided by) another production value. Therefore the OEE agent can measure TWO variables: the FIRST variable (the REAL input1 slot) the SECOND variable (the REAL input2 slot), used as a DIVISOR of the first (input1/input2). Note: If the SECOND variable is not spec

an measure TWO variables: the FIRST variable (the REAL input1 slot) the SECOND variable (the REAL input2 slot), used as a DIVISOR of the first (input1/input2). Note: If the SECOND variable is not specified, then the FIRST variable is simply divided by time. In this way it is possible to measure production figures, such as ton/hr, kWh/ton, total produced, actual run-hours, etc. The measured KPI can either compare actual performance with benchmark figures or compare shift performances or today’s performance with the previous day or the previous day's shifts. The PerfMon Agent Top The PerfMon Agent The Perfmon agent is used to monitor Windows Performance counters, which belong to performance objects such as the Agent Server, Processor, Memory, and others. These counters facilitate the monitoring of the computers performance and assist in detecting performance bottlenecks that could adversely affect the functioning of Adroit . The values of these counters are updated every second and can also be assigned to other tags, such as Analog agents, which can then be appropriately alarmed. Up to 16 performance counters can be monitored per agent. The following performance counters are added, by default, to first PerfMon agent created: CPU load i.e. \\Processor(_Total)\\% Processor Time Agent Server CPU load i.e. \\Process(as)\\% Processor Time Total memory used i.e. \\Memory\\Committed Bytes Agent Server memory usage i.e. \\Process(as)\\Private Bytes and \\Process(as)\\Virtual Bytes Agent Server put slots i.e. \\Agent Server(name (project))\\PutSlots Since Adroit is a 32 bit application, if you have installed a 64 bit operating system then when you run the default Performance Monitor (PERFMON.EXE) all the counters for Adroit will be missing, bec

s Since Adroit is a 32 bit application, if you have installed a 64 bit operating system then when you run the default Performance Monitor (PERFMON.EXE) all the counters for Adroit will be missing, because the 64 bit version of PERFMON is being run which can only load 64bit counter dlls! Therefore, in order to force Windows to load the 32 bit version of PERFMON, open the Command Prompt and specify the following statement: mmc /32 perfmon.msc To edit or configure a PerfMon agent . To Add a Performance Counter to the Grid . PerfMon Agent - Slot Details . PerfMon Agent - Database File Format . -->

The PID Agent Top The PID Agent The PID agent is a simply a faceplate agent for external PID controllers, encapsulating the 25 signals and tuning parameters associated with a PID within a single agent. These values can then be scanned to the outside world, via their raw slots. This provides great savings in the overall number of agents required in the configuration of a project that contains PID controllers. Configurable high and low operation limits are provided for the SP (set-point) and CV (control variable) slots, which will prevent these values from being set to potentially harmful values, when they are being manually configured. This agent also triggers alarm conditions based on configurable alarm limits that are indicated by the specific status bits . Added support for realtime catch-up To edit or configure a PID agent . Note1: This agent does not currently provide internal PID algorithm control. Note2: The PID agent supports real-time catch-up . Specific Status Bits . PID Agent - Slot Details . PID Agent - Database File Format . -->

The Primitive Agents Top The Primitive Agents The primitive agent types Boolean, Integer, Real and String are the simplest building blocks. Instances of these primitive agent types are used simply to hold a single value in the value slot. They do not contain any other slots or additional functionality such as inversion, pulsing, linearisation, etc, as found in the Digital, Analog and other agent types. PLEASE NOTE: These legacy agents do not support Alarming and other SCADA functionality, use Analog/Digital agents instead! These agents should ONLY be used where efficient use of memory is required. A Boolean agent will hold a Boolean value (0 or 1) An Integer agent will hold an integer number -2147483648 to +2147483647 (32 bits) Note: The specific status bits of the Integer agent will be set if its value is between 0 and 15. A Real agent will hold a double precision floating point number (64 bits) A String agent will hold a 79 character text string (this length excludes the mandatory zero terminator character). Due to the increasing need of customers for the Agent Server to support strings longer than 79 characters, the String agent now has a new slot called valueex that is able to

ro terminator character). Due to the increasing need of customers for the Agent Server to support strings longer than 79 characters, the String agent now has a new slot called valueex that is able to contain these longer strings. Usage examples for these longer strings include queries that are created dynamically and long descriptions. WARNING! This new "valueex" slot is NOT supported by the scanning subsystem because the scanning subsystem cannot handle strings larger than 80 characters in length. Note: This new valueex slot is now identical to the String slot type of Custom agents, which have always supported strings that are greater than 79 characters. The legacy "value" slot of the String agent will still remain and contain the first 79 characters of the "valueex" slot. Therefore the "valueex" slot will always be equal to the "value" slot its string length is less than 79 characters (excluding the zero terminator). Note: When editing the String agent, only the "valueex" slot can be configured, although the content of the "value" slot is also displayed. -->

The Project Explorer Top The Project Explorer The Adroit Project Explorer is a separate utility, which configures and manages both local and distributed Adroit projects. For details, see The Adroit Project Explorer Window . Note: When used within the Classic UI, this can be disabled using the Menu Security feature. Adroit -specific launching options . The Project Explorer provides access to one or more computers on a network. If these computers have Adroit installed on it then read and possibly write access may be gained to the following Adroit components on each computer: The Agent Server, its agent types and their agents. The configuration of Adroit on this computer. Note: This will only be possible if the Windows security configuration and the Adroit remote connection licenses permit such access. WARNING! If you wish to use this Project Explorer and your project has many (1000s) of analogs and other agent types, be aware that it will take a fairly long time to populate the lists in the grid and the tree windowpanes. This problem is further exacerbated when adding fields to the explorer lists which have a large number of slots or agents. -->

The Recipe Agent Top The Recipe Agent A Recipe agent consists of a master recipe and one or more control recipes. This can be used to defines how the control system is to process its raw materials to make the desired product and byproducts. Description of recipe agent . Note: Names used in the recipe agent e.g. to define recipes and batches, CANNOT contain the ‘%’ character. The Master Recipe consists of all the process variables or "ingredients" and the sequence in which they are to be downloaded. It is here that the procedure and associated tag names will be defined. Components of a Master Recipe . Editing the Master Recipe . Each Control Recipe will contain specific quantities and values for customizing the Master Recipe for a given production run, thus allowing a plant to produce variants of its base product; for example, differing colors of paint, different flavors of cola. For each master recipe, there may be one or more Control Recipes. Components of a Control Recipe . Creating the Control Recipes . Editing a Control Recipe . Order of Execution of a Step . Starting and Stopping a Control Recipe . Example of Master Recipe with two Control Recipes . Importing & Exporting Recip

the Control Recipes . Editing a Control Recipe . Order of Execution of a Step . Starting and Stopping a Control Recipe . Example of Master Recipe with two Control Recipes . Importing & Exporting Recipes . The Recipe Monitor. Recipe Agent - Slot Details . Recipe Agent - Database File Format . -->

The Scheduler Agent Top The Scheduler Agent The Scheduler agent can be used to define one or more periods of time during which its BOOLEAN output (value slot) will be enabled (set to slot to TRUE or 1); alternatively, it is also possible to manually set the output. Note: The Scheduler agent supports real-time catch-up . To edit or configure a Scheduler agent . To edit or configure a Scheduled Period of Time . Specific Status Bits . The Script Agent Top The Script Agent The Script agent provides a way for the user to execute complicated tasks such as batching, reporting or complex mathematical operations through a Visual basic script or Java script. IMPORTANT: If your Agent Server is running as a service and you create a script that needs access to protected network resources or that launch other Windows programs or perform any other function that requires a logged on user. Then ensure that the user profile that the Agent Server service uses to log onto the computer HAS the necessary rights to perform these functions. This should NOT be the default Local System account. See Configuring Agent Server Service User Profile. Note: This agent does not replace the expression agent , as the expression agent can execute simple calculations far more efficiently and faster than the Script agent. Each Script agent can be configured to have an associated list of module files that contain user-defined variables, functions and subroutines. The Script agent allows the user to interact with the Agent Server , in order to access and manipulate data within the Agent Server. A script is compiled after the Agent Server has started

ubroutines. The Script agent allows the user to interact with the Agent Server , in order to access and manipulate data within the Agent Server. A script is compiled after the Agent Server has started up or whenever the script agent is modified from within the Agent Configurator. The script agent executes a single subroutine, or "main" subroutine, in one of four different ways. For details, see Running the Main Subroutine . PLEASE NOTE: There is no way for the Agent Server to protect itself from badly written or buggy scripts and Adroit Technologies does not take responsibility for badly written or buggy scripts written by users. Users also have the ability to launch other applications, or manipulate other applications via OLE automation, for example to configure reports in Microsoft Excel or Microsoft Word. The Script agent may also be used as an alternative to using the Recipe agent and it can be used to perform simple scheduled tasks. Note1: If you are using scripts to obtain datetime tags such as systeminfo.currenttime – the time is now returned as a local time, therefore NO time CONVERSIONS are REQUIRED. Note2: An event is logged if a script is executed that contains compilati

me tags such as systeminfo.currenttime – the time is now returned as a local time, therefore NO time CONVERSIONS are REQUIRED. Note2: An event is logged if a script is executed that contains compilation errors, preventing it from being run. However, this event could result in the event log from being flooded, therefore ensure that the event log is closely monitored and that any buggy scripts are either fixed or disabled ASAP! The Script Engine Top The Script Engine When the Edit script button is pressed, when deriving a Custom agent , you need to choose the required scripting engine either Yes to use JavaScript or No to use VBScript. Then Adroit Script Editor is launched and the following applicable script components are added by default to this derived custom agent’s script: The slots of this derived agent are defined as constants, starting from 0 in the order in which they have been created. Script procedures are created for this derived Custom agent, which can either be left empty– to not provide a script engine for the derived custom agent or they can be coded to provide any additional functionality for this agent. Note: An event is logged if a script is executed that contains compilation errors, preventing it from being run. Since this event can FLOOD the event log PLEASE ensure that the event log is closely monitored and that any buggy scripts are either fixed or disabled ASAP! The Select Date to Exclude Dialog Top The Select Date to Exclude Dialog This is launched within the Scheduler agent to assist in choosing which dates need to be excluded from within the scheduled periods of time. Click the browse button next to the Dates to exclude edit box. In the Select date to exclude dialog: Either Click the arrow of the Date list box and use the supplied calendar to select the required Date, by using the < and > buttons to move to the required month of the required year and then clicking on the required date. Or click in the Date list box, over the required date digits to select them and type in the required unit. Note: Only numbers can be typed in and if the number that is entered is too great for the specified unit it will be disregarded Or click the Now button to select the current day’s date. Then click the OK button to accept the date or the Cancel button to exit. -->

text: The Shift Agent Top The Shift Agent Various agents in Adroit , such as OEE, require knowing the current shift number. Instead of configuring the shift pattern information into each instance of these agents, you can instead configure these shift patterns globally, in a Shift agent, for use by any interested agents. The value slot of the Shift agent should also be scanned, output enabled, to any PLCs that perform any shift end functions, such as resetting shift count accumulators. Tip: Multiple shift agents can define different shift patterns that may occur within a plant. The Shift agent continually monitors the current time and checks it against the configured shift pattern to determine the current shift number. If NO matching shift pattern is found, the shift value is set to 0. Configured shift patterns are selected using the following order of preference: In other words if one or more shift patterns have the current time configured, then the configuration of the shift pattern determines which is selected, in the following order: Special non-recurring dates, such as Voting Day 5 Apr 2011. Annually recurring holidays on a given day of the month, such as Christmas 25 Dec. Weekly rec

nes which is selected, in the following order: Special non-recurring dates, such as Voting Day 5 Apr 2011. Annually recurring holidays on a given day of the month, such as Christmas 25 Dec. Weekly recurring patterns on a given day of the week, such as Sundays. This agent supports real-time catch-up on a standby server from a master server. Configuring the Shift Agent : describes the required shift pattern configuration sequence and how to configure less than 6 shifts and provides configuration examples and other configuration options. Shift Agent - Specific Status Bits : to indicate when the current shift is at an end or the current shift configuration is invalid or when the OPTIONAL OLEDB connection string is invalid. Shift Agent - Slot Details . Shift Agent - Database File Format . -->

Examples of devices that can be monitored using SNMP include routers, switches, hubs, UPSs, printers, modems and computers. For details on how to use this agent to monitor and/or manage a network device, see Quick Start to Manage a Device (Computer) . IMPORTANT: NEVER run the Windows SNMP Trap (listener) service because it conflicts with the Adroit SNMP trap functionality! Note: This agent does NOT require the Windows SNMP Service to function, this service is ONLY required on each computer that this agent monitors. monitor this device: by writing the values of SNMP managed objects to one or more tag. This allows you to trend this data, such as bandwidth; alarm this data, such as when particular conditions arise like a device becoming unavailable and log this data, so you can analyze it for troubleshooting purposes

o trend this data, such as bandwidth; alarm this data, such as when particular conditions arise like a device becoming unavailable and log this data, so you can analyze it for troubleshooting purposes. control this device: by using tags to set the values of this data. The Statistical Agent Top The Statistical Agent Statistical Process Control and Acceptance Sampling are methods used to detect significant changes in the manufacturing process and to monitor the quality of manufactured items being produced in batches. The problem is to decide whether a batch should be accepted or rejected on the basis of a sample, which is randomly or otherwise, drawn from the batch. There are many ways to make a sample - whether at timed intervals or on triggered events. The Statistical agent provides the basic functionality for a user to build a statistical process control strategy using its built in data collection method and by linking the agent to other Adroit agents. Note1: The Statistical agent supports real-time catch-up . Note2: Use agent persistence files to prevent Statistical agents from losing their statistical data, instead of saving the Agent database (.WGP) file frequently. For further details, see Agent Persistence Files . PLEASE NOTE: When exporting Statistical agents, ensure that the Floating average enabled checkbox is UNCHECKED, then save the WGP file and export. After importing, re-enable this checkbox for the applicable Statistical agents. Th

tatistical agents, ensure that the Floating average enabled checkbox is UNCHECKED, then save the WGP file and export. After importing, re-enable this checkbox for the applicable Statistical agents. There is a Statistical agent Wizard to demonstrate its operation, which can be found in the Wizards folder under the Adroit system folder, typically C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit \Wizards. Data Specification Method . To configure the Statistical agent for streamed events . Specific Status Bits . To Create a Half Hour Average of a Process Input e.g. to be transferred to a database. The StringList Agent Top The StringList Agent The StringList agent provides a superset of functionality of the existing Frame agent . It can store a virtually unlimited number of ASCII character strings, each string has a maximum length of 79 characters. These strings are indexed by an integer number beginning at 1. Note: These strings can contain commas ",". The current string pointed to by the Index is duplicated in the Value field. It is also possible to specifying the error message that is displayed when an invalid index is used. Stringlist agents CAN be imported, if necessary. When importing, the import is committed directly to the Agent Server, so the user no longer needs to click the Update button, after clicking the Import button. Note: Once an import file name is specified, this file name is remembered for the remainder of the Agent Server session each time an application is started and stopped on a computer constitutes a single session of this program. . The System SystemInformation Page Top The System SystemInformation Page The System Information agent acts as an information center containing 5 tabbed pages of data slots that are global to the Agent Server. For details on how to access these pages of data, see Editing the SystemInformation Agent . Note: The actual slot names and NOT their literal descriptions are specified, for ease of reference, since you most likely will need to display one or more of these slots on mimics. Granularity or the Granularity period refers to the startGranularity slot of the SystemInformation agent, which is the time interval, in seconds, that this SystemInformation agent updates itself. By default, this is set to 1 second. Changes getSlots: This indicates the total number of getSlot operations that have been performed by the Agent Server, since startup. putSlots: This indicates the total number of putSlot operations that have been performed by the Agent Server, since startup. getSlotAverage: This indicates the average number of getSlot operations that have been performed within the Granularity period, hence if Granularity was set to 60 this would be the average number of getSlot operations that have

tes the average number of getSlot operations that have been performed within the Granularity period, hence if Granularity was set to 60 this would be the average number of getSlot operations that have been performed per minute by the Agent Server. Note: If this long integer, wraps, during this calculation this reported number will be inaccurate. Use the Performance Monitor counters if more accuracy is required. putSlotAverage: This indicates the average number of putSlot operations that have been performed within the Granularity period, hence if Granularity was set to 60 this would be the average number of putSlot operations that have been performed per minute by the Agent Server. The Tag-link Database Top The Tag-link Database Each WanClient application needs to create and maintain a tag link database. This database stores a list of WanServer(s) and tags whose values are to be fetched or sent to or from each of the Agent Servers residing on these WanServer computers and these database files are stored in the database-folder . The tag link database is typically (initially) created using the WanClient Configurator, which can be launched from the Open Configurator item of the WanClient File menu and is used to stores the following items: The communication settings of each remote (Wan)Server whose Agent Server contains tags that either need to be fetched or sent. The tag groups , these tag groups classify tag-links in terms of the type of communication that is required and are server-specific. For details on possible criteria to use for creating tag groups, see Criteria for Creating Tag Groups . The tag-links , specify the required local and the remote tag name, whose values are ‘linked’ and are tag group-specific. The local tag name, resides in the Agent Server on the WanClient computer, and typically received its value from the remote tag name UNLESS it is wi

ose values are ‘linked’ and are tag group-specific. The local tag name, resides in the Agent Server on the WanClient computer, and typically received its value from the remote tag name UNLESS it is within a control group, in which case it can set the value of the remote tag. The remote tag name, resides in the Agent Server on the WanServer computer, and typically supplies the value for the remote tag. Note: The data type of the local and the remote tag must be identical. The name of the file that stores the tag-link database for each WanServer is user-defined, typically when adding or editing the communication details of a WanServer. This file can be edited manually, in Excel or any other CSV file editor, for bulk configuration purposes. The onus is then upon the user to ensure that all the values entered into these files are correct. For details, see bulk configuration of tag groups and bulk configuration of tag links . -->

The Timer Agent Top The Timer Agent The Timer agent can perform several commonly used timing operations. This agent provides a Boolean value slot as an output, which is enabled (set to TRUE) and disabled (set to FALSE) by the agent, depending upon its current mode of operation. This slot can therefore be used as an enabling or disabling or scheduling tag for other agents. Note: Although the Timer agent does not provide a cold-start value, it does support real-time catch-up on a standby server from a master server, which means that if the master Agent Server fails, the timing operation will seamlessly continue. This agent can perform one of following three timing operations or modes: Example: to illustrate the action of the three timing operations. This is a trend of the value and start slots of three Timer agents, to indicate their timing actions. In this example: each Timer agent is named after its configured timing operation for the purposes of easy identification ONLY, you can name your Timer agents anything you like. all the delays and pulse widths are 3 seconds long. On timer: This mode can be used for the timing of specific events. The value slot is only enabled for the speci

your Timer agents anything you like. all the delays and pulse widths are 3 seconds long. On timer: This mode can be used for the timing of specific events. The value slot is only enabled for the specified period (pulse width). For details, see Configuring On Timers . Note: This, in effect, provides the same functionality as a pulsed digital. On delay timer: This mode can be used for the filtering out of specific events. The value slot is only enabled after the required period of delay has elapsed. For details, see Configuring On Delay Timers . Pulse generator: This mode can be used for generating free running square waves. The value slot is enabled for the duration of the required pulse width and then disabled for the required period of delay. The period of the generated pulse is the sum of the delay and pulse width times. For details, see Configuring Pulse Generators . Note: All the timing operations, with the exception of the Pulse generator , can be automatically reset. The status bits of this agent can show when the timer is running or has expired. Time Stamping Top Time Stamping Adroit achieves its accuracy by time stamping data at the point of creation whenever possible. Scanned values get their timestamp from the data packet returned by the front-end device, if the protocol driver is exception based and implements a time-stamping protocol. A time stamp may also be created in an agent when a user enters a value manually. The time is taken from the systemInformation agent, which in turns gets it from the system clock. The name of the operation which causes this is the putslot method, which as well as updating the value in the target slot (e.g. value ), also updates the agentTimeStamp slot. When the agent subsequently sends a subscription update to another agent, or picture element Behaviour, the same timestamp value is passed on. For example, if the Alarm agent receives a subscription update, it will route the timestamp it gets to whichever printers, event logs, alarm lists and beeper agents it has been configured with. Timestamps will propagate into the user interface, into mimics and ultimately into picture elements containing associated Behaviours. For this reason, it should be clear that tampering with the system clock i

ps will propagate into the user interface, into mimics and ultimately into picture elements containing associated Behaviours. For this reason, it should be clear that tampering with the system clock is NOT advised. In particular, setting the clock backwards (say from 10:00 to 09:00) will have the effect of freezing all mimic updates, datalogging and existing alarms, for a period of 1 hour, until the timestamping mechanism "catches up" with the new time. Note: Sites using the SystemInformation time for calculations should be especially careful. -->

Time Synchronization of an Adroit Cluster Top Time Synchronization It is essential that both the cluster Agent Servers and their clients have their system time synchronised, for clustering to work effectively. This is ALSO critical in a distributed Adroit installation (where there are multiple user interfaces and/or Agent Servers on different computers) that the system times of all of the computers are synchronised to a common source. Adroit will behave unpredictably on a system which system time is not synchronised with the computer it’s connecting to. Time synchronization is typically managed by the Windows Time service that is installed by the default installation of Windows XP and later operating systems. The following are symptoms of unsynchronised times: The User Interface does not seem to be updating with the most recent information. The Trend displays odd Behaviour: either the data seems to be inserted into the middle of the trend, or a strange unexplainable sudden change in the values being trended when pressing F5 to refresh the trend. The data logs of the two unsynchronised Agent Servers in a cluster seem to get corrupted (as a result of the data being inserted into the

metadata.title: Time Synchronization of an Adroit Cluster

text: e values being trended when pressing F5 to refresh the trend. The data logs of the two unsynchronised Agent Servers in a cluster seem to get corrupted (as a result of the data being inserted into the wrong place) after doing a Datalog catch-up with the SystemDatalog agent. This corruption is most notable in a trend. Agent Servers generate an event every minute if remotely connected Agent Servers have a time difference of more than two seconds. To indicate that there is a time synchronization issue. This feature does NOT affect Adroit clients (UIs) that connect to a remote Agent Server. In this case time synchronization issues are not reported. -->

Timer Agent - Slot Details Top Timer Agent - Slot Details The Timer Agent performs several commonly used timing operations, which previously could only be inefficiently accomplished by using expressions, recipes and scripts. This agent is located in the following file: T_TIMER.DLL Slots: Slot Name Type Function autoReset BOOLEAN If enabled (set to True) this will automatically reset the start slot, 100 milliseconds after the timer has expired. Not used if the freeRun slot is enabled. delayTime INTEGER The delay time (in ms) i.e. the time before the pulse (value slot) is switched on (set to TRUE). This must be left at zero if an "on timer" is configured. For details, see Configuring On Timers . freeRun BOOLEAN If enabled (set to True) this enables the "pulse generator" mode of operation. For details, see Configuring Pulse Generators . granularity INTEGER The granularity (in ms) determines how often the Timer agent monitors the time after the timer has started. If less than the duration of the timer, then the timeleft slot indicates the remaining time, in milliseconds, before this timer expires. The default value of 0, forces the granularity period to equal the required duration of t

of the timer, then the timeleft slot indicates the remaining time, in milliseconds, before this timer expires. The default value of 0, forces the granularity period to equal the required duration of the timer, so that this timeleft slot is never calculated. WARNING! The smaller the specified granularity, the greater the amount of work the Agent Server is required to perform in updating its clients with the timeleft slot value. Note: Although this granularity value is has a minimum of 100 ms, a minimum of 1000 ms is recommended as a "safe" value. inputTag TAGNAME This can automatically start the timer by subscribing to another tag in the Agent Server. Note1: If this tag is numeric, then the start slot is enabled (set to TRUE) when it’s value is non-zero. Note2: If this tag is a string, then the start slot is enabled when this string is not empty. pulseWidth INTEGER The pulse width (in ms) OR the time at which the pulse ( value slot) is switched on (set to TRUE). This must be left at zero if an "on delay timer" is configured. For details, see Configuring On Delay Timers . start BOOLEAN Starts and stops the timer. Note: When this slot is set to FALSE, the value slot is also set to FAL

o if an "on delay timer" is configured. For details, see Configuring On Delay Timers . start BOOLEAN Starts and stops the timer. Note: When this slot is set to FALSE, the value slot is also set to FALSE and the currently configured timer expires. timeLeft INTEGER If the granularity slot is set at 100 milliseconds or greater and is less than the required duration of the timer, then this slot displays the amount of time left in the timing cycle in milliseconds. value BOOLEAN The output of the timer. Note: This slot can be used to enable, disable or schedule other agents. Specific status bits: Note: These are of type BOOLEAN. Bit Number Name Function status bit 16 Running On if the timer is enabled i.e. the timer is operating. status bit 17 Expired On when the timer has terminated, the event which causes this to occur is timing operation-specific, as follows: The pulse width time expires, when configured as an on timer. For details, see Configuring On Timers . The delay time expires, when configured as an on delay timer. For details, see Configuring On Delay Timers . The timer is not running, when configured as a pulse generator. For details, see Configuring Pulse Generators . Methods

configured as an on delay timer. For details, see Configuring On Delay Timers . The timer is not running, when configured as a pulse generator. For details, see Configuring Pulse Generators . Methods of creation: Manual Agents created by default: None For a description of which of these slots are saved to the agent database file (.WGP), see: Timer Agent - Database File Format . -->

text: Title 21 CFR Part 11 Compliance Top Title 21 CFR Part 11 Compliance Title 21 CFR Part 11 (21 CFR 11) of the Code of Federal Regulations deals with the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) guidelines on electronic records and electronic signatures (ERES). This defines the criteria and circumstances under which electronic records and electronic signatures are considered to be trustworthy, reliable and equivalent to paper records by the FDA. In short, for those records that remain subject to part 11, need to adhere to the following requirements: the validation of computerised systems computer-generated time-stamped audit trails to ensure the trustworthiness and reliability of the records the need to provide investigators with reasonable and useful access to records during an inspection Furthermore, 21 CFR 11 also requires that the following controls and requirements be implemented: limiting system access to authorised individuals use of operational system checks use of authority checks use of device checks determination that persons who develop, maintain, or use electronic systems have the education, training, and experience to perform their assigned tasks establishment of

ty checks use of device checks determination that persons who develop, maintain, or use electronic systems have the education, training, and experience to perform their assigned tasks establishment of and adherence to written policies that hold individuals accountable for actions initiated under their electronic signatures appropriate controls over systems documentation -->

To Add or Edit an Alarm Type Top To Add or Edit an Alarm Type From the Edit Alarm Agent dialog, select the Types tab. The Types page is displayed. To add a new alarm type, click the Add button and enter the name, remembering that Alarm Types are case sensitive. To edit an existing alarm type, select it and click the Edit button to get a further dialog box. Hence, Route 2 of the defaultAlarmAgent routes to the same EventOutput(s) and EventLog(s) as will Route 2 of another alarm agent etc. Select an existing route number, by using the Select route number list box. The Routes dialog displays the following information: Route Numbers – specify as many routes as you require. However, the defaultAlarmAgent reserves Routes 0 and 1 for system alarms such as software faults and communication errors. Therefore, when configuring route destinations in the defaultAlarmAgent , the route number must begin at Route 2. When more alarm agents are created, Routes 0 and 1 are not reserved. Route Destinations – this is divided into: Alarm Route Destinations , which select the required Alarm Lists and Audio Devices for the selected route number, that only applies to this Alarm agent. Eventlog Route Destinations, which select the required Output Destination (EventOutput or Notify agents) and Event Logs for the selected route number. Note: Eventlog Route Destinations are GLOBAL settings that apply to ALL alarm agents. Hence, Route 2 of

Output Destination (EventOutput or Notify agents) and Event Logs for the selected route number. Note: Eventlog Route Destinations are GLOBAL settings that apply to ALL alarm agents. Hence, Route 2 of the defaultAlarmAgent routes to the same EventOutput(s) and EventLog(s) as will Route 2 of another alarm agent etc. Select an existing route number, by using the Select route number list box. To Configure Automatic Logon Top Configuring Automatic Logon IMPORTANT: If you are using Windows 7 or later, then please use the following method to configure automatic logon: To Configure Automatic Logon in Windows . If, for some reason, you’re not able to configure Windows to automatically logon by following the above method, please use this method: WARNING: Registry settings are recorded as ADVANCED information and should not be used unless you understand exactly how these will affect the operation of your Adroit installation, IF YOU HAVE ANY DOUBTS, PLEASE CONTACT Adroit SUPPORT, BEFORE CHANGING THE REGISTRY. PLEASE NOTE: When working on a 64 bit operating system, remember to add "\Wow6432Node" to the path of each registry setting after "\SOFTWARE", for instance: "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Adroit Technologies". If the following settings are correct the system will automatically log you on the next time that you boot. If the changes are bad, a message box will notify you, closing the box will invoke the standard logon procedure. From the Start menu, select Run …, type in REGEDIT and click OK Go to the section: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\WindowsNT\Current

ou, closing the box will invoke the standard logon procedure. From the Start menu, select Run …, type in REGEDIT and click OK Go to the section: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\WindowsNT\CurrentVersion\WinLogon . Select Add Value from the REGEDT32 Edit menu and enter the name of AutoAdminLogon with a data type of REG_SZ and a string value "1". Select Add Value again and enter the name DefaultPassword with a data type of REG_SZ and a string that is the password for your computer. Note: that you must use a password or the logon will not function. Ensure that the DefaultUserName and DefaultDomainName reflect the user name and domain or computer name that you want to use when you logon. You can change these values using the Edit String menu option. -->

To Configure Automatic Logon in Windows Top How To Automatically Logon To Windows Perform the following procedure to configure a user account to automatically log into Windows: Click on Start and then enter the following command in the search box: netplwiz and press the ENTER key. This will launch the Advanced User Accounts Control Panel applet. In the Users tab, uncheck the Users must enter a user name and password to use this computer checkbox. Click on the Apply button at the bottom of the User Accounts dialog. When the Automatically Log On dialog box appears, enter the user name you wish to automatically login to Window with and the associated account password twice. Example: Click OK and OK again in the User Accounts window to complete the process. From now on, when your computer starts up, Windows will log on automatically. -->

Clear: Configure this bit-mask field to specify

text: To Configure the SystemDatalog Agent for Datalog Catchup Top Configuring the SystemDatalog Agent for Datalog catch-up Datalog catch-up only applies to clustered Agent Servers and refers to the process of synchronizing, unsynchronised sections of logged data between the two Agent Server partners in the cluster. This involves fetching stored historical data from the datalog agents on the cluster partner and merging the data with the local datalog agents. Note: For performance reasons, the SystemDatalog agent ONLY provides the Time datalog catchup method, of catching up the data between two specified date/times. Select the systemDl SystemDataLog agent. For details, see To Select an Agent . Right click and select the Edit... menu item. This will display the Edit SystemDatalog Agent dialog. Click the Edit… button next to the catch-up Time to specify the required Time period . All of the data between the two specified times in the datalogs on one of the cluster partners is mirrored across to the datalog agents on the other cluster partner. Tip: Analyzing the data in a trend window to determine the required start and end time of a particular hole. Click the Update button to save these cha

To Edit or Configure a Counter Agent Top Configuring a Counter Agent Edit an agent of type: Counter . The Edit Counter Agent dialog box is displayed. Enable Counter agent persistence: This GLOBAL setting prevents the loss of the statistical values calculated by Counter agents. Use this method instead of saving the Agent database (.WGP) file frequently. WARNING! If there are large numbers of Counter agents, this setting can increase the CPU load of the Agent Server computer. For further details, see Agent Persistence Files . In the Input Tag box, enter the Input agent and slot. If the Input Tag field is left empty, the agent can use a value supplied from an Operator Action Behaviour linked to its inputValue slot, or directly using the Scheduler to run a PutSlot command, which inserts a new value into the inputValue slot. Trigger contains the triggering agent name and slot and the Triggered checkbox must be checked to permit external triggering. External triggering is used to update the On/Off time calculations regularly, if the Input Tag is changing at infrequent intervals, then triggering is required at faster intervals. If Trigger is blank, the agent defaults to using each togglin

text: To Edit or Configure a PerfMon Agent Top Configuring a PerfMon Agent The Perfmon agent . Since Adroit is a 32 bit application, if you have installed a 64 bit operating system then when you run the default Performance Monitor (PERFMON.EXE) all the counters for Adroit will be missing, because the 64 bit version of PERFMON is being run which can only load 64bit counter dlls! Therefore, in order to force Windows to load the 32 bit version of PERFMON, open the Command Prompt and specify the following statement: mmc /32 perfmon.msc Edit an agent of type: PerfMon . The Edit PerfMon Agent dialog box is displayed. Note: Due to the long names of these performance counters, it is possible to resize this edit dialog appropriately. This edit dialog will remember these settings when it is next opened. Use the grid to add, configure and remove the Performance counters. Counter: Use this field to specify a Performance counter, either type in this counter directly or click the Browse button, to launch the Browse Performance Count

Either type in this tag directly or click the Browse button, to launch the agent browser . For instance the total memory used i.e. \\Memory\\Committed Bytes could be sent to the value slot of an Analog agent, which could be alarmed if this value exceeded the physical memory of the computer. text: To Edit or Configure a PID Agent Top Configuring a PID Agent The PID agent is a simply a faceplate agent for external PID controllers, encapsulating the 25 signals and tuning parameters associated with a PID within a single agent. For details, see The PID agent . Edit an agent of type: PID . The Edit PID Agent dialog box is displayed. The PID agent’s data values can be broken down into 5 distinct groups with the following names and associated meanings: PID Signals: this contains the input to and the output from the PID and its desired SP (set-point). For both the PV (process value) and the CV (control variable) this defines their minimum and maximum engineering values and their corresponding minimum and maximum values that the raw value can attain in the front-end device in order to scale the raw values into engineering values using meaningful units of measurement. Since this may vary between device types, the user should ascertain the correct front-end device span is used for each value. The value of these PID signals, including the SP (the required set-point) can also be specified in engineering units, with their raw value equivalents being displayed. Both SP and PV will always s

metadata.title: To Edit or Configure a PID Agent

text: ue. The value of these PID signals, including the SP (the required set-point) can also be specified in engineering units, with their raw value equivalents being displayed. Both SP and PV will always share the SAME minimum and maximum Engineering and Raw values. The SP and CV values provide a Max limit and Min limit which specify their effective operation range. Note: Once these limits are set these values cannot be manually set above and below these limits. text: To Edit or Configure the Marshal Agent Top Configuring the Marshal Agent The Marshal agent . Edit an agent of type: Marshal . The Edit Marshal Agent dialog box is displayed. Configure each of the 16 component bits in the grid. . When using the grid, select the initial row, by selecting the required cell with a left mouse click. Once a row has been selected then all the values in that row, e.g. the toggled and checkbox values are immediately accessible. When moving between rows the row must first be selected before the contents of the cell(s) can be altered. Once a cell has been selected, it is possible to move through the grid using the arrow keys on the keyboard. PageUp and PageDown move the highlighted cell to the top and bottom of the current column, respectively. Each row of the grid represents a component bit, which has the functionality of a digital agent. Click Update All to save all the changes made to the Marshal agent. Click Update Current to only save the changes made to the currently selected row. Click Refresh to display the current state of the Marshal agent. Check Reverse Mapping to reverse the direction in which the individual bits for the digital agents are strippe

text: To Estimate the Disk Space Required for Data Logging Top To Estimate the Disk Space Required for Data Logging The user has no direct control over the speed at which the raw data log file will grow. Therefore, it is important to calculate the maximum space each agent may occupy, before the data log file wraps around and overwrites itself from the beginning. This figure can be compared to the actual free disk space available on the host computer. Two files are involved in storing historical data: the raw data log file (.LGD) and its index file (.LGI) which uses comparatively little space. Tip: If you use datalog backups, which create .LDB files, then you can extend the potential amount of logged data without creating larger log files. In this case, while the active log (LGD) file can remain small, the log backup (.LDB) files can store historical data for much longer time periods. For details, see Datalog backup and retrieval . The amount of disk space reserved for data logging is a function of the rate at which the tag is being logged i.e. the time between each sample and the total logging period specified for each tag, summed for all the tags being logged. Each log record takes 20 b

Each log record takes 20 bytes therefore it would be expected that the following formulae would be used to calculate the maximum raw disk space that may be used for each .LGD file: Raw Buffer size (bytes) = 20 x (Logging Period/Logging Rate) Raw File size (bytes) = Sum of all Raw Buffer sizes Example of raw disk space calculations . However, the original design of datalogging made the assumption that the data would only change 5 times slower than the rate actually configured and therefore Adroit is designed to only reserve 20% of the space calculated above. UNLESS a clean installation of Adroit is installed, in which case this logging factor is NOT applied. For details, see Adroit Logging Factor . Actual Buffer size (bytes) = [20 x (Logging Period/Logging Rate)]/

Actual Buffer size (bytes) = [20 x (Logging Period/Logging Rate)]/5 Actual File size (bytes) = Sum of all Buffer sizes While the above design assumption can be considered true for faster logging rates such as 1 second, this is definitely not the case for slower rates such as 1 minute or 1 hour where the values (especially analog values) will have definitely changed. In the latter Adroit will only have capacity to log for 1/5th of the configured period necessitating the user to over specify his logging period by a factor of 5. Note: It is possible to override this 20% data log capacity or the "divide by 5" storage factor, by setting the LogCompressionFactor registry setting. Each Datalog agent has a maximum of 53 million records, which can provide at least 30 days of logging at a log rate of 50 milliseconds! For instance: if the log rate is 100 ms, 10 values are logged per second, 36000 values/hour, 864000 values/day, so the total logging length of this datalog file = 53000000/864000 = 61.34 days. Two files are involved in storing historical data: the raw data log file (.LGD) and its index file (.LGI) which uses comparatively little space. Tip: If you use datalog backups, which create .LDB files, then you can extend the potential amount of logged data without creating larger log files. In this case, while the active log (LGD) file can remain small, the log backup (.LDB) files can store historical data for much longer time periods. For details, see Datalog backup and retrieval . The amount of disk space reserved for data logging is a function of the rate at which the tag is being logged i.e. the time between each sample and the total logging period specified for each tag, summed for all the tags being logged. Each log record takes 20 b

Type in as.exe followed by following commands and press ENTER: /install /u:"[Domain\]Username" /p:"Password" /quiet This command will install the Agent Server as a service. text: To Minimise the Risk of Datalog Corruption from a Power Failure Top To Minimise the Risk of Datalog Corruption from a Power Failure The following steps can be taken: Use only NTFS instead of FAT or FAT32 file partitions2. Remove "flush lazily" setting on Adroit Logging. The adverse side effect of this is that duty cycle on disk will be much more intense, as every change will be flushed right through to disk. In consequence disk may need replacing after several months/years (who knows). In addition system throughput may be reduced. Make sure a battery-backed UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) is installed so that power is never removed from the server in an uncontrolled fashion. This option allows "flush lazily" to be enabled. Note: This option provides the only cast iron guarantee, but most sites find option 1 sufficient. -->

metadata.title: To Minimise the Risk of Datalog Corruption from a Power Failure

text: To Remove the Shutdown Button Top Removing the Shutdown Button WARNING: Registry settings are recorded as ADVANCED information and should not be used unless you understand exactly how these will affect the operation of your Adroit installation, IF YOU HAVE ANY DOUBTS, PLEASE CONTACT Adroit SUPPORT, BEFORE CHANGING THE REGISTRY. PLEASE NOTE: When working on a 64 bit operating system, remember to add "\Wow6432Node" to the path of each registry setting after "\SOFTWARE", for instance: "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Adroit Technologies". From the Start menu, select Run… , type in REGEDIT and click OK. Go to the section: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\WinLogon Double click on the entry ShutdownWithoutLogon : REG_SZ : 1 and replace the string value "1" with "0". Toshiba : TOSHIBA Toshiba ASCII protocol driver Overview The TOSHIBA driver currently only supports the ascii-based protocol, the binary protocol is not supported in this driver. This driver supports the PROSEC T2 PLC, EX100 , EX500. Communication is RS-485. The ADROIT TOSHIBA driver will act as the master in a master-slave transaction system. See also: Toshiba binary driver and Toshiba Ethernet driver for T2. Device Configuration PLC Details PLC Station ID - Up to a maximum of 32 PLCs may be addressed. Local Details Port - The available serial ports on your machine. Baud rate - This is configurable. The TOSHIBA PROSEC T2 PLC supports the following baud rates : 300, 600, 1200, 2400, 4800, 9600 or 19200 bps. Select the appropriate baud rate from the dialogue’s drop-down list. Parity - This is configurable. Valid choices are None, Odd or Even. Printed 28-May-97 1 Protocol Driver Setup Manual Data bits - This is configurable. Valid choices are 7 or 8 bits. Stop bits - This is configurable. Valid choices are 1 or 2 bits. Retry - This is the number of times the ADROIT TOSHIBA driver will attempt a particular scan job before failing. Transaction Types of DbAccess Agents Top Transaction Types of DbAccess Agents The DbAccess agent can perform the following transactions: Insert row: Use this transaction to insert a new record of tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). /s into a table, hence a tag-to-field mapping is required. Row identification is not required for this transaction, as the new record is inserted at the end of the existing records in the table. Note: If the Disable on standby configuration setting is enabled, then when a cluster is accessing the same database, this setting prevents both nodes (Agent Servers) in a cluster from executing the transaction thereby causing double entries for "Insert" transactions. Update row: Use this transaction to update a row in a table with new tag/s, hence a tag-to-field mapping is required. Row identification is required for this transaction to take place. Delete row: Use this transaction to delete one or many rows from a table in a database. This is the only transaction that does not require a tag-to-field mapping. IMPORTANT: If the row identification field is left empty , then all of the rows in the table are removed and the entire table

his is the only transaction that does not require a tag-to-field mapping. IMPORTANT: If the row identification field is left empty , then all of the rows in the table are removed and the entire table is deleted . Retrieve row: Use this transaction to update tag/s with value/s from a row of a table in a database, hence a tag-to-field mapping is required. The DbAccess Agent has to know in what format date/time information is kept in the database to perform a successful translation. Note: This agent also supports the retrieval of time-stamped values from SQL into Adroit Filetime slot values. If the Disable on standby configuration setting is enabled, then the master Agent Server will perform the Retrieve transaction and shadow the result to the standby Agent Server tags. If this option is NOT enabled and client runtime transaction shadowing is also enabled, then any Retrieve transactions performed by this DbAccess agent will be performed by both cluster nodes (Agent Servers). For details on enabling client runtime transaction shadowing, see Cluster Server Options . -->

Translating graphic forms Top Translating graphic forms Translate each graphic form by using its own local translation table by using the Translation tool window, which provides a number of columns. For further details about the various columns provided by this window, see Translation tool window . When graphic forms are created the currently specified Graphic Form Language of the user profile of the user that created them becomes the primary or reference language of this graphic form used when importing other languages and CANNOT BE CHANGED. Any subsequent change to this user profile setting ONLY changes the preview language of the existing graphic forms (the language that used to display or preview the graphic form in the Designer). By default, this is the language of the Windows operating system. For details on how to configure this user profile setting, see Customizing the primary translation language of new graphic forms and the display language of new and existing graphic forms . This automatically adds any languages to the graphic form translation tables that are missing. For details, see Pushing translations to graphic forms . TrendConfigurator controls Top TrendConfigurator controls The TrendConfigurator control provides users the ability to configure and save trended values (pens) in a set, which they can then reload when they next logon. In this way, each user can customise the values trended using an associated LineChart control, according to their requirements. The following improvements have been made to the TrendConfigurator control: an optional inbuilt LineChart can be used; a new Adroit DataSource Mode is provided that allows you to directly browse, list and select Adroit data element names for each pen, without requiring the need for scripting, a database or Agent group to list Adroit data elements for pens; the list of set names in the Set Name drop-down list can be sorted in alphabetical order; Each pen provides advanced settings that affect how the series of this pen will be charted or how the vertical Y-Axis of the LineChart for the pen is displayed; the list of available pen (charted) values in the Pen drop-down list can be sorted in alphabetical order; the new Advanced Set Configuration dialog allows users to configure the display of the bottom (X) chart axis of each set; users can also c

n the Pen drop-down list can be sorted in alphabetical order; the new Advanced Set Configuration dialog allows users to configure the display of the bottom (X) chart axis of each set; users can also configure the chart axes of the associated LineChart at runtime and users can now export and import the configuration of all the sets in the currently logged on user’s profile to and from an XML file to bulk configure these.
