The Graph tabbed page displays a trend of the values of any tags that has been added to this trend, including a legend at the bottom of this page containing a list of the trended tags, each displayed in the colors used to represent their values, much like that displayed by the Tags tabbed page. For details, see Configuring Monitored Tags . Note: The tags that have been added to the Graph page are NOT saved when the utility is saved i.e. whenever the utility is started no tags will be added to this page. To add a tag to the Graph tabbed page: Ensure that the tag monitoring process is stopped i.e. the Stop button is clicked and is currently greyed out. text: Triggering spiders Top Triggering spiders Spiders need to be triggered so they can perform their functions. Spiders can be triggered using a variety of methods, choose the method that best suits your purpose: Silk triggering: The default triggering method, where each silk connected to the input of a spider can trigger this spider. In other words a silk will trigger its destination spider, after the output value of its source spider changes. Note: Certain spiders disable this triggering method by default. For instance, if spiderA is connected to spiderB, by silkA, then whenever the specified output value of spiderA changes, silkA will update spiderB’s input and then trigger spiderB to perform its operation. Note1: It is recommended to use silk triggering when transferring data between spiders instead of event triggering. Note2: It may be necessary to disable this default triggering of some or all of the silks connected to a spider, for instance, when using another means of triggering. For details, see Disabling silk triggering of spiders . Event triggering: This involves triggering the spider after a specific event or action is performed: by a spider, which has already been added to

or details, see Disabling silk triggering of spiders . Manual triggering: This involves immediately triggering the spider, by manually selecting its Trigger Now! menu item to simplify the process of testing spider functionality. This method of triggering allows a user to easily trigger any spider, as and when is necessary. For details, see Configuring spiders . details, see Configuring spiders . Spider triggering: The Trigger spider, allows users to tailor the triggering of their existing spiders to their own requirements. TroubleShooting an Intermittent Communication Problem Top TroubleShooting Driver Communication Failure Determine which request is causing the communication failure. If the driver fails once and then succeeds on the retry, then the fault lies within the PLC and that this is NOT an Adroit problem. But, if the retry also fails then either Adroit has a bug or has been incorrectly configured. Follow the steps below to trouble-shoot the location of the problem: Backup your database (WGP file) Unscan all the tags to that PLC. Save and restart the Agent Server. Gradually add the scanning back in (in very small groups) waiting about 30 seconds between each. Watch for errors, typically by using the Datascope screen of the Driver Monitor. When the problem occurs, you have the error somewhere in your last group of tags. Check that the scan-points, within the group that have just been added have actual addresses in the PLC. Sometimes due to a driver bug, if you read the last register/value in a memory block, the driver tries to read the (invalid) one after it. Verify that is not happening. Note: The above steps only apply if the problem is observed on the datascope as being repeatable, i.e. the

ory block, the driver tries to read the (invalid) one after it. Verify that is not happening. Note: The above steps only apply if the problem is observed on the datascope as being repeatable, i.e. the same driver request causing the same error. -->

Troubleshooting Clustered Agent Servers Top Troubleshooting Clustered Agent Servers Networking and security issues most often prevent Adroit clusters from working. Networking: Use the PING command to determine if your clustered Agent Server computers are networked correctly. For instance, in the command prompt, type the following: ping –l 64000 –t partnerServerComputerName If you have a low success rate (many packets being lost or a high round trip time), then your network is the problem, which requires input and action from your I.T. department. Security: Try to copy a file from the one agent server machine, across the network, to the other agent server machine. You should be able to achieve this without being prompted for authentication. If this fails, then your Windows security is not identical on the two machines and needs to be investigated. Other common problems: Different versions of the product on the two machines. To check this, open the Adroit File Version Information utility and ensure that the file versions of the installed files are identical on both computers. Firewalls blocking communication between the clustered Agent Server computers. To test this, isolate the syst

and ensure that the file versions of the installed files are identical on both computers. Firewalls blocking communication between the clustered Agent Server computers. To test this, isolate the system, then switch off the firewalls on both Agent Server computers. If communication is suddenly possible, you need to add the Agent Server process to the allowed programs on both firewalls. Inadequate licensing. Open the Adroit HASP License Reader and verify. All cluster information and operations including the historical synchronization can be viewed and managed within the UI by using the cluster-controlling graphic form. See the Active Cluster Control tab of the System Management graphic form in the System Information project. For more details on addressing the important issues that affect the operation and configuration of clustered Adroit Agent Servers, see Important Points to consider when Clustering Agent Servers . For more details on clustering Adroit Agent Servers, see Active Clusters Foundation . -->

Troubleshooting Continuous Writing Top Troubleshooting Continuous Writing The Scanning Monitor utility is designed to assist experienced users in fine-tuning the Adroit scanning subsystem to achieve optimal performance, by providing an intuitive report-like view of advanced diagnostic information. This utility is particularly useful in tuning polled driver's polling intervals. For details, see Using the Scanning Monitor . However, if after making changes to the scan rates configured for a polled device, you find no perceivable difference, then you may have a stuck continuous output. Since Adroit only sends controls or writes on change, it is possible that a rapidly changing output driven by some logic inside Adroit (example: systeminformation.second) can generate lots of control actions to a PLC. This flood of outputs will seriously affect all polling and is known as a stuck continuous output. Furthermore, since such a problem tag has to be an output, it will have the Output Enable status bit enabled, making it easier to find. To use the Scanning Monitor to locate a stuck continuous output: Launch the Scanning Monitor and connected it to the required Agent Server Select the require

tus bit enabled, making it easier to find. To use the Scanning Monitor to locate a stuck continuous output: Launch the Scanning Monitor and connected it to the required Agent Server Select the required device from topmost Device List . Select each entry in the middle Scan Job List , This will display the scanned tags within each of these jobs in the bottom Tag List . Observe the Output enable column of this tag list and investigate each of the tags that have this bit set within this device to locate the culprit. The tag configuration that causes these continuous outputs is often created quickly to test something and then forgotten about and not removed. Another common cause is when Adroit is used to time synchronise a PLC using a one-second interval, however, this is better achieved by using a 24-hourly digital pulse. -->

Trust Relationships Top Trust Relationships Trust Relationships in Windows specify the domains that this domain trusts, and the domains that are allowed to trust this domain. A trust relationship is a link between two domains, where one domain honors the users of another domain, trusting that other domain to authenticate the logons of its own users. When trust relationships are properly established between the domains of a network, they allow a user to have only one user account in one domain, yet to access the entire network. All the computers on the network can recognise the user account, requiring a user to log on and provide a password only once to access any computer on the network. Trust relationships move the convenience of centralised administration from the domain level to the network level. -->

Type List CSV File Format Top Type List CSV File Format This file is created when an Alarm agent is exported to store its alarm types that have been created. The filename adheres to the following naming convention: xxxxx-TYPLST.CSV, where xxxxx represents the name of this Alarm agent. The rows in this CSV file are sorted alphabetically and the alarm type name is used as an index, so that the first alarm type name has an index of 0. This file consists of the following columns, from left to right: Alarm type: The name for this alarm type, which MUST NOT be duplicated per agent-type. Agent type: The type of agent that this alarm type applies to. Bit-mask: A bit-mask of the relevant header bits that are set. This is the sum of all the bit-positions, which are calculated as 2 n , where n is a position from 16 through 31 of the agent status bit as the built-in status bits occupy the positions from 0 to 15. Value : If applicable, this contains the slot value that is shown with the alarm. For instance for Marshal agents this could be dig##.textValue. Alarm off-states: 0 is the normal alarming of bits in the mask, while 1 is the alarm off state. -->

Agent type: The type of agent that this alarm type applies to. Bit-mask: A bit-mask of the relevant header bits that are set. This is the sum of all the bit-positions, which are calculated as 2 n , where n is a position from 16 through 31 of the agent status bit as the built-in status bits occupy the positions from 0 to 15. Value : If applicable, this contains the slot value that is shown with the alarm. For instance for Marshal agents this could be dig##.textValue. Alarm off-states: 0 is the normal alarming of bits in the mask, while 1 is the alarm off state. -->

Set the sizeType property of the columns or rows containing the text (labels/textboxes) to Autosize Set the sizeType property of columns or rows containing their fields (edit boxes) to Percent and configure this percentage appropriately. Example: Proportionally distribute space on resize This means that when the graphic form is resized at runtime that its controls do not overlap one another, then configure your TableLayoutPanel control as follows: Ensure that the Autosize property of this TableLayoutPanel control is set to False . text: UDT Agent Type Designer Top UDT Agent Type Designer Certain new PLCs optimise their communication performance by consolidating multiple data values into a single User-Defined Type (UDT). Adroit provides the UDT Agent Type Designer to support this new functionality. This utility creates agent types (templates) that duplicate the structure of any UDTs used by your PLCs, by adding properties (basic data types) to them and if necessary to configure status slots for the purposes of alarming. Note : This only supports UDTs that are composed of data types that can be represented by Boolean, Integer, Real, Datetime, String (80 characters or less) and VarString values. Array data types are NOT supported. Since each defined UDT is a separate Adroit agent type, you can add more than one of each UDT to your Adroit installation, as is necessary. While this process of defining UDT agent types is similar to the process of creating custom agents, they differ from Custom agents, as follows: UDT agent types can ONLY contain data and do not provide any scripting intelligence and UDT agent types contain a "raw bytes" rawValue slot that communicates the ALL of its other SLOTS (the ENTIRE UDT) in ONE tr

ypes can ONLY contain data and do not provide any scripting intelligence and UDT agent types contain a "raw bytes" rawValue slot that communicates the ALL of its other SLOTS (the ENTIRE UDT) in ONE transaction. This accounts for the improved scanning performance of UDTs. PLEASE NOTE :Every instance (agent created) of an UDT agent type will consume (number of slots-1) scan points. The other scan point will be consumed if and when its rawValue slot is scanned. IMPORTANT : UDT agent types must exist on all Adroit computers that require access to the UDT agents from the Configurator. Once you have created one or more UDT agent types, you can import them to other computers. For details, see Importing UDT Agent Types . How to implement a UDT: Tip : If you have already created one or more UDT agent types on another Agent Server, you can simply import these into this utility. For details, see Importing UDT Agent Types . Stop your Agent Server. Launch the UDT Agent Type Designer and add and configure their properties (component data types) and, if necessary, to configure status slots for the purposes of alarming. For details, see Creating UDT agent types . Start your Agent Server. Create th

figure their properties (component data types) and, if necessary, to configure status slots for the purposes of alarming. For details, see Creating UDT agent types . Start your Agent Server. Create the necessary agents (instances) of each UDT type you have defined. Configure them, if necessary and scan them to their corresponding UDTs in the required PLCs. For details, see Configuring a UDT agent . IMPORTANT When you edit UDT agents you must also remove all existing agent instances of this UDT agent type from the Adroit agent database (.WGP) file! When you change the structure of a UDT agent (by using the UDT agent designer), then any UDT agents of that type that are already saved in a WGP file will prevent the WGP file from loading because their saved structures are now incorrect. Therefore when you change the structure of a UDT agent, you must remove all instances of this UDT agent type from the WGP file. For example if you have a UDT agent type called MOTORE, whose structure you have changed, then you need to: EITHER manually delete all agents of this MOTORE agent type. OR you can use the WGP Remove utility to do this for you and back up the original WGP file. Note: This utility

Note: This utility can be installed from the Additional Components install that provided on the Adroit 10 DVD or can be downloaded from the Adroit website. Understanding Protocols and Drivers Top Understanding Protocols and Drivers Protocols are essentially languages that are strictly adhered to and which accurately transfer information between any two devices. No one protocol works efficiently in every situation, since the following factors cause protocols to differ: The medium along which they are being communicated, for instance, microwaves, fiber optic cable or Ethernet. Which communication attribute has been optimised, for instance, speed, efficiency or timing. Adroit Protocol Drivers ensure that these protocols are adhered to by Adroit and by the devices with which Adroit is communicating. You typically need to install each protocol driver that one or more of your front-end devices use. Each Adroit protocol driver is supplied with documentation, which is installed to the Adroit system folder (typically: C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit ) when the driver is installed and provides a summary of the protocol, so that this ‘language’ can be learnt and adhered to. Having installed a protocol driver, you need to add a device added to an installed protocol driver to communicate using this protocol to a specific front-end devi

nguage’ can be learnt and adhered to. An essential tool, that deciphers and analyses these protocols, is the Datascope. Related topics: For details concerning the entire communication process, see the Scanning Overview . Understanding the NASA drivers and their new features Top Understanding the NASA drivers and their new features NASA stands for New Adroit Scanning Architecture and describes a sub-class of protocol drivers that are specifically written to take advantage of the scanning improvements and enhancements provided by NASA, such as demand scanning and highly optimised scan tasks. While many of these improvements are “under-the-hood”, this document aims to describe the new features that these NASA drivers provide and how they can benefit you. Note: The NASA driver DLLs are differentiated from the legacy drivers by being prefixed by a “d_” e.g. d_opcua_cl. Optimised scan tasks Typically when scanning process values to and from Adroit, the legacy drivers would create separate scan jobs for different: Agent types, such as: Analog, Digital, Integer, String, Marshal and Multistate and their Data type formats, such as: longs, words and dwords. This would therefore increase the total number of scan jobs and therefore the overhead required to communicate your process values. For this reason, less than optimum scan rates were typically attained. With NASA drivers, both different Agent types and dat

metadata.title: Understanding the NASA drivers and their new features

text: obs and therefore the overhead required to communicate your process values. For this reason, less than optimum scan rates were typically attained. With NASA drivers, both different Agent types and data type formats can co-exist within a single scan job, which ensures that the minimum number of separate transactions transmit the data to and from the front-end devices. This means that you will achieve improved throughput as the communication overhead is kept to an absolute minimum. Improved multi-channel performance Previously, only specific legacy drivers supported multi channels, such as Modbus EMC or Modbus Radio. All NASA drivers provide support for multi channels although this feature is off by default. When enabled, NASA drivers can support up to 8 channels, which are utilised as-needed to service the required transactions to achieve parallel communication on a single device. Dynamic configuration Legacy drivers would only attempt to reload the primary and secondary configuration from the registry during an outright fail of the device, once the maximum number of retries were exceeded. NASA drivers also reload the primary and secondary configuration from the registry when the de

metadata.title: Understanding the NASA drivers and their new features

text: rom the registry during an outright fail of the device, once the maximum number of retries were exceeded. NASA drivers also reload the primary and secondary configuration from the registry when the device is started and/or stopped to make it possible for online or runtime changes to running devices without needing to restart the Agent Server in order for these changes to take effect. Examples of possible runtime changes are adding additional debug information to the Datascope or to correct configuration errors like IP address typos etc. Improved Performance Monitoring NASA drivers provide support for up to 16 new counters that are common amongst all NASA drivers to facilitate their improved debugging and analysis. Demand Scanning Demand scanning is only supported by NASA This stands for New Adroit Scanning Architecture and describes a sub-class of protocol drivers that are specifically written to take advantage of the scanning improvements and enhancements provided by NASA, such as demand scanning and highly optimised scan tasks. drivers that are specifically written to support it, legacy drivers do not provide this feature. Process values (tags) configured to be demand scanned are

metadata.title: Understanding the NASA drivers and their new features

text: and scanning and highly optimised scan tasks. drivers that are specifically written to support it, legacy drivers do not provide this feature. Process values (tags) configured to be demand scanned are only communicated when they are being used (when there are one or more subscriptions or references to these tags). Note: In Adroit, a subscription to a process value essentially means that something else is using it. For instance if this process value is being: alarmed; actively logged; used by another Adroit agent or viewed by an operator. Therefore, demand scanning can reduce the number of process values that are communicated, which are especially useful in the following situations: when you are communicating process values over networks where there is an expense attached to the amount of data that is being transferred like a telemetry system using a GSM network or possibly satellite communications or as a means to improve the throughput (communication speeds) of a belabored network. But demand scanning can ONLY be used for any READ-ONLY process value that is typically ONLY displayed on a mimic (graphic form) or is used by any of its graphic form components like a Behaviour or spide

metadata.title: Understanding the NASA drivers and their new features

text: t demand scanning can ONLY be used for any READ-ONLY process value that is typically ONLY displayed on a mimic (graphic form) or is used by any of its graphic form components like a Behaviour or spider on the graphic form. In other words a process value that is NOT alarmed or logged or used by any other agent. Click for more details: In this case, when the graphic form is opened that contains or references this process value, then the NASA driver will become aware that this graphic form requires this process value and so it will communicate (scan) this value from its front-end device. When this graphic form is closed, then the NASA driver will become aware that this process value is no longer being used and so it will stop communicating (scanning) this value from its front-end device. Note: There is a fair amount of overhead involved for each demand scanned process value, since the NASA driver has to constantly query the Agent Server to determine when this process value is being used. Therefore due to this implicit overhead only configure process values to be demand scanned that will benefit from demand scanning, in other words, do not configure process values for demand scanning t

metadata.title: Understanding the NASA drivers and their new features

text: Therefore due to this implicit overhead only configure process values to be demand scanned that will benefit from demand scanning, in other words, do not configure process values for demand scanning that will NEVER make use of this mechanism (e.g. those that are logged or alarmed). WARNING: If you configure ALL your process values to be demand scanned then you could experience SLOWER system performance and not experience any other benefits since all the process values NOT used by ONLY one thing will ALWAYS be scanned anyway! Tip: You can determine which other agents are using (subscribed to) a tag, by opening the Agent Server Configurator and clicking the Used by… button. Usage scenarios NOT recommended for demand scanning: Demand scanning is NOT recommended for process values that are being alarmed or actively logged or used by another Adroit agent. Furthermore, any such tag configured for demand scanning could degrade the overall system performance due to the implicit overhead involved in constantly querying the Agent Server to determine when this process value is being used. Currently when a process value has the Output Enabled scanning setting configured then it is CONSTANTLY b

metadata.title: Understanding the NASA drivers and their new features

text: ed in constantly querying the Agent Server to determine when this process value is being used. Currently when a process value has the Output Enabled scanning setting configured then it is CONSTANTLY being scanned and therefore CANNOT be demand scanned. Demand scanning cannot be used as a strategy to “reuse” your scan points, since as explained above a scanned point license is not relinquished by a demand scanned tag when its tag is not being scanned, since the NASA driver has to constantly query the Agent Server to determine when this process value is being used. We do also NOT recommend the use of demand scanning for a clustered Agent Server that uses shadow scanning and a proxy server to handle requests for its tags from remote clients. Since this could return INCORRECT VALUEs. Therefore use the parallel clustering scanning strategy instead. Click for more details: Firstly, when a clustered pair of Agent Servers use shadow scanning, only the Master Agent Server performs the scanning and the Standby Agent Server does not. Secondly, when a client requests a tag from the proxy Agent Server, this proxy Agent Server it is UNABLE to specify which Agent Server partner it retrieves the r

metadata.title: Understanding the NASA drivers and their new features

text: and the Standby Agent Server does not. Secondly, when a client requests a tag from the proxy Agent Server, this proxy Agent Server it is UNABLE to specify which Agent Server partner it retrieves the requested tag from and only retrieves the tag from the first Agent Server in the list, as long as it is in a healthy state. Thirdly, demand scanning is the only type of scanning that requires at least one subscription to exist to the referenced tag before the tag is scanned. For this reason, if a remote client opens a mimic that has a demand scanned tag on it, it is possible for the proxy server to source the requested tag from the Standby Agent Server partner that is NOT being physically scanned (when its name is first in the list), which results in the WRONG VALUE being returned because: the Standby Agent Server is given the subscription to this demand scanned tag, but is unable to service this request because it is NOT performing any scanning and the Master Agent Server does NOT have a subscription to this demand scanned tag (since this subscription was made with the standby Agent Server) and so this tag will NOT be demand scanned! For this reason use parallel scanning instead, which

metadata.title: Understanding the NASA drivers and their new features

text: ubscription to this demand scanned tag (since this subscription was made with the standby Agent Server) and so this tag will NOT be demand scanned! For this reason use parallel scanning instead, which ensures that BOTH the Standby and Master Agent Server scan all the tags and so the value would be demand scanned regardless of which clustered partner is selected by the proxy Agent Server. -->

Demand scanning cannot be used as a strategy to “reuse” your scan points, since as explained above a scanned point license is not relinquished by a demand scanned tag when its tag is not being scanned, since the NASA driver has to constantly query the Agent Server to determine when this process value is being used. We do also NOT recommend the use of demand scanning for a clustered Agent Server that uses shadow scanning and a proxy server to handle requests for its tags from remote clients. Since this could return INCORRECT VALUEs. Therefore use the parallel clustering scanning strategy instead. Click for more details: Firstly, when a clustered pair of Agent Servers use shadow scanning, only the Master Agent Server performs the scanning and the Standby Agent Server does not. Secondly, when a client requests a tag from the proxy Agent Server, this proxy Agent Server it is UNABLE to specify which Agent Server partner it retrieves the r

text: and the Standby Agent Server does not. Secondly, when a client requests a tag from the proxy Agent Server, this proxy Agent Server it is UNABLE to specify which Agent Server partner it retrieves the requested tag from and only retrieves the tag from the first Agent Server in the list, as long as it is in a healthy state. Thirdly, demand scanning is the only type of scanning that requires at least one subscription to exist to the referenced tag before the tag is scanned. For this reason, if a remote client opens a mimic that has a demand scanned tag on it, it is possible for the proxy server to source the requested tag from the Standby Agent Server partner that is NOT being physically scanned (when its name is first in the list), which results in the WRONG VALUE being returned because: the Standby Agent Server is given the subscription to this demand scanned tag, but is unable to service this request because it is NOT performing any scanning and the Master Agent Server does NOT have a subscription to this demand scanned tag (since this subscription was made with the standby Agent Server) and so this tag will NOT be demand scanned! For this reason use parallel scanning instead, which

Unlocking datasources Top Unlocking datasources Once a datasource has been locked, no other user is able to modify this datasource. until it has been unlocked in the Enterprise Manager . For details, see Locking datasources . WARNING! If a user locks a datasource and then logs off, this datasource cannot be unlocked until its Server is restarted. Click for more details: Note1: Only users that have the necessary security permissions can do this. For details, see Securing datasources . Note2: Locked datasources can be identified by means of their red text in the Enterprise Manager . Note3: A locked datasource can either be unlocked by the same user who locked the datasource or by any user with global security access to this SmartUI Server (typically an Administrator). To unlock a datasource: Select the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager , as follows: Open the Enterprise Manager . Navigate to Servers > [Server Name] . Tip: The connection name is prefixed by the SmartUI Server computer name. If necessary, expand the Datasources category. Right-click the relevant datasource name or icon and select Unlock . This will changes the text color of this datasource in the Enterpr

er computer name. If necessary, expand the Datasources category. Right-click the relevant datasource name or icon and select Unlock . This will changes the text color of this datasource in the Enterprise Manager back to the default black color. -->

Update Queries Top Update queries Queries provide common tasks for managing your database that is connected to an OLE DB datasource. The Update Queries can update the values of specific fields within a table or view of a database. Click for more information: If necessary, limit this updating by defining criteria for fields which must be met before the table or view is updated. If you do not provide constraints on which records to update, you may update all the records in the specific table, which will take a long time if your table or view has a large number of records. Note1: Both the field and/or criteria values can specified by parameters. Note2: This query is ONLY able to update the records of a SINGLE table or view. Updating cached graphic forms Top Updating cached graphic forms By default, each SmartUI Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. caches the data that it requests from the SmartUI Server to improve its response time. For instance, if a graphic form that has been cached is opened by the Client, this graphic form is loaded from the local cache instead of retrieving it from the Server via the Internet/LAN so it opens quickly. Note: Use the (Caching) DataElementCachingEnabled setting to enable or disable this caching for a Client. By default, a cached graphic form will ONLY be loaded by the Client if it remains unchanged when it is opened again. In other words, no further design changes have been made to this graphic form that is stored on the Server. If you enable (set to ‘true’) the (Caching) DataElementCachingRetrieveRegardless setting, then the Client will ALWAYS load a cached graphic form from the local cache REGARDLESS of the subsequent changes that have been made to it, since the cache was last updated. This greatly improves the user experience but requires the additional administrative overhead of ensuring that t

of the subsequent changes that have been made to it, since the cache was last updated. This greatly improves the user experience but requires the additional administrative overhead of ensuring that the local cache is updated to include any changes made to the graphic forms of the project/s that it displays AND then copy this updated local cache to all the Operators that use this project/s. To save all graphic forms of a project to the local cache file: Open the Enterprise Manager . For details, see Accessing tool windows . If necessary, expand click the plus (+) box to the left of the current icon or name Servers . If necessary, expand the name of the required Server connection . Tip: The connection name is prefaced by the Server computer name. If necessary, expand the Projects category. Right click the project icon of the required name and select Update Local Cache . This updates the local cache with all the changes that have been made to the graphic forms of this project. The local cache data is located within the Caching sub-folder of the SmartUI l installation folder (typically C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit ) in the ‘CACHE’ and 'CACHEINDEX' files. Note: If you ne

cache data is located within the Caching sub-folder of the SmartUI l installation folder (typically C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit ) in the ‘CACHE’ and 'CACHEINDEX' files. Note: If you need to update more than one project then perform step 5 for each project to add these changed graphic forms to the cache. To copy the updated local cache to all the Operators that use its project/s: Either: manually copy the Caching sub folder of the SmartUI installation folder (typically C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit ) into the SmartUI Operator installation folder of each of your SmartUI Operator computers. Or: copy the updated Caching sub-folder into the Distribution folder with the other files required by the SmartUI Operator and then use the SmartUI Launcher (if supported) to distribute the SmartUI Operator (with the updated cache) to the necessary computers. -->

Updating datasources Top Updating datasources Due to the client-server model of SmartUI more than one user can modify the same datasource exposed by a SmartUI Server. Therefore you may need to "update" a datasource, which fetches any subsequent changes have been made to the datasource by other users from the SmartUI Server. Note1: Only users that have the necessary security permissions can do this. For details, see Securing datasources . Note2: You can also update all the datasources of a particular Server or for all the currently connected Servers. For details, see Updating connections . Note3: You can also lock a datasource to prevent other users from modifying it while you work on it. For details, see Locking datasources . To update a datasource: Select the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager , as follows: Open the Enterprise Manager . Navigate to Servers > [Server Name] . text: Usage Guidelines for DbAccess Agents Top Usage Guidelines for DbAccess Agents Note: All DbAccess Agents require a scan point license to run. This license is checked prior to actually doing a DbAccess transaction for the first time (on a per agent basis) and is only returned when the agent is deleted. For details of licensing, see Adroit Licensing . This is an alternative method to datalog agents by sending slow moving production and batch data values from the AS to OLE DB Servers. Whereas one datalog agent is required per value that is logged to an OLE DB Server, the DbAccess agent can transfer multiple tags in a single transaction and is therefore a more efficient mechanism. The DbAccess agents have the added functionality of retrieving data from OLE DB Servers. This is not intended for high speed logging i.e. data that changes within a minute. Instead, it is ideally suited to applications where data is periodically written to a database (such as at the end of a batch job or shift) for reporting reasons. These agents require careful consideration in terms of both the number of agents to be used and the amount of work that they are to do, as they are resource "hungry". Hence, both

The CPU usage should be monitored while during operation to ensure that the computer is able to handle the additional load. User Defined Protocol Driver: UserDrv User Defined Protocol: protocol driver Overview The UserDrv protocol driver for Adroit is a generic paging and text device driver. Messages configured in String or Notifier Agents may be sent via an encoder or modem to paging devices. Alarms that occur in Adroit can thus be routed to automatically page a person. This driver is intended for easy use with many varied text protocols, while allowing advanced users to configure custom protocols of their own. No windows drivers for a modem (is used) are needed, this driver provides it’s own interface and control over the modem via the serial port or IP address assigned to it. User Rights Policy Top User Rights Policy The Windows User Rights policy manages the rights granted to groups and user accounts. A right authorises a user to perform certain actions on the system. A user who logs on to an account to which the appropriate rights have been granted can carry out the corresponding actions. When a user does not have appropriate rights, Windows blocks attempts to carry out those actions. Rights apply to the system as a whole and are different from permissions, which apply to specific objects. The rights granted to a group are provided to the members of that group. In most situations, the easiest way to provide rights to a user is to add that user’s account to one of the built-in groups that already possesses the needed rights, rather than by administrating the User Rights policy. -->

text: Using Analog Agent Alarm Limits Top Using Analog Agent Alarm Limits The Analog agent provides extensive monitoring and alarming of its engineering value (the value slot), by providing low-low, low, high, high-high and/or rate of change alarm limits, which when reached set the relevant specific status bit, which can be alarmed. You can use these alarm limits and their deadbands, where applicable to monitor a process value, as follows: Using alarm limits and their deadbands: The Low (the lo slot) and High (the hi slot) inner alarm limits are the first warning that a process value has moved outside its acceptable range, and implies that corrective action must be taken as soon as possible. The Low-low (the loLo slot) and High-high (the hiHi slot) outer alarms are the second warning that the process value has moved further from its acceptable range and reached the second alarm limit. This implies that the first warning has been ignored and urgent and immediate corrective action is now required. Note: That whenever the Low-low alarm is on, the Low must by definition already be on. Similarly, whenever the High-high limit is reached, the High limit will already have been passed. The alarm

red. Note: That whenever the Low-low alarm is on, the Low must by definition already be on. Similarly, whenever the High-high limit is reached, the High limit will already have been passed. The alarm will become inactive (be cleared) once the process value goes past the limit AND through its deadband, if configured. Click here for an illustration: Using the Rate of Change alarm limit: The Rate of Change status bit is set when the difference between any two consecutive engineering values in ONE second exceeds the defined Rate-of-Change limit. Click here for an illustration: In other words, if this is set to 100, the default value, then if the engineering value (the value slot) of this Analog agent changes from 1 to 101 in 1 second then the Rate of Change status bit is set. But if the engineering value takes 2 seconds to change from 1 to 101 then the effective rate of change is (100/2 =) 50 so the Rate of Change status bit is NOT set. This rate of change measurement is independent of the condition of the low-low, low, high and high-high limits. The value change could be the result of a scan (from the front-end device), operator action or an output from another agent. -->

This implies that the first warning has been ignored and urgent and immediate corrective action is now required. Note: That whenever the Low-low alarm is on, the Low must by definition already be on. Similarly, whenever the High-high limit is reached, the High limit will already have been passed. The alarm

The alarm will become inactive (be cleared) once the process value goes past the limit AND through its deadband, if configured. Click here for an illustration: Using the Rate of Change alarm limit: The Rate of Change status bit is set when the difference between any two consecutive engineering values in ONE second exceeds the defined Rate-of-Change limit. Click here for an illustration: In other words, if this is set to 100, the default value, then if the engineering value (the value slot) of this Analog agent changes from 1 to 101 in 1 second then the Rate of Change status bit is set. But if the engineering value takes 2 seconds to change from 1 to 101 then the effective rate of change is (100/2 =) 50 so the Rate of Change status bit is NOT set. This rate of change measurement is independent of the condition of the low-low, low, high and high-high limits. The value change could be the result of a scan (from the front-end device), operator action or an output from another agent. -->

Using Pseudonyms and Macros Top Using Pseudonyms and Macros Pseudonyms and macros can be created to simply the process of specifying these commands by acting as placeholders for part or all of a textual command that is sent to a Command agent . Therefore they only need to be created for Command agents that have been enabled to receive commands. For details, see Allowing Commands to be Performed . Before pseudonyms and macros can be used in messages, it is necessary to alert the Command agent to their possible existence in its received messages, so that they can be correctly interpreted. For details, see Enabling Pseudonyms and Macros . Note1: Pseudonyms and macros are specific to the Command agent in which they are defined and are not global to all Command agents. However when a Command agent is copied, any defined macros and pseudonyms will also be duplicated. For details, see Copying Agents . Note2: Pseudonyms and macros can also be used to further restrict or limit the SET-table tags / commands that can be performed by this Command agent. For details, see Limiting SET Commands . A pseudonym is simply an abbreviation or alias for a tag (agent.slot), which once defined can be used

s / commands that can be performed by this Command agent. For details, see Limiting SET Commands . A pseudonym is simply an abbreviation or alias for a tag (agent.slot), which once defined can be used to represent this tag in commands that are sent to this Command agent. For details, see Creating Pseudonyms . Note: Although pseudonyms can reduce the typing required to specify commands, they need to be defined for this Command agent before they can be used. A macro is simply an abbreviation or alias for an ENTIRE command, which once defined can be used when issuing this command to this Command agent. For details, see Creating Macros or for details of the available commands that can be performed, see Available Commands . Note: Although macros can provide the most intuitive and the shortest command names, they are also the MOST restrictive, since this entire command must be pre-configured in this Command agent, before it can be used. It is also possible to remove any pseudonyms and/or macros that are no longer required. For details, see Removing Pseudonyms and Macros . -->

Using SQL Queries within Identify Row Top Using SQL Queries within Identify Row For each of the update, delete and retrieve transactions; a row in a table has to be identified, by entering the required identification text into the edit box of Identify row . In most cases, specifying the cell in the required field can uniquely identify the row. The required identification text in Identify row for this case is: FieldName = ‘CellInFieldName’ If more than one field is required to identify a row uniquely, then the row is identified using the "OR" or "AND" SQL keywords. The required identification text in Identify row for this case is: FieldName = ‘CellInField1Name’ AND Field2Name = ‘CellInField2Name’ OR Field3Name = ‘CellInField3Name’ In order to reduce the number of DbAccess Agents required to select each row in the selected table, it is possible to substitute the value of the cell in the field with a StringList agent. This StringList agent will then hold various strings, so that a different row can be selected, by manipulating its index value. The required identification text in Identify row for this case is: FieldName = <StringListAgent.value> Note1: Ensure that the value of the tag

text: Using Tagname Type Slots in an IOT Agent Top Using Tagname Type Slots in an IOT Agent Tagname type slots are used in an IOT agent when the IoT The Internet of Things (IoT) is the concept of connecting any device with an on and off switch to the Internet (and/or to each other). device needs to subscribe to external tags, such as systeminfo.second . When using Tagname type slots, there is a rule that must be applied: The Tagname slot must be immediately followed by the IOT agent slot that will ultimately contain the value of the specified tag. If the Tagname slot contains a valid tag name, the IOT agent will automatically subscribe to the specified agent and will place any values received for this tag into the next slot. For example, to subscribe to systeminfo.second then the XML stands for Extensible Markup Language, which defines a set of rules for encoding documents in a format that is both human-readable and machine-readable. slot value would look something like this: <IOT Name=" SecsInMinute " Description=" The second time value "> <Slots> <Slot Name=" source " Description=" Source of value " Type=" Tagname "> systeminfo.second </Slot> <Slot Name=" value " Description=" Seconds

metadata.title: Using Tagname Type Slots in an IOT Agent

text: sInMinute " Description=" The second time value "> <Slots> <Slot Name=" source " Description=" Source of value " Type=" Tagname "> systeminfo.second </Slot> <Slot Name=" value " Description=" Seconds " Type=" Integer "> 0 </Slot> </Slots> <HeaderSlots> </HeaderSlots> </IOT> In the above sample, the Slot Name “ source ” defines the tag to which we want to subscribe. the Slot Name “ value ” defines the slot where the subscribed tag value will be stored. Important: The slot names "source" and "value" used in the example above are merely placeholders to make this example clearer, you may use any names you choose. -->

text: Using the Agent Browser Top Using the Agent Browser The Agent Browser is a utility that allows one to browse the agents and slots of an Agent Server. This displays the status slot names and tag (agent.slot) values besides the slot type, description of the currently selected agent and slot. Launching the Agent Browser . For details on connecting this utility to the required Agent Server, see Connecting to the required Agent Server . Browsed agents and, if necessary, their slots are dynamically copied to the clipboard, so that it can be immediately pasted into any edit field in an Adroit user interface (or 3rd party application) that requires an agent (or agent.slot) entry. To select an agent and slot using the Agent Browser If the utility is launched with the /admin command line option, tag values can be modified and agents can be added or removed . To modify the value of a slot using the Agent Browser Adding or Removing Agents Using the Agent Browser This utility contains the following additional configuration checkbox options: Stay on top , which keeps the dialog on top of all other open windows. Include header slots , which lists all the status slots of the selected agent. Paste

additional configuration checkbox options: Stay on top , which keeps the dialog on top of all other open windows. Include header slots , which lists all the status slots of the selected agent. Paste slot names , to include the selected slot name with the selected agent name e.g. ANA01.value Paste server name , to include the selected Agent Server name with the selected agent name e.g. \\SERVER\ANA01 The information panel at the bottom of this dialog, has the following name \\AgentServerName\AgentType, where AgentServerName is the name of the connected Agent Server and AgentName is the name of the currently selected agent. This displays the following information regarding the currently selected tag (agent.slot): The description, of the currently selected agent. The slot type of the currently selected slot. For details, see Slot Types . The name (description) of the currently selected slot. The value of the currently selected slot. Note: When the selected slot is a LIST slot then a browse (...) button is displayed to the right of the slot value, which when clicked displays the contents of this LIST slot in a table with the required headings. Double clicking an agent displays a dialo

se (...) button is displayed to the right of the slot value, which when clicked displays the contents of this LIST slot in a table with the required headings. Double clicking an agent displays a dialog that allows you to view the real time status of an agent at a glance. By default this displays a categorised view, for instance the Status category displays agent specific statuses, although you can check the Sorted checkbox to display an alphabetical listing. You can also click the Previous / Next buttons (or use the PAGE UP / PAGE DOWN keys) to view other agents of the selected agent type. -->

Value formatting syntax Top Value formatting syntax When you can format the appearance of a value, this formatting is defined as a string, which adheres to the following syntax: { # [, alignment ][: dataFormat ]} General syntax information: Note1: Only the matching curly brackets ("{" and "}") and the number '#' are compulsory. Note2: Any text or numbers typed into the format string, which are not in curly brackets will be displayed as-is. Note3: Because opening and closing curly brackets are interpreted as starting and ending a format item, you must specify two opening curly brackets ("{{") in order to display one opening curly bracket ("{"), and, similarly, two closing curly brackets ("}}") to display one closing curly bracket ("}"). Note4: It is only possible to use one set of curly brackets when formatting a value. Where: The compulsory # , is the unique number, starting from 0, which denotes the input that is being formatted. Typically this will be 0, unless more than one value has been added. Specific syntax information: Note1: The same # can be formatted multiple times in the same format string. For example, if the value is numeric, this can be formatted in hexadecimal, scie

s been added. Specific syntax information: Note1: The same # can be formatted multiple times in the same format string. For example, if the value is numeric, this can be formatted in hexadecimal, scientific, and number format, in the same format string, as follows: "{0:X} {0:E} {0:N}". Note2: The order in which the # values are formatted is unimportant. For example, if there are three values, you can format the second, first, and third value by specifying a format string like this: "{1} {0} {2}". Note3: A # value that is not referenced within the format string it will NOT be displayed. Note4: If you specify a # that designates an input which has not been added yet, the Format input cell will prevent you from entering this format string until either a valid # is specified or it is removed. The optional alignment component is a signed integer indicating the preferred formatted field width, which can be specified for any value, irrespective of its data type. Specific syntax information Note1: The comma (,) is required if alignment is specified. Note2: If padding is necessary, white space is used. Note3: The examples specified in this table assume that a String value of ABCDEFGHIJ is a

Variable Data Element spiders Top Variable Data Element spiders The Variable Data Element spider can dynamically change a portion of or the entire names of data elements and if necessary configure their values. Example of usage: A typical example of usage would be for a redundant server system or process; where only the datasource portion of the datasource name changes between the common setups. In this case, this spider can be used for all the relevant data elements, instead of creating an entirely redundant set of spiders. Through the creation of named inputs, the Variable Data Element spider allows you to combine (concatenate) these inputs to dynamically specify several components of a data element name at runtime. Example: In this example a variable data element concatenates the {AgentServer}.{PUMP} inputs to dynamically specify the value of any pump on any Agent Server, which are specified via graphic form aliases. text: Versioning WGP Files Top Versioning WGP Files Adroit WGP files from version 6, contain versioning information to provide an audit trail of changes for debugging and troubleshooting purposes and to assist in locating the required backup file when recovering lost changes. Note: In addition to this version information, Adroit WGP files can ensure that changes made to the WGP file are safeguarded between the regular backups. For details, see Configuring Automatic WGP File Backups . WARNING! This feature is merely intended to AUGMENT the existing backup system and NOT to REPLACE it i.e. it is still imperative that an efficient backup system is in place! For details, see Creating Backup Procedures . Adroit WGP file structure has been modified to contain this versioning information, as follows: Line 1: This remains unchanged and contains the number of agents stored in the WGP file: SYS=#, where # is the number of agents currently added to this Agent Server. Line 2: From Adroit 6 onwards, this contains the version of Adroit : AVER=XYZ, where X is the major version number, Y is the minor version number and Z is the update number, therefore for Adroit 7.0.0, this number will be 700. Note: Th

contains the version of Adroit : AVER=XYZ, where X is the major version number, Y is the minor version number and Z is the update number, therefore for Adroit 7.0.0, this number will be 700. Note: This is especially important for forward compatibility. Line 3: From Adroit 6 onwards, this contains a sequential version number: FVER=1 Note: This version number will increment EACH time the WGP file is saved, regardless as to whether its contents have been changed or not. Line 4: From Adroit 6 onwards, this contains an optional version description for the WGP file, describing the changes made to it since its previous save: DVER= Adroit default configuration. The manner in which this description is specified, depends upon how this WGP file is being saved, as follows: The WGP file is being automatically saved: In this case, the new wgpdescription String slot of the System Information agent, can be used to programmatically provide the required version description instead. The WGP file is being manually saved: In this case, the Save WGP file pop-up dialog can be displayed to specify this version description or reason for changing the WGP file can be specified. This pop-up dialog only appea

g manually saved: In this case, the Save WGP file pop-up dialog can be displayed to specify this version description or reason for changing the WGP file can be specified. This pop-up dialog only appears when the Enable WGP version description entries checkbox is checked, when configuring the WGP Versioning group of advanced Agent Server settings, which is displayed as follows: Using the Adroit Config Editor : Launch the Adroit Config Editor . Click Agent Server Configuration in the right hand pane. Click Advanced Agent Server Configuration in the right hand pane. This displays a page of grouped advanced Agent Server settings. -->

View the defined attributes of an Object Instance Top Viewing the defined attributes of an Object Instance When an instance of an object template is created, you can view both the template- and object-specific attributes and their configured values for this object. To view the attribute values of an object instance: From the Object Model datasource in the Enterprise Manager Select the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager , as follows: Open the Enterprise Manager . Navigate to Servers > [Server Name] . Tip: The connection name is prefixed by the SmartUI Server computer name. Go to the Enterprise Manager category folders Datasources > Object Model > Instances. Right-click the required instance then select View Attributes . From the Context View window Select the Context tab at the bottom of the SmartUI Designer window. Select the required context from the list, which is typically the Default context. Expand the necessary node . Right-click the required instance then select View attributes . For more information about the Context View window, see the Context View tool window . -->

text: Viewing Agent Information Top Viewing Agent Information Open the Agent Configuration dialog, as follows: Tip: This also opens the Adroit Classic UI in the SmartUI Designer, which provides agent-specific menu functions, such as importing and exporting agents. In the SmartUI Designer: Click the Open Configurator tool in the Agent Server group of the Home tab of the SmartUI Designer ribbon. Note: When there is more than one Adroit datasource available, a list is provided to select which Agent Server to configure. The Agent Configuration dialog is displayed within the Classic UI. Select the Agent Information… command in the Classic UI Options menu. This displays an information window containing the system configuration and the current licensed capacity of the Agent Server. It can be used to check on the status of the Agent Servers in the project at any time. It displays some of the information, which can also be found in the System Information agent. For a more comprehensive breakdown of this information , refer to the Agent Server page in the Project Explorer i.e. press CTRL+E and select the Agent Server (the green gear icon), in its explorer-view. -->

Viewing and removing user-specific variables Top Viewing and removing user-specific variables User profile provide the facility for any SmartUI Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. or Server component or a user-defined script to store the value of user profile-specific variables for later retrieval. Profile users can also view the names of these variables and/or remove those that are no longer required. Typical user-specific variables: SuppressAskToSaveServerData : This stores the response to the Save Server Data question when exiting the SmartUI Designer. RecentlySelectedElements : This stores a list of 10 data elements that you have most recently selected, which is used to populate the Recently selected elements list of the data element browser. For details, see Data element browser . TrendConfigurator : The default name of the variable used by TrendConfigurator controls to store their run-time configuration. This name can be changed by editing the UserProfileSetting property of the TrendConfigurator control. For more details about these controls, see TrendConfigurator controls . name can be changed by editing the UserProfileSetting property of the TrendConfigurator control. For more details about these controls, see TrendConfigurator controls . Viewing Device Details Top Viewing Device Details The Device agent exposes the ‘device’ created in the Adroit Configuration Setup utility, through which the communication actually occurs to its front-end device. It is able to stop and start the communication to and from this front-end device and configure its communication settings, if necessary. For details on Device agents in general, see Device Agents . To View the Details of a Device Display the Tag scanning configuration dialog, as follows: Open the Agent Configuration dialog, as follows: Tip: This also opens the Adroit Classic UI in the SmartUI Designer, which provides agent-specific menu functions, such as importing and exporting agents. In the SmartUI Designer: Click the Open Configurator tool in the Agent Server group of the Home tab of the SmartUI Designer ribbon. Note: When there is more than one Adroit datasource available, a list is provided to select which Agent Server to configure. The Agent Configuration dialog is displayed within the Classic UI. Click on any agent and click the Scan... button. If necessary, select the name of the required device in the Device list box. Click the Details… button. This will display t

ayed within the Classic UI. Click on any agent and click the Scan... button. If necessary, select the name of the required device in the Device list box. Click the Details… button. This will display the Device: DeviceName dialog, where DeviceName is the same of the selected device. The Device dialog box typically provides the following information: the name of the protocol driver used to create this device. the list of valid address ranges for this protocol driver. the number of points ( Adroit tags) currently scanned to this device. the communication status of the device i.e. whether it is stopped or started. You can also reset (close and re-open) and switch the device’s connection, by using the Reset and Switch buttons, which will only work if the associated protocol driver supports this functionality. For further details, see Resetting or Switching Devices . Note1: Although it is also possible to start and stop this device from this dialog, by clicking the Start and Stop button, its easier to use the Started and Stopped selection from the main Tag scanning configuration dialog instead. For details, see Starting or Stopping Devices . Note2: It is also possible to configure the co

easier to use the Started and Stopped selection from the main Tag scanning configuration dialog instead. For details, see Starting or Stopping Devices . Note2: It is also possible to configure the communication settings that are used to communicate to and from its associated front-end device, by clicking the Setup… button. For further details, see Configuring Protocol Driver Settings . Note3: The Refresh button, simply updates the information displayed by this dialog. -->

Viewing Incident Queries Graphically Top Viewing Incident Queries Graphically The AlarmManagement agent provides a dialog from which you can perform various statistical queries to analyse the logged incidents. Many of these queries are derived from the EEMUA 191 guidelines a document created by the Engineering Equipment & Materials Users' Association ( EEMUA) of alarm management guidelines, developed by the users of alarm systems, and is the globally accepted and leading guide to good practice for alarm management. . The incidents returned by these queries are then displayed in a chart. WARNING! We do NOT RECOMMEND using this dialog for an alarm management database that contains a huge number of historical incidents - this can cause your system to become unstable. Note: While this dialog allows you to analyse your logged incidents, we recommend that you install the Adroit Report Suite and specifically the Alarm Management Reports report pack , which provides you with the necessary tools you need to analyse and, more importantly, to improve your alarming system. Tip: This dialog can be resized and maximised and its last size and position is saved for the current UI session. The curr

s you need to analyse and, more importantly, to improve your alarming system. Tip: This dialog can be resized and maximised and its last size and position is saved for the current UI session. The currently selected Query , changes the following items of this dialog: The title to the name of this query and displays its description. The description of the selected query. The default chart used to display the data (incidents) returned by the query. The available constraints. The information displayed by the Legend and/or Labels for this chart. This dialog provides a number of default queries. For details, see Default Alarm Management Queries . Note: If necessary, you can create your own queries. Certain queries support one or more of the following Constraints: These constraints are displayed by clicking the Constraints... button and can further refine the returned data. In other words they can eliminate unnecessary data. Top: If enabled, specify the topmost number of incidents for this query to return. For instance, when the table records are ordered by time in ascending order, the specified number of the most recent records are returned. Likewise, when the table records are ordered b

ery to return. For instance, when the table records are ordered by time in ascending order, the specified number of the most recent records are returned. Likewise, when the table records are ordered by time in descending order, the specified number of the oldest records are returned. From: If enabled, specify the date and time of the start of the interval of analysis. To: If enabled, specify the date and time of the end of the interval of analysis. The Now button, if clicked, will return the incidents that have been added in the last day, by setting the To field to the current date and time and the From field to one day before the current date and time. Or use shift times: If enabled, specify the required shift number to only view incidents that occur within this shift. Operator: If enabled, select the name of the required operator from the list to only view the incidents that are logged to this operator. Incident categorization: If enabled, select the name of the required category (as specified in the Category tree) that contains the incidents that you are interested in. PLEASE NOTE: These constraints are provided by adding special constraint parameters to these queries, so it is NOT possible to execute any queries that contain constraint parameters from 3 rd party applications. To change the frequency at which the charted data is updated: This will determine how often this query is performed on the database to include the latest logged incidents in the current chart. Specify the required interval in the Auto-refresh (secs) spin control. This exports the displayed chart as a .JPG image to the following file: This file is saved to the system temp folder, typically C:\Documents and Settings[\UserName]\Local Settings\Temp. This file adheres to the following naming format: QueryName as at YYYY_MM_DD HH_MM_SS.JPG. To print the displayed chart using the default printer: Click the Print… bu

To print the displayed chart using the default printer: Click the Print… button. To add a legend to the left of the chart: this displays the information for each data-point of the charted series. Click the Legend checkbox. To rotate the labels of the X axis of the chart: when there are numerous data points on the X axis, some of their labels are not displayed for visibility reasons. To toggle between pie or bar charts: by default, charts are displayed using their default chart type but you cha

ions. If this is ticked, the chart is displayed in 3 dimensions, the default selection. To toggle between pie or bar charts: by default, charts are displayed using their default chart type but you change the type of chart to bar or pie charts. Click the Swap pie/bar checkbox. If the current chart is a pie chart this becomes a bar chart and vice verse. To provide Y axis value labels for the charted series: this labels each charted data-point with its Y axis value. Click the Value Labels checkbox. To provide full labels (both the X and Y values) for the charted series: Click the Full Labels checkbox. text: Visibility Behaviours Top Visibility Behaviours This Behaviour can be applied to controls and graphic elements (vectors) to enable or disable Boolean properties that end-users can see. tag mapping, simply specifies the name of the local and the remote Adroit tag, whose values are to be ‘linked’. These are added to a tag group within a server. Wanlink Quickstart Top Wanlink Quickstart Wanlink allows data to be replicated over a slow or Wide Area Network (WAN) from one Agent Server to another. In other words, it allows remote Agent Servers to behave as if they were normal remote nodes on a Local Area Network (LAN). For further details, see General Description . In order to gain access to a local Agent Server from a remote Agent Server across a WAN (Wide Area Network) ensure that the following steps are followed: Note1: For ease of explanation the local Agent Server will be known as LOCAL and the remote Agent Server, will be known as REMOTE. Note2: This will assume that the FULL Adroit installation has been installed and that the Agent Servers have already been started on both computers. On the LOCAL computer, press the Windows key and start typing in Wanlink Server and select it from the list to run the WanServer. On the REMOTE computer, press the Windows key and start typing in Wanlink Client and select it from the list to run the WanClient. Note: If the Agent Server is not started, then the WanClient application will wait for it and attach to it when it is opened. On the REMOTE computer, in the WanClient program, open t

un the WanClient. Note: If the Agent Server is not started, then the WanClient application will wait for it and attach to it when it is opened. On the REMOTE computer, in the WanClient program, open the File menu and select the Open Configurator command. In the Configurator dialog do the following: Click the Add Server button to configure the connection settings required to reach the LOCAL computer. (Add as many servers as there are Agent Servers that require data from this computer’s Agent Server.) Click the Add Group button to configure a tag group , for the Select ed Server , that may only contain a subset of the total required Adroit tags, depending upon the requirements of the tags it is to contain e.g. the group type determines if the Adroit tags will be able to be modified by the other Agent Server or not. (Add as many groups as are needed to cater for the Adroit tags that are to be referred to by the selected server i.e. the current Select Server entry.) Click the New Link button to configure a tag link in which an Adroit tag on this computer’s Agent Server (REMOTE in this case) is linked to which Adroit tag on the Agent Server of the computer on the other side of the WAN (

on to configure a tag link in which an Adroit tag on this computer’s Agent Server (REMOTE in this case) is linked to which Adroit tag on the Agent Server of the computer on the other side of the WAN (LOCAL in this case). This link is added to the Select ed Group and also determines the method by which the data between these two Adroit tags is transferred. (Add all the linked tags that meet the criteria of the currently selected group i.e. the current Select Group entry.) Once all the tags have been added to their relevant groups and all the groups have been added to necessary servers, then click OK. Note: This is a once-only configuration, the next time that the WanClient is opened; this step can be skipped, unless alterations or additions need to be made to the configured tag mappings. On the REMOTE computer, in the WanClient program, after tag mappings have been configured, open the File menu and click on the Repack command and then open the File menu and click on the Reload command, to avoid stopping and restarting the WanClient. The LOCAL Agent Server will now have access to all the configured tags on the REMOTE Agent Server. Note1: It is possible to configure the WanServer app

to avoid stopping and restarting the WanClient. The LOCAL Agent Server will now have access to all the configured tags on the REMOTE Agent Server. Note1: It is possible to configure the WanServer application to run as a service on the LOCAL computer, so that it start automatically whenever the Agent Server starts up. The WanClient application does not have this facility, as it must be run from within windows. Note2: If the WanClient is started with the "/start" command-line parameter, then it will automatically start communications. Tip1: Both the WanClient (if using the "/start" command-line parameter) and WanServer applications can be started before the Agent Servers have started. Therefore once the Agent Servers are started/restarted the applications will resume communications as expected. Tip2: It is possible to start the WanClient application from an Adroit mimic by using an Execute Command Behaviour, in this case, specify "/start" after wanclient.exe in the "Application name:" field. This will saves the operator from opening WanClient manually each time and because the "/start" command-line parameter is used, will automatically start communicating. -->

What is maximum demand and why should you monitor it? Top What is maximum demand and why should you monitor it? Maximum demand is an additional cost for most non-domestic power users. It is the method used by your electricity provider to control how much electricity you use, especially at peak times, when your usage coincides with peak domestic usage. Your maximum demand limit is the maximum amount of electricity that you are allowed to use to run your process during peak demand times, which in South Africa is measured in kVAh. Both this amount and the cost of providing this power are agreed between you and your electricity provider, with the condition that if you exceed this amount then you will pay heavy penalties. Your electricity provider monitors your maximum demand in “block” periods (in South Africa these are every 30 minutes) during these peak times. Your monthly electricity bill uses the highest recorded block kVA usage as the kVA for the whole month. text: What is maximum demand and why should you monitor it? Top What is maximum demand and why should you monitor it? Maximum demand is an additional cost for most non-domestic power users. It is the method used by your electricity provider to control how much electricity you use, especially at peak times, when your usage coincides with peak domestic usage. Your maximum demand limit is the maximum amount of electricity that you are allowed to use to run your process during peak demand times, which in South Africa is measured in kVAh. Both this amount and the cost of providing this power are agreed between you and your electricity provider, with the condition that if you exceed this amount then you will pay heavy penalties. Your electricity provider monitors your maximum demand in “block” periods (in South Africa these are every 30 minutes) during these peak times. Your monthly electricity bill uses the highest recorded block kVA usage as the kVA for the whole month. In other words, at the end of the billing month you pay the penalty resulting from the largest divergence from your maximum demand for a block period, for the ENTIRE month. What is new in the Adroit 10 Release Apart from various performance enhancements of the existing functionality, Adroit provides the following additions: 1.1. Product Licensing Changes IMPORTANT: HASPs are NOT backwardly compatible with previous product versions due to a change in the internal licensing structure of the HASPs. The Adtech Licensing Utility allows you to get, view and/or update your Adroit product license. • The product license is now a .XML document to make it easier to read and is displayed in the License tab. IMPORTANT: The former Remote Nodes licenses that applied to all types of clients have been DISCONTINUED. These have now been replaced by the following client specific node licenses, each of which have different costs: • Clients: typically Operators and/or Designers and • Web Clients: typically Performanc

metadata.title: What is new in the Adroit 10 Release

text: These have now been replaced by the following client specific node licenses, each of which have different costs: • Clients: typically Operators and/or Designers and • Web Clients: typically Performance Anywhere clients. • Remote Desktop (RDP) clients can now get a free node connection to obtain engineering access to the Agent Server, by adding and configuring the RDAdminName WG.INI registry string value. Note: By default, this registry entry does not exist and therefore all Remote Desktop (RDP) clients are subject to node licensing. This registry value must be created and set to the required Windows username to establish free connections for this user. The OEM (separately-licensed) components are no longer specified by their associated OEM codes but now included as separate textual entries in the product license, so that users can easily see exactly which components they are currently licensed for. Tip: Only the OEM components that you are licensed for will appear. • All product licenses have a GLOBAL expiry and can also support product-specific expiries, which can be used for product trials. • .V2C (Vendor to Customer) and .C2V (Customer to Vendor) files are now used to create and

metadata.title: What is new in the Adroit 10 Release

A new licensing methodology has been added to support new product variants (Ignite and OPC/Edge Gateway) where rather than using traditional scan point licensing the system will count the number of user defined agents. Note: Full and Lite / HMI products continue to use the traditional scan point methodology 1.1.1. The Datalog agent should therefore only be used for proprietary logging and the datalog period ( Length... ) should not exceed what is required for operational trending purposes. In other words, should an operator only need to see 24 hours of trend data to properly monitor and control his plant then the datalog period should only be set for 1 day. Historical data (i.e. data outside of the datalog period), if requested, will be retrieved from the backup files, if required. When the allocated size of the datalog (.LGD) file is filled, it wraps (starts again at the beginning). At which time one or more datalog backup (.LGB) files are created to store this older (historical) data.
