In Adroit 10 , the naming convention of these backup files have improved compared to Adroit 8.4 to significantly reduce the number of files that are created. More details: When creating monthly datalog backup files in Adroit 8.4 , a separate file was created for each day of the month that had data logged, since the file name also included the day that the data was logged. For instance: 1. A data value with a timestamp of 2017-11-21 10:00:00 would go to a backup file called 2017-11-21-m-11 2. A data value with a timestamp of 2017-11-22 10:00:00 would go to a backup file called 2017-11-22-m-11 In Adroit 10 , the name of the backup file only specifies the year and month so that now only one file is created for the month. For instance: 1. A data value with a timestamp of 2017-11-21 10:00:00 would go to a backup file called 2017-11 2. Working with 21 CFR 11 mode Top Working with 21 CFR 11 mode 21 CFR 11 is a standard that defines the criteria and circumstances under which electronic records are considered to be trustworthy, reliable and equivalent to paper records by the FDA. This includes the auditing and authorization of changes to values. When engineering and commissioning a system, the system is not required to comply with 21 CFR 11, it is only once the system is deployed that 21 CFR 11 compliance is required. Therefore, you should ideally engineer your project, with 21 CFR 11 mode disabled, due to the design-restrictions that it imposes and then just before you start commissioning the project you can enable and configure the 21 CFR 11 mode. For more details of the controls and requirements required by 21 CFR 11, see 21 CFR 11 controls and requirements . Note: 21 CFR 11 mode is enabled in the Server Security Settings page of the Adroit Config Editor utility. What 21 CFR 11 mode enforces (design-restrictions): 21 CFR 11 compliance requires limiting system access to authorised individuals. Therefore the connection to the Adroit Agent Server is now secured to limit exactly which client connection to it is allow

Therefore the connection to the Adroit Agent Server is now secured to limit exactly which client connection to it is allowed to prevent unsanctioned access (from Classic or legacy Adroit Clients and third party applications). Note: This means that one cannot use the Configurator to configure Adroit agents in the SmartUI Designer when using 21 CFR 11 mode - so all Agent Server configuration must occur in the Designer itself. A node like an Agent Server, but transparently provides redundancy (especially for Agent Server clustering) by specifying a backup (standby) Agent Server, the backup server provides the values when the preferred server is unavailable. In other words nodename , specifies the network location of either one or two Agent Servers, so that if the first Agent Server becomes unavailable or becomes the standby Agent Server in a cluster, then the other Agent Server, will be queried for the required values. The Adroit OPC Server can run on any computer, from which it will connect to the Agent Server specified by the currently selected node. text: Working with aliases Top Working with aliases When you use graphic forms within other graphic forms to speed up their construction via TemplateGO controls, aliases allow you to expose specific properties of each graphic form (and/or their form components) that you add. Aliases therefore allow you to configure these properties and hence customise each SmartUI Template like any other form component that you add to a graphic form. Click for more details: Aliases expose selected properties of the graphic form and/or its form components to the TemplateGO control, so that these can be independently configured when graphic form is displayed within a TemplateGO control, as follows: A graphic form can associate any of its properties (or its added form component properties) to aliases (text strings). When this graphic form is displayed within a TemplateGO control, you can assign values to these exposed aliases. For this reason, multiple instances of the same graphic form each hosted in separate TemplateGO controls can be separately configured, just like any other form component. For more information and detailed procedures for this and other methods of re-using graphical components to speed

For more information and detailed procedures for this and other methods of re-using graphical components to speed up the process of creating graphic forms, see How to reuse graphical components . The following two secure database connections can contain the audited data elements (values): a mandatory, local SQL Server Compact database that stores the auditing locally on the relevant SmartUI Server computer. Example: Categories tree shows a hierarchical structure of the categories, while the top right-hand Incidents list displays all the incidents in the selected category and the bottom right-hand category/incident details list displays the selected category/ incident configuration. Note: The incident details list is disabled when more than one incident is selected. For a detailed description of why you should group incidents under categories, see Reasons for categorizing your incidents . To add a category: Right-click a category, such as the default Root category, and select Add category… . To arrange categories hierarchically: Add categories within categories. Working with Client security Top Working with SmartUI Client security Security is normally implemented by the SmartUI Server to secure the data exposed by it; however, the SmartUI Client (Designer and Operator)applications also implement its own security. Although, these Client security measures are distinct from SmartUI Server security, they can only be implemented after the necessary allowed groups and/or users have been added to the Server. SmartUI Client security can also be configured by means of user profiles to control the access a user has within the SmartUI Operator application and/or to configure an automatic log off after a specific period of inactivity. For details, see Configuring profiles . However, when designing graphic forms, it is also possible to specify which users have access to which properties exposed by the added form components. For details, see Securing graphic forms . -->

Working with configuration dialogs Top Working with configuration dialogs Configuration dialogs are used extensively for the purposes of configuration. A configuration dialog is essentially a common dialog that configures a process that can consist of one or more steps or components. Note: When a configuration dialog is launched within an application, all further user interaction with this application is prevented until the configuration process is either finished or cancelled. Configuration dialogs provide the following navigational features: The left pane contains a tree view, containing the headings of the steps or components that can be configured, using this configuration dialog. This pane can be hidden from view. Tip: Click on the required heading to select this configuration step. The right pane, which is always displayed, contains the dialog in which the configuration of the displayed step or element can be performed. The left border of this right pane contains a pane display bar, which can either hide or display and adjust the relative size of the left pane of the configuration dialog. For details on using a pane display bar, see Working with pane display bars . Buttons at

ar, which can either hide or display and adjust the relative size of the left pane of the configuration dialog. For details on using a pane display bar, see Working with pane display bars . Buttons at the bottom of the configuration dialog, such as the following commonly used buttons: Cancel: To close the configuration dialog and abort the configuration process, so that any configuration changes that have been made will be lost. <<Previous: To display the dialog of the previous step or element of the configuration process. Next>>: To display the dialog of the next step or element of the configuration process. Note: Depending upon the position of the current dialog in the sequence of steps, either the <<Previous or Next>> buttons may be disabled. Tip: Instead of using the <<Previous and Next>> buttons, click on the required step or element in the left pane of the configuration dialog. Finish: To save the configuration changes made and close the configuration dialog. -->

Working with Configurations Top Working with Configurations Adroit and/or SmartUI make use of configurations, where each configuration is completely separate or insular, containing its own files, application settings and/or registry keys. More details: This allows advanced users who engineer multiple systems at a time to easily separate these systems from each other. This functionality, coupled with the backup and restore functionality allows for the easy packaging and deployment of complete systems along with all their files and settings. Configurations are configured via the Configuration page, which is accessed by clicking the top Configuration item in the tree on the left. Note: Only one configuration can be loaded and used by the various applications at any given time. By default, the Allow Multiple Configurations checkbox is unchecked, so that only one configuration, namely Default, is used, in which case: Note: This Default configuration will either be in Full or HMI mode, depending upon the option you selected on installation. Working with data element security Top Working with data element security Every datasource exposes its data in the form of data elements. It is therefore essential that the access to these data elements be sufficiently controlled to provide the necessary security for your data. Click for more details: Each data element can be assigned security permissions that determine which users are able to configure its security settings and which users are able to view, set or remove it. For details on how to distinguish the available datasources, see About datasources and data elements . Since datasources are themselves data elements this security also applies to them. Data elements can only be secured once the allowed groups and/or users have been added. For details, see Adding allowed users and groups . Data elements need to be secured separately for EACH datasource that is created. By default, only those group(s) and/or user(s) that have global security access to each SmartUI Server have access to all datasources and their data elements. For more information, see Assigning global security to groups and users . The data element is the lowest level to which Server security can be applied. Th

s to all datasources and their data elements. For more information, see Assigning global security to groups and users . The data element is the lowest level to which Server security can be applied. The following strategy is the recommended for implementing data element security: Apply security permissions to the available datasources to ensure that only the necessary datasources are available the allowed users and/or groups for them to perform their required duties. For details, see Assigning security permissions to datasources . Note: The security permissions applied to a datasource can also be applied to all of its component data elements, if necessary. For details of the available security permissions, see Available data element security permissions .. In addition to these security permissions you can also specify which data elements can be audited and/or have their value changes authenticated. For details, see Configuring the auditing and/or authorizing of value changes . Apply security permissions to specific data elements within these datasources, so that only the necessary data is available for them to perform their required duties. For details, see Assigning security permis

urity permissions to specific data elements within these datasources, so that only the necessary data is available for them to perform their required duties. For details, see Assigning security permissions to data elements . In this way, the currently logged in user should only be able to see the datasources and their data elements that are necessary to perform his/her function. Furthermore, whenever any data element is accessed, this SmartUI Server always determines whether the currently logged in user is able to perform the requested data element operation, and accept or reject the request accordingly. -->

Working with pane display bars Top Working with pane display bars Pane display bars are used when tool windows or configuration dialogs contain at least one pane an entirely separate working area of a window, often separated by a pane display bar. See pane display bar. . These bars are located between two adjacent panes and can be used to do the following: to increase the size of one pane by hiding the adjacent pane to adjust the relative sizes of the two adjacent panes, like a splitter bar. to display a pane which has been hidden Pane display bars are indicated by two arrows separated by a row of dots and are always positioned in the center of the left and/or right border of the pane that is able to be enlarged. Note: When a pane display bar is situated between two panes, the border above and below this pane display bar becomes a splitter bar, therefore point above or below the display bar, until the mouse pointer assumes the splitter bar icon and drag this bar to adjust the widths of these adjacent panes accordingly. The direction in which the arrows point, indicate whether a pane will be hidden or displayed, as follows: If a pane display bar is between two adjacent panes, then t

these adjacent panes accordingly. The direction in which the arrows point, indicate whether a pane will be hidden or displayed, as follows: If a pane display bar is between two adjacent panes, then the pane that the arrows point to will be hidden, when the pane display bar is clicked. Working with policies Top Working with policies Policies are configurable sets of rules, which provide a general (large-scale) level of control to safeguard the services and data that the SmartUI Server provides. In other words, policies control the access to a SmartUI Server and to each datasource plugin a generic type of data supplier that interfaces between the Server and this specific type of data, so that it is exposed to the Server in the format of data elements. See data element. for the allowed groups and/or users, as follows: Each policy represents a specific service or activity that can be performed by this SmartUI Server. Certain policies are datasource plugin-specific. For details on the provided services, see Available policies . By associating the allowed users and/or groups with each policy, you are able to determine the extent of their access to this SmartUI Server and its datasource plugins. For details, see Associating policies with allowed users and groups . Any allowed user and/or group not associated with a policy is unable to perform the service that it represents. In this way, whenever a SmartUI Server receives a request for a service, it first determines whe

wed user and/or group not associated with a policy is unable to perform the service that it represents. In this way, whenever a SmartUI Server receives a request for a service, it first determines whether the currently logged in user is part of the allowed users or groups that are able to perform this request, and then denies or grants access based on this result. Click for more information: Policies are configured per Server connection in the Enterprise Manager , by using its Security component within the Management category. Any group(s) and/or user(s) that have been assigned global security access to this SmartUI Server, is automatically associated with every policy. For details, see Assigning global security to groups and users . Additional groups, over and above those that are assigned global security access, may initially be associated with every policy. For details on configuring this security setting, see Server security settings . Once a datasource plugin is secured using a policy, this security will be applied to all of its existing and future configured datasources. In order to secure a specific datasource, data element security needs to be employed instead. For details,

licy, this security will be applied to all of its existing and future configured datasources. In order to secure a specific datasource, data element security needs to be employed instead. For details, see Working with data element security . Configuring Server security . Adding allowed users and groups . -->

Working with security Top Working with security The SmartUI security system is user-centric and operates on top of the traditional Windows operating system security. This uses a configurable sub-set of the existing users and groups that are "allowed" on each SmartUI Server computer and are hence known as the Allowed users and groups. SmartUI Server security is configured in the Enterprise Manager , by using the Security component within the Management category. The ONLY mandatory SmartUI Server security configuration are the Allowed users and groups, which provides the first or foundational level of ALL user security and management within the SmartUI . For details, see Configuring Server security . Note: SmartUI Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. applications also provide security to control the access of the Allowed users and groups within these applications, amongst other functions. For details, see Working with Client security . Client security . See datasource. and/or special function optionally provided by a datasource plugin to perform additional functionality forinteracting with each datasource and / or its data. . Note: For those projects that require Title 21 CFR Part 11 Compliance, you can enable the 21 CFR 11 mode and implement the implicit security configuration such as specifying which data elements (values) are able to be audited and/or have their value changes authenticated. For further details, see Working with 21 CFR 11 mode . Click for more details: Security should typically be implemented during deployment, so that the initial allowed users and groups can be configured on each SmartUI Server. Then the access of these allowed users and groups should be speci

uld typically be implemented during deployment, so that the initial allowed users and groups can be configured on each SmartUI Server. Then the access of these allowed users and groups should be specified within each Server and Client application. However, security configuration should continue throughout the life of the project to secure new datasources; limit the access of new users and modify the access levels of existing users, as required etc. Note: The lowest level to which SmartUI Server security can be applied is the data element. It is therefore useful to determine the available data elements. For details, see About datasources and data elements . -->

text: Working with Show (All) Information Working with Show (All) Information To assist in troubleshooting your graphic forms, the Smart UI Operator can allow a control or vector, on the displayed graphic form, to display the list of all the data elements connected to its properties, to do the following: to view the quality (good or bad) status of the data element allow you to copy this data element name and in the case of Adroit can allow you to edit this tag. Enable this troubleshooting facility, as follows: To enable this for ONLY the topmost control or vector currently under the mouse pointer (for the current TEMPLATE SET), right-click and select Show Information . To enable this for ALL the controls and vectors on the graphic form (for the current TEMPLATE SET), press CTRL+S or right-click and select Show All Information . Any control or vector that has this troubleshooting facility enabled, indicates this by displaying the icon in the top right corner. Example Clicking on the icon, displays the Elements menu item, which displays the list of datasources whose data elements (values) have been connected to the properties of the selected control or vector. Clicking the name of the requ

plays the Elements menu item, which displays the list of datasources whose data elements (values) have been connected to the properties of the selected control or vector. Working with silks Top Working with silks Silks connect spiders and/or Data spiders (properties and data elements) within the spider workspace. Click for more information: Each silk connects the output of a spider to the input of another. For details, see Creating silks . In this way, the silk serves as a simple conduit that copies the value from the first spider to the second spider, whenever the second spider is triggered. For details, see Triggering spiders or Working with spiders . Silks do not provide a bidirectional value transfer; each silk indicates the direction in which the value transfer is performed by means of an arrow. Example: Related links Right-click a silk in the spider workspace, to display the Silk menu of available configuration options. For details, see Configuring silks . Select a silk to provide graphical assistance, when following a particular silk that is currently grouped with other silk(s). For details, see Selecting silks . Remove unwanted silks. s, see Removing silks . Organise silks into sets or groups, known as template sets to further control the transfer of data between spiders. For details, see Working with template sets . Working with SmartUI Templates Top Working with SmartUI Templates SmartUI Templates are reusable graphic forms that can be used at run-time. The fundamental difference between a graphic form and a SmartUI Template is that a SmartUI Template has aliases, some of which are automatically created, which allow data elements within Behaviours and/or spiders to be dynamically driven. Typically SmartUI Templates are used for graphic forms that are displayed as pop-ups or within TemplateGO a Template Graphic Object control that displays a graphic form and connects data elements to any aliases of this graphic form. controls. For more details about using aliases, see Working with aliases . IMPORTANT: The default action for values entered into the Aliases tab of the Advanced View has been changed to always specify the text that is either manually entered or browsed in, unless the Use Tag Value checkbox is checked, at which time it will try to resolve the required data element value from the entered (typically browsed in) text. Therefore when passing substitutions or aliases, in curly {} brackets, ensure that the Use Tag Value checkbox is NOT checked, which is its default setting. When launchin

For details, see Passing alias values from parent to child . Use {} notation to specify aliases, as follows: if you require the alias to specify the ENTIRE value/data element to be substituted then specify the single {requiredAliasName} - this is most typical. if you require multiple parts of the value/data element name to be separately replaced then specify multiple aliases, such as {DataSource}.{Structure}.{DataName}.{Value}. Working with special function security Top Working with special function security Special functions are additional functionality provided by a datasource for interacting with its data (data elements). Click for more details: Special functions can only be secured once the allowed groups and/or users have been added. For details, see Adding allowed users and groups . Special functions need to be separately secured for EACH datasource that is created. Special function security is unaffected by the security settings applied to the datasource itself. For details on securing datasources, see Working with data element security . By securing special functions, you are actually securing specific functionality provided by the datasource itself. This becomes especially apparent when the special function is the only provided means for performing a specific action. The following strategy is the recommended for controlling access to special functions: Specify which allowed users and/or groups are able to use special functions at all, by associating them to the Invoke Special Function policy. For details, see Associating policies with allowed users and groups . Note: Additional allowed users and

le to use special functions at all, by associating them to the Invoke Special Function policy. For details, see Associating policies with allowed users and groups . Note: Additional allowed users and groups may initially be associated to this policy. For details on configuring this security setting, see Server security settings . Specify which special functions these allowed users for and/or groups are able to use for each datasource, so that they will be able to perform their required duties. For details, see Assigning security permissions to special functions . In this way, whenever a special function is used: this SmartUI Server first determines whether the currently logged in user is part of the allowed users or groups that are able to use special functions. if so then this SmartUI Server determines whether the user is actually allowed to use the special function associated with this specific datasource, and accepts or rejects the request accordingly. Note: By default, only those group(s) and/or user(s) that have global security access to each SmartUI Server have access to all special functions. For more information, see Assigning global security to groups and users . -->

Spider workspaces can contain the following items to facilitate the transfer and/or manipulation of data: Spiders, which communicate and/or manipulate data from a set of inputs to a set of outputs. For details, see Working with spiders . Silks, which connect spiders together. For details, see Working with silks . Template sets, which are sets of silks that control the transfer of data between spiders. For details, see Working with template sets . Tip: Wizards that display one or more SmartUI Templates can use their substitutions to drive the values of the aliases of these child SmartUI Templates. For details, see Driving aliases with wizard substitutions . Working with template sets Top Working with template sets The PRIMARY function of template sets, is to connect DIFFERENT sets of data to the SAME graphic form. In this case create the Template sets connecting each of them to the SAME properties; then the currently active template set determines which set of data is displayed. Click for more information: PLEASE NOTE : Spider template sets have nothing to do with TemplateGOs or SmartUI Templates and should not be confused with them! Tip: If you need the SAME graphic form to connect to DIFFERENT data, then use TemplateGO controls to display the SAME graphic form the required number of times. For more information and detailed procedures for this and other methods of re-using graphical components to speed up the process of creating graphic forms, see How to reuse graphical components . Template sets are essentially sets of silks, which are used to control the transfer of data between spiders, by determining which of the silks are enabled or active as only one template set can be active at a time. Note: The name of the currently active template set is specified in the top left corner of the spider workspace. Once a template set is activa

active as only one template set can be active at a time. Note: The name of the currently active template set is specified in the top left corner of the spider workspace. Once a template set is activated, its associated silks are enabled and the silks not associated with it are disabled. Only when a silk is enabled, are the spiders it connects able to transfer their data and therefore perform their functions. For details on silks, see Working with silks . In this way, it is possible to vary the information and even its means of calculation, which is either displayed on a graphic form or mapped to a virtual data element. For details, see Animating graphic forms . Tip: In addition to manually configuring spiders and silks and template sets, it is also possible to perform bulk configuration, by exporting and importing this configuration. For details, see Importing spiders and silks . Working with the Agent Server Monitor Top Working with the Agent Server Monitor The Agent Server Monitor utility is typically provided for advanced users to diagnose or troubleshoot the Agent Server and its client connections. The information retrieved from the Agent Server is classified into the following tabs: General : this tab shows certain key pieces of information pertaining to the running state of the Agent Server. These include information such as: The number of available channels. The state of the internal subscription buffer. Various memory allocations. Tip: Depending on the installed version this can also displays the loading status of the WGP file, so that it is possible to view this even when running the Agent Server as a service. Channels : this tab shows the state of the Agent Servers communication channels. This includes which channels are currently connected to by a client as well as the state of health of each channel. Tip: This tab is particularly useful in understanding problems to do with remote client connections and quickly shows if the number of allowed channels is insufficient to service the required client connections. Function Counts : this tab provides a

Function Counts : this tab provides advanced diagnostic information that is only applicable to the Agent Server developers. Chart: this tab displays specific information concerning the performance of the Agent Server. This includes values such as CPU usage, memory consumption etc. This information is shown for a user defined time frame and allows analysis of these values over time. Eventlog : this tab shows the data contained in the Windows Application event log pertaining to the Agent Server (similar to the data displayed in the Adroit event viewer). text: Working with the Datascope Top Working with the Datascope The Datascope displays the data that is being sent to and from the specified device of a protocol driver. Most drivers make use of following colors to make this diagnostic information easier to read, as follows: Data going to the PLC is displayed in yellow, Data coming from the PLC is displayed in cyan, Important messages will be displayed in other colors etc. Example screenshot: Tip: The Datascope can also be displayed from within the driver and device configuration dialog for a specific device of a protocol driver, see Diagnosing installed Protocol Drivers or their configured Devices . The data displayed by the Datascope can either be displayed in HEX or RTU(BINARY), the default or in ASCII, which is RECOMMENDED. The currently selected mode is indicated in the title bar of this window, as follows: HEX or RTU(BINARY) mode: ASCII mode: Type “ A ” to toggle the display between these two modes. Click for more details: Tip: We recommend that you ALWAYS display the Datascope in ASCII format, even for known Binary(hex) type protocols, because the newer drivers provide extra information usually in a readable (English) format and a

mmend that you ALWAYS display the Datascope in ASCII format, even for known Binary(hex) type protocols, because the newer drivers provide extra information usually in a readable (English) format and also convert the hexadecimal display to ASCII to remain compatible. Note1: If the following characters are displayed in ASCII mode: as displayed in the screenshot example above, then it may be useful to type in “A” again to toggle the display of the Datascope back into RTU(BINARY) mode. Note2: Typing in “A” to toggle between the display modes is equivalent to using the command-line option "/A". Press the SPACEBAR to PAUSE this display of data to allow the window to be scrolled up and down. Press any other key to CONTINUE the display of data. Click for more details: Note: While the Datascope is ’paused’, the data is still being captured and will only wrap at 32 Kbytes. Tip: If the Datascope becomes clogged with data, it may take hours to decipher, to avoid this either increase the device polling times and/or stop other Scan agents. Create a Protocol Dump using the Datascope, as follows: press the “ L ” key, wait for the Datascope to fill with messages and then press the “ L ” key again.

ling times and/or stop other Scan agents. Create a Protocol Dump using the Datascope, as follows: press the “ L ” key, wait for the Datascope to fill with messages and then press the “ L ” key again. This creates a Devicename.txt file in the folder in which this utility is launched your Adroit system folder, typically C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit , where Devicename is the name of the device specified in the title bar of this window. Click for more details: Tip: Press the “ H ” key instead to log the output to an HTM file, which also preserves the color of the Datascope to make the troubleshooting process easier. The extension of this file is .HTM Note: If you are unfamiliar with communication protocols, then this log file or protocol dump can then be sent faxed or emailed to the support desk, to troubleshoot any communication problem experienced by this device. WARNING! Both the L and H options will append to an existing log file, which has no size limitation and so can consume all the free disk space, unless these log files are properly managed. Note: Typing in “L” or “H” to log the output to the Datascope is equivalent to using the command-line option "/L" or “/H”.

Working with the Health Monitor Service Top Working with the Health Monitor Service The common Health Monitor Service (HealthMonitorService.exe) is installed by all Adroit Technologies applications and it runs in the background and cannot be interacted with directly. Its function is to monitor various significant values of the system (computer) on which these Adroit Technologies applications are running, since these both directly and indirectly affect their performance (their health), such as the CPU load monitoring. This Health Monitor Service creates a Windows EventLog called “HealthMonitorService”, where it logs any related messages. What does it do? At start-up the service attempts to determine which network cards have Power Saving Enabled. At start-up the service will attempt to determine the UAC status of the currently logged on user. The Service will periodically attempt to check the following computer information (every 10 minutes): Total instantaneous CPU Usage as a % Total and available Memory (Physical & Virtual) Drive Information for all drives (Total size and available space) The Service will periodically check specific processes (every 30 seconds) The default processe

metadata.title: Working with the Health Monitor Service

text: d available Memory (Physical & Virtual) Drive Information for all drives (Total size and available space) The Service will periodically check specific processes (every 30 seconds) The default processes are "as.exe", "VIP Designer.exe", "VIP Operator.exe", "VIPServer.exe", "VIPService.exe". However you can add additional processes too - see below for details. The following CPU usages are checked for each process: If the CPU % is higher than 50% of 1 CPU Core it gets flagged for higher resolution monitoring. text: Working with the Launcher Top Working with the SmartUI Launcher Although the Launcher does not perform any client or server functionality, itself, it can install the SmartUI Operator remotely (either over a LAN or the Internet) and / or ensure that this component remains up to date with the latest files, if required. Tip: For a detailed step-by-step procedure of connecting Operators to a Server over the Internet, see How to Connect to the Server over the Web . The SmartUI Launcher connects to a pre-configured distribution computer over a LAN or the Internet and synchronises the contents of its installation folder with a specific folder on the distribution computer. Click for more details: For details on connecting to a pre-configured distribution computer, see Connecting to the distribution computer . This "distribution" computer is simply a computer that has the VIP Distributor service installed and running. This service specifies the required "distribution" folder that a Launcher application can connect to and synchronise its contents with, which is typically the C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI \Distribution folder of the SmartUI Server computer. For further d

lication can connect to and synchronise its contents with, which is typically the C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI \Distribution folder of the SmartUI Server computer. For further details of the procedure whereby contents of the Launcher's installation folder are synchronised with a specific folder on the distribution computer: In other words, once the SmartUI Launcher has connected to the specified distribution computer, the files and sub-folders within its installation folder are compared to those in the specified distribution folder. Only the file(s) and folder(s) which are newer on this remote computer or which do not exist on the local computer will be displayed for downloading. Any executables that are downloaded from the distribution computer can then be run or launched from this application, if necessary, hence the name of this application. Therefore the files placed in the user-configurable distribution folder on the distribution computer, will be the files that are distributed whenever a Launcher is connected to it. Tip: The Welcome section of the Config Editor provides a Setting up the Launcher page to specify the settings required to connect to the di

that are distributed whenever a Launcher is connected to it. Tip: The Welcome section of the Config Editor provides a Setting up the Launcher page to specify the settings required to connect to the distribution computer. For details, see Setting up the Launcher . Note: If the distribution computer uses firewall software ensure that the Distributor service has access to the necessary communication port. For details, see Firewall configuration . To run the Launcher: Either double-click the Launcher shortcut that is placed on the Desktop Or click the Start menu, Programs , VIP Launcher and the SmartUI Launcher item. WARNING! When the required files are downloaded they are currently not streamed and so if the connection is slow or breaks the application will not respond until after a timeout, which could take up to 30 seconds. Note1: The Launcher can only connect to a computer that has the Distributor service installed, which specifies the required folder that will be distributed. Note2: Newer files located in sub-folders can be optionally downloaded, however, newer files located in the root directory will always be copied. Command-line options when running the Launcher: To create a lo

ewer files located in sub-folders can be optionally downloaded, however, newer files located in the root directory will always be copied. Command-line options when running the Launcher: To create a log file, execute the Launcher with the "log" parameter in its command-line. To automatically execute a downloaded executable after the Launcher has finished processing, add the name of this executable (its extension is not required) as its command-line parameter e.g. add Operator to launch the Operator. Note: These command-line options can be added permanently, by simply editing the shortcut used to launch the SmartUI Launcher and adding the required command-line parameter to the Target field. The VIP Distributor service is installed with the SmartUI Server installation and the “Distribution” sub-folder contains the files required for the Operator. For this reason the Operator can be downloaded from a SmartUI Server by using the Launcher. Note: As the SmartUI Launcher is downloading the Operator, ensure that the computer complies with its software and hardware requirements. For details, see System requirements for the Operator. Also ensure that the necessary configuration is performed b

rator, ensure that the computer complies with its software and hardware requirements. For details, see System requirements for the Operator. Also ensure that the necessary configuration is performed before the Operator is launched. For details, see Configuration after installation . Note: If necessary, an entirely different folder can be specified by manually editing the path specified by the RedistPath setting. For details on accessing this setting, see Advanced Distributor service settings . -->

Working with the object model Top Working with the object model The object model datasource enables you to enhance your existing wizards, by adding SCADA Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition, used to monitor and control an industrial plant or process and its related equipment. configuration to them. Its main function is to save you engineering time when bulk creating objects, such as items of equipment, which require similar SCADA configuration. What does the object model do for you? It saves you SCADA engineering time by allowing you to reliably duplicate objects that can have all or most of their SCADA configuration pre-configured, such as their scanning, logging and alarming. The objects that you can create will typically be items of equipment, like pumps or motors and can be anything that you have already created a wizard to represent. You can also use the Object Model Template Export and Import utility to export one or more of your existing Object Model Templates to a proprietary .TEF (Template Export File) file and also to import Object Model Templates from a .TEF file. When creating an object template or an object instance, you are able to add one or more attributes or s

ary .TEF (Template Export File) file and also to import Object Model Templates from a .TEF file. When creating an object template or an object instance, you are able to add one or more attributes or searchable strings or identifiers to them that you can use to filter or group the objects that you deploy in the Context View window. What does the object model NOT do for you? It does not help you create the graphical representation of the object, it requires a working instance of a wizard to begin. It does not help you create the SCADA configuration required by this object, it requires that all the necessary agents already exist for the wizard instance that you have selected and that these agents have already been configured. How does the object model work? Up to now wizards have allowed you to create animated graphical representations of your objects, such as pumps and motors - so that you can duplicate them as needed in your SCADA process and linking them to the required process values. But any SCADA-related configuration, such as the required scanning, alarming and logging of this object was left up to you to manually implement for each instance of this wizard. Now by using the obj

But any SCADA-related configuration, such as the required scanning, alarming and logging of this object was left up to you to manually implement for each instance of this wizard. Now by using the object model datasource, you only need to implement the required SCADA-related configuration for one of your objects (a fully configured instance of a wizard) from which you can create a Template, in which you specify both the graphical representation/s and the required SCADA configuration for this object. Tip: If you have an object for which you have created identical wizards with different graphical representations, you can associate these other wizards to this object template. Then you can implement instances of this template, which both creates and configures the necessary agents required by this object and provides the required graphical representation of it too, to reliably duplicate pre-configured objects. In other words the salient idea about the object model datasource is the mass reuse of objects; where each object has a graphical component, much like the existing wizards and a SCADA component, which incorporates the scanning, alarming and logging of tags. It can therefore also

use of objects; where each object has a graphical component, much like the existing wizards and a SCADA component, which incorporates the scanning, alarming and logging of tags. It can therefore also be thought of as a bulk SCADA configuration tool, which also allows you to standardise the SCADA configuration of your equipment. The template and object instances only reference the wizard they do not encapsulate it so when you drop an object instance on a graphic form - it is a wizard instance that provides SCADA configuration. So you can interact with this wizard instance as normal - therefore if you update the original wizard you can update this wizard instance if you want to. Note: It is also possible for an object template to incorporate one or more existing object templates within this template, for instance by adding a faceplate to a pump etc. So you need to create your lower-level or commonly used object templates first. Practical example: Consider an industrial plant has a large number of similar pumps made by the same manufacturer, each of which had some characteristics that differed such as their power calibration. The engineer would initially create a wizard that provides

number of similar pumps made by the same manufacturer, each of which had some characteristics that differed such as their power calibration. The engineer would initially create a wizard that provides the graphical representation of this pump. Then the engineer would implement the wizard and create the necessary SCADA configuration for this pump, such as its required scanning, logging and alarming. The engineer would then test that this SCADA configuration was working correctly. Then the engineer would create a template from this working wizard, ensuring that the characteristics that differed between these pumps would be substitutable. Using this template the engineer would then create multiple instances of the pump, changing each of their differing characteristics as needed. So each instance of this pump would then have their scanning, logging and alarming pre-configured. What do you need before you can create an object template? You need a fully configured working instance of a wizard. In other words an instance of a wizard that you have fully configured its required SCADA configuration, so that this can be duplicated for all your other objects. Tip: Take the necessary time that y

. In other words an instance of a wizard that you have fully configured its required SCADA configuration, so that this can be duplicated for all your other objects. Tip: Take the necessary time that you need to test that this wizard has been fully configured and is working optimally and is being correctly scanned and/or logged and/or alarmed. Since any mistakes or omissions that you make will also be duplicated! Take a wizard, ideally an instance of a wizard on a graphic form, that is working as required and create a template from it, which incorporates the graphical components of the wizard (and any substitutions that it uses) along with SCADA configuration, from which you can create numerous instances each of which will create their own unique tags, which will be scanned, logged and/or alarmed, as specified by the template. For instance if you have created a wizard for a pump, you can create a template for this pump that not only displays the pump and its relevant values on a graphic form but which creates the tags that it requires and performs the necessary scanning, logging and alarming that you require. form but which creates the tags that it requires and performs the necessary scanning, logging and alarming that you require. Note: Since a template refers to an existing wizard, if the referenced wizard is deleted or modified, this does not affect the existing instances of this template that have already been added, it only affects the instances that you add after this. Working with the object model Top the object model The object model enables you to enhance your existing wizards by adding SCADA Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition, used to monitor and control an industrial plant or process and its related equipment. configuration to them. Its primary function is to help save engineering time when you are creating bulk objects, such as items of equipment, which require similar SCADA configuration. What the object model does for you? It saves you SCADA engineering time when creating object templates or instances: It lets you reliably duplicate objects that have all or most of their SCADA configuration pre-configured, such as scanning, logging and alarming. The typical objects you create will be items of equipment, like pumps or motors, including anything that you have already created to represent in a wizard. You can add one or more attributes, searchable strings or identifiers that you can use to filter or group the objects, that you deploy, in the Context View window. You may also use the Object Model Template Export and Import utility to import or export one or more of your existing Object Model Templates in a proprietary TEF (Template Expo

he Context View window. You may also use the Object Model Template Export and Import utility to import or export one or more of your existing Object Model Templates in a proprietary TEF (Template Export File) file format. What the object model does NOT do for you? The object model will not help you to: Create a graphical representation of the object, because it requires a working instance of a wizard. Create the SCADA configuration required by this object, as it requires that all the necessary agents are already assigned in the selected wizard instance and that these agents are correctly configured. How does the object model work? Up to now, wizards have let you create animated graphical representations of your objects, such as pumps and motors, which you can duplicate as needed in your SCADA process and then link them to the required process values. The primary function of the object model datasource is the mass reuse of objects, where each object has a graphical component, much like the existing wizards, and a SCADA component which incorporates the scanning, alarming and logging of tags. Essentially, it is a bulk SCADA configuration tool, which lets you standardise the configurat

the existing wizards, and a SCADA component which incorporates the scanning, alarming and logging of tags. Essentially, it is a bulk SCADA configuration tool, which lets you standardise the configuration of your equipment. It was mostly left up to you to manually implement for each object wizard instance of the SCADA configuration, such as the required scanning, alarming and logging. You can use the object model datasource to implement the required SCADA configuration for each of your objects (i.e. a fully configured instance of a wizard) and create a template, which specifies both the graphical representation and the required SCADA configuration for this object. Tip: If you have an object with identical wizards and different graphical representations, you can associate other wizards to this object template. To reliably duplicate pre-configured objects, you can implement instances of this template, which creates and configures the necessary agents required by this object, and also provides the required graphical representation. The template and object instances only reference the wizard and do not encapsulate it. When you drop an object instance on a graphic form, it is the wizard

ides the required graphical representation. The template and object instances only reference the wizard and do not encapsulate it. When you drop an object instance on a graphic form, it is the wizard instance that provides the SCADA configuration. You can interact with this wizard instance as usual. If you update the original wizard, you can update this wizard instance if you want to. Note: It is also possible for an object template to incorporate one or more existing object templates within this template, for instance by adding a faceplate to a pump. So you need to create your lower-level or commonly used object templates first. An example of a practical scenario: Consider an industrial plant having a large number of similar pumps made by the same manufacturer and each pump has some characteristics that differ, such as the pump’s power calibration. The engineer creates a wizard that provides a graphical representation of each pump, using the following steps: Implement a wizard and create the necessary SCADA configuration for each pump, such as its required scanning, logging and alarming. Test that the SCADA configuration is working correctly. Now, create a template from this worki

ate the necessary SCADA configuration for each pump, such as its required scanning, logging and alarming. Test that the SCADA configuration is working correctly. Now, create a template from this working wizard, ensuring that the characteristics that are different between the pumps are substitutable. Using this template, the engineer creates multiple instances of the pump, changing each of their different characteristics as needed. As a result, each instance of the pump would have their individual scanning, logging and alarming pre-configured. What do you need before you can create an object template? You need a configured working instance of a wizard where you have fully configured the required SCADA configuration. The instance is then available for duplication to all your other objects. Important: Take the necessary time to test that the wizard has been correctly configured and is working optimally. Ensure that it can be scanned, logged and alarmed correctly. Be aware that any mistakes or omissions will be duplicated. So, take care! Take a wizard on a graphic form, one that is working as required and use it to create a new template. The template must incorporate the graphical comp

s or omissions will be duplicated. So, take care! Take a wizard on a graphic form, one that is working as required and use it to create a new template. The template must incorporate the graphical components of the wizard, along with any substitutions that it uses, and including the SCADA configuration. You can now create numerous instances of each that will create their own unique tags and can be scanned, logged and alarmed, as specified by the template. For example, if you have created a wizard for a pump, you can create a template for the pump that displays the pump, all its relevant values on a graphic form and also creates the required tags and performs the necessary scanning, logging and alarming. Important: Creating templates is a task for advanced users who are fully aware of how their SCADA system (Agent Server) is configured. However, creating the template instances is a lot easier. Note: A template always refers to an existing wizard. However, if the referenced wizard is deleted or modified, it does not affect the existing template instances that have already been added, it will only affect the instances that you add later. Working with the Server Top Working with the SmartUI Server The SmartUI Server is a "data portal" which exposes data from a number of disparate sources that are both external and internal to it. Note: SmartUI Servers can be clustered to handle their combined workload evenly and to provide continued operation in the event that one or more fail. This is the only component of the SmartUI that requires a licence before it can be launched. For more information on licensing the SmartUI Server, see Licensing the Server . Note: It is possible use the SmartUI Server freely, with a Designer and an Operator connections for 2 hours, after which the Server must be restarted. The SmartUI Server can either be run as: An application, in which case the Activity Monitor provides additional Server-related functionality. For details, see Working with the Activity Monitor . A service within Windows, which ensures that it will not shutdown when you log off and where you can use the SmartUI Service Manager to manage (start/stop) this service. For details, see Working with the SmartUI Service Manager . The SmartUI Server can either be automatically saved on shut down and/or can be manually saved. For deta

o manage (start/stop) this service. For details, see Working with the SmartUI Service Manager . The SmartUI Server can either be automatically saved on shut down and/or can be manually saved. For details, see Saving the SmartUI Server . Tip: The Adroit Config Editor provides a System Backup and Restore feature that can backup and restore your SmartUI and/or Adroit user-configuration. For details, see System Backup and Restore . Troubleshooting The Server also provides methods for logging Server-related events in varying degrees of detail, for both diagnostic and auditing purposes. For details, see Diagnosing the SmartUI Server . The System datasource provides a view into the Server and exposes information and functions pertaining to the SmartUI Server itself and the SmartUI Clients (Operators and/or Designers) that are connected to it. See System Information . Related links The Server and/or service can be separately customised, if necessary. For details, see Setting up the Server or Advanced Server settings or Advanced Server service settings . For more details about running the Server either as an application or as a service within Windows. For details, see Launching the SmartUI

dvanced Server settings or Advanced Server service settings . For more details about running the Server either as an application or as a service within Windows. For details, see Launching the SmartUI Server . For further details about clustering Servers to share their combined workload evenly and to provide continued operation in the event that one or more fail, see Server clustering . For details on viewing your current license details, see Viewing Server license information . For details on locating this saved data, for backing up purposes etc., see Locating saved data . For details about both the internal and external datasources, see About datasources and data elements . -->

Working with the SimCSV driver Top Working with the SimCSV driver The SimCSV driver is not a true driver in the sense that it does not communicate to a front-end device; instead, it allows a user to define the required timestamped sequence of integer, real or Boolean values to simulate the scanning or logging of a real-time process value. If necessary, you can also: adjust the time intervals between successive values and/or specify historical values too and, if need be, specify the required quality or status (bad / good) of this value too. The SimCSV driver simply reads in a .CSV file that specifies which of its addresses should be changed in value at whatever time and/or whatever status (quality) should be applied to change in value in order to define the required sequence. Therefore, this driver can be very helpful when testing or demonstrating other agents like the Analog or DBLog agent, that require real world scanning and/or logging of real-time process values. CSV File Structure Seq T+x , Address , Value {, Time offset from seq , Fixed-Timestamp , Status } Note: This .CSV file structure is case insensitive. The following first three entries are required, but the others entrie

Seq T+x , Address , Value {, Time offset from seq , Fixed-Timestamp , Status } Note: This .CSV file structure is case insensitive. The following first three entries are required, but the others entries can be omitted: Seq T+x : this specifies how long after the .CSV file was initially loaded (or reloaded) to change the specified address to the specified value. So a value of 0 performs this change in value as soon as the .CSV file is loaded. But any positive value specifies the number of seconds to wait after the .CSV file loads before the specified address is changed to the specified value. IMPORTANT: If this time offset is configured then the order in which the values of the specified addresses are changed are NOT determined by the sequence of rows in the .CSV file, but by the specified time offsets instead! Address : the address (and therefore the applicable data type) to which the specified value will be written. Value : the required value to write to the Address at the specified time. For instance: 0 , DW0 , 1 In this case as soon as the .CSV file is loaded a value of 1 is written to the DW0 address (which is presumably being scanned to an Integer or Real tag). Since when no ti

me. For instance: 0 , DW0 , 1 In this case as soon as the .CSV file is loaded a value of 1 is written to the DW0 address (which is presumably being scanned to an Integer or Real tag). Since when no time is specified then the time of Now is assumed and when no status is provided then a status (quality) of good is assumed. Applicable Addresses Scan an Integer to one of these INDEX addresses either to read the value of the associated internal variable or to perform the associated action at runtime: Integer Address Function Description IN0 (last callback) The time that the last address changed in value. IN1 (Time since start) The time that has elapsed since the .CSV file started. IN2 (Reload csv) Action: reloads the .CSV file of this driver. IN3 (Execute csv) Action: starts processing the .CSV file of this driver. IN4 (Reload and execute) Action: reloads and processes the .CSV file. IN5 (Iteration count) The number of times that the .CSV file has reiterated. Use the following applicable addresses to write a value to an Integer, Real (Analog) or Boolean (Digital) tag: Address Type prefix Min Range Max Range BOOLEAN Tag INTEGER Tag REAL Tag STRING Tag Dataword DW 0 9 - DW0-9 DW0-9 - Data

dresses to write a value to an Integer, Real (Analog) or Boolean (Digital) tag: Address Type prefix Min Range Max Range BOOLEAN Tag INTEGER Tag REAL Tag STRING Tag Dataword DW 0 9 - DW0-9 DW0-9 - Databit DI 0 15 DI0-15 - - - Note: This driver does NOT support the writing of values to String tags. Skipping Optional Parameters If you want to skip one of the optional entries then include the comma and a space as the driver does a fixed lookup. For instance to only specifying the Status, specify TWO successive commas and spaces first: 5 , DW0 , 5 , , ,I Optional Parameters Time offset from seq The sequence time offset can be either a float or an integer value relative to the sequence, meaning that if the sequence is active the time (NOW) is used and the offset, if any, is appended to the active time. This offset can be either positive (future or forward in time) or negative (historical or back in time). For instance: 0,dw0,123 ……………… omitted 0,dw0,123,1 ……………. Time 0 + 1 0,dw0,123,-4 ……………. Time 0 - 4 Instead of the specifying the required number of seconds that are either added or subtracted from the start time when the .CSV file is loaded you can also specify the required timestamp u

. Time 0 - 4 Instead of the specifying the required number of seconds that are either added or subtracted from the start time when the .CSV file is loaded you can also specify the required timestamp using an IEEE754 float string or an OLEDT using the system locale settings. For instance: 0,dw0,123,29/09/2018 12:33:23 …… a specific datetime Fixed Timestamp This column allows you to specify the required timestamp of this change in value that uses the locale settings of the computer on which this is run. For instance: 4 , DW0 , 4 , , 1993/01/01 12:33:24 Status (Quality) The status (quality) that the system will apply to this update, which may or may not override the specified timestamp, as follows: [] – Good … Driver will send a {NOW} or {SPECIFIED} timestamp [I , i] – Item bad … Driver will send a {-2} timestamp just for this item [J , j] – Whole job that this item belongs to is marked bad {NULL} with this event… {old method} [K , k] – Whole job that this item belongs to is marked bad {-2} timestamp with this event… {new method} [D , d] – Whole Device is bad all its jobs will be marked bad {NULL} with this event… {old method} [E , e] – Whole Device is bad all its jobs will be marked

2} timestamp with this event… {new method} [D , d] – Whole Device is bad all its jobs will be marked bad {NULL} with this event… {old method} [E , e] – Whole Device is bad all its jobs will be marked bad {-2} timestamp with this event… {new method} IMPORTANT: It is not possible to update an item to a historical time and mark it bad at the same time, it is only possible to mark the latest value bad at time now! Special Lines Comments: Lines can be commented out using “//” For instance: //This is a comment Reiteration command The :reiterate command can be specified in the last line of the .CSV file to cause this file to loop around back to the top. For instance: :reiterate Tip: In this case you can query the IN5 address to determine how many times the .CSV file has been repeated. Usage Examples: The following provides a number of CSV rows followed by an explanation of what this means: 0 , DW0 , 123.45 , 0 , I At start time = T+0, which is now, update DW0 with 123.45 with a timestamp of now (same as index) and mark the item bad (new method) (this will actually change the new time to -2). IMPORTANT: It is not possible to update an item to a historical time and mark it bad at the same t

ow (same as index) and mark the item bad (new method) (this will actually change the new time to -2). IMPORTANT: It is not possible to update an item to a historical time and mark it bad at the same time; it is only possible to mark the latest value bad at time now! 0 , DW1 , 0 , , 1973/12/3 12:33:45 At start time = T+0, which is now, update DW1 with 0 with a timestamp of 1973/12/3 12:33:45. 0 , DW2 , 45 At start time = T+0, which is now, update DW2 with 45 with a timestamp of now (same as index). 1 , DW0 , 123.46 , 1 At start time = T+1, which is now, update DW0 with 123.56 with a timestamp of now (same as index). 2 , DW0 , 123.46 , , , J At start time = T+2, which is now, update DW0 with 123.46 with a timestamp of now (same as index) but the whole job will be marked bad {old method – returning failed (timestamp not overwritten)}. Working with the Web Service Top Working with the SmartUI Web Service The SmartUI Web Service provides an internet gateway between the SmartUI Server and its various client applications. Practically this means that the SmartUI Web Service is typically used to do the following: To typically allow a SmartUI Operator client to connect to the SmartUI Server over the internet or intranet . This method uses the VIP Distributor service that is installed by the SmartUI Server install and the SmartUI Launcher that needs to be installed on the user's computer. These two are then linked by the SmartUI Web Service, so that the necessary files are downloaded via the web. To allow a Performance Anywhere client to connect to the SmartUI Server over the internet or intranet. In this case, you ALSO need to install the SEPARATE SmartUI Performance Anywhere component, typically on this web server. Then users can use the provided URL to launch the Performance Anywhere dashboard in their Internet browser, as explained by the installed document. as explained by the installed document. Working with the WGP Inspector Top Working with the WGP Inspector This utility inspects the structure of your existing Agent database (.WGP) files. The following functions are provided: Open file… : Loads a new WGP file. Find text… : This provides standard “Find text” functionality, use F3 to “Find Next”. Find O/P enabled : Finds all the agents that that are configured as being "Output Enabled" and differentiates between complete agents that are Output Enabled (STS=) and individual slots (SSTx=). Find O/P initialised : Finds all the agents that that are configured as being “Output Initialise” and differentiates between complete agents that are Output Initialised (STS=) and their individual slots (SSTx=). Datalog file size… : Calculates the total amount of disk space required by LGD and LGI files. HMI compatible? : Click this button to test whether the loaded WGP file is HMI mode compatible (which is if it ONLY contains the agent types supported by HMI mode) and displays the result of this test in a message box. The Errors section, contains the following settings and checks for locating errors in the currently loaded Agent database (.WGP) file: If the Silent mode option is not check

his test in a message box. The Errors section, contains the following settings and checks for locating errors in the currently loaded Agent database (.WGP) file: If the Silent mode option is not checked a message box is displayed for each error that is found. If the Include default logfiles option is checked, this includes datalogs that log to the default log file. Find errors : Finds references to non existent agents/tags in alarm, datalog, device, eventlogging, expression and statistical agents; empty lines; illegal tag names; references to non existent tags; dead datalog agents (tag does not exist or datalog of a datalog). The results of this check are saved in the file “[wgpname].wgpinspectorerrors.csv”. Find dead : Finds boolean, integer, real, analog, digital and multistate agents that are not referred to by the device and/or expression agents. Usage by other agents is not yet supported. Note: Counters and Statistical agents are not checked. The results of this check are saved in the file “wgpname dead.csv”. -->

Working with tool windows Top Working with tool windows The work environment the user interface of the Designer i.e. the tool windows, toolbars, menus and the Design workspace. of the Designer consists of two types of windows: the Design workspace and tool windows. For details, see Design workspace . Note: Each tool window is a dockable window a window that can be either be attached to a docking area or that can float anywhere on the screen. See floating mode; docked mode; docking area. whose location can be customised to increase the viewing and editing space provided by the Design workspace . For more information, see Arranging tool windows . Tool windows have been used extensively within the work environment of the Designer. For details, see Available tool windows . Since tool windows are dockable, they have the following two display modes: Dockable mode, in which a tool window is usually attached to the Designer, typically along any of the four borders of the Design workspace window, where it can be accessed by means of a tab - if more than one tool window is currently docked at this location. For details, see Docking tool windows . Note: A tool window in Dockable mode can be u

w, where it can be accessed by means of a tab - if more than one tool window is currently docked at this location. For details, see Docking tool windows . Note: A tool window in Dockable mode can be undocked by double-clicking its title bar, in which case it is able to be moved to another location etc, however this is can at any time be re-docked. Tip: Dragging an item over a docked window tab, selects this window tab so that it can be dragged into this tool window. Floating mode, in which a tool window becomes a separate window, with a thin title bar and can appear anywhere on your screen and CANNOT be docked. A floating tool window is always on top of all other windows and can be resized as required. For details, see Floating tool windows . Tip: Simply double-click the title bar of a tool window to change from one display mode to another. Tool windows now provide the Window Position title bar icon, that can be used to perform many arranging tasks. For details, see Arranging tool windows . -->

Working with user accounts and groups Top Working with user accounts and groups SmartUI security uses the Windows user accounts and groups on each SmartUI Server computer. Click for more details: A user account is created in Windows to specify a user and contains his/her user name and password, which is used during log on. A group is created in Windows to contain one or more users. Ensure that the necessary user rights are assigned to each user and group. For details of the required user rights and how to apply them, see Windows security configuration . The default security applied to all datasources and their data elements, only assigns full access to specific administrative group(s) and/or user(s) that are given global access to this Server. For details, see Assigning global security to groups and users . Due to the nature of the SmartUI Server security, it is recommended to use a task-based security model, when creating the user accounts and groups within Windows. Where tasks, refer to the categories of users that you need to define, such as "Designers" or "Operators". Each task is assigned the appropriate permissions when accessing this SmartUI Server, its configured datasource

Working with wizards Top Working with wizards Wizards allow you to reuse the same graphical object and its assigned Behaviours (if any), over and over again, with different values (data elements), without having to recreate this object from scratch ever time. In other words, a wizard is a reusable design-time object, much like a Windows control. Also wizards have the facility to update their instances that have been added to graphic forms to their current configuration, when they are modified after having been used. A Wizard is a pre-drawn and/or pre-configured skeleton of graphical objects and their assigned Behaviours (if any), which has placeholders (substitutions) for data elements, which can simplify and speed up the task of creating graphic forms. But, instead of directly specifying the values that drive these Behaviours, these are replaced with value or static text placeholders (substitutions). Each time a wizard is inserted into a graphic form, a dialog is displayed whereby values must be specified for all the substitutions that occur within this wizard. For instance, instead of redrawing a pump or a motor, each time one is required, a wizard can be created and simply inser

ues must be specified for all the substitutions that occur within this wizard. For instance, instead of redrawing a pump or a motor, each time one is required, a wizard can be created and simply inserted wherever a pump or motor is needed, at which time you link the required data elements (values) to its pre-defined substitutions. The main differences between a wizard and a graphic form: Wizards cannot be displayed in the SmartUI Operator Wizards allow you to assign values to substitutions when they are pasted onto a graphic form (which can be edited later too). Creating wizards : describes the main options when creating wizards and substituting their values. Tip: To create a wizard with a transparent background, set its UseTransparentBackcolor property to True (this is False by default) - do not try setting the Backcolor property of the wizard to Transparent, this does not work. Substitution values : describes how to add, manage and edit substitutions in wizards and their substituted values (data elements) or static text . Note: In addition to substituting the entire value, you can also substitute multiple parts of the data element name too. Modifying or editing your wizards : the

text: Write Only Scanning Strategy Top Write Only Scanning Strategy This scanning configuration, should ONLY be used for write only scanning, but is NOT recommended since it does NOT guarantee than the value of the scanned tag will be in sync with its value in the front-end device (PLC). The reason for the existence of this strategy is to stop writes being permanently sent to the process and thereby consuming scanning bandwidth. For details of all the scanning strategies offered, see Scanning Strategies or for further details on the effect of combining the available global and tag-specific scanning settings, see The Effect of Combining Scanning Settings . Required global scanning settings: ForceOutputs = 0 SyncProcessToServerOnFirstScan should NOT be set to 1, if it is see below as to its effect. Required tag-specific scanning settings: Output Enable = 1 Scan Inhibit = 1 Operation of strategy: When the Agent Server is started, the Agent Server receives the values of these scanned tags from the front-end devices (PLCs). Note: If SyncProcessToServerOnFirstScan is set to 1, then when the Agent Server is started, The Agent Server does NOT receive the values of these scanned tags from the fro

he front-end devices (PLCs). Note: If SyncProcessToServerOnFirstScan is set to 1, then when the Agent Server is started, The Agent Server does NOT receive the values of these scanned tags from the front-end devices (PLCs). When a device stops or starts, the Agent Server does NOT receive the values of these scanned tags from the front-end devices (PLCs) – this is unhealthy. When the communications have been restored after a device has failed, the Agent Server does NOT receive the values of these scanned tags from the front-end devices (PLCs) – this is unhealthy. If a value of one of these scanned tags is changed in the Agent Server, this value is written to the front-end device (PLC). If a value of one of these scanned tags is changed externally, the Agent Server does NOT receive this value from the front-end device (PLC) – this is unhealthy. -->

Writing Scheduled Entries to the Registry Top Writing Scheduled Entries to the Registry After the list of scheduled entries have been modified, such as a new entry has been added or the details of an existing entry have been changed, it is necessary to write this information to the registry. In this way it is not necessary for the Scheduler to remain running in order to schedule the specified entries. This list of entries are written to the registry when the Scheduler is terminated, as follows: either right click on the Scheduler icon, in the tray bar, and select Terminate or by open the Scheduler window and click the Terminate button. Note: Logging off Windows also terminates the Scheduler application. -->
